### 🐛 Describe the bug # `tool_choice: "required"` causes xgrammar FSM crash / infinite hang with GLM-5.2 on vLLM 0.24.0 ## Summary When sending `tool_choice: "required"` with `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}` to GLM-5.2 served via vLLM 0.24.0, the request either returns a 500 error or hangs indefinitely. Omitting `tool_choice` or setting it to `"auto"` works without issue. ## Environment - **Model:** [GLM-5.2-NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4) (served via Ray Serve + vLLM) - **vLLM version:** 0.24.0 (`system_fingerprint: vllm-0.24.0-tp8`) - **Guided decoding backend:** xgrammar (default) - **Deployment:** Ray Serve cluster (multiple worker VMs, tensor parallelism across 8 GPUs (H200)) - **API:** OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` ## Reproduction Minimal request that triggers the bug: ```yaml llm_configs: - model_loading_config: model_id: glm-5-2 model_source: /vllm-workspace/models/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 deployment_config: num_replicas: 3 max_ongoing_requests: 20 engine_kwargs: tensor_parallel_size: 8 max_num_seqs: 32 max_num_batched_tokens: 2048 kv_cache_dtype: "fp8" tool_call_parser: "glm47" enable_auto_tool_choice: True reasoning_parser: "glm45" speculative_config: method: "mtp" num_speculative_tokens: 3 max_model_len: 262144 ``` ```python payload = { "model": "glm-5-2", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello"}], "tools": [ { "type": "function", "function": { "name": "test_tool", "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": {"arg": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["arg"], }, "description": "A test tool", }, } ], "tool_choice": "required", "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": False}, "stream": False, } # POST to /v1/chat/completions -> 500 Internal Server Error ``` With 4 tools and no `max_tokens`, the same request **hangs indefinitely** (no response ever returned). ## Server-side error logs From the vLLM EngineCore on the worker VMs: ``` (EngineCore pid=458) ERROR 07-24 20:32:41 [backend_xgrammar.py:162] Failed to advance FSM for request chatcmpl-55347ca6-... for tokens 5961. Please file an issue. (EngineCore pid=458) ERROR 07-24 20:32:41 [scheduler.py:1606] Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [5961, 13, 154842, 40] for request chatcmpl-55347ca6-... Terminating request. (EngineCore pid=458) ERROR 07-24 20:32:41 [serving.py:120] Request chatcmpl-55347ca6-... failed with an internal error during generation ``` A second pattern seen on another worker: ``` (EngineCore pid=466) ERROR 07-24 20:28:58 [backend_xgrammar.py:162] Failed to advance FSM for request chatcmpl-7008a7bc-... for tokens 154842. Please file an issue. (EngineCore pid=466) ERROR 07-24 20:28:58 [scheduler.py:1606] Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [154842, 9703, 0, 61370] for request chatcmpl-7008a7bc-... Terminating request. ``` The propagated error: ``` vllm.entrypoints.openai.engine.protocol.GenerationError: Internal server error ``` ## Analysis The xgrammar guided-decoding backend builds an FSM from the tools' JSON schemas when `tool_choice: "required"` is set. GLM-5.2 generates special tokens (154842, 5961) during its natural output flow. The xgrammar FSM has no transition for these tokens, causing: 1. **500 error** -- FSM fails to advance, scheduler terminates the request -> `GenerationError` 2. **Infinite hang** -- With more complex tool schemas (4 tools) and no `max_tokens`, the constrained sampler enters a state where it cannot find any valid next token that both the model wants to produce and the FSM accepts. The request loops indefinitely until the client times out. Token 154842 is likely a thinking-mode special token (e.g. `` or similar) that the FSM grammar for tool-call JSON does not account for. ## Two failure modes observed | Tools | `tool_choice` | `chat_template_kwargs` | `max_tokens` | Result | |-------|--------------|----------------------|-------------|--------| | 1 tool | `required` | `enable_thinking: false` | yes | 200 OK | | 4 tools | `required` | `enable_thinking: false` | yes (200) | 200 OK (`finish_reason: length`) | | 4 tools | `required` | `enable_thinking: false` | no | **Hangs forever** | | 4 tools | `required` | `enable_thinking: true` | yes | 500 error | | 4 tools | `required` | omitted | yes | 500 error | | 4 tools | `auto` | `enable_thinking: false` | no | 200 OK | | 4 tools | specific function | `enable_thinking: false` | no | 200 OK | Notable: with `max_tokens` set, the model always returns `finish_reason: "length"` -- it never stops on its own. Under `tool_choice: "required"`, the constrained grammar appears to prevent the model from emitting a natural stop token. ## Workaround Setting `tool_choice: "auto"` works correctly -- the model reliably calls tools due to the system prompt. Alternatively, forcing a specific function via `tool_choice: {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "..."}}` also works. ## Questions 1. Is this a known issue with the xgrammar backend and models that emit special/thinking tokens during generation? 2. Could the guided-decoding FSM be made to tolerate or skip special tokens that aren't part of the tool-call grammar? 3. Would switching to the `outlines` backend (`--guided-decoding-backend outlines`) avoid this issue? ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Performance] Measure Transformers backend startup time vs native
signals.text: This comes from an old comment and was never backed by measurements, so the first task is to establish whether the effect is real at all. It may not be. Runtime throughput was brought in line with native implementations in #47187, but nobody has measured startup time either before or since. ### Step 1: is there a difference? Time engine init for a model that has both implementations, e.g.: vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --model-impl transformers vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --model-impl vllm Compare time-to-ready across a few runs and a couple of model sizes. Warm vs cold HF cache matters, so control for it. If there is no meaningful difference, say so and close this issue. That is a perfectly good outcome and still worth having measured. ### Step 2: only if a delta shows up The backend does some work at load time that native implementations do not, so these are plausible starting points rather than known causes: - `fuser.py` — `get_fuser` traces each module class with `fx` to match it against the available fusers. Cached per class, but tracing is not free. - `base.py` — `recursive_replace` walks the module tree applying fusers per instance. - Config resolution and `auto_map` handling for remote-code models. A profile of init (py-spy or cProfile) will be more informative than guessing from this list. ### Done when Either the startup delta is quantified and explained, or it is shown that there isn't a meaningful one and this is closed.

signals.title: [RFC]: Complete Model Runner V2 pipeline parallelism: scheduling, speculative decoding, and PP-first DP/EP topology
signals.text: ### Motivation. > [!NOTE] > This RFC expands the original request-admission proposal into an end-to-end plan for Model Runner V2 (MRV2) pipeline-parallel feature composition. The original proposal remains Workstream A below, with its prototype in #50410. MRV2 pipeline parallelism (PP) already overlaps multiple batches to reduce pipeline bubbles (#42187). With asynchronous scheduling, it keeps `pp_size + 1` batch slots in flight, while a decode request becomes eligible again after a `pp_size`-step cadence. That foundation works for basic generation, but the surrounding features do not yet compose cleanly with PP: | Area | Current state | Gap addressed by this RFC | |---|---|---| | Request scheduling | Basic MRV2 PP works | A burst can fill the global request slots in one batch and leave later PP batches empty | | MTP speculative decoding | Work is in progress | Drafts produced and applied locally on the last rank must be published to non-last ranks and restored for the still-live rows of the stored step-`T` feedback slot | | EAGLE3, DFlash, and DSpark | Explicitly rejected with PP in MRV2 today | Auxiliary hidden states may be produced on earlier ranks but are consumed by the proposer on the last rank | | Index-sharing models | Rank-local buffers work when producer and consumer are colocated | A PP cut may fall between an index producer and a layer that reuses its top-k indices | | PP + DP/EP topology | Current deployments commonly place complete DP replicas contiguously | On multiple nodes this tends to keep PP local while DP/EP groups cross nodes; a PP-first placement should keep EP/TP inside a node and move PP traffic across nodes | The common theme is that PP is not only a partition of model layers. It also creates two state-transfer paths with different direction and lifetime: 1. **forward state**, sent from one PP rank to the next for the current microbatch; and 2. **deferred result state**, applied locally on the last rank and published to non-last ranks, which consume the stored `PPHandler` FIFO slot `pp_size` local feedback-ring steps later. Adding each new tensor with one-off communication code would make ordering, CUDA-graph capture, request-slot reuse, and multi-node topology assumptions increasingly fragile. This RFC therefore proposes both the missing feature support and a small declarative PP transport abstraction that can carry future optional state without redesigning the execution loop each time. #### Goals - Balance request admission across concurrent MRV2 PP batches. - Define correct MRV2 PP composition with MTP, EAGLE3, DFlash, and DSpark speculative decoding. - Carry auxiliary hidden states and cross-partition index-sharing state when a model partition requires them. - Define a PP-first multi-node placement in which each node hosts one complete PP stage's DP/EP domain, keeping EP/TP communication intra-node and PP communication inter-node. - Keep optional communication absent when a model or configuration does not need it. - Preserve static, graph-friendly buffer schemas and minimize extra collectives. #### Non-goals - Changing Model Runner V1. - Introducing a new speculative decoding algorithm. - Redesigning DP request routing, real/dummy execution cadence, or wave draining, or migrating live request/KV state between DP lanes. - Introducing a new pipeline schedule such as interleaved 1F1B. - Requiring every model to emit auxiliary hidden states or index buffers. - Enabling adaptive verification with PP in the first rollout; it needs a separate protocol for trimmed shapes, confidence/cost state, and rank agreement. - Supporting a PP-stage DP/EP footprint that cannot fit in a node-local topology domain in the first rollout. ### Proposed Change. Implement the RFC as four independently reviewable workstreams over one set of communication and correctness invariants. ```text current-microbatch forward plane scheduler -> PP rank 0 -> ... -> PP rank N (sample + propose) | IntermediateTensors | aux hidden states | shared indices | | +<---------- deferred result plane ----------+ sampled/count metadata and optional drafts (queued in the worker-side PPHandler feedback FIFO) PP-first multi-node placement: node 0 / PP stage 0: [DP0 ... DPN] <- EP/TP stays node-local | PP lanes | node 1 / PP stage 1: [DP0 ... DPN] <- EP/TP stays node-local ``` #### Workstream A: balance request admission across PP batches Within each scheduler/DP replica, the scheduler currently applies `max_num_seqs` as one global running-request limit and greedily fills a batch until an existing token, sequence, KV-cache, or model-specific constraint is reached. A burst of short, uniform requests can therefore consume all local request slots before the pipeline has formed multiple useful batches. For example: ```text pipeline_parallel_size = 2 max_num_seqs = 25 50 short requests arrive together ``` The current scheduler can produce `25, 0, 25, 0` scheduled requests over four steps. The prototype in #50410 instead caps the next batch at: ```python num_requests = min( max_num_running_reqs, get_num_unfinished_requests(), ) max_num_scheduled_reqs = ceil(num_requests / pp_size) ``` The prototype applies the cap to both requests already in `RUNNING` and admissions from `WAITING`, while all existing token, KV-cache, priority, preemption, structured-output, and model-specific constraints remain authoritative. In the example, the first two useful batches become approximately `13, 12` instead of `25, 0`. The divisor is `pp_size`, not `pp_size + 1`: the additional asynchronous queue entry covers result propagation and scheduler/worker overlap rather than an additional compute stage. Non-final chunked-prefill chunks remain eligible in adjacent steps because they do not depend on sampled-token feedback. This is intentionally a PP batch target, not a claim that request count always equals compute. Request count is a useful decode proxy; scheduled tokens are a better prefill proxy. The proposed MVP differs from the current prototype in one important respect: already-eligible `RUNNING` decode keeps its existing scheduling behavior, while the balance target is a soft cap on **new/resumed admission from `WAITING`**. The target may be exceeded when later phases have no runnable work, at low concurrency, at a KV/capacity boundary, or to prevent priority starvation. This preserves work conservation and avoids delaying active decode solely to make phase widths look uniform. Every DP replica computes this target locally. Evaluation should decide whether the final policy is request-count based, token based, or hybrid, and whether a persistent phase assignment is worth its complexity around completion, abort, preemption, resume, and priority changes. #### Workstream B: make PP state transport extensible Refactor PP state ownership into a small declarative module. `PPTransport`, `ForwardPayload`, and `DeferredResultPayload` below are conceptual names, not a required public API. One ownership module describes two independent schemas and communicators: **1. Forward payload: adjacent rank -> adjacent rank, current microbatch** - opaque model `IntermediateTensors` such as `hidden_states` and `residual`; - namespaced sidecars for auxiliary hidden states keyed by a global activation-boundary ID and configured slot; - a namespaced active top-k/index sidecar when the partition boundary crosses an index-reuse dependency. **2. Deferred result payload: last PP rank -> every non-last PP rank, delayed receiver slot** - sampled tokens; - sampled/rejected-token counts; - optional next-step draft tokens; - local queued request mappings and generation metadata that associate the received rows with still-live request slots (these do not need to be network fields). Each adjacent forward edge has its own field/liveness plan; the existing `PPHandler` sibling broadcast has one group-consistent feedback plan. They share descriptor and lifecycle machinery but not communicator, stream, cadence, or participant set. A conceptual field descriptor is: ```python @dataclass(frozen=True) class PPTensorSpec: name: str plane: Literal["forward", "deferred_result"] boundary_id: int | None slot: int | None dtype: torch.dtype trailing_shape: tuple[int, ...] tp_policy: Literal["replicated", "sharded", "direct"] carry: Literal[ "one_edge", "until_last", "until_consumed", "feedback_group" ] lifetime: Literal["forward_execution", "delayed_request_state"] ``` The exact fields can differ. The correctness MVP should run the declared plan over the existing tensor-dict path: - namespace and split opaque model tensors from optional sidecars; - keep each edge's field presence, key, dtype, slot ordering, carry policy, and TP policy deterministic after initialization; - export/import sidecars through model-specific adapters; - retain current tensor-dict metadata and allocation behavior where required for backend compatibility; - stream/event ownership and buffer reuse centralized in the transport module; - request generation/slot checks retained for delayed feedback, so an aborted or replaced request cannot consume stale state; - group-identical feedback row order, row count, dtype/shape, collective order, and whole-collective skip decisions; no branch on rank-local optional-field presence; - optional fields disabled add no bytes or collectives beyond the existing forward and sampled/count feedback paths. For forward sidecars, `N` means the execution row count after padding (`num_tokens_after_padding` / the batch execution descriptor), not only logical scheduled tokens. Buffers and wire shapes use `N`; adapters separately track which rows contain real tokens. For the initial models in this RFC, auxiliary hidden states are TP-replicated, and shared top-k is TP-replicated `[N, index_topk]` `torch.int32`. Existing model tensors such as sequence-parallel residual state retain their direct/sharded policy. Because the current tensor-dict path may automatically slice/all-gather based on tensor size, sidecar policy must be explicit rather than inferred from divisibility. Model-specific adapters should declare which sidecars a partition boundary needs, export locally produced fields, and import received fields into the correct persistent model buffer. The communication layer should not interpret EAGLE, DSpark, or model-specific index semantics. Namespaced wire keys such as `model/*`, `spec/aux_hidden_states`, and `model/shared_index_topk` can avoid collisions while keeping ordinary model tensors opaque. A later performance phase may compile a static wire schema, use persistent graph-address-stable receive buffers, and remove per-step CPU metadata. That requires explicit lower-level `GroupCoordinator`/backend protocol work and is not implied by adding the correctness wrapper. Compatible small fields should be packed when doing so removes latency-sensitive collectives, following the direction explored in draft #47686. Large auxiliary tensors should not be blindly packed with token metadata: grouping must respect direction, dtype, destination, lifetime, TP layout, and performance. The abstraction is unified at the ownership/schema layer, while the two data planes remain separate internally. #### Workstream C: compose PP with speculative decoding ##### C1. Base MTP draft-feedback synchronization Under MRV2 asynchronous scheduling, scheduler-side speculative token IDs are shape placeholders: their authoritative values remain in per-worker GPU request state. The speculative proposer runs on the last PP rank. Every stage's sampled/draft/sequence bookkeeping must nevertheless describe the same logical token sequence: the first stage materializes the correct sampled-plus-draft token IDs, while later stages consume the corresponding forward activations and attention metadata. Here `pp_feedback_step` means a local worker execute/control step that advances the `PPHandler` FIFO. It is not an EngineCore asynchronous batch-queue slot and is not advanced by a MoE DP dummy forward. #52295 implements the narrow synchronization piece. The last rank applies sampled state locally in feedback step `T`, runs proposal, retains its new draft state, and then publishes one feedback record to non-last ranks. The token wire payload is fixed at `[B, (K + 1) + K] = [B, 2K + 1]` (`int64` sampled plus draft columns), while the existing `[2, B]` (`int32`) sampled/rejected count collective remains. Draft synchronization therefore adds `K` token-ID columns per request but no new collective. Each non-last rank posts the matching receive in feedback step `T`, queues it with the saved row mapping, need mask, and slot-generation snapshot, and applies the surviving rows at feedback step `T + pp_size`. Sampled and draft rows use the same liveness/generation decision; invalid draft rows are compacted before index-copy because a `-1` destination is not valid for that operation. The association comes from FIFO feedback-step order and the saved step-`T` metadata, not from the composition of the current batch at `T + pp_size`. The required invariant is: > The last stage applies its sampling outcome and derived next-step drafts locally in feedback step `T` and publishes them as one causally consistent record. Every non-last stage posts the matching receive in step `T` and applies the stored live rows at feedback step `T + pp_size`, before that request's next verification input is prepared. #52295 should be treated as the base transport/state-synchronization change, not as the complete enablement of every MTP model. Its transport gate is PP plus any speculative configuration that has already passed validation, so this feedback mechanism should not be duplicated per speculative method. Broader model-specific work in #46994 includes PP capability declarations, model-specific projection paths, weight/embedding ownership, and a same-rank stale sparse-MLA buffer-reference fix. Those requirements should either land with the affected model or be guarded by an explicit support check; the same-rank buffer fix is distinct from the cross-rank dependency in C3. Fixed wire width also needs an explicit validity/padding protocol for a normal `[B, 1]` no-draft or prefill sampler source; `num_sampled` determines which sampled columns are valid. Existing #52295 coverage consists of two CPU/mock tests for payload splitting/event waiting and draft slot writeback. Real multi-rank communication, fixed-width send/receive, `T -> T + pp_size`, partial abort/reuse, and mixed prefill/decode are merge/enablement criteria, not established behavior. Delaying broadcast until after proposal may also change overlap, so validation must include TPOT and proposer latency. ##### C2. EAGLE3, DFlash, and DSpark auxiliary hidden states These methods require auxiliary target-model hidden states during proposal. MRV2 currently rejects EAGLE3, DFlash, and DSpark with PP before execution. If those guards were simply removed, each rank would capture only its local auxiliary outputs and a non-last rank would return ordinary `IntermediateTensors` without carrying those outputs, so the proposer on the last rank would still see incomplete state. For a configured set of auxiliary layers: 1. normalize each capture point to a global **activation-boundary ID** (`0` for the state before the first layer and `layer_idx + 1` for the state after that layer), including method-specific `+1` conversions; 2. map boundary IDs to the draft configuration's fixed slot order rather than numerically sorting IDs; 3. when an auxiliary state is produced, add it to the forward payload; 4. carry it through subsequent PP boundaries with `until_last` liveness; 5. combine upstream and last-rank-local states in configured slot order; 6. pass the ordered states to the proposer on the last PP rank. Auxiliary states are forward dependencies of the current microbatch, not delayed sampled-token feedback. They should therefore use the adjacent-rank forward plane and must not be added to the last-rank-to-non-last-ranks feedback broadcast. The schema must support zero, one, or multiple auxiliary tensors, and partition tests must cover auxiliary boundaries on the first, middle, and last PP ranks. Implementations that pack compatible states may use a stable `[N, slots, hidden]` layout where `N` is the padded execution row count, but correctness must not depend on all states having identical shapes. Persistent receive/pack buffers are a performance-phase optimization for avoiding per-step allocation and address changes under CUDA graphs. Transport is necessary but not sufficient to remove the current PP guards. Model-specific enablement must also normalize activation-boundary IDs and target layer counts to global (not stage-local) coordinates, validate draft embedding/head ownership on the last rank, and remove loader-level PP rejections only after the corresponding model path is tested. ##### C3. Index-sharing state across a PP cut Some models compute top-k routing/index information in one layer and reuse it in later layers. For example, an index-sharing pattern may contain one producing layer followed by layers that skip top-k computation and read a persistent buffer. If PP cuts between that producer and a consumer in the same reuse interval, a rank-local buffer on the downstream rank has not been populated for the current microbatch. The forward schema must then carry the active top-k buffer across one or more reuse-only stages until it is consumed or overwritten. At model/partition initialization, dependency analysis should determine whether a boundary crosses an index-reuse interval: - if it does not, no extra tensor is registered; - if it does, register the current contract—TP-replicated `[N, index_topk]` `torch.int32`, where `N` is the padded execution row count—and copy it into the downstream persistent shared buffer before model/graph execution; - tie buffer validity and lifetime to the forward microbatch/transport handle so data cannot leak between in-flight batches; - allow future model adapters to declare other trailing dimensions or dtypes without weakening this RFC's concrete acceptance contract. This cross-rank dependency is distinct from the stale-buffer-reference issue addressed by parts of #46994 when draft and target models share an indexer on the same rank. Both must be correct, but only the former requires PP-boundary transport. As an initial safety fallback, unsupported partitions may fail early with a precise error. The intended final behavior is to transport the dependency rather than permanently constraining PP cuts to index-reuse boundaries. #### Workstream D: PP-first DP/EP topology for multi-node serving This workstream is about **physical partition and placement order**, not a new DP load-balancing, dummy-forward, or drain protocol. Each request remains sticky to one logical DP lane, and that lane still traverses one complete PP pipeline. The proposal first assigns nodes to PP stages, then places the stage's DP/EP (and TP, when used) ranks inside that node. ##### D1. Background: why DP-first placement is suboptimal for multi-node MoE With a conventional DP-first placement, complete DP replicas are packed before moving to the next node. Consider two 8-GPU nodes with `PP=2`, `DP=8`, and `TP=1`: ```text default physical placement node 0: DP0{PP0,PP1} DP1{PP0,PP1} DP2{PP0,PP1} DP3{PP0,PP1} node 1: DP4{PP0,PP1} DP5{PP0,PP1} DP6{PP0,PP1} DP7{PP0,PP1} ``` This keeps several PP pipelines entirely inside a node, but the fixed-PP DP/EP domain spans both nodes. For MoE models, expert dispatch/combine is an all-to-all or all-gather/reduce-scatter style hot path repeated throughout the model. Sending that traffic across the inter-node fabric is substantially more topology-sensitive than keeping it on NVLink/NVSwitch. PP communication has a different shape: each logical DP lane sends activations across an ordered stage boundary, with small sampled/draft feedback in the reverse PP direction. This traffic is point-to-point or PP-scoped, regular, and can be overlapped with pipeline execution. It is therefore the preferable communication dimension to place across nodes. ##### D2. Proposed PP-first placement Place one complete PP stage's `DP x PCP x TP` footprint in a node-local topology domain before allocating the next PP stage: ```text PP-first physical placement node 0 / PP0: DP0 DP1 DP2 DP3 DP4 DP5 DP6 DP7 | | | | | | | | +--- matching cross-node PP lanes ---+ node 1 / PP1: DP0 DP1 DP2 DP3 DP4 DP5 DP6 DP7 ``` The resulting communication placement is: - `EP(pp)` stays inside the node containing that PP stage; - `TP(pp, dp, pcp)` also stays inside that stage's node-local domain; - `PP(dp, pcp, tp)` connects matching coordinates across nodes in stage order; - PP forward activations, optional sidecars from Workstream B, and small sampled/draft feedback are the steady-state model data that crosses nodes; - control-plane coordination may still cross nodes and is not the optimization target of this workstream. The physical placement can be PP-first without changing the logical identity of a DP lane. Scheduler, request, KV-cache, sampling, and speculative state remain owned by that lane; no request or KV state is migrated between DP lanes. ##### D3. Topology contract and scope The first rollout should target a uniform topology with one complete PP stage per node. Its contract is: - the stage footprint `DP x PCP x TP` fits completely in one node-local communication domain; - every EP and TP group is node-local; - each PP group contains matching `(dp, pcp, tp)` coordinates in increasing stage order; - every logical worker is placed exactly once, with no duplicated or missing device; - a requested placement that would spill an EP group across nodes fails before model execution; - disabling PP-first placement preserves the existing topology. Multiple complete stage blocks may share a node in a future extension, provided no EP/TP group is split across nodes. A stage footprint larger than one node, heterogeneous partial-stage placement, PCP+DP combinations that are otherwise unsupported, and elastic-EP composition are outside the initial scope. The existing DP/EP execution-order rules remain unchanged: ranks in a coupled EP domain must still enter model collectives consistently, and an idle logical DP lane still follows the existing dummy-execution behavior. These are compatibility requirements, not the feature proposed here. #### Cross-cutting correctness invariants 1. **Verification-state agreement:** every PP stage agrees on ordered request rows and logical token/position/spec-verification metadata; the first stage materializes the correct token IDs and downstream stages consume the corresponding stage-local forward state. 2. **Forward-dependency completeness:** the consumer of an auxiliary state or shared index sees the value produced for the same microbatch. 3. **Slot safety:** aborted, preempted, or replaced requests cannot consume delayed state from an earlier slot generation. 4. **Placement completeness:** every logical `(pp, dp, pcp, tp)` worker maps to exactly one physical device, and every selected device has exactly one owner. 5. **Topology locality:** in PP-first mode every EP/TP group is contained in one node-local communication domain, while PP groups connect matching coordinates in stage order. 6. **PP-lane isolation:** PP P2P and optional sidecars stay inside one logical DP lane and follow the per-edge transport plan. 7. **Feedback collective agreement:** every feedback participant uses group-identical row ordering, row count, dtype/shape, collective order, and whole-collective skip decisions for a feedback step. 8. **DP/EP execution compatibility:** changing physical placement does not change existing collective-order, dummy-execution, or execution-shape rules for a coupled EP domain. 9. **State isolation:** request, KV, sampling, and speculative state remain inside one sticky DP lane; PP transfer is not DP migration. 10. **Work conservation:** a soft balance target cannot indefinitely create empty PP phases while runnable work exists, and scheduler safety/fairness constraints take precedence. 11. **Feature transparency:** optional fields disabled add no bytes or collectives beyond the existing PP forward and sampled/count feedback paths; disabling PP-first placement preserves current topology. 12. **MRV1/non-PP compatibility:** this RFC does not change their scheduling or communication semantics. #### Rollout plan 1. Adapt the request-balancing prototype and scheduler tests from #50410 to the soft, work-conserving `WAITING`-admission MVP, then validate its policy/performance. 2. Introduce the ownership/adapter layer over the existing tensor-dict forward path and `PPHandler` feedback path without changing basic-generation behavior. 3. Land the base MTP draft-state synchronization from #52295, plus model-specific enablement or guards identified by #46994. 4. Add auxiliary-hidden-state descriptors and enable EAGLE3, DFlash, and DSpark model by model. 5. Add partition dependency analysis and cross-rank top-k/index transfer for index-sharing models. 6. Validate the PP-first multi-node topology contract, including node-local EP/TP groups and cross-node PP lanes. 7. Independently evaluate the static-wire/persistent-buffer transport performance phase. Steps that are independent may proceed in parallel, but every step should preserve the invariants above and keep unsupported combinations behind an early, actionable validation error. #### Compatibility and initial support limits - Target and draft model paths must explicitly satisfy PP capability, loader, projection, embedding/head ownership, and partition checks before their guard is removed. - Adaptive verification plus PP remains unsupported in the initial rollout. - Existing restrictions such as MRV2 PP with an external launcher, elastic EP with PP, and `PCP > 1` with `DP > 1` remain unchanged unless a separate RFC/PR addresses them. - `max_num_seqs` remains a per-EngineCore/per-DP-replica limit. - A draft model without its own embedding/head must either have a validated last-rank loading/aliasing path or fail early when the corresponding target component is a `PPMissingLayer`. - Initial PP-first support requires a uniform topology in which one complete `DP x PCP x TP` stage footprint fits inside one node-local communication domain. #### Alternatives considered 1. **Add model-specific tensors directly to each send/receive call.** This is smaller initially but duplicates buffer, ordering, and lifecycle logic and does not scale to the next optional state. 2. **Put every optional tensor in one always-present payload.** This simplifies branching but wastes memory/bandwidth and makes high-volume forward state share an unsuitable lifetime with small delayed token metadata. 3. **Use a separate collective for every field.** Simple semantically, but latency grows with features; #47686 shows why packing small PP feedback fields can matter. 4. **Force PP cuts to dependency boundaries.** Useful as a temporary guard, but reduces partition flexibility and can produce poor memory/compute balance. 5. **Send auxiliary hidden states directly from their producer to the last rank.** This creates a variable communication graph; forwarding through adjacent boundaries keeps ownership and ordering aligned with the existing pipeline. 6. **Keep DP-first physical placement.** This preserves current deployment behavior but can force EP traffic across nodes while underusing PP as the inter-node communication dimension. 7. **Use hierarchical cross-node EP collectives.** This may reduce the penalty but does not provide the same hard node-local EP/TP boundary and remains backend/topology dependent. 8. **Allow arbitrary heterogeneous stage placement immediately.** More flexible, but substantially harder to validate and reason about than a uniform one-stage-per-node first rollout. #### Evaluation plan **Correctness matrix** - PP sizes 2 and 4; DP sizes 1, 2, 4, and 8; TP 1/2 and representative EP configurations; - synchronous and asynchronous scheduling; eager and compiled/full-CUDA-graph execution; - no speculation, MTP, EAGLE3, DFlash, and DSpark; - speculative widths 1, 2, and 3, including no-draft/prefill feedback rows; - auxiliary layers before, on, and after PP boundaries; - PP cuts outside and inside an index-reuse interval; - burst admission, mixed prefill/decode, chunked prefill, preemption, abort storms, pause/resume, and request-slot reuse; - two 8-GPU nodes with `PP=2, DP=8, TP=1`; - two 8-GPU nodes with `PP=2, DP=4, TP=2`; - a representative `PP=4` topology; - both default DP-first and proposed PP-first physical placements. The model-level acceptance set should include: - Llama/Qwen EAGLE3 for global activation-boundary ID and configured-slot ordering; - DeepSeek V3.2 with a forced PP cut inside a producer-to-reuse interval; - DeepSeek V4 DSpark for post-mHC-mean auxiliary state; - Kimi K3 DSpark/EAGLE3 for model-specific attention-residual auxiliary state; - a draft model without its own embedding/head, covering either the validated last-rank loading path or the expected fail-fast error. Use synthetic/unit tests for exact transport contents, schema validation, boundary liveness, activation-boundary slot ordering, request generations, and topology membership. Add real multi-rank tests for `T -> T + pp_size` feedback cadence, abort/reuse filtering, fixed-width payloads, forward sidecars, and collective traces. Multi-node tests must collect actual node identities for every PP/DP/EP/TP group and prove that PP-first mode keeps EP/TP node-local. Representative end-to-end models should cover output parity and speculative acceptance; supported configurations should be compared with PP=1 using deterministic inputs where possible. Require no deadlock or collective-order mismatch under timeout/failure-injection tests. **Performance metrics** - requests and scheduled tokens per PP batch; - per-stage idle time and pipeline bubbles; - throughput, TTFT, and TPOT; - speculative acceptance rate and proposer latency; - PP bytes, collective/P2P count, and communication overlap; - CUDA-graph memory and capture/replay stability; - inter-node bytes attributed to PP forward/feedback versus EP/TP collectives; - EP all-to-all latency, PP overlap, node-local GPU utilization, and topology-induced idle time; - preemption count and KV-cache utilization. Optional transport disabled should have no material regression against current basic PP. Enabled configurations should be compared both before/after packing so communication optimizations remain evidence-driven. #### Related work - MRV2 pipeline bubble reduction and current PP/DP foundation: #42187 - Request-admission balancing prototype: #50410 - Isolated MTP draft-token synchronization: #52295 - Broader MTP-over-PP enablement and model-specific fixes: #46994 - Packed PP sampled/count/draft feedback draft experiment: #47686 - Async scheduling plan: #27679 - Persistent batch redesign: #23446 - Long-context optimized PP RFC: #41685 - Chunked pipeline parallel RFC: #33914 The long-context and chunked-PP RFCs focus on splitting long-context work, asynchronous P2P, and dynamic chunking. This RFC focuses on composing the existing MRV2 PP execution model with scheduler admission, speculative state, index-sharing dependencies, and a PP-first multi-node DP/EP topology. #### Open questions 1. Should the transport API extend `PPHandler` and `IntermediateTensors`, or should both become clients of a new internal `PPTransport` owner? 2. Which small fields should be packed, and what static layout/versioning is needed for full CUDA graphs? 3. Should auxiliary hidden states remain individually keyed by activation-boundary/slot or use one packed tensor plus offsets? 4. Should cross-boundary index state be transported for all supported models, or should the first rollout reject unsafe partition cuts? 5. Should PP admission balance requests, tokens, estimated compute, or a hybrid, and should it be opt-in initially? 6. Should PP-first placement be explicit-only at first, or selected automatically when the stage footprint matches node capacity? 7. Must the initial topology require exactly one PP stage per node, or may a node host multiple complete stage blocks? 8. If an EP domain cannot fit in one node, should configuration fail, fall back to DP-first placement, or require an explicitly selected hierarchical EP mode? 9. Which feature combinations are required before removing the current PP validation guards for EAGLE3, DFlash, and DSpark? ### Feedback Period. 2026-08-18 through 2026-09-01. ### CC List. @njhill @WoosukKwon @robertgshaw2-redhat @heheda12345 @youkaichao @eastwood-c @ChihayaK @yewentao256 ### Any Other Things. The author can provide scheduler traces, device profiles, representative PP partition layouts, and acceptance-rate results for the proposed combinations. Feedback is especially welcome on the transport ownership boundary, the minimum support matrix for the first rollout, and whether index-sharing dependencies should initially be transported or guarded by partition validation.

signals.title: [RFC]: Model Runner V2 Pluggable Design
signals.text: ### Motivation. vLLM's hardware pluggability (RFC #11162) lets each backend register its own Platform, Worker, Model Runner, and so on. This works, but in practice each backend ends up copying the entire GPU model runner and maintaining it independently. The v1 GPU model runner alone is ~8000 lines. Backend-specific runners are typically in the same range, and these files are mostly copies of the GPU runner with device-specific patches sprinkled in. When the GPU runner gets a bug fix or a new feature, every backend has to manually port the change. This is expensive and error-prone. Model Runner V2 already fixes the root cause on the GPU side: it breaks the single monolithic file into smaller modules (model_states, sample, spec_decode, mm, etc.). The total code drops from ~8000 to ~1800 lines. This also creates an opportunity for hardware backends. Instead of copying the runner, backends can now **reuse the V2 runner as a framework** and only override the pieces that actually differ. The problem is that V2 was not designed with this in mind. A backend that wants to reuse the V2 runner has to work around several friction points: - The runner creates internal components (RequestState, InputBatch, CudaGraphManager, Sampler, Speculator) by directly instantiating GPU-specific classes. A backend that needs its own version has to `del` the GPU object and recreate it in `__init__`. - Some logic that backends need to customize (e.g. `prepare_inputs`) is one big method. A backend either copies the whole thing or monkey-patches internal functions. - Triton kernels used inside the runner are GPU-specific. Backends have to rewrite many kernels and patch them in at runtime ### Proposed Change. The design follows three principles: - **GPU native** - **GPU zero burden** - **Flexible backend adaptation** Hardware differences show up at three different levels. Each level needs a different mechanism. Trying to solve everything at one level (either "copy the whole runner" or "make everything a plugin") is what caused the current mess. ``` Layer 3: Runner behavior -> hooks (prepare_inputs, execute_model, ...) Layer 2: Replaceable parts -> Platform factory methods Layer 1: Kernels / ops -> Triton Dispatcher (RFC #45133) ``` ### Layer 1: Kernels Already covered by the Triton Kernel Dispatcher proposal (#45133). `@pluggable_kernel` marks a kernel as replaceable, `@register_kernel(name)` lets a backend register its own implementation. On GPU, no override is registered and the default Triton kernel runs with zero overhead. V2 uses Triton kernels in sampling, rejection sampling, mamba ops, etc. With the dispatcher, backends register their kernel implementations at startup and the runner code stays untouched. **Layer 1 must be solved first** (or in parallel) because without it, backends have no clean way to handle kernel differences. --- ### Layer 2: Platform factory methods The V2 runner is built from several internal components, for example: - `InputBatch` / `InputBuffers` - holds the tensors passed to the model - `ModelCudaGraphManager` - manages CUDA graph capture and replay - `Sampler` - handles sampling logic - `PCPManager` - handles pcp feature Some backends need their own version of these. For example, a backend's attention implementation may need `seq_lens_cpu` which the GPU runner no longer tracks, so it needs an `InputBatch` subclass with that extra field. A backend may also use a different graph mechanism, so it needs a different graph manager. The runner creates these with direct instantiation today: ```python # vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py (today) self.input_buffers = InputBuffers(...) self.cudagraph_manager = ModelCudaGraphManager(...) ``` The fix is to let the Platform provide these classes, the same way it already provides `get_attn_backend_cls` and `get_device_communicator_cls`. A single method returns all V2 runner components as a group, so the Platform interface stays clean: ```python # vllm/platforms/interface.py @dataclass class V2RunnerComponents: input_batch_cls: type input_buffers_cls: type cudagraph_manager_cls: type sampler_cls: type pcp_manager_cls: type # future components can be added here class Platform: def get_v2_runner_components(self) -> V2RunnerComponents: """Return the default (GPU) component classes for V2 model runner. Backends override this to substitute their own implementations. """ from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.input_batch import InputBatch, InputBuffers from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.cudagraph_utils import ModelCudaGraphManager from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.sampler import Sampler from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.pcp_manager import PCPManager return V2RunnerComponents( input_batch_cls=InputBatch, input_buffers_cls=InputBuffers, cudagraph_manager_cls=ModelCudaGraphManager, sampler_cls=Sampler, pcp_manager_cls=PCPManager, ) ``` The runner fetches components from the Platform in `__init__`: ```python # vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py (proposed) components = current_platform.get_v2_runner_components() self.input_buffers = components.input_buffers_cls(...) self.cudagraph_manager = components.cudagraph_manager_cls(...) ``` A backend overrides a single method: ```python # backend platform class BackendPlatform(Platform): def get_v2_runner_components(self) -> V2RunnerComponents: base = super().get_v2_runner_components() return replace(base, request_state_cls=BackendRequestState, input_batch_cls=BackendInputBatch, input_buffers_cls=BackendInputBuffers, cudagraph_manager_cls=BackendGraphManager, speculator_factory=backend_init_speculator, ) ``` --- ### Layer 3: hooks (Not planned since this is much hack. Just point it here to get your feedback) Some differences are not about swapping a component, but about adding extra steps to a flow. The most common case is `prepare_inputs`: a backend may need to maintain `seq_lens_cpu` or update extra state before attention, but the rest of the logic (sorting requests, building index mappings, padding for cudagraph) is identical to GPU. A backend that needs these extra steps often copies the entire `prepare_inputs` (~200 lines) and adds its changes. When GPU fixes a bug, the backend does not get it automatically. The fix is to split large methods into steps with hooks: ```python # vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py (proposed) class GPUModelRunner(LoRAModelRunnerMixin): def prepare_inputs(self, scheduler_output, batch_desc): # Step 1: sort and compute basic numbers req_ids, num_reqs, num_tokens = self._sort_requests(scheduler_output, batch_desc) # Step 2: backend-specific setup before building the batch self._prepare_inputs_pre_hook(scheduler_output, req_ids, num_reqs) # Step 3: build the InputBatch (shared logic) input_batch = self._build_input_batch( scheduler_output, batch_desc, req_ids, num_reqs, num_tokens ) # Step 4: backend-specific post-processing input_batch = self._prepare_inputs_post_hook(input_batch, scheduler_output) # Step 5: PCP partitioning (shared) input_batch = pcp.maybe_partition_pcp_batch(self.pcp_manager, input_batch) return input_batch def _prepare_inputs_pre_hook(self, scheduler_output, req_ids, num_reqs): pass def _prepare_inputs_post_hook(self, input_batch, scheduler_output): pass ``` A backend overrides only the hooks: ```python # backend's v2 model runner (proposed) class BackendModelRunner(GPUModelRunner): def _prepare_inputs_pre_hook(self, scheduler_output, req_ids, num_reqs): ... def _prepare_inputs_post_hook(self, input_batch, scheduler_output): ... ``` Others, like `execute_model`, can add `_pre_forward_hook` / `_post_forward_hook` as well. **If a backend needs to copy more lines of a method, that method probably needs a hook.** Do not add hooks speculatively. Add them when a real backend demonstrates the need. ### Change summary The GPU path stays simple: - Factory methods return the default GPU classes. No config, no branching. - Hooks are empty no-ops. No runtime overhead. - No new dependencies, no frameworks, no containers. The only change to GPU code is replacing `RequestState(...)` with `components.request_state_cls(...)`. Mechanical, no control flow change. A backend goes from maintaining a large copy of the runner (often thousands of lines) to: - Overriding `get_v2_runner_components` on their Platform - Overriding 2-3 hooks - Registering kernels through the Triton Dispatcher (separate, not in runner ### Feedback Period. Two weeks. ### CC List. @WoosukKwon @simon-mo @youkaichao @DarkLight1337 @ProExpertProg @LucasWilkinson @njhill @ZJY0516 ### Any Other Things. - No backwards compatibility currently, since v2 is sill under develop. Once it's stable enough, We'd like to consider it then. - This RFC is about V2 only. V1 will eventually be deprecated and removed. ## Related RFCs - #11162 - Hardware pluggable - #45133 - Triton Kernel Dispatcher ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

The engine log shows the grammar rejecting token `200028` right after the JSON payload is complete: ``` (APIServer pid=9419) INFO: 127.0.0.1:37932 - "POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1" 200 OK (EngineCore pid=10458) ERROR 08-09 09:58:19 [scheduler.py:1841] Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [200028] for request chatcmpl-8da6fc665494abe1-b5b27872. Terminating request. (APIServer pid=9419) ERROR 08-09 09:58:19 [serving.py:175] Request chatcmpl-8da6fc665494abe1 failed with an internal error during generation (APIServer pid=9419) INFO: 127.0.0.1:37932 - "POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1" 500 Internal Server Error ``` ### Reproducer: Run the model (4xH100 in my case): ``` VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \ FLASH_ATTENTION_CUTE_DSL_CACHE_ENABLED=1 \ vllm serve \ --model thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small-NVFP4 \ --trust-remote-code \ --tokenizer-mode inkling \ --kernel-config.enable_flashinfer_autotune=False \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.75 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --tool-call-parser inkling \ --reasoning-parser inkling ``` Send a structured output request: ```bash curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{ "model": "thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small-NVFP4", "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Give me a person as JSON."}], "response_format": {"type":"json_schema","json_schema":{"name":"p","schema": {"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"age":{"type":"integer"}}, "required":["name","age"]}}} }' ``` I originally found this via [tool-eval-bench](https://github.com/SeraphimSerapis/tool-eval-bench), and can be reproduced with this command: ``` tool-eval-bench --scenarios TC-65 ```

signals.title: [RFC]: Pluggable KV Cache Data Types
signals.text: ### Motivation. The `--kv-cache-dtype` CLI parameter currently accepts only the values listed in the `CacheDType` literal: ```python CacheDType = Literal[ "auto", "float16", "bfloat16", "fp8", "fp8_e4m3", "fp8_e5m2", "fp8_inc", "fp8_ds_mla", "turboquant_k8v4", "turboquant_4bit_nc", "turboquant_k3v4_nc", "turboquant_3bit_nc", "int4_per_token_head", "int8_per_token_head", "fp8_per_token_head", "nvfp4", ] ``` These are hard-coded. Adding a new KV cache dtype requires modifying vLLM core in at least four places: 1. **`CacheDType` literal** — add the string 2. **`STR_DTYPE_TO_TORCH_DTYPE`** — map it to a `torch.dtype` 3. **`KVQuantMode`** — map it to specified quant mode 4. **`is_quantized_kv_cache()`** — teach it the new dtype's properties This makes it impossible for: - **Hardware backends** — to ship their own KV cache quantization format without editing vLLM (e.g., a new device-specific int8 variant) - **Third-party quantization libraries** — to integrate directly The quantization methods system (`--quantization`) already solved this exact problem with `register_quantization_config`. KV cache dtype should follow the same pattern. ### Proposed Change. > **Status:** Implemented in [PR #52670](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52670). > The design below is the finalized contract. The design follows the pattern established by `register_quantization_config` in `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/__init__.py`. ### 1. Define a KV Cache Dtype Plugin Interface ```python class KVCacheDTypeHandler(Protocol): """Contract for a registered `--kv-cache-dtype` value. A backend implements this interface to answer the questions vLLM currently answers with closed tables (STR_DTYPE_TO_TORCH_DTYPE / get_kv_quant_mode / is_quantized_kv_cache). A single handler may be device-aware (e.g., resolving different torch dtypes per Ascend generation). """ # Public name, e.g. "int8". Must match the registration key. name: str def torch_dtype(self, *args, **kwargs) -> torch.dtype: """Storage dtype for KV cache tensors. Called **once at registration time** and injected into the shared STR_DTYPE_TO_TORCH_DTYPE dict, so all existing direct dictionary access sites need no changes. May query the current platform.""" ... def is_quantized(self) -> bool: """True if the cache is quantized (non-native dtype). Replaces the ad-hoc string matching in is_quantized_kv_cache.""" ... def quant_mode(self) -> KVQuantMode: """Maps to the upstream KVQuantMode enum used by generic kernels, or returns KVQuantMode.NONE / a new BACKEND sentinel when the backend fully self-manages dispatch.""" ... ``` #### 1.2 `KVQuantMode.BACKEND` sentinel `quant_mode()` may return the new `KVQuantMode.BACKEND` when the backend fully self-manages kernel dispatch. Its semantics: - Reads as **quantized** (distinct from `KVQuantMode.NONE`, which means non-quantized). - Matches **no generic kernel mode**: `is_per_token_head is False`, `is_nvfp4 is False`, and it is not equal to `NONE`. - Signals to the attention selector / dispatch layer that the backend owns kernel selection — generic per-token-head / fp8 kernel paths must not be selected for it. ### 2. Registration API (inspired by `register_quantization_config`) ``` # 1. Upstream-known defaults (the closed Literal stays for docs / IDE / type-checking) # 2. Mutable mirror — custom entries are appended here KV_CACHE_DTYPES: list[str] = list(get_args(CacheDType)) # 3. Handler registry: name -> KVCacheDTypeHandler instance (eager) _KV_CACHE_DTYPE_HANDLERS: dict[str, KVCacheDTypeHandler] = {} def register_kv_cache_dtype(name: str): """Register a custom `--kv-cache-dtype` value (decorator, eager). @register_kv_cache_dtype("int8") class Int8Handler: def torch_dtype(self): ... def is_quantized(self): ... def quant_mode(self): ... During decoration the handler will: (a) append to the mutable KV_CACHE_DTYPES list (driving Pydantic + CLI validation); (b) resolve torch_dtype() once and **inject into STR_DTYPE_TO_TORCH_DTYPE**, so all existing `dict[name]` / `name in dict` sites need zero changes; (c) be stored for later quant_mode()/is_quantized() queries. """ def _decorate(cls): if name in KV_CACHE_DTYPES: # Override: warn but allow (replicates register_quantization_config) ... else: KV_CACHE_DTYPES.append(name) inst = cls() # Critical step: mutate shared dtype dict in-place — downstream zero changes STR_DTYPE_TO_TORCH_DTYPE[name] = inst.torch_dtype() _KV_CACHE_DTYPE_HANDLERS[name] = inst return cls return _decorate def get_kv_cache_dtype_handler(name: str) -> KVCacheDTypeHandler | None: """Return the handler for `name`; returns None for upstream dtypes that have no handler (the dtype table already covers these).""" return _KV_CACHE_DTYPE_HANDLERS.get(name) def is_known_kv_cache_dtype(name: str) -> bool: return name in KV_CACHE_DTYPES ``` The decorator **only touches platform-independent state** — `KV_CACHE_DTYPES`, `STR_DTYPE_TO_TORCH_DTYPE`, and the handler map. It deliberately does **not** read `current_platform`: an OOT backend registers from its `Platform.__init__`, where accessing `current_platform` would re-enter `__getattr__("current_platform")` while `_current_platform` is still `None` (assignment happens after instantiation returns), recursing. Keeping the decorator platform-agnostic mirrors `register_quantization_config`, whose decorator likewise stays off `current_platform`. Platform activation — and with it any OOT backend's `@register_kv_cache_dtype` decorators — is triggered separately by the `CacheConfig` validator (§4, §6), at a point where the platform is fully resolved. ### 3. Integrate Into Core Dispatch Points #### 3.1 quant-mode dispatch ```python def get_kv_quant_mode(kv_cache_dtype: str) -> KVQuantMode: handler = get_kv_cache_dtype_handler(kv_cache_dtype) if handler is not None: return handler.quant_mode() ... # existing branches ``` #### 3.2 `is_quantized_kv_cache` The duplicate `is_quantized_kv_cache` helpers (`vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py:77-83` **and** `vllm/utils/torch_utils.py:75-85` — currently two parallel implementations) should be merged into a single registry-aware implementation. `kv_cache_uses_per_token_head_scales()` follows the same handler-first / string-fallback pattern. Callers are repointed to `vllm.utils.torch_utils`. ### 4. Relax `CacheDType` Validation ``` # `vllm/config/cache.py:76` # Before cache_dtype: CacheDType = "auto" # After — accept arbitrary strings, validate against registry cache_dtype: CacheDType | str = "auto" ``` This replicates `quantization: QuantizationMethods | str | None` (`vllm/config/model.py:203`). Pydantic no longer rejects custom strings. The `CacheConfig.cache_dtype` validator: 1. touches `current_platform` to trigger platform activation, which lets out-of-tree backends register their dtypes (via `@register_kv_cache_dtype` in their `Platform.__init__`) into `KV_CACHE_DTYPES` / `STR_DTYPE_TO_TORCH_DTYPE` **before** membership is checked; 2. then `is_known_kv_cache_dtype(dtype)` rejects unknown names with `ValueError`. There is no per-platform whitelist. A backend that needs to reject a dtype on its device raises from its own `Platform.__init__` (or a higher-level config check), not from the `CacheConfig` validator. The single global registry is the sole gate. ### Feedback Period. _No response_ ### CC List. _No response_ ### Any Other Things. _No response_ ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Feature][DSpark]: Enable varlen for Kimi K3 (KDA)
signals.text: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch Adaptive verification has a firm requirement that the attention backend must not use the CPU-side query lengths as a source-of-truth, instead using the gpu tensors (so that we can run the confidence-based assignment on the GPU without synchronizing the CPU). Additionally, kernels must be able to support decode batches where requests have different query lengths per request. Currently, Kimi K3 kernels should (in theory) be compatible with this feature. We should wire it up, validate correctness, evaluate performance, and merge support. DEPENDS ON https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47808 ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug][ROCm/gfx942]: GLM-5.2-FP8 — first request after GPU idle emits garbage; piecewise CUDA graph cold replay corrupts the request's own prefill (workaround: cudagraph_mode=FULL_DECODE_ONLY)
signals.text: ## Environment - 8× AMD Instinct MI325X (gfx942), ROCm 7.14.0, amdgpu 6.19.14 - Images: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` 2026-08-12 (v0.26.1rc1.dev668+g3ee2df303) **and** 2026-08-13 (`8f515d1d`) — both reproduce - Model: `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8`, TP=8, `--kv-cache-dtype auto`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096`, MoE backend AITER blockscale-FP8 (`fmoe_bf16_a16_blockscaleFp8...`) - Reproduces identically at `--max-model-len` 131072 and 1048576 ## 🐛 Describe the bug After the engine sits idle for ≥ ~20–50 s, the **next** request returns garbage from its very first sampled token, e.g. `'!0.1.5,0.1 and1.1.1.0 21.1.'` (token-0/digit noise). Requests sent immediately afterwards are correct. Reproduction probability rises with idle time (~50–100 % at ≥ 50 s idle; back-to-back requests never fail, dozens of samples). Key observations: 1. **The corrupt request never self-heals**: with `max_tokens=300` the output is noise from token 1 through token 300, while a request issued ~0.5 s later is clean — i.e. the corrupt request's *own prefill* wrote garbage into its KV/indexer cache, and every decode step then consumes that poisoned context. 2. `temperature=0`; prompts are ~6–10 tokens (below the 16-token block size, so prefix caching is not involved). 3. No errors in the server log, container healthy, RAS/ECC counters unchanged. 4. Not JIT/autotune related: Triton JIT warnings (`_cp_gather_indexer_quant_cache_kernel`, `_fp8_mqa_logits_kernel`) appear only on the very first request after startup; later corrupt events have no JIT activity. 5. A 25 s-interval keepalive (unique prompts forcing real prefills, all HTTP 200) does **not** reliably prevent it. ## Bisection | config | result | |---|---| | defaults (FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graphs), 131k & 1M, nightly 08-12 & 08-13 | ❌ corrupt | | `--enforce-eager` | ✅ clean 8/8 (startup burst + 60 s idle ×3 + 25 s idle ×2) | | `--compilation-config='{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'` | ✅ clean 8/8 at 1M | → The corruption tracks **piecewise CUDA/HIP graph replay in the prefill path** after a cold window. With prefill graph-free (eager or `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`) the model is fully healthy: fact probes pass, tool calling OK, needle-in-haystack 3/3 at 2k/6k/12k/100k/900k tokens, and a 5-minute cold soak followed by a fresh request is correct. Other models on the same host/stack (Kimi-K3 with eager prefill + FULL decode graphs, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731) do not show this — consistent with the piecewise-prefill-graph attribution: decode-side graphs essentially never replay cold, because the preceding prefill has just warmed the GPU. This smells like a ROCm/HIP graph runtime issue (queue/doorbell state after idle → first graph replay misfires) rather than a model bug, but filing here since the practical impact is "GlmMoeDsa default config silently corrupts on gfx942" and the workaround is a vLLM flag. Related (same class — HIP graph replay silently wrong on AMD — but none match the idle-triggered gfx942 manifestation): - ROCm/hip#3887 — HIP graph replay reads stale device-pointer values (gfx1201/RDNA4, ~200+ nodes) - ROCm/aiter#3632 — W4A4 fused MoE kernel not HIP-graph-safe (gfx950) - pytorch/pytorch#155684 — HIP graph misuse yields silent wrong results where CUDA raises ## Workaround `--compilation-config='{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'` — no measurable decode-speed loss (decode keeps FULL graphs; only prefill runs graph-free). Single-stream decode on this host: 44.5 tok/s (prose) / 61.9 tok/s (code) at 1M `max_model_len`. ## Repro 1. Serve `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8` on 8×gfx942 with the default compilation config. 2. `sleep 60` 3. ```bash curl -s localhost:8000/v1/completions -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"glm","prompt":"The capital of France is","max_tokens":16,"temperature":0}' ``` → garbage (`!0.1...`). Repeat immediately → ` Paris.` (correct). Vary the prompt each round to rule out prefix-cache effects; alternate idle/burst to see the pattern.

signals.title: [RFC]: Extended online quantization roadmap
signals.text: ### Motivation. Continuation of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/32029. Online quantization API is now relatively stable at https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/online and documented at https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/features/quantization/online/. This RFC summarizes and motivates proposed features that would be helpful to make online quantization to be more flexible and more widely compatible with models, including pre-quantized ones. ### Proposed Change. ### 1. Support activation quant key override Implemented in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51808. This is necessary to dispatch on specific linear/moe backends that can be picked only through the `activation_quant_key` (see e.g. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c4e969294ecab9ffefb995b734303f13f62b723f/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/mxfp4.py#L441-L445) ### 2. Targeted online quantization configuration based on user patterns Implemented in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51285, RFC in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/50281. The goal is simply to extend the UI to support e.g. `--quantization-config.targets '{"re:.*o_proj.*":"mxfp8"}'`, e.g. to target a single layer similar to e.g. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/dc9f845ddc54c1df38fdbce5afe03f9fd15813bd/vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py#L935-L948 (that is currently hard-coded and may be causing accuracy issues if done silently https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48051), or e.g. `--quantization-config.targets '{"re:.*shared_expert.*":"fp8_per_block"}'` to enable fused shared expert. ### 3. Support online quantization with partially pre-quantized checkpoints Implemented in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51392. This is necessary to combine online quantization with already partially quantized checkpoints, which is notoriously the case recently. This is e.g. useful to test the accuracy/speed tradeoff of quantizing certain additional layers, or useful to e.g. release a single model compatible with fused shared expert / unfused shared expert. This has e.g. been requested in separate PRs: - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48983 - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49313 ### 4. Requantize already-quantized layers to different precision Not implemented yet, closest prototype is https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48427. This is similar to https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28291 & https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29328 on sglang side. This idea here would be to allow loading through a certain quantization method, dequantize and override the quantization method on request. This has e.g. been requested in: - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48427 - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51274 ### Feedback Period. One month ### CC List. @BowenBao @mgoin @kylesayrs @vkuzo @maeehart @tanpinsiang @fanxingran @access2rohit ### Any Other Things. _No response_ ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

sm_121, aarch64), 200 GbE RoCE fabric, serving `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8` with TP=2 × PP=3. **Fingerprint** (identical across every reproduction): - Every rank completes the first `mxfp8_gemm` autotune round (`Tuning mxfp8_gemm: 100%|… 16/16`). - Exactly one rank of a TP pair then prints `Tuning mxfp8_gemm: 0%| | 0/16` for the next round; its TP peer never enters that round. - Both ranks of the pair sit in `futex_do_wait` (one at ~50% CPU, the peer at ~20%), GPU 0%. - All other ranks park at the barrier; EngineCore emits `shm_broadcast … No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds` once per minute forever. Startup never completes; no error, no traceback. The ranks desynchronize between tuning rounds, after which the cross-rank per-tactic timing collective blocks forever — one participant is inside the round-N profiling loop, the other never joined it. **Reproduction matrix** — the deadlock is independent of everything except the vLLM version: | vLLM | FlashInfer | NCCL | JIT caches | Result | |---|---|---|---|---| | v0.27.1 (official image) | 0.6.16.post3 | pip-bundled | warm | deadlock | | v0.27.1 (official image) | 0.6.16.post3 | system 2.30.7 | warm | deadlock | | nightly `dev18+g3d204dfda` | 0.6.16.post3 | system 2.30.7 | cold | deadlock | | nightly `dev18+g3d204dfda` | **0.6.17** (forced) | system 2.30.7 | warm | deadlock | | source build `dev54+gb96bcd0b4` | 0.6.18 | system 2.30.7 | warm | deadlock | | pre-#50892 build `0.26.1rc1.dev247` (Aug 2) | 0.6.17 | same | warm | **tunes clean** | The Aug-2 build uses the previous flow (distributed ⇒ tune on every rank, no process group, no cache broadcast) and completes the identical tuning workload on the identical hardware every time. **Workarounds validated on this cluster:** - `VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_SKIP_OPS=mxfp8_gemm` — startup completes, but the un-tuned `FlashInferCutlassMxfp8LinearKernel` costs ~35% single-stream throughput (9.0 tok/s vs 14.4 tok/s tuned). - Patching `flashinfer_autotune` back to per-rank tuning (no `set_autotune_process_group`, no cache broadcast) — autotune completes on all 6 ranks and restores full performance (14.4–14.5 tok/s) on current main (`dev54+gb96bcd0b4`). Note: the synchronized flow already contains a mitigation for one hang trigger (`randomize_inputs=True` for EP ranks receiving no tokens) — this is a second, different trigger in the same design. I'll open a PR adding an opt-out env (`VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_DISTRIBUTED_SYNC=0`, default keeps current behavior) that restores the per-rank flow for affected fabrics. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug **Issue**: Running DSv3 with BF16 KV throws an error during JIT due to incompatible argument types. For context, this stems from two interlinked problems: 1. Issue 1: pure causal prefills are currently always run with a **FP8** PS ASM kernel, no matter the KV dtype. 1. Fix: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48712 2. However, this is due to a separate issue; the AITER_MLA currently incorrectly defaults to using an FP8 ASM prefill kernel during causal prefill, even with BF16 KV. This is fixed in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48712. **This means that during causal prefills, BF16 KV is truncated to FP8 and then run through an FP8 kernel. This is not correct.** ### Profiling proof of this issue Running the default MLA backend with BF16 KV: ``` docker run --rm --name repro-mla \ --init --network host --ipc host --privileged \ --cap-add SYS_PTRACE --security-opt seccomp=unconfined \ --ulimit memlock=-1 --ulimit stack=67108864 --shm-size 256G \ --group-add video --group-add render \ --device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri --device /dev/infiniband \ -v /sys:/sys \ -v "/root/.cache/huggingface/:/root/.cache/huggingface" \ -e HF_HOME=/root/.cache/huggingface -e HF_TOKEN=$HF_TOKEN \ -e HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 -e HF_HUB_ENABLE_HF_TRANSFER=0 \ -e VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \ vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-ac7509e2b1db40fec2f03dde1ed4e9dfdc2338c9 \ deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 --max-model-len 16K ``` **Causal prefills: FP8 asm kernel is running!** This is not what we would expect with BF16 KV with parent: In contrast, chunked prefills run both the causal and non-causal part with the (correct) BF16 AITER FA impl: So pure causal prefills have their BF16 KV are truncated to FP8 and ran in lower precision! ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

As a result, when a request omits the flag, the template produces a non-thinking prompt but the parser behaves as if thinking was enabled. This is directly observable in [`is_reasoning_end`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/925ea7e60f727bbb3fe3fcdb1c02b01a5bfb2749/vllm/parser/gemma4.py#L458-L477) for a prompt ending at a new model turn. Minimal reproduction: ```python from vllm.parser.gemma4 import Gemma4Parser class FakeTokenizer: bos_token_id = None eos_token_id = None pad_token_id = None def __init__(self): self._vocab = { "<|channel>": 100, "": 101, "<|tool_call>": 102, "": 103, "<|turn>": 104, "<|tool_response>": 105, } def get_vocab(self): return self._vocab def decode(self, token_ids): inverse = {value: key for key, value in self._vocab.items()} return "".join( inverse.get(token_id, f"") for token_id in token_ids ) tokenizer = FakeTokenizer() new_model_turn = [tokenizer.get_vocab()["<|turn>"]] for kwargs in ({}, {"enable_thinking": False}, {"enable_thinking": True}): parser = Gemma4Parser(tokenizer, chat_template_kwargs=kwargs) print( kwargs, "thinking_enabled=", parser._thinking_enabled, "reasoning_ended=", parser.is_reasoning_end(new_model_turn), ) ``` Actual output on the commit above: ```text {} thinking_enabled= True reasoning_ended= False {'enable_thinking': False} thinking_enabled= False reasoning_ended= True {'enable_thinking': True} thinking_enabled= True reasoning_ended= False ``` Expected output for the omitted case: ```text {} thinking_enabled= False reasoning_ended= True ``` The omitted case should resolve to the same policy as explicit `enable_thinking=False`; explicit `enable_thinking=True` should continue to enable reasoning. This would keep the parser aligned with the template, the documentation, and the [`reasoning_effort` request handling](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/925ea7e60f727bbb3fe3fcdb1c02b01a5bfb2749/vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/protocol.py#L582-L588). The closest issues I found are #39130 (structured output with explicit `enable_thinking=false`) and #48217 (channel-less output with explicit `enable_thinking=true`). Neither covers the omitted flag resolving to the opposite default from the Gemma 4 template. Downstream context: ai-dynamo/dynamo#12287 and ai-dynamo/dynamo#13061 gate Gemma 4 reasoning parsing on an explicit effective enable signal to avoid this mismatch. ## Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
