signals.title: [Bug]: Under async scheduling, stateful logits processors that read output_token_ids values see -1 placeholders — logitsprocs_need_output_token_ids only counts CLI custom processors
signals.text: ### Your current environment Observed on `releases/v0.27.1` (`6e448d0ea9`), reading the same code paths on current main. Runtime: vLLM 0.27.2.dev1 (source install), torch 2.13.0+cu130, 2x NVIDIA L20, TP=2, Python 3.12. The issue is scheduling logic, not environment-specific. ### 🐛 Describe the bug The v1 `LogitsProcessor` interface documents `output_tok_ids` as a live view of each request's generated tokens: > Key assumption: the `output_tok_ids` list (which is an element of each tuple in `added`) is a reference to the request's running output tokens list; via this reference, the logits processors always see the latest list of generated output tokens. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6e448d0ea9/vllm/v1/sample/logits_processor/interface.py#L45-L48 Under async scheduling (default-on since 0.27), that assumption only holds conditionally. The worker-side lists are extended with `-1` placeholders each step (real ids stay on the GPU in `prev_sampled_token_ids`): https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6e448d0ea9/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py#L3823-L3846 A repair mechanism exists precisely for this: `set_async_sampled_token_ids` / `update_async_output_token_ids` patch the `-1`s with real ids right before the logits processors run: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6e448d0ea9/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_input_batch.py#L1030-L1056 But the repair is gated by `needs_output_token_ids` (penalties / bad_words / thinking budget / `logitsprocs_need_output_token_ids`): https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6e448d0ea9/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_input_batch.py#L908-L922 and the logitsprocs contribution to that gate only counts **CLI-passed custom processors**: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6e448d0ea9/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py#L714-L726 ```python # We currently don't know whether a particular custom logits processor # uses output token ids so we set this conservatively. ... logitsprocs_need_output_token_ids=bool(custom_logitsprocs), ``` So there are three under-/over-approximations of the same unknown: 1. **Entry-point plugins** (`vllm.logits_processors` group) are not counted — being fixed by #38199. 2. **Builtin-registered processors are never counted.** The three in-tree builtins happen to only read the list's *length* (`MinTokensLogitsProcessor`), never its *values*, so nothing in-tree notices. Any stateful processor registered via `BUILTIN_LOGITS_PROCESSORS` that reads values silently computes on placeholder garbage: full per-step overhead is paid, results are wrong, and there is no warning or error. 3. Conversely, CLI custom processors that *don't* read values still force the repair path (the conservative `True`), paying an unnecessary sync in async mode. ### Reproduction / real-world impact We integrated Google DeepMind's SynthID-Text watermarking (via the HF `transformers` processor) as a builtin stateful logits processor on top of `releases/v0.27.1` — the first "reads values" consumer of this contract we know of: - with `--no-async-scheduling`: 8/8 watermarked outputs detected, mean-g z-score avg **7.86** (range 5.51–11.47), 0 false positives on controls; - with default async scheduling and identical code: **0/8 detected** (z avg 0.39 ≈ control 0.33), while still paying ~11% per-request latency for the watermark compute — the context window degrades to `[-1, -1, -1, -1]`. Branch with the processor and a fail-safe guard (refuses to watermark and warns when async scheduling is detected): https://github.com/danbo610/vllm/tree/feature/synthid-watermark (see commit `f18c17a3bb` for the guard). Minimal repro sketch: register any processor that prints `output_tok_ids` from `apply()` in `BUILTIN_LOGITS_PROCESSORS`, run with defaults (no penalties, no CLI `--logits-processors`), and observe `[-1, -1, ...]`; pass `--no-async-scheduling` (or any CLI custom processor, which flips the flag) and observe real ids. ### Suggested fix A declarative capability on the interface would solve all three cases at once, mirroring `is_argmax_invariant()`: ```python class LogitsProcessor(ABC): @classmethod def needs_output_token_ids(cls) -> bool: return True # conservative default for out-of-tree processors ``` - the three in-tree builtins override it to `False` (no behavior change, removes today's over-approximation for value-agnostic CLI procs); - `build_logitsprocs` ORs the declarations across builtin + entry-point + CLI processors and feeds `logitsprocs_need_output_token_ids`; - the `interface.py` "Key assumption" docstring gains a note that the live view is only guaranteed when this capability is declared (or async scheduling is off). Short of that, amending the docstring plus a startup warning when async scheduling is enabled with non-in-tree processors would at least make the failure mode discoverable — today it is completely silent. Happy to help validate a fix against the watermarking use case; we can also upstream the SynthID processor itself as a separate PR if there is interest.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Summary

Serving Kimi-K3 with TP16 across two 8× B200 nodes (EFA, no NVSwitch/MNNVL),any form of CUDA graph capture produces wrong output or crashes. enforce_eager is correct 100% of the time. Unlike #50147, this reproduces at batch=1 on the first request, with prefix caching disabled and no concurrency. I also tried TP=8 and PP=2, the issue persists

Critically, the FlashInfer fused all-reduce path is disabled on this topology, so the latent-MoE stale-residual fix in #50386 cannot apply here (details below).

Configuration

vllm serve flags:

  • -tensor-parallel-size 16 --trust-remote-code --load-format fastsafetensors
    --moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA
    --disable-custom-all-reduce --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune
    --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90

env: VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=0 VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM=0
VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM=0 NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=0 NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0
VLLM_ENABLE_K3_LATENT_MOE_TAIL_FUSION=0

Prefix caching is OFF. All tests below are single-stream, temperature=0, max_tokens=64, identical prompt.

Failure matrix

cudagraph config | result -- | -- enforce_eager: true | Correct output, every time, across many deploys (TP16 and TP8+PP2) default (FULL_AND_PIECEWISE) | Fluent but semantically random multilingual text; host SIGSEGV in cuGraphLaunch / at::cuda::CUDAGraph::replay() on the 3rd request cudagraph_mode: PIECEWISE | No crash. Deterministic collapse to a single repeated token (@ @ @ ...) from the first request VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 | AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered, surfaced at torch.cuda.set_rng_state during Dynamo tracing

Performance impact

Eager decode is ~2.6 tok/s at batch=1 (64 tokens in ~25 s), closely matching the ~2.7 tok/s eager figure in #50147 against ~85 tok/s with graphs. DSpark speculative decoding recovers this to ~10 tok/s, still far below the graph-enabled figure. Eager is therefore not a viable workaround for latency-sensitive serving, which makes graph capture on this topology effectively blocking.

Questions

  1. Is CUDA graph capture expected to be supported for Kimi-K3 on multi-node TP without NVSwitch, where the FlashInfer fused all-reduce path is inactive and collectives fall back to NCCL over EFA? But I tried TP=8 and PP=2 the issue still persist.
  2. Are there other buffers allocated outside capture in the K3 MoE/KDA paths, analogous to the one fixed in #50386, that would be reached on the non-FlashInfer path?

Reproduction

Serve:

vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \ --tensor-parallel-size 16 --nnodes 2 --node-rank $RANK \ --trust-remote-code --load-format fastsafetensors \ --moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA \ --disable-custom-all-reduce --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \ --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 # env: # VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=0 VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM=0 # VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM=0 NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=0 NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0 # VLLM_ENABLE_K3_LATENT_MOE_TAIL_FUSION=0 # Add --enforce-eager for the known-good control run.

Single request, greedy, no concurrency:

from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI(base_url="<http://localhost:8000/v1>", api_key="dummy", timeout=600.0) resp = client.chat.completions.create( model="moonshotai/Kimi-K3", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "can you write me a story about a cat"}], max_tokens=64, temperature=0, extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"thinking": False}}, ) print(resp.choices[0].message.content)

With --enforce-eager this returns a coherent story on every run. Without it, the first response is already corrupted. Send the same request 3+ times to reach the segfault under the default cudagraph mode.

signals.title: [Bug]: ModelOpt NVFP4 on SM120 dies or wedges under sustained load with CUDA graphs (not the NVFP4 GEMM backend)
signals.text: ### Your current environment <details> <summary>Environment</summary> - GPU: 2x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition (sm120, 96 GB), driver 595.71.05, ECC clean - Container: `vllm/vllm-openai` v0.26.0 (`sha256:ffb2d59b1c059a5bd8d781320c9f5189de8293693b7d95da54befddaa54abf52`) and v0.27.1 (`sha256:0a51ea5b4ae2dc5d81890e5173f54203d2a3ae0cfffe51b8fd2afd4391bfd967`), podman, `--ipc host` - CUDA 13.0.2, torch 2.11.0+cu130, flashinfer 0.6.14 - Model: Qwen3.8-27B quantized by ModelOpt 0.47.0.dev0 to `MIXED_PRECISION`. 193 layers NVFP4 (all 64 `mlp.{gate,up,down}_proj` plus `lm_head`), 208 layers FP8 (`linear_attn.*`, `self_attn.*`), `kv_cache_quant_algo: FP8`. Architecture `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` (hybrid GDN linear attention with full attention every 4th layer), hidden 5120, ffn 17408, vocab 248320, 64 layers. - vLLM resolves this to `quantization=modelopt_mixed` and selects `FlashInferCutlassNvFp4LinearKernel` for the NVFP4 GEMMs, `FlashInferFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` for FP8, and the `FLASHINFER` attention backend. </details> ### 🐛 Describe the bug Serving a ModelOpt-NVFP4 checkpoint on SM120 dies under sustained batch load, reliably, on two vLLM releases. The same base model quantized to FP8 and served from the same image with the same attention backend is stable. The failure is specific to the NVFP4 build. I have not isolated the mechanism, and two backends I suspected are now ruled out by measurement (see the update comment below). **One thing that is measured but is not the cause.** `flashinfer.mm_fp4` hands the CUTLASS FP4 GEMM a fixed 32 MiB shared workspace, and on SM120 the kernel asks for 34 MiB at every M from 1 to 256 for this model's fused gate/up projection (5120 → 34816). Every decode-sized call therefore takes a fallback branch in `csrc/fp4_gemm_cutlass_sm120.cu` that allocates a private workspace and releases it right after an asynchronous launch, including inside CUDA graph capture. That is filed as https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4549 with a fix in https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4550. Raising the shared workspace so the fallback never fires does **not** stop the crash: the patched build failed after 15.0 minutes against 16.5 for the unpatched one. Recording it here so nobody else spends the window I spent on it. **Symptoms, for searchability.** Two failure modes, both with CUDA graphs enabled: | vLLM | spec decode | time to failure | error | |---|---|---|---| | v0.26.0 | none | 16 min 35 s | illegal memory access | | v0.27.1 | none | 21 min 32 s | illegal memory access | | v0.26.0 | MTP, 3 tokens | not recorded | misaligned address | | v0.26.0 | none | 8 s, on a boot right after a prior fault | illegal memory access in `BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCache` | The exception always surfaces at an asynchronous synchronization point, so the reported frame is never the offending kernel: ``` File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 314, in get_output self.async_copy_ready_event.synchronize() torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered ``` The second mode is a wedge. The engine stops making progress without raising anything, `/v1/models` still returns 200 in about a millisecond, `/v1/chat/completions` never returns, and the GPU sits at 100% utilization. `py-spy` shows the engine thread blocked in a kernel launch that never returns, and the driver reports `Xid 8 ... GPU is probably locked` only much later. `dmesg` records MMU faults at wild addresses, `faulted @ 0x4_00000000` and `0xf_00001000`, both `FAULT_PDE`. **Differential.** The same base model quantized to FP8, same box, same image, same FlashInfer attention backend, CUDA graphs on, prefix caching on, `--max-model-len 262144`, logged 10,282 completions across 35 hours with no illegal-address or misaligned-address error. The NVFP4 build dies after roughly 570 completions. Both GPUs produce the NVFP4 fault and ECC is clean on both. `--enforce-eager` reduces the rate roughly tenfold without eliminating it. We also swept the NVFP4 GEMM for memory-safety problems and found none: every layer shape in the model, every M from 1 to 8192, all 32 SM120 CUTLASS FP4 tactics, under `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck` with `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1`, with both a zeroed and a randomly poisoned workspace. Those runs cannot catch this defect, because disabling the caching allocator turns every free into a synchronizing `cudaFree`. ### Workarounds available today from vLLM Either of these avoids the fallback path without a FlashInfer patch: 1. `VLLM_DISABLED_KERNELS=FlashInferCutlassNvFp4LinearKernel`, which falls through to vLLM's native `CutlassNvFp4LinearKernel`. On our workload that reached 0.65 completions per second against 0.67 for the FlashInfer kernel, and 50 deterministic classification prompts returned byte-identical answers, so the swap does not change results. Soak results below. 2. `--enforce-eager`, which reduces the failure rate roughly tenfold without removing it, and costs more than the kernel swap. Swapping to `CutlassNvFp4LinearKernel` does not fix the failure, so quarantining the FlashInfer kernel on SM12x would not be a fix either. Both workarounds above are partial.

signals.title: [Bug]: MiniMax-M3 (MXFP8) streaming: generation stops (empty delta, finish_reason=stop) right after reasoning closes, whenever a tool call should follow — non-streaming with identical payload succeeds
signals.text: ### Your current environment `collect_env.py` could not be run on this host — no outbound internet access (air-gapped deployment). Manually collected equivalent below. **Versions** - vLLM: `0.27.0` (build `vllm-0.27.0-tp4-41db7380`) - PyTorch: `2.13.0+cu129` - Transformers: `5.15.0` - GPU: 4x NVIDIA H200 (143771 MiB), driver `595.58.03` **Model** - `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3` - Quantization: `mxfp8` (NVIDIA ModelOpt MXFP8 checkpoint, `weight_block_size=[1,32]`, MoE via `MarlinMxfp8LinearKernel`/`MARLIN` backend) — vLLM's own startup log flags this format as *"experimental and could change in future"* **Launch command** ```bash vllm serve /model --served-model-name MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 --block-size 128 --max-model-len 65536 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.93 --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 \ --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 ``` ### 🐛 Describe the bug With `stream: true` and `tools` provided, for requests where the model's reasoning is longer / more hedging before deciding to call a tool, the SSE stream **stops immediately after the reasoning block closes**: the next chunk has an empty `delta` and `finish_reason: "stop"`. Nothing is generated after that — no content, no `tool_calls`. This is not a parsing failure; generation itself halts. The byte-identical payload sent with `"stream": false` succeeds reliably (tested 6/6). > **Note:** only reproduced so far on an MXFP8-quantized checkpoint (NVIDIA ModelOpt format). Untested whether an unquantized bf16 checkpoint is also affected. **Minimal repro** Flat 2-field tool schema — confirmed tool schema complexity/count is not the trigger (fails the same way with 1 tool or 5 tools): ```python import requests payload = { "model": "MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3", "stream": True, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "сделай docx с названием test и текстом привет"}], "tools": [{ "type": "function", "function": { "name": "generate_docx_report", "description": "Generate a Word document from content.", "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": { "filename": {"type": "string"}, "content": {"type": "string"}, }, "required": ["filename", "content"], }, }, }], "tool_choice": "auto", } r = requests.post("http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions", json=payload, stream=True) for line in r.iter_lines(): if line: print(line.decode()) ``` **Expected** Reasoning closes, then either visible content or a populated `tool_calls` delta follows — same as the non-streaming response to the identical payload (`"stream": False` above). **Observed** After the last reasoning chunk, the stream emits one more chunk with an empty delta and `finish_reason: "stop"`, then ends. Nothing else is generated. **Ruled out** - Tool schema size — reproduces with both a minimal flat 2-field schema and a real ~2KB docstring-heavy schema - Tool count — 1 tool vs 5 tools, same result - Payload size in general — byte-identical payloads, only `stream` differs **Correlation observed (not confirmed causal)** Requests where the model's own reasoning is short/decisive stream through fine. Requests where reasoning is longer with self-correction (*"But I should check... Actually... Let me reconsider..."*) reliably hit the halt. **Current workaround** Routing tool-decision through a separate non-streaming call instead of native streaming tool-calling (application-level, not a real fix — costs 2x LLM calls per turn). ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary LMCache prefill/decode disaggregation returns incorrect generation results after an apparently successful remote KV-cache transfer. The prefill and decode servers both: - Start successfully. - Return HTTP 200. - Remain healthy after the requests. - Report that LMCache P/D mode is enabled. - Report that the NIXL/UCX transfer channel is active. - Report complete prompt KV-cache hits on the decode receiver. Despite this, the P/D generation diverges from an equivalent monolithic vLLM server starting at generated token 0. The incorrect output frequently begins by reproducing tokens from inside the repeated prompt body: ```text alpha beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta ... ``` The monolithic server instead begins answering the instruction at the end of the prompt: ```text The problem is to summarize the operational sequence ... ``` This is a silent correctness failure. It is not a startup failure, HTTP failure, missing-transfer failure, or unhealthy-engine failure. The issue was reproduced locally: - 6/6 comparisons failed across two independent vLLM 0.26.0 runs. - 3/3 comparisons failed in a separate vLLM 0.27.1 run. - Total: 9/9 LMCache P/D versus monolithic comparisons failed. - Native NIXL and Mooncake passed the identical monolithic-equivalence oracle. ## Environment Primary reproduction environment: ```text OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (x86_64) CPU: AMD EPYC 9554 64-Core Processor GPU: NVIDIA L40S Prefill: 1 × L40S Decode: 1 × independent L40S NVIDIA driver: 595.71.05 Python: 3.12.13 vLLM: 0.26.0 LMCache: 0.5.3-g140819c9 NIXL: 1.3.2 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 Transformers: 5.14.1 Model: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B Model dtype: bfloat16 KV-cache dtype: bfloat16 Tensor parallel size: 1 Execution mode: eager Transfer channel: NIXL NIXL backend: UCX ``` The same failure was independently reproduced with: ```text Python: 3.12.13 vLLM: 0.27.1 LMCache: 0.5.3-g140819c9 NIXL: 1.3.2 PyTorch: 2.13.0 Transformers: 5.15.0 Model: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B GPU: NVIDIA L40S Model dtype: bfloat16 KV-cache dtype: bfloat16 Tensor parallel size: 1 Execution mode: eager ``` ## LMCache prefill configuration Save as `lmcache_prefill.yaml`: ```yaml local_cpu: false max_local_cpu_size: 0 remote_serde: null enable_pd: true transfer_channel: "nixl" pd_role: "sender" pd_buffer_size: 1073741824 pd_buffer_device: "cuda" nixl_backends: [UCX] pd_proxy_host: "127.0.0.1" pd_proxy_port: 37413 pd_skip_proxy_notification: true ``` ## LMCache decode configuration Save as `lmcache_decode.yaml`: ```yaml local_cpu: false max_local_cpu_size: 0 remote_serde: null enable_pd: true transfer_channel: "nixl" pd_role: "receiver" pd_buffer_size: 1073741824 pd_buffer_device: "cuda" nixl_backends: [UCX] pd_peer_host: "127.0.0.1" pd_peer_init_port: [37413] pd_peer_alloc_port: [42727] ``` The exact port numbers can be replaced with any two unused local ports. The values above are taken from one representative reproduction. ## Common environment variables Run the following before starting the servers: ```bash export LMCACHE_USE_EXPERIMENTAL=True export PYTHONHASHSEED=123 export UCX_TLS=cuda_ipc,cuda_copy,tcp export VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=1 export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn export VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 ``` ## Start the prefill server ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ LMCACHE_CONFIG_FILE="$PWD/lmcache_prefill.yaml" \ python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --served-model-name veritas-model \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 8100 \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --max-model-len 2048 \ --max-num-seqs 8 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.65 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --disable-log-stats \ --enforce-eager \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"LMCacheConnectorV1","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"discard_partial_chunks":false,"lmcache_rpc_port":"veritas-prefill"}}' ``` Wait until `GET /v1/models` returns HTTP 200. ## Start the decode server ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 \ LMCACHE_CONFIG_FILE="$PWD/lmcache_decode.yaml" \ python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --served-model-name veritas-model \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 8200 \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --max-model-len 2048 \ --max-num-seqs 8 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.65 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --disable-log-stats \ --enforce-eager \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"LMCacheConnectorV1","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"discard_partial_chunks":false,"lmcache_rpc_port":"veritas-decode"}}' ``` Wait until `GET /v1/models` returns HTTP 200. ## Input Three independent prompts are generated. Each prompt contains a unique random request marker to prevent accidental reuse between repetitions. ```python import uuid repeat = 0 marker = f"VERITAS_PD_{repeat}_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}" prompt = ( f"Request marker {marker}. " + "alpha beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta " * 96 + " Summarize the operational sequence in exactly three short bullets." ) request_id = f"veritas-pd-{repeat}-{uuid.uuid4().hex}" ``` Depending on how the random marker is tokenized, the complete prompt contains approximately 895–898 tokens. The same exact `prompt` and `request_id` are used for the corresponding prefill and decode requests. ## Prefill request ```python import requests prefill_payload = { "model": "veritas-model", "prompt": prompt, "temperature": 0.0, "stream": False, "max_tokens": 1, "kv_transfer_params": { "disagg_spec": { "req_id": request_id, "receiver_host": "127.0.0.1", "receiver_init_port": [37413], "receiver_alloc_port": [42727], } }, } prefill_response = requests.post( "http://127.0.0.1:8100/v1/completions", json=prefill_payload, headers={"X-Request-Id": request_id}, timeout=180, ) print("prefill status:", prefill_response.status_code) print("prefill body:", prefill_response.text) ``` Observed result: ```text prefill status: 200 ``` ## Decode request After the prefill request finishes, send the same prompt and request ID to the decode receiver: ```python decode_payload = { "model": "veritas-model", "prompt": prompt, "temperature": 0.0, "seed": 0, "max_tokens": 64, "logprobs": 5, "stream": False, } decode_response = requests.post( "http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/completions", json=decode_payload, headers={"X-Request-Id": request_id}, timeout=180, ) print("decode status:", decode_response.status_code) print("decode body:", decode_response.text) ``` Observed result: ```text decode status: 200 ``` Repeat this process three times with three independently generated markers and request IDs. ## Monolithic control After recording the P/D outputs, stop both the prefill and decode servers. Start a monolithic server without LMCache or any other KV connector: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --served-model-name veritas-model \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 8300 \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --max-model-len 2048 \ --max-num-seqs 8 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.65 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --disable-log-stats \ --enforce-eager ``` Replay each previously recorded prompt byte-for-byte: ```python monolithic_payload = { "model": "veritas-model", "prompt": prompt, "temperature": 0.0, "seed": 0, "max_tokens": 64, "logprobs": 5, "stream": False, } monolithic_response = requests.post( "http://127.0.0.1:8300/v1/completions", json=monolithic_payload, headers={"X-Request-Id": f"mono-{request_id}"}, timeout=180, ) print("monolithic status:", monolithic_response.status_code) print("monolithic body:", monolithic_response.text) ``` Observed result: ```text monolithic status: 200 ``` ## Comparison oracle For every prompt, compare the P/D result with the monolithic result using: 1. Generated token strings. 2. Generated text. 3. Selected-token log probabilities. 4. Top-5 token overlap at each generated position. The equivalence requirements are: ```text Generated tokens must be identical. Generated text must be identical. Maximum selected-token logprob absolute difference must be <= 0.25. Minimum top-5 overlap across generated positions must be >= 0.80. ``` The following inputs are identical between the P/D decode and monolithic control: ```text Prompt bytes Model Model dtype Execution mode Temperature Seed Maximum generated tokens Requested logprob count Prefix-caching setting ``` ## LMCache transfer evidence In a representative vLLM 0.26.0 run, the LMCache decode receiver logged: ```text Reqid: cmpl-veritas-pd-0-... Total tokens 895 Inference Engine computed tokens: 0 LMCache hit tokens: 895 need to load: 894 ``` ```text Reqid: cmpl-veritas-pd-1-... Total tokens 897 Inference Engine computed tokens: 0 LMCache hit tokens: 897 need to load: 896 ``` ```text Reqid: cmpl-veritas-pd-2-... Total tokens 897 Inference Engine computed tokens: 0 LMCache hit tokens: 897 need to load: 896 ``` In the vLLM 0.27.1 confirmation run, the receiver similarly logged: ```text Reqid: cmpl-veritas-pd-0-... Total tokens 897 Inference Engine computed tokens: 0 LMCache hit tokens: 897 need to load: 896 ``` ```text Reqid: cmpl-veritas-pd-1-... Total tokens 897 Inference Engine computed tokens: 0 LMCache hit tokens: 897 need to load: 896 ``` ```text Reqid: cmpl-veritas-pd-2-... Total tokens 895 Inference Engine computed tokens: 0 LMCache hit tokens: 895 need to load: 894 ``` The connector evidence collected from the server logs was: ```json { "lmcache_initialized": true, "pd_enabled": true, "nixl_channel": true, "cache_retrieval": true, "healthy_engine": true } ``` ## Representative output mismatch For one vLLM 0.26.0 repetition, the LMCache P/D output began with: ```text alpha beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta alpha beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta alpha beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta ``` Its first generated tokens were: ```json [ " alpha", " beta", " gamma", " delta", " epsilon", " z", "eta", " eta", " theta", " alpha", " beta", " gamma" ] ``` For the identical prompt, the monolithic output began with: ```text The problem is to summarize the operational sequence in exactly three short bullets. ``` Its first generated tokens were: ```json [ " ", "The", " problem", " is", " to", " summarize", " the", " operational", " sequence", " in", " exactly", " three" ] ``` The P/D and monolithic generations therefore diverged at generated token 0. A second prompt produced the following P/D output: ```text alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. alpha. ``` The monolithic server instead produced: ```text The first step is to identify the key elements of the system. The second step is to determine the appropriate tools and methods to achieve the goal. The third step is to implement the solution. ``` ## vLLM 0.26.0 results ### Independent run 1 ```text Prompt 0: tokens_equal: false text_equal: false maximum selected-token logprob difference: 3.4423 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.0 Prompt 1: tokens_equal: false text_equal: false maximum selected-token logprob difference: 3.6104 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.0 Prompt 2: tokens_equal: false text_equal: false maximum selected-token logprob difference: 3.3309 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.0 ``` ### Independent run 2 ```text Prompt 0: tokens_equal: false text_equal: false maximum selected-token logprob difference: 3.3705 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.0 Prompt 1: tokens_equal: false text_equal: false maximum selected-token logprob difference: 3.4516 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.0 Prompt 2: tokens_equal: false text_equal: false maximum selected-token logprob difference: 3.3782 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.0 ``` Result: ```text 6/6 LMCache P/D comparisons failed. All six comparisons diverged at generated token 0. ``` ## vLLM 0.27.1 results ```text Prompt 0: tokens_equal: false text_equal: false maximum selected-token logprob difference: 3.6067 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.0 Prompt 1: tokens_equal: false text_equal: false maximum selected-token logprob difference: 3.6052 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.0 Prompt 2: tokens_equal: false text_equal: false maximum selected-token logprob difference: 2.5831 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.0 ``` Result: ```text 3/3 LMCache P/D comparisons failed. All three comparisons diverged at generated token 0. ``` ## Native NIXL control The identical three prompts and monolithic-equivalence oracle were run using the native vLLM NIXL connector. ```text Prompt 0: tokens_equal: true text_equal: true maximum selected-token logprob difference: 0.0479 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.8 Prompt 1: tokens_equal: true text_equal: true maximum selected-token logprob difference: 0.0893 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.8 Prompt 2: tokens_equal: true text_equal: true maximum selected-token logprob difference: 0.0621 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.8 ``` Native NIXL verdict: ```text pass ``` ## Mooncake control The identical three prompts and monolithic-equivalence oracle were also run using the Mooncake connector. ```text Prompt 0: tokens_equal: true text_equal: true maximum selected-token logprob difference: 0.0942 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.8 Prompt 1: tokens_equal: true text_equal: true maximum selected-token logprob difference: 0.1162 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.8 Prompt 2: tokens_equal: true text_equal: true maximum selected-token logprob difference: 0.0640 minimum top-5 overlap: 0.8 ``` Mooncake verdict: ```text pass ``` These controls use the same: ```text Model Prompt generation Prompt lengths GPU type BF16 dtype Temperature Seed Maximum generated token count Logprob count Monolithic-equivalence oracle ``` ## Reproducibility summary | Runtime | Connector | Comparisons | Result | |---|---|---:|---| | vLLM 0.26.0 / LMCache 0.5.3-g140819c9, run 1 | LMCache | 3 | 3 mismatches | | vLLM 0.26.0 / LMCache 0.5.3-g140819c9, run 2 | LMCache | 3 | 3 mismatches | | vLLM 0.27.1 / LMCache 0.5.3-g140819c9 | LMCache | 3 | 3 mismatches | | vLLM 0.26.0 | Native NIXL | 3 | 3 equivalent | | vLLM 0.26.0 | Mooncake | 3 | 3 equivalent | Overall LMCache result: ```text 9/9 P/D versus monolithic comparisons mismatched. ``` ## Expected behavior When the LMCache receiver reports that the complete prompt KV cache was retrieved, decoding should be semantically equivalent to running the same prompt on a monolithic server with the same model and sampling configuration. In particular: - The first generated token should match. - The complete generated token sequence should match. - The generated text should match. - Token log probabilities should remain within normal BF16 numerical tolerance. - Top-k distributions should retain substantial overlap. ## Actual behavior The LMCache receiver reports a complete KV-cache hit and returns HTTP 200, but: - The first generated token differs from the monolithic result. - The complete 64-token output differs. - Generated text differs. - Minimum top-5 overlap reaches 0.0. - Maximum selected-token logprob differences reach approximately 2.58–3.61. - Output frequently begins with tokens taken from inside the repeated prompt body. - Both servers remain healthy. - No explicit runtime error is returned to the client. ## Classification This appears to be a remote KV restoration correctness failure rather than a transfer availability failure. The evidence shows that: - LMCache initializes successfully. - P/D mode is enabled. - The NIXL/UCX transfer path is active. - The receiver reports complete cache hits. - The inference engine reports zero computed prompt tokens. - Prefill and decode requests both return HTTP 200. - Both engines remain healthy. - The restored KV state does not preserve the expected next-token semantics. ## Reproduce * The full reproduction script can be seen here [repro_lmcache_pd.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31142926/repro_lmcache_pd.py). * Run it with 2 separate GPUs. `.../miniconda3/envs/vllm_0260/bin/python repro_lmcache_pd.py --prefill-gpu 0 --decode-gpu 1 --out-dir artifacts` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Description Using `ngram_gpu` speculative decoding together with the `xgrammar` structured-output backend causes valid concurrent structured-output requests to fail with HTTP 500. A single request using the same model, prompt, JSON schema, and server configuration succeeds. However, when 24 requests are sent with concurrency 8, most requests fail. On vLLM 0.27.1: ```text Single structured request: HTTP 200 Concurrent requests: 3 HTTP 200, 21 HTTP 500 Server health afterward: HTTP 200 ``` The server logs report: ```text Failed to advance FSM ... Please file an issue. Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [...] Terminating request. Request ... failed with an internal error during generation ``` The identical workload without speculative decoding succeeds 24/24. This was also reproduced with vLLM 0.26.0. ## Environment ```text OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (x86_64) CPU: AMD EPYC 9554 64-Core Processor GPU: NVIDIA L40S NVIDIA driver: 595.71.05 Python: 3.12.13 vLLM: 0.27.1 PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130 Transformers: 5.15.0 xgrammar: 0.2.3 Model: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B Model dtype: bfloat16 Tensor parallel size: 1 Maximum model length: 768 Maximum sequences: 16 Maximum batched tokens: 768 ``` Only one L40S GPU is required. ## Reproduction script The complete standalone reproduction script is attached as: [repro_ngram_gpu_xgrammar.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31143661/repro_ngram_gpu_xgrammar.py) The script does not depend on an external test framework. It automatically: 1. Starts vLLM with `ngram_gpu` and `xgrammar`. 2. Sends one structured request. 3. Sends 24 structured requests at concurrency 8. 4. Records the HTTP responses and relevant server errors. 5. Confirms that the server remains healthy. 6. Stops the server. 7. Starts an otherwise identical server without speculative decoding. 8. Repeats the same single and concurrent requests. 9. Writes all results to `result.json`. Run it with: ```bash python repro_ngram_gpu_xgrammar.py \ --gpu 0 \ --out-dir ngram_gpu_xgrammar_repro ``` A `bug_reproduced` result intentionally exits with status 1. ## Failing server configuration The failing phase starts the server with: ```bash python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --served-model-name veritas-model \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 8000 \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --max-model-len 768 \ --max-num-seqs 16 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 768 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.70 \ --disable-log-stats \ --structured-outputs-config '{"backend":"xgrammar"}' \ --speculative-config '{"method":"ngram_gpu","num_speculative_tokens":4,"prompt_lookup_min":1,"prompt_lookup_max":4}' ``` ## JSON schema Every request uses the following schema: ```json { "type": "object", "properties": { "status": { "type": "string", "enum": ["ok"] }, "items": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "integer" }, "minItems": 3, "maxItems": 3 }, "request_id": { "type": "integer" } }, "required": [ "status", "items", "request_id" ], "additionalProperties": false } ``` ## Request input For request index `N`, the prompt is constructed as: ```python prefix = ( "Shared prefix for structured-output speculative decoding stress. " "Follow the schema exactly and do not add prose. " ) * 6 prompt = ( f"{prefix}\nRequest id {N}. Return a JSON object with " '"status":"ok", "items":[1,2,3], and "request_id":' f"{N}." ) ``` The complete OpenAI-compatible request is: ```json { "model": "veritas-model", "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": "Shared prefix for structured-output speculative decoding stress. Follow the schema exactly and do not add prose. [repeated six times]\nRequest id 0. Return a JSON object with \"status\":\"ok\", \"items\":[1,2,3], and \"request_id\":0." } ], "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 80, "stream": false, "structured_outputs": { "json": { "type": "object", "properties": { "status": { "type": "string", "enum": ["ok"] }, "items": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "integer" }, "minItems": 3, "maxItems": 3 }, "request_id": { "type": "integer" } }, "required": [ "status", "items", "request_id" ], "additionalProperties": false } } } ``` ## Single-request result Before applying concurrent load, the script sends one request. Observed response: ```text HTTP 200 ``` The returned content is valid and satisfies the schema: ```json { "status": "ok", "items": [1, 2, 3], "request_id": 0 } ``` This confirms that: - The model is loaded correctly. - The request format is valid. - The schema is accepted. - xgrammar can compile and enforce the schema. - `ngram_gpu` can complete at least one structured request. ## Concurrent-load result The script sends: ```text Request count: 24 Concurrency: 8 ``` Observed result with vLLM 0.27.1: ```text Successful valid JSON responses: 3 HTTP 500 responses: 21 Invalid HTTP 200 responses: 0 Transport errors: 0 Timeouts: 0 ``` The failed requests return: ```json { "error": { "code": 500, "message": "Internal server error", "param": null, "type": "InternalServerError" } } ``` ## Server log errors Representative server log output: ```text ERROR [backend_xgrammar.py:162] Failed to advance FSM for request ... for tokens 151667. Please file an issue. ``` ```text ERROR [scheduler.py:1835] Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [151667] for request ... Terminating request. ``` Other rejected token IDs observed in the same run include: ```text 22335 630 ``` The API server subsequently reports: ```text Request ... failed with an internal error during generation ``` The following log markers were all present: ```json { "failed_to_advance_fsm": true, "please_file_issue": true, "grammar_rejected_tokens": true, "internal_generation_error": true } ``` ## Server health after the failures After the 21 HTTP 500 responses, the script calls: ```text GET /v1/models ``` Observed result: ```text HTTP 200 ``` Therefore, this is a per-request internal generation failure rather than a complete server crash. ## Control without speculative decoding The script stops the failing server and starts an otherwise identical server without: ```text --speculative-config ``` The following settings remain unchanged: ```text Model Model dtype xgrammar backend JSON schema Prompts Request count Concurrency Maximum model length Maximum sequences Maximum batched tokens GPU ``` Control result: ```text Single request: HTTP 200, valid JSON Concurrent successful responses: 24 Concurrent HTTP 500 responses: 0 Invalid JSON responses: 0 Transport errors: 0 Server health afterward: HTTP 200 ``` This isolates the failure to the interaction involving `ngram_gpu` speculative decoding. ## Reproduction on vLLM 0.26.0 The same interaction was previously reproduced with vLLM 0.26.0. One run produced: ```text Single structured request: HTTP 200 Concurrent requests: 3 HTTP 200, 21 HTTP 500 ``` A separate run with asynchronous scheduling produced: ```text Single structured request: HTTP 200 Concurrent requests: 2 HTTP 200, 22 HTTP 500 ``` The same server-side FSM and rejected-token errors were observed. The failure therefore reproduces on both: ```text vLLM 0.26.0 vLLM 0.27.1 ``` ## Expected behavior All valid concurrent structured-output requests should complete successfully. Speculative decoding may change performance, but it should not cause xgrammar to reject tokens that have already been accepted or committed by the scheduler. Expected result: ```text 24 HTTP 200 responses 24 valid JSON outputs 0 HTTP 500 responses ``` ## Actual behavior With `ngram_gpu` enabled: ```text 3 HTTP 200 responses 21 HTTP 500 responses ``` The structured-output FSM rejects generated tokens, the affected requests are terminated, and clients receive an internal server error. ## Reproducibility summary | Configuration | Single request | Concurrent result | Server after test | |---|---:|---:|---:| | vLLM 0.27.1, xgrammar + ngram_gpu | Pass | 3/24 pass, 21 HTTP 500 | Healthy | | vLLM 0.27.1, xgrammar without speculative decoding | Pass | 24/24 pass | Healthy | | vLLM 0.26.0, xgrammar + ngram_gpu | Pass | 3/24 pass, 21 HTTP 500 | Healthy | | vLLM 0.26.0, xgrammar + ngram_gpu, separate scheduling run | Pass | 2/24 pass, 22 HTTP 500 | Healthy | ## Attached evidence [result.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31143667/result.json) [ngram_gpu_stdout.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31143672/ngram_gpu_stdout.log) [ngram_gpu_stderr.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31143685/ngram_gpu_stderr.log) [no_spec_control_stdout.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31143690/no_spec_control_stdout.log) [no_spec_control_stderr.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31143699/no_spec_control_stderr.log) ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug]: Kimi-K3 silent output corruption in 1P1D NIXL Direct-PD disaggregated deployment
signals.text: ### Summary I am seeing intermittent silent output corruption / garbled generation when serving Kimi-K3 with TP=8 in a 1P1D disaggregated Prefill/Decode deployment using MooncakeStoreConnector together with NixlConnector through MultiConnector. The important A/B observation is: - **NIXL-only PD**: stable, no garbled output observed. - **NIXL + MooncakeStoreConnector through MultiConnector**: garbled output reproducibly appears under sustained load. - **Mooncake enabled + DSpark/speculative decoding disabled**: corruption still reproduces. - **Mooncake disabled**: corruption has not reproduced in my testing. Therefore speculative decoding does not appear to be required to trigger the corruption. The corrupted requests can generate long sequences of nonsensical mixed-language/repeated tokens, for example repeated words such as `Effective/effective` mixed with unrelated English/Chinese fragments. Some affected streams eventually surface at the application layer as HTTP 502 / `7104_UPSTREAM_STREAM_INTERRUPTED`. This looks like a correctness issue rather than a crash-only issue: the engine can continue running while individual outputs are already corrupted. ### Deployment topology Two-node 1P1D deployment: ``` Prefill node Kimi-K3 TP=8 | | NIXL PD transfer v Decode node Kimi-K3 TP=8 ``` Failing configuration additionally uses: ``` Prefill | +-- MultiConnector | +-- NixlConnector | kv_role=kv_producer | +-- MooncakeStoreConnector kv_role=kv_both load_async=true lookup_async=true ``` The Decode node remains a NixlConnector consumer. ### Environment - **Model**: Kimi-K3 - **Tensor parallel size**: 8 - **PD topology**: 1 Prefill + 1 Decode - **KV transfer**: NIXL - **Prefix caching**: enabled - **KV cache dtype**: fp8 - **MLA prefill backend**: FLASHINFER - **VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT**: DS - **vLLM version**: Latest main / nightly - **vLLM commit**: Latest main - **GPU**: 8x NVIDIA B300 - **CUDA**: CUDA 12.8 - **OS / container image**: Linux (Ubuntu 22.04 / Container) Relevant upstream fixes included: - #48425: yes (tested on latest main) - #49499: yes (tested on latest main) - #49502: yes (tested on latest main) - #50344: yes (tested on latest main) ### Failing Prefill configuration Relevant environment: ```bash export VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS export VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL=4608 ``` KV connector: ```json KV='{ "kv_connector": "MultiConnector", "kv_role": "kv_both", "kv_load_failure_policy": "fail", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "connectors": [ { "kv_connector": "NixlConnector", "kv_role": "kv_producer", "kv_load_failure_policy": "fail" }, { "kv_connector": "MooncakeStoreConnector", "kv_role": "kv_both", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "load_async": true, "lookup_async": true } } ] } }' ``` Relevant server arguments: ```bash vllm serve /modules/Kimi-K3 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --attention-config \ '{"mla_prefill_backend":"FLASHINFER","use_prefill_query_quantization":true}' \ --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \ --enforce-eager \ --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \ --kv-transfer-config "$KV" ``` *(For minimal reproduction, run without `--speculative-config`, as the corruption reproduces without DSpark).* ### Decode configuration The Decode side uses NIXL only: ```bash vllm serve /modules/Kimi-K3 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --attention-config \ '{"mla_prefill_backend":"FLASHINFER","use_prefill_query_quantization":true}' \ --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \ --kv-transfer-config \ '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail"}' \ --compilation-config \ '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \ --max-num-seqs 32 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 1024 ``` ### Stable control configuration If I remove `MooncakeStoreConnector` / `MultiConnector` and use only: ```json --kv-transfer-config \ '{ "kv_connector": "NixlConnector", "kv_role": "kv_producer", "kv_load_failure_policy": "fail" }' ``` on the Prefill side, the same Kimi-K3 TP8 PD setup is stable in my testing. The control setup still uses: - Kimi-K3 - TP=8 - prefix caching enabled - FP8 KV cache - FLASHINFER MLA prefill - NIXL PD transfer I have also tested DSpark/speculative decoding in the NIXL-only configuration without observing the same corruption. ### Reproduction A minimal A/B reproduction: 1. **Test A — Control**: - Start Kimi-K3 TP8 Prefill with NixlConnector only. - Start Kimi-K3 TP8 Decode with NixlConnector. - Enable prefix caching. - Run sustained concurrent traffic, including repeated/shared prefixes. - Confirm prefix-cache activity. - **Result**: No corrupted output observed. 2. **Test B — Failing**: - Keep the same model and PD topology, but replace the Prefill connector with `MultiConnector` (`NixlConnector` + `MooncakeStoreConnector`). - Run the same traffic and make sure Mooncake external cache hits are occurring. - **Result**: Intermittent silent output corruption / garbled text. 3. **Test C — DSpark disabled**: - Repeat Test B without any `--speculative-config`. - **Result**: Corruption still reproduces. (Speculative decoding is not the primary trigger). ### Actual behavior Affected generations suddenly degrade into nonsensical output containing repeated and unrelated multilingual tokens. Example pattern: ``` ... effective ... Effective ... effective ... ... random unrelated English words ... ... Chinese fragments ... ... repeated/degenerate text ... ``` The server does not necessarily crash immediately. At the upper service layer, affected streams can end as: ``` HTTP 502 7104_UPSTREAM_STREAM_INTERRUPTED ``` ### Attachments I can provide: - screenshot of a corrupted generation; - Prometheus graphs from the failing run; - Prometheus graphs from the stable/control run; - complete Prefill/Decode logs around an affected request; - Mooncake hit/load metrics; - exact request ID / prompt and response if needed. ### Additional observation about speculative decoding When DSpark is enabled, I have also observed abnormal MTP/spec-decode acceptance behavior during some bad runs. However, I currently consider this a secondary symptom, because the output corruption can still reproduce after DSpark is completely disabled. Therefore this report is specifically about the Mooncake/external hybrid-cache path, rather than the DSpark rejection sampler. ### Expected behavior Loading a prefix from MooncakeStore should be correctness-equivalent to either: 1. recomputing the prefix, or 2. serving the same prefix from local GPU prefix cache. For Kimi-K3, all cache/state groups required to resume generation should represent the same safe token boundary. Enabling Mooncake external caching should not change model output correctness. ### Suspected area The A/B result suggests the issue is somewhere in the interaction between: - Kimi-K3 hybrid cache - `MooncakeStoreConnector` + `MultiConnector` - external prefix cache lookup/load - KDA recurrent state / attention KV reconciliation A possible failure mode would be a resume boundary where the attention KV and KDA recurrent state do not correspond to the same token position. I am particularly interested in whether the following invariant is always guaranteed for Mooncake external hits: ``` reported reusable prefix <= safe Full-Attention/MLA prefix <= valid boundary with corresponding KDA recurrent state ``` and whether all hybrid cache groups are invalidated/reconciled together if one external group is unavailable or has a shorter valid hit. ### Possibly related issues / PRs - #48425 — per-group prefix-hit divergence for hybrid models with KV connector - #49499 — Mooncake TP-sharded Mamba/linear-attention state corruption - #49502 — reliable partial-tail KV offload for sub-block prompts - #50344 — divergent hybrid cache hits scoped to capable connectors / MultiConnector behavior - #47812 — group-aware recovery for KV load failures on hybrid models - #50630 — hybrid recurrent-cache correctness / hit-boundary coordination discussion If my commit already contains them, this may indicate a remaining Kimi-K3-specific or MooncakeStore/MultiConnector-specific correctness path.

signals.title: [Bug]: OffloadingConnector silently crashes at >64GB CPU RAM with GLM 5.2
signals.text:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Your output of `python collect_env.py` here ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug When running the GLM 5.2 FP8 model, I am unable to run a stable `OffloadingConnector` config with more than 64G of RAM specified: ``` '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"spec_name":"TieringOffloadingSpec","cpu_bytes_to_use":68719476736,"blocks_per_chunk":4,"eviction_policy":"lru","secondary_tiers":[{"type":"fs","root_dir":"/kvcache"}]}}' ``` If I double `cpu_bytes_to_use` to 128GB, the vLLM silently crashes and restarts after serving the model for a couple seconds. If I double it again to 256GB, the model never even reaches the serving state. By contrast, the `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` works absolutely fine with 256GB per rank (for a total of 2TB of RAM cache): ``` '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":274877906944,"lazy_offload":"false"}}' ``` But unfortunately with this connector, it's not possible to have a disk tier. I have tried this with vLLM 0.26.0 on NVIDIA (8x B200) and vLLM ROCm v0.27.1 on AMD (8x MI325X). I also tried LMCache and it fails to work with GLM 5.2, crashes as soon as you interact with the model. For reference, the full ROCm v0.27.1 launch config: ``` env: VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER: "1" VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS: "1" PYTHONHASHSEED: "0" VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER: "1" NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS: "112" extra_args: - "--kv-transfer-config" - '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"spec_name":"TieringOffloadingSpec","cpu_bytes_to_use":68719476736,"blocks_per_chunk":4,"eviction_policy":"lru","secondary_tiers":[{"type":"fs","root_dir":"/kvcache"}]}}' - "--kv-cache-dtype" - "fp8_e4m3" - "--enable-expert-parallel" - "--prefix-caching-hash-algo" - "sha256_cbor" - "--max-num-seqs" - "64" - "--max-num-batched-tokens" - "16384" - "--tool-call-parser" - "glm47" - "--enable-auto-tool-choice" - "--reasoning-parser" - "glm45" - "--chat-template" - "/models/weights/chat_template.jinja" - "--chat-template-content-format" - "string" - "--linear-backend" - "aiter" - "--moe-backend" - "aiter" - "--attention-backend" - "ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE" - "--block-size" - "1" ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug]: FP8 on RDNA3/gfx1100 exceeds the 600 s engine-ready timeout on first start — no AMD_Radeon_Graphics tuned configs shipped
signals.text:
### TL;DR - The official FP8 checkpoint (Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8) **loads and serves fine on a consumer RDNA3 card** (gfx1100, Radeon W7900 48 GB, `vllm==0.27.1+rocm723` on ROCm). There is no architecture refusal — community trackers currently report FP8 as "does not run on RDNA3", but it does. - The out-of-the-box failure is a **startup timeout**: for `device_name=AMD_Radeon_Graphics` the wheel ships **zero** tuned W8A8 block-FP8 configs (of 218 device-keyed configs it ships 76 for AMD Instinct and 142 for NVIDIA devices), so the default config is used and warmup **JIT-compiles the Triton GEMM kernels shape by shape**. First engine init measured **1474.26 s** — 2.5x the 600 s default of `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S` — and the APIServer aborts. - The abort message says the timeout is "**often caused by slow weight loading**". Our weights loaded in **16.33 s**; the 23+ minutes between kernel warnings were CPU-side Triton compilation with the GPU idle. - `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=1800` makes it start. Once the on-disk Triton cache is warm, engine init is **49 s** and every later start is ~2 min — the cost is one-time per host (until `~/.triton/cache` is cleared). - **Asks:** (1) ship tuned W8A8 configs for `AMD_Radeon_Graphics` (mirroring the MI300X/MI325 sets); (2) cheap: mention cold-start JIT/config warmup as a cause in the engine-ready timeout error or the env-var docs; (3) secondary observation: the **first inference** triggers a further ~43 min of JIT staging that `/health` does not reflect. - **I have the hardware** and am happy to run whatever tuning/profiling procedure you point at and PR the resulting `AMD_Radeon_Graphics` JSONs, and to test any RC on gfx1100. ### Your current environment
Output of python -m vllm.collect_env (venv used for all runs below) ```text Collecting environment information... uv is set ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 Clang version : Could not collect CMake version : version 3.28.3 Libc version : glibc-2.39 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.11.0+gitd0c8b1f Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : N/A ROCM used to build PyTorch : 7.2.53211 XPU used to build PyTorch : N/A ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.3 (main, Mar 3 2026, 12:15:18) [GCC 13.3.0] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-6.8.0-79-generic-x86_64-with-glibc-2.39 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True CUDA runtime version : Could not collect CUDA_MODULE_LOADING set to : GPU models and configuration : AMD Radeon Graphics (gfx1100) Nvidia driver version : Could not collect cuDNN version : Could not collect HIP runtime version : 7.2.53211 MIOpen runtime version : 3.5.1 Is XNNPACK available : True ============================== vLLM Info ============================== ROCM Version : 7.2.53211-e1a6bc5663 vLLM Version : 0.27.1 vLLM Build Flags: CUDA Archs: Not Set; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled GPU Topology: single GPU, NUMA node 0 ============================== Environment Variables ============================== PYTORCH_NVML_BASED_CUDA_CHECK=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/torchinductor_root ``` Install (per the ROCm install docs): `uv pip install vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/` → `vllm==0.27.1+rocm723`; `transformers==5.15.0`; host ROCm userspace 7.2.1. CPU: 2x AMD EPYC 9334 (full `lscpu` flags and the rocm-smi topology table omitted for brevity; available on request).
### 🐛 Describe the bug **Expected:** `vllm serve` (or `api_server`) with an official FP8 checkpoint on gfx1100 either starts within the default engine-ready budget, or fails with a message pointing at the real cost. **Actual (measured on Radeon W7900D, gfx1100, 48 GB):** | Run | `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S` | Triton cache | Result | |---|---|---|---| | cold serve | 600 (default) | cold | `TimeoutError` at 600 s mid-warmup; weights had loaded in 16.33 s | | cold serve | 1800 | cold | engine init **1474.26 s**, then `/health` 200, serving OK | | warm re-run | 1800 | warm | engine init **49.01 s** | | later starts (x3) | 1800 | warm | 49.10 / 49.11 / 49.19 s, server up in ~2 min | After unlock, serving works end-to-end (105/105 benchmark requests OK) — at untuned-config performance; see measured results below. #### Reproduce without hardware (2 minutes) Anyone with the wheel installed can verify the config gap that drives the cold-start cost: ```bash CFG=$(python -c "import vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.fp8_utils as m, os; print(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(m.__file__),'configs'))") ls "$CFG" | wc -l # 219 (218 device-keyed JSONs + README.md) ls "$CFG" | grep -c MI300X # 28 (+ 24 MI325X + 24 MI325_OAM = 76 Instinct) ls "$CFG" | grep -ci radeon # 0 ls "$CFG" | grep -c 'N=16384,K=5120' # 0 — not shipped for ANY device ``` The engine-side lookup is a plain file-exists check in `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py` (0.27.1, ~line 830): the filename is built from `get_device_name_as_file_name()` — which on RDNA3 consumer cards is literally the torch device name `AMD Radeon Graphics` → `device_name=AMD_Radeon_Graphics` — and when the JSON is missing the code logs the warning below and **returns `None` (default config)**. Nothing is ever written back to that directory, so the cost recurs for every fresh host/venv. #### Reproduce on gfx1100 (~35 min, needs a 24 GB+ RDNA3 card) ```bash # fresh venv — a warm ~/.triton/cache hides the bug (init drops to ~49 s) uv venv /root/venv-fp8 && VIRTUAL_ENV=/root/venv-fp8 uv pip install vllm \ --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/ # 0.27.1+rocm723 # model: official FP8 checkpoint, ~28.7 GiB # HF: huggingface-cli download Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 # (we used ModelScope: modelscope download Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8) SNAP=/path/to/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 # 1) default timeout → aborts at 600 s: /root/venv-fp8/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model "$SNAP" --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 \ --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --port 8199 # 2) unlocked: VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=1800 /root/venv-fp8/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model "$SNAP" --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 \ --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --port 8199 ``` (All measurements above were taken with `--enforce-eager` added to skip torch.compile/CUDA-graph capture; the cold abort also reproduces without it, with `torch.compile took 67.53 s` interleaved.) #### Verbatim evidence
1) Cold run, default timeout — aborts while weights were long done ```text (EngineCore pid=280186) INFO 08-17 01:42:46 [default_loader.py:430] Loading weights took 16.33 seconds (EngineCore pid=280186) INFO 08-17 01:42:46 [gpu_model_runner.py:5405] Model loading took 29.38 GiB memory and 17.353099 seconds (EngineCore pid=280186) INFO 08-17 01:44:23 [monitor.py:53] torch.compile took 67.53 s in total (EngineCore pid=280186) WARNING 08-17 01:44:23 [fp8_utils.py:851] Using default W8A8 Block FP8 kernel config. Performance might be sub-optimal! Config file not found at /root/venv-fp8probe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/configs/N=16384,K=5120,device_name=AMD_Radeon_Graphics,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128,128].json (EngineCore pid=280186) WARNING 08-17 02:07:49 [fp8_utils.py:851] Using default W8A8 Block FP8 kernel config. Performance might be sub-optimal! Config file not found at /root/venv-fp8probe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/configs/N=5120,K=6144,device_name=AMD_Radeon_Graphics,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128,128].json (APIServer pid=279547) TimeoutError: Timed out waiting for engine core processes to start. This is often caused by slow weight loading for large models. Waited 600s (configured by VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S). To increase the timeout, set the environment variable: VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S= ``` Note the **23 m 26 s gap between the two fp8_utils warnings** — that is one Triton GEMM kernel compiling (single CPU core pinned, GPU idle), not weight loading.
2) Same wheel, timeout raised — starts, and the cost is visible ```text (EngineCore pid=371418) WARNING 08-17 08:07:37 [fp8_utils.py:851] Using default W8A8 Block FP8 kernel config. ... N=16384,K=5120,device_name=AMD_Radeon_Graphics,... (EngineCore pid=371418) WARNING 08-17 08:31:17 [fp8_utils.py:851] Using default W8A8 Block FP8 kernel config. ... N=34816,K=5120,device_name=AMD_Radeon_Graphics,... (EngineCore pid=371418) INFO 08-17 08:31:42 [core.py:355] init engine (profile, create kv cache, warmup model) took 1474.26 s (APIServer pid=371094) INFO: 127.0.0.1:33878 - "GET /health HTTP/1.1" 200 OK ``` The warmup pass walks five GEMM shapes for this model (N=16384/K=5120, N=5120/K=6144, N=34816/K=5120, N=5120/K=17408, N=14336/K=5120); none has a shipped config.
3) Warm Triton cache — the whole cliff disappears ```text (EngineCore pid=378832) INFO 08-17 08:38:28 [core.py:355] init engine (profile, create kv cache, warmup model) took 49.01 s (APIServer pid=378511) INFO 08-17 08:38:45 [api_server.py:682] Starting vLLM server on http://0.0.0.0:8199 (APIServer pid=378511) INFO: Application startup complete. (APIServer pid=378511) INFO: 127.0.0.1:46230 - "GET /health HTTP/1.1" 200 OK ```
4) Secondary: first-INFERENCE JIT staging (~43 min), invisible to /health Even after a healthy start, the first completion request triggers more JIT compiles; the server answers `/health` 200 the whole time and a default-timeout client (ours: 300 s) just times out. Verbatim from the first served request on a cache-warm-start server: ```text (EngineCore pid=434612) WARNING 08-17 13:34:18 [chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py:419] Cannot use ROCm custom paged attention kernel, falling back to Triton implementation. (EngineCore pid=434612) WARNING 08-17 13:55:59 [jit_monitor.py:135] Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: _causal_conv1d_update_kernel. This causes a latency spike; consider extending warmup to cover this shape/config. (EngineCore pid=434612) WARNING 08-17 13:55:59 [jit_monitor.py:135] Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode_kernel. ... (EngineCore pid=434612) WARNING 08-17 13:55:59 [jit_monitor.py:135] Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: layer_norm_fwd_kernel. ... ``` The very first request (13:34:18) outlived the client's 300 s ceiling; the first fully-served response landed at ~14:17:41 — **43 min after the first request was sent** (the request that completed was issued 14:07:52 and took `total_s=608.536757`). Subsequent traffic is normal: a 16-request warmup burst after this returned all 200 in ~26–28 s.
### Root cause (as far as the code shows) 1. `fp8_utils.py` builds the tuned-config filename from the torch device name — on RDNA3 consumer cards that is `AMD Radeon Graphics` → `device_name=AMD_Radeon_Graphics` — and the wheel ships **no** JSONs for that name (the entire AMD set is Instinct-only). Missing file → warning → `return None` → default W8A8 config. 2. With the default config, `w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm` JIT-compiles its Triton kernel for each distinct (N, K) shape during engine warmup. On this host each big compile takes ~20+ min of single-threaded CPU (GPU idle); the shape-by-shape walk (first warning 08:07:37 → init done 08:31:42) accounts for essentially all of the 1474.26 s engine init. 3. The APIServer's engine-ready deadline (default 600 s, `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S`, consumed in the v1 engine core client) expires mid-warmup, and the error names "slow weight loading" as the likely cause. 4. The Triton disk cache (`~/.triton/cache`) makes every subsequent start fast, and nothing writes tuned JSONs back — so the cliff is a **per-host one-time cost that looks like a hard failure** the first time. ### Proposed fixes (ranked) 1. **Ship tuned W8A8 block-FP8 configs for `AMD_Radeon_Graphics`** (gfx1100 at minimum), mirroring the shipped MI300X/MI325 sets. This is what the runtime warning already asks for, it removes the "sub-optimal default" path entirely, and it is the lever for the performance gap below. I have a W7900 and am glad to run the config-generation/benchmark procedure on it and open a PR with the resulting JSONs if you can point me at the tooling. 2. **Cheap message/docs improvement:** `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S` is documented, but the timeout error's cause list ("often caused by slow weight loading") sends users down the wrong path when the real cost is JIT/config warmup on an untuned device (weights: 16.33 s here). One extra sentence in the error string or in the env-var docs — "first-start JIT compilation of untuned kernels can take tens of minutes on newly-supported platforms; raise the timeout or pre-warm" — would have saved us hours. 3. **Secondary observation** (same platform gap, different surface): the first inference after a cold start triggers ~43 min more of Triton JIT that `/health` does not reflect (details block 4). If preferred I'll split this into its own issue — keeping it here because it shares the root cause (no RDNA3 tuning artifacts shipped). ### Measured results after unlock (context for prioritization, not a complaint) `--enforce-eager`, temp 0, fixed 100-token prompt, 128-token generations, 5 reps per cell, non-streaming: | concurrency | aggregate decode tok/s | requests OK | p50 request wall | |---|---:|---|---:| | 1 | 0.612 | 5/5 | 209.2 s | | 4 | 2.301 | 20/20 | 222.4 s | | 16 | 8.730 | 80/80 | 234.5 s | For scale on the same GPU, llama.cpp with a Q4_K_M GGUF of the same model does 28.6 tok/s single-stream and 164.4 tok/s aggregate at c=32 — so FP8-on-RDNA3 today is ~47x slower per stream, which the tuned-config gap plausibly explains a large part of. Capacity is not the issue: 29.38 GiB of FP8 weights on the 48 GB card with ~19 GiB headroom. ### Related issues (searched; not duplicates) - #51136 — AITER not enabled on RDNA3 (gfx1100): same GPU class, different mechanism (INT8/Quark + AITER gating vs FP8 W8A8 Triton path here); complementary data point. - #35547, #32116 — same engine-ready timeout symptom class on NVIDIA (slow weight loading / DeepGEMM warmup). This issue adds the RDNA3/FP8 instance where the dominant cost is per-shape Triton JIT under a missing tuned config, plus the configs gap itself. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] I searched existing issues (linked above) and found no report of FP8-on-RDNA3 failing startup via untuned-config JIT with this mechanism. - [x] `collect_env` output attached. - [x] Repro is self-contained; the configs-gap part needs no hardware. Happy to contribute: tuning runs on gfx1100 → `AMD_Radeon_Graphics` config PR, and RC testing on this card.

### 🐛 Describe the bug PR [#36787](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/36787) moved Gemma's `sqrt(hidden_size)` normalization from `forward()` into text-only `embed_input_ids()`, but PaliGemma retained the inverse scale that previously compensated for the old common forward multiplication. Current vLLM consequently feeds projected image features into Gemma at `1 / sqrt(hidden_size)` of their intended magnitude. Before #36787, the operations were balanced: ```text text: embed_tokens ------------------------> Gemma.forward * sqrt(H) image: projector / sqrt(H) -> merge --------> Gemma.forward * sqrt(H) ``` After #36787, current vLLM scales only text: ```text text: embed_tokens * sqrt(H) -> merge -> Gemma.forward unchanged image: projector / sqrt(H) ----> merge -> Gemma.forward unchanged ``` Current `main` scales text in [`gemma.py:284-308`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/60c3a31b12b0a735baa79684885391747771ec64/vllm/model_executor/models/gemma.py#L284-L308), but still inverse-scales images in [`paligemma.py:376-383`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/60c3a31b12b0a735baa79684885391747771ec64/vllm/model_executor/models/paligemma.py#L376-L383). Multimodal merge only replaces placeholder rows, and `GemmaModel.forward(inputs_embeds=...)` applies no compensating scale. Transformers changed both halves atomically in [`0e7cb4e3`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/commit/0e7cb4e3ea3daaeef626148522f80b751e9559bd): Gemma text lookup gained `sqrt(H)` scaling and PaliGemma stopped dividing projected image features. Transformers 5.14.1 directly inserts raw projected image features into the already-scaled text embeddings. For ColPali's `hidden_size=2048`, the contract reduction is: ```python import math hidden_size = 2048 raw_projected_image = 1.0 print( "before #36787:", raw_projected_image * hidden_size**-0.5 * math.sqrt(hidden_size), ) print("current vLLM:", raw_projected_image * hidden_size**-0.5) print("expected:", raw_projected_image) ``` ```text before #36787: 1.0 current vLLM: 0.022097086912079608 expected: 1.0 ``` The stale factor is therefore about `0.0221`: projected image features enter Gemma at about 2.21% of their intended magnitude. Controlled one-variable A/B against the pinned Transformers reference: | Variant | Text cosine mean | Image cosine mean | Image p01 | Image minimum | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Current stale inverse scale | 0.999797 | 0.903149 | 0.430221 | 0.225688 | | Inverse scale removed only | 0.999797 | 0.987502 | 0.726556 | 0.436249 | The request, preprocessing, checkpoint, plugin SHA, and reference were held constant; only `vision_embeddings *= hidden_size**-0.5` was removed. The remaining image mismatch is a separately measured Neuron eager-vision drift, so this one-line change should not be represented as fixing all ColPali parity issues. Full ColPali command used for validation: ```bash vllm serve vidore/colpali-v1.3-hf \ --revision 7d3c8ab1c1908b32d701308fb1dfb2968d150c67 \ --served-model-name vidore/colpali-v1.3-hf \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --max-num-seqs 1 \ --max-model-len 4096 \ --trust-remote-code \ --runner pooling \ --convert none \ --pooler-config.task token_embed \ --port 20000 ``` Expected behavior: PaliGemma should return raw projected image features from `embed_multimodal()`, matching Transformers' scaled-text/raw-image contract. Suggested fix: ```diff def embed_multimodal(self, **kwargs: object) -> MultiModalEmbeddings: image_input = self._parse_and_validate_image_input(**kwargs) if image_input is None: return [] vision_embeddings = self._process_image_input(image_input) - vision_embeddings = vision_embeddings * (self.config.hidden_size**-0.5) return vision_embeddings ``` Suggested tests: pass known projected `image_embeds` to PaliGemma and assert they are returned unchanged; add one fixed-image Transformers parity test that compares first-step logits or top-k probabilities. Current ColPali tests verify shape, L2 normalization, and weak relevance ordering, which cannot detect this pre-language-model scaling error. The final downstream ColPali branch passes with pristine vLLM only because its host-vision path supplies raw projected features and bypasses `PaliGemma.embed_multimodal()`. The one-line patch is not part of that final plugin apply set, and the pristine pass does not validate the stale upstream method. This regression was introduced by #36787 (`65986db6ba71abf4cf0639c5fd1477b0d8df8f5e`). Searches for PaliGemma image scaling, inverse scaling, `sqrt(hidden_size)`, `hidden_size**-0.5`, and #36787 found no matching issue or follow-up fix. Severity: major silent correctness regression. The source contract is confirmed; broad current-main CUDA generation impact has not yet been quantified. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug] Streaming input: zero-token continuation crashes EngineCore (Invalid request status: RUNNING) — client-triggerable via temperature>0 chat sessions
signals.text: ## Summary A streaming-input (resumable) session **kills the entire engine** (`EngineDeadError`) when a continuation turn produces **zero output tokens** — i.e. the model samples a stop token as the very first token of the turn. The scheduler then finds the resumed request still marked `RUNNING` in the waiting queue and raises, taking down `EngineCore` and every concurrent request on the server. This is a follow-up to #52471 (streaming-input depth costs); splitting the crash into its own issue because it is a distinct correctness/availability bug with a clean trigger. ## Severity The trigger is **ordinary chat traffic**: multi-turn sessions with temperature > 0 (the default for conversational serving; e.g. gemma-4's own `generation_config.json` ships `temperature: 1.0`). A zero-token stop-finish is a normal, per-turn sampling outcome, so a long enough conversation hits it with high probability — and one unlucky sample from one user crashes the shared engine for everyone. We observed **9 engine deaths across 5 fresh instances and 4 configurations**. ## Traceback (v0.25.1, deployed) ``` File ".../vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 1304, in _process_engine_step outputs, model_executed = self.step_fn() File ".../vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 547, in step_with_batch_queue scheduler_output = self.scheduler.schedule(self._should_throttle_prefills()) File ".../vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py", line 981, in schedule raise RuntimeError(f"Invalid request status: {request.status}") RuntimeError: Invalid request status: RUNNING ``` The traceback is entirely within `EngineCore` → `Scheduler` — **no frontend frames**. It is reachable by any driver of streaming input (the native `AsyncLLM.generate()` async-generator interface, the `/v1/realtime` handler, or a custom router); our runs used a thin HTTP shim over `AsyncLLM.generate()`, but the shim is irrelevant to the crash. ## Trigger conditions (all three required) 1. **Streaming input / resumable session** — the request re-enters the update-and-requeue loop. One-shot requests are unaffected. 2. **A continuation turn generates zero output tokens** — the first sampled token is a stop/terminator token, so after the "discard last sampled token" step there is nothing left. Requires **temperature > 0** so a stop token can win the first draw; we hit it within 1–3 continuation turns at `temperature=0.7`. 3. **It is a continuation, not the first turn** — turn 1 of a fresh session never triggered it. ## Root-cause hypothesis `Scheduler._update_request_as_session()` keeps `_all_token_ids[num_prompt_tokens:num_computed_tokens]` and discards the final sampled token, on the assumption a finished turn produced ≥1 token. When the turn produced **zero** tokens (first sample was a stop token), this degenerates and the request is re-queued in a state the next `schedule()` pass rejects as invalid (`RUNNING` while waiting). This matches the "discard the last sampled output token" design described in the streaming-input blog, which implicitly assumes a token exists to discard. ## Reproduction Open a resumable streaming session and drive two turns of a chat model at `temperature=0.7`: - Turn 1: system preamble + a question + (in our case one image). Completes normally. - Turn 2: a follow-up question appended to the same session. Within a few such continuation turns, one returns `finish_reason=stop` with 0 tokens in ~15–20 ms, and the engine dies on the next schedule. **Negative control:** the identical turns at `temperature=0.0` complete normally, every time — isolating the zero-token sampling outcome as the cause (not request format; we also ruled out `max_num_batched_tokens`, `compile_ranges_endpoints`, and re-supplying the discarded stop token as text). A deterministic variant can be built by constructing a prompt where a stop token is the greedy first choice. Observed with a multimodal model; the mechanism is not image-specific and likely reproduces text-only. Happy to share our full runner script. ## Suggested fixes 1. Handle the zero-token completion in `_update_request_as_session()` (a turn that stops before generating leaves the session in a valid resumable state). 2. Make the scheduler's invalid-status check **fail the offending request**, not raise into `EngineCore` — a per-request error should not crash the whole engine (defense-in-depth regardless of root cause). ## Environment vLLM v0.25.1 (cu129), gemma-4-31b-it (multimodal), TP=4, streaming input via `AsyncLLM.generate()`.
