signals.title: [Bug]: Missing `has_cutedsl()` guard in `DeepseekCompressor` (head_dim == 512 path)
signals.text: ### Your current environment cant share this at the moment. ### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Summary In the DeepSeek V4 `DeepseekCompressor` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/compressor.py`), the CuTe DSL kernel path for `head_dim == 512` is selected without checking `has_cutedsl()`. Every other DeepSeek V4 CUDA/DS kernel selection site in the repo gates on `has_cutedsl()`, so this looks like an inconsistency that was missed in one spot. ### Where the guard is already established - `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/common/ops/cache_utils.py:412` -> `if has_cutedsl():` - `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/common/ops/fused_indexer_q.py:353` and `:422` -> `if has_cutedsl():` - `vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py:57` -> `if not has_cutedsl():` - `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/ops/__init__.py` explicitly documents that leaf modules must only be imported under a `has_cutedsl()`/`is_cuda()` gate. ### The missing guard `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/compressor.py` currently uses: ```python if current_platform.is_cuda() and self.head_dim == 512: ``` which unconditionally selects the CuTe DSL compressor (`compress_norm_rope_store_cutedsl`), even when the optional `cutlass` (CuTe DSL) package is not importable. ### Suggested change ```python if current_platform.is_cuda() and self.head_dim == 512 and has_cutedsl(): ``` with the existing import (`from vllm.utils.import_utils import has_cutedsl`) added if not already present. ### Why it matters - On builds where `cutlass`/CuTe DSL is not available, the `head_dim == 512` compressor path currently fails at kernel dispatch even though the framework already supports a graceful Triton fallback and the rest of the DSv4 ops check `has_cutedsl()`. - Consistent with the established pattern in the same feature area. ### Environment (for reference) This was found while building/running vLLM 0.26 for an H200 (sm_90a) target where the optional CuTe DSL package is not shipped. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.text:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Collecting environment information... ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 Clang version : Could not collect CMake version : version 4.4.2 Libc version : glibc-2.39 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.13.0+xpu Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : None ROCM used to build PyTorch : N/A XPU used to build PyTorch : 20260000 ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.3 (main, Jun 19 2026, 12:46:00) [GCC 13.3.0] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-7.0.0-28-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 ============================== Intel XPU / GPU Info ============================== Is XPU available : True XPU runtime version : 20260000 Intel GPU models : GPU 0: Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B70 Graphics --Compile time-- oneAPI compiler version : Could not collect SYCL compiler build : Could not collect oneCCL version : 2022.0.0 --Runtime-- Intel Graphics Compiler (IGC): 2.34.4 Intel GMM (libigdgmm) : 22.10.0 ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug `compressed_tensors` channel-strategy quantization leaves `group_size` unset (`None`). Two independent sites compare it against `int` instead of handling `None` — different exception, different bit-width: - **int4** — `check_moe_marlin_supports_config` (`marlin_utils.py:378`/`:383`, `group_size <= 0`) raises `TypeError` from inside `_backend_incompatibility_reason` (`int_wna16.py:163`), which is supposed to *return* a reason string, not raise — backend selection aborts instead of falling back. A second int4 site, `marlin_moe_padded_intermediate` (`marlin_utils.py:344`, `group_size if group_size > 0 else 1`), fails the same way during weight-prep. - **int8** — `CompressedTensorsWNA16MoEMethod.__init__` (`compressed_tensors_moe_wna16.py:85`, `assert self.group_size == -1`) raises `AssertionError` unconditionally, *before* backend selection even runs. Six existing sites already normalise this the same way (`-1 if group_size is None else group_size`) — e.g. `compressed_tensors_wNa16.py:67`, `compressed_tensors_moe.py:104`. This file (`compressed_tensors_moe_wna16.py:69`) doesn't. Reproducer (int4 — int8 crashes the same root cause earlier, in `__init__`, via `assert`): ```python from compressed_tensors.quantization import ( QuantizationArgs, QuantizationStrategy, QuantizationType, ) from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.marlin_utils import ( check_moe_marlin_supports_config, ) from types import SimpleNamespace args = QuantizationArgs( num_bits=4, type=QuantizationType.INT, strategy=QuantizationStrategy.CHANNEL, symmetric=True, dynamic=False, ) assert args.group_size is None config = SimpleNamespace( hidden_dim=4096, intermediate_size_per_partition_unpadded=1024, ) check_moe_marlin_supports_config(config, args.group_size, allow_tile_padding=True) ``` ### Real-world impact - Defensive-correctness gap, not an observed production failure. - Real checkpoints exist and are loadable: [Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-W4A16-channel-quantized](https://huggingface.co/nm-testing/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-W4A16-channel-quantized) (int4, hits the `TypeError` above) and [DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct-W8A8](https://huggingface.co/nm-testing/DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct-W8A8) / [Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-W8A8](https://huggingface.co/nm-testing/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-W8A8) (int8, hits the `__init__` `AssertionError` instead). - All three belong to `nm-testing` — compressed-tensors/llm-compressor's own CI-fixture account: single- to low-double-digit downloads, zero likes, over a year stale. No channel-strategy MoE checkpoint found from a more production-facing source (RedHatAI currently ships no MoE + W8A8 checkpoints at all). - Real and reproducible, but no evidence this affects an actively deployed model today. I have a patch that normalises at all read sites above (both bit-widths) and will open it against this issue. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] I have searched for similar issues. - [x] I have already asked the chatbot for help.

signals.title: [Feature]: Low-overhead asynchronous early-exit checks & KV-cache reclamation for Continuous Batching
signals.text: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch Problem Statement In high-throughput production environments running long-context agent loops or strict JSON-enforcement pipelines, models frequently burn a significant portion of generation cycles on post-plateau tail-tokens (e.g., polite wrappers, redundant formatting) after the core semantic task is complete. While stop_strings and custom LogitsProcessor hooks exist, evaluating them per-step in Python introduces severe bottlenecks: CPU-GPU Sync & GIL Contenter: Per-step synchronous callbacks disrupt the execution loop, create heavy interpreter friction, and degrade throughput at scale (batch size > 64). Even in Python-heavy orchestration stacks, this creates unacceptable micro-lags. KV-Cache Bloat & Fragmentation: Finished or logically complete sequences linger in the active batch until the explicit stop token hits or max tokens are reached, occupying precious blocks in PagedAttention and artificially inflating latency for concurrent requests. An Economic Perspective In high-volume enterprise deployments (e.g., fintech, customer ops, logistics), long-context generation loops routinely burn 20–30% of output tokens on post-plateau tail generation. For enterprise clients processing tens of millions of requests monthly, this translates to hundreds of thousands of dollars in wasted infrastructure costs annually, plus artificial latency inflation due to occupied KV-cache slots. Has anyone in the community tackled token overconsumption and mid-batch memory reclamation from a production-economy standpoint? How are large-scale deployments justifying or mitigating these dead compute cycles today? Proposed Solution Introduce a lightweight, optimized mechanism at the scheduler level to handle dynamic early-exit flags and asynchronous KV-cache recycling without heavy interpreter roundtrips: Allow registering low-overhead termination predicates directly within the vLLM scheduler loop. Provide efficient memory reclamation hooks to instantly free PagedAttention blocks for completed sequences mid-batch, avoiding dead compute cycles. Questions for Maintainers & Community Are there existing internal plans or hooks to handle asynchronous early-termination predicates inside the vLLM engine core without hitting Python GIL limits? What is the current accepted benchmark for evaluating per-step scheduling overhead in vLLM? We are currently profiling custom asynchronous volatile-flag checks and would like to share benchmarks if there is interest in contributing a PR. ### Alternatives _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_ ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary When vLLM is started with `--cudagraph-metrics`, CUDA Graph execution is active and normal periodic statistics are logged, but the documented CUDA Graph statistics table is never emitted. The issue reproduces with: - vLLM 0.27.1 - NVIDIA L40S - `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=INFO` - `ObservabilityConfig.cudagraph_metrics=True` - `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA Graph mode - sustained inference load spanning multiple logging intervals - stdout and stderr captured together The server remains healthy and all requests complete successfully. This is an observability bug rather than an inference correctness bug: CUDA Graph execution works, but the metrics enabled by `--cudagraph-metrics` are silently absent. ## Environment - vLLM: `0.27.1` - Python: `3.12.13` - PyTorch: `2.13.0+cu130` - CUDA runtime reported by PyTorch: `13.0` - GPU: NVIDIA L40S - NVIDIA driver: `595.71.05` - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` - Engine: V1 - CUDA Graph mode: `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` - Logging level: explicitly set to `INFO` The server system fingerprint was: ```text vllm-0.27.1-55fa4e7f ``` ## Expected behavior According to `ObservabilityConfig.cudagraph_metrics`, enabling CUDA Graph metrics should report: - unpadded token count - padded token count - number of padding tokens - runtime CUDA Graph dispatch mode - observed frequency The implementation also defines a log table beginning with: ```text **CUDAGraph Config Settings:** - Mode: ... - Capture sizes: ... **CUDAGraph Stats:** | Unpadded Tokens | Padded Tokens | Num Paddings | Runtime Mode | Count | ``` Relevant source: - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/config/observability.py - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/compilation/cuda_graph.py At least one CUDA Graph statistics table should be emitted during or after the sustained workload. ## Actual behavior The logs confirm that the option is enabled: ```text non-default args: { ... 'cudagraph_metrics': True, ... } ``` The engine configuration also confirms it: ```text ObservabilityConfig( ... cudagraph_metrics=True, ... ) ``` CUDA Graph capture succeeds: ```text Graph capturing finished in 1 secs, took 0.09 GiB ``` Normal periodic statistics are emitted at INFO level: ```text Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 2734.6 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 2234.3 tokens/s, Running: 15 reqs, Waiting: 1 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 0.9%, Prefix cache hit rate: 0.0% Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 989.1 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 819.1 tokens/s, Running: 0 reqs, Waiting: 0 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 0.0%, Prefix cache hit rate: 0.0% ``` However, the combined stdout/stderr log contains none of the following: ```text CUDAGraph Config Settings CUDAGraph Stats Unpadded Tokens Padded Tokens Runtime Mode ``` The server remains healthy and all inference requests succeed. ## Why this does not appear to be a logging configuration issue The reproduction explicitly rules out the common configuration explanations: | Possible explanation | Result | |---|---| | `--cudagraph-metrics` was not enabled | The parsed CLI arguments show `cudagraph_metrics=True` | | `ObservabilityConfig` did not receive the option | `ObservabilityConfig.cudagraph_metrics=True` appears in the engine log | | Log level was too restrictive | `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=INFO` is explicitly set | | INFO logging was disabled | Normal periodic engine statistics appear at INFO | | The logging interval was not reached | The workload runs continuously for 25 seconds and is followed by another request after 12 seconds | | Output was written to a different stream | stdout and stderr are redirected into the same log | | CUDA Graph execution was inactive | Graph capture completes successfully | | The server failed during the test | Requests succeed and `/health` remains available | The issue was also observed with asynchronous scheduling disabled, so it does not appear specific to the async scheduler. ## Reproduction Download [repro_cudagraph_metrics.sh](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31173012/repro_cudagraph_metrics.sh) Run it with: ```bash chmod +x repro_cudagraph_metrics.sh PYTHON_BIN="$(command -v python)" GPU=0 ./repro_cudagraph_metrics.sh ``` The script exits with status `1` when the bug is reproduced. ## Reproduction result On vLLM 0.27.1 with an NVIDIA L40S: ```text Server is healthy Completed requests: 256 Errors: 0 Logging-trigger request HTTP status: 200 BUG REPRODUCED --cudagraph-metrics was enabled and normal INFO logging ran, but no CUDA Graph runtime statistics were emitted. ``` ## Additional control runs The same missing-output behavior was observed in both configurations: 1. Default asynchronous scheduling. 2. Explicit synchronous scheduling using `--no-async-scheduling`. Therefore, the missing statistics do not appear to be caused solely by asynchronous scheduling. ## Related context - CUDA Graph logging implementation: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/compilation/cuda_graph.py - Observability configuration: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/config/observability.py - Original CUDA Graph logging PR: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/29825 - Draft Prometheus CUDA Graph counter PR: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/37576 PR #37576 concerns adding a Prometheus counter. This report concerns the existing verbose text table controlled by `--cudagraph-metrics`. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug] DeepseekV4 cannot start on sm_121 (GB10): unguarded DeepGEMM call, and CutlassScaledMM.is_supported() ignores compute capability
signals.text: ### Your current environment - vLLM `0.26.1rc1.dev608+g99a10304d` (container image, aarch64) - 2× NVIDIA GB10 (**sm_121**, 121 GiB unified memory each), CUDA 13.0, driver 580.173.02 - Two-node TP=2 via the built-in multi-node `mp` executor (`--nnodes 2 --node-rank {0,1} --master-addr … --distributed-executor-backend mp`, rank 1 `--headless`) - Model: `MJPansa/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-NVFP4` (mixed precision: routed experts NVFP4, attention / shared experts / head not quantized) - `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` and `VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` are set Other models start and serve fine on the same two-node setup with the same image (Qwen3-235B-A22B-NVFP4, Mistral-Small-4-119B, Qwen3.8-27B-FP8), so the cluster wiring itself is good. ### 🐛 Describe the bug DeepseekV4 cannot start on sm_121. There are two separate architecture gates that report "supported" and then fail inside compiled kernels. **1. `mhc_pre_broadcast_tilelang` calls DeepGEMM unconditionally** `vllm/model_executor/kernels/mhc/tilelang.py` has three call sites for `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm`. Two of them are guarded: ```python use_deep_gemm = is_deep_gemm_supported() ... if use_deep_gemm: tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm(...) else: _tilelang_hc_prenorm_gemm(...) ``` The third one, inside `mhc_pre_broadcast_tilelang` (the first-layer 2-D input path taken from `models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/model.py`), is not: ```python from vllm.utils.deep_gemm import tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm( residual_flat, fn_broadcast, gemm_out_mul, gemm_out_sqrsum, n_splits, ) ``` On sm_121 this aborts during `determine_available_memory`: ``` RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'Assertion error (/workspace/.deps/deepgemm-src/csrc/apis/hyperconnection.hpp:56): Unsupported architecture' ``` The shipped DeepGEMM extension only contains kernels for two architectures: ``` $ strings vllm/third_party/deep_gemm/_C.cpython-312-aarch64-linux-gnu.so | grep -oE 'sm[0-9]{2,3}' | sort -u sm100 sm90 ``` Note this happens **even with `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`**. That env var does work — `is_deep_gemm_supported()` returns `False` with it set and `True` without it — but this call site never consults it. A fix that works: guard the call and fall back to `_torch_hc_prenorm_gemm`, which already exists in the same file and implements exactly this contract (`out[0] = x.float() @ fn.t()`, `sqrsum[0] = x.float().square().sum(-1)`); the broadcast shapes line up as-is. It requires a single split, so `n_splits` has to be forced to 1 on the fallback path before the output tensors are allocated. With that patch the model loads all 48 shards and gets past this point. **2. `CutlassScaledMM.is_supported()` ignores compute capability** Past the first issue, DeepseekV4's attention input projections fail: ``` File "vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py", line 493, in _run_parallel_input_projections File "vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/fp8.py", line 461, in apply File "vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/BlockScaledMMLinearKernel.py", line 132, in apply_weights File "vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/cutlass.py", line 320, in apply_block_scaled_mm RuntimeError: dispatch_scaled_mm, /workspace/csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/w8a8/cutlass/c3x/scaled_mm_helper.hpp:17 ``` The selection gate in `kernels/linear/scaled_mm/cutlass.py` is: ```python @classmethod def is_supported(cls, compute_capability: int | None = None) -> tuple[bool, str | None]: if not current_platform.is_cuda(): return False, "requires CUDA." return True, None ``` `compute_capability` is accepted and never used, so the CUTLASS c3x kernel is selected on any CUDA device and then rejects sm_121 in the C++ dispatcher. A Triton implementation exists in the same directory, but `use_triton` on `BlockScaledMMLinearKernel` only affects the input-quantisation step, not the matmul, and there is no env var to override the backend choice. ### Suggested fix Both gates should consult compute capability rather than assuming Hopper/datacenter-Blackwell: - `CutlassScaledMM.is_supported()` should return `False` on architectures without the compiled c3x kernels so selection can fall through to the Triton kernel. - `is_deep_gemm_supported()` should reflect the architectures actually compiled into the extension (currently sm90/sm100), not just the env var — otherwise every DeepGEMM call site needs to be individually correct. - `mhc_pre_broadcast_tilelang` should be guarded like its two siblings regardless. Happy to open a PR for the `mhc_pre_broadcast_tilelang` guard if that shape of fix is acceptable.

signals.title: [Feature]: Support per-request dynamic LoRA scale
signals.text: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch Currently `LoRARequest.lora_scale` is fixed at request creation and baked into the CUDA graph / kernel as a scalar. This prevents: - same-adapter requests in one batch from using different strengths; - adjusting LoRA strength mid-generation. A real ASR service works around this by baking scale into separate adapter copies (one slot per scale). This wastes slots and limits scale to discrete presets. **Proposal:** Add `LoRAScaleState` — a per-request `UvaBackedTensor` (`[max_num_reqs]`) following `SamplingStates`, passed to the LoRA kernel along with `token_to_req`. Effective scale = `base_scale * request_lora_scales[token_to_req[token_idx]]`. No per-token memory, CUDA-graph-compatible. **Evaluation (real adapter + WER A/B):** | Condition | CN mean \|B-A\| | EN mean \|B-A\| | | --- | --- | --- | | off (noise floor) | 0.022% | — | | 1.0 pre-fix | 17.184% | — | | 1.0 post-fix | 0.038% | 0.028% | - 4 adapter slots → 1 slot. - Arbitrary continuous scale values. - Two bugs found & fixed: CUDA graph captured the scale-free kernel variant (`tl.constexpr`), and the all-ones buffer wasn't refreshed. ### Alternatives - **Baking scale into separate adapter copies** (current workaround) — consumes one adapter slot per scale, limited to discrete presets such as `LORA_SCALES=0.5,0.7,0.9,1.0`. - **Storing a per-token scale array** — would require more GPU memory (e.g. 128 KB per batch vs 1 KB per request) and does not follow vLLM V1 persistent-batch style. ### Additional context - Full per-test-set breakdowns and logs are available on request. - Happy to open a PR if this direction is reasonable. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary With `OffloadingConnector` + `CPUOffloadingSpec`, KV blocks are written to host memory correctly but are **never read back** while speculative decoding is enabled. Disabling `--speculative-config` — changing nothing else — makes the same workload serve from the CPU tier immediately. The CPU tier appears not to *retain* entries: `kv_offload_cpu_cache_usage_perc` rises while a request is in flight and returns to `0.0` as soon as the engine goes idle, never accumulating across requests. Lookups run ( `kv_offload_lookup_sync_delay_seconds_count` increments) and always miss, and the `CPU_to_GPU` transfer metric is absent entirely rather than merely small. ## Environment - Intel Arc Pro B70 32 GB, single card, `device_config=xpu`, TP=1 - vLLM built from source, `main` @ `3756bf1e2ba0909500fbe77e03fe02eafb7f7080` - vllm-xpu-kernels @ `4509e9f9791299e24622cb1d4ff63b61cd03925a` - Model: `Vishva007/Qwen3.8-27B-W4A16-AutoRound-GPTQ` — `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, dense, 64 layers with hybrid linear_attn / full_attention, 24 Q / 4 KV heads, head_dim 256, `mtp_num_hidden_layers: 1` - `--dtype float16 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align --max-model-len 179200 --max-num-seqs 8 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --enable-chunked-prefill` - `--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"spec_name":"CPUOffloadingSpec","cpu_bytes_to_use":17179869184}}'` Startup logs this, as expected: ``` Creating offloading spec with name: CPUOffloadingSpec KV offloading: EAGLE/MTP draft attention groups [0, 1, 2, 3] detected. The trailing chunk of these groups will be excluded from offloading due to volatility. ``` Note the fallback at `offloading/scheduler.py:218-219` marks **every** group as an eagle group, because no group self-identifies via `is_eagle_group` on this model (MTP shares the target's weights/KV). ## Reproduction `max_tokens=1` on every request, so wall time is essentially prefill. 1. send prompt A (~29.8K tokens) — cold 2. send A again — GPU prefix-cache hit 3. send 7 distinct ~35K-token prompts — flushes the 179,200-token GPU cache 4. send A again — GPU-evicted; should be served from the CPU tier Host pool is sized so the flush cannot evict A from CPU: 8 prompts × ~1.4 GB ≈ 11.5 GB against a 16 GiB pool, and the run's own `kv_offload_total_bytes_total{GPU_to_CPU}` confirms 11.69 GB stored. ## Results | step | `--speculative-config` MTP **on** | MTP **off** | |---|---|---| | 1. cold | 17.84 s | 16.59 s | | 2. GPU-cached | 1.92 s | 0.74 s | | 4. post-evict | **16.78 s** (recomputed) | **1.61 s** (served) | MTP off, the arithmetic closes exactly: ``` step 4 (CPU fetch) 1.61 s step 2 (GPU cache) 0.74 s ------- difference 0.87 s ≈ kv_offload_load_time_total = 0.851 s ``` ### Metrics, MTP on ``` kv_offload_total_bytes_total{transfer_type="GPU_to_CPU"} = 1.1685986304e+10 (11.69 GB, 24 transfers) kv_offload_total_bytes_total{transfer_type="CPU_to_GPU"} = (absent) kv_offload_store_bytes_total = 1.1685986304e+10 kv_offload_lookup_sync_delay_seconds_count = 10 ``` Per-window `kv_offload_cpu_cache_usage_perc` against `Running`: ``` Running: 0 usage 0.0 Running: 1 usage 0.0844 <- 8.44% of 16 GiB = ~1.45 GB = exactly one prompt Running: 0 usage 0.0 Running: 1 usage 0.0844 Running: 0 usage 0.0 ``` It never exceeded 0.088 across the whole run, so LRU eviction was never in play. ### Metrics, MTP off (only change) ``` kv_offload_total_bytes_total{transfer_type="CPU_to_GPU"} = 1.097662464e+09 (1.10 GB) kv_offload_load_bytes_total = 1.097662464e+09 kv_offload_load_time_total = 0.851 s kv_offload_load_size_count = 1 ``` `kv_cache_size_tokens` also rises 179,200 → 215,647 with the draft model gone, but that only changes how much is evicted, not whether reads happen at all. ## What I ruled out - **Undersized pool.** Usage peaks at one prompt and returns to zero; the pool never fills. Raising 8 GiB → 16 GiB changed nothing. - **A lookup-side off-by-one.** `is_eagle_unverified` widens the query by one chunk only for sliding-window groups (`scheduler.py:695-700`) but applies `num_hit_chunks -= 1` unconditionally (`:733`). This model has no sliding window (`sliding_window="None"`), so the decrement is uncompensated. I patched `:696` to widen for all eagle groups and it made **no difference** — and on reflection an ~18-chunk prompt losing one chunk should produce a partial hit, not a total miss. So this asymmetry looks wrong but is not the cause. - **`offload_prompt_only`.** Already defaults to `True` (`v1/kv_offload/base.py:597`), so the volatile decode tail should already be excluded. The evidence points at the **store/retention** path rather than lookup: entries are written and counted, then not committed for future lookup, so lookups search an empty index. Other `is_eagle_group` sites I have not traced are `scheduler.py:359` (store-side chunk decrement while decoding) and the `is_store_reachable_swa_chunk` gate. ## Ask Is `OffloadingConnector` expected to work with EAGLE/MTP speculative decoding at all, particularly on hybrid Mamba/GDN + attention models? If the volatility handling is meant to exclude only the trailing chunk, something is dropping the whole entry instead. Happy to run instrumented builds — the reproduction is deterministic and takes about three minutes. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Feature]: Map unsupported reasoning_effort values to the nearest level the chat template accepts
signals.text: ## 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch Some chat templates accept only a subset of the reasoning effort ladder and raise a Jinja error on anything else. For example, the official `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` template validates `reasoning_effort` directly against `('xhigh', 'medium', 'low')`, so a request with `high` returns HTTP 400: `Unexpected reasoning effort high. Supported types are xhigh (default), medium, and low.` Meanwhile the `ChatCompletionRequest.reasoning_effort` field accepts the full ladder (`none`/`minimal`/`low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max`), and OpenAI-compatible clients — agent harnesses especially — routinely send `high` or `minimal`. The request validates at the API layer, then fails at template render time. Today the only ways around this are patching vLLM, forking the chat template, or rewriting requests in a fronting proxy. Proposal: let the operator declare the levels the served model's template accepts, and have vLLM remap any other requested value to the nearest supported level: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \ --supported-reasoning-efforts low medium xhigh \ --reasoning-effort-rounding down ``` Semantics (on the ladder `minimal < low < medium < high < xhigh < max`): - `--reasoning-effort-rounding down` (default): highest supported level at or below the requested one; if nothing is at or below, the lowest supported level. With the set above: `high` → `medium`, `minimal` → `low`. - `--reasoning-effort-rounding up`: lowest supported level at or above the requested one; if nothing is at or above, the highest supported level. With the set above: `high` → `xhigh`. - `none` (reasoning disabled) always passes through and cannot be listed in the supported set — the mapping never toggles thinking on or off. - Flags unset → passthrough, exactly today's behavior. - Each distinct (requested → effective) remap is logged once as a warning. The mapping applies at the serving layer (Chat Completions, Responses, and Anthropic Messages APIs), so every derivation path a client uses converges on the same normalization before the template renders. There is in-tree precedent for the underlying concept: the Harmony path keeps its own private `REASONING_EFFORT` mapping in `vllm/entrypoints/openai/parser/harmony_utils.py` because GPT-OSS supports a subset too. This proposal makes the capability declarative and general instead of per-model-family. I have a working implementation (small: one new helper module, two frontend flags, wiring in the chat/responses serving layers, unit tests, docs) and will open a PR if this is welcome. ## Alternatives - **Explicit mapping strings** (`--reasoning-effort-map high=medium,...`): more flexible but more configuration surface and easy to misconfigure; the supported-set + rounding-direction form covers the real cases with two short flags. Could be added later if a concrete need appears. - **Fix in each chat template**: templates come from model repos; operators can't always change them, and every template author would have to re-implement tolerant handling. - **Client-side/proxy rewriting**: works but must be re-implemented per client/proxy and per derivation path (effort can be derived from thinking budgets, explicit fields, etc.). - **Do nothing**: requests keep failing at render time with a template error that's hard to trace back to the offending request field. ## Additional context Observed with an OpenAI-compatible agent harness driving a Qwen3.8 model: the harness derives `reasoning_effort` values (`high`, `minimal`) that the template rejects, and affected turns fail with the HTTP 400 above until the operator patches the server or the requests. Verified end-to-end on `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` (BF16): stock serve 400s on `high` as quoted; with `--supported-reasoning-efforts low medium xhigh` the same request returns 200 with `high` remapped to `medium` (rounding=`down`) or `xhigh` (rounding=`up`, confirmed via the injected reasoning-instructions block in the prompt token count), one warning logged per distinct remap. Also verified `minimal` → `low` (400 → 200) on a community NVFP4 re-quantization of the same model. Note: some third-party re-uploads ship modified templates that alias `high`→`xhigh` themselves; the official template does not, and `minimal`/`max` fail on both.
signals.author: dkrisman

signals.title: [Bug]: OpenAI `strict` flag on tool definitions is rendered into the model-visible chat template, changing tool-call behaviour
signals.text: ### Your current environment vLLM 0.24.0, `Qwen3.6-27B-FP8`, TP=2 (2× RTX 3090), served via `/v1/chat/completions`. Requests below go **directly to vLLM** (no gateway/proxy in the path). ### Describe the bug The request-level `strict` flag on a function definition (`tools[].function.strict`, part of the OpenAI protocol) is passed through to `apply_chat_template()` and therefore serialized verbatim into the `<tools>` block that the model sees. `strict` is a **server-side decoding directive** — vLLM uses it in `vllm/tool_parsers/structural_tag_registry.py::_any_tool_strict()` to decide whether to attach structural tags. It is not part of the JSON Schema the model needs. Leaking it into the prompt makes it model-visible, and the model reacts to it. #### 1. The field reaches the prompt (minimal, fully reproducible) Same request, only `strict` differing, via `/tokenize`: | `tools[0].function.strict` | prompt tokens | |---|---| | absent | 411 | | `false` | 416 | | `true` | 416 | `return_token_strs: true` shows it rendered inside the tools block: ``` ..."required": ["city"]}, "strict": false} </tools> ``` #### 2. It measurably degrades tool calling With a realistic agent payload (24 tools, ~3.8 KB system prompt, a task where calling a tool is optional), `strict: false` causes the model to emit a **malformed tool call as plain text in `content`** — an arguments-only object with no function name and no `<tool_call>` wrapper — instead of a real tool call. `finish_reason` is `stop`, `tool_calls` is empty. Identical request, only `strict` differing, 5 trials each, non-streaming: | `strict` | `tool_calls` | malformed call leaked into `content` | |---|---|---| | absent | **5/5** | 0/5 | | `false` | 0/5 | **4/5** | Example of what lands in `content`: ```json {"command": "cat << 'EOF' > \"$(dirname '$WORKSPACE')/essay.md\"\n...", "description": "Write essay to file"} ``` #### 3. It is semantic, not prompt-length noise Adding a **neutral filler string of the same token cost** to every tool description, with `strict` absent, does *not* reproduce it: | variant (24 tools, 5 trials) | `tool_calls` | |---|---| | `strict` absent | 4/4 | | `strict: false` | **0/4** | | `strict` absent + equal-length filler text | 4/4 | So it is the *meaning* of `"strict": false` in the tools block, not the extra tokens. #### 4. `strict: false` and absent take the identical server-side path `_any_tool_strict()` returns `False` for both, so with `tool_choice="auto"` both skip structural tags: ```python if tool_choice == "auto" and not _any_tool_strict(tools): return None ``` The only difference between the two requests is therefore what the **model** sees. ### Expected vs actual **Expected:** `strict` is consumed by the server to select the decoding strategy and does not appear in the rendered prompt. `strict: false` and an absent `strict` should be behaviourally identical, as the structural-tag code already treats them. **Actual:** `strict` is rendered into `<tools>`, and `strict: false` measurably degrades tool-call formatting relative to omitting the field. ### Where it happens `vllm/renderers/online_renderer.py`: ```python tool_dicts = [tool.model_dump() for tool in request.tools] ... tool_dicts=tool_dicts, # -> apply_chat_template(tools=...) ``` `model_dump()` is called with no `exclude`, so the whole function object — including `strict` — is handed to the chat template, which serializes it into `<tools>`. ### Suggested fix Exclude `strict` from the dicts passed to `apply_chat_template()`. vLLM has already consumed it (`_any_tool_strict()`) before this point, and a chat template has no way to know which fields are protocol-level rather than part of the function schema. ### Notes / limitations - The behavioural degradation (#2) needs a large, realistic tool set. It did **not** reproduce with 2, 3, or 6 tools, nor with the first 16 or 20 tools of the same set — in those cases both variants behave identically. The prompt-leak itself (#1) reproduces minimally with a single tool. - I have not tested >0.24.0. Between v0.24.0 and v0.27.1 I could find no merged PR touching this path (#40894 and #42292 are both already ancestors of v0.24.0). - This may be as much a chat-template question as a vLLM one, but vLLM controls what is passed to the template.

signals.title: [Performance]: DeepEP v2 (ElasticBuffer) finalize_async runs combine synchronously — the shared-expert overlap window is never used
signals.text: ### Report `prepare_finalize/deepep_v2.py` issues the DeepEP v2 (ElasticBuffer) combine **synchronously** at both call sites ([L171](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/41f179b57aa8ab6f634f508128ce1f1efadd0eb1/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/deepep_v2.py#L171), [L390](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/41f179b57aa8ab6f634f508128ce1f1efadd0eb1/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/deepep_v2.py#L390) pass `async_with_compute_stream=False`; the module docstring at [L45](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/41f179b57aa8ab6f634f508128ce1f1efadd0eb1/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/deepep_v2.py#L45) states both modes are synchronous). The modular-kernel orchestration already supports overlapping **shared experts** with finalize (`finalize_async` -> shared experts on the compute stream -> receiver join, `MK_INTERNAL_OVERLAPPED`), but with a synchronous combine that window is fully occupied by the combine itself. For MoE models with a shared expert (DeepSeek-R1/V3), the shared-expert FFN therefore serializes behind the cross-node all-to-all on every MoE layer during decode. ### Prototype + evidence We run DeepSeek-R1-671B (FP8) with `--all2all-backend deepep_v2` under full cudagraphs and prototyped a flag-gated change: combine issued with `async_with_compute_stream=True` (+ `allocate_on_comm_stream`), with `finalize_async` returning a receiver closure that waits the combine event on the compute stream (graph-replay safe). Observations on EP8 (2 nodes x 4 GPUs, TP4xDP2, GB300 / multi-node NVLink): - **Pre-registered A/B** (4 independent server starts in ABBA order; greedy, forced 128 output tokens; steady-state ITL after warmup): **ITL p50 -8.8% @C=1 (15.71 -> 14.32 ms), -5.3% @C=24**; p99 improves similarly (no tail regression). TTFT unchanged (-0.1 ms), as expected for a decode-only change (negative control). - **Correctness**: greedy outputs bit-identical across all four arms (same text hash). Kernel-level: 300 varied-input replays bitwise-equal vs the sync reference, both eager and inside a captured graph. - **Serving traces**: with the flag ON, each combine kernel is overlapped by shared-expert GEMMs for ~9.7 us on average (~22% of combine busy time, consistent across ranks); with it OFF the measured overlap is exactly 0. - **Ablation**: async combine with the event-wait placed *before* the shared-expert GEMMs (offload without overlap) shows ~0 gain - the benefit is true overlap, not stream offload. The per-layer benefit grows with EP size (~13 us/layer @EP4 -> ~18 us/layer @EP32 in isolated microbenchmarks). ### Question Is there maintainer interest in a PR enabling this (initially env-gated, default off, disabled under DBO)? Happy to submit with a CPU contract test plus a bitwise oracle added to the DeepEP v2 GPU test, and to adapt the shape (e.g. always-on) per your guidance.

signals.title: [Bug]: V1 MTP max_model_len skip emits zero token IDs as drafts and causes 0% acceptance
signals.text: ### Your current environment <details> <summary>Environment</summary> ```text vLLM: 0.27.1 Container image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1-x86_64-ubuntu2404 GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120) CUDA: 13.0.2 PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130 FlashInfer: 0.6.16.post3 Model: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 Engine: V1, synchronous scheduling, text-only ``` </details> ### 🐛 Describe the bug In vLLM 0.27.1, `SpeculativeConfig.max_model_len` is now consumed by the V1 legacy GPU model runner. However, when a sequence exceeds the configured drafter limit, the skip path returns zero-valued token IDs with shape `[num_requests, num_speculative_tokens]` instead of returning zero draft tokens for those requests. The scheduler then treats those zeros as real speculative token IDs. On the next step, the target model verifies them, they are rejected, and the metrics continuously report drafted tokens with 0% acceptance. This makes the intended "skip speculation" path perform unnecessary verification work. The current eligibility check also uses the batch-wide `common_attn_metadata.max_seq_len`. Therefore, one over-limit sequence makes speculation stop for every request in the same GPU batch, including otherwise eligible short requests. Related issue: #52258 reports that `max_model_len` was not consumed at runtime in an earlier V1 version. This report is about the behavior after the runtime check was added in v0.27.1. #### Server command ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 \ --language-model-only \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.6 \ --max-model-len 262144 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --max-num-seqs 12 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 24576 \ --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2,"max_model_len":80000}' ``` #### Reproduction 1. Start the server with the command above. 2. Send a normal short request. MTP works and has a healthy acceptance rate. 3. Send a request whose tokenized context is longer than 80,000 tokens (we used approximately 115,000 input tokens). 4. Observe the speculative-decoding metrics during generation. Sampling parameters used by the workload included `temperature=0.1`, `top_p=0.95`, `top_k=20`, and `presence_penalty=1.5`. #### Actual logs A short request immediately before the long-context request shows normal MTP behavior: ```text (APIServer pid=1) INFO 08-18 02:27:46 [loggers.py:310] Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 608.2 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 18.3 tokens/s, Running: 0 reqs, Waiting: 0 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 0.0%, Prefix cache hit rate: 37.6% (APIServer pid=1) INFO 08-18 02:27:46 [metrics.py:120] SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 2.73, Accepted throughput: 0.29 tokens/s, Drafted throughput: 0.33 tokens/s, Accepted: 116 tokens, Drafted: 134 tokens, Per-position acceptance rate: 0.910, 0.821, Avg Draft acceptance rate: 86.6% ``` After the over-limit request enters generation, the draft count continues to increase but every draft is rejected: ```text (APIServer pid=1) INFO 08-18 02:28:16 [loggers.py:310] Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 0.0 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 33.5 tokens/s, Running: 1 reqs, Waiting: 0 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 19.1%, Prefix cache hit rate: 29.2% (APIServer pid=1) INFO 08-18 02:28:16 [metrics.py:120] SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 1.00, Accepted throughput: 0.00 tokens/s, Drafted throughput: 66.99 tokens/s, Accepted: 0 tokens, Drafted: 670 tokens, Per-position acceptance rate: 0.000, 0.000, Avg Draft acceptance rate: 0.0% (APIServer pid=1) INFO 08-18 02:29:26 [loggers.py:310] Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 0.0 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 33.1 tokens/s, Running: 1 reqs, Waiting: 0 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 19.6%, Prefix cache hit rate: 29.2% (APIServer pid=1) INFO 08-18 02:29:26 [metrics.py:120] SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 1.00, Accepted throughput: 0.00 tokens/s, Drafted throughput: 66.19 tokens/s, Accepted: 0 tokens, Drafted: 662 tokens, Per-position acceptance rate: 0.000, 0.000, Avg Draft acceptance rate: 0.0% ``` The drafted throughput is approximately 2x generation throughput, matching `num_speculative_tokens=2`, even though speculation should have been skipped. #### Relevant v0.27.1 code path `GPUModelRunner._input_fits_in_drafter()` checks the batch-wide `common_attn_metadata.max_seq_len` against `effective_drafter_max_model_len`. When the check fails, `GPUModelRunner.sample_tokens()` currently creates: ```python self._draft_token_ids = torch.zeros( 1, device=self.device, dtype=torch.int32 ).expand(len(self.input_batch.req_ids), self.num_spec_tokens) ``` `_get_draft_token_ids_cpu()` then returns those rows as normal lists such as `[[0, 0]]`. `Scheduler.update_draft_token_ids()` assigns that list to `request.spec_token_ids`, so token ID 0 is scheduled and verified as a real draft. #### Expected behavior - An over-limit request should receive an empty draft list (`[]`), so no speculative tokens are scheduled or counted for it. - Ideally, the limit should be checked per request: in a mixed batch, eligible short requests should still use MTP while only over-limit requests skip it. - At minimum, when the entire batch is over the limit, `Drafted throughput` should be zero and there should be no target verification of placeholder token IDs. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Searched existing and past issues. This is related to, but distinct from, #52258. - [x] Reviewed the issue text for credentials, private endpoints, paths, and user data; none are included.

signals.title: [Bug]: MTP spec decode still advances the grammar matcher after termination when a structural tag is built (residual after #44297)
signals.text: ### Your current environment vLLM **v0.27.1**, Qwen3.6-27B-FP8, TP=2 (2× RTX 3090), `--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder`, served via `/v1/chat/completions`. Spec decode enabled with `--speculative-config {"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}`. ### Describe the bug When a structural tag is built for tool calling **and** MTP spec decode is enabled, the grammar matcher is still handed a token after it has terminated: ``` /project/cpp/grammar_matcher.cc:612: Warning: The matcher has terminated after accepting the stop token, but is trying to accept new token with id 198. ``` This looks like a **residual of #44006 / #44297** rather than a regression of it. That fix ("Constrain bitmask and trim grammar advance at the reasoning boundary", merged 2026-07-04) is an ancestor of v0.27.1, and the fatal half is indeed gone — no `Failed to advance FSM`, no `grammar rejected tokens`, no terminated requests, no 500s. But token **198** is the same token that appears in that issue's `grammar rejected tokens [198, 248069]`, and it is still reaching a matcher that has already accepted the stop token. ### Conditions Two things must hold together. Either alone is silent. 1. A structural tag is actually built — i.e. `get_model_structural_tag()` does **not** return early. That needs `strict: true` on some tool, or a `tool_choice` other than `auto`/`none`. 2. Spec decode is enabled. 3 tools, 3 trials per arm, walking that gate. Only `--speculative-config` differs between the two columns; nothing else changed: | `strict` | `tool_choice` | structural tag | warnings, MTP on | MTP off | |---|---|---|---|---| | absent | `auto` | skipped | 0 | 0 | | `false` | `auto` | skipped | 0 | 0 | | `true` | `auto` | **built** | 3 | 0 | | absent | `required` | **built** | 6 | 0 | | `true` | `required` | **built** | 6 | 0 | | absent | named fn | **built** | 6 | 0 | | | | **total** | **21** | **0** | ### Impact Modest, and I want to be accurate about it: **the tool calls themselves were correct 3/3 in all twelve arms in both configurations** (36 requests, worker healthy throughout). At this payload size this is log noise plus wasted matcher work, not wrong output. I have not tried to find a size or shape where it becomes user-visible, so I cannot say it stays harmless. Filing it because it sits in the code path a recently-fixed fatal bug came from, and the warning suggests the trim at the reasoning boundary is not covering every path that advances the grammar under speculative decoding. ### Reproduce Serve the model with `--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder` and `--speculative-config {"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}`, then send any tool-calling request that builds a structural tag — simplest is one tool with `"strict": true` and `tool_choice: "auto"` — and watch the server log. Remove `--speculative-config`, change nothing else, and the warnings stop. Reported separately from #52741, which is about `strict` being rendered into the prompt and is unrelated to decoding; raised there by @gaby, who is seeing these warnings independently.

signals.title: [Performance]: Hybrid + KV offloading discards reusable divergent prefix hits — offloaded boundary state is never consulted
signals.text: ### Proposal to improve performance With hybrid models (Mamba/recurrent + full attention), per-group local prefix hits can diverge under block pressure: the full-attention prefix often survives deeper in HBM than the recurrent state, which can only resume at a boundary where a state snapshot exists. The *correctness* side of this was settled by #46453 → #48425 (reconcile to the boundary every group agrees on) and #50344 (scope divergent hits to capable connectors). What is still left on the floor is *performance*, in both of the two regimes that exist on `main` today: 1. **Store-style connectors (e.g. `OffloadingConnector`) never see the divergent hit.** `supports_divergent_local_hybrid_hits` defaults to `False`, so `Scheduler._get_local_prefix_cache_hit()` uses `get_computed_blocks()` — the common boundary. Everything the full-attention group still holds in HBM above that boundary is re-fetched from the offload store (or recomputed where not offloaded), even though the KV is resident and only the recurrent state at one boundary is missing. 2. **Capable connectors reconcile without a second look.** On the divergent path, when `get_num_new_matched_tokens()` — queried at the *deep* boundary — returns 0, the scheduler falls back to the common boundary (the `hit_diverged and num_external_computed_tokens == 0` branch in `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`) without ever asking whether the connector can back an *intermediate* boundary. In the common write-through setup the offload store holds full per-group chunk sets, i.e. exactly the boundary state needed to keep the deeper hit — but no path ever asks for it. #### Measured impact Measured on v0.27.1, where `OffloadingConnector` still took the divergent-hit path (pre-#50344), with a Nemotron-H-style hybrid (7 recurrent + 1 full-attention KV cache groups, 1408-token offload chunks, CPU offloading, write-through) on H100: - On a revisit/fork workload, whenever the full-attention prefix was resident but the boundary state had been evicted from HBM, the resume depth collapsed from 5632 tokens to 0. - Cost per event: recomputing ~6k tokens ≈ 231 ms, vs ≈ 2.9 ms to load the one full per-group boundary set (~154 MiB H2D) that would have kept the hit — roughly **80×**. On current `main` the same scenario is served by regime 1 instead: correct, but the resident full-attention KV above the common boundary is given up and re-transferred from CPU. #### Proposed fix: backfill the boundary instead of discarding the hit Before reconciling, ask the connector for the deepest boundary at or below the divergent hit whose chunk is offloaded in *every* group. If one exists, keep the local prefix below that boundary and async-load just the boundary chunk (restoring the lagging recurrent state): - a new optional `KVConnectorBase_V1.get_hybrid_backfill_tokens(request, num_computed_tokens) -> (num_local, num_external)`, default `(0, 0)`; - `OffloadingConnector` implements it with a boundary-walk probe over the per-group offload keys, and opts into `supports_divergent_local_hybrid_hits` when every group resumes from a single chunk (uniform chunk size; recurrent groups have a one-chunk window; wider sliding-window and eagle groups keep today's behavior); - the scheduler consults it in the `hit_diverged and ext == 0` branch and otherwise reconciles exactly as today. Draft PR: (linked below.) #### Alternatives considered Re-querying `get_num_new_matched_tokens()` at the reconciled common boundary would also recover the tokens, but it re-transfers the whole `(common, deep]` range that the full-attention group already holds locally, and connector implementations do not currently expect a second query per scheduling pass. #### Related work - #46453 / #48425 / #50344 / #46455 / #48195 — the correctness lineage for divergent hybrid hits; all correctness-scoped, none consult the store below the divergent hit. - #46896 / #51358 — Mooncake-side PRs preserving recurrent boundary state in external stores: the supply side of the same problem; they do not change the scheduler-side discard. ### Report of performance regression _No response_ ### Misc discussion on performance _No response_ ### Your current environment (if you think it is necessary) Measurements taken on v0.27.1 (8× H100 80GB, CUDA), mechanism verified against `main` (d29dc3ab8).

signals.title: [RFC]: Extensible GEMM Epilogue Contracts for Residual, Norm, and Gated Activation Fusion
signals.text:
### Motivation. vLLM has mature linear-kernel selection and several compiler fusion passes, but the kernel interface and the graph-fusion interface do not yet share one typed contract for fusing a producer GEMM with adjacent residual, normalization, scaling, quantization, or gated-activation work. Today a provider is generally selected to produce the linear output, after which model code or a compilation pass applies downstream operations. This leaves two recurring gaps: 1. a provider that can evaluate a valid epilogue while accumulators are still in registers cannot advertise that capability through the same selection path; and 2. correctness constraints around reduction domains and tensor-parallel collective boundaries are encoded in one-off fused modules/patterns instead of one fail-closed contract. This RFC proposes an optional `GemmEpilogueSpec` understood by linear-kernel providers and compiler rewrites. It is not a request to fuse every decoder block or to require one backend. A provider may accept a spec only when it can implement the exact shape, dtype, reduction, aliasing, and distributed semantics; otherwise vLLM uses the existing unfused path. The initial target is the common Transformer structure in which GEMMs are interleaved with residual addition, RMSNorm-style normalization, scaling/quantization, and SwiGLU-like gated activations. Diffusion/omni models are a downstream consumer, but the abstraction belongs in vLLM's kernel boundary if it is sufficiently generic. ### Proposed Change. #### 1. Design principles - Optional and fail closed: existing kernels and model paths are unchanged without a matched spec. - Typed semantics, not arbitrary Python callbacks in the hot path. - Provider-neutral: CUTLASS/CuTe DSL, Triton, FlashInfer, vendor plugins, or native code may implement a capability. - Compiler-aware: a graph pass may request a spec only after matching a proven graph. - TP-aware: a row-parallel partial sum cannot be normalized as though it were the complete tensor before all-reduce. - Numerically explicit: accumulation dtype, cast points, reduction dtype, and output/alias semantics are part of the contract. - Measured enablement: a valid fusion is not automatically faster for every shape/batch. #### 2. Proposed types Illustrative API: ```python class EpilogueOp(Enum): BIAS = "bias" RESIDUAL_ADD = "residual_add" ROW_SCALE = "row_scale" RMS_NORM = "rms_norm" STATIC_QUANTIZE = "static_quantize" SILU_MUL = "silu_mul" class CollectiveBoundary(Enum): NONE = "none" PRE_COLLECTIVE_PARTIAL = "pre_collective_partial" POST_ALL_REDUCE_COMPLETE = "post_all_reduce_complete" @dataclass(frozen=True) class GemmEpilogueSpec: ops: tuple[EpilogueOp, ...] accumulation_dtype: torch.dtype output_dtype: torch.dtype reduction_dtype: torch.dtype | None collective_boundary: CollectiveBoundary auxiliary_inputs: tuple[str, ...] outputs: tuple[str, ...] mutates: frozenset[str] class MMLinearKernel(...): @classmethod def can_implement_epilogue( cls, config, spec: GemmEpilogueSpec ) -> tuple[bool, str | None]: ... def apply(self, layer, x, bias=None, *, epilogue=None, **kwargs): ... ``` The final interface may use specialized subtypes rather than an enum list. The important property is that supported compositions are explicit and inspectable. #### 3. Compiler/provider flow ```mermaid flowchart LR Graph["FX/model graph
GEMM + adjacent ops"] Match["Semantic pattern match
shape, alias, reduction, TP boundary"] Spec["Build GemmEpilogueSpec"] Select["Existing linear-kernel selector"] Cap{"Provider can implement
this exact spec?"} Fused["Provider fused GEMM + epilogue"] Fallback["Existing GEMM
+ existing separate ops"] Verify["Debug/CI reference checks
and benchmark gate"] Graph --> Match --> Spec --> Select --> Cap Cap -->|yes| Fused --> Verify Cap -->|no| Fallback ``` Graph matching remains in compilation/model integration. Kernel providers do not parse arbitrary FX graphs. Providers receive a normalized, validated spec. #### 4. Correct placement around tensor parallelism ```mermaid flowchart TD Col["Column-parallel GEMM
output shard is semantically complete
for shard-local eligible epilogues"] Row["Row-parallel GEMM
rank-local partial sums"] AR["Tensor-parallel all-reduce"] Full["Complete output tensor"] Post["Residual / norm / gated op
when reduction domain is complete"] Col --> Post Row --> AR --> Full --> Post ``` Some operations can run on a shard; others require the full hidden dimension or the globally reduced value. The pattern matcher must encode the mathematical reduction domain. A provider cannot accept `POST_ALL_REDUCE_COMPLETE` work on a rank-local partial accumulator. An implementation may eventually fuse all-reduce plus a post-collective epilogue through a communicator/provider that supports it, but that is a separate capability. This RFC must not move normalization across a collective merely to make a kernel shape convenient. #### 5. Initial supported compositions Start small and evidence-driven. Candidate specs: - GEMM + bias; - GEMM + row scale; - GEMM + static output quantization; - GEMM + residual add when aliasing and broadcast semantics are simple; - paired gate/up projections + SiLU-multiply where the provider exposes a joint output contract; and - post-all-reduce residual/RMSNorm only through an existing correctly placed fused collective capability. RMSNorm inside a GEMM epilogue is valid only if the provider can compute the full required row reduction correctly. A tiled GEMM that sees only part of the normalized dimension must reject the spec or use a proven multi-tile reduction scheme. #### 6. Integration with current kernel selection The current `MMLinearKernel` selection lifecycle already separates: - hardware support; - whether a kernel can implement a layer configuration; - parameter processing; and - execution. Add epilogue capability after ordinary layer compatibility. `--linear-backend` continues to constrain providers. A selected backend may still reject a particular epilogue and execute the ordinary linear path; no new backend should be selected solely because it claims a fusion unless the existing priority/benchmark policy allows it. The contract should also be visible in debug logs/metrics: requested spec, selected provider, rejection reason, and fallback path. #### 7. Numerical and aliasing contract Every supported spec declares: - GEMM accumulation dtype; - when the accumulator is cast; - epsilon and reduction dtype for normalization; - whether residual is read before an output write; - exact broadcasting rules for weights/scales/bias; - output dtype(s), including optional dual output; - allowed non-contiguous inputs; and - mutation/alias behavior for `torch.compile` fake/meta implementations. Tests compare against an independent high-precision reference as well as the existing unfused path. A fusion may be numerically closer to the high-precision reference while not bitwise equal to bf16 eager execution; that must be represented by a declared tolerance and model-level gate, not silently treated as exact. #### 8. Validation matrix Unit/kernel tests: - multiple `M/N/K`, including small decode and larger prefill batches; - bf16/fp16/fp8 inputs and supported accumulation/output dtypes; - contiguous and declared non-contiguous layouts; - bias/residual broadcast cases; - alias/mutation checks under eager and `torch.compile`; - negative tests for unsupported reduction domains/spec orderings; - TP world sizes 1/2/4 with a distributed reference; and - graph pass fallback when no provider accepts the spec. End-to-end tests: - at least one autoregressive decoder block; - one diffusion/omni Transformer consumer if the abstraction is shared downstream; - compilation enabled/disabled; and - output/accuracy gates appropriate to the model. #### 9. Benchmark and enablement policy For each provider/spec/shape regime report: - kernel latency and achieved compute/bandwidth; - kernel launch count; - HBM bytes when measurable; - end-to-end latency/throughput; - compile/capture compatibility; - peak workspace memory; and - numerical results. Enable only where end-to-end evidence supports it. A fusion can regress low-batch execution because fixed scheduling/collective overhead outweighs saved launches. The selector/config may need shape-regime gating rather than a universal boolean. #### 10. Alternatives considered - **Keep adding one-off fused modules.** Fast for a single pattern but duplicates capability, fallback, and correctness logic. - **Rely only on compiler-generated fusion.** Valuable and should remain the first option, but does not expose provider-specific GEMM epilogues or distributed placement semantics uniformly. - **Allow arbitrary Python epilogue callables.** Hard to validate, serialize, select, and support across providers. - **Put the abstraction only in vLLM-Omni.** Diffusion is a motivating consumer, but linear-kernel selection and several relevant fusion passes are upstream vLLM concepts. #### 11. Phased plan 1. Agree on the typed spec and rejection/fallback behavior. 2. Implement one minimal existing capability (for example bias/static scaling) through the contract without changing defaults. 3. Connect one compiler pattern and add debug observability. 4. Add distributed-boundary negative/positive tests. 5. Benchmark one residual/norm or gated-activation composition. 6. Let downstream vLLM-Omni/SGLang work evaluate additional providers separately. ### Feedback Period. At least one week. ### CC List. No specific CC requested; feedback from linear-kernel, compilation, distributed, and quantization maintainers would be valuable. ### Any Other Things. Relevant code and discussions: - vLLM linear-kernel interface and providers: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/main/vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear - `MMLinearKernel` base contract: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/base.py - Existing all-reduce/RMSNorm compilation fusion: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/allreduce_rms_fusion.py - Hardware-agnostic model-definition RFC: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/44219 - vLLM-Omni diffusion kernel optimization RFC: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/3186 - vLLM-Omni diffusion operator-boundary RFC: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/5582 - SGLang CUTLASS dynamic epilogue investigation: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/30809 ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [RFC]: Rank-Skew-Aware Collective Attribution for Tensor-Parallel Serving
signals.text:
### Motivation. Tensor-parallel traces often report a large amount of GPU time inside all-reduce or another collective. That observation alone does not identify the cause. The interval may contain: - useful data transfer limited by the interconnect/backend; - rank-arrival skew, where an early rank waits for a slower peer; - host dispatch or graph-launch skew before the collective; - additional copies/registration imposed by a selected communicator; or - a correctness failure in which ranks issue different collective sequences. These causes require different remedies. Replacing a collective kernel cannot fix time dominated by peer arrival, while reducing host skew cannot raise a genuinely saturated bandwidth ceiling. vLLM has communicator benchmarks and several collective implementations, but it does not expose a common, request/layer-correlated attribution workflow that combines production traces, a message-size-matched zero-skew baseline, and controlled skew injection. This RFC proposes an opt-in profiling facility and offline report that classify collective cost as transfer-dominated, arrival-skew-dominated, mixed, or inconclusive. It complements, but does not duplicate, TP consensus/deadlock work such as #48720: that RFC detects/recoveries collective-sequence failures; this RFC attributes performance when execution is correct. ### Proposed Change. #### 1. Goals - Assign a stable logical ID to sampled TP collectives. - Record per-rank arrival/enqueue and completion evidence without adding a synchronizing collective to the measured hot path. - Run the same operator/message sizes in an isolated calibration benchmark. - Inject controlled rank delay to learn latency sensitivity to skew. - Produce a causally conservative classification with confidence/evidence. - Point optimization work toward host scheduling, batching/parallel policy, overlap, or communicator/backend changes based on the classification. #### 2. Non-goals - Always-on per-collective production tracing. - A new collective implementation. - Automatically changing NCCL algorithms from one trace. - Treating `collective_duration - arrival_skew` as an exact transfer time. - Detecting/recovering mismatched collective sequences (covered by separate reliability work). #### 3. Trace record Illustrative schema: ```python @dataclass(frozen=True) class CollectiveTraceRecord: run_id: str request_class: str step_id: int layer_id: str collective_ordinal: int group_name: str rank: int world_size: int op: str shape: tuple[int, ...] dtype: str payload_bytes: int backend: str execution_mode: str # eager / compile / cuda_graph host_enqueue_ns: int gpu_begin_ns: int | None gpu_end_ns: int | None ``` `(step_id, layer_id, collective_ordinal, group_name)` must be derived from control flow shared by all ranks, not assigned by a rank-local counter that can silently diverge. Trace artifacts are merged after the run. The profiler must not call an extra all-gather/barrier around each measured collective, because that would manufacture or hide the skew being measured. #### 4. Three-source attribution ```mermaid flowchart TD Prod["Sampled production/profile run
per-rank arrival and collective spans"] Base["Isolated calibration
same op, size, dtype, topology, backend"] Inject["Controlled skew sweep
delay one rank by known intervals"] Join["Join by collective signature"] Features["Derived evidence
arrival spread, zero-skew floor,
throughput headroom, skew sensitivity"] Classify{"Conservative classifier"} Wait["Arrival-skew dominated
reduce host/rank imbalance"] Transfer["Transfer dominated
backend/topology/overlap candidate"] Mixed["Mixed
optimize both / change parallel plan"] Unknown["Inconclusive
collect more evidence"] Prod --> Join Base --> Join Inject --> Join --> Features --> Classify Classify --> Wait Classify --> Transfer Classify --> Mixed Classify --> Unknown ``` Evidence sources: 1. **Production arrival spread.** Difference between earliest/latest rank enqueue/readiness for the same logical collective, after clock calibration where needed. 2. **Zero-skew calibration curve.** Latency/throughput distribution for the exact op, payload, world size, topology, backend, and registration mode under synchronized inputs. 3. **Skew-injection curve.** Repeat calibration while delaying selected ranks by controlled intervals. This establishes how the backend's observed span changes when arrival skew is known. The report should not claim an exact decomposition if clocks or execution mode cannot support it. It can still classify when multiple independent measurements agree. #### 5. Clock and execution-mode handling Same-node phase 1 can use a shared host monotonic clock source plus CUDA/CUPTI timestamps, with startup/end calibration and explicit uncertainty. Multi-node support must estimate clock offsets/drift or rely on profiler data with a documented cross-node time base. CUDA graphs require special handling because Python wrappers run at capture rather than each replay. Supported choices include: - graph-node/CUPTI/Nsight evidence correlated to a deterministic collective ordinal; - sampled eager/compile runs for arrival instrumentation plus a separate graph-mode calibration; or - backend profiler callbacks that execute on replay. The report must label evidence as capture-time or replay-time and must not reuse capture timestamps as though they describe every replay. #### 6. Instrumentation modes Proposed modes: - `off` (default): no records or extra state; - `trace`: short, explicitly profiled run with detailed sampled records and NVTX ranges; - `aggregate`: optional low-rate sampled summaries if a provider can supply replay-safe timestamps without synchronization; and - `calibrate`: isolated communicator benchmark plus optional skew sweep. Instrumentation belongs near `GroupCoordinator`/device-communicator dispatch so custom all-reduce, pynccl, symmetric-memory, and platform providers emit the same schema. High-level `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce()` can add request/layer context without owning timing. #### 7. Derived report For each collective signature, report: - call count and total payload bytes; - per-rank enqueue spread distribution; - observed collective span/duration distribution; - calibrated zero-skew p50/p95 and achieved bandwidth; - hardware/topology bandwidth ceiling when available; - skew-injection response curve; - backend/algorithm/registration and graph mode; - classification and confidence; - missing evidence/clock uncertainty; and - suggested next experiment, not an automatic configuration change. Example decision logic (thresholds to be validated, not hard-coded by this RFC): - observed latency near zero-skew calibration and bandwidth near measured ceiling -> transfer-dominated; - observed excess latency tracks arrival spread and injected-skew curve while zero-skew calibration has headroom -> arrival-skew-dominated; - both arrival spread and zero-skew transfer cost are material -> mixed; - mismatched op IDs/call counts -> stop performance attribution and route to correctness/consensus diagnostics; - otherwise -> inconclusive. #### 8. Optimization routing The report maps classifications to candidate work: | Classification | Candidate next steps | | --- | --- | | Arrival-skew dominated | profile host dispatch/pre-collective compute, remove rank-asymmetric work, reduce tiny collective fragmentation, evaluate smaller TP | | Transfer dominated | evaluate backend/algorithm/topology, fusion, overlap, payload/layout, or a different parallel axis | | Mixed | address largest source first; rerun attribution after each change | | Inconclusive | improve clock/replay instrumentation or collect a longer isolated trace | This table is guidance, not an auto-tuner. #### 9. Validation Synthetic tests: - zero injected skew with payload sweep; - fixed delay on one rank and alternating delayed rank; - compute imbalance before a collective; - bandwidth saturation with large payloads; - many small collectives dominated by launch overhead; - custom all-reduce registered/unregistered buffers; - eager, compile, and CUDA-graph replay where supported; and - intentionally mismatched collective IDs to verify handoff to reliability diagnostics. Correctness/safety tests: - `off` adds no hot-path allocation or thread; - profiler emits no additional measured-group collectives; - trace collection cannot change collective order; - bounded buffers drop samples with a counter rather than blocking execution; - artifacts exclude prompt/output tensor contents by default; and - profiler teardown works after request cancellation/error. #### 10. Benchmark plan Use the existing device-communicator benchmark as the calibration entrypoint where possible. Add: - exact production payload list import; - controlled pre-call delay per rank; - output JSON matching the trace schema/signature; - at least two TP world sizes and small/large payload regimes; and - comparison across the communicator(s) available on the test topology. Then run one representative model in trace mode and verify that the tool's classification matches the synthetic regime introduced before selected layers. #### 11. Alternatives considered - **Use only Nsight time inside NCCL.** It identifies where time is observed, not why peers entered at different times. - **Use only an isolated NCCL benchmark.** It gives a ceiling/floor but cannot show whether production ranks arrive together. - **Subtract arrival spread from duration.** Collective protocols overlap waiting and transfer nonlinearly; the result is not a reliable exact decomposition. - **Insert barriers around each collective.** This destroys the phenomenon under measurement and adds overhead. - **Reuse the TP consensus guard.** Collective-count health is valuable but does not quantify healthy-run transfer versus skew cost. #### 12. Phased plan 1. Define schema and add skew injection/output JSON to the communicator benchmark. 2. Add `trace` instrumentation for eager same-node TP behind an explicit profiler option. 3. Build the offline join/classification report with uncertainty. 4. Validate against synthetic known-skew and bandwidth regimes. 5. Add compile/CUDA-graph replay evidence. 6. Consider multi-node clock calibration and low-rate aggregate mode separately. ### Feedback Period. At least one week. ### CC List. No specific CC requested; feedback from distributed, observability, benchmark, and CUDA-graph maintainers would be especially useful. ### Any Other Things. Relevant code and discussions: - High-level TP communication operations: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/communication_op.py - Group/device communicator dispatch: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/parallel_state.py - Custom all-reduce implementation: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/device_communicators/custom_all_reduce.py - Device communicator benchmark: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_device_communicators.py - Complementary TP consensus/deadlock RFC: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48720 ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
