signals.title: Bolins/shm tensor arena
signals.text: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Purpose `MessageQueue.enqueue` (`shm_broadcast.py`) already routes CPU tensors out-of-band via `_reduce_tensor` (protocol-5 `PickleBuffer`, #48442), which removed the dominant cost of the old in-band path — copying tensor bytes into the pickle stream. Two costs remain for a large multimodal `pixel_values` tensor on a TP=N worker: 1. the out-of-band buffer is published **once per node-local reader** (N transport copies for TP=N), and 2. each reader's H2D copies from a **pageable** ZMQ frame (pageable staging + first-touch faults). This PR adds an opt-in **slotted shared-memory tensor arena** that layers *on top of* `_reduce_tensor`: the writer does **one** memcpy into a free slot, every reader takes a **zero-copy view** of the *same* slot (no per-reader transport copy), and the mapping is `cudaHostRegister`-pinned so the H2D is a true DMA. Large contiguous CPU tensors are diverted by `_ArenaPickler.reducer_override`; anything it declines (too small, non-contiguous, or arena exhausted) **falls through to `_reduce_tensor` unchanged**. Net for a ~200 MB image at TP=8: **1 memcpy + 8 pinned DMAs** instead of **8 transport copies + 8 pageable stagings**. The gain scales with TP degree and tensor size, and is zero at TP=1 (no multiproc broadcast) — both now confirmed empirically below. Design doc: `docs/design/shm_tensor_arena.md`. **Safety / scope:** controlled by the `--enable-shm-tensor-arena` / `--no-enable-shm-tensor-arena` CLI flag (`ParallelConfig.enable_shm_tensor_arena`, default on — happy to flip to default-off if preferred); activates only when all queue readers are node-local; the writer **never blocks** (no free/oversized slot → fall back to `_reduce_tensor`, deadlock structurally impossible); slot reuse is gated on an **H2D-completion CUDA event**, so the writer can't overwrite a slot whose async DMA is still in flight — correct under `--async-scheduling`. ## Test Plan A/B against **current `main`**: the baseline arm is the unmodified `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image (`nightly-65b7662d3f…`, includes #48442); the arena arm is the same image plus this PR's four files. A third arm runs this PR's code with `--no-enable-shm-tensor-arena` as a disable-control (must be behaviorally identical to base; also bounds run-to-run noise). Two setups, so the TP axis and the model-realism axis are both covered: 1. **TP-scaling sweep** — Qwen2.5-VL-3B, TP ∈ {1, 2, 4} (ViT MLP dim caps this family at TP≤4), image sizes 512²–3072², 150 prompts @ 2 req/s. 2. **Production-scale VLM** — Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B (ModelOpt NVFP4) on 8×B300, TP ∈ {4, 8}, image sizes 1024²/2048²/3072², 120 prompts @ 1 req/s. Common method: `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random-mm` (openai-chat backend), one image per request at a fixed size per cell, poisson arrivals at a **non-saturated** rate, 20 warmups (excludes the one-time arena pinning), seed 42, **2 repeats per cell**. Built-in negative controls: TP=1 (arena structurally inactive) and 512² images (~3 MB `pixel_values`, below the 8 MB divert threshold). <details> <summary>Repro commands</summary> Server (one per arm × TP; arena arms = same image + this PR's files): vllm serve $MODEL --tensor-parallel-size $TP --max-model-len 32768 \ --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 [--enable-shm-tensor-arena | --no-enable-shm-tensor-arena] Load (per image size HW, per repeat): vllm bench serve --model $MODEL --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \ --dataset-name random-mm --random-mm-bucket-config "{($HW, $HW, 1): 1.0}" \ --random-mm-base-items-per-request 1 --random-mm-limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1}' \ --random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 64 --ignore-eos \ --num-warmups 20 --num-prompts 150 --request-rate 2 --seed 42 \ --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99 --save-result </details> Still outstanding: port the standalone correctness harness (21 checks: byte-exact round-trip incl. bf16, zero-copy sharing, slot lifecycle with per-reader release, event-gated reuse, exhaustion/oversize/non-contiguous fallbacks) into `tests/distributed/test_shm_broadcast.py` alongside the #48442 tests. ## Test Result **Qwen3-VL-235B (NVFP4) on 8×B300 — E2E p99, base → arena (mean of 2 repeats):** | image (`pixel_values` size) | TP=4 | TP=8 | |---|---:|---:| | 1024² (~23 MB) | 1021 → 995 ms (−2.6%) | 1025 → 999 ms (−2.5%) | | 2048² (~96 MB) | 1584 → 1298 ms (**−18.1%**) | 1807 → 1363 ms (**−24.6%**) | | 3072² (~213 MB) | 3340 → 2771 ms (**−17.0%**) | 4132 → 3083 ms (**−25.4%**) | TTFT p99 moves the same direction (TP=8: −21.5% at 2048², −11.9% at 3072²), and at these payload sizes TTFT p50 improves too (TP=8/3072²: 1185 → 948 ms). Request throughput is identical in every cell (rate-limited by design). **TP-scaling sweep (Qwen2.5-VL-3B — separate setup from the table above):** TP=1 and 512² images are neutral (negative controls behave as designed — the arena never activates); gains appear only at TP≥2 with ≥8 MB tensors and grow with TP and size. On this small model the relative effect is larger than the 235B numbers above — up to −34% E2E p99 at 3072²/TP=4 (3020 → 1992 ms) — because the same transport cost is a much bigger fraction of a 3B's per-request time, and at 2 req/s its large-image cells carry queueing that the stall removal also drains. The 235B table above is the more conservative, production-representative measurement. The disable-control arm on this setup bounds noise at roughly ±5% per cell. **Statistical honesty:** with n=2 repeats, individual p99 cells are noisy (the 235B control shows single-cell swings up to ~±17%). The claim rests on the pattern, not any one cell: the arena is ahead in **all 12** TTFT/E2E comparisons across both models, monotonically in TP degree and tensor size — the shape the mechanism predicts (per-reader transport + pageable staging replaced by one memcpy + pinned DMA), and the E2E-tail bias matches head-of-line blocking on co-scheduled decodes. **Summary:** neutral outside the large-image + TP≥2 regime; **~18–25% p99 reduction** inside it on a production-scale VLM. **Process note:** the disable-control caught a bug in an earlier revision of this PR — `--no-enable-shm-tensor-arena` was silently ignored (the gate read `get_current_vllm_config()` outside its context and fell back to the default). Fixed by threading the flag explicitly through the executor; the control was re-validated inert (0 arena activations) before the numbers above. <details> <summary>Historical: original measurement vs the pre-#48442 in-band baseline</summary> Same-seed interactive multimodal workload (uncapped images, TP=4 ×2 workers on one 8-GPU node, ~1.2k aligned requests): TTFT p50 93→89, p90 401→241, p99 1321→862, max 2139→1375 ms; requests >1.5 s: 9→0. These numbers predate #48442 and therefore overstate the delta vs current main; kept only as provenance for the original problem analysis. </details> --- <details> <summary>Essential Elements Checklist</summary> - [x] Purpose of the PR - [x] Test plan — executed (repro commands above); unit-test port to `tests/distributed/` still outstanding - [x] Test results — A/B vs current `main` on two models × TP 1–8, with disable-control - [x] Documentation — `docs/design/shm_tensor_arena.md` </details>

signals.title: [Online quantization] Add targeted online quantization configuration based on user patterns
signals.text: ## Motivation Enable targeted online quantization on specific layers. This includes: - (future PR) preventing silent layer-specific online quantization: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/dc9f845ddc54c1df38fdbce5afe03f9fd15813bd/vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py#L547 ==> should use this API instead (as this hard-coding causes issues, see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48051) - (future PR probably) enable shared expert quantization on checkpoints shipping unquantized shared experts (e.g. useful for evaluation purposes) - Simplify the online quantization API (see e.g. complex pattern `--quantization-config '{"linear":"fp8_per_channel","ignore":["lm_head","re:.*embed_tokens.*","re:.*mlp\\.gate$","re:.*expert.*","re:.*kv_b_proj.*"]}'` to achieve this `targets` feature (e.g. in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49313)) ## Purpose Implements per-layer online quantization through `quantization_config.targets`, which follows the same spec as existing `quantization_config.ignore`. This addresses the [per-layer online quantization RFC](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/50281). Exact layer names, `re:` regex or `fnmatch`-style patterns allow to select different online shorthands per linear or MoE layer names patterns. Implementation details: - unmatched layers remain unquantized, - conflicting matches with `ignore` raise errors, - fused-layer matching is shared by `ignore` and `targets`. Additionally, an info log is added so that users are aware of what online quantization actually does, as: `INFO 08-06 16:35:33 [base_loader.py:106] Quantized 48 layers of types: block_sparse_moe.experts: 24 (from targets: re:.*block_sparse_moe\.experts, fp8_per_tensor); self_attn.o_proj: 24 (from targets: re:.*self_attn\.o_proj, fp8_per_block)` Additionally, Fused projections can now be targeted either by their fused module name (for example, `re:.*self_attn\.qkv_proj`) or by patterns that match every original shard (for example, `re:.*self_attn\.[qkv]_proj)`. This was a TODO: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/81be2e09aebfd1c45b3ed9f73d2850da8a72984c/tests/quantization/test_online.py#L64-L65 Note: **this behavior is now aligned for quark/compressed-tensors/online**. Note: previous ambiguous ignore regex as `re:.*v_proj` that did NOT resolve to `qkv_proj` now do. This is a "breaking" change. These kind of ambiguous patterns should probably not be used. Left to do: - [x] Probably left to an other PR: implement online quantization compatibility with other quantization methods (done in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51392) - [ ] End-to-end test on real model - [ ] Shared experts quantization support - [ ] Shared experts fusion support (in an other PR) ## Test Plan - `pytest tests/quantization/test_online.py -s -vvvvv` (includes new tests) - `pytest tests/quantization/test_config_utils.py -s -vvvvv` (includes new tests for targets case) - `pytest tests/quantization/test_config_utils.py -s -vvvvv` (includes tests for `ignore`/`targets` parity and `should_ignore_layer` refactor correctness) ## Test Result Tests pass. ## Disclosure AI assistance was used to develop this PR.

signals.title: [Core] Disable fuse_allreduce_rms under VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT (non-deterministic under TP)
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #51290. `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` is bit-stable on a single GPU but **non-deterministic under tensor parallelism**: repeating a byte-identical workload against the same engine returns different logprobs (and, on near-ties, different tokens) once `tensor_parallel_size > 1`. The cause is the fused all-reduce + RMSNorm pass (`fuse_allreduce_rms`, a FlashInfer kernel), which reduces in a run-to-run-varying order under TP. It is enabled by `enable_allreduce_rms_fusion()` exactly when `TP > 1` on Hopper/Blackwell with flashinfer, i.e. the regime where batch invariance is expected to hold. This disables the fusion when batch invariance is requested, mirroring the existing `disable_custom_all_reduce = True` guard in `ParallelConfig` (which handles the analogous non-batch-invariant custom all-reduce path). It is an 8-line early return; TP=1 and non-batch-invariant runs are unaffected. ### Relationship to #50505 This is the Hopper/Blackwell-side complement to #50505. On cc≥90 the `fuse_allreduce_rms` pass replaces the TP all-reduce with a FlashInfer fused kernel, bypassing the custom all-reduce that #50505 pins to its deterministic 1-stage path. Disabling the fusion here lets the all-reduce fall through to that path. The two compose: with #50505 the fallback is the fast 1-stage custom all-reduce (~97% throughput); without it, NCCL (see Performance). On A100 the fusion pass is inactive (cc<90), so #50505 alone covers that hardware; this PR is what extends the fix to Hopper/Blackwell. ## Test Plan Run the same workload 8 times against one engine and count distinct bit-exact outputs (from #51290). Requires the `if __name__ == "__main__":` guard because TP>1 uses spawn. ```python import os, itertools os.environ["VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT"] = "1" from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams def main(): llm = LLM(model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct", tensor_parallel_size=4, gpu_memory_utilization=0.9, enable_prefix_caching=True) sp = SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=1, logprobs=20) prompts = [f"{'the quick brown fox ' * 50} item {i}:" for i in range(2000)] runs = [] for _ in range(8): out = llm.generate(prompts, sp, use_tqdm=False) runs.append([(o.outputs[0].token_ids[0], o.outputs[0].logprobs[0][o.outputs[0].token_ids[0]].logprob) for o in out]) groups = [] for i, r in enumerate(runs): if not any(runs[g[0]] == r and g.append(i) is None for g in groups): groups.append([i]) print(f"{len(groups)} distinct bit-exact outputs over {len(runs)} identical runs") if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` ## Test Result Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, H100, vLLM 0.25.1 (the fix function is byte-identical on `main`): | config | distinct bit-exact outputs / 8 | verdict | |---|---|---| | `tensor_parallel_size=1` | 1 | deterministic (unaffected) | | `tensor_parallel_size=4`, before | 8 | non-deterministic | | `tensor_parallel_size=4`, after this PR | 1 | deterministic | With the fix, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` at TP=4 auto-disables the fusion (the `Enabled custom fusions: allreduce_rms` / `Auto-selected flashinfer allreduce` log lines disappear) and the 8 identical runs collapse to a single bit-exact output. Also confirmed on Llama-3.1-70B (dense, TP=4), and the bug reproduces on both 0.20.2 and 0.25.1. ## Performance Disabling the fusion has a throughput cost, confined to `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` + TP>1 (non-batch-invariant runs and TP=1 are unaffected). Decode-heavy generation, TP=4, H100: | model | fusion on (baseline) | fusion off (this PR) | cost | |---|---|---|---| | Qwen2.5-7B (128 x 256 tok) | 18,355 tok/s | 7,450 tok/s | ~2.5x slower | | Llama-3.1-70B (64 x 128 tok) | 1,618 tok/s | 935 tok/s | ~1.7x slower | This cost reflects the NCCL fallback used before #50505. With #50505's deterministic 1-stage custom all-reduce enabled, the all-reduce falls through to that path instead, which runs at ~97% of fused throughput at default dispatch. So the number above is a pre-#50505 artifact, not an inherent cost of this PR. The cost is largest for decode-heavy workloads, where the all-reduce runs every layer per token; prefill-heavy workloads (long prompt, few output tokens) see considerably less. I checked whether a cheaper, performance-preserving fix inside the fused kernel exists, and none does. The fused kernel is nondeterministic by construction, and no config knob restores determinism: - **Backend:** both `mnnvl` and `trtllm` are nondeterministic on 0.25.1 (H100). `mnnvl` (multicast/Lamport) diverges with token flips. `trtllm` (fixed-order fp32 reduction, but Lamport/two-shot) is smaller-magnitude yet still not bit-exact: 8 distinct logprob groups over 8 identical runs (0 token flips that run, but the sub-bit-exact residual still tips near-ties at scale). - **`fp32_acc`:** already `True` by default, insufficient. - **Autotune:** `enable_flashinfer_autotune=False` does not help. The divergence is intra-process (repeated `generate()` against one engine diverge with the kernel selection already fixed), so it is the kernel's runtime reduction order, not autotune selection. - **One-shot:** forcing `use_oneshot=True` overflows the one-shot workspace on large tensors, and the one-shot path is itself nondeterministic on small tensors. So disabling the fusion under BI is the correct trade, consistent with the existing `disable_custom_all_reduce` guard. Performance is recovered by #50505 (the deterministic 1-stage custom all-reduce this PR falls through to). A fully-fused deterministic kernel would only claw back the last few percent over that and is not needed here.

signals.title: [Bugfix][Model] deepseek-vl2: restore original DeepseekV2Config defaults for omitted language_config fields
signals.text: ## Purpose Loading `deepseek-ai/deepseek-vl2-small` (and `deepseek-ai/deepseek-vl2`) currently crashes during model initialization: ``` TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'NoneType' and 'int' ``` at `DeepseekV2Attention.__init__` (`self.kv_lora_rank + self.qk_rope_head_dim`). Working around that surfaces a second failure while loading `embed_tokens`: ``` AssertionError # loaded_weight.shape[output_dim] == self.org_vocab_size ``` Both failures share one root cause. DeepSeek-VL2 checkpoints ship an incomplete `language_config` that relies on the defaults of the *original* DeepSeek-VL2 `DeepseekV2Config` (`vocab_size=102400`, `kv_lora_rank=512`, `qk_nope_head_dim=128`, `qk_rope_head_dim=64`, `v_head_dim=128`). For example, `deepseek-vl2-small`'s `language_config` contains neither `vocab_size` nor `kv_lora_rank`. vLLM does not use the model's remote config; `DeepseekVLV2Config` parses `language_config` with the built-in Transformers `DeepseekV2Config` (`DeepseekVLV2TextConfig`), whose generic defaults differ: - `DeepseekV2Config().vocab_size == 32000` (not 102400) - `DeepseekVLV2TextConfig.kv_lora_rank` is forced to `None` So omitted fields silently resolve to wrong values: 1. `kv_lora_rank=None` makes `ModelConfig.is_deepseek_mla` return `False` (`use_mla=False`); combined with the non-zero `qk_*_head_dim` defaults the decoder falls through to `DeepseekV2Attention`, which computes `kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim` → `None + int` → `TypeError`. 2. `vocab_size=32000` mismatches the checkpoint's 102400-row `embed_tokens`, tripping the assertion in `VocabParallelEmbedding.weight_loader`. This fix restores the original DeepSeek-VL2 defaults **only for fields the checkpoint does not set**, before building the text config: ``` deepseek_vl2_reference_defaults = { "vocab_size": 102400, "kv_lora_rank": 512, "qk_nope_head_dim": 128, "qk_rope_head_dim": 64, "v_head_dim": 128, } for key, value in deepseek_vl2_reference_defaults.items(): language_config.setdefault(key, value) ``` ## Test Plan Serve deepseek-ai/deepseek-vl2-small and confirm it no longer crashes ## Test Result --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.title: [Perf] Cache streaming parser drop metadata
signals.text: ## Summary - cache immutable special-token drop metadata used by streaming parser engines - key the bounded cache by the config and tokenizer content the builder actually reads - verify equivalent per-request parser configs hit the cache ## Why `StreamingParserEngine` is created per request, while its config and tokenizer contents are effectively engine-wide. Each construction currently recompiles escaped special-token regexes and rebuilds the same immutable `LexerShape`. In the originating B200 profile at a batch around 975, parser construction accounted for 1.9% of engine-thread samples, primarily in this builder. The cache is content-keyed rather than object-identity-keyed, so equivalent config instances share an entry and tokenizer special-token changes naturally miss. It is capped at 64 entries. ## Duplicate check I searched open vLLM PRs for `build drop info reasoning parser cache` and `_build_drop_info`. I found no open PR changing or caching this path; the broad search results were unrelated model, parser-regression, and kernel work. ## Measured performance A pinned-hardware Nebius B200 A/B (`qwen35_per_request_patch_ab_2026-08-06.md`) used an Intel Xeon Platinum 8580 host, structured mode, 1,000 concurrency, and 180-second unprofiled runs: - Output throughput was **11,857 → 11,890 tok/s (+0.28%)**, inside the independently measured **0.32% noise floor**; both arms had zero errors. - In separate py-spy captures, `_build_drop_info` fell **1.5% → 0 samples** of the EngineCore main thread. Its `_get_reasoner` parent fell **1.9% → 0.4%**. - `scheduler.schedule` fell **33.5% → 32.0%**, while `gpu_wait` rose **9.7% → 12.1%**, consistent with the removed CPU work becoming main-thread slack on an already GPU-saturated workload. The benchmark used the SafetyKit memo implementation rather than this bounded `lru_cache`, but it memoized the same pure `_build_drop_info` result. The unambiguous result is removal of the targeted parser-construction work; the +0.28% throughput delta is noise, not a claimed serving-throughput win. ## Validation - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine/test_engine.py -q` — 38 passed - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine -q` — 3,738 passed - targeted Ruff check and format hooks — passed - commit-time pre-commit suite — passed The planned Nebius validation adds a serving-level reasoning/tool-call corpus comparison and an A/B/A high-concurrency profile to confirm output identity and reduced parser initialization samples. ## AI assistance This change was prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance. The human submitter must review every changed line, understand and defend the implementation, and run the listed Nebius validation before marking the PR ready.

signals.title: [RFC][Bug Fix][Spec Decode] Require explicit speculative methods
signals.text: This PR removes speculative-method guessing and makes method selection an explicit contract. ## Problem On current `main`, vLLM guesses the speculative method from model path/name substrings such as `eagle3`, `dflash`, and `dspark`. A DFlash or DSpark checkpoint at a neutral training path can therefore be treated as the generic autoregressive `draft_model`, while renaming or moving the same checkpoint changes serving behavior. For example: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \ --speculative-config '{ "model": "/path/to/checkpoints/6", "num_speculative_tokens": 15 }' ``` Previously, this could silently select `draft_model`. In the original end-to-end Qwen3-8B + DFlash reproduction, the misdetected path produced acceptance length 1.02; adding explicit `"method": "dflash"` produced 3.88. Serving a specialized checkpoint through the wrong proposer is worse than requiring an explicit algorithm, so unresolved configurations now fail closed. ## Design - `method` is the sole algorithm selector. It may come from `"method"` in `--speculative-config`, `--spec-method`, or a known checkpoint schema that explicitly declares its algorithm. - There is no method inference from paths, names, checkpoint architectures, structural `model_type`, or other compatible metadata. - `model` only identifies an external draft source; it never selects or validates the method. - Known declarations, currently the speculators format, act as field-wise defaults for settings such as `method`, `num_speculative_tokens`, and PEagle's `parallel_drafting`. Every user-provided field takes precedence independently. - If a legacy or ambiguous checkpoint does not declare its algorithm and the user omits `method`, vLLM raises a clear error instead of falling back to `draft_model`. - Model-free methods—`ngram`, `ngram_gpu`, `suffix`, and `extract_hidden_states`—reject `model`. - Methods backed by an external draft source require `model`. For `custom_class`, it contains the proposer module path. - `mtp` and `dspark` may omit `model` when their weights are embedded in the target checkpoint; otherwise they accept an external draft source. - After method selection, checkpoint metadata may configure the selected implementation. This includes the embedded DeepSeek-V4 DSpark loader and token-count defaults from speculators `speculative_tokens`, `n_predict`, and DFlash/DSpark block layouts. - DFlash reads both top-level and nested `dflash_config.block_size`. DSpark accounts for whether the anchor is sampled. These are defaults only; an explicit `num_speculative_tokens` still wins. - DFlash and DSpark parallel-drafting behavior is enabled by the explicit method. For an embedded DeepSeek-V4 checkpoint, the same checkpoint metadata is handled according to the requested method: `draft_model` keeps the ordinary model loader, `mtp` uses `DeepSeekV4MTPModel`, and `dspark` uses `DSparkDraftModel`. The metadata does not choose among them. ## User experience and breaking change Configurations that relied on implicit path/name matching must add a method. Before: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \ --speculative-config '{ "model": "/path/to/checkpoints/6", "num_speculative_tokens": 15 }' ``` After: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \ --spec-method dflash \ --spec-model /path/to/checkpoints/6 ``` When the DFlash checkpoint exposes its block size, `num_speculative_tokens` defaults from that metadata; users may still set `--spec-tokens` explicitly. A speculators-format draft declares both its algorithm and proposal depth, so this also works without guessing: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \ --spec-model /path/to/speculators-checkpoint ``` For a generic autoregressive draft model, use `method="draft_model"`. Legacy EAGLE/EAGLE3, Medusa, MLP-speculator, and custom-proposer configurations must likewise state their method and external source. Model-free configurations state only the method and its settings: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \ --speculative-config '{ "method": "ngram", "num_speculative_tokens": 5, "prompt_lookup_max": 5 }' ``` The old `"model": "[ngram]"` and `"model": "ngram"` sentinels are rejected. A speculators-format checkpoint used as the top-level model still works without an explicit `--speculative-config`, because its schema declares the algorithm and proposal depth. ## Validation - End-to-end reproduction recorded before this design change: - misdetected `draft_model`: acceptance length 1.02 - explicit `dflash`: acceptance length 3.88 - This PR now rejects the unresolved configuration instead of silently serving it autoregressively. - Full `tests/test_config.py` except the two tests requiring gated `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct` access: 222 passed, 2 deselected. - Focused schema/default regression matrix: 17 passed. - DSpark configuration module: 12 passed. - Full draft HF override module: 11 passed. - Structured-output speculative decoding: 3 passed. - Extract-hidden-states configuration regressions: 2 passed. - All configured pre-commit hooks passed on the changed follow-up files, including Ruff, mypy, Markdown lint, SPDX, and configuration validation. The commit sign-off hook also passed. - GPU model evaluation was not rerun for this configuration follow-up; the earlier DFlash measurement above is retained as the motivating model result. <details> <summary>Commands run</summary> ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_config.py \ -k 'not test_rope_customization and not test_eagle_draft_model_config' .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_config.py \ -k 'spec_model_declaration or block_drafters_default_tokens or speculators_format_declares or speculators_format_preserves' .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/transformers_utils/test_dspark_mla_config.py .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/config/test_speculative_draft_hf_overrides.py .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/v1/structured_output/test_backend_guidance.py::test_grammar_bitmask_with_specdec \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py::test_bitmask_with_padded_invalid_drafts .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_extract_hidden_states.py::test_extract_hidden_states_text_only_config_regression \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_extract_hidden_states.py::test_extract_hidden_states_config_preserves_vlm_text_config .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \ docs/features/speculative_decoding/README.md \ tests/test_config.py \ vllm/config/speculative.py \ vllm/transformers_utils/config.py ``` </details> ## Contribution notes - This is not a duplicate of #47490: that PR preserves auto-detection and validates explicit-method mismatches; this PR removes automatic method selection and fails when neither the user nor a declared schema supplies a method. - This is not a duplicate of #44566: that PR only propagates token depth from a speculators-format draft; this PR changes method-selection semantics while preserving declared token defaults. - This is not a duplicate of #52165: that PR detects embedded DeepSeek-V4 DSpark metadata for routing; this PR keeps the explicit method authoritative and uses metadata only to configure the selected implementation. - AI assistance was used. I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation listed above.

signals.title: [Render][1/n] Paged shared memory storage for mm tensor ipc.
signals.text:
## Purpose Paged shared memory storage for mm tensor ipc. 0. This compares two approaches for IPC of mm tensors: - **Paged shared memory (pshm):** mm tensor → shm → swap_blocks_batch → GPU - **ZMQ RPC:** mm tensor → ZMQ IPC → CPU Buffer → Pin Memory → GPU 1. CPU‑to‑GPU (H2D) bandwidth saturates when transferring 1 MiB blocks, so a page size of 1 MiB is a reasonable choice for shared memory storage. 2. A typical multimodal data payload is around 10 MiB, which is larger than page size of 1 MiB. Therefore, using paged shared memory for storing and transferring mm tensors is practically meaningful. 3. For payloads smaller than one page (e.g., 0.5 MiB), shared memory space is wasted, and the performance is nearly identical to that of ZMQ RPC. Hence, such small payloads offer no practical advantage. 4. Every copy operation along the mm data path introduces overhead, with dynamic memory allocation and pin memory being particularly expensive. Thus, removing the ZMQ IPC → CPU Buffer → Pin Memory steps in the ZMQ RPC path would bring significant performance gains. Supplement↓
### 1. CPU‑to‑GPU (H2D) bandwidth saturates when transferring 1 MiB blocks PTAL: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48936 ### 2. A typical multimodal data payload is around 10 MiB Qwen2VL outputs 10,764 patches when the input is a 1920×1080 image. Stored in bf16, this takes about 24 MiB; stored in uint8 (see #50411), it uses about 12 MiB. ### 3. For payloads smaller than one page (e.g., 0.5 MiB), the performance is nearly identical to that of ZMQ RPC. Hence, such small payloads offer no practical advantage. https://github.com/noooop/snippet/tree/main/benchmarks/pshm/h2d | Scenario | Data Path | ZMQ Usage | |----------|-----------|-----------| | **zmq** | CPU Source → ZMQ Send → ZMQ IPC → ZMQ Receive → CPU Buffer → Pin Memory → GPU | **Transfers full data payload** | | **zmq+shm (copy)** | Shared Memory → CPU Read → Clone → Pin Memory → GPU | **Control only** | | **zmq+shm (no-copy)** | Shared Memory → Zero-copy CPU Read → GPU | **Control only** | ### 4. Removing the ZMQ IPC → CPU Buffer → Pin Memory steps in the ZMQ RPC path would bring significant performance gains. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5ac2684976ee22c04fe0d2f968c6cf6096b383f2/vllm/v1/serial_utils.py#L416-L425
## Test Plan tests/models/multimodal/generation_ppl_test/test_qwen.py::test_pshm ## Test Result Model: Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct mm_device_do_normalize: True VLLM: dtype:torch.bfloat16 head_dtype:torch.bfloat16 41096328.0 Transformers: Constant 41081356.0 Difference (%): 0.03644475610785584 PASSED ---

signals.title: support rl feature : weight checker
signals.text: ## Purpose In the RL training loop: start_weight_update → update_weights* → finish_weight_update, we need to confirm that after the training side pushes/synchronizes the Actor weights to the rollout inference engine, the weights held by the engine are indeed consistent with what we intended to push. Before the training loop begins, check the correctness of the weight-update function to avoid off-policy training crashes. To confirm that this weight update actually landed and was not corrupted or partially written, a reproducible verification mechanism is needed. **weight_checker** is designed for exactly this: it computes a **SHA-256 checksum for each weight tensor of the model** and takes **snapshots (snapshot)** and **comparisons (compare)** before and after the update, so that you can verify ahead of time "whether the weights actually changed / whether they are complete." The four actions that weight_checker depends on: * **snapshot**: Compute a SHA-256 value of the current weights and store it as a baseline * **compare**: Recompute the current SHA-256 values Gang compare them with the snapshot, returning `match` + `mismatches` * **checksum**: Return the current per-tensor SHA-256 values without storing them (idempotent) * **reset**: Randomize the weights after a snapshot, to set up detection of whether a later weight update was correct #[52689](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52689) ## Test Plan A single parameterized test file drives the dev server for each TP setting and verifies: -snapshot returns a structured response with a positive tensor count, and repeated snapshots are consistent. -compare requires a prior snapshot (400 otherwise), matches when weights are unchanged, and still matches after a sleep/wake cycle and after a generate request. -checksum returns per-tensor 64-character SHA-256 digests, is stable across calls, and does not clobber an existing snapshot. -reset rewrite the model weight to check update is correct. -error handling rejects missing/unknown actions cleanly while /health stays up. -world size matches the configured tensor_parallel_size. | Test group | Functional points covered | Priority | | --- | --- | --- | | Snapshot | world size, snapshot behavior | P0 | | Compare | state handling during comparison | P0 | | Checksum | checksum stability and behavior | P0 | | Reset | reset behavior | P0 | | Errors | invalid-request handling | P1 | ## Test Result default test tp=1 and 2 signals.title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Save exact Mamba boundary states
signals.text: ## Summary Fix Mooncake Store persistence for Mamba `align` mode by saving the exact core-selected boundary-state blocks and keeping those physical blocks alive until every worker rank has finished the asynchronous store attempt. This fixes a correctness bug that could persist null, stale/reassigned, or live speculative Mamba state under a valid prefix hash. A later external prefix hit could then restore poisoned recurrent state and produce garbled or runaway output. ## Root cause Mooncake's normal save path resolved each group's source block positionally from a worker-side snapshot of the request's block IDs. That is valid for append-only attention block tables, but a Mamba `align` table is sparse and mutable: - superseded state positions are replaced by the null block and their physical blocks are freed; - speculative scratch blocks are relocated to different logical positions; - the connector's block-ID mirror is append-only and does not observe those in-place changes. Consequently, a positional Mamba save could interpret `NULL_BLOCK_ID` as a physical source, or read a block that had already been freed, reassigned, or was still speculative, while using the correct chained prefix hash as its key. Mooncake's `batch_is_exist` deduplication could then preserve the bad value and prevent a later correct save from replacing it. The production symptom was exposed by the DSpark/EAGLE lookup path landing on an affected interior key. Without that path, a later valid CoW boundary key could win and mask the corruption. ## Design - Core emits exact `(group_id, block_id, boundary_tokens)` entries for committed Mamba `align` boundary states, including the CoW target for a sub-block partial tail. The connector never reconstructs these source IDs positionally. - Mooncake excludes Mamba groups from the normal positional `store_mask`; exact boundary handoffs are the only Mamba writer. The normal path also skips null or missing source IDs for every group as a defense-in-depth guard. - The scheduler claims each accepted physical block with `BlockPool.touch()` before it can be recycled. Consumer-only roles are gated before claiming or queueing handoffs. - Each claimed block receives a monotonic handoff ID. A one-ID/one-pin mapping makes reference release and the bounded in-flight capacity exact, even though a request-level batch ID could work while all entries in a request complete together. - Workers report a cross-rank completion watermark. After seeing its first handoff, a rank reports watermark `0` while that handoff is pending rather than omitting metadata; this prevents aggregation from ignoring a lagging rank and releasing a block early. Dedup, successful upload, pressure drop, cancellation, and store failure are all terminal outcomes for lifetime purposes. - The scheduler releases the connector-owned refs only through `BlockPool.free_blocks()` after the aggregated watermark says every rank is terminal. The configurable in-flight cap bounds pinned GPU blocks if acknowledgements stop; saves beyond the cap remain best-effort and are dropped. - Resumed prefills use the tracked prefill/save boundary, not the request's original prompt length, so replayed generated tokens retain the same cross-group save coverage. - Mamba speculative scratch relocation remains an in-table move, but now fails closed unless `BlockPool.is_block_writable()` confirms the block is non-null, exclusively owned (`ref_cnt == 1`), and unhashed. If shared or pinned speculative blocks become valid in the future, this path must use CoW instead of relocating them. This implementation is intentionally limited to Mamba `align` mode. Mooncake Store's configuration validation rejects incompatible non-align/`all` Mamba layouts; this PR does not add `all`-mode support. ## Retention semantics `VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL` remains effective even though Mooncake's positional `store_mask` is false for Mamba: 1. Core `MambaManager.cache_blocks()` applies the retention policy first. 2. Only retained/materialized states receive a block hash. 3. Handoff emission skips null or unhashed blocks. 4. Mooncake stores the exact retained states from those handoffs. Therefore dense default retention, sparse interval checkpoints, and replay-boundary behavior are preserved. External persistence is still best-effort: an eligible checkpoint may be absent if the handoff cap is reached or the store operation fails. ## Scope and overlap This is not duplicate work: - #50359 validates external lookup boundaries. - #46896 and #46906 concern Mamba all-mode support and retention policy. - #51362 independently adds the same defensive null/missing-block check to Mooncake's normal save loop. That check is included here, but this PR also removes unsafe positional Mamba saving and fixes exact source selection, asynchronous lifetime, retention-aware handoff, partial-tail handling, and speculative ownership. In that sense, this PR subsumes #51362's behavior rather than relying on it. ## Validation Focused Mooncake Store and prefix-cache suites were run through the final design, including exact block-ID handoff, dense and sparse retention, partial tails, resumed prefills, more than two Mamba groups, null/missing sources, consumer skip-save behavior, cross-rank watermarking, bounded pins, failure paths, and exclusive speculative ownership. ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_connector.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_hma_e2e.py ``` Result: 183 passed. Additional focused reruns after the watermark, save-gate, and ownership-invariant changes passed (195 tests), and a broader Mooncake Store + prefix-cache run in the k3-debug container on a GB300 worker passed (219 tests). Ruff and `git diff --check` also passed. Serving/model evaluation on `k3-pd-mooncake aa-lcr`: - post-fix: 0/200 garbled responses; - `llm_judge`: approximately 0.77/0.76; - external prefix hit rate: approximately 91–98%; - pre-fix baseline: garbled/runaway outputs, with `llm_judge` approximately 0.76/0.78. No model kernels or numerical computation were changed. AI assistance was used. The human submitter reviewed the changes and is responsible for understanding, testing, and defending the final submission.

signals.title: [Frontend] Add reusable TP1 initialized-engine snapshots
signals.text: <!-- markdownlint-disable MD013 MD038 MD041 --> ## Purpose RFC #34303 and #37921/#37925 separate in-process CUDA checkpoint primitives from CRIU disk persistence. #35934 explores a CRIU-safe engine lifecycle. #42790, #46089, and #52132 use provider or runtime-sleep boundaries. #40323 tested a pre-model image containing Python imports and a CUDA context. My closed #48996 measured the earlier boundary at about 29.08 seconds ordinary versus 29.09 seconds restored, n=3 per arm. Engine construction still happened after restore. This PR captures a TP1 engine after initialization and a deterministic generation canary, but before HTTP bind. The same-host artifact serves operators who repeatedly activate the same stopped engine. They exchange local disk and host privilege for activation time. ```bash vllm snapshot create MODEL --snapshot-dir PATH --revision MODEL_SHA [serve args] vllm snapshot inspect PATH vllm snapshot restore PATH --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 ``` Restore validates artifact identity before CRIU, then restores the process tree and CUDA state. It binds HTTP only after the public API reproduces the captured token IDs, text, and sampled-token log probability. It fails closed and does not silently fall back to ordinary startup. ## Measured The largest matched campaign used source `5dd888926ffecb2409874810bd07402f3bc7dd3c`, Qwen3-32B BF16 TP1, and one H100 PCIe 80 GB. Model and generated-cache files were fully resident. Compact artifact files were fully evicted before each restore. Each arm ran three times through the first checked public token. | Path | Median activation | Samples | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Ordinary warm process | 54.7029 s | 3 | | Compact snapshot restore | 20.3795 s | 3 | | Reduction | 34.3234 s, 62.7% | 3 per arm | The compact artifact used 5,879,914,496 allocated bytes, about 5.88 GB. Creation took 78.5275 seconds, n=1. The model files remain external and totaled 65,540,298,478 bytes. Counting creation, the measured saving breaks even on the third activation. Every accepted trial returned token ID `12095` and text ` Paris`. Each completed six additional exact-token requests and left no matching process or GPU process. Restore logs contained no CUDA graph recapture markers after the captured boundary. The earlier matched full-state result used Qwen3-0.6B FP16 TP1 with warm local caches, n=5 per arm: | GPU | Ordinary warm process | Full-state restore | Reduction | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | NVIDIA A10 | 23.9121 s | 9.4234 s | 14.4888 s, 60.6% | | RTX 4090 Laptop GPU | 15.7790 s | 5.5488 s | 10.2302 s, 64.8% | On Qwen3-8B FP16 TP1 on the A10, compact state reduced allocated storage by 78.8 percent, from 24,231,231,488 to 5,144,281,088 bytes. Compact restore was 21.2396 seconds versus 23.7633 seconds for full-state restore, median n=3 per path. This cell uses a different model and starting state from the full-state benchmark, so the savings are not additive. Cold or slow model storage can reverse the compact latency result. ## The fix `vllm snapshot create` defaults to compact capture. The existing sleep level 2 lifecycle releases reloadable model and KV state. Creation restores that state, reruns the canary, then releases it again before capture. Restore reconstructs the released state before HTTP bind. `--include-model-state` keeps full state for local or mutable model sources and speculative decoding. It also supports deployments that prefer a larger artifact over model reload. The user contract includes: - strict manifest validation over the supported host, software, model, engine arguments, selected environment, process tree, sockets, and checkpoint tools, - private atomic artifact publication only after a complete dump, - exact token ID and text validation plus a bounded sampled-token log-probability comparison before readiness, - pidfd-pinned ownership for post-restore cleanup, with no signaling from an untrusted numeric PID, - fail-closed rejection of unsupported topology, external established TCP connections, active `io_uring`, mutable compact model sources, and incompatible runtime options, and - no concurrent initialized-snapshot or external CRIU link-remap workflow in the shared `/dev/shm` namespace. ## Review update This revision addresses the four maintainer review points: - The console entry point is `vllm.entrypoints.cli.main:main`. There is no top-level `vllm_bootstrap` package. - Top-level and snapshot-restore parsing happen before runtime imports. `vllm --help` and the useful core surface of `vllm serve --help` stay lightweight, while rich serve help uses the canonical parser. - Snapshot create and restore preserve the caller's complete `VLLM_*` mapping. Restore recomputes the selected environment identity and rejects divergence before calling CRIU. Child-only defaults are passed through a copied subprocess environment. - The official Linux x86-64 runtime image builds pinned CRIU 4.2.1 and its matching CUDA plugin from source. It also builds a pinned Apache-2.0 helper from NVIDIA Dynamo against the public CUDA Driver checkpoint APIs. The install is gated to x86-64, and initialized snapshots remain unsupported on arm64. The obsolete `VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS=1` examples are removed because #51219 is merged. Compact capture is now the default, and `vllm snapshot restore` accepts only the artifact plus frontend bind arguments. The H20 report on the previous public head found three issues. CRIU dump and restore now use `--file-locks`. The documentation includes external package, library, and generated-cache files in the artifact-lifetime contract. GPU identity now comes from the actual CUDA-holder PIDs rather than `nvidia-smi --id=0`. ## Verification The feature patch was rebased onto canonical main at `f1178f3a06fa30a0cc282376924210cedad08c44`. `git range-diff` reported all 56 feature commits unchanged. The resulting head is `f55fd30311b5b6b250ec80b13cceed8aa7d33d02`. Before the pure rebase, a fresh image at feature head `da56fe43ea242bb59c2dd2e3aa64f5536a2a8943` passed a compact-default V2 acceptance cell on one RTX 4090 Laptop GPU, n=1. Creation took 31.1366 seconds and restore took 2.8608 seconds. The public API returned token ID `12095`, text ` Paris`, and sampled-token log probability `-0.42565488815307617`, exactly matching the captured scalar. The image also passed runtime CUDA allocation, CRIU 4.2.1, CUDA checkpoint helper/plugin, `nvcc`, and RDMA-header compile probes. Cleanup left zero containers and zero GPU processes. The H100 campaign observed two sampled-token log probabilities across separate ordinary engine initializations. Raw pre-capture fit gates produced both values before CRIU was involved, while every restore exactly reproduced its captured oracle. A free 4090 control across ordinary and sleep-enabled processes did not reproduce a snapshot-specific difference. The product therefore keeps the captured-engine restore-fidelity contract instead of treating unrelated cross-process numerical variability as a restore failure. ## Test plan Focused verification on the exact current head: ```bash pytest -q \ tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_launch_cli.py \ tests/cuda/test_cuda_compatibility_path.py ``` ```text 54 passed, 1 unchanged base warning ``` The branch adds 16 test functions and 22 collected feature cases, all folded into the existing CLI suite. There is no standalone snapshot test file. The retained cases cover the four maintainer requests, both lifecycle boundaries, the public canary, cleanup, PID ownership, and private paths. They also cover CRIU file locks, GPU identity, TCP preflight, and `io_uring` preflight. Ruff 0.14.0, branch-owned scoped mypy, eight Docker metadata tests, lazy-import checks, Markdown lint, and `git diff --check` passed. The 11 diagnostics from the all-changed-file mypy run reproduce unchanged on the rebased upstream tree. All 56 commits carry DCO signoffs. Upstream [Buildkite #84050](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/84050) and [#84474](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/84474) ran on the pre-rebase head `da56fe43ea242bb59c2dd2e3aa64f5536a2a8943`. In #84474, 242 check contexts passed. The five failed leaf jobs were a PyPI 502 before NIXL tests, a 2-of-4-rank DP rendezvous, a three-GPU allocation for a four-GPU Ray test, a `SYS`-linked H100 pair that NIXL/UCX could not use, and the known Gemma4 CUDA-graph memory failure. The rebase inherits #52441, whose shared Gemma4 CUDA-graph budget applies to both image and video tests; its CPU-retention change is video-specific. No snapshot-specific failure was reported. Full Buildkite coverage on `f55fd30311b5b6b250ec80b13cceed8aa7d33d02` awaits a maintainer trigger. ## Product envelope and tradeoffs - Linux x86-64, one NVIDIA GPU, TP1, PP1, DP1, and prefill-context parallel size 1. - Same trusted host and GPU, with matching driver, kernel, runtime, engine arguments, selected environment, and checkpoint tools. - Compact capture requires an immutable remote model revision. Full-state capture supports local or mutable model sources by retaining model state. - Root or passwordless `sudo`, plus a compatible kernel and NVIDIA driver. - One plaintext HTTP frontend without built-in API authentication, TLS, custom middleware, or a Unix domain socket. - No external established TCP peer at capture and no active `io_uring` descriptors. - A private local artifact that can contain process memory, model state, and secrets. - Package files, shared libraries, model files, and generated-cache roots must remain available for the artifact lifetime. - No cross-host migration, GPU relocation, multi-GPU communicator restore, concurrent restore, or automatic ordinary-start fallback. This is adjacent to, but does not replace, in-process sleep and provider orchestration. The boundary stays narrow because that is where the correctness and hardware evidence stops. AI assistance was used. I take responsibility for the implementation, constraints, and measurements.

signals.title: fix: lazy-import model_hosting_container_standards to prevent log suppression
signals.text: ## Purpose Fix [Bug]: model_hosting_container_standards changes a shared root/vllm handler to ERROR and suppresses vLLM startup logs importing `vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server` triggers a side effect where `model_hosting_container_standards.logging_config` calls `configure_root_logger()` at module level, setting all root handler levels to `ERROR`. When `VLLM_LOGGING_CONFIG_PATH` shares the same handler object between root and `vllm` loggers, this silences vLLM startup INFO/WARNING logs (e.g. chunked prefill diagnostics). The fix defers the `sagemaker_standards_bootstrap` import from module-level into `build_app()` where it is actually called, so the side effect is avoided unless SageMaker integration is actively used. ## Test Plan ```bash VLLM_LOGGING_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/vllm-logging.json \ python - <<'PY' import logging from vllm.logger import init_logger init_logger("vllm.repro") vllm_logger = logging.getLogger("vllm") root_logger = logging.getLogger() import vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server # noqa: F401 # Both handlers should still be INFO (20), not ERROR (40) assert vllm_logger.handlers[0].level == 20, \ f"vllm handler level changed to {vllm_logger.handlers[0].level}" assert root_logger.handlers[0].level == 20, \ f"root handler level changed to {root_logger.handlers[0].level}" print("PASS: handler levels unchanged") PY ``` Test Result Before: vllm handlers: [<StreamHandler <stdout> (ERROR)>] After: vllm handlers: [<StreamHandler <stdout> (INFO)>] ---<details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating supported_models.md and examples for a new model. </details>

signals.title: [Bugfix] Fix DeepSeek V4 mHC broadcast buffer for dummy load
signals.text: ## Purpose With `--load-format dummy`, `load_weights()` is skipped, so `hc_attn_fn_broadcast` stays `None` and the first decoder layer's 2-D broadcast path fails at `assert self.hc_attn_fn_broadcast is not None`. Fix: define a model-level `process_weights_after_loading()` on `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`. The loader invokes this hook for every load format — including dummy load — so the broadcast buffer is always populated before the first forward. The hook also finalizes MegaMoE weights, replacing the lazy `finalize_weights()` call in the MegaMoE forward that existed only to cover dummy load. This takes the branch out of the forward hot path and moves the heavy weight repack (which also frees the original params) out of the first forward, so profiling sees steady-state memory. The EPLB-side guard call in `get_expert_mapping` is unchanged. Because the MTP and DSpark drafters load as their own top-level models (registry → `get_model` → loader → PWAL), each gets a matching hook — the removed forward-time call was their only finalize path under dummy load. The companion fix for weight refit (in-place `copy_()` refresh so the buffer address stays stable for captured CUDA graphs) is split into a separate PR. ## Test Plan ## Purpose With `--load-format dummy`, `load_weights()` is skipped, so `hc_attn_fn_broadcast` stays `None` and the first decoder layer's 2-D broadcast path fails at `assert self.hc_attn_fn_broadcast is not None`. signals.title: [Quantization] Support online quantization with partially pre-quantized checkpoints
signals.text: ## Disclosure AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually. ## Purpose Allow online quantization on the unquantized `linear` or `moe` portions of a partially pre-quantized checkpoint **from ANY `quant_method` (Quark, ModelOpt, compressed-tensors, etc.)**. The original `quant_method` remains responsible for its pre-quantized layers, the composed config applies the requested online method only when the checkpoint returns an unquantized method. Example use cases: - Supersedes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49313 that attempts to do the same for `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4` that quantizes only the MOE layers. - Take e.g. [`nvidia/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-NVFP4`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-NVFP4) (modelopt checkpoint) or [`amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4`](https://huggingface.co/amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4) (quark checkpoint) that apply non-shared MOE expert only quantization, and quantize additional layers as needed (for evaluation or optimization purposes - Relax the need to release several models with different preset pre-quantized layers / different ignore lists). - Eventually, support `shared_experts` online quantization (not in this PR) This PR will work nicely with https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51285 once it is merged. Implementation details: - Online quantization is stored as `QuantizationConfig.online_quant_config`. `QuantizationConfig.get_effective_quant_method` **resolves the global quant method, including both the base checkpoint quant method and the online quant method**. The original `QuantizationConfig` subclass instantiation is preserved (e.g. `Fp8Config`), so **model developers do not need to be aware of this online quantization composition** (see examples below). - Selected layers for `online` that are already pre-quantized fail clearly instead of being silently replaced. - Activation-only overrides remain owned by the original checkpoint quantizer - `quantization_config.ignore` excludes applies only to `online`, as done currently on `main`. Preserving the original checkpoint config type is required for existing model-specific behavior: - Quark Qwen3Next shared-expert fusion reads Quark exclusion metadata and controls fusion: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4f76c8ad9d8ec06e91ac9c84895e07a1913d7726/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_next.py#L81-L98 https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4f76c8ad9d8ec06e91ac9c84895e07a1913d7726/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_next.py#L154-L162 - Kimi K2.5 checks for `CompressedTensorsConfig` before quantizing its multimodal projector: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4f76c8ad9d8ec06e91ac9c84895e07a1913d7726/vllm/model_executor/models/kimi_k25.py#L393-L396 - GLM4.1V selects a compressed-tensors-specific QKV prefix: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4f76c8ad9d8ec06e91ac9c84895e07a1913d7726/vllm/model_executor/models/glm4_1v.py#L303-L308 - Qianfan OCR applies `Fp8Config` visual-layer safety exclusions: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4f76c8ad9d8ec06e91ac9c84895e07a1913d7726/vllm/model_executor/models/qianfan_ocr.py#L69-L92 Behavior change from `main`: `--quantization-config` can now be used with a checkpoint `quant_method` for online weight composition. A request that selects an already pre-quantized layer now fails clearly instead of replacing the checkpoint method. Left to do: - [ ] Real model testing. - [ ] Is `--quantization-config` usage for different `quant_method` (base + online) ok? - [ ] Is `QuantizationConfig.online_quant_config` ok? - [ ] Shared experts online quantization (in an other PR). ## Test Plan Added tests in - `pytest tests/quantization/test_online.py -k test_online_prequantized_compatibility -vvvvv -s` - `pytest tests/quantization/test_online.py -k test_online_prequantized_checkpoint_selected_layer_fails -vvvvv -s` - `pytest tests/quantization/test_online.py -k tinysmokeqwen3moe -vvvvv -s` The tests cover Quark, ModelOpt, and compressed-tensors dispatch; activation-only overrides; online ignore retaining checkpoint quantization; and real tiny compressed-tensors checkpoint conflicts for selected linear and MoE layers. ## Test Result Passes on MI355.

signals.title: [ROCm] Enable fused QK-norm+RoPE+gate Triton kernel for Qwen3-Next/Qwen3.5
signals.text: ## Purpose `Qwen3NextAttention` fuses the gated QKV split + QK-RMSNorm + (partial) NeoX RoPE + gate copy into a single Triton kernel (`fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate`, added in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44176). The kernel is pure Triton and backend-agnostic, but it is gated behind `current_platform.is_cuda()`, so ROCm falls back to the slow multi-op eager path, even though the kernel runs correctly and fast on AMD GPUs. This PR relaxes that one-line guard to `is_cuda_alike()` so ROCm gets the same fusion. It affects the whole `Qwen3NextAttention` family: Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5, Qwen3.5-MoE Measured on MI325X (gfx942), bf16, against the model's real eager branch (`GemmaRMSNorm` + the `rotary_emb` custom op), 300 timed iters after 50 warmup: | Seq len (tokens) | Eager (µs) | Fused (µs) | Speedup | |---|---|---|---| | 1 (decode) | 279.4 | 33.0 | 8.47× | | 8 | 279.3 | 33.6 | 8.32× | | 64 | 281.7 | 33.9 | 8.32× | | 512 | 277.4 | 33.7 | 8.22× | | 4096 | 562.3 | 138.7 | 4.05× | Note: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47719 is an opt-in AITER path that additionally fuses the KV-cache write. ## Test Plan Add a test case in `tests/kernels/core/test_fused_qk_norm_rope.py` ## Test Result ### Benchmarks Measured on MI325X (gfx942), Qwen3.5-4B with `--language-model-only` (bf16). Fused path confirmed active on all 8 full-attention layers vs. off. **Isolated kernel** — `fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate` vs. eager (GemmaRMSNorm ×2 + partial NeoX RoPE + gate copy): | T (tokens) | fused µs | eager µs | speedup | |-----------:|---------:|---------:|--------:| | 1 | 34.1 | 288.3 | 8.45× | | 64 | 34.8 | 288.3 | 8.29× | | 512 | 34.5 | 285.8 | 8.28× | | 4096 | 139.3 | 560.8 | 4.03× | **End-to-end decode throughput (tok/s), fused vs. eager path:** | Batch | eager: ON | eager: OFF | Δ | graphs: ON | graphs: OFF | Δ | |------:|----------:|-----------:|---:|-----------:|------------:|---:| | 1 | 63.1 | 57.2 | +10.3% | 286.9 | 281.1 | +2.1% | | 4 | 239.6 | 219.4 | +9.2% | 956.6 | 937.2 | +2.1% | | 16 | 785.8 | 724.2 | +8.5% | 3113.7| 3060.0| +1.8% | | 64 | 2972 | 2764 | +7.5% | 8875 | 8776 | +1.1% | | prefill 4001 tok | 103.7k | 100.3k | +3.4% | 162k | 165k | ≈ parity | --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.title: [CI] Fix and extend PR/issue auto-labeling
signals.text: ## Purpose Auditing the labeling setup against the actual repo turned up rules that had stopped matching the code they were written for, plus issue-side labeling that covered only 6 of 62 labels. ### Rules that were missing real work - **`deepseek` missed the `vllm/models/` tree.** Newer models live in `vllm/models/<model>/` rather than `vllm/model_executor/models/`. The rule only knew the old location, so only the title match applied — **64 of 99 PRs** touching `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/` went unlabeled. Same gap for `deepseek_v32`. - **`speculative-decoding` missed the Model Runner V2 subtree.** `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/` has seen 94 PRs in 6 months, more than the original `vllm/v1/spec_decode/` at 81. This also folds `dflash` and `dspark` under the umbrella label, per review feedback that both are spec decoding techniques. ### Rules that could never fire Four conditions used `files=` (exact match) with regex syntax, or carried a doubled backslash that YAML passes through literally: ```yaml - files=^examples/features/speculative_decoding/ # never matches - files~=^\\.buildkite/intel_jobs/ # never matches ``` A further 13 conditions pointed at files that have since moved or been deleted — `harmony` moved to the Rust frontend, `pallas` is gone. Repointed where the code moved, removed where it is gone. ### Retired: `new-model` The rule fired on any PR touching a model file **and** `registry.py`. `registry.py` is edited for renames, aliases, refactors and removals, not just additions. Of the 25 most recent PRs carrying the label, 10 added a model. The rest included: - `[Model] Remove Ouro`, `[Model] Remove Plamo2`, `Remove PersimmonForCausalLM and FuyuForCausalLM` — PRs that **delete** models - `[model registry] some simple typos` - `[Perf] Optimize clamp to clamp_`, `[Kernel] ReplaySSM: cache SSM inputs`, `Revert "Blackwell decode optimizations"` Whether a new architecture was registered depends on what changed *inside* `registry.py`. Mergify matches file paths, not diff contents, so this rule cannot be made accurate — tightening the paths does not help. 111 open PRs currently carry the label. The label remains on issues, applied by the New Model template, where the requester states the intent explicitly. ### Rule that fired too often `nvidia` matched `requirements/cuda.txt`, so dependency bumps were tagged as NVIDIA backend work. Measured across 200 merged PRs, 17 carried the label and this was the one clear miss. ### New rules `scheduler`, `kv-cache-manager`, `glm`, `minimax`, `inkling`, `DSv4`, `dflash`, `torch.compile`, `ray`, `vllm-ir`. ### Issue labeling Extended from 6 labels to 31. Terms match **titles only** by design: issue bodies carry pasted `collect_env` output that names unrelated hardware and libraries, which tags the reporter's environment rather than the topic. ### Guard against recurrence `tools/pre_commit/check_label_rules.py` fails when a file condition matches nothing in the tree, and runs via pre-commit when `mergify.yml` changes. It caught two bugs in this change while it was being written. ### Also removed: the New Model issue template `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/600-new-model.yml` is deleted. - Usage fell from 155 issues in 2025 to 30 in 2026, only 3 since July - It applied a label named `new model`, but the label is `new-model`. GitHub silently skips a label that does not exist, so requests went untagged from the March rename onward — five months, unnoticed - 292 of the 304 ever filed are closed - Model support arrives as planned work rather than as community requests `blank_issues_enabled` is `false`, so model requests route to Feature Request. **Nothing applies `new-model` after this change.** The label is left in place so it stays on the 917 PRs and 304 issues carrying it; deleting the label itself is a separate call. ## Before merging **The five new labels must be created first** — `scheduler`, `kv-cache-manager`, `glm`, `minimax`, `inkling`. Mergify errors on a label that does not exist. Two related items a PR cannot do: - `mrv1-only`'s description currently reads "apply only to Model Runner V2 (not applicable to Model Runner V2)" — says V2 twice. - `DSv4` has a rule here mirroring the `kimi`/`k3` split, but whether to keep it as a distinct label is a maintainer call. ## Test Plan Rules were validated against the real file tree and against real issues and PRs, rather than by inspection. ```bash # every file condition in mergify.yml matches at least one tracked file python tools/pre_commit/check_label_rules.py pre-commit run check-label-rules --files .github/mergify.yml pre-commit run ruff-check --files tools/pre_commit/check_label_rules.py pre-commit run ruff-format --files tools/pre_commit/check_label_rules.py ``` ## Test Result ``` tracked files: 6430 rules: 44 file conditions matching >=1 file: 154 file conditions matching NOTHING: 0 Check auto-label rules still match real files............................Passed ruff check...............................................................Passed ruff format..............................................................Passed ``` Negative test: injecting a condition pointing at a nonexistent path makes the check exit 1 and name the offending rule. New rules were spot-checked against the tree — `glm` matches 21 files and correctly ignores `midashenglm.py`, which contains the substring "glm" but is an unrelated model. Issue rules were replayed over 600 real issues: 43% now receive at least one label, and the existing rules agreed with hand-applied labels (`kimi` 35 fires / 31 already labeled, `rocm` 34 / 33, `k3` 27 / 26). No model evaluation is included because this change touches only CI labeling configuration. It does not affect inference, model output, accuracy, or serving. ## Note on AI assistance AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to audit the existing rules, measure PR and issue volumes, and draft these changes. Every measurement quoted above is reproducible with the commands shown. I have reviewed each changed line.

signals.title: [Bugfix][DP] Don't assume the engines started when forwarding a wake
signals.text: Fixes the first of the two problems described in #51476. ## Purpose `DPCoordinator` holds `engines_running`. Front-ends read it through `dp_engines_running()`, and `wait_for_requests_to_drain()` polls it. It is written in two places, and the two writes are not the same kind of claim: - **True** is set when the coordinator *forwards* a wake — `FIRST_REQ` → broadcast `START_DP_WAVE` ([coordinator.py:361](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/engine/coordinator.py#L361)). Nothing is confirmed; the coordinator assumes the engines will act on the broadcast. - **False** is set when DP rank 0 reports `wave_complete`, having observed the group go idle. True is a prediction. False is an observation. The two-phase pause added `ignore_start_dp_wave`: once the ranks reach pause consensus, **every rank discards `START_DP_WAVE`** ([core.py:2054](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/engine/core.py#L2054)). That removes the premise the prediction rests on. A request arriving after `pause_generation(mode="abort")` makes the coordinator set True, no engine steps, no `wave_complete` is ever produced, and the flag stays True for the life of the process. The state is unrecoverable: aborting the request does not help, because nothing makes a paused engine step. `wait_for_requests_to_drain()` can then only end in a `TimeoutError`, and the stale True is published to every front-end, where `add_request_async` skips `FIRST_REQ` because it believes the engines are already running. This is not pause-specific: any mechanism that stops engines from stepping reaches the same state. A request arriving while the engines are `sleep()`ing latches the flag identically, which the second of the two new tests pins down. `_drain_requests_for_elastic_ep` is the only in-tree caller of `wait_for_requests_to_drain`, so that scaling path takes its go/no-go from the same signal. ## Change Stop predicting. Report both edges from where they happen. - `coordinator.py`: the `FIRST_REQ` branch still broadcasts, but no longer claims the result. - `core.py`: rank 0 already reports the True→False edge as `wave_complete`. It now reports False→True from the same place, as the `elif` of that branch, reusing the existing `start_wave` field that the coordinator already interprets as "engines started" ([coordinator.py:436](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/engine/coordinator.py#L436)). The report sits after `self.engines_running = self._has_global_unfinished_reqs(...)`, which is where the engine that received the request actually transitions — an equal-wave `ADD` does not set the flag in `add_request`. Reporting from the top of the busy loop instead reads the previous iteration's value and misses the edge entirely; the first assertion in the pause test exists to catch exactly that. Three guards on the new branch: `not was_running` makes it an edge rather than a per-iteration message; `dp_rank == 0` keeps a single writer, matching the existing `wave_complete` convention; `not pending_pause` excludes the kick-start in phase 1 of the pause protocol, which sets `engines_running = True` only so that an idle rank stops `continue`-ing and reaches the consensus all-reduce. No new message type, no new field, no new socket, and no notion of pausing inside the coordinator. Its `engines_running` becomes rank 0's `engines_running`, one message behind: a single writer, both edges from one source. ### Not #38009 [#38009](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/38009) was rejected for adding per-engine state that diverged across ranks and deadlocked an all-reduce. Here the decision stays in the single coordinator process. The engine side gains one `output_queue.put_nowait` — a report, not a decision — emitted by rank 0 only, after the existing collective has completed. `was_running` is a per-iteration local snapshot: it does not change any rank's participation in any collective, nor any input to `sync_dp_state()`. ### Cost The coordinator now lags engine start by one round trip (broadcast → step → report). Walking every reader of the flag: | path | which copy it reads | effect | |---|---|---| | offline `LLMEngine` (`SyncMPClient`) | its own local copy — `add_request` sets True, `wave_complete` sets False | none; coordinator publishes never reach it | | SPMD / no coordinator | — | none; the new report is gated on `has_coordinator` | | elastic-EP state sync (`elastic_state.py`) | the engine's own `engines_running` | none | | online API server (`DPAsyncMPClient`) | the coordinator's 100ms publish | a second `FIRST_REQ` can be sent inside the lag window, costing one extra broadcast; engines are idempotent there, so it never causes an extra step | | `wait_for_requests_to_drain` | same | can return one round trip early | Measured on 2-way DP + EP with the coordinator instrumented, over four wave starts: **4 `START_DP_WAVE` broadcasts unpatched, 7 patched**, with rank 0 emitting exactly one `start_wave` report per wave start. The extra broadcast is the coordinator's own echo when it processes the report. A burst of 16 concurrent requests produced **one** broadcast in both arms — the client-side `FIRST_REQ` throttle is untouched. The early return trades a false positive that hangs for 300s and cannot recover for a false negative of a few milliseconds, and downstream operations carry their own barrier (`sleep()` contains the pause consensus). That window is not removable in this architecture: an engine that is not stepping cannot report, so any scheme that waits for an acknowledgement re-latches under pause. ## Test Plan Two tests in `tests/v1/distributed/test_async_llm_dp.py`, MoE-only because `enable_wave_coordination` is `model_config.is_moe`, so a dense model never reaches this coordinator state. `test_dp_pause_late_request_does_not_block_drain` has to rule out two different failures, since a signal that is never True satisfies every drain assertion while being useless. It asserts, in order: 1. the engines report themselves as running two seconds into a live request — past the coordinator's 100ms publishes, so the front-end's own optimistic value has been overwritten by then; 2. the flag returns to False when that request finishes; 3. after `pause(mode="abort")` and a late request, the flag first goes True (the latch is armed — otherwise the next assertion is vacuous) and then settles back to False by itself; 4. the late request was held rather than dropped, and completes on resume. `test_dp_sleep_late_request_does_not_block_drain` pins the same latch reached through `sleep()`, with the same arm-then-settle structure, and checks the held request survives `wake_up()`. It is worth guarding separately because it is the shape that reaches `_drain_requests_for_elastic_ep`. ## Test Result All runs on `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (`0.26.1rc1.dev457+gc810e5ee9`) with this diff applied to the image's `site-packages`, each arm printing which variant it loaded. `before` is the unpatched image; `after` is the same image with this change. | suite | before | after | |---|---|---| | `test_async_llm_dp.py -k "dp_pause or dp_sleep"` | **2 failed** / 8 passed | **10 passed** | | `test_engine_core_client.py` (4 GPUs, full file) | 22 passed | 22 passed | | `test_pp_dp_v2.py` (DP=2, PP=2, MoE) | 6 passed | 6 passed | | `test_internal_lb_dp.py` (1 and 4 API servers) | 10 passed | 10 passed | The two `before` failures are exactly the two new tests, each failing on the assertion that the flag settles back to False. Every pre-existing case passes in both arms, including `test_dp_pause_keep_race_staggered_engines` and `test_dp_pause_barrier_request_deadlock`, the all-reduce rendezvous guards. The full `test_async_llm_dp.py` file, with ray installed, is 23 passed / 4 skipped in the `after` arm. Beyond the suites, on 2-way DP + EP: - **Scenarios.** A live request must report True; it must return to False when idle; a late request after `pause(abort)` must settle back; a request admitted microseconds before the pause lands must not strand drain; a request arriving while `sleep()`ing must not latch and must complete on `wake_up()`. All pass. The pause and sleep cases latch on unpatched code — polling for 30s after the late request never observes False, in either flavour. The instrumented coordinator log shows every True paired with a later `wave_complete`, and no True at all while paused or asleep. - **Stress.** 20 rounds alternating `abort`/`keep`/`wait`, varying in-flight request count and how long before the pause lands: 0 hangs, every request completed, identical to baseline. ## Essential Elements - Not a duplicate: no open PR matches `engines_running`, `DPCoordinator drain`, or `pause coordinator`. Filed as part of #51476. - Control-plane only; no effect on model output, so no eval run is included. - AI assistance was used. The submitter has reviewed each changed line and the runs above.

signals.title: [MM][CG][WIP] Encoder CUDA graph support for HunyuanVL
signals.text: ## Summary Encoder CUDA graph support for HunYuanVL (`HunYuanVLForConditionalGeneration`), tracked in #38175. This PR has two parts: 1. **Prerequisite refactor**: `HunYuanVisionTransformer` previously processed images by splitting the batch into a Python list and running each image through every layer separately (`O(num_layers * num_images)` split/cat calls). This packs all images into a single sequence and uses `cu_seqlens`-scoped attention instead, matching the pattern used by Qwen2-VL/Qwen3-VL. Standalone perf win and a prerequisite for graph capture (a per-image Python loop across layers isn't graph-friendly). 2. **`SupportsEncoderCudaGraph` wiring**: HunyuanVL's patch merger reshapes tokens into an explicit `(h, w)` spatial grid per image before a Conv2d-based merge step (per-row newline tokens, begin/end/sep tokens) — it needs the real aspect ratio, not just the token budget, so the "uniform dummy shape per token budget" trick used for Qwen2-VL/Qwen3-VL doesn't directly apply. Resolved by splitting the encoder into two phases: `run_layers` (the packed, `O(num_layers)` transformer stack — a pure function of total token count, no per-image control flow) is what gets captured/replayed; `embed` (positional-embedding interpolation) and `merge` (the conv-based merger) both need each image's real `(h, w)` and stay eager, outside the graph, always. This is a narrower fix than the "secondary capture axis / per-shape graph pool" I originally expected to need — instead of trying to make the shape-sensitive part graph-friendly, it just stays out of the graph entirely, since it's `O(num_images)` rather than `O(num_layers * num_images)` and was never the expensive part. ## Why this isn't a duplicate Checked #38175's checklist and comments, `gh pr list --search "hunyuan"` — no open PR or issue comment claims HunyuanVL for encoder CUDA graph work as of this PR. ## Test plan - [x] `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` pass on the changed file - [x] Standalone (non-vLLM) PyTorch script confirming packed `cu_seqlens`-masked SDPA attention is numerically equivalent to the old per-image split-attention loop (max abs diff ~1.8e-7) - [x] Unit tests: `tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py -k "TestEncoderCudaGraphCaptureReplay or TestEncoderCudaGraphVideoReplay"` — 20 passed - [x] E2E: `tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py -k hunyuan_vl` — image test + eager-vs-cudagraph greedy-decode parity both pass (deterministic token-id match), video skipped (model has no video mode) - [x] Nsight Systems profiling: cudagraph reduces wall time by ~6-8% on the encoder path; see comment below for full methodology and numbers All run on an A100 (driver 570.124.06, CUDA 12.8) with `tencent/HunyuanOCR` (`load_format=dummy` weights, so no download needed to reproduce). ## AI assistance disclosure Portions of this PR (the refactor, the CUDA graph wiring, this description, and the GPU verification/profiling in the comment below) were written and run with AI assistance (Claude). I've reviewed the diff and run the tests and profiling myself.
