signals.title: [ROCm][Perf] Enable fused KDA decode on gfx942 (MI325X)
signals.text: ## Purpose PR #50654 added the fused Kimi-K3 KDA decode kernel (`csrc/libtorch_stable/kimi_k3/fused_kda_decode_kernel_rocm.cu`), but gated it to gfx950 (MI355X) in two places, so it never activates on gfx942 (MI325X): - **Build gate** — `CMakeLists.txt` filtered the HIP source to `gfx950` only, so the kernel was not compiled and `VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_KDA_DECODE` (and therefore `torch.ops._C.fused_kda_decode`) was never defined on a gfx942-only build. - **Runtime gate** — `is_fused_kda_decode_supported()` in `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/ops/kda_decode.py` ended with `return on_gfx950()`. This change extends both gates to gfx942 as well, so MI325X can take the fused decode path instead of falling back to the three-launch Triton path. The kernel body is unchanged. It uses only CDNA-common primitives — wave64, DPP row/quad permutes (`quad_perm`, `row_half_mirror`, `row_mirror`), `__builtin_nontemporal_load/store`, and bf16 intrinsics — with no MFMA / FP8 / gfx950-only paths, so no source-level changes are required for gfx942. LDS use is ~2.8 KiB/block and register pressure ~130 VGPR, both well within CDNA3 limits. ## Changes - `CMakeLists.txt`: HIP arch filter `gfx950` -> `gfx942|gfx950` (and comment). - `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/ops/kda_decode.py`: gate `on_gfx950()` -> `on_gfx950() or on_gfx942()`. - `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_decode.py`: extend the module skip guard from gfx950 to gfx942 / gfx950 so the correctness suite runs on MI325X. All other backends and the CUDA path are unchanged; the shape/dtype/head-count guards in `is_fused_kda_decode_supported()` are unchanged. ## Performance The kernel-level win is large, but the end-to-end win on MI325X is currently small: the Kimi-K3 decode step is dominated by the MXFP4 MoE (int4) and the MLA attention plus the TP8 collectives, which dwarf the KDA linear-attention block. The fusion removes ~66 us of per-layer kernel time (mostly launch overhead), but that is a small fraction of today's total per-token cost. It should become more visible once #50817 (MXFP4 MoE Triton a16w4 for gfx942) lands and shrinks the dominant MoE cost — the fixed KDA saving then represents a larger share of a smaller decode step. ### End-to-end (tp8, 256-in / 256-out, max-concurrency 4) | Metric | Triton fallback | Fused KDA | Delta | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Mean TPOT (ms) | 425.95 | 422.66 | -0.77% | | P99 TPOT (ms) | 427.64 | 424.19 | -0.81% | | Output tok/s | 9.29 | 9.36 | +0.75% | | Mean TTFT (ms) | 1577.24 | 1574.03 | -0.20% (flat) | TTFT is unchanged, as expected for a decode-only kernel. ### Per-layer kernel sequence (torch profiler medians, us) Baseline runs the KDA decode as ~16 separate kernels per layer — the conv1d update, the recurrent delta-rule step, and the gated output RMSNorm decomposed into a chain of launch-overhead-bound (~4 us floor) elementwise ops. Fused collapses all of them into a single kernel: | # | Baseline kernel | us | Fused kernel | us | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | _causal_conv1d_update_kernel | 5.01 | kda_decode_fusion_kernel<true, 12, true, true, true> | 7.77 | | 2 | fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode_kernel | 6.45 | | | | 3 | __amd_rocclr_copyBuffer | 4.37 | | | | 4 | bfloat16->float32 copy | 4.41 | | | | 5 | pow (tensor, scalar) | 4.41 | | | | 6 | reduce Mean | 5.01 | | | | 7 | add | 4.45 | | | | 8 | rsqrt | 4.37 | | | | 9 | mul | 4.21 | | | | 10 | bfloat16->float32 copy | 4.17 | | | | 11 | mul | 4.21 | | | | 12 | bfloat16->float32 copy | 4.45 | | | | 13 | sigmoid | 5.05 | | | | 14 | mul | 4.33 | | | | 15 | float32->bfloat16 copy | 4.49 | | | | 16 | __amd_rocclr_copyBuffer | 4.57 | | | | | **total (16 kernels)** | **~73.96** | **total (1 kernel)** | **7.77** | ~9.5x less kernel time for the KDA decode block (~74 -> 7.8 us/layer). The `12` template arg is 12 heads/rank (96 KDA heads at TP8). Across the model's KDA layers (~69 per the kernel header) that is ~4.6 ms/token of raw kernel time removed, in the same ballpark as the ~3.3 ms/token TPOT drop measured above (the remainder overlaps with other work). ## Not a duplicate - `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "KDA decode gfx942"` - `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "fused_kda_decode MI325"` ## Test Plan Run on an MI325X (gfx942) box after building with gfx942 in the arch list: 1. Build compiles the kernel and registers the op: `python -c "import torch, vllm; print(hasattr(torch.ops._C, 'fused_kda_decode'))"` -> expect `True`. 2. Kernel correctness: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_decode.py -v` 3. Model accuracy (output-affecting change) — serve Kimi-K3 on MI325X and run gsm8k, compared against the Triton fallback path: `make gsm8k` 4. Decode latency / throughput before vs after (fused vs Triton fallback): `make bench-kda-mi325` ## Test Result - Op registered: **True** on the gfx942 build (`hasattr(torch.ops._C, "fused_kda_decode")`); the fused kernel appears in the trace (see Performance). - Latency/throughput: **-0.77% mean TPOT**, +0.75% output tok/s - gsm8k (fused vs Triton): **parity** — both 1.00 exact_match on flexible-extract and strict-match (5-shot, limit=100, stderr 0). The fused kernel matches the Triton fallback exactly. - `test_amd_kda_decode.py`: **12/12 passed** on MI325X (gfx942) — fused output matches the Triton reference across heads {12, 24, 96} x tokens {1, 7, 128}, plus the null-slot, no-output-norm, and padding edge cases. ## Checklist - [x] Compiles for gfx942 (kernel present in the .so with gfx942 codegen) - [x] `test_amd_kda_decode.py` passes on MI325X (12/12) - [x] gsm8k parity with the Triton path - [x] AI assistance used (see below) ## AI assistance This change was drafted with AI assistance (Claude). A human must review every line and run the build, tests, and eval on MI325X hardware before merge; the correctness and accuracy results above are not yet filled in.

signals.title: [LoRA] Avoid false target matches for unsupported module types
signals.text: LoRA target matching previously relied only on module-name suffixes. This can produce false matches when modules with the same suffix have different runtime types. This behavior was reported in [this Gemma 4 LoRA test](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42662#issuecomment-4830505389). The vision tower emitted warnings for modules such as: - `vision_tower.encoder.layers.0.self_attn.o_proj` - `vision_tower.encoder.layers.0.mlp.down_proj` These modules are `Gemma4ClippableLinear` containers and cannot be wrapped directly. However, LoRA was successfully loaded into their inner linear layers: - `vision_tower.encoder.layers.0.self_attn.o_proj.linear` - `vision_tower.encoder.layers.0.mlp.down_proj.linear` The warnings were therefore false alarms caused by suffix-only matching. This PR passes the runtime module instance to `is_supported_lora_module` and checks both the module-name suffix and its actual type. Supported inner linear layers continue to receive LoRA, while unsupported container modules with the same suffix are skipped. ## Purpose ## Test Plan ## Test Result --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.title: [Bugfix] Let an optional Literal flag accept the None it advertises
signals.text: ## Problem `_compute_kwargs` makes an optional field's flag accept `None` by wrapping its type, then advertising the sentinel: ```python if type(None) in type_hints and not contains_type(type_hints, bool): kwargs[name]["type"] = optional_type(kwargs[name]["type"]) if kwargs[name].get("choices"): kwargs[name]["choices"].append("None") ``` but `optional_type` returns the **object** `None`, not the string: ```python def _optional_type(val: str) -> T | None: if val == "" or val == "None": return None return parse_type(return_type)(val) ``` argparse applies `type` **before** it checks `choices`, so the converted value is `None` while the registered choice is `"None"`, and the flag rejects the value its own help text offers: ``` $ vllm serve ... --collect-detailed-traces None error: argument --collect-detailed-traces: invalid choice: None (choose from 'all', 'model', 'worker', 'None') ``` The message is self-contradictory: it lists `'None'` among the valid choices in the same breath as refusing it. The empty string, the other spelling `optional_type` accepts, fails identically. There is no way to pass these flags the value they document, so the only route to `None` is to omit the flag entirely. 16 flags are affected: ``` --kv-role --pooling-type --profiler --safetensors-load-strategy --seq-pooling-type --proton-backend --ssu-algorithm --tok-pooling-type --proton-hook --mm-encoder-attn-dtype --task --proton-output-format --collect-detailed-traces --method --moe-backend --kv-cache-dtype ``` ## Fix Append the sentinel that survives the conversion: ```python kwargs[name]["choices"].append(None) ``` argparse `str()`s choices when it renders help, so `--help` is byte-identical: ``` before: [--collect-detailed-traces {all,model,worker,None}] after: [--collect-detailed-traces {all,model,worker,None}] ``` ## Not a duplicate Searched `argparse_utils`, `load_config_file`, `optional_type`, `choices`, and `"invalid choice"` across open issues and PRs. The nearby open work is on a different defect in a different file: #49057 fixes `false` booleans in YAML configs and #51623 / #52077 handle empty YAML configs, all in `vllm/utils/argparse_utils.py`. This one is in `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py` and is about CLI choices, and this PR does not touch `argparse_utils.py` at all. ## Tests `test_optional_literal_accepts_none_on_the_cli` in `tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py`, built on the `DummyConfig.optional_literal` fixture that file already defines. It pins both spellings `optional_type` accepts, that a real choice still works, and that `None` is still advertised in help, which is what made the rejection contradictory. ``` before after test_optional_literal_accepts_none_on_the_cli FAIL PASS (SystemExit 2) ``` **How it was run.** `python -m pytest tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py` exits 139 on this machine, on a clean tree as well as with this change, because collection segfaults inside native `xgrammar` init. That is unrelated to this PR, so the test body was executed standalone against the real `get_kwargs` and the real `DummyConfig` lifted from the file with `ast`, once against unmodified `arg_utils.py` and once with the change. The 16-flag list above was produced the same way, by running `get_kwargs` over every dataclass in `vllm.config` and reporting fields whose choices contain the string `"None"` but not the object; it goes from 16 to 0 with this change. `ruff check` gains no new findings (the file's 2 pre-existing ones are unchanged) and `ruff format --check` reports both files already formatted. **No model evaluation results.** This changes argument parsing only: nothing about model output, accuracy or serving behaviour moves. The sole behavioural difference is that a value already listed in `--help` is now accepted instead of erroring out, so there is nothing to evaluate. AI assistance was used for this change.

signals.title: [Build] Add CUDA 13.4 prerelease image pipeline
signals.text: ## Summary Add an image-only CUDA 13.4rc1 preview path for initial Rubin enablement: - overlay NVIDIA's `cuda-toolkit==13.4.0rc1` PyPI packages while public CUDA 13.4 container images are unavailable - accept a full PyTorch nightly package-index URL, with `PYTORCH_NIGHTLY=1` retained as a compatibility shorthand - pin the public CUDA 13.4 PyTorch, torchvision, and torchaudio nightlies used by the staging pipeline - use the existing `10.0f` family-compatible build target instead of native `sm_107` - preserve the CUDA driver stub and expose linker names/NCCL needed by native and JIT extensions - install a host C/C++ compiler and point Triton at the preview toolkit's `ptxas` - add a manually gated, multi-arch Buildkite staging pipeline The normal CUDA image and release paths are unchanged unless the preview build arguments are supplied. CUTLASS DSL remains at the repository's existing version because the initial Rubin path uses Blackwell family-compatible kernels; native SM107 support can follow once CUTLASS DSL 4.8 is public. Tracks #49735. ## Duplicate-work check The required issue and open-PR searches found no other PR addressing the CUDA 13.4 preview image path. This does not duplicate the separate SM107 kernel-build and NVLink workstreams tracked by #49735. ## Validation - `pre-commit run --files docker/Dockerfile docker/versions.json .buildkite/cuda134-prerelease-pipeline.yaml .buildkite/test_areas/docker.yaml requirements/cuda134-nightly.txt` — passed - Buildkite YAML parsing with Ruby's standard YAML parser — passed - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tools/test_docker_build_metadata_args.py -v` — 7 passed - live public-source check on 2026-08-18: NVIDIA's CUDA 13.4 base/devel Docker Hub tags return 404; PyPI's latest `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` release is 4.7.0 An earlier ARM64 image from this PR passed vLLM import, CUDA 13.4 `nvcc`/`ptxas`, compiler, driver-link, `torch.compile`, FlashInfer sampling JIT, server-startup, and GSM8K smoke checks. The current head changes the compile target from native SM107 to family-compatible SM100 and still needs the manually gated image build to produce a fresh artifact. The image changes do not intentionally affect model output, so no model evaluation change is expected. ## AI assistance and human accountability OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, review resolution, and validation. The human submitter must review every changed line, understand and defend the image/toolkit design, and verify the fresh staging image before merge.
signals.author: tlrmchlsmth

signals.title: Harden DeepSeek V3.2 fused kernel grids
signals.text: ## Purpose Harden the DeepSeek V3.2 fused Triton kernels against large single-iteration token counts. `fused_norm_rope` and the Triton fallback for `fused_q` placed `num_tokens` on CUDA grid-y. A launch with 65,536 tokens therefore exceeded grid-y's 65,535 block limit and failed with `Triton Error [CUDA]: invalid argument`. This change swaps the token and task grid axes so the unbounded token count is on grid-x. Token indices are promoted to int64 for safe address arithmetic. It does not change the kernel math or the CuTeDSL `fused_q` path. This does not duplicate an existing PR. Searches for the kernel names, DeepSeek V3.2 grid limits, and the 65,535/65,536 boundary found no matching open fix. PRs #52046 and #51915 touch the same kernel file but retain the affected launch grids. OpenAI Codex was used. ## Test Plan - Reproduce both Triton launch failures at 65,536 tokens on NVIDIA B300. - Add minimal public-API regression tests for `fused_norm_rope` and the quantized `fused_q` Triton fallback at the boundary. - Run the complete DeepSeek V3.2 fused-kernel test file on NVIDIA B300. - Run repository pre-commit hooks on the modified files. Model evaluation is not applicable because this only changes launch geometry and program-id mapping; the output computation is unchanged. ## Test Result - Before the fix, both launches succeeded at 65,535 tokens and failed at 65,536 tokens with `Triton Error [CUDA]: invalid argument` on NVIDIA B300. - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v32_norm_rope.py -q` - `52 passed, 14 warnings in 27.33s` - `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v32/common/kernels.py tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v32_norm_rope.py` - All applicable hooks passed. - `git diff --check` - Passed. ROCm hardware was not available for this test run. The modified Triton kernels are shared by the CUDA and ROCm DeepSeek V3.2 paths.
signals.author: yimdev

signals.title: [K3 Perf] Optimize k3 mamba metadata preparation, 6.6~7.6x kernel performance improvement
signals.text: ## Purpose Optimize Kimi K3 Mamba `align` metadata preparation by computing aligned state indices for all KV-cache groups in one Triton launch. Before: ```text prepare_attn -> builder group 0 -> allocate buffer -> launch kernel -> builder group 1 -> allocate buffer -> launch kernel -> builder group N -> allocate buffer -> launch kernel ``` After: ```text prepare_attn -> persistent output buffer -> one multi-group Triton kernel -> directly use the buffer ``` ## Test Acc covered in current unit tests Perf can be seen in this AI generated script ```bash from types import SimpleNamespace import torch from vllm.models.kimi_k3.nvidia.kda_metadata import ( _mamba_get_block_table_tensor, ) from vllm.triton_utils import triton from vllm.v1.worker.mamba_utils import ( get_aligned_state_indices_multi_group_kernel, ) # Decode-only benchmark: one token per request, so tokens == batch size. TOKENS = [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256] NUM_GROUPS = 4 BLOCK_SIZE = 32 MAX_BLOCKS = 1024 BLOCK_ROWS = 32 DEVICE = "cuda" def main() -> None: max_tokens = max(TOKENS) seq_lens = torch.randint( 1, BLOCK_SIZE * MAX_BLOCKS + 1, (max_tokens,), dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE, ) block_tables = [ torch.randint( 0, 1_000_000, (max_tokens, MAX_BLOCKS), dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE, ) for _ in range(NUM_GROUPS) ] block_table_ptrs = torch.tensor( [table.data_ptr() for table in block_tables], dtype=torch.int64, device=DEVICE, ) output = torch.empty((NUM_GROUPS, max_tokens, 1), dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE) spec = SimpleNamespace(block_size=BLOCK_SIZE, num_speculative_blocks=0) print("tokens old (us) new (us) saved (us) speedup") for tokens in TOKENS: current_seq_lens = seq_lens[:tokens] def old( tokens: int = tokens, current_seq_lens: torch.Tensor = current_seq_lens, ) -> None: for table in block_tables: _mamba_get_block_table_tensor( table[:tokens], current_seq_lens, spec, "align" ) def new( tokens: int = tokens, current_seq_lens: torch.Tensor = current_seq_lens, ) -> None: get_aligned_state_indices_multi_group_kernel[ (triton.cdiv(tokens, BLOCK_ROWS),) ]( block_table_ptrs, current_seq_lens, output, block_tables[0].stride(0), current_seq_lens.stride(0), output.stride(0), output.stride(1), output.stride(2), tokens, CACHE_BLOCK_SIZE=BLOCK_SIZE, NUM_GROUPS=NUM_GROUPS, BLOCK_GROUPS=triton.next_power_of_2(NUM_GROUPS), NUM_STATE_SLOTS=1, BLOCK_STATE_SLOTS=1, BLOCK_ROWS=BLOCK_ROWS, num_warps=1, ) expected = torch.stack( [ _mamba_get_block_table_tensor( table[:tokens], current_seq_lens, spec, "align" ) for table in block_tables ] ) new() torch.testing.assert_close(output[:, :tokens], expected) old_us = triton.testing.do_bench(old, warmup=100, rep=500) * 1000 new_us = triton.testing.do_bench(new, warmup=100, rep=500) * 1000 print( f"{tokens:>6} {old_us:>8.2f} {new_us:>8.2f} " f"{old_us - new_us:>10.2f} {old_us / new_us:>7.2f}x" ) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` And we get ```bash tokens old (us) new (us) saved (us) speedup 1 49.76 7.12 42.65 6.99x 2 48.91 7.14 41.77 6.85x 4 48.40 7.14 41.26 6.78x 8 50.25 7.12 43.12 7.05x 16 48.42 7.12 41.30 6.80x 32 47.47 7.12 40.35 6.67x 64 50.72 7.12 43.60 7.12x 128 49.79 7.13 42.66 6.98x 256 53.86 7.13 46.72 7.55x ```

signals.title: [Bugfix][XPU] Skip oneCCL warm-up all_reduce when world_size == 1
signals.text: ## Purpose Skip the oneCCL warm-up all_reduce in `XPUWorker.init_device()` when `world_size == 1`. The warm-up is guarded only by `is_xccl_available()`, so single-device XPU serving still requires a working oneCCL communicator. On platforms where oneCCL cannot enumerate GPU topology this aborts engine startup, even though no collective is issued during inference. Fixes #52386 ## Test Plan - Single XPU (`--tensor-parallel-size 1`): server starts and serves; no behavioral change on hardware where oneCCL already worked, since the communicator is created lazily on first use. - Multi-XPU (`--tensor-parallel-size 2`): warm-up path unchanged. ## Test Result Verified on Intel Arc B390 (Xe3) with `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, TP=1: engine starts, `/v1/chat/completions` returns correct output. Multi-device verification would be appreciated from someone with an Arc Pro B60/B70 system. Multi-device (`--tensor-parallel-size > 1`) is not covered by my hardware. The changed condition is a strict narrowing, so the warm-up still runs whenever more than one worker is present. Verification on an Arc Pro B60/B70 system would be appreciated.
signals.author: studioego

signals.title: [Bugfix] Muse Glimmer: apply structured outputs to the to=user answer
signals.text: ## Purpose `response_format: json_schema` (and other guided-decoding requests) are silently ignored for Muse Glimmer: the model free-generates prose instead of schema-constrained JSON. `json_object` works, so the gap is specific to schema-constrained output. **Root cause:** the structured-outputs backend only applies the grammar after the reasoning parser reports reasoning-end, but `MuseGlimmerReasoningParser.is_reasoning_end` only returned `True` when a *tool* channel opened — a `to=user` final answer was never treated as reasoning-end. On a no-tool request the grammar was therefore never engaged. ## Approach Muse Glimmer's channel handling is kept out of the shared `DelegatingParser`. A dedicated composite `MuseGlimmerParser(DelegatingParser)` (mirroring `KimiK3Parser`) owns the model-specific routing, and grammar activation is separated from stream ownership: - **Grammar activation** lives in `MuseGlimmerReasoningParser.is_reasoning_end`, which the structured-outputs backend calls directly. It fires once the current turn opens any non-`self` channel (the `to=user` answer **or** a `to=<tool>` call), detected on the *last* channel header so a turn that answers the user and then calls a tool is not pinned to the answer channel. This is what lets `response_format` engage on a no-tool request. - **Stream ownership** lives in `MuseGlimmerParser`: `is_reasoning_end_streaming` only transitions the phase machine when a tool channel opens, so the reasoning parser keeps emitting the `to=user` answer body itself and never hands it to the tool parser prematurely (which would otherwise drop the body or leak the channel header). The `tool_choice="none"` and no-tool-parser paths are handled locally in the composite, stripping channel framing rather than leaking it into content. The shared `vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py` and `vllm/reasoning/abs_reasoning_parsers.py` are unchanged, so other models are unaffected. ## Test Plan ```bash # focused unit tests for this fix pytest tests/tool_use/test_muse_glimmer.py tests/tool_use/test_muse_glimmer_parse_delta.py # regression for the shared DelegatingParser / parser registry pytest tests/parser/ tests/reasoning/ ``` E2E against a served `meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B` (bf16, 2x H100) with `--tool-call-parser muse_glimmer --reasoning-parser muse_glimmer`: ```bash SCHEMA='{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"capital":{"type":"string"}},"required":["name","capital"],"additionalProperties":false}' curl -s localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d "{\"model\":\"muse-glimmer\",\"temperature\":0,\"max_tokens\":2048,\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"What is France?\"}],\"response_format\":{\"type\":\"json_schema\",\"json_schema\":{\"name\":\"country\",\"schema\":$SCHEMA}}}" ``` Also tested `response_format: json_object`, plain chat, and `tool_choice` auto/required/named, streaming and non-streaming. ## Test Result **`json_schema`** returns schema-conformant JSON, non-streaming and streaming: ```json { "name": "France", "capital": "Paris" } ``` - Unit tests pass (`tests/tool_use/test_muse_glimmer*.py`). - Live-server E2E: `json_schema` is schema-conformant across several schema shapes, streaming and non-streaming; `json_object`, plain chat, and `tool_choice` auto/required/named remain correct with no channel framing leaked into content. --- This PR was developed with AI assistance. All changed lines were reviewed by the submitter and validated end-to-end on a live Muse-Glimmer-30B server as above. Co-authored-by: OpenAI Codex
signals.author: sid-rp

signals.title: Fix `max_offload_tokens` assertion error.
signals.text: # [Bugfix][KV Offload] Assertion failure when `max_offload_tokens` is below the partial-tail boundary ## Purpose The issue is in `OffloadingConnector` — the native CPU/tiered KV offload path (not P/D disaggregation, not the Mooncake store connector) — on a hybrid Mamba attention model, like the Qwen3.5 series. On those models a physical KV block has to be large enough to hold the Mamba state (e.g. 528 tokens on Qwen3.5-4B at TP1), so a prompt that ends mid-block used to lose everything after the last block boundary. #50507 fixed that by letting the connector store the partial tail: the sub-block piece of a prompt between the last complete block checkpoint, saved under its own key so a later request can reuse it. Separately, a request can cap how much of itself is eligible for offload by setting `max_offload_tokens` in `kv_transfer_params` (`docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md:303-324`). These two features together can cause an issue: a request that sets `max_offload_tokens` can fail an assertion and thus kill the scheduler if that cap is below the partial-tail boundary. `_build_partial_tail_store_jobs` checks the partial-tail boundary against that per-request cap with an assert: ```python max_boundary = min( req.num_prompt_tokens, req_status.max_offload_tokens or req.num_prompt_tokens, ) assert boundary <= max_boundary ``` The boundary is chosen by the core as `(num_prompt_tokens // hash_block_size) * hash_block_size`, and the core has no knowledge of `max_offload_tokens`. So any cap below the boundary fails the assert, leaving an error like: ``` File "vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py", line 1298, in schedule File "vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py", line 1320, in _build_kv_connector_meta File ".../offloading/scheduler.py", line 1476, in build_connector_meta File ".../offloading/scheduler.py", line 1176, in _build_partial_tail_store_jobs AssertionError ``` The same expression has a second bug: `or` treats a falsy `max_offload_tokens=0` as "no cap", but the documented meaning is the opposite — "`0` disables offload for the request entirely" (`docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md:309`). Fix: skip the tail if the boundary exceeds the cap, instead of asserting. ## Test Plan New in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py`: - `test_partial_tail_store_skipped_when_boundary_exceeds_cap[0|16]` — a cap below the boundary, and a cap of `0`, both produce no store job and no pending transfers. - `test_partial_tail_store_honors_cap_at_boundary` — a cap at the boundary still stores, so the fix doesn't disable the feature. `_make_partial_tail_request` gains an optional `kv_transfer_params` argument. The existing `test_max_offload_tokens_validation` can't cover this path: it builds its runner with `blocks_per_chunk=3`, and `supports_partial_tail` requires `blocks_per_chunk == 1`. ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/ -q pre-commit run --files vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py ``` End-to-end, `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B` on 1×L40S: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B --max-model-len 16384 --enforce-eager \ --enable-prefix-caching --prefix-match-unit 16 \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both", "kv_connector_extra_config":{"spec_name":"CPUOffloadingSpec","cpu_bytes_to_use":8000000000}}' ``` then three distinct 1000-token prompts (boundary `1000 // 16 * 16 = 992`), the middle one carrying `"kv_transfer_params": {"max_offload_tokens": 512}`. ## Test Result Unit tests: `254 passed`. ruff-check, ruff-format and mypy-3.12 all pass. End-to-end, HTTP status of the three requests, same script on both builds: | # | request | before | after | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | no cap | 200 | 200 | | 2 | `max_offload_tokens=512` | **500** | 200 | Before the fix, request 2 fails the assertion. After the fix, there's no such issue. Note: parts of this change were written with AI assistance. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Return all choices from /inference/v1/generate when n > 1
signals.text: ## Purpose closes #52398 `serve_tokens` sets `sampling_params.output_kind` only for streaming requests, so non-streaming ones keep the `SamplingParams` default, `CUMULATIVE`. With `n > 1`, `serve_tokens_full_generator` keeps only the last streamed `RequestOutput` and reads `final_res.outputs`, which under `CUMULATIVE` holds just the sequences updated in that step, the other completions are silently dropped. No error is raised; the response is simply short. `CompletionRequest.to_sampling_params` already uses `FINAL_ONLY` when not streaming, so this makes the token-in-token-out path match it. ## Test Plan 10 non-streaming requests per `n` (2, 4, 8) against `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B` on an H100, before and after the patch, counting the choices returned by `/inference/v1/generate`. Same check with multimodal input (`/v1/chat/completions/render` → `token_ids` + `features`, Qwen2.5-VL-3B). Streaming, `logprobs`, `prompt_logprobs` and `n=1` re-checked after the patch. Adds a regression test asserting the response carries indices `0..n-1`. ## Test Result Before: ``` n=2 -> {1: 6, 2: 4} n=4 -> {2: 5, 3: 3, 4: 2} n=8 -> {5: 2, 7: 5, 3: 1, 6: 2} multimodal, n=4 -> 3 choices on 6/6 runs ``` After: ``` n=2 -> {2: 10} n=4 -> {4: 10} n=8 -> {8: 10} multimodal, n=4 -> 4 choices on 6/6 runs ``` `n=1`, streaming, `logprobs` and `prompt_logprobs` behave as before. The measurements were taken on v0.27.1 with this patch applied to the installed package; the added test follows the existing fixtures in `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_tokens.py` and will get its first full run in CI. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.title: [Bugfix][Gemma4] Align parser enable_thinking default with template
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #52410. Gemma4 has two places that need to agree on the effective `enable_thinking` value: 1. The chat template renders the prompt that is sent to the model. 2. The parser interprets the model output and decides whether a new model turn is still inside reasoning. The existing Gemma4 chat template defaults omitted `enable_thinking` to `false`: * `examples/tool_chat_template_gemma4.jinja` uses `enable_thinking | default(false)`. * `docs/features/reasoning_outputs.md` states that Gemma 4 reasoning is disabled by default and can be enabled with `enable_thinking=True`. However, the Gemma4 parser used `chat_kwargs.get("enable_thinking", True)`, so a request that omitted `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking` rendered a non-thinking prompt but initialized the parser as if thinking were enabled. At a new model turn, this caused `is_reasoning_end()` to return `False` for the omitted case, as if thinking were enabled. This PR changes the parser default to `False`, so omitted `enable_thinking` matches explicit `enable_thinking=False` and the existing chat template behavior. Explicit `enable_thinking=True` still enables reasoning. No documentation update is needed because this change aligns the parser with the existing documented and template default. ## Test Plan Update the Gemma4 reasoning parser test to cover all three `enable_thinking` cases at a new model turn: * omitted `enable_thinking` * explicit `enable_thinking=False` * explicit `enable_thinking=True` The expected behavior is: * omitted `enable_thinking` behaves like explicit `enable_thinking=False` * explicit `enable_thinking=True` keeps the existing reasoning-enabled behavior Also run the Gemma4 streaming parser test suite to ensure existing tests that depend on thinking being enabled still pass after making that test setup explicit. ## Test Result ```text python -m pytest tests/reasoning/test_gemma4_reasoning_parser.py -q 31 passed, 14 warnings in 13.68s python -m pytest tests/parser/engine/test_gemma4_streaming_reasoning.py -q 57 passed, 14 warnings in 1.16s ``` Parser-only reproduction after the fix: ```text {} thinking_enabled= False reasoning_ended= True {'enable_thinking': False} thinking_enabled= False reasoning_ended= True {'enable_thinking': True} thinking_enabled= True reasoning_ended= False ``` ## AI assistance This work was produced with AI assistance. The submitter has reviewed every changed line, and the tests above were executed locally.

signals.title: feat: use safetensors prefetch
signals.text: Sister PR: https://github.com/safetensors/safetensors/pull/827 ## Purpose Integrate the new safetensors prefetch API. This is a PoC atm, but performance is promising. #### benchmark setup 4×H100-80GB, local NVMe (8-drive LVM stripe). `load_weights` seconds from the server startup log. Page cache evicted before every round via `posix_fadvise(DONTNEED)`, verified with `fincore`; values are the mean of 2 reps (rep-to-rep spread < 3%). #### results | Model | Arch | GB | Tensors | TP | prefetch cold | fastsafetensors cold | prefetch warm | fastsafetensors warm | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct | dense bf16 | 1.0 | 290 | 1 | 0.52 | 0.98 | 0.34 | 0.67 | | Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct | dense bf16 | 1.0 | 290 | 2 | 0.58 | 0.94 | 0.34 | 0.69 | | Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct | dense bf16 | 29.5 | 579 | 1 | 8.06 | 15.11 | 2.34 | 5.54 | | Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct | dense bf16 | 29.5 | 579 | 4 | 4.67 | 4.41 | 4.15 | 1.70 | | Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct | dense bf16 | 65.5 | 771 | 2 | 8.75 | 16.90 | 5.13 | 6.04 | | Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct | dense bf16 | 65.5 | 771 | 4 | 9.29 | 9.60 | 8.79 | 3.65 | | Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct | dense bf16 | 145.4 | 963 | 4 | 20.21 | 22.42 | 23.21 | 8.51 | | Qwen3-30B-A3B | MoE bf16 | 61.1 | 18867 | 1 | 13.43 | 32.05 | 4.57 | 12.36 | | Qwen3-30B-A3B | MoE bf16 | 61.1 | 18867 | 4 | 8.55 | 10.27 | 8.44 | 7.27 | | Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP4 | MoE NVFP4 | 18.1 | 74835 | 1 | 9.49 | 15.52 | 9.53 | 13.81 | | Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP4 | MoE NVFP4 | 18.1 | 74835 | 4 | 9.81 | 25.07 | 10.22 | 24.29 | | Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8 | MoE FP8 | 239.0 | 73417 | 4 | 35.76 | 36.88 | 41.68 | 27.97 |

signals.title: [Perf] Scale num_warps with tile size in Triton reshape-and-cache kernels
signals.text: ## Purpose Both CUDA launch sites in `triton_reshape_and_cache_flash.py` hardcode `num_warps = 16`, i.e. 512 threads, regardless of tile size. When the tile is smaller than that, the surplus warps hold thread slots without doing work, which limits how many blocks stay resident on an SM. `_reshape_cache_per_token_head` in the same file already derives the count from the shape — `min(16, max(1, head_size_padded // 32))` — as does the CUDA version of this operation (`dim3 block(std::min(num_heads * head_size, 512))`). This PR applies the same rule at the two remaining sites. Only the launch geometry changes; the kernels write the same bytes to the same slots. Tiles of 512 elements or more still get 16 warps, so the shapes the original benchmarks covered are unaffected. ROCm and XPU take a separate branch and are untouched. ## Test Plan ``` pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py -k diffkv ``` The DiffKV kernel had no direct coverage. The new test checks against a PyTorch reference that key and value land in their own halves of the packed cache row, over three `(head_size_k, head_size_v)` pairs, three block sizes, two dtypes and both cache dtypes, and that padded tokens leave the cache untouched. ``` python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_reshape_and_cache_flash.py \ --implementation triton --mode cudagraph --num-heads 2 --head-size 64 ``` `--num-heads 8 --head-size 64` gives n = 512, where both versions launch identically. That row is the control. ## Test Result All 18 tests passed on an A100, on both the patched and the unpatched kernel (18 more skip below SM89, where the Triton fp8 path is unsupported). Latency change on an A100-SXM4-80GB, median of 5 repetitions alternating patched and unpatched, CUDA graph mode. Negative means the patch is faster. Rows are labelled by `n = num_kv_heads * head_size`, the value that sets `TILE_SIZE`. | config | 1024 tok | 4096 | 16384 | 65536 | |---|---|---|---|---| | n=512 (control) | −0.6% | +0.2% | +0.3% | −0.05% | | n=256 | −11.2% | −26.0% | −33.5% | −45.1% | | n=128 | −10.6% | −29.6% | −50.9% | −67.7% | | n=64 | −9.2% | −27.3% | −49.1% | −73.0% | | DiffKV 192/128 (MiMo-V2 shape) | −29.8% | −40.9% | −44.6% | −47.1% | | DiffKV 256/256 | −31.9% | −41.5% | −45.2% | −46.2% | Below ~1000 tokens there are fewer blocks than the GPU has SMs, so nothing overlaps and there is no effect. Above that the gain grows with the token count, because more blocks fit on each SM and more stores are in flight. I ran the kernel comparison three times across two A100 variants; the control stayed within 0.08% each time, and varying the DiffKV cache strides or slot pattern moved the result by less than 0.15 points. ## End-to-end gpt-oss on A100. Sinks need FA3/4, so FlashAttention is out on sm80 and Triton is the only backend vLLM can pick: `Using TRITON_ATTN attention backend out of potential backends: ['TRITON_ATTN']`. `n` is per rank, so TP is what puts gpt-oss in range: 512 at TP=1 (unchanged), 256 at TP=2, 128 at TP=4. Each cell is the mean of 3 runs, each one `llm.generate()` over the whole batch: 128 prompts of 2048 token ids, `max_tokens=1`, prefix caching off. The order alternates per run, and each run asserts that its label matches the `num_warps` line of the source it ran, and that the engine selected TRITON_ATTN. | config | `num_warps = 16` (today) | scaled | delta | |---|---|---|---| | gpt-oss-20b, 2xA100, TP=2, 16384-token steps | 7.2094 s | 7.1951 s | −0.198% | | gpt-oss-120b, 4xA100, TP=4, 16384-token steps | 6.7100 s | 6.6816 s | −0.424% | | gpt-oss-120b, 4xA100, TP=4, 65536-token steps | 6.5420 s | 6.5191 s | −0.349% | In all three, every scaled run was faster than every `num_warps = 16` run. Larger steps do not help. The per-call saving is superlinear in tokens (25.1 us at 16384, 171.4 us at 65536) but the step count falls by the same factor, and the 65536 row came out slightly worse. The DiffKV path has no e2e number; MiMo-V2-Flash does not fit in 4xA100. ## Counters `ncu` on both versions at three shapes, to confirm the change does what it claims and nothing else. Counters only: the container cannot lock clocks, so this ran with `--clock-control none` and the durations from it are not usable. | metric | n=512 (control) | n=128 (TP=4) | DiffKV 192/128 | |---|---|---|---| | `launch__block_size` | 512 → 512 | 512 → 128 (−75%) | 512 → 256 (−50%) | | `launch__waves_per_multiprocessor` | 37.93 → 37.93 | 37.93 → 9.48 (−75%) | 303.4 → 151.7 (−50%) | | `dram__bytes.sum` | −0.1% | −0.1% | −0.1% | | global store sectors | identical | identical | identical | `block_size` matches `min(16, TILE_SIZE // 32) * 32` at all three shapes and the control does not move. Waves per SM track it exactly: smaller blocks leave more of them resident per SM. DRAM bytes and store sectors are unchanged, consistent with the kernels writing the same bytes to the same slots. The correctness argument is the new test rather than these counters, and for the same reason I did not run accuracy evals. <details> <summary>DiffKV benchmark script</summary> ```python import random, time import torch from vllm.v1.attention.ops.triton_reshape_and_cache_flash import ( triton_reshape_and_cache_flash_diffkv, ) NUM_HEADS, DK, DV, BLOCK, NUM_BLOCKS, ITERS = 8, 192, 128, 16, 8192, 200 def run(num_tokens): torch.manual_seed(42) random.seed(42) dev, dt = "cuda", torch.bfloat16 key = torch.randn(num_tokens, NUM_HEADS, DK, dtype=dt, device=dev) value = torch.randn(num_tokens, NUM_HEADS, DV, dtype=dt, device=dev) slots = random.sample(range(BLOCK * NUM_BLOCKS), num_tokens) slot_mapping = torch.tensor(slots, dtype=torch.long, device=dev) # the backends pass a (B, H, N, C).transpose(1, 2) view kv_cache = torch.empty( NUM_BLOCKS, NUM_HEADS, BLOCK, DK + DV, dtype=dt, device=dev ).transpose(1, 2) k_scale = (key.amax() / 64.0).to(torch.float32) v_scale = (value.amax() / 64.0).to(torch.float32) graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph() with torch.cuda.graph(graph): triton_reshape_and_cache_flash_diffkv( key, value, kv_cache, slot_mapping, "auto", k_scale, v_scale ) torch.cuda.synchronize() def timed(n): torch.cuda.synchronize() start = time.perf_counter() for _ in range(n): graph.replay() torch.cuda.synchronize() return (time.perf_counter() - start) / n timed(3) # warm-up return timed(ITERS) for n in [64, 256, 1024, 4096, 16384, 65536]: print(f"{n:>7} {run(n) * 1e6:9.3f} us") ``` </details> --- **AI assistance disclosure** (per `AGENTS.md`): Developed with Claude Code. I reviewed and refined every line, and ran all tests. **Duplicate check**: I did not find any open or merged PR changing `num_warps` at either site. #46060 rewrites the capability check in both launch blocks of this file; if it lands first I will rebase. #47535 adds an opt-in CUDA DiffKV op and keeps Triton as the default, which is the path this PR speeds up.

signals.title: [Attention][MLA] Add GLM-5.2 TurboQuant sparse backend with DCP/MTP
signals.text: ## Summary - extends the TurboQuant MLA work in #41803 with the GLM-5.2 sparse MLA path on current main - adds packed 4-bit latent KV storage, fused sparse decode, sparse prefill, and GLM-4 MoE MTP plumbing - adds DCP/MTP/PP correctness fixes, canonical DCP interleave handling, CUDA-graph-safe workspaces, and asynchronous MTP handoff ## Validation - end-to-end cold and hot inference workloads completed successfully - hot-cache median TTFT improved by 31x and median end-to-end latency improved by 8.26x in the validation workload - all requests completed without connector, engine, worker, or completion errors - changed-file pre-commit suite passes, including Ruff, mypy, configuration validation, and forbidden CUDA API checks ## Relationship to existing work #41803 provides the dense Triton-fused TurboQuant MLA decode foundation. This PR adds GLM-5.2 sparse attention, DCP/MTP/PP integration, and the end-to-end sparse prefill/decode path. Opened as draft because the change should likely be split for review.

signals.title: [ROCm][CI] Fix intermittent GPU memory fault during sleep-mode wake-up
signals.text: ROCm sleep-mode wake-up can intermittently abort the EngineCore on MI300 while remapping roughly 172 GiB, as seen in [build 12090](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12090/list?sid=01a004a6-9a94-48ba-8be1-20f23544b8e0&tab=output) and the earlier signature-matched [build 11862](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/11862/list?sid=019fe4e5-8d10-4dca-8454-8c50409fefda&tab=output). Both failures occurred about 0.53 seconds into the first wake on different MI300 hosts, with the same GPU address-`nil` fault and `create_and_map -> wake_up` stack, while their MI355 jobs passed. PR #44972 added an allocator-wide ROCm `hipMemset` after VMM remapping to scrub stale VRAM on older amdgpu drivers and prevent discarded Mamba/GDN state from corrupting generation. That memset is the only device-wide access at the observed fault point and unnecessarily touches the full attention KV allocation, making it the high-confidence vLLM trigger even though the underlying defect may be a ROCm VMM race. A controlled restoration of the old leaf passed 40/40 local cycles, so this remains an intermittent mitigation rather than a deterministic native A/B reproduction. This change forward-ports the unmerged `0ab7e793` design by clearing only bound Mamba/GDN state after KV remapping and preserving packed cache offsets and strides. It preserves the functional motivation of #44972 but intentionally does not retain its broader allocator-wide scrubbing guarantee for discarded bytes on affected old drivers. Proposed changes: - Remove the ROCm whole-allocation `hipMemset` from `create_and_map`. - Rebuild packed Mamba cache views with their configured byte offset and per-block stride in both model runners. - Zero only bound Mamba/GDN conv and recurrent state views after a full or KV-tagged wake, without touching attention KV or weights-only wakes. - Deduplicate aliased state views so shared storage is cleared once. - Add assertion-level regression coverage that fails 4/4 on the pre-fix implementation and passes 4/4 with this change.

signals.title: [Bugfix] Reload speculative draft weights after Level 2 sleep wake
signals.text: Addresses #52479 ## Problem After the documented Level 2 sleep/wake sequence, MTP speculative decoding silently stops helping: every drafted token is rejected (`Mean acceptance length: 1.00`, `Accepted throughput: 0.00`) and decode throughput falls to approximately the no-speculation rate. Target-model outputs remain correct, so the failure appears only as a large performance regression. Level 2 sleep discards draft parameters together with the target parameters. `wake_up()` restores the saved draft buffers, but the documented subsequent `reload_weights()` call reloads only the target model. The drafter is a separate module and therefore continues with discarded parameter storage. ## Fix Put the disk-backed draft reload in `GPUModelRunner.reload_weights` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py`), on the existing `weights_iterator is None` path, before the target load: - Resolve the draft through the existing `get_draft_model()` accessor. - Read the configured draft checkpoint with its model loader. MTP configurations without a separate `draft_load_config` use the target load configuration. - Load in place through `initialize_layerwise_reload` / `finalize_layerwise_reload`, preserving the parameter addresses captured by the compiled runtime. - Invoke the helper unbound (`GPUModelRunner._reload_draft_weights_from_disk(self)`) because Model Runner V2 already delegates this method with a V2 `self` and does not inherit the helper. - Reload the target last because EAGLE-style drafts can share embeddings or an output head with it; the target checkpoint therefore remains authoritative for any shared storage. - Leave iterator-based reloads unchanged; those weights are supplied by their caller and are not assumed to contain a second draft checkpoint. Model Runner V2 keeps its existing one-line delegate into that method. There is no V2 wrapper and no production-file diff under `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/`. This mirrors Level 1 sleep semantics: both paths restore the existing target and draft modules in place. Level 1 restores their tagged allocations from host RAM, while Level 2 restores saved buffers during `wake_up()` and reloads model parameters from their disk checkpoints during `reload_weights()`. ### Why not `start_draft_weight_update()`? The draft weight-update API added by #46725 selects the draft as the destination of an already-configured `WeightTransferEngine`. Its built-in NCCL and IPC backends receive weights supplied by an external trainer; they do not accept a checkpoint path or read weights from disk. The API also requires the server to start with `weight_transfer_config`. It remains the correct path for runtime trainer/RL weight transfer; this PR does not replace it. The failing workflow is the separate, documented disk-restore path and does not require a trainer or weight-transfer engine: ```python llm.sleep(level=2) llm.wake_up(tags=["weights"]) llm.collective_rpc("reload_weights") llm.wake_up(tags=["kv_cache"]) ``` This change reuses #46725's `get_draft_model()` accessor and the same layerwise reload lifecycle used by checkpoint-format transfer engines, while keeping the checkpoint source appropriate to this workflow. This is not a duplicate of #46725: that change added externally supplied runtime draft updates, while this PR completes the separate documented disk-backed `reload_weights()` recovery path. ## Live evidence Measured on the previous MRV2-wrapper revision of this PR (same disk draft loader, layerwise lifecycle, and draft-first / target-last order) on 2x RTX 5090, TP=2, Qwen3.8-27B-FP8, MTP `num_speculative_tokens=2`, with sleep mode enabled. Each throughput entry is the median of three 256-token HTTP generations. This head was not re-run on GPU; the placement change is covered by the unit tests below. | State | Throughput | Mean acceptance length | Reload RPC | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Cold baseline | 109.4 tok/s | not recorded | — | | L2 wake cycle 1 | 108.9 tok/s (100% of baseline) | 2.17 | 4.18 s | | L2 wake cycle 2 | 104.9 tok/s (96% of baseline) | 2.43 | 4.11 s | Both cycles used the documented staged sequence above plus a prefix-cache reset. Both produced coherent, non-empty output. The harness's final service restart also completed normally and the health endpoint returned ready. No errors or tracebacks were recorded. Reload RPC timing covers the complete disk-backed draft-plus-target `reload_weights()` call. For comparison, the unpatched reproduction was 51.8 tok/s with acceptance length 1.00 and zero accepted draft tokens. ## Tests Four focused unit tests cover: 1. A disk-backed reload restores the draft through its configured loader and the layerwise lifecycle before reloading the target. 2. The same disk path through Model Runner V2's existing `GPUModelRunnerV1.reload_weights(self, ...)` delegate. 3. A disk-backed reload without a draft still reloads the target normally. 4. A caller-supplied weight iterator does not trigger an implicit draft reload. ```text .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py::TestReloadDraftWeights -q # 4 passed ``` ## Scope and limitations - The serving path of interest is Model Runner V2. The implementation lives in the shared `GPUModelRunner.reload_weights` that V2 already calls, so a legacy V1 engine using that method also gets the disk draft reload. - Live validation covers same-checkpoint MTP on one TP=2 hardware/model configuration, measured on the previous wrapper revision. Separate EAGLE checkpoints were not tested live; target-last ordering protects shared target storage, but does not establish compatibility between an arbitrary target and draft checkpoint. - The configured draft checkpoint remains the source of draft weights. This change does not redefine draft selection during `weights_path` model swaps. - Draft formats whose loaders do not implement `get_all_weights` raise `NotImplementedError`, matching the existing target-model disk reload. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, review-response analysis, and test orchestration. The submitter reviewed the changes and the live validation described above.

signals.title: [Bugfix][MLA] Do not use Dense MHA for GLM-5.2
signals.text: ## Purpose Fix incorrect short-prefill dispatch in the NVIDIA DeepSeek-V3.2 attention wrapper. The generic sparse-MLA metadata path may select dense MHA when a prefill's sequence length is at most `index_topk`. It then allows the sparse indexer to skip top-k scoring. `DeepseekV32Attention`, however, only invokes `forward_mqa`; it does not execute the dense-MHA backend. For a pure prefill above the backend's decode-like threshold, MQA therefore consumed the cleared all-`-1` top-k buffer and GLM-5.2 output degenerated into repeated tokens. This change adds a model-layer dense-prefill capability in addition to the backend capability. The NVIDIA DeepSeek-V3.2 wrapper declares that it is MQA-only, so sparse MLA keeps its prefill on top-k MQA and the indexer does not advertise the dense-MHA scoring skip. This does not duplicate the open related work: - #51395 disables dense prefill only for the SM120 sparse-MLA backend. - #52046 adds a dense branch for the PCP path; the reproduced failure is the non-PCP SM100 path. - #49790 routes DSA architectures to the NVIDIA implementation but does not resolve this dispatch mismatch. Issue #46715 reports a different GLM-5.1 failure at a 65,536-token scheduler budget and multi-thousand-token prompts on the registered model path. ## Test Plan ```text .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py -q pre-commit run --files \ vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py \ vllm/models/deepseek_v32/attention.py \ tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py ``` Real-model validation uses `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`, TP=4, the explicit NVIDIA DeepSeek-V3.2 class override, FP8 E4M3 KV cache, eager execution, FP32 indexer logits, GVR disabled, and FlashInfer autotuning disabled. It serially probes the 128/129-token routing boundary without setting `sparse_mla_force_mqa=true`. ## Test Result - Focused pytest: `7 passed`. - Pre-commit on all three changed files: all hooks passed. - `compileall` and `git diff --check`: passed. - Before this change, the real model passed through 127 actual prompt tokens and failed at 129 and every tested larger prompt through 1,001 tokens. Adding only `sparse_mla_force_mqa=true` made all 19 boundary cases pass, causally confirming the routing mismatch. - Patched real-model result: all 19/19 cases passed exact retrieval without the force-MQA workaround, spanning 97, 101, 122, 127, 129, 130, 131, 132, 162, 191, 192, 193, 194, 196, 202, 257, 301, 502, and 1,001 actual prompt tokens. AI assistance was used to diagnose, implement, test, and draft this change. The human submitter must review every changed line and understand and defend the change end-to-end before marking the PR ready for review. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR is described. - [x] The test plan includes exact commands. - [x] Unit and real-model results are reported. - [x] Related open work was checked for duplication. </details>

signals.title: Bump setuptools to a CVE-2025-47273-fixed release across build/platform/test requirements
signals.text: ## Summary Several requirement files pin or permit setuptools releases below the `78.1.1` floor that fixes [CVE-2025-47273](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-47273) ([GHSA-5rjg-fvgr-3xxf](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5rjg-fvgr-3xxf)), a path traversal in setuptools' package-index/archive handling: - `pyproject.toml`'s PEP 517 `build-system.requires` and several `requirements/build/*.txt` files allow `setuptools>=77.0.3` with no lower bound at the fixed release - `requirements/build/cpu.txt` and `requirements/cpu.txt` pin the exact vulnerable `setuptools==77.0.3` - `requirements/tpu.txt` pins `setuptools==78.1.0`, one patch release short of the fix - The generated test locks `requirements/test/cpu.txt` and `requirements/test/cuda.txt` also resolve to `setuptools==77.0.3` This bumps every affected pin/lower-bound to `78.1.1`. Other parts of the repo (`docker/Dockerfile.ppc64le`, `build_vllm_ppc64le.sh`, `requirements/test/rocm.txt`, `requirements/test/xpu.txt`) already use a setuptools version at or above this floor, so this brings the rest of the requirement set in line with that existing practice. This is a MODERATE-severity supply-chain issue per the project's own [severity guide](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/SECURITY.md) (build-time, requires a malicious package index/archive to be exercised during a build step; no RCE or privileged-access path demonstrated), which is why this is a plain PR rather than a private security advisory. **Note on `requirements/build/cpu.txt` / `requirements/cpu.txt`:** the prior exact pin carried a comment that `setuptools==77.0.3` "can reuse CMake build dir". I don't have a way to independently confirm whether `78.1.1` preserves that specific behavior, so I've flagged it inline for maintainer judgment — if it doesn't, please pick another `setuptools` release `>=78.1.1` that does. ## Test plan - [x] Confirmed no remaining `setuptools==77.0.3` / `setuptools==78.1.0` / unbounded `setuptools>=77.0.3` reference anywhere in `pyproject.toml` or `requirements/` - [ ] Maintainer: confirm `setuptools==78.1.1` still supports the CMake build-dir reuse the prior pin's comment referenced - [ ] Maintainer: confirm the generated test locks (`requirements/test/cpu.txt`, `requirements/test/cuda.txt`) don't need a full `uv pip compile` regeneration instead of the direct edit here

signals.title: [Spec Decode] Warn that speculative max_model_len has no effect
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #52258. `speculative_config.max_model_len` is accepted and validated, then never read. V0 used it to skip speculation for sequences past a threshold. V1 has no consumer: ``` $ grep -rn "draft_model_config" vllm/ --include=*.py | grep max_model_len \ | grep -v ^vllm/config/ (no matches) $ grep -rn "speculative_config\.max_model_len" vllm/ --include=*.py \ | grep -v ^vllm/config/ (no matches) ``` For `ngram` and `custom_class`, `draft_model_config` aliases `target_model_config` (`config/speculative.py:834`, `:848`), so the override at `:1127` never runs. For draft-model methods the override does run, but nothing reads the result. ## Modifications Warn at the end of `SpeculativeConfig.__post_init__` when the field is set, and replace this PR's original test with one asserting the warning. Warn rather than reject so existing configs keep starting, and rather than implementing the V0 skip, which is a feature rather than a bug fix and needs a scope decision. I asked about scope on #52258 and have not heard back, so this PR covers only the silent-ignore part; I'm happy to follow up with the skip if maintainers want it. Note on the change of approach: this PR previously added a failing test asserting the value reached the draft config. That test was wrong. For `ngram` the draft and target configs are the same object, so it asserted `draft == 80` and `target == 200` simultaneously, which cannot hold. Even un-aliased it would have passed while the option stayed unread, which is worse than no test. ## Test Plan ``` pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_max_len.py -k warns_that_it_has_no_effect ``` ## Test Result `1 passed`. Reverting only the `speculative.py` change makes it fail, so it is not passing vacuously. Whole file on an RTX 4090, `6 failed, 6 passed`, against `6 failed, 5 passed` for the same file on `017e9f4448` without this change: the same six `test_eagle_max_len` cases fail either way (pre-existing on this hardware) and the extra pass is the new test. Note the file imports `get_attn_backend_list_based_on_platform()` at module scope, so it does not collect without a supported accelerator. ## Notes Not a duplicate: no other open PR references #52258. No model output changes, so no evals: the only runtime change is an added warning. AI assistance was used for this change. I have reviewed every changed line.

signals.title: [Deprecation] Warn that use_prefill_decode_attention has no effect
signals.text: ## Purpose `--attention-config.use_prefill_decode_attention` is accepted, documented, and has no effect. It used to select `ROCM_ATTN` on ROCm. #36702 made `ROCM_ATTN` the unconditional first entry in the ROCm priority list and removed the branch that read the flag, so the field has had no reader in `vllm/` since. Its original purpose is now the default behaviour, making this leftover surface rather than a regression. Two tests suggest otherwise: `tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py` asserts the flag parses, and the `RocmAttn` entry in `tests/v1/attention/utils.py` passes it beside an explicit `"backend": "ROCM_ATTN"`. ## Modifications Per [deprecation_policy.md](docs/contributing/deprecation_policy.md), CLI flags must pass through the pipeline rather than be removed outright, so this is stage 1 only: - warn in `AttentionConfig.__post_init__` when set, naming v0.29.0 for removal - record in the docstring that it is deprecated and inert - drop the flag from the `RocmAttn` test config; the explicit backend selection is unchanged, so behaviour is identical - test that the warning fires when set and not otherwise No behaviour change for anyone not setting the flag. For anyone who is, the only change is that they are now told. ## Test Plan ``` pytest tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py ``` ## Test Result `97 passed`. `pre-commit` passes on the three changed files, mypy included. The new test clears `_print_warning_once`'s `lru_cache` first: `warning_once` is cached and `test_attention_config` sets this flag earlier in the same file, so without the clear the assertion depends on test ordering. ## Notes Not a duplicate: no open PR or issue references `use_prefill_decode_attention`. No evals included; the flag has no consumer and the only runtime change is an added warning. AI assistance was used for this change. I have reviewed every changed line and run the tests above. cc @gshtras (authored #36702), @yewentao256 (deprecation precedent in #32812)

signals.title: [Model] Add Qwen3-Omni DSpark support
signals.text: ## Purpose Add framework support for using a dedicated `Qwen3OmniDSparkModel` draft with a Qwen3-Omni thinker target. This change: - registers a dedicated Qwen3-Omni DSpark architecture instead of silently treating it as generic Qwen3 DSpark; - exposes the target thinker's post-DeepStack auxiliary hidden states required by DSpark; - preserves the dedicated architecture and DSpark sampling fields when converting msModelSpec configuration; - validates the target/draft hidden size, attention geometry, target-layer selection, vocabulary contract, and DSpark algorithm settings at startup; - makes embedding/lm-head sharing and rejection-sampling buffers safe when the draft input/output vocabulary differs from the target vocabulary; - adds focused registry, configuration, model-contract, and configuration-bridge tests. A repository search for `Qwen3 Omni DSpark` and `Qwen3OmniDSpark` found no existing PR implementing this support, so this does not duplicate known work. This is a framework integration PR. Qwen3-Omni DSpark checkpoints are not yet available, so it does not claim model quality or acceptance-rate results. AI assistance disclosure: this draft was prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance. It should remain in draft until the submitter has reviewed every changed line and completed the required NPU/model evaluation. ## Test Plan ```bash .venv/bin/ruff check vllm/config/speculative.py \ vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dflash.py \ vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dspark.py \ vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_omni_dspark.py \ vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_omni_moe_thinker.py \ vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py \ vllm/transformers_utils/configs/speculators/algos.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dspark/speculator.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dspark/utils.py \ tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni.py \ tests/models/registry.py tests/test_config.py \ tests/transformers_utils/test_speculators_dspark_config.py .venv/bin/ruff format --check <the same 13 files> .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/transformers_utils/test_speculators_dspark_config.py \ tests/test_config.py \ -k 'qwen3_omni_dspark or dspark_updater' .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni.py \ -k 'dedicated_model_class or incomplete_vocab_weights or probabilistic_buffer' ``` Before marking ready: - run the Qwen3-Omni hidden-state module tests in an environment with `torchvision`; - load a compatible Qwen3-Omni DSpark checkpoint; - run NPU end-to-end eager and ACLGraph speculative-decoding tests in the dependent vLLM-Ascend PR; - report acceptance length, output correctness, memory, and throughput. ## Test Result - Ruff check: passed. - Ruff format check: passed; 13 files already formatted. - Configuration and msModelSpec bridge tests: 21 passed, 183 deselected. - Dedicated model/vocabulary/sampling-buffer tests: 5 passed, 3 deselected. - `git diff --check`: passed. - Qwen3-Omni hidden-state import tests were not runnable on the local macOS environment because `torchvision` is unavailable. - Model evaluation: not run because no Qwen3-Omni DSpark checkpoint is available.

signals.title: [Rust Frontend] Add MiniMax M2 append-think reasoning parser
signals.text: ## Summary - add the explicit `minimax_m2_append_think` Rust reasoning parser - prepend `<think>` once while preserving all generated output as visible content - preserve special tokens and keep automatic MiniMax model routing on the normal parser - cover parser lifecycle, empty deltas, factory registration, and parser-name diagnostics ## Duplicate-work check This does not duplicate an existing PR. Before implementation I checked: - roadmap issue #44280 and its comments - open PRs referencing `44280` - open PR searches for `minimax_m2_append_think` and MiniMax M2 append-think parser terms No overlapping Rust implementation or claim was found. The item was claimed in #44280 before implementation. ## Tests - `cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-parser --lib` — 420 passed - `cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-chat --lib` — 266 passed - `cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat --all-targets -- -D warnings` — passed - `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` — passed ## Full-model serving regression A CPU-only end-to-end serving regression was run with the locally built PR Rust binary and the full `allenai/Olmo-3-7B-Instruct` weights (13.59 GiB), using `--reasoning-parser minimax_m2_append_think`. A different model was intentionally used because the parser is selected explicitly and MiniMax M2.5 itself is approximately 434 GiB across 125 weight shards. - Rust frontend, Python engine, tokenizer/template loading, and OpenAI HTTP serving all started successfully. - Non-streaming output preserved generated text as content and prepended exactly one marker: `content = "<think>hello world"`, `reasoning = null`. - Streaming reconstruction produced `content = "<think>hello world"`, empty reasoning, one `<think>` prefix, and `finish_reason = "stop"`. A model-quality evaluation is not applicable because this change does not affect model execution, logits, or sampling; the full-model run validates parser integration and HTTP behavior. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used to analyze the parser architecture, implement the change, and run validation. This PR is intentionally opened as a draft and must be reviewed line by line by the human submitter before being marked ready.

signals.title: [Rust Frontend] Simplify data-parallel size ownership
signals.text: ## Purpose Follow up on #51245 after the effective runtime fix landed in #51178. This PR focuses on simplifying deployment-wide data-parallel size ownership and adding a dense-DP regression test. - Store the explicit deployment-wide DP size only in `TransportMode::Bootstrapped`; `HandshakeOwner` derives it from `engine_count`. - Expose the deployment-wide value through `EngineCoreClient` and use it for `/get_world_size` and gRPC server information. - Remove the duplicate value and override path from server `Config` and `AppState`. - Move topology validation into the engine-core client so direct client users receive the same validation before sockets are opened. - Rename the Rust-only Ready field to `effective_data_parallel_size` while preserving the Python wire key with serde. Dense independent-DP engines may report `1` here, while the client transport owns deployment topology. - Add a dense-DP `/get_world_size` E2E test covering both the default response and `include_dp=false`. Valid Python-managed production configurations retain the behavior introduced by #51178. The refactor removes redundant state that could diverge from the client transport. ## Test Plan - Build the complete Rust workspace and all targets. - Run the engine-core-client, server, and command crate tests. - Verify Python/Rust Ready msgpack field parity. - Lint and format-check the dense-DP E2E test. - Run the GPU-backed dense-DP test in distributed CI. ## Test Result - `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`: passed - `cargo test -p vllm-engine-core-client --all-targets`: 98 passed - `cargo test -p vllm-server --lib`: 339 passed - `cargo test -p vllm-cmd --all-targets`: 63 passed - `cargo test -p vllm-engine-core-client python_msgpack_fixtures_match_rust_encoding`: passed - `cargo test -p vllm-server control_aggregates_multi_engine_capacity`: passed - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: passed - `uvx ruff check tests/v1/distributed/test_internal_lb_dp.py`: passed - `uvx ruff format --check tests/v1/distributed/test_internal_lb_dp.py`: passed --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [x] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.title: [Rust Frontend] Add Olmo3 tool parser
signals.text: ## Purpose Add the Olmo3 tool parser to the experimental Rust frontend. - Parses `<function_calls>...</function_calls>` blocks containing newline-separated Python-style calls. - Supports parallel calls, nested dict/list/tuple literals, Python and JSON boolean/null literals, parameterless calls, and arbitrary stream chunk boundaries. - Preserves visible text before and after tool calls in event order. - Falls back to ordinary text for incomplete or unsupported tool-call expressions instead of panicking. - Registers the `olmo3` parser and automatic `olmo-3` / `olmo3` model matchers. - Adds a real `allenai/Olmo-3-7B-Instruct` tokenizer/template roundtrip fixture. Tracks the Olmo3 tool-parser item in #44280. ### Duplicate-work check Before implementation and again before opening this PR, I checked: - comments on #44280; - open PRs referencing #44280; - open PR searches for `olmo3 rust tool parser` and related Rust frontend keywords. I found no open PR implementing the Olmo3 Rust tool parser. #47345 is an Olmo3 reasoning-parser PR and does not overlap this change. ### AI assistance AI assistance was used to inspect the existing parser architecture, implement the Rust changes, and prepare tests. The submitting human will review every changed line and must be able to explain and maintain the implementation before this PR is marked ready for review. ## Test Plan ```bash cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-parser --lib cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-chat --lib HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml \ -p vllm-chat --test roundtrip roundtrip_olmo3 cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml \ -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat --all-targets -- -D warnings pre-commit run --files \ rust/Cargo.lock rust/Cargo.toml rust/src/chat/src/lib.rs \ rust/src/chat/src/parser/tool/mod.rs rust/src/chat/src/parser/tool/tests.rs \ rust/src/chat/tests/roundtrip.rs rust/src/parser/Cargo.toml \ rust/src/parser/src/tool/mod.rs rust/src/parser/src/tool/olmo3.rs ``` The roundtrip test uses cached tokenizer/template files from the official `allenai/Olmo-3-7B-Instruct` repository; no model weights or GPU are required. A model-quality evaluation is not applicable because this change does not alter model execution or generated outputs. A full-model serving regression was performed to validate parser integration, as recorded below. ## Test Result - `vllm-parser`: 421 passed. - `vllm-chat` library: 265 passed. - Olmo3 real model-family roundtrip: 1 passed. - Clippy with `-D warnings`: passed. - Changed-file pre-commit hooks: passed. ## Full-model serving regression Downloaded and served the complete `allenai/Olmo-3-7B-Instruct` checkpoint (13.59 GiB) on the CPU backend with the locally built PR Rust binary, `--tool-call-parser olmo3`, and the real model tokenizer/chat template. - `/health` and `/v1/models`: passed. - Plain chat: returned exactly `hello`. - Required single tool: returned one `get_weather` call with `{"city":"Shanghai"}` and `finish_reason = "tool_calls"`. - Required parallel tools: returned ordered Shanghai and Beijing calls. - Text before tool call: preserved `content = "I will check."` before the parsed tool call. - Streaming parallel tools: six SSE chunks reconstructed into two complete ordered calls and ended with `finish_reason = "tool_calls"`.

signals.title: [Build] Propagate vLLM version to Rust binaries
signals.text: ## Summary - derive a device-independent vLLM source version with setuptools-scm for Python-driven and standalone Rust builds - embed the same version in `vllm-rs`, `vllm-bench`, and the Rust frontend version endpoint - expose Git metadata to selective Docker Rust build stages while suppressing the artificial dirty state caused by omitted tracked files ## Affected outputs | Surface | Effect | | --- | --- | | `vllm-rs --version` | Reports the embedded vLLM source version. | | `vllm-bench --version` | Reports the embedded vLLM source version instead of the workspace crate version (`0.1.0`). | | Rust frontend `GET /version` | `rust_frontend_version` reports the embedded vLLM source version. The engine-reported `version` field keeps its existing behavior. | ## Affected build paths | Build path | Embedded Rust version | | --- | --- | | Nightly/release wheel builds from a Git checkout | The setuptools-scm source version. `VLLM_VERSION_OVERRIDE` is honored through `SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION`. | | Docker builds using `docker/Dockerfile`, `.cpu`, `.rocm`, `.rocm_gfx1250`, or `.xpu` | The source version resolved from the mounted Git metadata. Selective-copy stages set `dirty=false` because omitted tracked files would otherwise make the partial worktree appear dirty. | | Local `bash build_rust.sh` | The setuptools-scm source version when Git metadata is available. | | Direct `cargo build` | `VLLM_RS_BUILD_VERSION` when explicitly supplied; otherwise the workspace crate version (`0.1.0`). | The embedded Rust version stays device-independent. Python distribution version handling remains unchanged, including platform suffixes such as CPU, CUDA, ROCm, TPU, and XPU variants. Repackaging an existing prebuilt Rust binary preserves the version embedded when that binary was built. ## Motivation Rust artifacts currently identify themselves using workspace crate metadata, which stays at `0.1.0` and does not identify the corresponding nightly or release vLLM source revision. This change resolves the source version before compiling Rust and passes it through `VLLM_RS_BUILD_VERSION`. `get_vllm_version()` runs first during Python packaging so `VLLM_VERSION_OVERRIDE`, propagated through `SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION`, also applies to the Rust artifacts. ## Validation - `cargo nextest run -p vllm-build-info -p vllm-bench -p vllm-cmd -p vllm-server --no-fail-fast` (552 passed, 10 skipped) - injected version output: `vllm-bench 9.8.7` and `vllm-rs 9.8.7` - Cargo fallback output: `vllm-bench 0.1.0` - existing Docker build metadata tests (7 passed) - Ruff, Dockerfile parsing, shell syntax, and `git diff --check`

signals.title: [Quantization] Remove the dead ocp_mx_scheme branch from moe_kernel_quantize_input
signals.text: ## Purpose Shortly, remove dead code. `moe_kernel_quantize_input()` in `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/utils.py` carries an `ocp_mx_scheme: str | None = None` parameter and opens its body with a block that short-circuits `*_a_fp8` OCP MX schemes into `_fp8_quantize_dequantize` before the normal `quant_dtype` dispatch ever runs. Nothing reaches that block. This PR removes the parameter and the block. This is the follow-up @fxmarty-amd asked for when introduced the `quantization_emulation` path that superseded the block, in #46142 (`e368415daa`): > [r3452957212](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46142/files#r3452957212): > "Yes I don't think this code block is needed" > [r3453008225](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46142/files#r3453008225): > "Let's address in an other PR." This is the left TODO: ```python # TODO: Remove this `ocp_mx_scheme is not None` block and rely solely # on `quantization_emulation`. ``` and reconfirmed the ask in review on #43983 ([review 4904664996](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43983#pullrequestreview-4904664996)), linking `utils.py#L288-L301` — exactly the lines removed here. ### Why deleting it changes no behavior The only arm with behavior was `.endswith("a_fp8")`, and the only **reachable** a_fp8 scheme is `w_mxfp4_a_fp8` — `w_mxfp6_e3m2_a_fp8` and `w_mxfp6_e2m3_a_fp8`, both raise `NotImplementedError` earlier, in `QuarkOCP_MX_MoEMethod.get_fused_moe_quant_config`. For `w_mxfp4_a_fp8` the two paths are identical: | | deleted arm | surviving dispatch | |---|---|---| | condition | `ocp_mx_scheme.endswith("a_fp8")` | `quant_dtype == current_platform.fp8_dtype()` and `quantization_emulation` | | action | `return _fp8_quantize_dequantize(A, A_scale)` | `return _fp8_quantize_dequantize(A, A_scale)` | `_fp8_quantize_dequantize` takes only `A` and `A_scale`, so nothing else was being bypassed. `OCP_MXQuantizationEmulationTritonExperts.__init__` sets both inputs (`quantization_emulation = True`, `_quant_dtype = current_platform.fp8_dtype()`), and `TritonExperts.apply` forwards them. ## Test Plan ### Unit test ```bash python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py -q python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_cutlass_moe.py -q pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/utils.py ``` ### End-to-end test Same as what tested in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43983 - ROCm, MI325 - Model: amd/gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8 - MXFP4 emulation MoE backend --moe-backend emulation ## Test Result Coming soon. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>
