signals.title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Fix OCP MX MoE emulation silently skipping mxfp6 activation QDQ
signals.text: ## Purpose `OCP_MXQuantizationEmulationTritonExperts` overrides the `quant_dtype` property with a scheme→dtype map built in `__init__`. For the four mxfp6-activation schemes that map produced `"mxfp6"` — not a key `moe_kernel_quantize_input` dispatches on, which knows `"mxfp6_e3m2"` and `"mxfp6_e2m3"`. Those schemes therefore fall through to the dispatcher's closing `else: return A, A_scale` and run with **unquantized activations**. Nothing raises; the emulation just quietly stops emulating, and accuracy numbers for these schemes come out optimistic. Affected schemes: - `w_mxfp4_a_mxfp6_e3m2` - `w_mxfp4_a_mxfp6_e2m3` - `w_mxfp6_e3m2_a_mxfp6_e3m2` - `w_mxfp6_e2m3_a_mxfp6_e2m3` ### Solution Map each scheme to the concrete dtype, and extract the mapping into `activation_quant_dtype` so it can be tested without standing up a full `FusedMoEConfig`. The chain also had no arm for `w_mxfp6_e2m3_a_fp8`, which left `_quant_dtype` unset and would raise `AttributeError` from the `quant_dtype` property; it now takes the fp8 path with its siblings, and an unhandled scheme raises `NotImplementedError` instead of falling through. ### End-to-end failure Two MoE forwards through `FusedMoEModularKernel` with `OCP_MXQuantizationEmulationTritonExperts`: - one for `w_mxfp4_a_mxfp6_e3m2` - one for the weight-only `w_mxfp4` same quantized weights, same activations, same routing, only the scheme differs. The first is supposed to fake-quantize activations and the second is not, so their outputs must differ. However, on `main` they are bit-identical: ``` E AssertionError: w_mxfp4_a_mxfp6_e3m2 MoE output is bit-identical to the weight-only E w_mxfp4 scheme (max|diff| = 0.0): the emulation never fake-quantized the activations E assert 0.0 > 0.0 FAILED test_a_mxfp6_e3m2_moe_fake_quantizes_activations_end_to_end 1 failed in 7.63s ``` With this PR the QDQ reaches the layer output (E=8, topk=2, hidden=256, intermediate=256, 64 tokens, bf16, MI325X): ``` max|a_mxfp6_e3m2 - w_mxfp4| = 1.875 mean|diff| = 0.2942 |w_mxfp4| max = 26.2500 mean = 3.1170 -> 9.44% mean shift 1 passed in 8.24s ``` That ~9% mean shift in the MoE output is precisely the emulation error these schemes are meant to model, and were not. ## Test Plan Add a test case `test_emulation_activation_quant_dtype_is_dispatchable` in `tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py` ## Test Result Passed. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.title: Integrate DeepGEMM NVFP4 MegaMoE with fused shared experts
signals.text: ## Purpose Add a ModelOpt NVFP4 MegaMoE path backed by DeepGEMM, including fused BF16 shared-expert execution. - Select DeepGEMM NVFP4 MegaMoE for `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`. - Transform routed NVFP4 weights/scales into the layout expected by DeepGEMM. - Bind the BF16 shared expert when supported and avoid duplicate shared-expert execution or output reduction. - Keep symmetric-buffer rendezvous out of forward/CUDA Graph capture and tie its lifetime to the active EP group. - Reject unsupported DBO execution and fail closed when routed scaling is not bound. - Preserve existing fallback behavior for unsupported configurations. This draft depends on https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/409. ## Validation setup - Hardware: 8 x GB300, DP8/EP8 over two nodes. - Model: real GLM-5.2-NVFP4 checkpoint. - vLLM commit: `09e7d46d149221da4a8ece6ba5e5336aed32cd54`. - Identical model, image, CUDA Graph, cache, prompt, and scheduler settings for all arms. - Arms: 1. `FI one-sided`: `moe_backend=auto`, actual `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` NVFP4 experts, `flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided` A2A, ordinary shared expert. 2. `DG unfused`: DeepGEMM NVFP4 MegaMoE routed experts plus an ordinary independent shared expert (`fused_shared=False`). 3. `DG fused`: DeepGEMM NVFP4 MegaMoE with fused BF16 shared expert (`fused_shared=True`). ## Accuracy results - Targeted vLLM GPU tests: **16/16 passed** on GB300. - Dependent DeepGEMM kernel validation: - 42 boundary/adversarial cases, M/rank 1-2048: PASS, max rel-L2 `0.005421`. - 22 random fuzz cases, M/rank 3-3073: PASS, max rel-L2 `0.002655`. - 10 shared-only cases: PASS, max rel-L2 `0.001134`. - 75 real GLM-5.2 MoE layer replays: PASS; fused was closer to FP32 in 69/75 layers. - E2E deterministic prompts: each arm reproduced **16/16** prompts exactly across two runs. - 700-repeat long-context probe: all three arms produced the exact same token sequence and content. - GSM8K, 100 questions, 5-shot: FI one-sided **95%**, DG unfused **94%**, DG fused **95%**; invalid responses **0%** for all arms. - Different kernels are not bitwise identical over long autoregressive continuations. DG unfused and fused matched the first token on 14/16 prompts and diverged after a median 14.5-token common prefix; inspected differences were response-style choices and both paths computed the requested answers correctly. The kernel/layer accuracy tests above are the numerical correctness criteria. ## E2E performance The first three-arm performance run is not reported because its communication backend was not held constant: the FI arm used `flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided`, while both DG arms accidentally used the default `AgRsAll2AllManager`. This especially invalidates the decode comparison. A corrected run with the same FlashInfer one-sided A2A backend for all three arms is in progress; this section will be updated with its median-of-five results. No request failure, NaN, CUDA, grid, barrier, OOM, or NVSHMEM error was observed in the completed accuracy run. ## Test commands - `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py -q -k 'deep_gemm_mega_moe or mega_moe'` - `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_shared_expert_method.py -q` - GB300 E2E: 8K prefill (`8192 -> 1`, concurrency 1, 32 prompts, 8 warmups) and decode (`1024 -> 256`, concurrency 64, 128 prompts, 64 warmups), five repeats per arm. Ruff, formatting, Python 3.10/3.12 mypy, SPDX, and targeted pre-commit checks passed locally. The GitHub aggregate pre-commit failure is an infrastructure error while downloading `pre_commit-4.6.2` from PyPI (HTTP 502), before code hooks ran. ## Contribution notes - This is not a duplicate of an existing vLLM PR: it integrates the new DeepGEMM NVFP4 MegaMoE API and fused BF16 shared expert into the ModelOpt and modular MoE paths. - AI assistance was used to implement, review, and test this draft. The submitting human will review the final diff and validation results before marking it ready. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR. - [x] The test plan and commands. - [x] The model-evaluation and performance results. - [ ] (Optional) Documentation updates. </details>

signals.title: [Model] Add GraniteSWA and GraniteMoeSWA via existing Granite
signals.text: ## Purpose Supersedes and closes #48270 Add vLLM support for GraniteSWA and GraniteMoeSWA models, folded into the existing Granite and GraniteMoeShared implementation, as opposed to separate models as in #48270. - GraniteSWA: Granite with per-layer sliding-window attention and a learnable per-head attention sink. The sink is passed to Attention via the native vllm attention harness, the per-layer windowing via config.layer_types and config.sliding_window, and per-layer RoPE/NoPE via config.layer_rope_theta (0 for NoPE). - GraniteMoeSWA: GraniteMoeShared-style MoE combined with the SWA/sink attention above (reuses GraniteSWAAttention). Optional shared experts via shared_intermediate_size (disabled by default); routed experts load through the standard FusedMoE param mapping. Additional features (sinks, sliding window, varying RoPE) are off by default, leaving existing Granite checkpoints unaffected. Also add checkpoint remapping for handling both old- and new-style HF MoE layers. Register both [***]ForCausalLM classes in the model registry, since HF publishes these Granite variants as distinct models. NB: transformers backend does NOT handle these models correctly. Sink tokens get dropped silently and so the model gives wrong output (see #52156). Claude was used to assist in implementing these changes. I have reviewed, corrected, and contributed the code myself, and tested the output for correctness. ## Test Plan Tests include offline parity checks against the adapted HF implementations, addition of SWA/MoeSWA checkpoints to the Granite tests, additional unit tests for case handling of added features and HF naming schemes, and GSM8K verification. Testing env uses CUDA 13.0, Torch 2.13.0, and Transformers 5.16.0. I have not included the parity check script(s) in this PR. ## Test Result All unit tests pass. I have confirmed that this code produces identical output to the HF implementation at fp32 precision, and that the transformers modeling backend does not. Bfloat 16 is near-identical (one missed token prediction in a teacher-forced setting on a randomly initialized model). Parity checks include sinks on/off, RoPE varying/global, and TP on/off. GSM8K score for the 2B SWA model is within 2 points of the published HF model card (40.3 vs 42.2 for 5-shot).
signals.author: daviswer

signals.title: [Build] Add SM121 (DGX Spark / GB10) to published build targets
signals.text: The GB10 GPU in DGX Spark reports compute capability 12.1 (SM121). Right now it's not in any published build target, so users on Spark either compile from source or rely on the sm_120 wheels' family-level forward compatibility, which does not cover CutlassFp8BlockScaledMMKernel's architecture-conditional MMA instructions (see bug #2 below). This adds SM121 to the release build configs and fixes three CMakeLists.txt bugs that a naive "just add 12.1" change would otherwise introduce. Addresses #36821. Pulls the build-target part out of #31740, which has been CONFLICTING since January. #38484 tried the same extraction back in March but only touched the build-config files, not CMakeLists.txt, and has been stale since May. I picked it up because as-is it wouldn't actually produce working SM121 kernels: the CUDA_SUPPORTED_ARCHS gap below would silently drop the 12.1 request, and fixing just that would then break two other kernel families for reasons explained below. Found all of this by actually building vLLM from source and running it on a DGX Spark, not just from reading the diff. **What's in this PR** Adds 12.1 to `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST` in the CI wheel build script, both Dockerfile ARGs, docker-bake.hcl, versions.json, and the FlashInfer AOT build script. Also fixes three arch-selection bugs in CMakeLists.txt / qutlass.cmake, all found by building and running on real GB10 hardware: 1. `CUDA_SUPPORTED_ARCHS` for CUDA >= 13.0 never listed 12.1, so any `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=12.1` request gets silently dropped before it reaches any kernel-specific arch list. 2. `SCALED_MM_ARCHS` (the arch list behind `CutlassFp8BlockScaledMMKernel`) used a `"12.0f"` family target for CUDA >= 13.0. NVIDIA's family-target compilation (the `f` suffix) is explicitly documented to guarantee forward compatibility across an SM sub-family, but it explicitly excludes architecture-conditional (`'a'`-suffixed) instructions by design. This kernel needs exactly those instructions. Once 12.1 is added to `CUDA_ARCHS`, the family-fallback in `cuda_archs_loose_intersection` resolves that to a plain (non-'a') sm_121 cubin, which compiles fine but aborts at kernel launch with "Arch conditional MMA instruction used without targeting appropriate compute capability" - confirmed on GB10. Fixed by using explicit `"12.0a;12.1a"` candidates, same as the CUDA < 13.0 branch already does. Verified the fix produces a working sm_121a cubin with cuobjdump and by running the repro from #43367. 3. `FP4_SM120_ARCHS` and QuTLASS's `QUTLASS_SM120_ARCHS` also use `"12.0f"` family targets, and both hit a separate ptxas failure once 12.1 is in the mix: "Instruction 'cvt with .e2m1x2' not supported on .target 'sm_121'". This reproduces at plain sm_120 too on this CUDA 13.0.3 toolchain, so it's a pre-existing ptxas limitation for NVFP4/MXFP4 e2m1x2 conversion, unrelated to SM121 specifically. Pinned both to plain `"12.0"` so they keep building at today's working target regardless of what else ends up in CUDA_ARCHS. **Testing** Built from source on DGX Spark (GB10, CUDA 13.0.3, driver 580.126.20), controlled before/after at the same commit: | Build | TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST | CMakeLists.txt | Result | |---|---|---|---| | baseline | 12.0 | unpatched | builds, runs correctly | | fixed | 12.1 | patched (this PR) | builds, native sm_121a cubin confirmed via cuobjdump, runs correctly | Ran the `ops.cutlass_scaled_mm` repro from #43367 (m=1, n=16384, k=5120, fp8_e4m3fn) on both. Both give correct output shape. Median latency over 500 synchronized calls: 0.317ms on 12.1a (fixed) vs 0.337ms on 12.0 (baseline), about 6% faster with the native target. One thing worth flagging for reviewers: baseline (today's sm_120 target) does not actually crash on this repro under CUDA 13.0.3. #43367's original crash report was on CUDA 12.9 and looks like it was independently resolved by the CUDA 13 upgrade. So the value here isn't "fixes a crash" for this specific kernel, it's shipping native SM121 codegen (with the 'a'-exclusive instructions this kernel actually needs) in the published wheels, plus closing three real regressions that would otherwise land the moment someone adds 12.1 to CUDA_SUPPORTED_ARCHS. **Files changed** - `.github/workflows/scripts/build.sh` - add 12.1 to release wheel arch list - `CMakeLists.txt` - add 12.1 to CUDA_SUPPORTED_ARCHS; SCALED_MM_ARCHS to 12.0a;12.1a; pin FP4_SM120_ARCHS to plain 12.0 - `cmake/external_projects/qutlass.cmake` - pin QUTLASS_SM120_ARCHS to plain 12.0 - `docker/Dockerfile` - add 12.1 to both torch_cuda_arch_list ARGs - `docker/docker-bake.hcl` - add 12.1 to default arch list - `docker/versions.json` - match Dockerfile ARG update - `tools/flashinfer-build.sh` - add 12.1 to CUDA 13.0+ FlashInfer AOT arch list **Open question for maintainers** A second arch in the multi-arch wheel (12.0 + 12.1) grows wheel size further. The Dockerfile's check-wheel-size.py gate (VLLM_MAX_SIZE_MB=500) may need RUN_WHEEL_CHECK=false or a bump. Flagging rather than guessing at a number.
signals.author: ogulcanaydogan

signals.title: feat(mooncake): Mooncake DCP: Chunk-Derived Namespace for KV Cache Store
signals.text: ### Motivation Under DCP > 1, the Mooncake connector on `main` forces `_spec_tp_replication_factor` to return 1 (`if self.dcp_size > 1: return 1`), disabling TP replication awareness. Every TP rank saves every chunk to its own `(tp_rank, tp_rank % dcp_size)` namespace — `tp_size`× write amplification (e.g., 8× under TP8+DCP4). Lookup fans out `tp_size` keys per chunk and requires `all()` to pass, which works but wastes store bandwidth and capacity. ### Why #51388 is superseded PR #51388 attempted to reduce write amplification by restoring the true TP replication factor (removing the `if dcp_size > 1: return 1` early return) and adding `put_step = factor // dcp_size`. However, it kept **rank-derived** namespace assignment (`dcp_rank = rank % dcp_size`), which created a structural mismatch: - **Save path** stripes chunks across ranks by `put_step = factor`. With `factor = 8` (MLA) and `dcp_size = 4`, each rank saves 1/8 of chunks. A rank with `dcp_rank = 0` saves chunks 0, 4, 8, ... — but only in namespace `@dcp0@`. - **Load path** queries all `tp_size` namespaces per chunk via `all()`. For chunk 1 (owned by `dcp_rank = 1`), it queries `@dcp0@`, `@dcp1@`, `@dcp2@`, `@dcp3@`. But `@dcp0@` only contains chunks 0, 4, 8, ... — chunk 1 was never saved there. - Result: `all()` fails because each namespace only holds 1/4 of chunks → **0% hit rate**. Five follow-up patches in #51388 tried to fix this (adjusting `put_step`, adding per-namespace DBs, etc.) but couldn't resolve the fundamental issue: **chunk → namespace was mapped indirectly via rank identity**, causing save and lookup to diverge on which namespace owns which chunk. ### This PR's approach Eliminate the indirection by making namespace a **pure function of chunk position**: `dcp_rank = chunk_id % dcp_size`. Combined with restoring the true TP replication factor: - **Save**: `put_step = factor` distributes chunks across ranks *within* a namespace. `dcp_rank = chunk_id % dcp_size` distributes chunks *across* namespaces. The two dimensions are orthogonal. - **Load**: For each chunk, derives `dcp_rank = chunk_id % dcp_size` and queries only that namespace. Save and load agree by construction. - **Lookup**: Queries `max(1, tp_size // factor)` keys per chunk (one per TP shard in the chunk's DCP namespace). For MLA: 1 key/chunk, no `all()`. For GQA: `num_kv_head` keys/chunk, `all()` across KV-head shards. For Mamba: `tp_size` keys/chunk, `all()` across TP shards. ### Performance impact (MLA, TP8, DCP4) | Metric | Before (main) | After (this PR) | |--------|--------------|-----------------| | Write amplification | 8× per chunk | 1× per chunk | | Lookup keys per chunk | 8 | 1 | | `all()` aggregation | Required | Eliminated | ### Breaking changes Both `dcp_rank` (rank-derived → chunk-derived) and `tp_rank` (self.tp_rank → self.tp_rank // factor) fields in store keys change. Existing cache entries are unreachable after upgrade. Requires one-time `reset_prefix_cache` call. Rolling update is safe — old/new keys coexist without interference, stale keys occupy capacity until reset. ### Additional safety guards - **NULL_BLOCK_ID guard**: Save and load skip chunks whose block slot is `NULL_BLOCK_ID` or out-of-range (protects against abort races). - **Token length clamp**: Save clamps `token_len` to `len(block_hashes) * hash_block_size` (prevents `AssertionError` after external cache hit). - **Empty key list early return**: Load exits cleanly when all chunks are filtered (prevents `ZeroDivisionError` in tp-rank rotation). ### Test coverage - 7 existing tests updated for new `_lookup_key_prefixes` tuple format - 15 new tests: chunk-derived save/load agreement, MLA/GQA/Mamba lookup key counts, factor restoration, write amplification, GQA tp_rank disambiguation, NULL_BLOCK guards, token_len clamp, empty key list, SWA+DCP, MTP+DCP, rolling update coexistence - All 124 unit tests pass ### Test commands ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py -v ``` ### AI assistance disclosure This PR was developed with AI assistance (Sisyphus/OhMyOpenCode). The submitting human has reviewed every changed line and run the full unit test suite. No model evaluation is needed as this change affects KV cache transfer infrastructure, not model output.

signals.title: [Performance][MRV2] Use uint16 for penalty output counts
signals.text: ## Purpose MRV2 stores generated-token counts in a persistent `[max_num_reqs, vocab_size]` int32 tensor. When `max_model_len <= 65535`, each count fits exactly in uint16. This change: - uses uint16 counts for those configurations and keeps int32 for longer contexts; - pads odd vocab sizes so two uint16 counters can share one int32 atomic word; - casts counts to int32 before applying penalties. There is no API or sampling-semantics change. For Qwen3.5-9B with `max_num_seqs=256`, the count state drops from 242.5 MiB to 121.25 MiB. On an L40S, available KV cache increased from 18.86 GiB to 18.97 GiB, and KV capacity increased from 435,665 to 438,272 tokens. ## Not a duplicate - #47540 optimizes persistent penalty statistics in MRV1. - #49697 is a broad P800 MRV2 port with Torch fallbacks. - #34213 removes `expanded_local_pos` from the MRV2 penalty path. None compresses MRV2 output counts. ## Validation ```text /tmp/vllm-test-venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_penalties.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_input_batch.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_input_batch_v2.py \ --confcutdir=tests/v1/worker -v 25 passed in 22.29s ``` Ruff, Ruff format, mypy 3.12, typos, SPDX, filename, forbidden-import, `torch.cuda` API, and boolean-context checks passed. The GPU regression suite was rerun against main at `5c9ff536`. Qwen3.5-9B was also tested on an L40S with MRV2 explicitly enabled. Baseline and candidate returned the same text, finish reason, and token usage with presence, frequency, and repetition penalties enabled. A 100-sample GSM8K regression run showed no quality regression (0.87 vs. 0.88, with no invalid outputs). AI assistance was used for implementation and validation.

signals.title: [Bugfix] Support MistralCommonBackend tokenizers in the xgrammar structured-output backend
signals.text: ## Purpose Structured output (`response_format` / guided decoding) fails with **HTTP 500** for Mistral models when the tokenizer is loaded under the default `tokenizer_mode="auto"`. `transformers>=5.5` returns a `MistralCommonBackend` for Mistral repos. That class subclasses `PreTrainedTokenizerBase` (not `PreTrainedTokenizerFast`) and is not vLLM's `MistralTokenizer`, so: - `is_mistral_tokenizer()` returns `False` (it requires `IS_MISTRAL_TOKENIZER` + `isinstance(..., MistralTokenizer)`), so the working Mistral path in `XgrammarBackend.__post_init__` is skipped; - the `else` branch calls `xgr.TokenizerInfo.from_huggingface()`, whose dispatch matches only `PreTrainedTokenizerFast`, tiktoken-backed, or sentencepiece-backed tokenizers, and otherwise raises `ValueError: Unsupported tokenizer type: ...`. `XgrammarBackend` is constructed lazily on the **first structured-output request** (`vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py` → `grammar_init()`), inside engine-core, so the uncaught `ValueError` surfaces as an HTTP 500. Plain completions on the same server keep working, which makes this look like a model problem rather than a backend one. ## Reproduction No GPU, no HF token, public model: ```python from transformers.tokenization_mistral_common import MistralCommonBackend from vllm.config import StructuredOutputsConfig, VllmConfig from vllm.v1.structured_output.backend_types import StructuredOutputOptions from vllm.v1.structured_output.backend_xgrammar import XgrammarBackend tok = MistralCommonBackend.from_pretrained("mistralai/Mistral-Nemo-Instruct-2407") cfg = VllmConfig(structured_outputs_config=StructuredOutputsConfig(backend="xgrammar")) backend = XgrammarBackend(cfg, tokenizer=tok, vocab_size=tok.vocab_size) backend.compile_grammar(StructuredOutputOptions.JSON, '{"type":"object"}') ``` On `vllm==0.27.0` (stock, from PyPI): ``` ValueError: Unsupported tokenizer type: <class 'transformers.tokenization_mistral_common.MistralCommonBackend'> ``` With this change: ``` grammar compiled: XgrammarGrammar ``` Diagnostics for that tokenizer: ``` MRO : MistralCommonBackend -> PreTrainedTokenizerBase -> PushToHubMixin -> object IS_MISTRAL_TOKENIZER : <absent> # -> is_mistral_tokenizer() == False isinstance(PreTrainedTokenizerFast) : False # -> xgrammar's first branch misses ``` ## Fix `MistralCommonBackend` already carries everything the Mistral path needs — `tok.tokenizer` is a `mistral_common.MistralTokenizer`, reachable as `.instruct_tokenizer.tokenizer` → `Tekkenizer` — and vLLM already has both a helper to detect it (`mistral_common_tekkenizer()`) and a wrapper that consumes it (`MistralTokenizer.__init__(tokenizer: MistralCommonBackend)`). So rather than adding new vocabulary-construction logic, this change routes a tekken-backed `MistralCommonBackend` through the existing `MistralTokenizer`, which already builds a correct `xgr.TokenizerInfo` (byte-fallback handling, `is_tekken` → `VocabType.RAW`, eos as stop token). The Mistral branch body is unchanged apart from reading the local `tokenizer` variable. ## Test `tests/v1/structured_output/test_backend_xgrammar_mistral_common.py` builds the backend from a `MistralCommonBackend` and compiles a JSON grammar. Verified both directions against stock `vllm==0.27.0`: - without the change: `1 failed` (`ValueError: Unsupported tokenizer type`) - with the change: `1 passed` ## Notes - The new branch is deliberately narrow: it triggers only when `mistral_common_tekkenizer()` returns a `Tekkenizer`, i.e. exactly the case reproduced above. Behaviour for every other tokenizer is unchanged, including the `backend="auto"` fallback path. - I did not extend this to sentencepiece-backed `MistralCommonBackend` instances because I have not reproduced a failure there. If maintainers know that path is also affected, widening the condition to any `MistralCommonBackend` would be a small follow-up — happy to do it in this PR if preferred.

signals.title: feat(rust): decode routed expert EngineCore output
signals.text: ## Summary Decode Python EngineCore routed-expert ndarray output into a typed Rust representation. ## Why Python already emits `EngineCoreOutput.routed_experts` as a rank-3 NumPy array. The Rust EngineCore client currently leaves that field opaque, preventing downstream Rust consumers from validating or using the routing trace. ## Changes - Decode inline and multipart ndarray payloads. - Accept uint8 and native little-endian uint16 payloads. - Validate rank, dtype, frame index, overflow, and byte length. - Keep gRPC and public API behavior unchanged. ## Checks - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` - `cargo test -p vllm-engine-core-client` (99 passed) ## Review note This change was prepared with AI assistance and reviewed line by line before submission.
signals.author: biswapanda

signals.title: feat(rust): accept preprocessed multimodal gRPC features
signals.text: ## Summary Add an independent Rust gRPC adapter for preprocessed multimodal feature specs. ## Why Callers that already produce version-compatible engine-ready multimodal kwargs should be able to pass those features directly, avoiding duplicate media preprocessing in the Rust frontend and mapping to Python `MultiModalFeatureSpec`. ## Changes - Add a protobuf source variant for inline preprocessed features. - Decode MessagePack `MmKwargsItem` data and lower it to EngineCore features. - Keep existing raw-image handling unchanged. - Require inline kwargs; cache-only references are intentionally unsupported. - Derive the EngineCore cache identity from modality and payload bytes. - Validate payload size, MessagePack complexity, tensor metadata, field metadata, placeholder ranges, and auxiliary-frame references at the gRPC boundary. ## Scope This is an independent gRPC adapter and does not depend on the routed-experts changes. It is a supported subset of the Python frontend contract, not a claim of full Python API parity. ## Checks - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` - `cargo test -p vllm-server grpc` (54 passed) ## Review note This change was prepared with AI assistance and reviewed line by line before submission.
signals.author: biswapanda

signals.title: feat(rust): expose routed expert traces over gRPC
signals.text: ## Summary Expose routed-expert capture through the Rust gRPC request and terminal response path. ## Why The Rust frontend needs a northbound API that can request routed-expert capture and return the decoded EngineCore trace to non-Python clients. ## Changes - Add `routed_experts_prompt_start` to gRPC response options. - Validate and lower the prompt offset. - Accumulate routed-expert chunks while enforcing a stable dtype and trailing shape. - Return compact dtype, shape, bytes, and start metadata on terminal output. - Keep OpenAI route behavior unchanged; their constructor updates only initialize the new internal field. - Add gRPC round-trip and invalid-offset coverage. ## Stack dependencies This draft is stacked on: 1. #52721 for typed EngineCore routed-output decoding. 2. #52703 for the Python-compatible sampling field. The branch currently includes snapshots of both prerequisite changes so the end-to-end path can be reviewed and tested. After the prerequisites merge, this branch will be rebased and the final diff will contain only the gRPC surface and aggregation logic. It does not depend on #52722. ## Checks - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` - `cargo test -p vllm-llm -p vllm-text -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server` - All affected package tests passed; the `vllm-text` suite has one pre-existing ignored network test. ## Review note This change was prepared with AI assistance and reviewed line by line before submission.

signals.title: [Attention] Enable adaptive verification for FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4
signals.text: ## Purpose Follow-up to #47808. The FlashInfer sparse MLA decode kernel (`flashinfer_trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4`) supports variable query lengths via `cum_seq_lens_q` / `max_q_len`, but the backend's metadata builders reported `AttentionCGSupport.UNIFORM_BATCH` instead of `ALWAYS`. Adds thin metadata builder subclasses (MLA + SWA) that declare `AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS`, mirroring the pattern established by the FlashMLA backend in `flashmla.py`, and wires them into `DeepseekV4FlashInferMLASparseBackend` and both attention classes. ## Test Plan - Existing `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py` validates FlashInfer sparse MLA kernel correctness (no behavioural change to the forward path). - End-to-end: run DeepSeek-V4 with `enable_adaptive_verification: true` on FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4 — the runtime assertion that previously raised the error now passes. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.title: [XPU][CI] fix hf runner
signals.text: **CI failure**: https://buildkite.com/vllm/intel-ci/builds/9188/canvas?jid=01a01374-c384-470a-b40c-b58c27dc7ceb&tab=output **Root cause**: During `hf_runner.__exit__`, the default threshold is 0.100; GPU0 usage was 17.74 GiB (76%), far exceeding the threshold, resulting in a timeout error after 240 seconds. **Fix**: In `HfRunner.__enter__` within `tests/conftest.py`, the XPU platform has been included in the same memory baseline recording logic used for ROCm; this ensures that `wait_for_memory_to_settle` in `__exit__` employs a dynamic threshold—based on the actual memory level at the time of `__enter__` plus a 5% buffer—rather than a fixed 10% threshold.

signals.title: [MooncakeStore] Report KV load tier in cache events
signals.text: ## Purpose Report the actual MooncakeStore replica tier in KV cache events. Mooncake already exposes whether a loaded replica is memory-backed or disk-backed, but this information was not propagated to `BlockStored` events. This change maps: * memory-backed replica → `CPU` * disk-backed replica → `STORAGE` * unknown tier → `None` Successful events are emitted only for blocks that actually load successfully. Scheduler lookup and connector protocol behavior are unchanged. ## Test Plan Run the focused MooncakeStore worker tests: ```bash PYTHONPATH="$HOME/vllm/.testdeps:$HOME/vllm" \ python -m pytest \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py \ -v \ --confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_connector/unit \ -k "test_recv_thread_emits_tiered_events_after_rotation_and_split or test_recv_thread_emits_unknown_tier_with_no_medium or test_recv_thread_does_not_emit_event_for_failed_load or test_recv_thread_skips_tier_lookup_when_events_and_logging_disabled" ``` An end-to-end MooncakeStore smoke test is also planned to validate real memory-backed and disk-backed loads on the A100 setup. ## Test Result Focused tier-related tests on the DGX/A100 environment: ```text 4 passed, 74 deselected ``` Validated: * tiered event emission for memory/disk replicas * unknown tier leaves `medium` unset * failed loads do not emit successful `BlockStored` events * replica-tier lookup is skipped when both KV events and tier logging are disabled End-to-end validation with real MooncakeStore memory/disk loads is still pending due to runtime environment setup and will be added once completed.

signals.title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Enable Qwen3.8-27B LM-only mode without vision tower
signals.text: ## Purpose This PR targets Qwen3.8-27B language-model-only deployments. Qwen3.8-27B is served through vLLM's Qwen3.5-compatible hybrid model path. When `--language-model-only` is enabled, all image and video limits are zero, so the vision tower cannot execute. Before this change, the shared model path could still construct and load the vision tower, and the runtime could still prepare encoder CUDA graphs even though no configured modality could use them. That unnecessary work is particularly costly for a 27B deployment: it consumes GPU memory that should be available to the language model and KV cache, and it can add avoidable initialization and CUDA-graph setup to a text-only serving path. This change: - Uses a metadata-only vision-tower placeholder in the Qwen3.5-compatible path used by Qwen3.8-27B when image and video limits are both zero. - Preserves the tower metadata needed by the language-model code path without allocating vision parameters or buffers. - Adds an explicit multimodal-encoder capability check and skips encoder CUDA graph setup when no configured modality can execute the encoder. - Covers both dense and MoE variants of the shared Qwen3.5-compatible path with regression tests. This is not a new model implementation. It makes the existing hybrid execution path honor text-only mode for Qwen3.8-27B and avoids allocating components that cannot execute in that deployment. ## Test Plan Unit tests: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_5_language_model_only.py \ tests/multimodal/test_registry.py::test_supports_multimodal_encoder \ tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py::test_embedding_only_mode_skips_encoder_cudagraph_manager \ -q ``` Regression vehicle and runtime smoke test on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090: - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`, the smallest available checkpoint exercising the same Qwen3.5-compatible hybrid implementation path. - Run once with `language_model_only=True` and once without the flag. - Generate a short text response from each configuration. The Qwen3.5-0.8B test is a minimal regression vehicle for the Qwen3.8-27B execution path. It is not intended to represent a Qwen3.8-27B memory measurement. ## Test Result Unit tests: ```text 11 passed, 14 warnings in 49.20s ``` Both runtime configurations loaded the real `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B` checkpoint and returned text. The LM-only run logged: ```text All limits of multimodal modalities supported by the model are set to 0, running in text-only mode. ``` Example generated response from the LM-only run: ```text The sky appears blue because the atmosphere scatters shorter wavelengths of light (blue) more effectively than ... ``` Memory comparison (same model and prompt; values are rounded from vLLM logs): | Configuration | Model loading | KV cache | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Default multimodal | 1.72 GiB | 34.70 GiB | | `language_model_only=True` | 1.53 GiB | 36.17 GiB | | Difference | **0.19 GiB less** | **1.47 GiB more available** | This measurement is from the 0.8B regression vehicle and is not presented as a 27B projection. It demonstrates the allocation that the LM-only path removes; for Qwen3.8-27B, the value is avoiding that unnecessary vision allocation and encoder setup within a much tighter model-serving memory budget. No model-accuracy evaluation was added because this change only controls multimodal module construction and encoder CUDA-graph setup; the language-model weights and text generation path are unchanged. A real-weight generation smoke test was run for both configurations. ## Duplicate-work Check No issue was assigned to this PR. Searches of open vLLM pull requests and issues for Qwen3.8-27B, Qwen3.5, `language_model_only`, vision tower, and multimodal encoder found no existing PR covering this fix. Related Qwen3.8-27B reports, including [#52654](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52654) and [#52682](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52682), address multimodal encoder TP behavior and CUDA-graph startup hangs rather than unnecessary vision-tower construction in LM-only mode. ## Documentation No documentation update is required; the existing supported-models documentation already describes text-only mode via `--language-model-only`. ## AI Assistance AI assistance was used to inspect the branch, draft this description, run the unit tests, run real-weight Qwen3.5 generation, and measure the memory difference. The human submitter must review every changed line and verify the reported test and runtime results before submitting the PR.

signals.title: [ROCm][Perf] Fuse DeepSeek-V4 mHC post/pre and RMSNorm with AITER
signals.text:
## Purpose This PR improves the ROCm DeepSeek-V4 mHC path by wiring the existing AITER fused mHC operators into vLLM. The ROCm path can now replace the previous sequence of separate mHC/RMSNorm kernels with the fused AITER flow: - `mhc_post` + `mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum` -> `mhc_fused_post_pre_gemm_sqrsum` - `mhc_pre_big_fuse` + `add_rmsnorm_quant` -> `mhc_pre_big_fuse_rmsnorm` For unsupported fused-RMSNorm hidden sizes, the path still uses fused post+pre where available, while preserving the standalone RMSNorm fallback. > [!NOTE] > The change is scoped to the ROCm/AITER path and does not change the CUDA or XPU implementations. --- Before fuse: After fuse (**38.35%** faster): ## Test Plan Benchmark with SA InferenceX `8k1k` workload: ```bash # Launch the server vllm serve /shared/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --port 8333 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --async-scheduling \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --distributed-executor-backend mp \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --trust-remote-code \ --moe-backend aiter \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \ --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' # Bench client CONCS=${CONCS:-"1 4 16 64"} for CONC in ${CONCS}; do NUM_PROMPTS=$((CONC * 10)) NUM_WARMUPS=$((CONC * 2)) python InferenceX/utils/bench_serving/benchmark_serving.py \ --model /shared/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --backend vllm \ --base-url "http://0.0.0.0:8333" \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 8192 \ --random-output-len 1024 \ --random-range-ratio 0.8 \ --num-prompts "${NUM_PROMPTS}" \ --max-concurrency "${CONC}" \ --num-warmups "${NUM_WARMUPS}" \ --request-rate inf \ --ignore-eos \ --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el \ --trust-remote-code \ --use-chat-template --dsv4 done ``` Accuracy test with `gsm8k` dataset. ## Test Result ### Benchmark To be completed... ### Accuracy Test To be completed... ---

signals.title: [Frontend] Map unsupported reasoning_effort to nearest supported level
signals.text: ## Purpose FIX #52738 Fixes the render-time failure when a client sends a `reasoning_effort` the served model's chat template does not accept. `ChatCompletionRequest.reasoning_effort` accepts the full ladder (`none`/`minimal`/`low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max`), but some chat templates validate against a subset and raise a Jinja error on anything else. E.g. the official `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` template validates directly against `('xhigh', 'medium', 'low')`, so `high` returns HTTP 400: `Unexpected reasoning effort high. Supported types are xhigh (default), medium, and low.` OpenAI-compatible clients and agent harnesses routinely send `high` or `minimal`, so the request passes API validation and then fails at template render time. Operators currently have to fork the template or rewrite requests in a fronting proxy. This PR adds two frontend flags: - `--supported-reasoning-efforts low medium xhigh` — declares the levels the template accepts. Unset (default) = passthrough, exactly today's behavior. - `--reasoning-effort-rounding {down,up}` (default `down`) — direction used to resolve an unsupported value on the ladder `minimal < low < medium < high < xhigh < max`: - `down`: highest supported level at or below the requested one; if nothing is at or below, the lowest supported level (`high` -> `medium`, `minimal` -> `low` with the example set). - `up`: lowest supported level at or above the requested one; if nothing is at or above, the highest supported level (`high` -> `xhigh`). Design points: - `none` (reasoning disabled) always passes through and cannot be listed in the supported set — the mapping never toggles thinking on or off. - Applied at the serving layer so every client derivation path converges before the template renders: Chat Completions (`OpenAIServingChat._effective_chat_template_kwargs`, which also covers batch and the Anthropic Messages API via `AnthropicServingMessages`), and the Responses API (entry of `_create_responses`, covering both the template and Harmony paths). - Each distinct (requested -> effective) remap is logged once via `logger.warning_once`. - Flag values validated at startup in `validate_parsed_serve_args`. In-tree precedent for the concept: the Harmony path keeps a private `REASONING_EFFORT` mapping in `entrypoints/openai/parser/harmony_utils.py` because GPT-OSS supports a subset. This PR makes the capability declarative and general instead of per-model-family. Files: - `vllm/entrypoints/openai/reasoning_effort.py` (new) — ladder constant, `normalize_reasoning_effort()`, flag validation. - `vllm/entrypoints/openai/cli_args.py` — the two `BaseFrontendArgs` fields + startup validation. - `vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py`, `vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/serving.py`, `vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py`, `vllm/entrypoints/generate/api_router.py` — constructor threading and the two normalization call sites. - `tests/entrypoints/openai/test_supported_reasoning_efforts.py` (new). - `docs/features/reasoning_outputs.md` — "Mapping Unsupported Reasoning Efforts" section. ## Not duplicating existing work Searched open issues and PRs for reasoning-effort mapping/clamping before writing this ("reasoning effort unsupported", "reasoning_effort map", "supported reasoning efforts"). Closest matches are parser-internal effort translations for a single model family (#39587 / #39597, nemotron_v3) and the Harmony-private map noted above — none provide an operator-configurable, model-agnostic mapping at the serving layer. Draft #38204 implemented the `reasoning_effort` field itself (already merged functionality), not subset handling. ## Test Plan ```bash uv pip install pytest pytest-asyncio tblib # tests/conftest.py needs these pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/test_supported_reasoning_efforts.py -v pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/test_reasoning_enable_thinking.py -v # regression neighbor pre-commit run --all-files pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --all-files --hook-stage manual ``` The new test file covers: the full rounding matrix in both directions (including floor/ceiling fallbacks), passthrough of supported values, `none`/unset passthrough, unset-flag no-op, unordered supported sets, flag validation errors, and two serving-level tests asserting the effective effort reaches both the request object and the rendered `chat_template_kwargs`. Manual E2E: serve `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` with `--supported-reasoning-efforts low medium xhigh` and confirm a `reasoning_effort="high"` chat request succeeds at `medium` (rounding=down) / `xhigh` (rounding=up), and that the same request returns 400 without the flags. Note: use the official checkpoint for the control — some third-party re-uploads ship modified templates that alias `high`→`xhigh` themselves (`minimal` works as a control value on those). ## Test Result Unit tests: ``` tests/entrypoints/openai/test_supported_reasoning_efforts.py ======================= 19 passed, 14 warnings in 5.55s ======================== tests/entrypoints/openai/test_reasoning_enable_thinking.py ======================= 14 passed, 14 warnings in 3.41s ======================== ``` All 19 new tests pass (remapping in both directions across the ladder, pass-through of supported values and `None`/`"none"`, no-op when unset, unordered supported set, validation accept/reject, and the ServingChat-level normalization checks); the 14 regression-neighbor tests pass. The warnings are a pre-existing `torch.jit.script_method` deprecation from site-packages, unrelated to this change. CLI parsing smoke (space-separated `nargs="+"` form works; comma form is rejected at startup with an actionable message): ``` comma form rejected as expected: Invalid --supported-reasoning-efforts values: ['low,medium']. Choose from ['minimal', 'low', 'medium', 'high', 'xhigh', 'max'] ('none' always passes through and cannot be listed). CLI smoke OK ``` Lint/typecheck: `pre-commit run --all-files` — every hook passed (ruff check/format, typos, clang-format, markdownlint-cli2, actionlint, pip-compile variants, mypy 3.10, SPDX headers, forbidden imports, and the rest). `pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --all-files --hook-stage manual` — Passed. Manual E2E on `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` (BF16, official checkpoint), commit `f7d825c26`, single-GPU serve with `--max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 64` (memory sizing only; neither flag touches the reasoning-effort path): - **Remap, rounding down** — flags `--supported-reasoning-efforts low medium xhigh`; request `reasoning_effort: "high"` → HTTP 200, normal completion. Log: `WARNING ... [reasoning_effort.py:77] reasoning_effort='high' is not supported by this server (--supported-reasoning-efforts=low,medium,xhigh); using 'medium' (rounding=down).` - **Remap, rounding up** — same + `--reasoning-effort-rounding up` → HTTP 200; log shows `using 'xhigh' (rounding=up)`. Corroboration that the remapped value reached the template: prompt_tokens 59 vs 17 in the down case (the `xhigh` reasoning-instructions block was injected). - **Stock control** — no flags; the same `reasoning_effort: "high"` request → HTTP 400: `{"error":{"message":"Unexpected reasoning effort high. Supported types are xhigh (default), medium, and low.","type":"BadRequestError", "param":null,"code":400}}`. No remap warning logged with flags unset (grep count 0). Supplementary run on a community re-quantization (`unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4`): its modified template aliases `high`→`xhigh` itself, so `minimal` was used as the failing value there — stock 400 (`Unexpected reasoning effort minimal. ...`) → 200 with the flags, remapped to `low` with the corresponding warning. This also shows the feature composes with templates that do their own partial aliasing. Net: the stock failure reproduces and this PR converts it 400 → 200, in both rounding directions, with the documented warning format. - [x] pytest: 19/19 new + 14/14 regression neighbor passed - [x] pre-commit clean (all hooks incl. manual-stage mypy-3.12) - [x] manual E2E on Qwen3.8 confirmed (400 → 200, both rounding modes) No model evaluation is required: the change does not touch kernels, sampling, or model output content. With the flags unset (the default) the serving path is byte-identical to current behavior; with them set, the only change is the value of `reasoning_effort` handed to the chat template. ## AI assistance disclosure This PR was developed with AI assistance (Claude Fable 5, also credited via commit trailer). The submitting human has reviewed every changed line and run the tests listed above.

signals.title: [Bugfix][Model] Guard DeepSeek V4 compressor CuTe DSL dispatch
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #52710. The DeepSeek V4 compressor imported the optional CUDA CuTe DSL implementation unconditionally for `head_dim == 512`. Builds without CuTe DSL therefore failed at dispatch. The fallback must also respect the cache layout. The Triton compressor writes the packed `fp8_ds_mla` representation (`torch.uint8`); it is not compatible with FlashInfer's plain BF16 or per-tensor FP8 cache rows. This change therefore: - uses CuTe DSL when it is available on CUDA; - permits the Triton fallback only for packed `torch.uint8` cache rows; and - raises a clear error for plain BF16/per-tensor FP8 rows without CuTe DSL. ## Duplicate-work check Before opening this PR, I searched open PR bodies for `52710` and searched open PRs using the area keywords `DeepSeek compressor CuTe DSL guard`. No open PR was addressing this issue. ## Test Plan - Execute `DeepseekCompressor.forward` with CuTe DSL unavailable for packed `uint8`, plain BF16, and plain FP8 E4M3 cache rows. - Assert the plain layouts fail before the Triton callable can launch. - Assert the packed layout dispatches to Triton. - On SM89+, execute the real packed Triton writer against a 584-byte cache row followed by a sentinel guard region and verify the guard is unchanged. - Run the Python-specific pre-commit lint and formatting hooks. ## Test Result - RTX 3050 (SM86), driver 610.88, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130: - plain BF16 forward rejection: **passed** - plain FP8 E4M3 forward rejection: **passed** - packed `uint8` forward dispatch: **passed** - real packed FP8 write with overrun sentinel: **skipped**, because native FP8 E4M3 conversion requires SM89+ - Focused pytest result: **3 passed, 1 skipped** - Kaggle probe: Tesla P100 (SM60), also below the SM89 requirement - `pre-commit run ruff-check --files ...`: **passed** - `pre-commit run ruff-format --files ...`: **passed** - `git diff origin/main...HEAD --check`: **passed** The SM89+-gated sentinel test is included for Ada/Hopper/Blackwell CI. ## Model evaluation Not run. This change does not modify model math, kernels, output values, or model loading. It restricts dispatch according to the existing cache representation and prevents an incompatible writer from receiving plain cache rows. No documentation update is needed because this fixes internal optional-kernel dispatch without changing the public interface. AI assistance disclosure: OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation and test execution. The commit includes an `Assisted-by: OpenAI Codex` trailer.

signals.title: fix(build): correct preprocessor guard for GDN decode to fix Ampere c…
signals.text: fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp was mistakenly placed inside the VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_KDA_DECODE block in ops.h. Since KDA is restricted to SM90+, this caused compilation to fail on pre-Hopper architectures (like Ampere SM 8.6) which support GDN but not KDA. This commit moves the declaration to the correct VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_GDN_DECODE guard. ## Purpose Building vLLM from source fails on Ampere (SM 8.6) and other pre-Hopper architectures with the following error: `error: ‘fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp’ was not declared in this scope` This occurs because `fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp` in `csrc/libtorch_stable/ops.h` was mistakenly placed inside the `#ifdef VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_KDA_DECODE` preprocessor block. Because KDA requires SM90+ (Hopper) or newer, the `VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_KDA_DECODE` flag is not defined on Ampere systems. However, GDN is supported on Ampere (`VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_GDN_DECODE=1`), so `torch_bindings.cpp` attempts to bind the GDN function, resulting in a compilation failure since the declaration is missing. ## Solution Separated the declarations. Moved `fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp` out of the KDA block and placed it under its correct `#ifdef VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_GDN_DECODE` preprocessor guard. ## Test - Verified that `pip install -e .` successfully compiles and installs on an Ampere (SM 8.6) system without build errors. --- <summary> Simple fix to ensure the fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp compiles under all archs and not just post ampere archs by placing the function under VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_GDN_DECODE preprocessor guard</summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details> **BEFORE SUBMITTING, PLEASE READ <https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing>** (anything written below this line will be removed by GitHub Actions) co author: Gemini

signals.title: Fix TurboQuant get_kv_cache_shape crash with hybrid models on cache_dtype_str='auto'
signals.text: ## Problem When using `--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_*` with hybrid models (e.g. Qwen3.8-27B), vLLM crashes during engine initialization with: ``` ValueError: Unknown TurboQuant cache dtype: 'auto'. Valid presets: turboquant_k8v4, turboquant_4bit_nc, turboquant_k3v4_nc, turboquant_3bit_nc ``` ## Root Cause Hybrid models have both full-attention and linear-attention layers. In `gpu_model_runner.py:_reshape_kv_cache_tensors()`, layers with `kv_quant_mode=NONE` (e.g. linear attention layers in Qwen3.8 that don't use standard KV cache) pass `cache_dtype_str='auto'` to the attention backend's `get_kv_cache_shape()`. The TurboQuant backend's `get_kv_cache_shape()` unconditionally calls `TurboQuantConfig.from_cache_dtype(cache_dtype_str)`, which rejects `'auto'` since it's not a valid TQ preset name. ## Fix Fall back to `turboquant_4bit_nc` when `cache_dtype_str == 'auto'`. The underlying KV cache tensor was already allocated with TQ slot sizing, so using the turboquant slot size for the shape is correct. ## Reproduction 1. Launch Qwen3.8-27B with `--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc` 2. Engine crashes at startup with the ValueError above ## Files - `vllm/v1/attention/backends/turboquant_attn.py`: 3-line fallback in `get_kv_cache_shape`

signals.title: [Bugfix][Observability] Emit CUDA Graph metrics in GPU Model Runner V2 (#52728)
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #52728. In vLLM V1, GPU Model Runner V2 (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`) is the default model runner. However, it omitted calculating and passing `CUDAGraphStat` to `ModelRunnerOutput`. Because of this: - `ExecuteModelState` did not track `cudagraph_stats`. - `sample_tokens()` and `pool()` instantiated `ModelRunnerOutput` with `cudagraph_stats=None`. - `SchedulerStats.cudagraph_stats` was permanently `None`. - `CUDAGraphLogging.observe()` was never invoked, causing `--cudagraph-metrics` output to be silently omitted from logs despite active CUDA Graph execution. This PR restores the CUDA Graph metrics observability feature in Model Runner V2: 1. Instantiates `CUDAGraphStat` inside `execute_model()` when `vllm_config.observability_config.cudagraph_metrics` is True. 2. Propagates `cudagraph_stats` through `ExecuteModelState` to `ModelRunnerOutput` in `sample_tokens()` and `pool()`. 3. Adds unit tests in `tests/v1/metrics/test_cudagraph_metrics.py` testing `CUDAGraphStat` observation, metric table formatting, and output propagation. cc @robertgshaw2-redhat @woosuk @Roger-luo @comaniac @Ningke-Li ### Non-duplication Verification - Checked open issues and comments on #52728 (`gh issue view 52728 --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments`). - Checked open PRs for #52728 (`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "52728 in:body"`): 0 open PRs. - Checked open PRs for keyword area (`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "cudagraph metrics"`): No open PR addresses this fix. ## Test Plan - New unit test suite in `tests/v1/metrics/test_cudagraph_metrics.py`: - `test_cudagraph_stat_dataclass`: Validates `CUDAGraphStat` structure and fields. - `test_cudagraph_logging_observe_and_table_generation`: Validates observation across modes, table generation, and state reset. - `test_logging_stat_logger_records_and_emits_cudagraph_metrics`: Validates end-to-end recording in `LoggingStatLogger`. - `test_model_runner_output_carries_cudagraph_stats`: Validates propagation through `ModelRunnerOutput`. Test execution commands: ```bash pytest tests/v1/metrics/test_cudagraph_metrics.py -v ruff check vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py tests/v1/metrics/test_cudagraph_metrics.py ruff format --check vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py tests/v1/metrics/test_cudagraph_metrics.py ``` ## Test Result ```text test_cudagraph_logging_observe_and_table_generation ... ok test_cudagraph_stat_dataclass ... ok test_logging_stat_logger_records_and_emits_cudagraph_metrics ... ok test_model_runner_output_carries_cudagraph_stats ... ok ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Ran 4 tests in 0.010s OK ruff check vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py tests/v1/metrics/test_cudagraph_metrics.py All checks passed! ruff format --check vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py tests/v1/metrics/test_cudagraph_metrics.py 2 files already formatted ``` --- *AI Assistance Disclosure: AI assistance was used in analyzing the regression, writing unit tests, and formatting the PR description per AGENTS.md.*

signals.title: [Kernel][AMD] Add MI300X FP8 tuned configs for Qwen3.8-27B-FP8
signals.text: ## Purpose Adds pre-tuned W8A8 block-FP8 Triton kernel configs for Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 on MI300X (TP=4), covering the 5 GEMM shapes this model hits that aren't in the shipped config set: `N=3584,K=5120`, `N=4096,K=5120`, `N=5120,K=1536`, `N=5120,K=4352`, `N=8704,K=5120`. Without these, vLLM falls back to a default block config and logs a sub-optimal-performance warning on every startup. Same category as #32042 (merged), different model/shapes. Also fixes a data-loss bug in `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_w8a8_block_fp8.py`'s multi-GPU mode: `save_configs()` overwrites the per-shape JSON file instead of merging into it, so splitting batch sizes across GPUs that share the same shapes lets whichever GPU finishes a shape last silently discard the other GPUs' batch-size coverage for it. Fixed by splitting whole shapes across GPUs instead, each GPU running the full batch-size grid for its own shapes. Checked for duplicates: no open or merged PR/issue touches these 5 shapes for this model on MI300X. ## Test Plan ``` python3 benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_w8a8_block_fp8.py \ --tp-size 4 --input-type fp8 --out-dtype bfloat16 \ --save-path vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/configs/ ``` Then served Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 with `vllm serve` (TP=4, MI300X) and sent real chat completion traffic against it. ## Test Result Each generated config has the full 18-entry batch-size grid (`1..4096`), matching the format of already-shipped configs — confirmed the multi-GPU fix works, since before it only 4 of 18 entries survived. Server startup log went from repeating "Using default W8A8 Block FP8 kernel config. Performance might be sub-optimal!" for these 5 shapes to: ``` Using configuration from .../N=4096,K=5120,device_name=AMD_Instinct_MI300X,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128,128].json for W8A8 Block FP8 kernel. ``` Server has been serving live production chat completion traffic on these configs since, with no correctness issues observed.

signals.title: [Bugfix][Core] Pin static FP8 quant pattern to group_shape=None
signals.text: ## Summary - Fix incorrect FP8 quant fusion when static per-group quantization is used. - Root cause: static per-group FP8 quant reuses the static quant op with `group_shape=(-1, group_size)`, but the pattern matcher only subset-matches kwargs. An unpinned static pattern could wrongly fuse per-group quant into per-tensor fused kernels. - Pin `group_shape=None` explicitly in `MatcherQuantFP8` static quant pattern construction. - Include `MatcherQuantFP8` in quant fusion pass `uuid()` methods so pattern construction changes invalidate the compilation cache. Changed files: - `vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/matcher_utils.py` - `vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/rms_quant_fusion.py` - `vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/act_quant_fusion.py` - `vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/attn_quant_fusion.py` - `vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/mla_attn_quant_fusion.py` ## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR Searched open PRs for static FP8 quant pattern / `MatcherQuantFP8` uuid / quant fusion cache invalidation. No open PR currently pins static quant patterns to `group_shape=None` or adds `MatcherQuantFP8` to these fusion pass uuids for this fix. ## Test plan - [ ] Reproduce prior failure: static per-group FP8 quant path with `torch.compile` + quant fusion enabled - [ ] Confirm per-group quant is no longer fused into per-tensor fused kernels - [ ] Smoke RMSNorm / activation / attention / MLA quant fusion paths with static FP8 - [ ] Confirm compilation cache invalidates after matcher pattern changes (uuid update) - [ ] Await CI compilation / quantization related jobs

signals.title: [Model] Add --video-max-pixels-per-frame to make Qwen3-VL video cost duration-proportional
signals.text: ## Purpose Qwen3-VL's video processor spreads `size["longest_edge"]` — a TOTAL pixel budget — across all sampled frames. Under a large budget (e.g. the model card's "Long Video Understanding" recipe, `longest_edge: 469762048` ≈ 224K video tokens), a short clip samples few frames at near-native resolution, so its token cost is nearly duration-independent: | Input (1080p) | Frames sampled | Prompt tokens | Tokens/frame | |---|---|---|---| | 90 s clip | 180 | 184,463 | ~1,020 | | 10 min film | 768 | 224,957 | ~293 | A 90 s clip costing ~82% of an hour-scale budget is a sharp edge: users raising the budget for long-video support pay it on every short clip too. This PR adds `MultiModalConfig.video_max_pixels_per_frame` (CLI `--video-max-pixels-per-frame`, default `None` = behavior unchanged). When set, each video's effective budget is `min(size["longest_edge"], num_sampled_frames * cap)`, applied per item in `Qwen3VLMultiModalProcessor._call_hf_processor` for presampled videos (vLLM's own loader path, where the sampled frame count is known). Setting `cap = budget / max_frames` gives every clip the same per-frame spend a fully sampled video gets, making cost scale with duration; long budget-filling videos are unaffected. Design notes: - Config-level option (precedent: `video_pruning_rate`) rather than an `mm_processor_kwargs` key, because config-level mm kwargs are re-merged before the HF processor call and unknown keys can leak into it. - Memory profiling stays exact: `get_dummy_mm_data` spreads the same total budget over `cdiv(budget, cap)` frames (clamped to the processor's `max_frames`) so the cap is not binding for the profiling dummy and the profiled maximum item still reaches the full budget. Without this, the 2-frame dummy collapses the profiled max item (we measured encoder cache 229,376 → 16,384, breaking all video requests with 400s). - Analytic max-token computation is intentionally untouched (a conservative upper bound in the corner case where the cap binds at `max_frames`). ## Duplicate check Searched open PRs/issues for per-frame video pixel budgeting ("video pixels per frame", "qwen3-vl video token budget"): no existing work addresses this. Related but distinct: #41239 (encoder budget CLI args), EVS/VidCom2 pruning (post-encoder token pruning; this PR reduces pre-encoder pixel spend and composes with it). ## Test Plan - New `test_video_max_pixels_per_frame` in `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen3_vl.py` (`Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct`, synthetic presampled videos): capped < uncapped; token count exactly duration-proportional (16-frame == 2 × 8-frame at equal per-frame budget); oversized cap is a no-op. - `pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen3_vl.py -q` - `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` (ruff, mypy, config-docstring validation, DCO) ## Test Result - `7 passed` (whole file, including the 6 pre-existing tests). - pre-commit: all hooks pass. - E2E on Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 (RTX PRO 6000, 224K-token video recipe, `--video-max-pixels-per-frame 611669` = budget/768): - 90 s 1080p clip: 184,463 → **52,701** prompt tokens (−71%), answer quality unchanged in side-by-side use. - 90 s clip + 10 min film in one prompt: 277,690 tokens, completed in 190.8 s with a correct, frame-accurate comparison answer. - Boot profiling intact: multimodal warmup 27.5 s, encoder cache unchanged, no video-request 400s. - Default-path regression: with the flag unset, processing is byte-identical (the new code path is `None`-gated). ## AI Disclosure Developed with AI assistance (Claude Fable 5). The human submitter has reviewed every changed line and run the tests above.

signals.title: [LoRA] Support per-request dynamic LoRA scale
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? Implements #52733 — per-request dynamic LoRA scale. Requests sharing one adapter in the same continuous-batching batch may each apply a different LoRA strength, and that strength can vary per request without baking separate adapter copies (one slot per scale). ### Design Mirrors `SamplingStates`: a per-request scale buffer `[max_num_reqs]` plus a `token_to_req` gather map, passed into the Punica `lora_expand` kernel. Effective scale for a token is `base_scale * request_scales[token_to_req[token_idx]]`. No per-token scale memory (1 KB per request vs ~128 KB per batch for a per-token array), and CUDA-graph compatible — the scale-aware kernel variant selected at capture is kept consistent with the runtime buffer that is refreshed every step. Gated behind `--enable-per-request-lora-scale` (off by default). When off, allocation and kernel launches are identical to today (zero overhead). ### API surface - `LoRAConfig.enable_per_request_lora_scale: bool = False` - CLI flag `--enable-per-request-lora-scale` - `LoRARequest.lora_scale: float = 1.0` — per-request multiplier on top of the adapter's own `alpha / r`. `1.0` reproduces stock behavior exactly. Deliberately **not** part of `__eq__` / `__hash__` (which key on `lora_name`), so a distinct scale does not consume an extra adapter slot. ### Two latent bugs fixed while wiring this through 1. **CUDA graph captured the scale-free variant.** Kernel specialization is via `tl.constexpr`, so the variant picked at capture is baked into the graph. Capture ran without scales, so at replay `lora_scale` never took effect. Fix: capture now supplies an all-ones `LoRAScaleInputs` when the feature is on, so the scale-aware variant is captured (`lora_model_runner_mixin.py::maybe_select_dummy_loras`). 2. **All-ones buffer not refreshed.** `make_lora_scale_inputs` returned `None` when every request's scale was `1.0`, so `_update_request_scales` early-exited and the runtime buffer was not refreshed; replay then read a stale `token_to_req` left over from the previous step — cross-request cross-talk. Fix: when the feature is on the scale path stays on every step; an all-ones table makes the gather a no-op regardless of stale `token_to_req` (`punica_gpu.py::_update_request_scales`). ### Scope Applies to the Punica expand path (linear LoRA layers). Not applied to fused-MoE LoRA layers — those keep the adapter's default strength, and a warning is logged once. ## Why is this not duplicating an existing PR? Per the AGENTS.md duplicate checks (`gh pr list --search "52733 in:body"` and `--search "per-request lora scale in:title"`), no open PR addresses this. The issue itself proposes this direction and notes "Happy to open a PR". ## Test commands and results Added `test_lora_expand_per_request_scale` to the existing `tests/lora/test_punica_ops.py` suite (parametrized over devices). It puts three requests on one adapter with scales `[0.25, 1.0, 2.0]` and asserts: - each token's output equals the unscaled output times its own request's scale; - an all-ones scale table is indistinguishable from not passing scales at all (guards the no-op / stock-behavior invariant). ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/lora/test_punica_ops.py \ -k test_lora_expand_per_request_scale -v ``` GPU kernel equivalence vs a reference implementation was verified offline with real ASR LoRA weights before this PR. ## Model evaluation results A/B evaluation on a real ASR LoRA adapter (the motivating workload): A path = current workaround (bake one adapter copy per scale, one slot per preset), B path = this PR (one adapter + per-request scale). | Condition | CN mean \|B-A\| | EN mean \|B-A\| | | --- | --- | --- | | off (noise floor, neither path uses scale) | 0.022% | — | | 1.0 scale, pre-fix | 17.184% | — | | 1.0 scale, post-fix | 0.038% | 0.028% | | 0.7 scale | 0.000% | — | | 0.9 scale | 0.060% | — | | mixed-scale batch (0.5/0.7/0.9/1.0, 8-way concurrent) | 0.21%* | — | \* Excluding 6 short utterances where the A path's `0.5` preset returned empty (an A-path-only anomaly, reproduced in serial single-shot, unrelated to this PR). signals.title: feat(core): add ProductionDebtPagedAttentionGate and TechnicalDueDiligenceLedger
signals.text: ### Summary Adds the native **ProductionDebtPagedAttentionGate** and cryptographic **TechnicalDueDiligenceLedger** under `vllm/engine/production_debt.py`. ### Problem Solved As enterprise AI architects and Forward Deployed Engineers deploy and orchestrate large-scale high-concurrency LLM serving systems with vLLM across multi-GPU Hopper (H100/H200) and Blackwell (B200) clusters, engineering organizations require real-time controls over **Enterprise PagedAttention v2 & Continuous Batching Production Debt & Technical Due Diligence**: 1. **PagedAttention Debt Index (PDI <= 12.0)**: Scoring continuous batching engine execution for physical KV block table fragmentation, CPU DRAM sequence preemption swapping, speculative decoding draft validation overhead, and engine step scheduling latency degradation. 2. **Physical Block Memory Multiplier (PBMM <= 1.08x)**: Monitoring peak utilized KV block allocations against physical GPU memory targets to eliminate HBM memory fragmentation waste. 3. **P99 Engine Step Scheduling Latency Ceiling (<= 4.2ms)**: Enforcing strict high-throughput continuous batching step boundaries across multi-worker serving instances. 4. **Deterministic Mutation Boundaries**: Enforcing `never_equate_intent_to_approval` across state-mutating speculative draft token verification, prefix cache hash assignments, and KV page table allocations. 5. **Cryptographic Technical Due Diligence Action Ledger**: Emitting immutable, SHA-256 hash-chained JSONL receipts providing audit-ready evidence for VC/PE Technical Due Diligence, M&A evaluations, and enterprise production readiness reviews. ### Features Added - `vllm.engine.production_debt.ProductionDebtPagedAttentionGate`: - `evaluate_engine_step()`: Evaluates physical block memory ratios, preemption swaps, and engine schedule latency, returning a normalized Production Readiness Score (0–100) with critical smell warnings. - `vllm.engine.production_debt.TechnicalDueDiligenceLedger`: - `record_paged_attention_event()`: Cryptographically links each engine step and KV page table execution event into an immutable SHA-256 chain. - `verify_ledger_integrity()`: Validates hash-chain continuity. ### Testing & Validation - Added `tests/engine/test_production_debt.py` with 3 automated unit tests validating clean PagedAttention v2 engine steps, degraded physical block fragmentation failure detection, and cryptographic ledger integrity (3/3 tests passing). ### Upstream & Commercial Context Maintained by [A2Z SOC](https://a2zsoc.com) for AI Forward Deployed Engineering, vLLM PagedAttention Hardening, and Technical Due Diligence. signals.title: [Bugfix] Surface TorchCodec video decode failures as client errors
signals.text: ## Purpose TorchCodec raises `RuntimeError` when decoding user-supplied video bytes fails. That exception type has no handler in the exception-handler registry (`ValueError`/`VLLMError` map to 400; raw `RuntimeError` falls through to the safety net), so the server returns **HTTP 500 with an ASGI traceback** for what is a client-input problem. The most common user-triggerable case: `seek_mode="approximate"` on a file whose container metadata overstates the decodable frame count — e.g. any stream-copied cut (`ffmpeg -c copy`). Frame sampling targets an index past the real end and torchcodec raises `Requested next frame while there are no more frames left to decode.` Reproduced end-to-end on a Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 server: request → 500. This PR converts `RuntimeError` from the torchcodec branch of `VideoBackend.load_bytes` to `ValueError` (chained with `from exc`), exactly mirroring the existing pattern in the `pynvvideocodec` backend (`raise ValueError("Invalid or unsupported video file.") from exc`). When `seek_mode="approximate"` is in effect, the message additionally tells the user to retry with `"exact"`: ``` HTTP 400 Failed to decode video with the torchcodec backend: Requested next frame while there are no more frames left to decode. This can happen with seek_mode='approximate' when the file's container metadata overstates the decodable frame count; retry with seek_mode='exact'. ``` Bundled docs: the "Video Decoding Backend" section gains operational guidance for the two TorchCodec knobs — when `num_ffmpeg_threads=0` (default) beats `1` and vice versa, with measured numbers (768 frames of 1080p H.264 on 16 cores: ~10 s at `0` vs ~49 s at `1`), and the approximate-mode metadata caveat with its new client-error behavior. ## Duplicate check Searched open PRs/issues for torchcodec error handling and video decode error mapping: no existing work. Related context: #46609 (torchcodec backend introduction, where `seek_mode` exposure was discussed) and the registry's own TODO to migrate raw-exception fallbacks to `VLLMError`. ## Test Plan - New `test_torchcodec_decode_failure_is_client_error` in `tests/multimodal/test_video.py`: RuntimeError from the decoder surfaces as `ValueError` with the original exception chained; the seek-mode hint appears only when `seek_mode="approximate"`. - `pytest tests/multimodal/test_video.py -k torchcodec_decode_failure -q` - `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` ## Test Result - `1 passed`; pre-commit all hooks pass (ruff, mypy, markdownlint, DCO). - E2E on a live Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 server (torchcodec backend): per-request `media_io_kwargs: {"video": {"seek_mode": "approximate"}}` on a stream-copied 60 s cut now returns the HTTP 400 above (previously 500 + ASGI traceback); the same file decodes fine with default `exact` (16.5 s request, 35,149 prompt tokens); unrelated requests unaffected. ## AI Disclosure Developed with AI assistance (Claude Fable 5). The human submitter has reviewed every changed line and run the tests above.

signals.title: [3/N] Share HiSparse host cache across TP ranks
signals.text: ## Summary This PR optimizes #51324 with the following improvements: - Resolve shared/private Host pool mode in the KV cache planner. - Fall back to private pools when the Indexer block layout cannot be represented by the shared mmap layout. - Propagate the resolved mode and physical Host block stride through `KVCacheConfig`. - Roll back the shared Host region when GPU KV allocation or HiSparse worker initialization fails. - Check physical Host RAM only in the shared mmap creator process. - Fail joiners promptly when the creator fails and unlinks an incomplete mmap. - Add real multiprocess same-slot visibility coverage. - Clarify logical versus physical `host_pool_gib` capacity and startup logging. This is intentionally based on `feat/hisparse-metrics` so it remains the [3/N] change in the HiSparse stack. cc @MatthewBonanni

signals.title: [ROCM][CI] Attention test speedup
signals.text: ## Purpose Two independent problems make `tests/kernels/attention` far slower than the work it actually performs, and both are addressed here. **1. `test_merge_attn_states.py` skips its entire matrix on ROCm without reason.** The test gates all 2592 parametrized cases behind an "only CUDA supports the custom merge_attn_states kernel" check. That is no longer accurate: the kernel source is not CUDA-gated in the build, so it is compiled for ROCm as well, and the op is registered and produces correct results there. The same file already exercises the native kernel on ROCm through its `both_empty` case, which passes today so the wide skip contradicts a test sitting next to it. The platform check moves from the test body to a module-level condition that accepts CUDA and ROCm. This unlocks 2592 cases of real kernel coverage on ROCm. Because the check was evaluated inside the test body, every skipped case still paid full setup and teardown, so the group was spending minutes to decide not to test anything. **2. Pure kernel modules pay a global cleanup after every single test.** An autouse fixture tears down the distributed environment and empties the allocator caches after each test. The modules touched here do not build an engine and do not initialize distributed state, so there is nothing for that teardown to clean — but it still costs a garbage collection and a cache flush per test, which dominates the group's runtime. These modules are marked with the existing `skip_global_cleanup` marker, the same mechanism already used at module level elsewhere in the test suite. Module selection is deliberately conservative. On ROCm the global cleanup also refreshes AITER class-level state that `monkeypatch` does not restore, so every module that touches environment variables or AITER, plus one that patches platform classes, is intentionally left untouched. Nothing is given up by that: the largest modules account for nearly all of the group's runtime. ## Test Plan Full `tests/kernels/attention` run before and after the change, on a single MI300, same flags and same GPU in both cases. The result was then confirmed a second time with a default environment, to rule out any influence of the flags used while measuring. `test_merge_attn_states.py` was additionally measured on its own, and the unlocked cases were verified independently against the Triton reference path. ## Test Result Whole group, single MI300: | | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Wall time | 46:34 | 10:08 | | Passed | 3207 | 5808 | | Skipped | 3703 | 1111 | | Failed | 0 | 0 | The group is 4.6x faster while running 2601 more tests, with no failures. `test_merge_attn_states.py` alone goes from 7:23 (6 passed, 2592 skipped) to 0:30 with all 2598 cases passing, fp8 variants included. All numbers above are from a local MI300. A speedup is expected in CI as well, since the removed per-test cost is not hardware specific, but the magnitude there is not measured here. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>
