signal.title: [Model][MoE] DeepSeek-V4: add opt-in FlashInfer moe_ep expert backend
signal.text: Add a FlashInfer `moe_ep` compute path for the DeepSeek-V4 mega-MoE experts, selectable at runtime alongside the existing native `deep_gemm_mega_moe` backend. - New module `vllm/utils/flashinfer_moe_ep.py`: model-agnostic plumbing only — backend registry and predicates, flashinfer `moe_ep` runtime bootstrap/finalize (bootstrap passes `device=torch.cuda.current_device()`, see review item on the LOCAL_RANK pin), NVFP4 prequant weight packing + epilogue alphas, config validation, and mega-layer construction. - New module `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/fi_moe.py`: `DeepseekV4MegaMoEExpertsFI`, a subclass of the native `DeepseekV4MegaMoEExperts` (same weight layout + loader; overrides weight finalize and forward with the flashinfer compute path), plus the DSV4-specific helpers (NVFP4 checkpoint detection, prequant pack, routing preprocess). - `model.py`: pick `DeepseekV4MegaMoEExpertsFI` when an fi backend is active and thread the swiglu activation clamp through; the `use_mega_moe` checks (including sequence-parallel eligibility) test membership in `MEGA_MOE_BACKENDS`. - `config/kernel.py`: register the two new names in the `MoEBackend` literal and host the `MEGA_MOE_BACKENDS` set next to it. Required, not cosmetic — `KernelConfig` validates `moe_backend` against that literal and rejects unknown values before the model is ever constructed. - New tests `tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_fi_moe_ep.py`: 11 unit tests (no GPU; flashinfer faked) covering backend registration, the device-pinned bootstrap, SP eligibility for every mega backend, config building, and the fp4 dequant helper. Two backends are added, selected by `moe_backend` string: | `moe_backend` | megakernel | notes | |---|---|---| | `flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm` | `deep_gemm_mega` | consumes an MXFP4 checkpoint verbatim (e2m1 + E8M0 per-32 scales) — the same recipe the native path uses, so this isolates the integration layer from kernel work | | `flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_cutedsl` | `nvfp4_cutedsl` | needs NVSHMEM. The checkpoint picks the weight path, not the kernel: an NVFP4 checkpoint is consumed prequantized, MXFP4 weights are dequantized to bf16 and requantized | Opt-in and off by default: the fi path is taken only when `moe_backend` is one of the two names above, so the native path keeps its own compute. Selection is by backend string alone. **Sequence-parallel ready; benchmark numbers below predate SP.** Since the numbers below were taken (v0.25.1), main integrated sequence-parallel MoE, which shards the MoE batch across TP ranks — 8x fewer tokens/rank at TP8 — and moves the e2e operating point down the tokens/rank curves in the microbenchmark tables. This PR runs SP exactly like native: mega-MoE eligibility, SP included, is keyed on the shared `MEGA_MOE_BACKENDS` set, with a regression test (without this the fi backends silently ran the MoE full-batch on every rank). On the current stack `fi_dg` holds 0.997–1.008x parity with native across prefill/decode cells on 8xB200. CuTeDSL perf tuning at the sharded operating points (knob autotune at sharded token counts, quantized combine wire) is ongoing and will come as follow-ups — this PR is the correct, SP-ready plumbing. The native `DeepseekV4MegaMoEExperts` class body is unchanged. Everything in the diff either widens the `use_mega_moe` checks from an equality test to `MEGA_MOE_BACKENDS` membership — which still matches `deep_gemm_mega_moe` — or adds the fi experts class and its config validation alongside the native one. `flashinfer.moe_ep` is a soft dependency — imported lazily inside the fi code paths, never at module import. The backends need flashinfer >= 0.6.17 (`BootstrapConfig.device`, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4348), which the vLLM FlashInfer requirements pin will carry; selecting a fi backend against a build without the moe_ep runtime raises a clear ImportError at config time. The fi backends also validate an SM100 device capability up front, and reject `--enable-eplb`, since the FlashInfer experts neither apply the logical-to-physical expert map nor report per-expert load. **Tests** ``` .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_fi_moe_ep.py -v # 10 passed pre-commit run --all-files # clean ``` GPU validation on 8xB200: smoke across MXFP4/NVFP4 checkpoints on both fi backends including remapped `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` (the regression case for the bootstrap device pin), the GSM8K gate below, and the e2e cells below, native vs fi. **Duplication check:** no open PR adds a FlashInfer moe_ep / mega-MoE backend (searched `moe_ep`, `mega moe`, `flashinfer moe`). **AI assistance was used** in developing this PR; every changed line was reviewed, tested, and is defended by the submitter. ## Reproducing the MoE-EP benchmarks > The section below reproduces the numbers as measured on **vLLM 0.25.1** (pre-SP stack) with that stack's matched FlashInfer/DSL pins; it is the environment the tables were recorded in, not the requirement for this PR (flashinfer >= 0.6.17 via the requirements pin, see above). Both harnesses, the patch, and the numbers live in a companion repo on a branch carrying only what a reproduction needs: **[mhoqueanik/moe_ep_benchmark @ `vllm_repro_8_gpu_v2`](https://github.com/mhoqueanik/moe_ep_benchmark/tree/vllm_repro_8_gpu_v2)**. [RUNBOOK_REPRO.md](https://github.com/mhoqueanik/moe_ep_benchmark/tree/vllm_repro_8_gpu_v2/RUNBOOK_REPRO.md) is the whole procedure — [§1 prep](https://github.com/mhoqueanik/moe_ep_benchmark/tree/vllm_repro_8_gpu_v2/RUNBOOK_REPRO.md#1-prep) (clone, image, checkpoints, venv), [§2 microbenchmark](https://github.com/mhoqueanik/moe_ep_benchmark/tree/vllm_repro_8_gpu_v2/RUNBOOK_REPRO.md#2-kernel-microbenchmark-25-min-per-shape), [§3 e2e throughput](https://github.com/mhoqueanik/moe_ep_benchmark/tree/vllm_repro_8_gpu_v2/RUNBOOK_REPRO.md#3-vllm-e2e--throughput) (offline in-process, plus the serving-mode server+client sweep in §3g), [§4 accuracy](https://github.com/mhoqueanik/moe_ep_benchmark/tree/vllm_repro_8_gpu_v2/RUNBOOK_REPRO.md#4-accuracy) — and every number below appears in [expected_results.md](https://github.com/mhoqueanik/moe_ep_benchmark/tree/vllm_repro_8_gpu_v2/expected_results.md) with its tolerance and the SLURM job it came from. All numbers: **one 8-GPU B200 node (SM100)**, flashinfer `4_5_2-perf-fix` @ `1ee41bcd` (https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4101), **nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.5.2** — vLLM 0.25.1's own pin. Do not unpin it: the DSL version and the flashinfer branch are a matched pair, and both harnesses assert 4.5.2 at run time. CUDA 12 and 13 both work. Backend is selected by the `moe_backend` string — one per run, no env gating: | config | `moe_backend` | checkpoint | |---|---|---| | native | `deep_gemm_mega_moe` | mx original | | fi_dg | `flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm` | mx original | | fi_cutedsl | `flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_cutedsl` | NVFP4 cast | In serving mode that string is an ordinary server CLI flag. One process serves an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (the decode-1k cell shown; the per-cell engine flags are the table in RUNBOOK §3g): ```bash hf download deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --revision 6e763230a9d263eca2023f1d4a5ce1bfe126cf48 \ --local-dir $CKPT/deepseek-v4-flash export MODEL_MX_FLASH=$CKPT/deepseek-v4-flash vllm serve $MODEL_MX_FLASH\ --trust-remote-code \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \ # or either fi backend above --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --block-size 256 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --max-model-len 4096 \ --max-num-seqs 1024 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \ --compilation-config '{"max_cudagraph_capture_size": 4096, "cudagraph_capture_sizes": [256, 1024, 2048, 4096]}' \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 ``` (fi_cutedsl additionally takes `FLASHINFER_MOE_EP_KNOB_CACHE=<repo>/vllm_e2e/results/knob_cache_ep8.json` and the NVFP4 checkpoint.) A second process benchmarks it over HTTP: ```bash vllm bench serve \ --backend vllm --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 \ --model $MODEL --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 256 --random-range-ratio 0 \ --num-prompts 1024 --max-concurrency 1024 \ --ignore-eos --seed 0 --save-result ``` The first client pass after boot is discarded as warmup and the timed passes are repeated with the median reported — the native decode baseline drifts run-over-run by more than the fi-vs-native delta, so single-pass serving numbers are quoted nowhere below. **EP8 throughout, but the two levels reach it differently.** The microbenchmark builds the MoE layer alone with synthetic weights, so there is nothing for tensor parallelism to shard: one process per GPU, `DP8 / EP8 / TP1`, no vLLM and no checkpoint. The e2e sweeps have a whole model to place, so they run `TP8 / EP8 / DP1`. Expert parallelism is 8 in both, which is the axis under test. One vLLM-side hazard is worth surfacing here rather than leaving in the runbook: **a cell that sets `MAX_CAPTURE` must also pin `CAPTURE_SIZES`.** With the dense default ladder, the cudagraph memory profiler reserves ~48 GiB/GPU for the flashinfer backends against a real ~6 GiB cost — the same ~6 GiB it estimates correctly for native — and the difference comes out of the KV cache. The tell is a backend that is *fast per step and slow overall*: better ITL than native, far worse throughput, because the engine is holding a fraction of the sequences requested. The other two ways to get plausible-but-wrong numbers are [§5](https://github.com/mhoqueanik/moe_ep_benchmark/tree/vllm_repro_8_gpu_v2/RUNBOOK_REPRO.md#5-things-that-will-bite-you). ## Microbenchmark That makes every ratio cross-checkpoint, which is what the GSM8K gate below is for. ### Offline (in-process `llm.generate()`, median of repeated rounds) **DeepSeek-V4-Flash** (4096 hidden / 2048 inter / 256 experts / top-6): | cell | native tok/s | fi_dg | fi_cutedsl | |---|---|---|---| | prefill-8k | 38986 | 40225 (1.032x) | 46584 (**1.195x**) | | decode-1k | 30845 | 31494 (1.021x) | 32741 (**1.061x**) | | 100K ISL / 1K | 29632 | 30230 (1.020x) | 32913 (**1.111x**) | | 32K ISL / 32 | 35700 | 36597 (1.025x) | 42028 (**1.177x**) | **DeepSeek-V4-Pro** (7168 hidden / 3072 inter / 384 experts / top-6): | cell | native tok/s | fi_dg | fi_cutedsl | |---|---|---|---| | prefill-8k | 15240 | 15630 (1.026x) | 20074 (**1.317x**) | | decode-1k | 12897 | 13157 (1.020x) | 15368 (**1.192x**) | | 100K ISL / 1K | 12223 | 12453 (1.019x) | 15053 (**1.231x**) | | 32K ISL / 32 | 14117 | 14435 (1.023x) | 18250 (**1.293x**) | Latency on the interactivity cells, fi_cutedsl vs native — Flash: TTFT 42.2s vs 49.3s at 100K and 12.8s vs 15.1s at 32K, ITL p50 51.9ms vs 56.1ms and 191.2ms vs 226.5ms. Pro: TTFT 95.0s vs 122.3s and 29.5s vs 38.4s, ITL p50 111.8ms vs 134.3ms and 441.3ms vs 573.9ms. ### Serving mode (`vllm serve` + `vllm bench serve` over HTTP, same four cells) Same workloads and per-cell engine settings, but the backend is the `--moe-backend` server flag and the measurement is entirely client-side over streaming HTTP — so tokenize/detokenize, HTTP and scheduling gaps are included. Total tok/s, median of the timed client rounds: **DeepSeek-V4-Flash:** | cell | native tok/s | fi_dg | fi_cutedsl | |---|---|---|---| | prefill-8k | 38074 | 39280 (1.032x) | 45643 (**1.199x**) | | decode-1k | 29419 | 29958 (1.018x) | 30861 (**1.049x**) | | 100K ISL / 1K | 29457 | 30059 (1.020x) | 32765 (**1.112x**) | | 32K ISL / 32 | 35661 | 36518 (1.024x) | 41932 (**1.176x**) | **DeepSeek-V4-Pro:** | cell | native tok/s | fi_dg | fi_cutedsl | |---|---|---|---| | prefill-8k | 15216 | 15609 (1.026x) | 19860 (**1.305x**) | | decode-1k | 12408 | 12619 (1.017x) | 14518 (**1.170x**) | | 100K ISL / 1K | 12190 | 12417 (1.019x) | 14909 (**1.223x**) | | 32K ISL / 32 | 13976 | 14290 (1.022x) | 18052 (**1.292x**) | **The two harnesses agree.** Serving lands within 1–3% of the offline absolutes and the fi_cutedsl ratio matches the offline column to ±0.022x on all eight cells (e.g. Flash prefill-8k 1.199x serving vs 1.195x offline; Pro 32K 1.292x vs 1.293x) — the kernel win survives the full serving stack, HTTP included. Interactivity latency over HTTP, fi_cutedsl vs native — Flash: TTFT p50 42.5s vs 49.7s at 100K and 12.9s vs 15.2s at 32K. Pro: 95.5s vs 122.4s and 29.9s vs 38.9s. **`fi_dg` is the control, and it reads 1.02x — in both harnesses.** It is the same deep_gemm kernel reached through this integration layer rather than a torch op, so its ratio measures the layer and nothing else — parity is the expected answer, and the fi_cutedsl deltas above it are kernel-side. A `fi_dg` far from 1.02x means the run is misconfigured, not that the layer is expensive. **The fi_cutedsl win grows with model size** — 1.19–1.32x on V4-Pro against 1.05–1.20x on V4-Flash, on identical cells, offline and serving alike. ### Accuracy gate — GSM8K, 200 questions, greedy, both checkpoints | model | native | fi_dg | fi_cutedsl (NVFP4 cast) | delta | |---|---|---|---|---| | Flash | 0.965 | 0.965 | **0.965** | +0.000 | | Pro | 0.880 | 0.880 | **0.890** | +0.010 | **The delta is what gates the throughput claim.** Because fi_cutedsl runs a different checkpoint, its numbers are only comparable if its accuracy is; ±0.010 on 200 questions is two questions. Both models pass. V4-Pro scoring 0.88 is a property of the model and this eval, not of `moe_ep` — all three backends agree exactly (176/176/178 correct), and it is not a truncation artifact: raising `--max-tokens` 512 → 1024 → 2048 moves accuracy 0.8800 → 0.8750 → 0.8750 while truncated completions only fall 15 → 14 → 13. ### Reproducibility of the numbers themselves Ratios are stable to about ±0.02x between sessions; absolute throughput moves more with node and thermal state. That tolerance is measured rather than assumed, three ways: repeating the entire offline set on a second pass, from the branch's own scripts against a freshly built venv, reproduced it to within **0.5% on absolute throughput and 0.008x on every ratio**; the serving 32K cell was measured in two independent sessions on different nodes and its ratios reproduced to **0.001x**; and the serving decode-1k cell re-run by hand from the runbook's pasted server/client commands landed within **1% absolute and 0.008x on the ratio** of the recorded sweep. One measured caveat drives the methodology: the *native* serving baseline drifts run-over-run by up to 8% under an identical warm protocol — more than the fi-vs-native delta on that cell — which is why every serving number above is a median of repeated client rounds with a discarded warmup pass, never a single run.

signal.title: [Model Runner V2] batch-sharded sample
signal.text: # Summary Currently before sampling, the full target logits are materialized, allocating memory of size `O(batch_size * (num_spec_tokens + 1) * vocab_size)`. This PR reduces that per-step memory allocation by a factor of `1/P` during tensor parallelism by sharding the logits and sampler inputs along the batch dimension, and sampling in parallel on a subset of the batch. Sharding the sampler inputs (`InputBatch`) was straightforward, and is handled by `BatchSharder.shard_sampler_inputs`. Requests are assigned to ranks by partitioning the request state index mapping (using `idx_mapping % tp_size`) in a deterministic way. From there, we derive the new sharded input batch CPU arrays & GPU tensors for the local rank, based on the requests that it "owns". Sharding the logits along the batch dimension is accomplished by having the model compute logits for only its slice of the vocab size by implementing the `compute_logits_local` method. After that, each rank has a `[num_tokens, vocab_size // P]` slice of the full logits. However, instead of all-gathering to get the full `[num_tokens, vocab_size]`, we instead all-to-all along the batch dimension, so that each rank ends up with `[num_tokens // P, vocab_size]`. In summary, this PR (1) reduces peak target logits memory from `O(batch_size * (num_spec_tokens + 1) * vocab_size)` => `O(batch_size * (num_spec_tokens + 1) * vocab_size / P)`, and (2) parallelizes the sampling operation, which can be particularly beneficial for TPOT whenever heavy sampling operations (e.g. top-k, top-p, block verification, etc) are performed. No changes had to be made to the `Sampler` or `RejectionSampler` because they work perfectly fine with smaller batch sizes as long as we shard the `InputBatch` properly, which we do. NOTE: A big motivation for this PR is to enable sharding of the draft logits. The cached draft logits from the speculator forward pass(es) are preallocated in memory for the worst case, with a size of `O(max_num_reqs * num_spec_tokens * vocab_size)`. We can reduce that by a factor of `1/P` as well, but sharded sampling is a prerequisite. # Speed-Bench 2K/2K, Temp=1.0, Top-p=0.95 ## DSV4 + DSpark (7 spec tokens) ### Concurrency 64 | Metric | signal.title: [ROCm][MoE] Split AITER CK and Triton MXFP4 W4A16 into separate backends
signal.text: # [ROCm][MoE] Split AITER CK and Triton MXFP4 W4A16 into separate backends ## Summary Split the overloaded `AITER_MXFP4_BF16` backend into two: - **`AITER_MXFP4_BF16`** → CK only (`AiterExperts`), behavior unchanged (gfx950). - **`AITER_TRITON_MXFP4_BF16`** (new) → aiter Triton `moe_gemm_a16w4` (`AiterW4A16ExpertsMonolithic`), available on gfx942 / gfx950 / gfx1250, selectable via `--moe-backend aiter_triton_mxfp4_bf16` and auto-selected for gpt-oss where CK is unavailable. On gfx942 this makes the Triton path the default for a16w4 (CK's `_supports_quant_scheme` returns False for `kMxfp4Static` off gfx950, so it declines and the next priority entry wins). On gfx950 CK still wins, so this is opt-in there. ## Not a duplicate No open PR splits the CK vs Triton MXFP4-BF16 backends. ## Test results Hardware: AMD MI300X (gfx942). Model: `openai/gpt-oss-120b`. ### Unit tests ``` pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py \ -k "rocm_mxfp4_moe_oracle or emulation_rounds_up or unsupported_reasons or preserves_native_tp_shard" → 9 passed, 2 skipped (AITER_MXFP4_BF16 / AITER_MXFP4_FP8, gfx950-only) ``` `ruff check` and `ruff format --diff` clean on all changed files. ### Accuracy `lm_eval` gsm8k (flexible-extract, TP1): `aiter_triton_mxfp4_bf16` = 0.903 vs `--moe-backend triton` = ~0.906 — parity. GPQA (low, temp 1.0) across TP, this PR vs `--moe-backend triton`: | TP | AITER Triton | OAI Triton | |---|---|---| | 1 | 0.6616 | 0.654–0.669 | | 2 | 0.6496 | 0.667 | | 4 | 0.6528 | 0.6502 | | 8 | 0.6660 | 0.67 | Note: gsm8k **cannot** detect the TP4 defect fixed here (it was 0.903 both ways); GPQA can. Anyone validating this path should use GPQA or watch the harmony non-terminal warning count. ### Performance `vllm bench serve`, random dataset, input 1024 / output 256, `--ignore-eos`, warmup = 2× concurrency (min 16), ≥200 prompts per point (1024 at c=128). Backends interleaved within each TP so machine drift is not confounded with the backend difference. **6720 requests per arm, 0 failed.** Geometric mean of ratios, AITER Triton vs OAI Triton: | metric | all 32 points | favors AITER | TP1 | TP2 | TP4 | TP8 | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | Output throughput | **+55.7%** | 30/32 | +55.1% | +49.8% | +56.6% | +61.7% | | TPOT mean | **−39.6%** | **32/32** | −38.7% | −36.7% | −39.3% | −43.7% | | E2EL mean | **−35.8%** | 30/32 | −35.5% | −33.2% | −36.1% | −38.1% | Output throughput by point: | | c=1 | c=8 | c=32 | c=128 | |---|---|---|---|---| | TP1 | +141.7% | +68.3% | +52.6% | **−6.8%** | | TP2 | +141.7% | +63.3% | +48.3% | **−14.0%** | | TP4 | +154.5% | +72.4% | +17.6% | +16.6% | | TP8 | +112.1% | +76.4% | +30.6% | +39.7% | ## AI assistance This change was developed with AI assistance. Andy has reviewed every changed line and run the tests and evals reported above.

signal.title: [ROCm] Give EngineCore cleanup grace after request abort
signal.text: This PR separates immediate request abort from the time allowed for EngineCore process cleanup on ROCm. `shutdown_timeout=0` still tells EngineCore to abort in-flight requests immediately. When both the configured request timeout and the process manager's remaining budget are zero, the parent now gives the EngineCore process a bounded 15-second cleanup window before escalating to a force-kill. - Non-ROCm behavior is unchanged. - Positive and `None` process timeout budgets are preserved. In particular, an exhausted budget originating from a positive request-drain timeout does not receive a new grace period. - The DP supervisor uses the same EngineCore process timeout plus its existing 5-second child-exit margin, so the ROCm zero/zero path waits for at most 20 seconds before force-killing the process tree. - After a successful, quiesced `shutdown_timeout=0` ROCm exit completes explicit executor, scheduler, distributed, and cache cleanup, the dedicated EngineCore process freezes the surviving GC graph to avoid another cyclic-GC scan during interpreter finalization. [AMD CI build 12007](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12007/list?sid=019ffc53-a1ab-472f-8b77-7c52a7d6edc0&tab=output) exposed the shutdown race: the request completed, but the zero timeout also gave the parent no time for ROCm cleanup before force-killing EngineCore. GPU memory then remained at 11.72 GB for the full 120-second release wait. The GC optimization is limited to a terminal child-process path: the exit code must be successful, the shutdown state must be `SHUTTING_DOWN`, no EngineCore work may remain, and the configured timeout must be zero. `gc.freeze()` does not disable reference-counted destruction. Cycles retained after the freeze are bounded to the immediately terminating dedicated process and are reclaimed when that process exits. Failure, outstanding-work, positive-timeout, and non-ROCm paths do not freeze the GC graph.

signal.title: [Core] Make prefix-cache NONE_HASH deterministic by default
signal.text: ## Summary Prefix-cache block hashes chain from `NONE_HASH`. When `PYTHONHASHSEED` was unset, `NONE_HASH` was seeded with `os.urandom(32)`, so every process produced different block hashes for identical content. This forced distributed KV cache users (shared-FS/object tiers, Mooncake connector) to pin a common `PYTHONHASHSEED` on every node just to get cache hits, and made the P2P tier refuse to start without it. This makes `NONE_HASH` derive from a fixed default seed instead, so independent instances share a prefix cache out of the box. `PYTHONHASHSEED`, if set, still overrides the default seed. Reported by a user who found that all vLLM instances need the same `PYTHONHASHSEED` to reuse KV cache across nodes. ## Why the per-process randomness is no longer needed The random seed dates to #12621, when prefix caching used Python's built-in `hash()` and a predictable `hash(None)` (constant on Python 3.12+) made intentional collisions feasible. The default hash algorithm is now **SHA-256**, whose collision resistance does not depend on a secret seed, and `cache_salt` is the supported mechanism for intentional cache isolation. The random seed therefore no longer adds meaningful protection while it does add operational complexity. This also makes CBOR-based hashes reproducible by default, so the prior non-reproducibility warning is removed. ## P2P tier The P2P tier no longer requires `PYTHONHASHSEED`: it resolves the same effective seed (`PYTHONHASHSEED` or the default) and still advertises and verifies it during the connect handshake, so mismatched peers are rejected loudly instead of silently missing. ## Docs FS/object tiers, Mooncake connector, and P2P tier docs are updated to reflect that a shared `PYTHONHASHSEED` is now optional. ## Not a duplicate Searched open PRs and issues for `NONE_HASH`, `PYTHONHASHSEED`, and `deterministic block hash`. The nearest hits are prefix-cache tooling/routing (#48838, #48369, #43483); none change the seed behavior. ## Tests run - `pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_manager.py tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_sessions.py` → **241 passed** - `pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py` → **89 passed** - Full `pre-commit` (ruff, ruff-format, mypy, typos, SPDX, config validation) → clean ## Model evaluation Not applicable: block content still fully determines the hash, so serving correctness (never serving another request's KV) is unchanged. This only changes the chain's starting seed. --- AI assistance (Claude) was used for this change. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: [Observability] Add OpenTelemetry tracing to GPU-less render server endpoints
signal.text: ## Summary Add OpenTelemetry tracing to the GPU-less render server (`vllm launch render`): every endpoint the command opens now emits a `SpanKind.SERVER` span linked to the caller's W3C trace context. - **`vllm/entrypoints/cli/launch.py`** — `run_launch_fastapi` built `VllmConfig(model_config=...)` directly, silently dropping the observability CLI args. It now passes `observability_config` via `AsyncEngineArgs.create_observability_config()`, so `--otlp-traces-endpoint` takes effect (this is the same path `vllm serve` uses through `create_engine_config`). - **`vllm/entrypoints/openai/api_server.py`** — `init_render_app_state` calls `init_tracer("vllm.renderer", otlp_traces_endpoint)` when configured, mirroring `AsyncLLM` in the engine. - **`vllm/entrypoints/serve/utils/api_utils.py`** — new `request_span` async context manager that emits a `SpanKind.SERVER` span with `extract_trace_context(raw_request.headers)` as the parent, so spans join the caller's trace when `traceparent`/`tracestate` headers are present. - **Routers** — render (`/v1/chat/completions/render`, `/v1/completions/render`), derender (`/v1/chat/completions/derender`, `/v1/completions/derender`, incl. streaming variants), tokenize (`/tokenize`, `/detokenize`) now wrap their serving calls in `request_span`. - **`tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render_tracing.py`** — e2e test launching the render server against a fake OTLP collector; asserts exported spans carry the trace/span IDs from the request's `traceparent` header. ## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR Open PR #39438 ("Extend OpenTelemetry instrumentation to remaining HTTP route handlers") covers the same area. It differs materially and is quite old (>2 months old). ## AI assistance This PR was created with AI assistance (opencode). A human reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

signal.title: [Bugfix][Structured Output] Stop XGrammar token batches at termination
signal.text: ## Purpose Prevent XGrammar from receiving additional tokens after accepting a terminating stop token within the same batch. Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52767. This covers two related problems: 1. `accept_tokens()` could return early after rejection without synchronizing LLM's cached `_is_terminated` state. 2. Batched speculative acceptance and validation could continue past a terminating token, producing XGrammar warnings and possible FSM state inconsistencies. ## Test Plan Unit test: ``` pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py ``` Live model test: ``` vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B --tensor-parallel-size 2 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder --reasoning-parser qwen3 --mm-encoder-tp-mode data --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3} ``` | Scenario | How the bug was triggered | Before fix | After fix | |---|---|---|---| | Tokens after termination | Aligned EOS with MTP draft slot 1 or 2, leaving additional draft tokens after EOS | Matcher processed tokens after termination and emitted warnings | 20/20 requests returned HTTP 200 without matcher errors | | Second advance after termination | Used strict JSON with `ignore_eos=true` to force another grammar advance after EOS | HTTP 500 | 5/5 requests returned HTTP 200 | | Normal tool calling | Sent strict-tool requests using `tool_choice=auto` and `required` | Baseline behavior | 10/10 requests returned correct tool calls |

signal.title: [Frontend][Core][Spec Decode] Per-request acceptance stats in OpenAI API responses
signal.text: ## Purpose Speculative decoding guesses a few tokens ahead, then checks them. Some guesses get accepted, some don't. How many get accepted tells you how well spec decode is working. Today you can only see this as a server-wide average on `/metrics`. You can't tell how any single request did. Tools like AIPerf want that per-request number, and right now they'd have to wrap the engine to get it. This PR reports it in the response. It's off by default; turn it on at server start with `--per-request-spec-decode-metrics summary` (or `detailed`). When it's off, the response is unchanged. It goes in the top-level `metrics` object — the same one the per-request timing metrics from #46768 use — under `speculative_decoding`: ```json { "choices": [ ... ], "usage": { ... }, "metrics": { "speculative_decoding": { "mean_acceptance_length": 1.2325581395348837, "draft_acceptance_rate": 0.07751937984496124, "acceptance_histogram": [39, 1, 0, 3], "num_spec_steps": 43, "num_accepted_draft_tokens": 10, "num_draft_tokens": 129, "num_spec_tokens": 3 } } } ``` `acceptance_histogram` is a dense list: index `j` is the number of verify steps that accepted exactly `j` draft tokens. `summary` gives the fields above; `detailed` also adds `per_step_accepted` / `per_step_drafted` arrays (one entry per step). Like the timing metrics, it's only reported for single-sequence requests and is `null` for `n>1`. It's a typed model (`SpeculativeDecodingMetrics`) and marked experimental so we can still change the shape. ## Relationship to prior work This continues @reed-meyerson's #47322 — thanks to them for the original design; they're credited as a co-author. The main evolution: it's typed and tucked into the existing top-level `metrics` object (converging with #46768's timing metrics, per review), leads with a compact histogram, and has a `summary`/`detailed` verbosity switch. A few others are nearby but doing something else: - #43310 also returns per-request spec-decode counts, but on vLLM's native `/inference/v1/generate` endpoint, at the request level, for RL-rollout tools (verl). This targets the OpenAI-compatible API. - RFC #48202 (impls #48204 / #48692) is about *changing* how many tokens get drafted per request (adaptive drafting) — a behavior change. This is behavior-neutral observability, and `detailed`'s `per_step_drafted` already records the proposed length per step, so it stays correct if drafting becomes variable. - #44487 adds a per-request acceptance histogram to the `/metrics` Prometheus page — server-side scraping, not response fields. ## Test Plan ``` .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_request_acceptance.py -v .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k spec_decod -v .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_error.py -k spec_decode -v .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py -k per_request_spec_decode_metrics -v ``` E2E (H100, n-gram spec decode, no draft weights needed): ``` vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --port 8000 \ --speculative-config '{"method":"ngram","num_speculative_tokens":3,"prompt_lookup_max":3,"prompt_lookup_min":1}' \ --per-request-spec-decode-metrics detailed --max-model-len 4096 ``` - Non-streaming: `metrics.speculative_decoding` populated for `n=1`. - `n=2`: `metrics` is `null` (suppressed, same as timing). - Streaming: rides the final usage chunk, so it appears only with `stream_options.include_usage: true`. - `summary`: no `per_step_*` arrays; default `none`: the field never appears. ## Test Result Unit + scheduler integration + serving-level tests (present for `n=1`, `null` for `n>1`, absent when off, coexists with timing) + the config-validation test all pass. E2E on NVIDIA H100 80GB: `metrics.speculative_decoding` matches the schema above; `n>1` suppressed; streaming gated by `include_usage`. Summed across single-sequence requests, the counts reconcile with the aggregate `vllm:spec_decode_*` Prometheus counters — they match exactly for all-`n==1` workloads (`n>1` requests still count toward the aggregate but aren't reported per-request). Representative `detailed` block (n-gram, `num_speculative_tokens=3`): ```json {"mean_acceptance_length":1.2325581395348837,"draft_acceptance_rate":0.07751937984496124,"acceptance_histogram":[39,1,0,3],"num_spec_steps":43,"num_accepted_draft_tokens":10,"num_draft_tokens":129,"num_spec_tokens":3,"per_step_accepted":[3,3,3,0,"…"],"per_step_drafted":[3,3,3,3,"…"]} ``` ## Model evaluation Purely observational — no change to sampling, scheduling, or generated tokens. Output is byte-identical across `none`/`summary`/`detailed`. No accuracy eval applicable. ## AI assistance AI assistance (Claude) was used for implementation and test authoring. All changed lines were reviewed by the submitting human, and the tests above were run and verified.

signal.title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Offload producer partial tails on request finish
signal.text: ## Summary Offload a producer's final partial Mamba `align` tail when the request finishes before another allocation can trigger copy-on-write. The core now finalizes the unchanged table source only when the request ends exactly at the registered boundary with no tokens in flight. The handoff is routed through `KVConnectorBase_V1` and `MultiConnector`; Mooncake retains the request until the next metadata build assigns a store job, then uses the existing per-job GPU block pin until every worker reports completion. ## Root cause Partial-tail offloads were emitted only when a later allocation triggered CoW and moved the registered boundary state into a durable private block. A prefill-only producer that finished at that boundary never allocated again, so its final partial Mamba state was dropped and could not be persisted for later prefix hits. ## Impact Later requests can reuse a producer's final partial hybrid prefix from Mooncake Store even when the producer ends immediately after prefill. Safety checks consume the marker without emitting a handoff if tokens remain in flight or computation advanced past the registered boundary. ## Duplicate-work check This is not duplicate work: - #51358 handles exact Mamba boundary states emitted during the CoW path; it does not finalize a producer that finishes before CoW. - #50409 changes local replay-boundary scheduling and does not implement connector finish-time handoff. - #52371 adds tests for separate EAGLE/Mamba prefix-cache defects and has no production fix. No open PR was found for the head branch or for searches covering producer partial-tail finish-time offload. ## Validation ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py::test_register_finished_partial_tail_notifies_every_connector \ -q ``` Result: **62 passed**. Pre-commit passed on every changed file, including ruff, formatting, mypy, SPDX, and repository policy hooks. A broader MultiConnector run reached 71 passed and 1 skipped; its remaining test could not start because the environment was not authenticated for the gated `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct` model. ## Model evaluation Not run. This PR remains a draft pending serving/model evaluation on a Mooncake deployment and human end-to-end review. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used to resolve conflicts, adapt the change to the current per-store-job pinning design, run validation, and prepare this PR. Before marking it ready for review, the human submitter must review every changed line and be able to understand and defend the change end-to-end.

signal.text: ## Purpose Add runtime LoRA lifecycle operations to the Rust frontend's existing gRPC APIs. - Add load, unload, and list RPCs to the existing `Control` service. - Let unary and streaming generation select a loaded adapter by name. - Reuse the same `LoraManager` registry for HTTP and gRPC so adapter identity, duplicate-name handling, capacity checks, and load order remain consistent across transports. - Allocate adapter IDs for HTTP loads while accepting explicit nonzero IDs from gRPC clients and rejecting ID collisions. - Centralize transport-independent `LoraRequest` validation for nonempty names and paths and nonzero IDs. signal.title: [XPU][Tests] Make tests device-agnostic
signal.text: ## Purpose Eight `tests/kernels/` suites hardcoded `device="cuda"` or gated on `torch.cuda.is_available()` / `is_cuda()` / `has_device_capability()`, so the Triton kernels they cover had no XPU coverage even though all of them already build and run there. Every commit does the same two things: resolve the device from `current_platform.device_type`, and widen the skip guard to CUDA-alike **or** XPU. References, tolerances and CUDA behaviour are unchanged. Part of RFC #48480. signal.title: [CI][ROCm] Prevent Git maintenance races during shallow fetches
signal.text: The ROCm test-image build in [Buildkite build 84415](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/84415/summary?jid=01a015b8-b7d5-453a-9aba-b7ea591fa5a9&tab=output#L86) failed before the Docker build with: ```text Deepening history to reach a version tag fatal: shallow file has changed since we read it ``` `ci-bake-rocm.sh` performs several shallow-history fetches in sequence. By default, `git fetch` may start automatic repository maintenance in a detached process. That maintenance can outlive the fetch that launched it and update `.git/shallow` while a later deepen operation is reading it, causing Git's consistency check to abort with exit status 128. The same [Buildkite step was retried on a different agent](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/84415/summary?jid=01a015c3-9b1e-4b7c-b33b-d265fe7aabe6&tab=output) and passed the history-deepening operation, image build, and `AMD image smoke OK`, confirming that the original failure was transient rather than caused by the PR's dependency change. This change: - adds `--no-auto-maintenance` to the centralized ROCm Git fetch helper; - applies the protection to both its timeout and no-timeout paths; and - preserves every fetch caller's existing arguments and failure behavior.
signal.author: AndreasKaratzas

signal.title: [Perf] Skip logits and sampling for unfinished prefills
signal.text:
## Purpose Model Runner V2 currently produces one sampling-logit row for every request in the common non-speculative path, including chunked-prefill requests whose prefill does not finish in the current step. Although these sampled tokens are discarded later by setting `num_sampled` to zero, the model has already performed the vocabulary projection and the sampler has already applied logits processors and sampling kernels. This introduces unnecessary GPU work, especially for workloads with multiple concurrent long prompts and a small `max_num_batched_tokens`. This PR avoids that work by: - Determining whether each request finishes prefill before constructing the logits batch. - Assigning zero logits rows to unfinished chunked-prefill requests. - Compacting mixed prefill/decode batches so output projection and sampling run only for requests that can produce an output token. - Short-circuiting `compute_logits` and sampling when the entire batch consists of unfinished prefill chunks. - Expanding compact sampled-token and NaN-count results back to the original per-request layout with a small Triton kernel, preserving existing downstream interfaces. - Preserving the existing pure-decode fast path. The change is limited to Model Runner V2's common non-speculative path. Speculative decoding remains unchanged. LoRA batches retain the existing dense logits layout because the per-request mapping is reused by prompt-logprob projection. This should reduce unnecessary vocabulary-projection and sampling work for chunked-prefill-heavy serving workloads without changing generated outputs. ## Test ### start server ``` VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \ vllm serve Qwen3.5-4B \ --served-model-name Qwen3.5-4B \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 8000 \ --enable-chunked-prefill \ --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \ --max-num-seqs 32 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \ --disable-log-stats ``` ### vllm bench ``` vllm bench serve \ --backend vllm \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 8000 \ --endpoint /v1/completions \ --model Qwen3.5-4B \ --tokenizer Qwen3.5-4B \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 8192 \ --random-output-len 32 \ --random-range-ratio 0 \ --ignore-eos \ --request-rate inf \ --max-concurrency 32 \ --num-warmups 16 \ --num-prompts 256 \ --seed 0 \ --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el \ --metric-percentiles 50,90,99 ``` ## Test Result ### before ### after - Output token throughput increased from **174.72 tok/s** to **191.97 tok/s**, an improvement of **9.87%**. - Mean TTFT decreased from **4311.56 ms** to **3904.83 ms**, a reduction of **9.43%**. - Mean TPOT decreased from **43.97 ms** to **40.15 ms**, a reduction of **8.69%**. ---

signal.title: [Docs] Explain cold vs warm prefix cache output at temperature=0
signal.text:
Documents why the same request can return different output at `temperature=0` depending on whether its prefix is already cached. This started out as an xfail test. Per review feedback the test is dropped and this is now docs only. ## What I found I looked into the cause on an H100 with FLASH_ATTN and Qwen3-0.6B and did not find a prefix caching bug in sampled output: - With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, and prefix caching still enabled, output is bit exact across 12 chained prefix lengths, 20 repeated requests, and with other traffic interleaved. The same runs in default mode drift by up to 2.6e-02. - The drift does not grow as the cache is reused. I chained prefixes 1 through 12 so each builds on KV that came from a cache hit, and the later ones are no worse than the earlier ones. - Where output changes, two tokens are nearly tied and greedy picks the other one. That matches the `' 
'` vs `' 

'` at token 0 in #40896. - Deterministic tie breaking would not fix it. The top two are exactly tied on the cold run (gap 0.0) and 0.125 apart on the warm run, so the values move. This is scoped to sampled output. It says nothing about `prompt_logprobs`, which has a separate reported issue in #42019. The previous version of this text implied cold vs warm divergence still happens with FLASH_ATTN under batch invariance. That did not reproduce, so it has been rewritten. ## Not a duplicate No open PR touches the batch invariance limitations docs. #42245 is nearby but different, it fixes uninitialized memory behind `prompt_logprobs` rather than documenting floating point variance in sampled output. ## Testing Docs only, no code change, so no model evals apply. I verified the FLASHINFER/TRITON_MLA auto disable claim against `vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/attention.py` and `mla_attention.py` rather than restating it from the old text. `pre-commit run` passes, including markdownlint. signal.title: [Attention][MLA] FlashMLA sparse: DCP on the fp8_ds_mla mixed-batch path + MTP
signal.text: DCP support for the `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` backend on the `fp8_ds_mla` KV path, including MTP spec decode under full cudagraphs. `fp8_ds_mla` is what the backend selector picks on Hopper for DSA models with small per-rank head counts (GLM-5.2 / DeepSeek-V3.2 at TP4/DCP4), and this path previously refused DCP outright. Earlier revisions stacked on #46076 and carried the sparse-indexer DCP machinery (global top-k merge, `--dcp-sparse-indexer-mode`); all of that has since landed in main via #46076 and its follow-ups, so the PR is now backend-side only: +234/−34 across `flashmla_sparse.py`, `flashmla.py` and one test file. (#45426 was our earlier standalone version with its own indexer; this supersedes it and reuses the upstream merge machinery instead.) ## Changes `flashmla_sparse.py`: - Opt the backend into the shared DCP decode merge (`can_return_lse_for_decode`): the fp8 mixed-batch kernel now returns decode LSE, sliced together with the head padding and reshaped to the `(tokens, heads)` layout the reducer consumes. - Under DCP the indexer emits global token ids: keep this rank's shard and convert to local `fp8_ds_mla` slots via `triton_filter_and_convert_dcp_index` with `compact_valid_to_front=False` — the scattered `-1`s stay in place and the fp8 kernel masks them natively, skipping the per-call front-pack. Rows where this rank owns none of the selected tokens get `(0, -inf)`, the identity of the cross-rank LSE merge, so they drop out of the reduce. - Allow varlen decode under DCP (`supports_dcp_with_varlen` when `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size == 1`): causality comes from the indexer's top-k indices, not kernel metadata. This is what makes MTP + DCP work under full cudagraphs. - Fail-closed guards instead of silent corruption: `ag_rs` comm backend only; fp8 mixed-batch path only (the split prefill/decode path returns LSE for decode tokens only, and the bf16 sparse path is rejected under DCP); a head-envelope guard rejecting configs where local and DCP-gathered head counts pad to different fp8 decode kernel envelopes (e.g. 128 q-heads at TP8/DCP8). `flashmla.py` (dense FlashMLA decode): flatten the kernel's `[batch, heads, seq_len]` LSE to `[tokens, heads]` for the DCP reducer — matters under spec decode, where `seq_len > 1`. Tests: `test_fp8_dcp_head_envelope_guard` in `test_sparse_mla_backends.py`, parametrized over local head counts × DCP world sizes, both accepting and rejecting cases. ## Testing 4×H200, GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4/DCP4/EP + MTP, `fp8_ds_mla`, current rebase: - `test_sparse_mla_backends.py` + `test_indexer_dcp_localize.py`: 140 passed / 0 failed (SM90). - Full cudagraph capture clean; exact needle recovery at 198k context across all ranks. - Warm decode 78 tok/s at batch 1, 854 aggregate at batch 32 (786k context window). - dcp=1/2/4 byte-identical on long (>2048-tok) contexts in earlier revisions of the same merge path. The branch has also been soaking continuously since mid-July on a production 4×H200 GLM-5.2-NVFP4 deployment (TP4/DCP4/EP + MTP) via nightly-based images carrying this PR. Related fixes in the surrounding DCP infra that this path exposed were split out and handled separately: #48379 (fp8_ds_mla boot on main, merged), #50823 (block-table width under DCP, merged), #50883 (offload block-size scaling under DCP, open). AI assistance (Claude) was used; every line reviewed by the submitter, tests run by the submitter. <details> <summary>History: pre-rebase description (union indexer mode, perf vs #45426) — superseded</summary> Earlier revisions added an opt-in `--dcp-sparse-indexer-mode {exact,union}` on top of #46076's global top-k merge, motivated by a ~30% batch-1 decode regression of the exact merge vs our standalone indexer (#45426): 52.0 → 36.4 tok/s warm at batch 1, with union recovering to 43.5 and a follow-up localizer opt to 50.7. After the indexer machinery landed upstream in its final form, the flag and the indexer-side changes were dropped from this PR; the numbers above no longer describe the current diff. </details>

signal.title: [Bugfix][CI] Release the shared ColBERT engine before `test_colbert_hf_comparison`
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes the four failing `test_colbert_hf_comparison` tests. The failure was introduced by #52570 (commit `53e211d29`), which replaced the per-test runners in `tests/models/language/pooling/test_colbert.py` with a module-scoped `colbert_model` fixture. Error message: > ValueError: Memory of devices devices=[0] not free after dur_s=240.14 (threshold='device=0: max(0.00 GiB, 0.080)') A module-scoped fixture is only finalized at the end of the module, so the engine of the last parametrization is still alive when the four `test_colbert_hf_comparison` tests declared in the same module, start their own runner. The live engine holds `gpu_memory_utilization` (0.92 by default) of the device, while a starting engine requires that same fraction to be free, so the second engine can never come up. The condition is proportional, so device size does not help. These tests cannot simply share the fixture's engine: they compare against a HuggingFace reference at `rtol=atol=1e-2` and therefore need `float32` rather than the fixture's `half`, and each one pins `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER`. So instead of sharing, the six tests that do share an engine now live in a class and their fixtures are class-scoped. pytest finalizes class-scoped fixtures when the class ends, before moving on to module-level tests, so the engine is always gone by the time `test_colbert_hf_comparison` runs. The startup savings of #52570 are kept: still one engine per model instead of one per test. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest -q tests/models/language/pooling/test_colbert.py ``` ## Test Result | Run | Result | Duration | | --- | --- | --- | | Before, whole file | 4 failed, 24 passed | 17m22s | | Before, `test_colbert_hf_comparison` alone | 4 passed | 2m49s | | After, whole file | **28 passed** | 2m57s | The four failures reproduce deterministically before the fix and only when the file is run as a whole, which confirms the shared engine as the cause. The run is also much faster afterwards, since the four VRAM waits that ended in a timeout are gone. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [ROCm][CI] Add AMD CI Pull-Request Commands
signal.text: Add an AMD-only mirror of the existing pull-request comment commands: - `/amd-ci run` - `/amd-ci run all` - `/amd-ci run nightly` - `/amd-ci retry` - `/amd-ci cancel` The new commands map explicitly to the Buildkite `amd-ci` pipeline, while the existing `/ci` commands remain scoped to the upstream `ci` pipeline. signal.title: [Core] Skip broadcasting mm tensor data to workers for prefix-cache-covered items
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #52040. ## Background: why this gap exists and who it affects The EngineCore->TP-worker broadcast was designed when request inputs were token IDs (kilobytes), so shipping them unconditionally was both correct and free. Multimodal grafted large tensors onto the same path, but for the classic workload (a fresh image per chat request) the workers genuinely need every tensor, so unconditional shipping remained necessary. What changed recently is multimodal **prefix caching**: there now exists a state -- "this item's tokens are fully KV-covered" -- in which the shipped tensors are provably never consumed, and the broadcast becomes pure per-request CPU overhead. The workload that exposes this is the emerging **streaming / agentic multimodal** pattern: an assistant that re-sends a rolling window of frames every turn (a live camera or video feed with a position-stable layout, so prefix caching covers all history images). For that pattern the cost is linear in window size on every request -- ~19 ms x 25 images = ~0.5 s of EngineCore CPU per turn in our deployment -- while the tensors themselves (fixed-size fp32 pixel patches, ~15.5 MB per image at our processor settings) are re-serialized into the ring for workers that will never touch them. As this workload class grows (streaming VLM assistants, video agents, multi-turn visual memory), the benefit of skipping compounds: it turns fully-cached multimodal TTFT from linear-in-images into flat. When a multimodal item's placeholder span lies entirely within the prefix-cache-covered region, no encoder run can ever be scheduled for it — yet its processed tensors are still serialized into the EngineCore→TP-worker broadcast, per unique item, on every request. For workloads that re-send a rolling window of images (fully prefix-cached), this makes TTFT grow linearly with attached image count: we measured ~19 ms per unique image at TP=4 with 15.5 MB `pixel_values` per image (evidence, flamegraphs, and a duplicate-image control experiment in #52040). This PR extends the existing `MultiModalFeatureSpec.data = None` convention (already used to skip API-server→EngineCore IPC on processor-cache hits) one hop further, to the worker broadcast: - `NewRequestData.from_request` strips `data` from items whose span is fully inside `num_computed_tokens` (new helper `strip_covered_mm_data`, same file). - The scheduler-side `Request` keeps the full features, so nothing is lost engine-side. - **Preemption safety**: requests resumed from preemption re-ship their features via a new `CachedRequestData.resumed_mm_features` field, re-stripped against the post-eviction computed-token count — so items uncovered by eviction regain their data before their encoder runs are scheduled. The worker applies these in its resumed-request branch. - The worker's encoder-input batching already tolerates `data is None` (existing `continue` in `_batch_mm_inputs_from_scheduler`), and the v2-runner path folds resumed requests through `from_request`, so it re-evaluates the strip condition naturally. For the rolling-window workload this removes ~25 tensor broadcasts per request; the fully-cached TTFT floor becomes flat in image count (~4 ms/image of parse+hash remains, which is intrinsic to content addressing). ## Test Plan - Added unit tests for `strip_covered_mm_data` in `tests/v1/core/test_output.py`: fully-covered and boundary items stripped, uncovered kept, already-None preserved, input list not mutated, zero-computed no-op. - Logic additionally verified standalone; I was not able to run the full test suite locally (no GPU dev box) — relying on CI here, and happy to iterate. - Live-workload validation available on our deployment (TP=4, Gemma-4-31B vision, 26-image rolling window): expected effect is the fully-cached floor dropping from ~630 ms to near the 2-image floor. Can report numbers once a build with this change is deployable. ## Test Result Unit tests pass locally at the logic level; awaiting CI for the full suite. ## Notes for reviewers - The strip is deliberately conservative: it only removes data for items that *cannot* have encoder runs scheduled given current `num_computed_tokens` at ship time; every path that changes that quantity downward (preemption/resume) re-ships. - An alternative, larger design would move mm tensor transport to `scheduled_encoder_inputs` time entirely (ship exactly when an encoder run is scheduled). Happy to pursue that instead if preferred — this PR takes the minimal-diff route.

signal.title: [RFC]: Derive KV offload save sources from prefix-cache records
signal.text: ### Motivation. Two related changes are proposed for KV connector save paths: 1. Derive offload sources from prefix-cache records for every KV-cache group instead of resolving a physical block positionally from a connector-owned copy of the request block table. 2. For connectors using this path, allow saving only when prefix caching is enabled and produces validated content keys. Together, these make one correctness argument cover both systems: if the GPU prefix cache says a physical block holds a particular prefix hash, KV offload may save that block under that key. This is narrower than the general offloading architecture in #19854 and the multi-tier design in #38260. It concerns how a save identifies the bytes belonging to a content key. Several public fixes expose parts of the same invariant: | PR | Relevant invariant | |---|---| | #51358 | Save exact core-selected Mamba boundary states rather than resolving them positionally | | #51766 | Preserve running-request Mamba CoW ownership after external hits | | #52372 | Keep GPU blocks referenced while asynchronous Mooncake store jobs read them | | #43468 | Publish self-describing offload events | | #44784 | Make MTP/EAGLE offloading lifecycle safe | | #46972 | Store interior chunk-boundary blocks under MTP/EAGLE | | #48596 | Save final blocks and prevent reuse races | | #49671 | Defer request finalization until the final store completes | These changes are useful and should be kept. The RFC asks whether the underlying save-source contract should be made content-addressed across cache groups so correctness does not depend on connector-specific exclusions and positional bookkeeping. #### Root cause A positional save typically has this shape: ```python block_idx = start // block_size block_id = block_ids_per_group[group_idx][block_idx] ``` That is valid only while logical position to physical block is a stable, total mapping. It holds for a conventional full-attention block table. It does not generally hold for hybrid cache managers: - Mamba managers may null and free superseded interior state blocks, relocate speculative scratch blocks, and move a durable partial-tail hash to a CoW destination. - Sliding-window attention releases head-prefix blocks as the window advances. - A connector-side mirror or append log does not necessarily observe in-place nulling, freeing, reuse, or CoW movement. A stale physical ID can therefore refer to another request's live bytes while the save still uses a valid prefix hash. Deduplicating backends can preserve that bad value because a later correct save sees the key as already present. Per-group exclusions contain known cases but leave the same trap for the next hybrid layout. The desired invariant is stronger: the source block and content key should come from the same cache transition. ### Proposed Change. #### 1. Record save candidates at prefix-cache insertion Every path that makes a block reachable under a hash funnels through `BlockPool._insert_block_hash`, including the operations used by: - `cache_full_blocks` for block-aligned boundaries; - `cache_partial_block` for sub-block entries; - `move_block_hashes` for CoW re-pointing. When recording is armed for a cache group, produce a self-contained entry such as: ```text (request_id, group_id, block_id, num_tokens, block_hash/content_key) ``` The connector consumes those records instead of reconstructing either the physical source or content key from positional request snapshots. Recording at the cache insertion boundary has several useful properties: - It inherits the prefix cache's reachability, retention, and null filtering. - A recycled block fails closed: reuse resets or replaces its hash binding, so a stale record can be rejected before pinning. - Full attention, sliding-window attention, and Mamba use the same handoff contract. - The request ID becomes a routing/lifecycle label rather than the source of truth for content identity. Durability remains a property of the producer transition. Two examples: - An append-only attention block or an off-table checkpoint whose model write has completed can be recorded when its hash is inserted. - A live Mamba partial-tail block must not be offered while the next forward can overwrite it. Record the durable CoW destination when the hash is re-pointed instead. Before accepting a record, verify that the block still holds the recorded hash. Once accepted, pin the physical block and release it only after all required ranks report the store attempt terminal. Success, deduplication, pressure drop, cancellation, and failure are all terminal for lifetime purposes; a failed save remains a future cache miss rather than a reason to retain an unbounded pin. Recording should be explicitly armed by a producer connector and scoped per cache group so unused records cannot accumulate. #### 2. Saves become record-driven; loads remain positional A load asks where incoming bytes should be written. The request's newly allocated block table is the correct destination address, so loads should remain positional. A save asks which physical block currently holds the content named by a key. That is a content lookup, so saves should be record-driven. This distinction also makes pinning and retry semantics explicit: - The connector pins exactly the blocks it accepts. - A preempted request's unaccepted records can be dropped. - Accepted records survive request completion or preemption as long as the hash binding remains valid. - Retry can be bounded within a handoff without keeping unrelated later blocks pinned behind a token watermark. #### 3. Require prefix caching for the record-driven save path With prefix caching disabled, no prefix-cache hash binding exists to validate a save record. The record-driven path should therefore not save. This is intended as a correctness rule for connectors migrated to this path, not an assumption that every existing offload implementation already follows it. The standard `OffloadingConnector`, `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`, LMCache integrations, and other connectors that maintain their own content index need an explicit decision: adopt the same validated record contract, provide an equivalent independent invariant, or remain on their current path temporarily. #### 4. Migration A staged migration can remain independently revertible and gated per group: 1. Move Mamba saves to record-driven handoffs, building on the exact-state and lifetime work in #51358. 2. Re-measure correctness, store coverage, streaming latency, and prefix-hit behavior. 3. Move sliding-window groups. This is a correctness step because head-prefix entries are mutable. 4. Move full-attention groups, then remove the positional save-source path and its per-group exclusions. 5. Revisit token-watermark state such as `_saved_offset`; self-contained handoffs may make range-based resume/retry bookkeeping unnecessary. Full attention is last because its table is genuinely append-only today. Moving it is primarily a uniformity and code-deletion argument. #### Expected benefits - One correctness argument: a save is valid only while the prefix cache validates the content-key-to-block binding. - Unified handling for full attention, sliding-window attention, and Mamba. - No latent correctness dependency on a connector's stale block-table mirror. - Well-defined pin/release behavior across asynchronous stores, preemption, failure, and request completion. - Less connector-specific machinery: positional source resolution, save masks used only for exclusions, and eventually range-watermark retry state can be removed. #### Open questions 1. What resume behavior must remain for any positional saver while migration is incomplete, and what should replace `_saved_offset`? 2. KV events are currently emitted from particular aligned-save paths. Should events be emitted directly from accepted/completed records so moving a group does not suppress publication? 3. Should `OffloadingConnector`, `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`, LMCache, and other positional savers adopt the same record type immediately or in separate follow-ups? 4. #51358 already provides exact Mamba handoffs, pinning, cross-rank completion watermarks, and fail-closed behavior. Should its emission site carry a self-contained content key and become the first implementation of this more general contract? 5. Should prefix caching be required globally for saving, or should connectors with an independently validated content index implement an equivalent capability/interface? 6. How should sub-block boundaries be represented so the record is self-describing across groups with different physical block sizes? ### Any Other Things. The closest existing RFCs are #19854 and #38260. This proposal does not replace either one; it tightens the save-source identity and lifetime contract within those architectures. Public implementation context: #51358, #51766, #52372, #43468, #44784, #46972, #48596, and #49671. AI assistance was used to draft this RFC. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signal.title: [Bugfix][AMD] Count store offers, not lookups, for CPU offload store_threshold
signal.text:
## Purpose store_threshold >= 2 asks CPUOffloadingManager to admit a block to the CPU offload tier only after it has been seen that many times. The counter was bumped in lookup(), and the callers make that unreachable for a cold prefix: - OffloadingConnectorScheduler._maximal_prefix_lookup breaks on the first MISS (offloading/scheduler.py:629), so on any given pass only the first not-yet-cached key of a prefix is ever looked up. - _lookup returns 0 before scanning at all when the GPU cache already covers the request (offloading/scheduler.py:751-753), so a resident repeated prompt is never counted. Admission therefore advanced by at most one chunk per two repetitions, and a GPU-resident repeated prompt was never admitted at all. Warming an N-chunk prefix took 2N+1 repetitions — for a 1M-token prefix at 768 tokens/chunk, on the order of 2,700 repetitions of the same prompt before the tier was fully populated. In practice the feature never warms up. Fix: count store offers instead. prepare_store() receives the request's whole offerable key set, so a block crosses store_threshold after that many repetitions of the content — independent of prefix length, and unaffected by the early return. ## Test Plan pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py -q, plus a reproducer (full source in the file) that drives the real access pattern — prefix scan breaking on first MISS, then a store offer of the tail — and counts repetitions to full residency. Also ruff check / ruff format --check. ## Test Result ---

signal.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][NIXL] Support PCP producers
signal.text: ## Purpose Support NIXL P/D disaggregation when the producer uses prefill context parallelism (PCP) and decode context parallelism (DCP) is disabled on both sides. PCP expands the worker world without increasing the KV-cache shard count, so every PCP rank holds an equivalent KV replica. NIXL should publish and wait for one replica instead of treating all PCP workers as distinct KV shards. This change: - records each NIXL worker's PCP rank; - publishes handshake metadata only from PCP rank zero on a producer; - forwards producer send completions only from PCP rank zero; - aggregates canonical sends over `TP * PP` while retaining full-world receive aggregation for bidirectional transfers; and - rejects PCP consumers, `kv_both`, and combined PCP+DCP configurations. It does not change the NIXL handshake protocol, worker addressing, transfer topology, KV layout, or token mapping. ## Scope and related work This PR is intentionally limited to `DCP=1` on both producer and consumer. It does not enable consumer-side PCP or combined PCP+DCP layouts. PR #50611 owns NIXL DCP support and its shard-routing/configuration changes. This PR is complementary: it only selects a canonical replica along the PCP axis when no DCP sharding exists. The duplicate-work searches for `NIXL PCP`, `prefill context parallel NIXL`, and `PCP producer KV connector` found #38433, #45340, #49109, #49342, and #50611. None implements this PCP-only NIXL replica selection on current main: - #50611 handles DCP sharding and currently requires PCP to be disabled. - #45340 handles CP-scaled scheduler block accounting. - #49109 is Mooncake-specific. - #49342 is the older mixed PCP+DCP version of this work and is superseded by this smaller PR. ## Tests ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_output_aggregator.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py \ -k "not abort_timeout_on_prefiller and not register_kv_caches and not reqs_to_send_deadline_rebased_to_worker_clock" \ -q # 149 passed, 7 deselected ``` ```bash .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files <changed files> # passed ``` Four-GPU P/D validation on `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat`: - Producer: `TP=1, PCP=2, DCP=1, EP=2` - Consumer: `TP=2, PCP=1, DCP=1, EP=2` - NIXL transport: local UCX TCP/CUDA IPC - Final-commit smoke: four prompts passed, including a long multi-block transfer - GSM8K: 1,319 questions, 5-shot, accuracy `0.636846`, invalid rate `0.000758` (159,800 output tokens) ```bash chg run -g 4 --timeout 45m -- env \ MODEL=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat \ GSM8K_QUESTIONS=1319 GSM8K_CONCURRENCY=64 \ bash ./pd_test.sh pcp2-nodcp-gsm8k \ '--tensor-parallel-size 1 --prefill-context-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel --max-num-batched-tokens 2048' \ '--tensor-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel' ``` ## AI assistance disclosure OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, testing, and drafting this PR. The human submitter remains responsible for reviewing every changed line and understanding and defending the change end-to-end.

signal.title: [ROCm][K3] Extend FP8 asm MLA prefill to non-divisor small head counts
signal.text: ## Context The AITER FP8 MLA **prefill** path (`mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd` + `mla_reduce_v1`) is gated on `num_heads % 16 == 0`. Kimi-K3 has 96 heads over `kv_lora_rank=512` → **12 heads/rank at TP8**, a non-divisor of 16, so its FP8 prefill falls back to the BF16 FMHA decompress path. That fallback builds a bf16 working set not covered by the FP8 KV-pool accounting and exhausts the activation arena at long context (K3 OOM'd at ~197k tokens, KV pool <4% used). This is the **prefill counterpart to #50578** (asm decode pad 12→16). MLA attention is independent per query head over the shared latent KV, so padding the query heads up to 16 and slicing the result back is exact. Rebased onto current `main` (includes merged #50578). Prefill-only diff: **+48 / −11**, one file (`rocm_aiter_mla.py`). ## Changes **FP8 prefill enablement (this PR):** - Relax the `_fp8_prefill_enabled` gate to also allow `0 < num_heads < 16`, and **gate it on FP8 KV** (`kv_cache_dtype_str == "fp8"` in the metadata builder; `is_quantized_kv_cache(kv_cache_dtype)` in the impl). Without this, a bf16-KV serve would reserve PS workspace unnecessarily. - In `_mla_fp8_prefill_attn`: replicate-pad Q/K/V to 16 via `AiterMLAHelper.get_mla_padded_q` (from #50578), run PS asm prefill + `mla_reduce_v1` at 16 heads, slice output back to `num_heads`. - Set `num_head_k = max(16, num_heads)` in `_init_fp8_prefill_ps_buffers` and `_build_fp8_prefill_ps_metadata` so work/reduce maps match padded tensors — also cuts partial tiles (`gcd(16,256)=16` vs `gcd(12,256)=4`), reclaiming **~6 GiB** PS workspace. Decode padding / Gluon routing is **not** in this PR — that is #50578 (merged). ## Dependencies / related - **#50578** (merged) — `AiterMLAHelper.get_mla_padded_q` / asm decode for non-divisor heads. - **ROCm/aiter#4452** (merged `a63ede724`) — 64-bit paged-KV byte offsets for >4 GB addressing. - Composes with **#48712** (gate PS workspace on fp8 KV) — this PR includes the same gate locally. ## vllm serve command **Hardware:** 8× MI355X (gfx950), TP8 **Model:** `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` (mxfp4) ```bash export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1 export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 export AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1 export SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1 export GPU_ARCHS=gfx950 export HF_HUB_CACHE=/dev/shm/hf-cache HF_HOME=/dev/shm/hf-cache export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 export VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=3600 export VLLM_HTTP_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE=900 export HIPBLASLT_WORKSPACE_SIZE=32768 export CUBLASLT_WORKSPACE_SIZE=32768 MODEL=/path/to/Kimi-K3 # e.g. /shared_nfs/models/Kimi-K3 vllm serve "$MODEL" --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8888 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --async-scheduling \ --distributed-executor-backend mp \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \ --max-num-seqs 64 --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \ --trust-remote-code --load-format auto --moe-backend aiter \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \ --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"]}' \ --enable-prefix-caching --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \ --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --enable-prompt-tokens-details --disable-uvicorn-access-log ## Test results ### Long-context prefill (functional) | | Before PR-A | After PR-A | |---|-------------|------------| | Fresh prefill @ util 0.95 | OOM ~197k tokens (BF16 FMHA fallback, KV <4%) | **470k (68 s)**, **590k (28.6 s)** OK | | PS workspace | ~4032 partial tiles (~12 heads) | ~960 partial tiles (~6 GiB saved) | ### Accuracy — GSM8K (lm-eval, full 1319-test split, 5-shot greedy, conc=32, ctx=16384) Patches applied for this run: **#50578 + PR-A + #50618 only** (no cgmem/MoE/kv_b_proj). Server at `gpu-memory-utilization 0.88`. ```bash export HF_HUB_CACHE=/dev/shm/hf-cache HF_HOME=/dev/shm/hf-cache export OPENAI_API_KEY=EMPTY python3 -m lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --apply_chat_template \ --include_path /path/to/InferenceX/utils/evals \ --tasks /path/to/InferenceX/utils/evals/gsm8k.yaml \ --output_path /tmp/eval_out --log_samples \ --model_args "model=moonshotai/Kimi-K3,base_url=http://localhost:8888/v1/chat/completions,api_key=EMPTY,eos_string=</s>,max_retries=5,num_concurrent=32,timeout=1800,tokenized_requests=False,max_length=16384" \ --gen_kwargs "max_tokens=12288,temperature=0,top_p=1" ``` | Run | n | strict-match EM | flexible-extract EM | |-----|---|-----------------|---------------------| | **With PR-A** (MI355X node 193, 2026-08-09) | 1319 | **97.04%** ± 0.47% | **96.97%** ± 0.47% | | Prior stack (cgmem+MoE+PR-A, node 1319, util 0.95) | 1319 | 96.89% ± 0.48% | 96.89% ± 0.48% | | Baseline replicate (stock + ASM deps, node 1319) | 1319 | 96.66% ± 0.49% | 96.66% ± 0.49% | No accuracy regression vs baseline; delta within run noise.

signal.title: [Quantization] Remove the dead ocp_mx_scheme branch from moe_kernel_quantize_input
signal.text: ## Purpose Shortly, remove dead code. `moe_kernel_quantize_input()` in `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/utils.py` carries an `ocp_mx_scheme: str | None = None` parameter and opens its body with a block that short-circuits `*_a_fp8` OCP MX schemes into `_fp8_quantize_dequantize` before the normal `quant_dtype` dispatch ever runs. Nothing reaches that block. This PR removes the parameter and the block. This is the follow-up @fxmarty-amd asked for when introduced the `quantization_emulation` path that superseded the block, in #46142 (`e368415daa`): > [r3452957212](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46142/files#r3452957212): > "Yes I don't think this code block is needed" > [r3453008225](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46142/files#r3453008225): > "Let's address in an other PR." This is the left TODO: ```python # TODO: Remove this `ocp_mx_scheme is not None` block and rely solely # on `quantization_emulation`. ``` and reconfirmed the ask in review on #43983 ([review 4904664996](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43983#pullrequestreview-4904664996)), linking `utils.py#L288-L301` — exactly the lines removed here. ### Why deleting it changes no behavior The only arm with behavior was `.endswith("a_fp8")`, and the only **reachable** a_fp8 scheme is `w_mxfp4_a_fp8` — `w_mxfp6_e3m2_a_fp8` and `w_mxfp6_e2m3_a_fp8`, both raise `NotImplementedError` earlier, in `QuarkOCP_MX_MoEMethod.get_fused_moe_quant_config`. For `w_mxfp4_a_fp8` the two paths are identical: | | deleted arm | surviving dispatch | |---|---|---| | condition | `ocp_mx_scheme.endswith("a_fp8")` | `quant_dtype == current_platform.fp8_dtype()` and `quantization_emulation` | | action | `return _fp8_quantize_dequantize(A, A_scale)` | `return _fp8_quantize_dequantize(A, A_scale)` | `_fp8_quantize_dequantize` takes only `A` and `A_scale`, so nothing else was being bypassed. `OCP_MXQuantizationEmulationTritonExperts.__init__` sets both inputs (`quantization_emulation = True`, `_quant_dtype = current_platform.fp8_dtype()`), and `TritonExperts.apply` forwards them. ## Test Plan ### Unit test ```bash python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py -q python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_cutlass_moe.py -q pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/utils.py ``` ### End-to-end test Same as what tested in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43983 - ROCm, MI325 - Model: amd/gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8 - MXFP4 emulation MoE backend --moe-backend emulation ## Test Result Coming soon. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>
