signal.title: [Kernel][ROCm] Cover OCP MX MoE emulation in the mxfp4 oracle test
signal.text: ## Purpose `test_rocm_mxfp4_moe_oracle` covers the Triton and AITER mxfp4 MoE backends but never `Mxfp4MoeBackend.EMULATION` — which is what ROCm parts *without* native MX support actually run. This PR adds coverage for it, one row per activation scheme the backend supports: - `w_mxfp4_a_mxfp4` (`EMULATION`) - `w_mxfp4_a_fp8` (`EMULATION_A_FP8`) Both new rows run on **gfx942**. The four existing AITER rows all require gfx950, so on MI300-class hardware this test previously exercised only the two Triton rows. > [!NOTE] > **The scope of this PR changed since it was opened, and this description has been rewritten to match.** > It originally also carried a source fix in `ocp_mx_emulation_moe.py` and `triton_moe.py` for two crashes on the `w_mxfp4_a_fp8` emulation path. #46142 (merged 2026-06-23) fixed those, so the source changes are gone and **this PR is now test-only**. The previous description described that fix and no longer applied. ## Test Plan ```bash python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py -q \ --deselect tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py::test_mxfp4_loading_and_execution_moe ``` ## Test Result Coming soon. ======================================= Original PR body (staled, for ones interested in the history) ======================================= ## Purpose Running an OCP MX MoE model with **fp8 activations** (e.g. `w_mxfp4_a_fp8`) through the **emulation** backend crashes on the first forward pass. There are **two** distinct crashes on this path, one per GEMM: 1. **GEMM1 (input activation):** `AssertionError: assert A_scale is None` in the bf16 Triton MoE kernel — the static fp8 activation scale leaks in from the quant config. 2. **GEMM2 (intermediate activation):** `NotImplementedError: ... quant_dtype='mxfp8' MOE quantization emulation` — the intermediate quantize call is missing the OCP MX scheme, so it routes to the unsupported `mxfp8` emulation branch instead of the fp8 QDQ branch. The emulation experts dequantize the MXFP4/MXFP6 weights to bf16 and run the plain bf16 Triton MoE, which needs no scales. This PR makes both GEMMs consistent: it nulls the activation scales in the emulation experts, and threads `ocp_mx_scheme` into the intermediate-activation quantize so the fp8 fake-QDQ path is used end to end. **Two files change:** - `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/ocp_mx_emulation_moe.py` (GEMM1) - `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/triton_moe.py` (GEMM2) ### Environment - ROCm, MI325 - Runtime base image: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.20.0` - Model: `amd/gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8` - MXFP4 **emulation** MoE backend `--moe-backend emulation` ### Traceback **Crash 1 — GEMM1, `assert A_scale is None`**: ``` File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 396, in determine_available_memory self.model_runner.profile_run() ... File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/gpt_oss.py", line 215, in forward x = self.experts(hidden_states=x, router_logits=g)[:, : self.hidden_size] ... File ".../fused_moe/experts/ocp_mx_emulation_moe.py", line 179, in apply super().apply(...) File ".../fused_moe/experts/triton_moe.py", line 250, in apply invoke_fused_moe_triton_kernel(...) File ".../fused_moe/fused_moe.py", line 746, in invoke_fused_moe_triton_kernel assert A_scale is None AssertionError ``` **Crash 2 — GEMM2, `NotImplementedError` mxfp8**: ``` File ".../fused_moe/experts/ocp_mx_emulation_moe.py", line 179, in apply super().apply(...) File ".../fused_moe/experts/triton_moe.py", line 322, in apply qintermediate_cache2, a2q_scale = moe_kernel_quantize_input(...) File ".../fused_moe/utils.py", line 314, in moe_kernel_quantize_input raise NotImplementedError( NotImplementedError: moe_kernel_quantize_input does not support quant_dtype='mxfp8' MOE quantization emulation. Please open an issue. ``` ## Fix ### File 1 — `ocp_mx_emulation_moe.py`: null activation scales in `__init__` Mirror the weight-scale handling. Activations are fake-QDQ'd to bf16 in `apply`, so no activation scale should reach the bf16 kernel. ### File 2 — `triton_moe.py`: pass `ocp_mx_scheme` to the intermediate quantize Thread the scheme into the GEMM2 input quantize, matching the GEMM1/input QDQ already done in the emulation experts. For `a_fp8` this routes to the fp8 fake-QDQ branch (returns bf16, scale `None`); for `a_mxfp4` it hits the no-op branch and proceeds to the identical `mxfp4` quantize (no change); for non-OCP configs `ocp_mx_scheme` is `None` and behavior is unchanged. ## Test Plan Integration smoke test — on ROCm, emulation backend, an `a_fp8` model. ```bash VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 \ python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model amd/gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --moe-backend emulation \ --trust-remote-code ``` ## Test Result - Before: crashes during profile run — first at `fused_moe.py:746` (`assert A_scale is None`), then after nulling the activation scales, at `utils.py:314` (`NotImplementedError: ... quant_dtype='mxfp8'`). Engine init fails before any forward completes. - After: both GEMMs run the bf16 path with the fp8 activations fake-QDQ'd; profiling and startup complete, and the model serves correctly. **gsm8k_platinum** (5-shot) on the served model: | filter | metric | value | |---|---|---| | flexible-extract | exact_match | **0.9413 ± 0.0068** | | strict-match | exact_match | 0.1919 ± 0.0113 | --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [ROCM][CI] Attention test speedup
signal.text: ## Purpose Two independent problems make `tests/kernels/attention` far slower than the work it actually performs, and both are addressed here. **1. `test_merge_attn_states.py` skips its entire matrix on ROCm without reason.** The test gates all 2592 parametrized cases behind an "only CUDA supports the custom merge_attn_states kernel" check. That is no longer accurate: the kernel source is not CUDA-gated in the build, so it is compiled for ROCm as well, and the op is registered and produces correct results there. The same file already exercises the native kernel on ROCm through its `both_empty` case, which passes today so the wide skip contradicts a test sitting next to it. The platform check moves from the test body to a module-level condition that accepts CUDA and ROCm. This unlocks 2592 cases of real kernel coverage on ROCm. Because the check was evaluated inside the test body, every skipped case still paid full setup and teardown, so the group was spending minutes to decide not to test anything. **2. Pure kernel modules pay a global cleanup after every single test.** An autouse fixture tears down the distributed environment and empties the allocator caches after each test. The modules touched here do not build an engine and do not initialize distributed state, so there is nothing for that teardown to clean — but it still costs a garbage collection and a cache flush per test, which dominates the group's runtime. These modules are marked with the existing `skip_global_cleanup` marker, the same mechanism already used at module level elsewhere in the test suite. Module selection is deliberately conservative. On ROCm the global cleanup also refreshes AITER class-level state that `monkeypatch` does not restore, so every module that touches environment variables or AITER, plus one that patches platform classes, is intentionally left untouched. Nothing is given up by that: the largest modules account for nearly all of the group's runtime. ## Test Plan Full `tests/kernels/attention` run before and after the change, on a single MI300, same flags and same GPU in both cases. The result was then confirmed a second time with a default environment, to rule out any influence of the flags used while measuring. `test_merge_attn_states.py` was additionally measured on its own, and the unlocked cases were verified independently against the Triton reference path. ## Test Result Whole group, single MI300: | | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Wall time | 46:34 | 10:08 | | Passed | 3207 | 5808 | | Skipped | 3703 | 1111 | | Failed | 0 | 0 | The group is 4.6x faster while running 2601 more tests, with no failures. `test_merge_attn_states.py` alone goes from 7:23 (6 passed, 2592 skipped) to 0:30 with all 2598 cases passing, fp8 variants included. All numbers above are from a local MI300. A speedup is expected in CI as well, since the removed per-test cost is not hardware specific, but the magnitude there is not measured here. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Kernel] Add adaptive layouts to TRTLLM MXFP8 linear backend
signal.text: ## Summary - Add opt-in `128x4` activation-scale layout support to the FlashInfer TRTLLM MXFP8 linear backend. - Add an `adaptive` policy that uses `8x4` for flattened activation rows at or below a configurable boundary and `128x4` above it. - Preserve the existing fixed `8x4` path as the default. This PR is stacked on #52204 and does not duplicate another open PR. Review the commit after #52204; the parent diff will disappear after that PR merges. ## Usage ```bash # Existing behavior VLLM_MXFP8_TRTLLM_LAYOUT=8x4 # Force the high-M layout VLLM_MXFP8_TRTLLM_LAYOUT=128x4 # Runtime selection, with an optional positive-integer boundary VLLM_MXFP8_TRTLLM_LAYOUT=adaptive VLLM_MXFP8_TRTLLM_SWITCH_M=256 ``` The adaptive boundary is configurable because the best crossover can vary with GEMM shape and GPU. The policy dispatches inside an opaque custom op, so it does not claim or modify user Inductor passes. ## Tests - `pytest -q tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp8_trtllm_linear.py tests/test_envs.py`: 80 passed - Pre-commit on all changed files: passed - Added Blackwell GPU tests for 128x4 numerics, M=256/257 adaptive boundaries, custom-op contracts, and fixed/adaptive CUDA Graph capture and replay. GB200 GPU and model-level performance validation is still in progress, so this PR is draft. ## AI assistance OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation and review. I reviewed the full diff and ran the tests listed above.

signal.title: [Kernel] Add FlashInfer TRTLLM MXFP8 linear backend
signal.text: ## Purpose FlashInfer exposes a TRTLLM backend for dense MXFP8 GEMM, but vLLM's `flashinfer_trtllm` linear selector currently covers NVFP4 only. This change adds an opt-in `FlashInferTrtllmMxfp8LinearKernel` selected with: ```text --linear-backend flashinfer_trtllm ``` The kernel prepares the TRTLLM weight and scale layouts once after weight loading. At runtime it keeps the actual activation row count, quantizes activation scales in the 8x4 layout, calls FlashInfer's TRTLLM MXFP8 GEMM, and slices a padded physical output back to the logical output width before adding bias. The backend accepts BF16 activations, matching the output type supported by FlashInfer's TRTLLM MXFP8 runner. The default `auto` priority remains CuTeDSL, CUTLASS, and the existing fallbacks. This PR does not add tactic hints, MoE kernel changes, or the high-M 128x4 activation-scale path. A follow-up can switch between 8x4 and 128x4 by M while reusing the same prepared TRTLLM weight. No matching open PR was found with the searches `MXFP8 TRTLLM linear` and `mm_mxfp8 trtllm`. The closest merged implementations are the NVFP4 TRTLLM linear backend (#39129) and the MXFP8 CuTeDSL linear backend (#46393); this change follows their backend registration and load-time preparation patterns. Open PR #52016 adds the independent B12X CuTeDSL package as an optional backend for SM120/SM121. It does not expose FlashInfer's TRTLLM MXFP8 runner and is not an alternative implementation of this change. AI assistance from OpenAI Codex was used to implement and test this draft. The author remains responsible for reviewing and defending the change before it is marked ready for review. ## Test Plan - Test explicit backend selection and exact SM100/SM103/SM107 gating. - Test N padding, weight/scale preparation, checkpoint-format reload, BF16-only input validation, idempotent processing, and invalid K. - Test actual-M 8x4 quantization, operand orientation, output slicing, and bias. - Compare real GPU output with BF16 matrix multiplication for low and high M. - Capture and replay the path with a CUDA Graph after prewarming. - Run a model-level accuracy test before requesting final review. ## Test Result ```text .venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/kernels/quantization \ tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp8_trtllm_linear.py -vv 11 passed ``` ```text .venv/bin/ruff check \ vllm/utils/flashinfer.py \ vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/mxfp8/flashinfer.py \ vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py \ tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp8_trtllm_linear.py \ tests/kernels/quantization/test_flashinfer_mxfp8_trtllm.py All checks passed ``` The GB200 test passed all five cases: three numerical shapes with M=1, 7, and 128, custom-op checks, and CUDA Graph capture and replay. The padded-output cases also verify contiguous logical output. The run used commit `37d19a7edd7559c3f8da24703d53feea198f96b4` and FlashInfer 0.6.16.post3, matching the vLLM dependency pin. Model-level accuracy and same-version performance results are not yet available, so this draft makes no accuracy or performance claim.
signal.author: seonjinn

signal.title: [Bugfix] Fix speculative decoding for short_conv (LFM2) models
signal.text: ## Purpose Supersedes #44296 (rebased onto main with the original commit and authorship preserved — thanks @Tonoken3); that PR has had failing pre-commit since opening and merge conflicts since July 6 with no author activity, so this revives it to make the merge cheap. Speculative decoding (ngram, EAGLE-3, any method) on `short_conv` (LFM2 / LFM2.5) targets silently corrupts output at the first rejected token: attention KV rolls back, but the conv sliding window retains rejected-token activations. `mamba2` / GDN already handle this via the spec-aware `causal_conv1d_update` path; `short_conv` was never wired in: 1. `MambaStateShapeCalculator.short_conv_state_shape` sizes the conv state `conv_kernel - 1` (no `num_spec`), so there is no room to roll the window back (mirror: `mamba2_state_shape` adds `num_spec`). 2. `GPUModelRunner._build_attn_group_metadata` never injects `num_accepted_tokens` for `ShortConvAttentionMetadataBuilder`, so the layer never sees the accepted-token counts. Changes vs #44296: rebased onto current main, fixed the mypy failure that blocked its pre-commit (`assert state_indices_tensor_d is not None`), added a regression test for the spec-widened conv state shape. ## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR #44296 is this fix (red CI + conflicts + stale for 8 weeks; original commit and authorship preserved here). #50146 bundles a rebase of the same target-side fix with 6 further drafter-side changes across 9 files and depends on other open PRs; this PR is the minimal, independently mergeable target-side correctness fix for released models. ## Test plan - `pre-commit run` (incl. mypy-3.10): pass. - New `tests/kernels/mamba/test_short_conv_state_shape.py`: pass. - E2E (we are the model vendor — Liquid AI serving team; LFM2.5-230M fine-tune + trained EAGLE-3 drafter with ~0.9/step acceptance, ROCm MI325X, v0.26.0 + this patch): without the fix, low-concurrency spec decode diverges after the first rejection (doubled/fused tokens, occasionally flipped outputs; under default cudagraphs it degrades to garbage from ~token 2). With it, `--enforce-eager`, `PIECEWISE`, and default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` all produce identical, correct output on fixed-seed content probes. AI assistance was used to rebase, fix, and validate this change; I reviewed every changed line and am accountable for it.
signal.author: zwischenraum

signal.title: [Bug]: --mm-processor-kwargs cannot scope an override to one modality: videos_kwargs is ignored by profiling while a flat "size" leaks into the image budget (Qwen3-VL)
signal.text: ## Your current environment <details> <summary>Environment</summary> ``` OS : Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS (x86_64) Python : 3.12.3 PyTorch : 2.13.0+cu130 CUDA runtime : 13.0.88 Nvidia driver : 580.126.20 GPU : NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GB) vLLM : 0.27.2rc1.dev193+gaa9903490 (nightly image for aa9903490) ``` Code paths are unchanged on current main (verified at 7ddb50788). </details> ## 🐛 Describe the bug The Qwen3.8 / Qwen3-VL model card's "Long Video Understanding" recipe raises the **video** processor's pixel budget (`size.longest_edge` from 25,165,824 to 469,762,048, i.e. ~12K to ~224K video tokens). The natural way to apply a processor override in vLLM is `--mm-processor-kwargs`, and per the review guidance in #52754, that flag is meant to correspond directly to what the HF processor accepts. The HF processor does accept a modality-scoped form: `Qwen3VLProcessor._merge_kwargs` honors `videos_kwargs={"size": ...}` and applies it to videos only (verified against transformers 5.x). But vLLM cannot express this override safely in either form: 1. **Scoped form is silently ignored by vLLM's own reads.** `--mm-processor-kwargs '{"videos_kwargs": {"size": ...}}'` passes CLI validation and reaches the HF processor call (it survives the `allow_var_kwargs` filter in `call_hf_processor`), but every place vLLM consults mm kwargs itself — `get_max_video_tokens`, the dummy-input builder, the data parser's per-item size overrides in `qwen3_vl.py` — only reads the flat namespace. Result: encoder-cache profiling reserves for a ~12K-token max item while runtime processing can legitimately produce ~229K-token items. That is the known under-reservation failure class (encoder cache starvation / livelock, cf. #51603). 2. **Flat form leaks across modalities.** `--mm-processor-kwargs '{"size": {"longest_edge": 469762048, ...}}'` does lift the video budget, but the same flat key is read by the image paths and passed to the image processor, so the maximum image item goes from ~16K to ~448K tokens. Observed at boot: ``` Encoder cache will be initialized with a budget of 458752 tokens, and profiled with 1 image items of the maximum feature size. ``` Profiling then runs a 448K-token image dummy through the vision encoder (grinds for minutes, and with the default processor cache it aborts boot, see #52835). So the only working way to apply the model card's own recipe today is to edit `video_preprocessor_config.json` inside the cached checkpoint, which is not reproducible from serve config and silently reverts on re-download. ### Reproduction (CPU-only, no GPU needed) ```python from vllm.config import ModelConfig from vllm.multimodal import MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY def probe(mm_kwargs, label): mc = ModelConfig(model="Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8", mm_processor_kwargs=mm_kwargs) info = MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY.create_processor(mc).info v = info.get_max_video_tokens(seq_len=500000, mm_counts={"video": 1, "image": 1}) print(label, "video =", v, "image =", info.get_max_image_tokens()) probe(None, "stock") probe({"videos_kwargs": {"size": {"longest_edge": 469762048, "shortest_edge": 4096}}}, "scoped") probe({"size": {"longest_edge": 469762048, "shortest_edge": 4096}}, "flat") ``` Output on aa9903490: ``` stock video = 12288 image = 16384 scoped video = 12288 image = 16384 <- scoped override ignored flat video = 229376 image = 458752 <- image budget contaminated ``` Expected: the scoped row should read `video = 229376, image = 16384` (matching what the HF processor itself would do with the same kwargs), and profiling should agree with runtime processing. I have a working fix that overlays HF-style `<modality>s_kwargs` onto the flat namespace at each of Qwen3-VL's mm-kwargs read sites (flat kwargs keep their current shared-namespace behavior): https://github.com/dkrisman/vllm/commits/feat/mm-kwargs-modality-scoped With it, the probe above returns `video = 229376, image = 16384` for the scoped form. Happy to turn it into a PR if this direction is acceptable, or to discuss a generic (non-model-specific) resolution layer instead.
signal.author: dkrisman

signal.title: [Bug]: EngineCore fails to start with ValueError("value too large") when one processed multi-modal item exceeds mm_processor_cache_gb
signal.text: ## Your current environment <details> <summary>Environment</summary> ``` OS : Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS (x86_64) Python : 3.12.3 PyTorch : 2.13.0+cu130 CUDA runtime : 13.0.88 Nvidia driver : 580.126.20 GPU : NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GB) vLLM : 0.27.2rc1.dev193+gaa9903490 (nightly image for aa9903490) ``` Code paths are unchanged on current main (verified at 7ddb50788). </details> ## 🐛 Describe the bug `cachetools.Cache.__setitem__` raises `ValueError("value too large")` when a single item is bigger than the cache's entire `maxsize`. The multi-modal processor caches (`vllm/multimodal/cache.py`) insert processed items without guarding against this, so any configuration where one processed multi-modal item exceeds `mm_processor_cache_gb` turns into a hard failure instead of an uncached item. The worst case is memory profiling: the profiling dummy is by construction the maximum-size item, so if the model's max item is larger than the cache, the engine cannot even boot. Hit in practice with the Qwen3.8 model card's "Long Video Understanding" recipe (video pixel budget 469,762,048, a processed max-size video item is several GiB) and the default `mm_processor_cache_gb=4`: ``` (EngineCore pid=520) ERROR [core.py:1346] EngineCore failed to start. ... File ".../vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py", line 1650, in _cached_apply_hf_processor File ".../vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py", line 1531, in _merge_mm_kwargs File ".../vllm/multimodal/cache.py", line 392, in get_and_update_item File ".../cachetools/__init__.py", line 299, in __setitem__ File ".../cachetools/__init__.py", line 81, in __setitem__ raise ValueError("value too large") ValueError: value too large ``` Raising `--mm-processor-cache-gb` (e.g. to 24) works around it, but the error gives no hint that the cache size is the problem, and an item bigger than the whole cache can never be a cache hit in the first place — evicting the entire cache to fail the insert is lose/lose. Expected behavior: items larger than the cache capacity are served uncached (with a warning suggesting `mm_processor_cache_gb`), and the engine boots. Reproduction sketch (any oversized item does it; no GPU needed to see the raise itself): ```python import torch from vllm.multimodal.cache import MultiModalCache cache = MultiModalCache.get_lru_cache(0.000001, object) # ~1 KiB cache["big"] = torch.zeros(4096, dtype=torch.uint8) # 4 KiB # ValueError: value too large ``` End to end: serve `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8` with the model card's long-video `video_preprocessor_config.json` (`size.longest_edge: 469762048`) and default `mm_processor_cache_gb`; boot dies with the traceback above. I have a working fix that routes the three insert sites through a size guard (deterministic by item size, so the P0 metadata shadow and P1 receiver caches stay coherent — oversized items are simply always resent with data): https://github.com/dkrisman/vllm/commits/fix/mm-cache-skip-oversized Happy to open it as a PR.

signal.title: [Bugfix] Truncate all full-attention groups to the shared prefix-cache hit
signal.text: ## Purpose Hybrid prefix lookup iteratively reconciles target attention, draft attention, and Mamba hits. A later group can reduce the final hit length due to eagle block drop, but currently the cleanup only truncated the first full-attention group based on the hit length and fails to account for the draft model full attention group. This results in corrupted prefix caching behavior: Kimi K3 DCP + Dspark: ``` vllm serve ~/models/Kimi-K3 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ -dcp 8 \ --load-format fastsafetensors \ --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \ --trust-remote-code \ --language-model-only \ --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"TRTLLM_RAGGED","use_prefill_query_quantization":true}' \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --speculative-config '{"model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark","method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":4,"rejection_sample_method":"standard"}' \ --enable-prompt-tokens-details \ --prefix-match-unit 128 prompt_length=10000, cache_hit_length=0 prompt_length=20000, cache_hit_length=0 prompt_length=30000, cache_hit_length=0 prompt_length=50000, cache_hit_length=0 prompt_length=100000, cache_hit_length=0 prompt_length=200000, cache_hit_length=0 cache_hit_lengths=[0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0] ``` After the fix: ``` prompt_length=10000, cache_hit_length=0 prompt_length=20000, cache_hit_length=0 prompt_length=30000, cache_hit_length=9984 prompt_length=50000, cache_hit_length=9984 prompt_length=100000, cache_hit_length=29952 prompt_length=200000, cache_hit_length=98304 cache_hit_lengths=[0, 0, 9984, 9984, 29952, 98304] ``` ## Test Plan ## Test Result --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [ROCm] Pad non-aligned AITER MLA heads
signal.text: ## Summary - pad non-16-aligned ROCm AITER MLA query heads to the next supported multiple of 16 and slice padding from the output - size dense and sparse persistent metadata for the padded launch shape - enable Kimi-K3 TP4's 24 heads/rank to use AITER MLA instead of falling back to Triton MLA ## Performance 8x MI355X, Kimi-K3 TP4/DP2/EP8, 100,000 input tokens (95,911 shared prefix + 4,089 suffix), OSL 1024, one API server, three runs per cohort. | Cohort | Triton MLA TPOT | AITER padded TPOT | TPOT change | Triton output tok/s | AITER output tok/s | Throughput change | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | C16 | 62.696 ms | 41.013 ms | -34.6% | 205.40 | 286.48 | +39.5% | | C24 | 76.061 ms | 46.816 ms | -38.5% | 256.32 | 373.99 | +45.9% | Source base: vLLM `61c1dd0966fd8d91954003cf6b7ab746448a46f8`, AITER `ca68b4f3501762c15c550cb920a5516e9710cf89`. ## Test plan - [x] targeted ROCm AITER MLA tests: 32 passed, 2 skipped - [x] Ruff check and format check on all changed files - [x] GSM8K-100: 99/100, 0 malformed outputs, 0 invalid numeric answers - [x] TP4/DP2/EP8 full-graph server startup and 100K C16/C24 decode benchmark Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

signal.title: [Bug]: GLM 5.2 MTP didn't work in AMD MI300x
signal.text: ### 🐛 Describe the bug GLM-5.2-FP8 with MTP speculative decoding hangs on 8x MI300X (gfx942). Startup finishes, but the engine deadlocks in the vocab-parallel logits all-gather on the first real spec-decode step (RCCL `no transport for peer on channel N`). **Repro:** `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8`, ROCm+AITER, `--tensor-parallel-size 8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --linear-backend aiter --moe-backend aiter --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":K}'`. **Root cause 1 (hits the config above):** warmup runs `compute_logits`' all-gather at 1 row/req, but spec decode verifies `1 + num_speculative_tokens` rows/req. That larger message maps onto extra RCCL channels whose transports connect lazily on first use, and that first use is a live decode step, so the connect fails and hangs. Fix: after the profile `_dummy_run`, warm `compute_logits` once at `min(max_num_reqs*(1+num_spec_tokens), max_num_tokens)` rows (guarded by `num_spec_tokens > 0`). **Root cause 2 (only with `--enable-expert-parallel`, TP>1):** under sequence-parallel MoE, MTP's `mtp_block` reduce-scatters its output but `DeepSeekMultiTokenPredictorLayer.forward` never restores full tokens (unlike `DeepseekV2Model.forward`), so ranks feed mismatched token counts into the collective. Same class as the Qwen MTP fix #48429. Fix: when `hidden_states.shape[0] != positions.shape[0]`, all-gather `[hidden_states, residual]`, slice to full length, and split. Fix 1 validated e2e on MI300X (coherent output, num_spec=1 accept 75-82%).
signal.author: haosdent

signal.title: [BugFix] Skip GDN/KDA recurrent state updates for stale zero-accept spec rows
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes an illegal memory access (CUDA crash) in the GDN and Kimi-K3 KDA attention backends when speculative decoding runs with async scheduling. When an async-scheduling step is discarded, `update_num_computed_tokens_for_batch_change` writes the row's `valid_sampled_token_count` — which is `0` for a row whose sampled tokens were thrown away — into `num_accepted_tokens`. Every consumer of that tensor assumes the count is in `1..1+num_speculative_tokens` and indexes the request's state slots with `num_accepted_tokens - 1`. A `0` therefore produces index `-1`: - In the Triton kernels (`fused_recurrent`, `fused_sigmoid_gating`, `causal_conv1d_update`, and the vendored KDA recurrent kernels) that is an out-of-bounds load → illegal memory access. `causal_conv1d_update` usually faults first. - On the CPU align-mode paths in `mamba_utils.py` it is worse than a crash: `-1` is a *valid* Python index, so the copy silently reads from the end of the state and corrupts output with no error. The fix treats `0` as what it actually means — "this row is stale, it has no valid spec state to resume from" — rather than as a count to be clamped. In the metadata builders, stale rows get their whole `spec_state_indices_tensor` row set to `NULL_BLOCK_ID`, which makes the existing `state_idx <= 0` guards in the FLA kernels and the null-block check in `causal_conv1d_update` skip those rows entirely: no initial-state read, and no final-state write. That last part matters — a clamp-only patch keeps the row in bounds but lets the kernel advance the recurrent state of a request whose step was discarded, silently corrupting it. Both ops are elementwise and introduce no CPU sync, and they sit before the full-cudagraph buffer copies, so the eager and cudagraph paths both inherit the fix. The kernel-level clamps are kept as defense in depth, mirroring the existing pattern in `mamba_ssm.py` and `bailing_linear_attn.py`. Note that `KimiK3KDAMetadataBuilder` subclasses `GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder` but fully overrides `build`, so it does **not** inherit the builder-level fix and needs its own copy. Its version is deliberately out-of-place (`masked_fill`, not `masked_fill_`): the packed-decode branch slices `block_table_tensor` with a basic slice, and in `"all"`/`"none"` cache modes `_mamba_get_block_table_tensor` returns the runner's persistent block table unchanged — an in-place fill there would write `NULL_BLOCK_ID` into the block table and corrupt subsequent steps. The GDN builder is safe in-place because both of its branches build the tensor via boolean-mask indexing, which copies. Deliberately left alone: the CPU GDN backend (asserts spec decode unsupported), and the Mamba2/Bailing paths (already memory-safe via existing clamps; their clamp-to-slot-0 semantics are unchanged). The bogus 100%-acceptance metric reported for all-invalid draft rows is cosmetic and independent of this crash. Related bug reports: - #41190 - #40756 Related open PR (proposing a workaround): - #48475 ## Test Plan ```bash # Builders directly modified by this PR pytest tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py -v pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py -v # Kernels modified by this PR pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_causal_conv1d.py -v pytest tests/kernels/mamba/ -v # Async spec-decode path that produces the zero count pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_backup_token_async_spec.py -v pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dynamic_sd.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dynamic_sd_cug.py -v # E2E reproduction: GDN-backed model, spec decode + async scheduling, # concurrent streams, eager and cudagraph ``` Before this PR the existing builder suites all passed `torch.ones(...)` for `num_accepted_tokens`, so no test exercised the zero case at all. This PR adds that coverage: - `test_gdn_metadata_builder.py::test_zero_accepted_tokens_nulls_state_slots` — stale rows nulled, live rows untouched, counts clamped; parametrized over cudagraph modes. - `test_gdn_metadata_builder.py::test_zero_accepted_tokens_does_not_corrupt_block_table` — guards the in-place-fill hazard. - `test_kda_metadata.py::test_zero_accepted_tokens_nulls_state_slots[_cuda]` — same contract for the overriding KDA builder, across `none`/`align` cache modes and both cudagraph modes. - `test_fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule.py::test_spec_decoding_null_state_row_leaves_state_untouched` — asserts a nulled row's state blocks are **bit-identical** after the kernel runs, i.e. no state advanced, while a live row in the same batch still updates. This is the property that distinguishes this fix from a clamp-only patch like proposed in PR #48475. - `test_fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule.py::test_spec_decoding_zero_accepted_tokens_is_in_bounds` — defense-in-depth: a raw `0` reaching the kernel is clamped rather than indexing at `-1`. ## Test Result Run on a single RTX 5090 (sm_120), CUDA 13.0, torch from `--torch-backend=auto`. ### Suites | Suite | Result | | --- | --- | | `tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py` | 12 passed | | `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py` | 17 passed | | `tests/kernels/test_fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule.py` + `test_fused_recurrent_packed_decode.py` | 57 passed (combined with the two above) | | `tests/kernels/mamba/test_causal_conv1d.py` | 164 passed | | `tests/kernels/mamba/` (rest) | 567 passed, 26 skipped (18m51s) | | `tests/kernels/mamba/test_precopy_mamba_align.py`, `test_gdn_forward_core_split.py`, `test_fused_gdn_post_conv.py` | 109 passed, 1 skipped | | `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_eagle_step_kernel.py`, `test_rejection_sampler_utils.py` | 45 passed | `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on all changed files. ### Before/after on the new tests The new tests were run against the parent commit's source (fix reverted, tests kept). **9 fail without the fix, all pass with it:** ``` FAILED test_gdn_metadata_builder.py::test_zero_accepted_tokens_nulls_state_slots[False] E AssertionError: every state slot of a stale row must be nulled so the kernel's state_idx <= 0 guard skips it, got [944, 944, 944, 944] ``` i.e. without the fix the stale row keeps a live block (944) that the kernel then both reads and **writes**. For the KDA builder, which overrides `build()` and does not inherit the GDN fix: ``` pre-fix KDA stale row: [776, 425, 274, 182] counts: [0, 2] post-fix KDA stale row: [0, 0, 0, 0] counts: [1, 2] block table intact: True ``` ### Correction to the crash characterization Under `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck`, the pre-fix kernel at these tensor shapes reports **`ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors`** — the `-1` index lands inside the allocation, on the neighbouring row. What it actually produces is silent numerical corruption: ``` E AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not equal! E Mismatched elements: 24870 / 32768 (75.9%) E Greatest absolute difference: nan at index (0, 0, 2, 86) ``` So at these shapes the bug is **NaN output, not a fault**; whether it faults depends on allocation layout. This does not change the fix, but it means the failure mode in the wild may be bad output rather than a clean crash. With the fix applied, the same sanitizer run is clean (4 passed, 0 errors). --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Bug]: GLM-5.2 MTP accepts 0% of drafts on MI355X (gfx950); disabling expert parallelism hits hipErrorIllegalAddress
signal.text: ### Your current environment `collect_env.py` output isn't available (the nodes were tied up); details taken from the container image and run logs: ``` vLLM : 0.27.1+rocm723 PyTorch : 2.11.0+gitd0c8b1f ROCm : 7.2.3 Container : vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.27.1 GPU : 8x AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950) amdgpu : 6.16.13, kernel 6.8.0-137-generic Model : amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 (quark MXFP4) MoE backend: aiter ``` ### 🐛 Describe the bug GLM-5.2 MTP starts fine on MI355X and then accepts **zero** draft tokens. Speculative decoding is pure overhead — it drafts at ~40-230 tok/s and accepts none of it. ```bash export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 vllm serve /models/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 \ --served-model-name amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 \ --trust-remote-code \ --async-scheduling \ --distributed-executor-backend mp \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 \ --max-model-len 262144 \ --max-num-seqs 2 \ --moe-backend aiter \ --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \ --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \ --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' ``` Startup resolves as expected — target `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, draft `DeepSeekMTPModel` — then: ``` SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 1.00, Accepted throughput: 0.00 tokens/s, Drafted throughput: 37.80 tokens/s, Accepted: 0 tokens, Drafted: 378 tokens, Per-position acceptance rate: 0.000, 0.000, 0.000, Avg Draft acceptance rate: 0.0% ``` What I tried: | # | change | result | |---|---|---| | A | as above | `acceptance length 1.00`, per-position `0.000, 0.000, 0.000` | | B | `num_speculative_tokens: 1` | `acceptance length 1.00`, per-position `0.000` | | C | `--kv-cache-dtype auto` | `acceptance length 1.05`, per-position `0.046, 0.000, 0.000` | | D | drop `--enable-expert-parallel` | crashes, see below | B rules out the startup warning's explanation: ``` WARNING [speculative.py:912] Enabling num_speculative_tokens > 1 will run multiple times on same MTP layer, which may result in lower acceptance rate ``` Position 0 is 0.000 at `num_speculative_tokens=1` too, so re-running GLM-5.2's single nextn layer isn't what's breaking this — the very first draft token is never accepted. C says fp8 KV contributes but isn't the cause: bf16 KV lifts position 0 from 0.000 to ~0.05, still far from usable. D, without expert parallelism, dies during memory profiling instead: ``` terminate called after throwing an instance of 'c10::AcceleratorError' Search for `hipErrorIllegalAddress' in https://rocm.docs.amd.com/projects/HIP/en/latest/index.html Exception raised from ~CUDAGraph at /app/pytorch/aten/src/ATen/hip/HIPGraph.cpp:302 ``` I also checked whether the unquantized nextn layer is being mis-handled by the quark loader — it isn't, as far as I can tell. Layer 78 is genuinely unquantized in this checkpoint (789 `.weight`, 0 `.weight_scale`, 781 entries in `quantization_config.exclude`), but `DeepSeekMTPModel` sets `mtp_start_layer_idx = num_hidden_layers` and names it `model.layers.78`, which is what the exclude patterns match on. So the exclusions should apply. For reference, SGLang on the same node with the same checkpoint gets a working draft: ``` Decode batch, #running-req: 1, ..., accept len: 3.00, accept rate: 0.67, cuda graph: True ``` This may be the same root cause as #48568 (MI300X / gfx942), which points at MTP's `mtp_block` reduce-scattering under `--enable-expert-parallel` with TP>1 while the predictor layer doesn't restore full tokens. Filing separately because the symptom here is different in a way that matters: on gfx950 there's no hang and no error — it silently produces a 0% acceptance rate, so a benchmark run looks healthy and just reports worse numbers. Disabling EP also fails differently (illegal address rather than working around it). Happy to run further diagnostics on gfx950 if that helps. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] I have searched for similar issues and read the [documentation](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/).

signal.title: [Spec Decode] Enable adaptive verification on DSv4 + sm90
signal.text: ## Purpose Enable adaptive verification for the DeepSeek V4 indexer on Hopper (SM90). The native variable-length DeepGEMM paged-MQA path remains restricted to SM100. On SM90, this change instead uses the existing flattened decode path and builds the single-token rows from the device-side decode lengths. This is necessary because adaptive verification can trim each request to a different length while the CPU metadata contains only a uniform placeholder. The builder forces this device-length flattening for adaptive verification, advertises support for the device/CPU query-length mismatch, and enables CUDA graph capture for this path. When there is only one decode request, the CPU and device request boundaries necessarily agree, so that case reuses the cheaper uniform flattened metadata path. This addresses the Hopper startup failure reported in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47808#issuecomment-5264762911. ### Duplicate-work check I searched the open PRs for `adaptive verification Hopper SM90`, `DeepseekV4IndexerBackend adaptive verification`, `varlen indexer Hopper`, and `SM90 DeepGEMM indexer`; no open PR implements this fix. #51972 concerns a separate indexer bounds bug, while #47808 is the merged SM100 implementation where the SM90 failure was reported. ## Test Plan Targeted correctness and regression tests: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_native_next_n.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py -v .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_ordering.py -v CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py -v .venv/bin/pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD ``` End-to-end validation used DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 on 4x H200 (SM90): - TP2 / DP2 / expert parallel startup and serving with 7 DSpark speculative tokens, probabilistic drafting, and adaptive verification enabled. - The repository GSM8K 5-shot evaluation with TP4 / expert parallel and the adaptive DSpark configuration from `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark-confidence-TP4.yaml`. The Blackwell-only `--attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype=mxfp4` option was removed for Hopper; the rest of the speculative configuration was unchanged. - Warmed throughput comparison against fixed verification on TP2 / DP2 / expert parallel, averaged over three runs. - Matched fixed and adaptive torch-profiler traces at concurrency one. ## Test Result - Indexer and adaptive-verification tests: **15 passed**. - GPU batch-ordering tests: **10 passed**. - DeepGEMM attention kernel tests on H200: **5 passed**. - Pre-commit, including ruff and Python 3.10 mypy: **passed**. - User-equivalent 4x H200 server: **started and served successfully**. The log confirms `use_flattening=True supports_varlen=False`. - Hopper GSM8K: **94.996% accuracy**, **0% invalid**, **4.106 mean acceptance length** (1,319 questions, 5-shot). Warmed output throughput (tokens/s): | Concurrency | Fixed verification | Adaptive verification | Delta | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 256.5 | 240.2 | -6.35% | | 16 | 1520.9 | 1608.9 | +5.78% | | 64 | 2663.6 | 3032.5 | +13.85% | The concurrency-one regression is reduced but remains a known limitation of this draft. Reusing uniform flattened metadata for a single decode request improved adaptive throughput from 236.9 to 240.2 tokens/s (+1.4%) and reduced mean ITL from 12.455 to 12.355 ms. This matches the metadata microbenchmark: device-ragged preparation took 115.08 us versus 24.14 us for uniform preparation, accounting for about 0.100 ms of the original 0.961 ms per-verification-step gap. Matched torch-profiler traces show that fixed and adaptive verification both execute an 8-token target graph at concurrency one. Median target GPU execution was effectively identical (10.181 ms fixed versus 10.185 ms adaptive), but the median gap between target graph executions increased from 1.811 to 2.517 ms. The adaptive trace contains one blocking confidence-copy event synchronization per step in `AdaptiveVerificationManager.record_confidences`; its approximately 0.706 ms net critical-path effect, together with the 0.100 ms metadata cost, explains most of the original step-latency gap. CUDA graph capture also increased in the TP2 / DP2 comparison (121 s / 4.71 GiB adaptive versus 52 s / 2.61 GiB fixed). The existing SM100 path is unchanged and was not rebenchmarked here. ## AI assistance AI assistance from OpenAI Codex was used to investigate, implement, test, benchmark, and draft this PR. Before this draft is marked ready, the human submitter will review every changed line and must be able to defend the change end-to-end. --- - [x] The purpose and related report are documented. - [x] Exact test commands are provided. - [x] Correctness, model-evaluation, and performance results are provided. - [x] No documentation update is required for this backend-only change. **BEFORE SUBMITTING, PLEASE READ <https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing>**

signal.title: [Bugfix] Sync xgrammar termination state after failed token acceptance
signal.text: ## Summary Fix a termination-state desynchronization between `XgrammarGrammar` and its underlying xgrammar matcher. With speculative decoding, an `accept_tokens()` batch can contain a stop token followed by additional speculative tokens. The matcher terminates after accepting the stop token, then rejects the following token. Because `accept_tokens()` returned early, `XgrammarGrammar._is_terminated` was not updated and remained stale. This change synchronizes `_is_terminated` with the matcher before returning `False`, preventing subsequent code from treating a terminated matcher as active and calling operations such as `fill_next_token_bitmask()` on it. Without this synchronization, vLLM may continue using a matcher that has already terminated, causing later bitmask generation to fail. Related to #49210 ## Reproduction The original issue was reproduced with: - xgrammar structured output - EAGLE3 speculative decoding - `ignore_eos=true` - a speculative token batch continuing after EOS Before the fix, this produces the xgrammar warning that a token is being accepted after the matcher has terminated, followed by a later bitmask failure. The same state desynchronization was independently reproduced by @jayanth922 using xgrammar 0.2.1 and a four-token toy tokenizer without a model or GPU.
signal.author: wangyxbh

signal.title: [Core][V1] Support trace_decode_token_ids for deterministic decode replay
signal.text: Add inference trace-replay: a new SamplingParams.trace_decode_token_ids field that forces the v1 sampler to emit a predetermined sequence of decode token IDs, step by step, instead of sampling. Real logprobs and token ranks are still computed from the unmodified logit distribution. The sampler injects each trace token after sampling (so logprobs stay real); InputBatch tracks the trace per request in parallel with spec_token_ids; and EngineCore.add_request caps generation to the trace length / forces ignore_eos, falling back to normal sampling (with a warning) for incompatible modes (speculative decoding, n > 1). Tests cover the SamplingParams field, sampler injection (including async -1 placeholders and past-end-of-trace), and engine-core admission. A demo example script is added under examples/generate/. ## Purpose Add **inference trace-replay**: a new `SamplingParams.trace_decode_token_ids` field that forces the v1 sampler to emit a predetermined sequence of decode token IDs, step by step, instead of sampling. Real logprobs and token ranks are still computed from the unmodified logit distribution at each step. **Motivation.** The goal is to make a request follow a *fixed* token trace and return the logprobs the model assigns to that exact trace. This is useful for: - **Quantifying differences between settings/backends.** Replaying the same trace under different configs (dtype, quantization, attention/MoE backend, TP size, etc.) and comparing per-token logprobs gives a direct, apples-to-apples measure of numerical divergence on identical token sequences. - **RL training.** It lets you recompute logprobs for a rollout's exact tokens under the training engine, so the rollout↔train logprob gap can be measured and minimized — without re-sampling and drifting onto a different trajectory. **Why decode-replay and not prefill-only scoring?** Computing logprobs by prefilling the full (prompt + response) sequence does *not* faithfully reproduce the decode-time distribution: many models run **different operators / kernels in the prefill path vs. the decode path** (e.g. attention and MoE kernels differ between the two phases). To measure the logprobs a model would actually produce while *decoding*, the tokens must go through the decode path one step at a time — which is exactly what trace-replay does. ### How it works 1. Set `SamplingParams.trace_decode_token_ids` to the list of decode token IDs to force. 2. The sampler injects each trace token **after** sampling (`Sampler._inject_trace_tokens` in `vllm/v1/sample/sampler.py`), so logprobs stay real — they are computed from the original logits, before injection. 3. `InputBatch` tracks the trace per request in parallel with `spec_token_ids` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_input_batch.py`); the per-request step index counts real output tokens, skipping the trailing `-1` async-scheduling placeholder. 4. `EngineCore.add_request` caps generation to the trace length and forces `ignore_eos`, so EOS tokens inside the trace do not halt generation early. It falls back to normal sampling (with a warning) for incompatible modes (speculative decoding, `n > 1`). ### Not a duplicate No open PR addresses this — searched the repo for open PRs matching `trace_decode_token_ids` and `trace`/`replay` in title (0 results). The closest existing features are `logprob_token_ids` (only *scores* a fixed token set, doesn't force the output sequence) and `spec_token_ids` (speculative decoding, different purpose); neither forces a predetermined decode trace. ## Test Plan ```bash # Unit tests (CPU-only, no GPU required) .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/v1/sample/test_trace_replay.py \ tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core_trace_replay.py -v # Lint / type-check as in CI pre-commit run --all-files pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --all-files --hook-stage manual ``` - `tests/v1/sample/test_trace_replay.py` — `SamplingParams` field defaults, clone preservation, and validation (empty / negative / non-int rejected); sampler injection covering step 0, mixed per-request steps, past-end-of-trace (no-op), the async `-1` placeholder, and the unset/none path. - `tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core_trace_replay.py` — engine-core admission: generation bounds capped to trace length + `ignore_eos` forced; fallback to normal sampling for speculative decoding and `n > 1`. - Demo: `examples/generate/trace_replay_offline.py` — greedy-generate to capture decode tokens, then replay them and assert a token-by-token match while printing per-token logprobs. ## Test Result ```text $ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/sample/test_trace_replay.py \ tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core_trace_replay.py tests/v1/sample/test_trace_replay.py .............. [ 82%] tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core_trace_replay.py ... [100%] ======================= 17 passed, 16 warnings in 0.14s ======================== ``` `pre-commit run --all-files` and `mypy-3.12` (CI hook stage) pass on the changed files (ruff-check, ruff-format, SPDX headers, forbidden-imports, etc.). > ⚠️ Unit tests were run on a CPU-only box; the end-to-end demo > (`examples/generate/trace_replay_offline.py`) should be run on a GPU to confirm > token-by-token replay before merge. > **AI assistance disclosure:** developed with AI assistance (Claude). The > submitter has reviewed every changed line and is responsible for the change > end-to-end. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [x] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [XPU] Add PyTorch fallback for per-block SiLU-and-Mul FP8 quantization
signal.text: ## Summary Fix three issues preventing FP8 quantized MoE models (e.g., Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8) from running on Intel XPU devices. ## Problem 1. `silu_and_mul_per_block_quant` custom op is not available in the XPU kernel pack, causing an `AttributeError` at runtime during MoE expert computation. 2. `per_token_group_fp8_quant` XPU call sites pass 8 arguments but the registered op signature expects 10 (missing `dummy_is_scale_transposed` and `dummy_is_tma_aligned`), causing a `RuntimeError` during memory profiling. ## Changes - **`vllm/_custom_ops.py`**: Add `hasattr` guard for `silu_and_mul_per_block_quant` with a fallback to `silu_and_mul_quant` (per-token quantization) when the per-block kernel is unavailable. - **`vllm/_xpu_ops.py`**: Pass the missing `dummy_is_scale_transposed=False` and `dummy_is_tma_aligned=False` arguments to `per_token_group_fp8_quant` in the MXFP8 quantization path. - **`vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py`**: Pass `column_major_scales` and `tma_aligned_scales` to the XPU path of `per_token_group_fp8_quant`, matching the CUDA call site. ## Testing Verified with `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8` on Intel Arc Pro B60 GPUs (TP=2, eager mode). Model loads and serves inference requests successfully.
signal.author: slokesha

signal.title: [Bugfix] Surface TorchCodec video decode failures as client errors
signal.text: ## Purpose TorchCodec raises `RuntimeError` when decoding user-supplied video bytes fails. That exception type has no handler in the exception-handler registry (`ValueError`/`VLLMError` map to 400; raw `RuntimeError` falls through to the safety net), so the server returns **HTTP 500 with an ASGI traceback** for what is a client-input problem. The most common user-triggerable case: `seek_mode="approximate"` on a file whose container metadata overstates the decodable frame count — e.g. any stream-copied cut (`ffmpeg -c copy`). Frame sampling targets an index past the real end and torchcodec raises `Requested next frame while there are no more frames left to decode.` Reproduced end-to-end on a Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 server: request → 500. This PR converts `RuntimeError` from the torchcodec branch of `VideoBackend.load_bytes` to `ValueError` (chained with `from exc`), exactly mirroring the existing pattern in the `pynvvideocodec` backend (`raise ValueError("Invalid or unsupported video file.") from exc`). When `seek_mode="approximate"` is in effect, the message additionally tells the user to retry with `"exact"`: ``` HTTP 400 Failed to decode video with the torchcodec backend: Requested next frame while there are no more frames left to decode. This can happen with seek_mode='approximate' when the file's container metadata overstates the decodable frame count; retry with seek_mode='exact'. ``` Bundled docs: the "Video Decoding Backend" section gains operational guidance for the two TorchCodec knobs — when `num_ffmpeg_threads=0` (default) beats `1` and vice versa, with measured numbers (768 frames of 1080p H.264 on 16 cores: ~10 s at `0` vs ~49 s at `1`), and the approximate-mode metadata caveat with its new client-error behavior. ## Duplicate check Searched open PRs/issues for torchcodec error handling and video decode error mapping: no existing work. Related context: #46609 (torchcodec backend introduction, where `seek_mode` exposure was discussed) and the registry's own TODO to migrate raw-exception fallbacks to `VLLMError`. ## Test Plan - New `test_torchcodec_decode_failure_is_client_error` in `tests/multimodal/test_video.py`: RuntimeError from the decoder surfaces as `ValueError` with the original exception chained; the seek-mode hint appears only when `seek_mode="approximate"`. - `pytest tests/multimodal/test_video.py -k torchcodec_decode_failure -q` - `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` ## Test Result - `1 passed`; pre-commit all hooks pass (ruff, mypy, markdownlint, DCO). - E2E on a live Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 server (torchcodec backend): per-request `media_io_kwargs: {"video": {"seek_mode": "approximate"}}` on a stream-copied 60 s cut now returns the HTTP 400 above (previously 500 + ASGI traceback); the same file decodes fine with default `exact` (16.5 s request, 35,149 prompt tokens); unrelated requests unaffected. ## AI Disclosure Developed with AI assistance (Claude Fable 5). The human submitter has reviewed every changed line and run the tests above.
signal.author: dkrisman

signal.title: [Bugfix] vLLM crashes at startup when DeepEP v2 is used with `--enforce-eager` wiht TRTLLM Bf16
signal.text: ## Purpose When running the following command: ``` vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite \ --data-parallel-size 2 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --all2all-backend deepep_v2 \ --enforce-eager ``` vLLM will crash at startup with the following error ``` expert_indices.size(1) == args->top_k (1 vs. 6) : expert_indices dim1 must match top_k. ``` This error is caused by `TrtLlmBf16ExpertsModular` not properly extracting the `top_k` value when DeepEP V2 returns the topk_ids in it's "expanded" layout. This PR updates the logic to use the correct value for `top_k` in this backend and improves the DeepEP V2 + MoE unit test to cover the expanded and non expanded layouts for the `flashinfer_trtllm`, `flashinfer_cutlass`, and `trtllm_fp8` backends. ## Test Plan I expanded the existing unit test to cover more cases and ran lm_eval on ``` vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite \ --data-parallel-size 2 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --all2all-backend deepep_v2 \ --enforce-eager ``` ## Test Result lm_eval results ``` |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.3821|± |0.0134| | | |strict-match | 5|exact_match|↑ |0.3783|± |0.0134| ```

signal.title: feat(rust): expose routed expert traces over gRPC
signal.text: ## Summary Expose routed-expert capture through the Rust gRPC request and terminal response path. ## Why The Rust frontend needs a northbound API that can request routed-expert capture and return the decoded EngineCore trace to non-Python clients. ## Changes - Add `routed_experts_prompt_start` to gRPC response options. - Validate and lower the prompt offset. - Accumulate routed-expert chunks while enforcing a stable dtype and trailing shape. - Return compact dtype, shape, bytes, and start metadata on terminal output. - Keep OpenAI route behavior unchanged; their constructor updates only initialize the new internal field. - Add gRPC round-trip and invalid-offset coverage. ## Stack dependencies This draft is stacked on: 1. #52721 for typed EngineCore routed-output decoding. 2. #52703 for the Python-compatible sampling field. The branch currently includes snapshots of both prerequisite changes so the end-to-end path can be reviewed and tested. After the prerequisites merge, this branch will be rebased and the final diff will contain only the gRPC surface and aggregation logic. It does not depend on #52722. ## Checks - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` - `cargo test -p vllm-llm -p vllm-text -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server` - All affected package tests passed; the `vllm-text` suite has one pre-existing ignored network test. ## Review note This change was prepared with AI assistance and reviewed line by line before submission.

signal.title: [XPU] Enable MiniMax-M3 on non-CUDA backends: portable fallbacks for CUDA-only paths
signal.text: ## Purpose `MiniMaxM3SparseForConditionalGeneration` cannot be loaded on any non-CUDA/ROCm backend. Five independent blockers, each of which fully prevents startup or the first generated token. This PR fixes all five, targeting XPU but with three of them applying to CPU and any other backend equally. The common root cause: M3's implementation lives under `vllm/models/minimax_m3/` and correctly falls through to the generic Triton paths on XPU, but several supporting ops reach for CUDA-only facilities with no fallback — `torch.ops._C` (built only for CUDA/HIP), `flashinfer`, and a Triton `tl.dot` tile shape that is only legal on NVIDIA. | # | File | Problem | Fix | |---|------|---------|-----| | 1 | `rotary_embedding/common.py` | `ApplyRotaryEmb.forward_static` assumes `rotary_dim == head_size`; M3's vision tower passes partial 3D RoPE (`cos/sin` of 39 vs `head_dim` 80) | derive `rotary_dim = 2 * cos.shape[-1]`, rotate the leading part, pass the tail through | | 2 | `minimax_m3/nvidia/model.py` | `MiniMAXGemmaRMSNorm.forward` hard-imports `flashinfer.norm` | `try/except ImportError`, fall back to the `ir.ops` primitives backing vLLM's own `GemmaRMSNorm` | | 3 | `_custom_ops.py` | `fused_minimax_m3_qknorm_rope_kv_insert` has **no** non-CUDA implementation | unfused PyTorch reference mirroring the CUDA kernel's semantics, `hasattr` dispatch guard | | 4 | `fused_moe/activation.py` | `apply_moe_activation()` calls `torch.ops._C.silu_and_mul_with_clamp` directly, bypassing the `CustomOp` layer | torch fallback + `hasattr` guard | | 5 | `minimax_m3/common/ops/index_topk.py` | `_decode_index_score_kernel`'s `tl.dot` N = `num_idx_heads * BLOCK_SIZE_Q`, which is 1 at TP=8 without spec decode; Intel DPAS requires N >= 16 | pad N to the backend's `min_dot_size` | **CUDA/ROCm behaviour is provably unchanged in all five cases:** #1 is bit-identical when `rotary_dim == head_size` (tail is empty); #2 still imports FlashInfer where it exists; #3/#4 dispatch to the fused kernel whenever `torch.ops._C` is present; #5's `CUDABackend` declares no `min_dot_size`, so the tile width is untouched. Bug 5 is worth reviewer attention: it is **structurally invisible on NVIDIA**. The Triton assertion that catches it is only evaluated by backends that declare `min_dot_size`, and `CUDABackend` has no such attribute — the narrow tile compiles there and the hardware pads implicitly. The sibling `_gqa_sparse_decode_kernel` in `common/ops/sparse_attn.py` already hardcodes the same `max(16, ...)` padding; the indexer kernel just never got it. ## Test Plan Each fix was verified numerically against an explicit reference in fp32 and bf16. Drafts of four regression tests: - `ApplyRotaryEmb.forward_static` with `rotary_dim < head_size` (#1) - `_fused_minimax_m3_qknorm_rope_kv_insert_ref` vs the CUDA kernel, incl. fp8 and padded slots — CPU-only, no accelerator needed (#3) - `_silu_and_mul_with_clamp_native` vs `SiluAndMulWithClamp.forward_native` with `alpha != 1` / `beta != 0` (#4) - `_decode_index_score_kernel` compiled at `num_idx_heads * BLOCK_SIZE_Q == 1`; needs a backend declaring `min_dot_size`, passes trivially on NVIDIA (#5) ## Test Result End-to-end on an 8x Intel B70 box (TP=8, `xccl`, `--moe-backend triton`, `--enforce-eager`, `--block-size=128`): server reaches ready, `/v1/models` and `/health` respond, and completion requests return correct output.

signal.title: [Kernel] Add B12X FP4 MoE backend
signal.text: ## Purpose Builds on the optional B12X dependency, shared lazy imports, packed-storage reuse, and warmup integration merged in #52016. This PR adds an explicitly selected [B12X](https://github.com/local-inference-lab/b12x) FP4 MoE backend for NVIDIA SM120 and SM121 GPUs using vLLM's existing fused-MoE backend interfaces. It does not introduce a new MoE abstraction. Supported paths include: - Native NVFP4 and MXFP4 W4A4. - W4A16 and supported dynamic W4A8 activation modes. - MXFP4 defaults to MXFP8 activations where supported; NVFP4 retains its checkpoint activation format. - `VLLM_B12X_MOE_FP4_FORCE_A16=1` forces both FP4 formats onto the BF16 activation path. - Tensor parallelism, warmup, reload-stable packed storage, and CUDA graph replay. Expert parallelism, expert maps, EXL3, and NF3 are unsupported. B12X 1.2.4 owns and registers the custom operator used by the backend. Warmup supplies the complete set of serving sizes available to vLLM. B12X deduplicates sizes that resolve to identical internal policy choices; vLLM does not duplicate or guess those package-internal policies. The documentation covers explicit `--moe-backend b12x` selection, supported activation modes, the A16 override, and unsupported expert configurations. This is the MoE component split from #51696, which it supersedes rather than duplicates. Related PRs #41243 and #47577 do not provide this standalone optional-package MoE integration. AI assistance from OpenAI Codex was used while developing this PR. I reviewed every changed line and am responsible for understanding and defending the integration end-to-end. ## Test Plan Run the B12X MoE backend-selection, correctness, warmup, storage-reuse, and CUDA graph coverage: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<idle-gpu> .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/kernels/moe/test_b12x_moe.py -q .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/model_executor/test_b12x_warmup.py \ tests/quantization/test_auto_round.py::test_inc_mxfp4_moe_method_registers_weights_and_builds_kernel \ -q ``` Run pre-commit over every file changed by this PR layer: ```bash mapfile -t changed_files < <(git diff --name-only upstream/main...HEAD) .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files "${changed_files[@]}" git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD ``` Benchmark `nvidia/MiniMax-M2.7-NVFP4` on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q GPU, comparing B12X with FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE at TP2. Use five warmup and ten measured requests. ## Test Result Focused tests against the published `b12x==1.2.4` wheel: ```text 43 CPU-safe backend tests passed; 11 GPU correctness and CUDA graph tests passed 6 shared warmup tests passed 1 AutoRound integration test passed ``` All changed-file pre-commit hooks passed, and `git diff --check` reported no errors. Single-request end-to-end decode throughput; higher is better: | Path | Model/configuration | TP | Comparison backend | Comparison tok/s | B12X tok/s | Change | | --- | --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | NVFP4 MoE | MiniMax-M2.7-NVFP4 | 2 | FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE | 132.1558 | 137.8276 | +4.29% | --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR. - [x] The test plan, including commands. - [x] The test and performance results. - [x] The necessary documentation update. </details>

signal.title: [ROCm][Quant] Requantize serialized MXFP8 linears to FP8 PTPC
signal.text: ## Summary This PR lets ROCm users requantize serialized MXFP8 linear weights to FP8 per-token/per-channel (PTPC) at model startup: ```text MXFP8 values + E8M0 block scales -> BF16 -> FP8 PTPC ``` The supported activation flag is: ```bash --quantization-config.linear fp8_per_channel ``` The implementation is source-format-aware and model-agnostic. It adds no model-specific quantization class or model-name routing. `ModelOpt` names vLLM's existing checkpoint-format handler: `ModelOptMxFp8Config` and `ModelOptMxFp8LinearMethod`. MiniMax-M3 checkpoints tagged with `quant_method: mxfp8` use the same serialized E4M3-value plus E8M0 block-scale format, so vLLM routes them through this handler. This does not mean the checkpoint was created by NVIDIA ModelOpt. The PTPC target is generic, but this PR currently provides source reconstruction for the ModelOpt MXFP8 loader. ## Implementation - `LinearRequantizationSource` is the small generic interface between a serialized source method and an online quantizer. - `ModelOptMxFp8LinearMethod.dequantize_weight()` reconstructs BF16 from the checkpoint's MXFP8 values and E8M0 scales. - `Fp8PtpcOnlineLinearMethod` performs PTPC quantization and AITER preshuffling from the reconstructed weight. - Routing uses checkpoint quantization and `QuantizationConfigArgs`; there is no `model_type` check or hard-coded layer-name list. - Excluded and unspecified linears keep checkpoint quantization. MoE remains MXFP8. - Tensor-parallel row weights synchronize their per-channel scale before final quantization. ## Usage ```bash vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN \ --moe-backend aiter \ --linear-backend auto \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --language-model-only \ --quantization-config.linear fp8_per_channel ``` Without the final flag, the checkpoint keeps its native MXFP8 linear path. ## Validation ### environment | Item | Value | |---|---| | Current-main base | `b6754f536e9cb40a1e117705a44d74218873b437` | | PR head | `85199f11c15b8860429c2eb8f37ff2b8dec143cf` | | Hardware | AMD Instinct MI355X | ### Startup and backend checks | Test | Configuration | Result | |---|---|---| | Current Main | Base, `auto`, no PTPC flag | `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` | | PR with PTPC | Head, `auto`, `fp8_per_channel` | `AiterPreshuffledPerTokenFp8ScaledMMLinearKernel` | | PR without Flag | Head, `auto`, no PTPC flag | Unchanged native MXFP8 | | Invalid Backend | Head, `emulation`, `fp8_per_channel` | Expected early actionable failure | | Forced Emulation | Base, `emulation`, no PTPC flag | `EmulationMxfp8LinearKernel` | ### Quality: does PTPC preserve native MXFP8 accuracy? The required paired GSM8K run used `lm-eval[api]==0.4.12`, 25-shot, 200 samples, chat template, temperature 0, max 4096 tokens, concurrency 200, and the same dataset revision. | Metric | Current Main | PR with PTPC | Difference | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Strict exact match | 0.965 | 0.955 | -0.010 | | Flexible exact match | 0.965 | 0.955 | -0.010 | Because this two-sample difference lacked per-sample records, a separate full-dataset run repeated the protocol on all 1,319 samples with sample logging: | Metric | Current Main | PR with PTPC | Difference | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Strict exact match | 0.948446 | 0.951478 | +0.003033 | | Flexible exact match | 0.947688 | 0.950720 | +0.003033 | ### C64: does PTPC improve over current native MXFP8? | Metric | Current Main | PR with PTPC | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Output throughput / GPU (tok/s) | 315.378 | 328.463 | +4.149% | | Total output throughput (tok/s) | 1261.512 | 1313.853 | +4.149% | | Total token throughput (tok/s) | 22259.993 | 23183.570 | +4.149% | | Mean TTFT (ms) | 1229.384 | 1143.733 | -6.967% | | p99 TTFT (ms) | 12933.988 | 11926.503 | -7.789% | | Mean TPOT (ms) | 47.398 | 45.379 | -4.260% | | p99 TPOT (ms) | 73.013 | 72.471 | -0.742% | | p99 ITL (ms) | 405.151 | 378.142 | -6.666% | | Server startup (s) | 237.961 | 257.985 | +8.415% | | Ready TP4 VRAM (GB) | 1165.783 | 1166.422 | +0.055% | PTPC improved throughput by 4.149%; every reported request-latency metric also improved in this run. ### C256: does PTPC improve over current native MXFP8? signal.title: [Model] Declare SupportsEagle3 on Qwen3ASRForConditionalGeneration
signal.text: ## Purpose Qwen3ASRForConditionalGeneration does not declare SupportsEagle3, so speculative decoding refuses to attach an EAGLE3 draft head to a Qwen3-ASR target even though its inner decoder self.language_model (a Qwen3ForCausalLM) supports it fully. Declaring the interface is the only required change, because SupportsEagle3.set_aux_hidden_state_layers already resolves a multimodal wrapper: ```python parent_ref = self.get_language_model() or self.language_model assert isinstance(parent_ref.model, EagleModelMixin) parent_ref.model._set_aux_hidden_state_layers(layers) ``` ## Test Plan Trained an EAGLE3 draft head against Qwen3-ASR-1.7B and served it on vLLM 0.26.0 with a W4A16 target on an L4: ``` vllm serve <qwen3-asr-w4a16> --max-model-len 8192 \ --speculative-config '{"method":"eagle3","model":"<draft>","num_speculative_tokens":5}' ``` We can use acceptance per draft as the diagnostic to determine if speculation actually works. ## Test Result Accepted tokens per draft, num_speculative_tokens=5: | draft head | accepted per draft | |---|---| | A | 2.3942 | | B | 2.9167 | End-to-end on an L4 | | RTFx | vs baseline | |---|---|---| | no draft | 160.1 | — | | + draft A | 202.9 | +26.8% | | + draft B | 212.9 | +33.0% | Before this change the same configuration fails at engine init since supports_eagle3 is absent and the proposer rejects the target.
