signal.title: Fix/granitemoe fp8 split experts rebased
signal.text: # [Bugfix] Load GraniteMoE FP8 checkpoints with split per-expert weights Fixes #42463 (in combination with #44739 for the fused layout). ## Purpose GraniteMoE FP8 checkpoints ship in two distinct on-disk expert layouts, and `GraniteMoeModel.load_weights` handles only the fused one today: 1. **Fused layout** (`input_linear`/`output_linear`, as in the base BF16 checkpoint). The existing loader chunks `input_linear` into gate/up and copies `output_linear` to `w2`, but only for `.weight` — it drops the `.weight_scale` tensors, triggering a `KeyError` on FP8 checkpoints. This is the bug reported in #42463 and fixed by #44739. 2. **Split per-expert layout** (produced by current `llm-compressor` FP8 quantization): one tensor per expert per projection, named `...block_sparse_moe.experts.{e}.{gate,up,down}_proj.{weight,weight_scale}`. Neither the current loader nor #44739 understands these names, so loading raises `KeyError` on e.g. `...experts.0.down_proj.weight`. This PR reworks `load_weights` to route **both** layouts through the `FusedMoE` weight loader, carrying `weight_scale` alongside `weight` on every path — with the split per-expert layout as the primary addition. ## Relationship to existing work / not a duplicate Duplicate-work checks (AGENTS.md): ```bash gh issue view 42463 --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "42463 in:body" gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "granitemoe fp8" ``` - **Issue #42463** (filed by this submitter): GraniteMoE loader drops `.weight_scale` on the fused layout → `KeyError` for FP8_DYNAMIC. - **PR #44739** (`@javierdejesusda`, open): fixes exactly the fused-layout scale case from #42463 by extending the load guards to match `.weight_scale`. It does **not** handle the split per-expert layout. This PR is **not a duplicate of #44739**: its new, non-overlapping contribution is the **split per-expert layout** path (`experts.{e}.{gate,up,down}_proj.`), which #44739 does not cover. It also reworks the fused path to go through the FusedMoE `weight_loader` (carrying scales), so the two PRs overlap on the fused-layout scale fix. Suggested resolution to avoid stepping on #44739: if #44739 merges first, this PR can be rebased and narrowed to just the split per-expert path (`get_expert_mapping` + `_load_quant_expert`) on top of it. If maintainers prefer a single loader rewrite covering both layouts, this PR already does that and #44739 can be closed in its favor. Deferring to maintainer preference.

signal.title: [Bug]: PD Multi Tier supplies nothing when the producer already holds the blocks
signal.text: ### Summary In the PD Multi Tier flow (`remote_decoder` / `remote_prefiller`, secondary tier of `type: p2p`), a producer that **already holds the requested blocks** supplies nothing to the consumer. The consumer's fetch demand parks unsatisfied, waits out `_LOAD_TIMEOUT_S = 30.0`, aborts, and recomputes the prompt locally. The effect is inverted from the intent: the better the producer's prefix cache works, the more often the Multi Tier path fails to deliver. ### Environment - vLLM `v0.27.1`, stock `docker.io/vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1` - `openai/gpt-oss-120b`, TP=1, `--block-size 128`, `--no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager`, `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` on all instances - 2x H200, RDMA between pods - Connector on both instances: ``` --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both", "kv_load_failure_policy":"recompute", "kv_connector_extra_config":{"spec_name":"TieringOffloadingSpec", "cpu_bytes_to_use":107374182400,"block_size":128,"eviction_policy":"lru", "offload_prompt_only":false, "secondary_tiers":[{"type":"p2p","host":"$(POD_IP)","port":7777}]}}' ``` Two files (`tiering/p2p/session/server.py`, `.../client.py`) carried added `logger.info` counters only, no behavioural change; the timings and byte counts below come from vLLM's own metrics and logs. ### Reproducer Two instances, A (producer) and B (consumer). No P/D topology, router or proxy required — three HTTP calls. 1. **Producer leg** on A: `POST /v1/completions`, `max_tokens=1`, `kv_transfer_params={"remote_decoder":{"kv_request_id":ID}}` 2. **Consumer leg** on B: `POST /v1/completions`, `kv_transfer_params={"remote_prefiller":{"kv_request_id":ID,"remote_host":A,"remote_port":7777}}` Run that pair twice with a **unique prompt each time** (so the consumer is always cold). Before the second pair, send the prompt to A once on its own with no `kv_transfer_params`, so A already holds the blocks. Prompt ~8K tokens. Watch `vllm:kv_offload_load_bytes_total` on B. ### Observed | case | producer leg | consumer leg | consumer bytes loaded | | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | | A cold for the prefix | 0.20 s | 0.16 s | +268,959,744 (256 MiB) | | A pre-warmed | 0.03 s | **32.9 s** | **0** | Identical with a real P/D pair (prefill producer, decode consumer): 0.086 s / +256 MiB cold vs 30.2 s / 0 bytes warm. Reproduces every time. Consumer log for the warm case: ``` P2PSession <A>:7777: <id> round=0 timed out, sending abort P2PSession <A>:7777: load request <id> (job_id=N) timed out; load job completed with failure. If this recurs, ensure PYTHONHASHSEED is set to the same value on all nodes. ``` `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` was set and verified identical on every instance, so that hint is misleading for this failure mode. ### Analysis Supply for a PD round can only come from that request's store jobs (`session/server.py` `_OutboundRequestState.add_stored_blocks`). A warm producer creates no store job, so demand parked in `demanded` (`key -> remote_block_idx: blocks peer wants, awaiting supply`) is never matched. Two gates prevent the blocks from being offered: 1. `distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py` (~L941): ```python # Skip prefix-hit chunks for block-level policy; for # request-level, next_stored_chunk_idx stays at 0 so all # chunks (including hits) are offloaded. if req_status.offloading_context.policy == OffloadPolicy.BLOCK_LEVEL: group_state.next_stored_chunk_idx = num_chunks ``` `P2PTierManager.on_new_request` returns a bare `RequestOffloadingContext()`, which defaults to `BLOCK_LEVEL`. `grep -c REQUEST_LEVEL` is **0** for every tier (`p2p`, `fs`, `obj`, `example`) at `v0.27.1` **and on `main`**, so `request_level_tiers` is always empty and `TieringOffloadingManager._cascade_existing_blocks_to_request_level_tiers` never runs. 2. Forcing `REQUEST_LEVEL` for producer-side requests clears gate 1 — verified, the request then reaches the store path with `next_stored_chunk_idx=0` and 56 storable chunks — but the keys are then dropped by `if block_id == 0: continue`, since a prefix-hit request has no GPU block ids recorded for those blocks (measured: 55 keys dropped). `new_offload_keys` empties, `prepare_store` is skipped, and with it the cascade. ### Why symmetric (non-PD) Multi Tier is unaffected `session/server.py`: > `# Supply came from inbound lookup pins (symmetric): no late submit_store can arrive, so unmatched fetch demand fails fast. PD rounds park demand for stores instead.` `session/client.py`: > `PD-only loads leave probes/unsent empty ... PD clients never probe and stay on round 0.` The symmetric path supplies from tier lookups and pins, which need neither a store job nor GPU block ids, so a warm producer is its best case. PD has no equivalent route. ### Impact at scale Shared-prefix workload, 8 producers + 8 consumers, 10,800 requests. Supply match rate tracks producer cache warmth: | | cold | warming | warm | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | fetch demand matched | 93.8% | 51.5% | **36.7%** | 6,083 load timeouts were logged against 10,800 requests. End to end this made PD Multi Tier slower than plain NIXL P/D on the same hardware (1571 s vs 1032 s to completion; mean TPOT 92 ms vs 10.7 ms). ### Question Should the PD Multi Tier path gain a lookup/pin supply route like the symmetric one, or should the p2p tier declare `REQUEST_LEVEL` (and the store path then be able to offload prefix-hit blocks that have no GPU block id)? The second looks like it fights both the `BLOCK_LEVEL` optimisation and the missing block-id constraint, so the first seems closer to the existing design — but that is your call. cc @liranschour

signal.title: [Quantization] Support online quantization with partially pre-quantized checkpoints
signal.text: ## Disclosure AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually. ## Purpose Allow online quantization on the unquantized `linear` or `moe` portions of a partially pre-quantized checkpoint **from ANY `quant_method` (Quark, ModelOpt, compressed-tensors, etc.)**. The original `quant_method` remains responsible for its pre-quantized layers, the composed config applies the requested online method only when the checkpoint returns an unquantized method. Example use cases: - Supersedes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49313 that attempts to do the same for `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4` that quantizes only the MOE layers. - Take e.g. [`nvidia/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-NVFP4`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-NVFP4) (modelopt checkpoint) or [`amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4`](https://huggingface.co/amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4) (quark checkpoint) that apply non-shared MOE expert only quantization, and quantize additional layers as needed (for evaluation or optimization purposes - Relax the need to release several models with different preset pre-quantized layers / different ignore lists). - Eventually, support `shared_experts` online quantization (not in this PR) This PR will work nicely with https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51285 once it is merged. Implementation details: - Online quantization is stored as `QuantizationConfig.online_quant_config`. `QuantizationConfig.get_effective_quant_method` **resolves the global quant method, including both the base checkpoint quant method and the online quant method**. The original `QuantizationConfig` subclass instantiation is preserved (e.g. `Fp8Config`), so **model developers do not need to be aware of this online quantization composition** (see examples below). - Selected layers for `online` that are already pre-quantized fail clearly instead of being silently replaced. - Activation-only overrides remain owned by the original checkpoint quantizer - `quantization_config.ignore` excludes applies only to `online`, as done currently on `main`. Preserving the original checkpoint config type is required for existing model-specific behavior: - Quark Qwen3Next shared-expert fusion reads Quark exclusion metadata and controls fusion: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4f76c8ad9d8ec06e91ac9c84895e07a1913d7726/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_next.py#L81-L98 https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4f76c8ad9d8ec06e91ac9c84895e07a1913d7726/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_next.py#L154-L162 - Kimi K2.5 checks for `CompressedTensorsConfig` before quantizing its multimodal projector: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4f76c8ad9d8ec06e91ac9c84895e07a1913d7726/vllm/model_executor/models/kimi_k25.py#L393-L396 - GLM4.1V selects a compressed-tensors-specific QKV prefix: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4f76c8ad9d8ec06e91ac9c84895e07a1913d7726/vllm/model_executor/models/glm4_1v.py#L303-L308 - Qianfan OCR applies `Fp8Config` visual-layer safety exclusions: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4f76c8ad9d8ec06e91ac9c84895e07a1913d7726/vllm/model_executor/models/qianfan_ocr.py#L69-L92 Behavior change from `main`: `--quantization-config` can now be used with a checkpoint `quant_method` for online weight composition. A request that selects an already pre-quantized layer now fails clearly instead of replacing the checkpoint method. Left to do: - [ ] Real model testing. - [ ] Is `--quantization-config` usage for different `quant_method` (base + online) ok? - [ ] Is `QuantizationConfig.online_quant_config` ok? - [ ] Shared experts online quantization (in an other PR). ## Test Plan Added tests in - `pytest tests/quantization/test_online.py -k test_online_prequantized_compatibility -vvvvv -s` - `pytest tests/quantization/test_online.py -k test_online_prequantized_checkpoint_selected_layer_fails -vvvvv -s` - `pytest tests/quantization/test_online.py -k tinysmokeqwen3moe -vvvvv -s` The tests cover Quark, ModelOpt, and compressed-tensors dispatch; activation-only overrides; online ignore retaining checkpoint quantization; and real tiny compressed-tensors checkpoint conflicts for selected linear and MoE layers. ## Test Result Passes on MI355.

signal.title: [Online quantization] Add targeted online quantization configuration based on user patterns
signal.text: ## Motivation Enable targeted online quantization on specific layers. This includes: - (future PR) preventing silent layer-specific online quantization: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/dc9f845ddc54c1df38fdbce5afe03f9fd15813bd/vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py#L547 ==> should use this API instead (as this hard-coding causes issues, see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48051) - (future PR probably) enable shared expert quantization on checkpoints shipping unquantized shared experts (e.g. useful for evaluation purposes) - Simplify the online quantization API (see e.g. complex pattern `--quantization-config '{"linear":"fp8_per_channel","ignore":["lm_head","re:.*embed_tokens.*","re:.*mlp\\.gate$","re:.*expert.*","re:.*kv_b_proj.*"]}'` to achieve this `targets` feature (e.g. in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49313)) ## Purpose Implements per-layer online quantization through `quantization_config.targets`, which follows the same spec as existing `quantization_config.ignore`. This addresses the [per-layer online quantization RFC](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/50281). Exact layer names, `re:` regex or `fnmatch`-style patterns allow to select different online shorthands per linear or MoE layer names patterns. Implementation details: - unmatched layers remain unquantized, - conflicting matches with `ignore` raise errors, - fused-layer matching is shared by `ignore` and `targets`. Additionally, an info log is added so that users are aware of what online quantization actually does, as: `INFO 08-06 16:35:33 [base_loader.py:106] Quantized 48 layers of types: block_sparse_moe.experts: 24 (from targets: re:.*block_sparse_moe\.experts, fp8_per_tensor); self_attn.o_proj: 24 (from targets: re:.*self_attn\.o_proj, fp8_per_block)` Additionally, Fused projections can now be targeted either by their fused module name (for example, `re:.*self_attn\.qkv_proj`) or by patterns that match every original shard (for example, `re:.*self_attn\.[qkv]_proj)`. This was a TODO: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/81be2e09aebfd1c45b3ed9f73d2850da8a72984c/tests/quantization/test_online.py#L64-L65 Note: **this behavior is now aligned for quark/compressed-tensors/online**. Note: previous ambiguous ignore regex as `re:.*v_proj` that did NOT resolve to `qkv_proj` now do. This is a "breaking" change. These kind of ambiguous patterns should probably not be used. Left to do: - [x] Probably left to an other PR: implement online quantization compatibility with other quantization methods (done in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51392) - [ ] End-to-end test on real model - [ ] Shared experts quantization support - [ ] Shared experts fusion support (in an other PR) ## Test Plan - `pytest tests/quantization/test_online.py -s -vvvvv` (includes new tests) - `pytest tests/quantization/test_config_utils.py -s -vvvvv` (includes new tests for targets case) - `pytest tests/quantization/test_config_utils.py -s -vvvvv` (includes tests for `ignore`/`targets` parity and `should_ignore_layer` refactor correctness) ## Test Result Tests pass. ## Disclosure AI assistance was used to develop this PR.
signal.author: fxmarty-amd

signal.title: [RFC][Bug Fix][Spec Decode] Require explicit speculative methods
signal.text: This PR removes speculative-method guessing and makes method selection an explicit contract. ## Problem On current `main`, vLLM guesses the speculative method from model path/name substrings such as `eagle3`, `dflash`, and `dspark`. A DFlash or DSpark checkpoint at a neutral training path can therefore be treated as the generic autoregressive `draft_model`, while renaming or moving the same checkpoint changes serving behavior. For example: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \ --speculative-config '{ "model": "/path/to/checkpoints/6", "num_speculative_tokens": 15 }' ``` Previously, this could silently select `draft_model`. In the original end-to-end Qwen3-8B + DFlash reproduction, the misdetected path produced acceptance length 1.02; adding explicit `"method": "dflash"` produced 3.88. Serving a specialized checkpoint through the wrong proposer is worse than requiring an explicit algorithm, so unresolved configurations now fail closed. ## Design - `method` is the sole algorithm selector. It may come from `"method"` in `--speculative-config`, `--spec-method`, or a known checkpoint schema that explicitly declares its algorithm. - There is no method inference from paths, names, checkpoint architectures, structural `model_type`, or other compatible metadata. - `model` only identifies an external draft source; it never selects or validates the method. - Known declarations, currently the speculators format, act as field-wise defaults for settings such as `method`, `num_speculative_tokens`, and PEagle's `parallel_drafting`. Every user-provided field takes precedence independently. - If a legacy or ambiguous checkpoint does not declare its algorithm and the user omits `method`, vLLM raises a clear error instead of falling back to `draft_model`. - Model-free methods—`ngram`, `ngram_gpu`, `suffix`, and `extract_hidden_states`—reject `model`. - Methods backed by an external draft source require `model`. For `custom_class`, it contains the proposer module path. - `mtp` and `dspark` may omit `model` when their weights are embedded in the target checkpoint; otherwise they accept an external draft source. - After method selection, checkpoint metadata may configure the selected implementation. This includes the embedded DeepSeek-V4 DSpark loader and token-count defaults from speculators `speculative_tokens`, `n_predict`, and DFlash/DSpark block layouts. - DFlash reads both top-level and nested `dflash_config.block_size`. DSpark accounts for whether the anchor is sampled. These are defaults only; an explicit `num_speculative_tokens` still wins. - DFlash and DSpark parallel-drafting behavior is enabled by the explicit method. For an embedded DeepSeek-V4 checkpoint, the same checkpoint metadata is handled according to the requested method: `draft_model` keeps the ordinary model loader, `mtp` uses `DeepSeekV4MTPModel`, and `dspark` uses `DSparkDraftModel`. The metadata does not choose among them. ## User experience and breaking change Configurations that relied on implicit path/name matching must add a method. Before: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \ --speculative-config '{ "model": "/path/to/checkpoints/6", "num_speculative_tokens": 15 }' ``` After: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \ --spec-method dflash \ --spec-model /path/to/checkpoints/6 ``` When the DFlash checkpoint exposes its block size, `num_speculative_tokens` defaults from that metadata; users may still set `--spec-tokens` explicitly. A speculators-format draft declares both its algorithm and proposal depth, so this also works without guessing: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \ --spec-model /path/to/speculators-checkpoint ``` For a generic autoregressive draft model, use `method="draft_model"`. Legacy EAGLE/EAGLE3, Medusa, MLP-speculator, and custom-proposer configurations must likewise state their method and external source. Model-free configurations state only the method and its settings: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \ --speculative-config '{ "method": "ngram", "num_speculative_tokens": 5, "prompt_lookup_max": 5 }' ``` The old `"model": "[ngram]"` and `"model": "ngram"` sentinels are rejected. A speculators-format checkpoint used as the top-level model still works without an explicit `--speculative-config`, because its schema declares the algorithm and proposal depth. ## Validation - End-to-end reproduction recorded before this design change: - misdetected `draft_model`: acceptance length 1.02 - explicit `dflash`: acceptance length 3.88 - This PR now rejects the unresolved configuration instead of silently serving it autoregressively. - Full `tests/test_config.py` except the two tests requiring gated `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct` access: 222 passed, 2 deselected. - Focused schema/default regression matrix: 17 passed. - DSpark configuration module: 12 passed. - Full draft HF override module: 11 passed. - Structured-output speculative decoding: 3 passed. - Extract-hidden-states configuration regressions: 2 passed. - All configured pre-commit hooks passed on the changed follow-up files, including Ruff, mypy, Markdown lint, SPDX, and configuration validation. The commit sign-off hook also passed. - GPU model evaluation was not rerun for this configuration follow-up; the earlier DFlash measurement above is retained as the motivating model result. <details> <summary>Commands run</summary> ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_config.py \ -k 'not test_rope_customization and not test_eagle_draft_model_config' .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_config.py \ -k 'spec_model_declaration or block_drafters_default_tokens or speculators_format_declares or speculators_format_preserves' .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/transformers_utils/test_dspark_mla_config.py .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/config/test_speculative_draft_hf_overrides.py .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/v1/structured_output/test_backend_guidance.py::test_grammar_bitmask_with_specdec \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py::test_bitmask_with_padded_invalid_drafts .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_extract_hidden_states.py::test_extract_hidden_states_text_only_config_regression \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_extract_hidden_states.py::test_extract_hidden_states_config_preserves_vlm_text_config .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \ docs/features/speculative_decoding/README.md \ tests/test_config.py \ vllm/config/speculative.py \ vllm/transformers_utils/config.py ``` </details> ## Contribution notes - This is not a duplicate of #47490: that PR preserves auto-detection and validates explicit-method mismatches; this PR removes automatic method selection and fails when neither the user nor a declared schema supplies a method. - This is not a duplicate of #44566: that PR only propagates token depth from a speculators-format draft; this PR changes method-selection semantics while preserving declared token defaults. - This is not a duplicate of #52165: that PR detects embedded DeepSeek-V4 DSpark metadata for routing; this PR keeps the explicit method authoritative and uses metadata only to configure the selected implementation. - AI assistance was used. I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation listed above.

signal.title: [Model] Add GraniteSWA and GraniteMoeSWA via existing Granite
signal.text: ## Purpose Supersedes and closes #48270 Add vLLM support for GraniteSWA and GraniteMoeSWA models, folded into the existing Granite and GraniteMoeShared implementation, as opposed to separate models as in #48270. - GraniteSWA: Granite with per-layer sliding-window attention and a learnable per-head attention sink. The sink is passed to Attention via the native vllm attention harness, the per-layer windowing via config.layer_types and config.sliding_window, and per-layer RoPE/NoPE via config.layer_rope_theta (0 for NoPE). - GraniteMoeSWA: GraniteMoeShared-style MoE combined with the SWA/sink attention above (reuses GraniteSWAAttention). Optional shared experts via shared_intermediate_size (disabled by default); routed experts load through the standard FusedMoE param mapping. Additional features (sinks, sliding window, varying RoPE) are off by default, leaving existing Granite checkpoints unaffected. Also add checkpoint remapping for handling both old- and new-style HF MoE layers. Register both [***]ForCausalLM classes in the model registry, since HF publishes these Granite variants as distinct models. NB: transformers backend does NOT handle these models correctly. Sink tokens get dropped silently and so the model gives wrong output (see #52156). Claude was used to assist in implementing these changes. I have reviewed, corrected, and contributed the code myself, and tested the output for correctness. ## Test Plan Tests include offline parity checks against the adapted HF implementations, addition of SWA/MoeSWA checkpoints to the Granite tests, additional unit tests for case handling of added features and HF naming schemes, and GSM8K verification. Testing env uses CUDA 13.0, Torch 2.13.0, and Transformers 5.16.0. I have not included the parity check script(s) in this PR. ## Test Result All unit tests pass. I have confirmed that this code produces identical output to the HF implementation at fp32 precision, and that the transformers modeling backend does not. Bfloat 16 is near-identical (one missed token prediction in a teacher-forced setting on a randomly initialized model). Parity checks include sinks on/off, RoPE varying/global, and TP on/off. GSM8K score for the 2B SWA model is within 2 points of the published HF model card (40.3 vs 42.2 for 5-shot).

signal.title: [AMD] Add a guard for EPLB/DBO plus fused share expert conflict
signal.text: ## Purpose VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS fuses the shared expert into the routed-expert MoE by appending a per-rank shared-expert slot. That extra slot changes the routed-expert count each rank sees, which silently breaks features that assume a stable per-rank routed-expert layout: * EPLB – per-expert bookkeeping/relocation relies on a consistent routed-expert count (the fused slot inflates it), so enabling both produces wrong expert accounting. * Dual batch overlap (DBO / AITER "TBO") – the batch-overlap microbatching path (enable_dbo / ubatch_size > 1) is not compatible with the fused MoE layout. Today these combinations fail deep in the MoE path (or produce incorrect results) instead of a clear config-time error. This PR adds a single, centralized guard in RocmPlatform.check_and_update_config that rejects fused shared-experts together with EPLB or DBO up front. It's the natural place to extend as other mutually exclusive features are added. This is a follow-up to #47220 (Enable EPLB for Quark OCP MXFP4 MoE), moving the incompatibility check out of the per-quant-method supports_eplb property and into config validation so it applies to all MoE methods, not just Quark MXFP4. ## Test Plan Added unit tests ## Test Result ``` ============================= test session starts ============================== platform linux -- Python 3.12.13, pytest-9.1.1, pluggy-1.6.0 -- /usr/bin/python3 cachedir: .pytest_cache rootdir: /tmp plugins: asyncio-1.4.0, anyio-4.14.1 asyncio: mode=Mode.STRICT, debug=False, asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope=None, asyncio_default_test_loop_scope=function collecting ... collected 5 items test_guard.py::test_no_conflict_when_fused_se_disabled PASSED [ 20%] test_guard.py::test_fused_se_alone_is_allowed PASSED [ 40%] test_guard.py::test_fused_se_with_eplb_raises PASSED [ 60%] test_guard.py::test_fused_se_with_ubatching_raises PASSED [ 80%] test_guard.py::test_eplb_conflict_checked_before_ubatching PASSED [100%] =============================== warnings summary =============================== <frozen importlib._bootstrap>:488 <frozen importlib._bootstrap>:488: DeprecationWarning: builtin type SwigPyPacked has no __module__ attribute <frozen importlib._bootstrap>:488 <frozen importlib._bootstrap>:488: DeprecationWarning: builtin type SwigPyObject has no __module__ attribute ../usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/torch/jit/_script.py:365: 14 warnings /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/torch/jit/_script.py:365: DeprecationWarning: `torch.jit.script_method` is deprecated. Please switch to `torch.compile` or `torch.export`. warnings.warn( -- Docs: https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/how-to/capture-warnings.html ======================== 5 passed, 16 warnings in 3.63s ======================== --- ``` <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Core][Quantization] Support ModelOpt layer-wise mixed KV cache
signal.text: ## Purpose This is the vLLM consumer for [NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer#2211](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer/pull/2211). The ModelOpt PR searches a layer-wise KV-cache recipe and exports the selected formats in the versioned `kv_cache_quantized_layers` checkpoint metadata. This PR reads that metadata and selects the KV-cache dtype for each vLLM attention layer. With this PR alone, a checkpoint produced by the ModelOpt PR can mix: - full FP8 K/V layers, using vLLM's existing FP8 KV implementation; and - full NVFP4 K/V layers, using vLLM's existing NVFP4 KV implementation. There are no CUDA/C++ or attention-kernel changes here. FP8-K/NVFP4-V within a single layer is intentionally rejected because that format requires the separate mixed-K/V kernel implementation. The two full-K/V formats above do not require that kernel work. The checkpoint recipe is used only when `kv_cache_dtype="auto"`. An explicit `--kv-cache-dtype` continues to override every layer, and `--kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers` continues to take precedence for selected layers. Layers omitted from the checkpoint mapping remain in the model dtype. This does not duplicate existing mixed-KV work: - #41684 keeps selected token ranges in a high-precision sibling cache; it does not load a layer-wise ModelOpt format map. - #49623 detects packed mixed cache specs; it does not parse checkpoint-selected per-layer KV dtypes. This contribution was developed with AI assistance. The human submitter reviewed the complete diff and remains responsible for the implementation and validation. ## Test Plan - Validate ModelOpt schema-v1 parsing for full FP8 K/V and full NVFP4 K/V. - Verify Hugging Face-to-vLLM layer-name mapping, including the vLLM `.attn` suffix. - Verify only mapped layers load KV scaling factors. - Reject unknown schema versions and FP8-K/NVFP4-V entries without the required kernel integration. - Run the changed-file pre-commit suite and a ModelOpt-exported checkpoint smoke on CUDA. ## Test Result - Changed-file pre-commit suite: passed. - Ruff check and format - mypy (Python 3.10) - typos and Markdown lint - repository policy/configuration checks - Python byte-compilation of all changed Python files: passed. - Focused CUDA unit suite on NVIDIA GB300: 4 passed in 7.14 seconds (AWS-CMH Slurm job `3133718`). This covers FP8/NVFP4 layer resolution, omitted layers, schema/format rejection, and composed Gemma layer mapping. - The focused pytest invocation is currently environment-blocked on the local macOS host: the CUDA-oriented vLLM test stack exits before collection in `xgrammar`'s `TVMFFIEnvRegisterCAPI` static initialization. No test assertion ran or failed. - End-to-end ModelOpt-exported checkpoint smoke: pending; this PR remains a draft until that result is attached. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The current test results and explicit pending CUDA validation. - [x] The necessary documentation update. </details>

signal.title: [Bugfix][CPU] Take an attention group's query head count from its layers
signal.text: ## Purpose `CPUAttentionMetadataBuilder` sizes the split-KV scratchpad from the model-wide query head count, but the kernel runs with each layer's own count. so models that vary it per layer (e.g. Laguna) index past the end of the scratchpad and the decode segfaults or hangs. Attention groups are keyed on `num_heads_q`, so take the count from the group's layers via `get_num_attention_heads_from_layers()`, as `triton_attn` and `flashinfer` already do. Models with a uniform count are unaffected. Change-Id: I671eadc2b5601f1a3af12f39391657a11df1c9f7 ## Test Plan - `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_group_head_counts.py` — new unit test, mirroring `test_group_sliding_window.py`: uniform heads, Laguna-style alternating heads, and a default that is not the most common count. - A tiny Laguna config with per-layer heads `[8, 16, 8, 16]` against 2 KV heads and random weights (`load_format=dummy`, so no checkpoint is needed), decoding 512 tokens so split-KV reduction engages. Run both on unpatched `main` and with this change. - Laguna-XS-2.1-INT4 end to end on CPU with TP=2: a 300-token decode, plus GSM8K 5-shot over the full 1319 prompts via lm_eval. <details> <summary>Reproducer</summary> ```python import json, os, tempfile from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams CONFIG = { "architectures": ["LagunaForCausalLM"], "model_type": "laguna", "hidden_size": 512, "intermediate_size": 1024, "num_hidden_layers": 4, "num_attention_heads": 8, "num_attention_heads_per_layer": [8, 16, 8, 16], "num_key_value_heads": 2, "head_dim": 64, "max_position_embeddings": 4096, "rms_norm_eps": 1e-6, "rope_theta": 500000.0, "tie_word_embeddings": False, "torch_dtype": "bfloat16", "mlp_only_layers": [0, 1, 2, 3], "num_experts": 4, "num_experts_per_tok": 2, "moe_intermediate_size": 128, "shared_expert_intermediate_size": 128, } model_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp() with open(os.path.join(model_dir, "config.json"), "w") as f: json.dump(CONFIG, f) llm = LLM(model=model_dir, tokenizer="<any tokenizer>", load_format="dummy", dtype="bfloat16", max_model_len=2048, enforce_eager=True) out = llm.generate(["context " * 64], SamplingParams(max_tokens=512, temperature=0.0, ignore_eos=True)) print("SURVIVED", len(out[0].outputs[0].token_ids)) ``` </details> ## Test Result - Unit tests: 6 passed (3 new, plus the 3 existing sliding-window cases). - Reproducer: hangs on current `main` and is killed at the timeout; passes in 1.5s with this change. - Laguna-XS 300-token decode: previously segfaulted or hung, now completes in 47s with coherent output. - GSM8K 5-shot, full 1319 prompts. Before this change the same run died with an `execute_model` timeout. | Filter | exact_match | stderr | | --- | --- | --- | | flexible-extract | 0.9014 | ±0.0082 | | strict-match | 0.8908 | ±0.0086 | Instrumenting the scratchpad bounds shows the overrun directly on unpatched `main`: the region holds 6336 bytes per KV head while the split-KV write path needs 8384, because sizing assumes 6 query heads per KV head (48 heads / 8 KV heads) and the 64-head layers address it with a stride of 8. ``` [SCRATCHPAD-SIZING] split_num=2 max_tile=6 q_heads=24 kv_heads=4 q_per_kv=6 per_kv_head=6336 [SCRATCHPAD-OVERFLOW] per_head_need=8384 per_kv_head=6336 q_head_tile_size=8 ``` Models whose layers share one head count keep the existing single-blob path, so there is no extra allocation or lookup for them. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Bugfix] Muse Glimmer: apply structured outputs to the to=user answer
signal.text: ## Purpose `response_format: json_schema` (and other guided-decoding requests) are silently ignored for Muse Glimmer: the model free-generates prose instead of schema-constrained JSON. `json_object` works, so the gap is specific to schema-constrained output. **Root cause:** the structured-outputs backend only applies the grammar after the reasoning parser reports reasoning-end, but `MuseGlimmerReasoningParser.is_reasoning_end` only returned `True` when a *tool* channel opened — a `to=user` final answer was never treated as reasoning-end. On a no-tool request the grammar was therefore never engaged. ## Approach Muse Glimmer's channel handling is kept out of the shared `DelegatingParser`. A dedicated composite `MuseGlimmerParser(DelegatingParser)` (mirroring `KimiK3Parser`) owns the model-specific routing, and grammar activation is separated from stream ownership: - **Grammar activation** lives in `MuseGlimmerReasoningParser.is_reasoning_end`, which the structured-outputs backend calls directly. It fires once the current turn opens any non-`self` channel (the `to=user` answer **or** a `to=<tool>` call), detected on the *last* channel header so a turn that answers the user and then calls a tool is not pinned to the answer channel. This is what lets `response_format` engage on a no-tool request. - **Stream ownership** lives in `MuseGlimmerParser`: `is_reasoning_end_streaming` only transitions the phase machine when a tool channel opens, so the reasoning parser keeps emitting the `to=user` answer body itself and never hands it to the tool parser prematurely (which would otherwise drop the body or leak the channel header). The `tool_choice="none"` and no-tool-parser paths are handled locally in the composite, stripping channel framing rather than leaking it into content. The shared `vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py` and `vllm/reasoning/abs_reasoning_parsers.py` are unchanged, so other models are unaffected. ## Test Plan ```bash # focused unit tests for this fix pytest tests/tool_use/test_muse_glimmer.py tests/tool_use/test_muse_glimmer_parse_delta.py # regression for the shared DelegatingParser / parser registry pytest tests/parser/ tests/reasoning/ ``` E2E against a served `meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B` (bf16, 2x H100) with `--tool-call-parser muse_glimmer --reasoning-parser muse_glimmer`: ```bash SCHEMA='{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"capital":{"type":"string"}},"required":["name","capital"],"additionalProperties":false}' curl -s localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d "{\"model\":\"muse-glimmer\",\"temperature\":0,\"max_tokens\":2048,\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"What is France?\"}],\"response_format\":{\"type\":\"json_schema\",\"json_schema\":{\"name\":\"country\",\"schema\":$SCHEMA}}}" ``` Also tested `response_format: json_object`, plain chat, and `tool_choice` auto/required/named, streaming and non-streaming. ## Test Result **`json_schema`** returns schema-conformant JSON, non-streaming and streaming: ```json { "name": "France", "capital": "Paris" } ``` - Unit tests pass (`tests/tool_use/test_muse_glimmer*.py`). - Live-server E2E: `json_schema` is schema-conformant across several schema shapes, streaming and non-streaming; `json_object`, plain chat, and `tool_choice` auto/required/named remain correct with no channel framing leaked into content. --- This PR was developed with AI assistance. All changed lines were reviewed by the submitter and validated end-to-end on a live Muse-Glimmer-30B server as above. Co-authored-by: OpenAI Codex

signal.title: [AMD][K3] Write KDA decode output straight into the layer buffer
signal.text:
## Purpose fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode allocated its own output, so the layer then copied it into the core_attn_out buffer it had already allocated. Give the op an out= parameter and pass core_attn_out on the plain-decode path, which drops one device-to-device copy per KDA layer. Only safe when there is no spec-decode output to interleave: that path places both halves via index_copy_ into a separate tensor, so it keeps its own buffer. The sibling fused_recurrent_kda already took out= this way. ## Test Plan E2E perf tests accuracy test using aiperf recipe ## Test Result Measured on Kimi-K3 MXFP4, 8xMI355X, ISL 131072 / conc 16 decode: 615 of 1445 copyBuffer kernels removed and the KDA epilogue drops from 47.8 to 42.6 us per layer. Output and the in-place recurrent state are bitwise identical to the allocating path. E2E AgentX for 8k1k cocn 1,8,16. E2E AgentX for 128k1k conc 16 Accuracy n-samples: {"original": 1319, "effective": 1319} ---

signal.author: SageMoore

signal.title: [ROCm][CI] Fix intermittent GPU memory fault during sleep-mode wake-up
signal.text: ROCm sleep-mode wake-up can intermittently abort the EngineCore on MI300 while remapping roughly 172 GiB, as seen in [build 12090](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12090/list?sid=01a004a6-9a94-48ba-8be1-20f23544b8e0&tab=output) and the earlier signature-matched [build 11862](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/11862/list?sid=019fe4e5-8d10-4dca-8454-8c50409fefda&tab=output). Both failures occurred about 0.53 seconds into the first wake on different MI300 hosts, with the same GPU address-`nil` fault and `create_and_map -> wake_up` stack, while their MI355 jobs passed. PR #44972 added an allocator-wide ROCm `hipMemset` after VMM remapping to scrub stale VRAM on older amdgpu drivers and prevent discarded Mamba/GDN state from corrupting generation. That memset is the only device-wide access at the observed fault point and unnecessarily touches the full attention KV allocation, making it the high-confidence vLLM trigger even though the underlying defect may be a ROCm VMM race. A controlled restoration of the old leaf passed 40/40 local cycles, so this remains an intermittent mitigation rather than a deterministic native A/B reproduction. This change forward-ports the unmerged `0ab7e793` design by clearing only bound Mamba/GDN state after KV remapping and preserving packed cache offsets and strides. It preserves the functional motivation of #44972 but intentionally does not retain its broader allocator-wide scrubbing guarantee for discarded bytes on affected old drivers. Proposed changes: - Remove the ROCm whole-allocation `hipMemset` from `create_and_map`. - Rebuild packed Mamba cache views with their configured byte offset and per-block stride in both model runners. - Zero only bound Mamba/GDN conv and recurrent state views after a full or KV-tagged wake, without touching attention KV or weights-only wakes. - Deduplicate aliased state views so shared storage is cleared once. - Add assertion-level regression coverage that fails 4/4 on the pre-fix implementation and passes 4/4 with this change.
signal.author: AndreasKaratzas

signal.title: [Bugfix] Fix cross-batch buffer race corrupting DiskBackend loads
signal.text: ## Purpose I had a look at the recently merged DiskBackend for KV offloading (#49644), thanks @chengy-sysu. I noticed a subtle bug in `_do_load`'s double-buffer pipeline: pending H2D events were tracked in a list local to each call and, unlike `_do_store`, never drained before returning. A later `_do_load` call's preadv could therefore overwrite a buffer slot while the previous call's trailing H2D copy was still reading it, silently corrupting the GPU KV cache on reload. This PR drains the trailing events before `_do_load` returns, mirroring `_do_store`'s existing pattern, and adds a regression test that fails without the fix and passes with it. Tagging @ivanium & @aoshen02 who reviewed https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49644. AI-assisted, every line reviewed and tested by the submitter. ## Test Plan ``` pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_disk_backend.py -v ``` ## Test Result All 3 tests pass with the fix. `test_do_load_drains_inflight_before_next_batch` fails on main (preadv overwrote slot(s) [0, 1] while a prior batch's H2D was still reading them) and passes with this patch.
signal.author: fjosw

signal.title: [Bugfix][Model] Fix DiffusionGemma silently freezing attention mask under CUDA graph replay
signal.text: ## Purpose While looking into whether FULL CUDA graphs are worth the added complexity for DiffusionGemma, I found that `DiffusionGemmaModelState._causal_buf` (the per-request flag that switches each request between causal/encoder and bidirectional/denoise attention) stops being updated once `CUDAGraphMode.FULL` graphs are captured. It's bool, but FlashAttentionMetadataBuilder.build() casts non-int32 causal tensors via `causal.to(torch.int32)`, allocating a new tensor every call. A FULL-mode graph binds to the address it saw at capture time, so once captured it keeps reading that orphaned tensor forever. Later updates to `_causal_buf` never reach it. Any request served through an already-captured FULL graph gets whatever causal/bidirectional pattern existed at capture (warmup) time for its slot, for the graph's whole lifetime, silently. This isn't opt-in: vLLM's default optimization level (O2) resolves cudagraph_mode to FULL_AND_PIECEWISE, whose decode_mode() is FULL, so `vllm serve google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it` with no flags already runs every denoise/decode step under FULL cudagraphs. I couldn't pin observed output corruption on this specifically: an E2E FULL-vs-PIECEWISE comparison was inconclusive, since DiffusionGemma's denoising has its own run-to-run variance of similar magnitude. The capture/replay test below reproduces the mechanism directly instead. So overall, this is a silent bug that likely has some unpredictable impact on output quality. Fix: make `_causal_buf` int32 from construction and update it in place (`.copy_()` / direct assignment) instead of = from a bool source, so build() takes its dtype-matched fast path and never reallocates. Tagging @LucasWilkinson, who authored the original FULL-cudagraph path in #45163. AI-assisted, every line reviewed and tested by the submitter. ## Test Plan `pytest tests/models/test_diffusion_gemma_cudagraph.py -v` ## Test Result New regression test constructs a real DiffusionGemmaModelState and drives _causal_buf through an actual torch.cuda.CUDAGraph capture/replay cycle mirroring FlashAttention's cast. Fails on main: replay returns the stale `[0, 0, 0, 0]` instead of the updated `[1, 1, 1, 1]`. Passes with this patch. Run on H100 (SM90).

signal.title: [ROCm][AMD] Kimi-K3 gfx942 / MI325X Gap and Roadmap
signal.text: Sibling of [#50682](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/50682). That tracker is the general Kimi-K3 ROCm roadmap. Most of it is gfx950 / MI355X. This issue is the gfx942 / MI325X (and MI300X) plan on top of current `vllm-project/vllm` main. gfx942 is already listed as a one-line gap in #50682, with [#50817](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50817) as the enablement PR. The work below should land as stacked PRs on main, not as a private fork. CC: - [@xaguilar-amd](https://github.com/xaguilar-amd) - [@hissu-hyvarinen](https://github.com/hissu-hyvarinen) - [@jhartika-amd](https://github.com/jhartika-amd) - [@hongxiayang](https://github.com/hongxiayang) - [@tjtanaa](https://github.com/tjtanaa) - [@seanfilimon](https://github.com/seanfilimon) - [@mpashkovskii](https://github.com/mpashkovskii) - [@LucasWilkinson](https://github.com/LucasWilkinson) - [@fxmarty-amd](https://github.com/fxmarty-amd) ## Why gfx942 is a separate plan Kimi-K3 is 93 layers, 69 KDA + 24 gated MLA, 96 heads. TP8 is 12 heads per rank. The day-0 image and [recipes.vllm.ai Kimi-K3](https://recipes.vllm.ai/moonshotai/Kimi-K3?hardware=mi355x&features=reasoning) target MI355X. On gfx942 today: - [#50516](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50516) makes the MXFP4 checkpoint constructible via lossless EMULATION. That path is about 9x to 15x slower than a real quantized MoE kernel, and it does not survive CUDA-graph capture. See the gfx942 measurements on #50682. - The fused KDA decode kernel from [#50654](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50654) is still gfx950-only in current main. Runtime gate is `on_gfx950()` in `is_fused_kda_decode_supported`. CMake only adds `fused_kda_decode_kernel_rocm.cu` when `gfx950` is in the arch list. - Gluon MLA decode asserts `mla_gluon requires gfx950` for the 12-head TP8 shape unless the asm pad-to-16 path is used. ## KDA decode fallback is still on main This is not leftover fork code. On gfx942, current main still runs the unfused KDA decode path: `causal_conv1d_update` + `fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode` + `FusedRMSNormGated.forward_native`. The native gated RMSNorm is `pow` / `mean` / `rsqrt` / `sigmoid` as separate ATen launches. Inductor does not fuse this on ROCm. Measured on MI325X, TP8, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, `moonshotai/Kimi-K3`, one representative KDA+MoE decode layer. CUDA-graph replay, so these are real launches inside the graph. KDA decode block only (conv + recurrent + gated output RMSNorm), 16 launches, 74.9 us: | Step | Launches | Time (us) | | --- | ---: | ---: | | `causal_conv1d_update` | 1 | 4.7 | | `fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode` | 1 | 10.8 | | `FusedRMSNormGated.forward_native` (`aten::pow`, `mean`, `rsqrt` path, `sigmoid`, copies) | 14 | 59.4 | | **KDA decode fallback total** | **16** | **74.9** | That is about 17% of this KDA+MoE layer. There are 69 KDA layers. [#52293](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52293) collapses the same block to one kernel at 7.8 us on gfx942. End-to-end TPOT barely moves until MoE is no longer the emulation path. The fusion is still required. The 14 ATen launches sit on the ~4 us launch floor and will not get cheaper by themselves. The rest of a KDA+MoE layer is MoE routing, expert GEMM, TP all-reduce, and AttnRes. Those are later waves. The table above is the KDA fusion case. ## Wave 0: make gfx942 a real upstream baseline Nightly is not a gfx942 baseline until a real MoE kernel and a small-head MLA route exist on main. 1. **AITER pin that includes [ROCm/aiter#4646](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4646).** [#51728](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51728) bumps to `v0.1.19.post2`. That tag is 2026-08-05. aiter#4646 (FlyDSL a16wi4) merged 2026-08-13, so it is not in post2. #51728 is still open, so including 4646 in this bump is still doable. Either retarget #51728 at a SHA after `4bbc57db`, or land post2 and follow immediately with a pin that contains 4646. #50682 already lists 4646 under the AITER docker upgrade. gfx942 should not wait for a later release if this pin can take it now. 2. **[#50817](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50817).** Native MXFP4 Triton `moe_gemm_a16w4` on gfx942, plus pad-to-16 MLA for 12 heads at TP8. This is the default enablement path. It does not depend on aiter#4646. Reported decode went from the emulation baseline to about 100 tok/s. 3. **Recipes and CI.** A gfx942 recipe on recipes.vllm.ai, and a gfx942 gsm8k / serve job on the public ROCm image. Without that, gfx942 keeps regressing silently. 4. **Load-time INT4 through the online-quant RFC, not extra checkpoints.** See the quantization section below. ## Wave 1: KDA fusion on gfx942 All of this is on top of #50654 / [#52606](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52606), not a second KDA stack. 1. **[#52293](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52293).** Enable the existing fused KDA decode kernel on gfx942. This is the PR that removes the 16-launch block in the table. Do not open a competing o_norm fusion PR. 2. **[#51183](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51183).** Write KDA decode into the layer buffer. 3. **KDA prefill on gfx942.** #52606 is the fused prefill work, currently gfx950-gated. After it lands, a small gfx942 gate PR, same shape as #52293. ## Wave 2: MLA (blocked on open AITER) K3 MLA is dense gated MLA, NoPE, QK 192 / V 128, 12 heads per rank at TP8. Pad-to-16 in #50817 / [#50578](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50578) is the bridge. 1. [ROCm/aiter#4582](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4582) then draft [#51195](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51195) (native CDNA3 Gluon decode for measured verify shapes). 2. [ROCm/aiter#4645](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4645) then draft [#51551](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51551) (opt-in FP8 D192/V128 prefill). 3. A durable sub-16-head gfx942 decode in AITER, so we do not pad 12 heads to 16 forever. DSA sparse-MLA kernels (indexer + top-k) do not apply here. K3 is hybrid KDA + dense MLA. ## Wave 3: after MoE is not emulation Only after Wave 0. Otherwise the e2e signal is noise. - Latent-MoE all-reduce overlap: draft [#51437](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51437) - AttnRes follow-ups on top of [#50593](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50593) - GEMM / FlyDSL tile work that #50817 still has to runtime-patch [#52190](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52190) (`torch.compile` for `fused_qk_rmsnorm`) is not the gfx942 KDA o_norm fix. ## Load-time INT4 belongs in the online quantization RFC [#52167](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52167) item 4 is "Requantize already-quantized layers to different precision." It already cites draft [#51274](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51274). That is the right place. I think that we should not keep publishing extra Hugging Face checkpoints every time a new MXFP4 MoE model needs a gfx942 kernel. That is a bottleneck, and the models will keep coming. Kimi-K3, Qwen3.8, and likely more upcoming MXFP4 MoE models can use one opt-in at-load conversion onto an INT4 expert kernel that AITER already has (groupwise INT4 / a16wi4 once aiter#4646 is in the pin). #51274 is a Kimi-K3 prototype of that: `--quantization-config.moe.weight int4_per_group_32`, default path unchanged, lossy and explicit. It should be generalized under #52167 rather than cloned per model. It stays draft until the AITER pin contains [ROCm/aiter#4646](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4646). #50817 remains the native MXFP4 gfx942 path. Load-time INT4 is the opt-in when that kernel is missing or slower, not a silent default. ## How to use this issue Stack PRs on main. For each PR: full gsm8k if it can change text, and `vllm bench serve` with `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` if it claims perf. Same bar as #50682. Please comment here with gfx942 PRs so they do not only land on the gfx950 tracker. AI assistance was used to draft this tracker. I reviewed the plan, the public PR list, and the kernel table.

signal.title: [ROCm] Bump AITER to v0.1.19.post2
signal.text: ## Purpose Bump the ROCm base image's AITER pin from `v0.1.19` to `v0.1.19.post2` to pick up [ROCm/aiter#4312](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4312), which makes `fused_qk_norm_rope_cache_pts_quant_shuffle()` stride-aware for `block_size` and heads. Without it, the fused QK-norm+RoPE+KV-cache kernel hard-asserts and **aborts the process** (SIGABRT, exit 134) on the packed KV-cache layout: ``` [AITER] csrc/kernels/fused_qk_norm_rope_cache_quant.cu:3278 k_cache/v_cache must be contiguous within a block (dims >= 1) Fatal Python error: Aborted ``` `#44455` packed K/V into the content dim, `(num_blocks, num_kv_heads, block_size, 2*head_size)`, and `#49373` wired the AITER backends to read it via `transpose(1, 2).split(head_size, -1)`. Those views have a contiguous head *dim* but a head *stride* of a whole block (e.g. `(8192, 256, 4096, 1)` for `H=2, hs=128, N=16`), which the pre-#4312 kernel rejects. This is the AITER half of the fix agreed in [#49590](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49590), where a vLLM-side `.contiguous()` workaround was declined: > Duplicate of #49373, also this inserts a `.contiguous` which will break perf. The correct > fix is to bump AITER to include ROCm/aiter#4312, then land 49373. The vLLM half (#49373) merged on 2026-08-07; the AITER pin was never moved, so the abort is still live on the pinned version. ### Version arithmetic | ref | contains #4312 | guard | |---|---|---| | `v0.1.19` (current pin) | no — 15 commits behind the merge | asserts at line 3278 | | `v0.1.19.post1` | yes (ahead 40) | — | | `v0.1.19.post2` | yes (ahead 44) | assert removed | In `.post2` the `is_contiguous_from_dim1` guard is gone, replaced by explicit `k_stride_token` / `k_stride_head` / `k_stride_dim` indexing. ## Test Plan MI300X (gfx942). Built `v0.1.19.post2` from source and ran the fusion suite against **unmodified** `640a09086d` (no vLLM changes), so the pin is the only variable: ``` git clone --recursive --branch v0.1.19.post2 https://github.com/ROCm/aiter.git PYTHONPATH=/path/to/aiter-post2 \ pytest tests/compile/passes/test_rocm_aiter_qk_norm_rope_kvcache_fusion.py ``` ## Test Result | aiter | targeted subset (`ROCM_AITER_FA and full-neox and auto`) | |---|---| | 0.1.16.post2 (pre-#4312, same guard as `v0.1.19`) | **SIGABRT on the first case** | | `v0.1.19.post2` | **18 passed**, 18 skipped | The test asserts `fusion_pass.matched_count == 1` and compares fused vs unfused q/k/v **and** the KV cache, so these exercise the fused kernel and check it numerically on the packed layout. Full-suite run in progress; will update. ## Notes - `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base_gfx1250` tracks `AITER_BRANCH="main"` and is unaffected. - This does **not** unblock the `patch_gating_output` TODOs in `aiter_mxfp4_w4a8_moe.py` — those wait on [ROCm/aiter#4530](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4530), which is still open. - **AI assistance was used** for the investigation and testing above. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: [Misc] Bump `openai` to `>=2.25.0` to support namespace tools types
signal.text: ## Purpose Fix the dependency lower bound issue #49103. We have recently added OpenAI responses API namespace tools support, but the corresponding openai types are only supported for `openai>=2.25.0`. Hence the lower bound bump. Note that the dependency bump is necessary in the sense that any client with `openai<2.25.0` got an inevitable `ImportError` from the very beginning of vllm online serving process (see the error traceback in the linked issue). ## Test Plan No additional tests required - it just resolves the missing dependency lower bound bump. ## Test Result N/A --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [x] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Bugfix] Detect all attention-spelling variants in ModelConfig.is_hybrid
signal.text:
## Purpose `ModelConfig.is_hybrid`'s carve-out for granite-4.0-micro (a hybrid-capable architecture with zero actual mamba layers) only matched `layer_types` entries spelled `"attention"`. Transformers >= 5.13 normalizes pure-attention entries to `"full_attention"` instead (the model's own `granitemoehybrid.py` already handles both spellings in `ALL_DECODER_LAYER_TYPES` for layer dispatch, but `is_hybrid` never learned the new spelling). As a result `is_hybrid` stayed `True` for granite-4.0-micro. Combined with prefix caching now defaulting `mamba_cache_mode` to `"align"` for any hybrid-flagged model, `_get_mamba_bufs()` runs unconditionally and hits `AssertionError: no mamba layers in the model` on the first inference request — the engine starts and loads fine, then dies on the first completion. Fix: match both spellings in the carve-out. AI assistance was used to root-cause and author this fix; I reviewed every changed line and reproduced/verified the behavior end-to-end myself before opening this PR. ## Test Plan Reproduced on vLLM HEAD `37c3bdf5a` (2026-08-13): ``` vllm serve ibm-granite/granite-4.0-micro --max-model-len 8192 # then, once the server is up: curl http://localhost:8000/v1/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"ibm-granite/granite-4.0-micro","prompt":"The capital of France is","max_tokens":10}' ``` Then applied the fix and repeated the same two steps, plus a direct property check: ```python from vllm.config import ModelConfig mc = ModelConfig(model="ibm-granite/granite-4.0-micro") print(mc.is_hybrid) ``` ## Test Result **Before fix:** server starts and loads the model successfully, then the completion request fails the engine: ``` AssertionError: no mamba layers in the model File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 4437, in execute_model mamba_bufs = self._get_mamba_bufs() File ".../vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py", line 554, in get_mamba_groups assert len(mamba_group_ids) > 0, "no mamba layers in the model" vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue. ``` `ModelConfig("ibm-granite/granite-4.0-micro").is_hybrid` → `True` (incorrect). **After fix:** `is_hybrid` → `False` (correct — this model has no mamba layers). Server starts and the same completion request succeeds: ```json {"id":"cmpl-...","choices":[{"text":" Paris.

**Output:**
..."}], ...} ``` No crash, no assertion. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Hardware][XPU] Register matmul and linear batch-invariant kernels for XPU
signal.text: ## Purpose This is the second (2/2) PR introducing batch invariance to Intel XPU devices. You can find the first one [here](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41934). This PR registers the missing matmul and linear kernels. It also adds a new matmul_kernel_descriptor_persistent Triton kernel for better matmul performance on XPU. ## Test Plan Tested with unit tests covering batch invariance on XPU. ## Test Result All tests pass. ### Note The code was co-developed with GitHub Copilot. --- <details> Matmul and linear kernels were skipped in the previous PR, because they required more work. I tested batch invariance in Reinforcement Learning context and there I hit an error, because backward kernels were not registered for the "XPU" dispatch key. Also, I wanted to introduce a new Triton matmul kernel based on Tensor Derscriptors, because that implementation has shown ~3x speedup on XPU vs. the one based on pointers. </details>

signal.title: [K3 Perf] Optimize k3 mamba metadata preparation, 6.6~7.6x kernel performance improvement
signal.text: ## Purpose Optimize Kimi K3 Mamba `align` metadata preparation by computing aligned state indices for all KV-cache groups in one Triton launch. Before: ```text prepare_attn -> builder group 0 -> allocate buffer -> launch kernel -> builder group 1 -> allocate buffer -> launch kernel -> builder group N -> allocate buffer -> launch kernel ``` After: ```text prepare_attn -> persistent output buffer -> one multi-group Triton kernel -> directly use the buffer ``` ## Test Acc covered in current unit tests Perf can be seen in this AI generated script ```bash from types import SimpleNamespace import torch from vllm.models.kimi_k3.nvidia.kda_metadata import ( _mamba_get_block_table_tensor, ) from vllm.triton_utils import triton from vllm.v1.worker.mamba_utils import ( get_aligned_state_indices_multi_group_kernel, ) # Decode-only benchmark: one token per request, so tokens == batch size. TOKENS = [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256] NUM_GROUPS = 4 BLOCK_SIZE = 32 MAX_BLOCKS = 1024 BLOCK_ROWS = 32 DEVICE = "cuda" def main() -> None: max_tokens = max(TOKENS) seq_lens = torch.randint( 1, BLOCK_SIZE * MAX_BLOCKS + 1, (max_tokens,), dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE, ) block_tables = [ torch.randint( 0, 1_000_000, (max_tokens, MAX_BLOCKS), dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE, ) for _ in range(NUM_GROUPS) ] block_table_ptrs = torch.tensor( [table.data_ptr() for table in block_tables], dtype=torch.int64, device=DEVICE, ) output = torch.empty((NUM_GROUPS, max_tokens, 1), dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE) spec = SimpleNamespace(block_size=BLOCK_SIZE, num_speculative_blocks=0) print("tokens old (us) new (us) saved (us) speedup") for tokens in TOKENS: current_seq_lens = seq_lens[:tokens] def old( tokens: int = tokens, current_seq_lens: torch.Tensor = current_seq_lens, ) -> None: for table in block_tables: _mamba_get_block_table_tensor( table[:tokens], current_seq_lens, spec, "align" ) def new( tokens: int = tokens, current_seq_lens: torch.Tensor = current_seq_lens, ) -> None: get_aligned_state_indices_multi_group_kernel[ (triton.cdiv(tokens, BLOCK_ROWS),) ]( block_table_ptrs, current_seq_lens, output, block_tables[0].stride(0), current_seq_lens.stride(0), output.stride(0), output.stride(1), output.stride(2), tokens, CACHE_BLOCK_SIZE=BLOCK_SIZE, NUM_GROUPS=NUM_GROUPS, BLOCK_GROUPS=triton.next_power_of_2(NUM_GROUPS), NUM_STATE_SLOTS=1, BLOCK_STATE_SLOTS=1, BLOCK_ROWS=BLOCK_ROWS, num_warps=1, ) expected = torch.stack( [ _mamba_get_block_table_tensor( table[:tokens], current_seq_lens, spec, "align" ) for table in block_tables ] ) new() torch.testing.assert_close(output[:, :tokens], expected) old_us = triton.testing.do_bench(old, warmup=100, rep=500) * 1000 new_us = triton.testing.do_bench(new, warmup=100, rep=500) * 1000 print( f"{tokens:>6} {old_us:>8.2f} {new_us:>8.2f} " f"{old_us - new_us:>10.2f} {old_us / new_us:>7.2f}x" ) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` And we get ```bash tokens old (us) new (us) saved (us) speedup 1 49.76 7.12 42.65 6.99x 2 48.91 7.14 41.77 6.85x 4 48.40 7.14 41.26 6.78x 8 50.25 7.12 43.12 7.05x 16 48.42 7.12 41.30 6.80x 32 47.47 7.12 40.35 6.67x 64 50.72 7.12 43.60 7.12x 128 49.79 7.13 42.66 6.98x 256 53.86 7.13 46.72 7.55x ```

engine initialization fails during weight loading with a `ValueError`: ValueError: Following weights were not initialized from checkpoint: {'model.layers.16.enorm.weight', 'model.layers.16.hnorm.weight', 'model.layers.16.mtp_block.post_mlp_layernorm.weight', 'model.layers.16.mtp_block.input_layernorm.weight', 'model.layers.16.mtp_block.post_attention_layernorm.weight', (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/mtp/speculator.py`) attempts to initialize and load the draft model. However, the weight mapping logic fails to correctly bind the `model.layers.16.mtp_block.*` tensor keys to the MTP module parameters. 3. **Result:** During `track_weights_loading`, vLLM detects these MTP keys as uninitialized weights and throws a `ValueError`, halting `EngineCore` startup. Since `zai-org/GLM-OCR`'s checkpoint format adheres to standard GLM MTP structure, this is a weight loader / key mapping issue in vLLM's MTP speculator module rather than a model checkpoint defect. ### Repro Steps 1. signal.title: [Bugfix] compressed-tensors: restore int8 grouped WNA16 MoE support
signal.text: ## Purpose Restores the fix from #47154, which was lost in #44570. #47154 dropped the `group_size == -1` assert from the int8 branch of `CompressedTensorsWNA16MarlinMoEMethod` so that checkpoints with group-quantized int8 experts could load. #44570 then merged that class into `CompressedTensorsWNA16MoEMethod`, deleting the fixed file and keeping the other class's version of the branch, which still carried the assert. Net effect: any compressed-tensors checkpoint whose MoE experts are not all quantized to the same width fails to load again, on 0.27.0 onwards. | tag | `assert self.group_size == -1` | |---|---| | v0.25.1 | absent | | v0.26.0 | absent | | v0.27.0 | present | | v0.27.1 | present | | main | present | ## Test Plan Repro is `poolside/Laguna-XS-2.1-INT4`, the checkpoint #47154 was written for. Its experts are mixed: int4 g128 on layers 1-30, int8 g128 on layers 31-39 (we are testing with A4500 GPUs). vllm serve poolside/Laguna-XS-2.1-INT4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 131072 Layers 1-30 build, layer 31 hits `assert 128 == -1`. No download needed to see it — the constructor alone is enough: ```python from compressed_tensors.quantization import ( QuantizationArgs, QuantizationStrategy, QuantizationType) from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.compressed_tensors.compressed_tensors_moe.compressed_tensors_moe_wna16 import ( # noqa: E501 CompressedTensorsWNA16MoEMethod) CompressedTensorsWNA16MoEMethod( QuantizationArgs(num_bits=8, type=QuantizationType.INT, strategy=QuantizationStrategy.GROUP, symmetric=True, dynamic=False, group_size=128), None, moe_config, # any FusedMoEConfig ) ``` Test Result Before, on 0.27.0 (2x RTX A4500, TP=2). This is the whole output — the assert has no message and no worker traceback surfaces, even at VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG: ``` INFO [gpu_model_runner.py:5308] Starting to load model poolside/Laguna-XS-2.1-INT4... INFO [compressed_tensors_moe.py:132] Using CompressedTensorsWNA16MoEMethod INFO [int_wna16.py:297] Using 'MARLIN' WNA16 MoE backend. ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:912] AssertionError ERROR [core.py:1349] Exception: WorkerProc initialization failed due to an exception in a background process. ``` The MARLIN/WNA16 lines are info_once from layer 1 and are misleading: the assert runs during layer construction, before backend selection and before any weights are read. No flag works around it — --moe-backend, --enable-expert-parallel, --enforce-eager and the VLLM_*_MOE_* / VLLM_MARLIN_* env vars are all evaluated later. After, with the line removed: the assert no longer fires and construction proceeds to backend selection.

signal.title: Fix MRV2 Gumbel sampling for non-finite logits
signal.text: ## Summary Fix MRV2 Gumbel sampling when the candidate logits contain `-inf` entries. The current Gumbel path only clamps the uniform draw away from zero. If the draw reaches the upper endpoint after floating-point rounding, the Gumbel noise becomes `inf`. Adding that noise to a masked/non-candidate `-inf` logit produces `NaN`, and a subsequent Triton reduction can return an invalid token index. This change: - clamps fp32/fp64 uniform draws away from both `0` and `1`; - only adds Gumbel noise to finite logits; - adds a CUDA/Triton regression test that deterministically reproduces the `-inf + inf -> NaN` edge case. ## Why this matters We hit this downstream in a Kimi K2.6 MRV2 speculative decoding deployment with DCP8 and Eagle/MTP. The failure surfaced during spec-decode/logprobs warmup as an invalid sampled token id and then a CUDA illegal memory access: ```text Invalid sampled token ids for spec logprobs: count=1 vocab=163840 idx=[508] vals=[9223372034707292159] ``` The DCP8/Kimi setup makes the bug easy to trigger, but the root cause is not DCP-specific. It is the generic Gumbel sampler being asked to sample from residual logits where rejected tokens are represented as `-inf`. A minimal deterministic reproduction of the arithmetic issue is: ```python logits = -inf u = 1.0 gumbel_noise = -log(-log(u)) # inf logits + gumbel_noise # NaN ``` After this patch, the same case stays `-inf` and does not poison the reduction. ## Tests ```text python3 - <<'PY' import importlib.util path = "tests/v1/sample/test_gumbel.py" spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("test_gumbel_direct", path) mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec) spec.loader.exec_module(mod) mod.test_gumbel_noise_does_not_turn_negative_inf_logits_into_nan(False) mod.test_gumbel_noise_does_not_turn_negative_inf_logits_into_nan(True) print("direct test passed") PY python3 -m py_compile vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/gumbel.py tests/v1/sample/test_gumbel.py git diff --check ``` I could not run the repository pytest entrypoint in this local container because `tests/conftest.py` imports `tblib`, which is not installed in the environment: ```text ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tblib' ```

signal.title: [ROCm][CI] Extended Fused MoE and FP8 MoE test support
signal.text: This PR makes the fused MoE layer test matrix usable on ROCm/MI355 by fixing the real ModelOpt FP8/FP4 failures it exposes and by making distributed subcase failures visible to pytest. Key changes: - Propagate fused MoE distributed subcase failures back to the parent pytest process instead of allowing child-rank failures to print as failed subcases while the parent test reports `PASSED`. - Allow `modelopt_fp4` MoE test configs on gfx950 alongside the existing SM100 path, where native or emulated NVFP4 execution is available. - Use the existing NVFP4 reference quantization path to create packed FP4 test weights on ROCm, since `ops.scaled_fp4_quant` is not available there. - Keep NVFP4 emulation lookup tensors on the same device as the packed FP4 input during dequantization. - Preserve reduced ModelOpt FP8 tensor-wise MoE activation scales as backend-neutral 0-D tensors, reshaping them only at the Triton launch boundary so FlashInfer retains its scalar ABI while Triton receives a loadable pointer. - Gate the experimental MoRI fused MoE layer matrix behind `VLLM_TEST_ENABLE_MORI_MOE_LAYER=1`; when enabled, the test sets the AITER fused MoE env requirements and disables AITER shared expert fusion. - Enable the modular OAI Triton MoE test on CUDA-like platforms and pad MXFP4 test weights/inputs to the CDNA4 scale-layout alignment on ROCm while slicing outputs back to the original test shape. AI assistance: OpenAI Codex was used to analyze the CI and review feedback and to prepare the changes.

signal.title: [Rust Frontend] Wait for all utility calls to finish
signal.text: ## Purpose Make multi-engine utility fanout wait for every engine outcome before returning an error. - Replace fail-fast send and response joins with collection that waits for all engines while preserving result order. - Let callers compensate partially applied mutations only after every engine call has finished. - Unregister utility response waiters when request preparation fails, a send fails, or the calling future is cancelled. - Keep the existing utility request and response wire formats unchanged. This changes only the Rust frontend engine-core client. It does not change the Python utility protocol or successful single-engine behavior. ## Test Plan - `UV_PYTHON=/usr/bin/python3.12 cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-engine-core-client` - `cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check` - `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` ## Test Result - Engine-core client: 98 passed. - Rust formatting and whitespace checks passed. - The multi-engine regression test holds one engine response pending after another engine fails and verifies that the call waits for the remaining outcome. - The cancellation regression test verifies that pending utility waiters are unregistered. - Model evaluation is not applicable because this change does not affect inference output or accuracy. **AI assistance disclosure:** This PR was authored with AI assistance and reviewed by the submitter. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR is described. - [x] The test plan is included. - [x] The test results are included. - [x] No documentation update is required for this focused engine-core client lifecycle change. </details>

signal.title: [Feature]: Tracking Whisper feature requests
signal.text: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch This issue is for keeping track of the recurrent Whisper asks as well as the linked on-going efforts to support that feature, if any. When a feature request has no linked PR, feel free to claim the work here if you want to help! - [ ] Support different `response_formats` https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/audio/createTranscription - Related issues: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/19556, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/14818, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/24302 - PR(s): https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/24209 (`verbose_json`, **help needed with other formats**) - [ ] Support timestamp granularities: - Context: Very much related to the above. Unfortunately outputting by `word` requires aligning encoder latents (usually extrapolated from the crossattn layers) with decoder ones. I feel a lot of these whsper-specific techniques bring in added complexity to vLLM. However, I think we're open to exploring in this direction if we can come up with a less invasive solutions. Some references to get started https://github.com/m-bain/whisperX https://github.com/openai/whisper/discussions/684 . - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/24209 *partially* addresses this issue by letting whisper predict the segments through timestamp tokens. - [x] Automatic language detection: - Context: one should be able to let the decoder predict part of its "preamble" prompt, **including the language and task token, conditioned on the encoder output**. This is effectively utilizing whisper "built-in automatic language detection" feature. Mind that it would be ideal to _guide_ the output tokens among valid languages.
