signal.title: [Bugfix][MLA] Do not use Dense MHA for GLM-5.2
signal.text: ## Purpose Fix incorrect short-prefill dispatch in the NVIDIA DeepSeek-V3.2 attention wrapper. The generic sparse-MLA metadata path may select dense MHA when a prefill's sequence length is at most `index_topk`. It then allows the sparse indexer to skip top-k scoring. `DeepseekV32Attention`, however, only invokes `forward_mqa`; it does not execute the dense-MHA backend. For a pure prefill above the backend's decode-like threshold, MQA therefore consumed the cleared all-`-1` top-k buffer and GLM-5.2 output degenerated into repeated tokens. This change adds a model-layer dense-prefill capability in addition to the backend capability. The NVIDIA DeepSeek-V3.2 wrapper declares that it is MQA-only, so sparse MLA keeps its prefill on top-k MQA and the indexer does not advertise the dense-MHA scoring skip. This does not duplicate the open related work: - #51395 disables dense prefill only for the SM120 sparse-MLA backend. - #52046 adds a dense branch for the PCP path; the reproduced failure is the non-PCP SM100 path. - #49790 routes DSA architectures to the NVIDIA implementation but does not resolve this dispatch mismatch. Issue #46715 reports a different GLM-5.1 failure at a 65,536-token scheduler budget and multi-thousand-token prompts on the registered model path. ## Test Plan ```text .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py -q pre-commit run --files \ vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py \ vllm/models/deepseek_v32/attention.py \ tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py ``` Real-model validation uses `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`, TP=4, the explicit NVIDIA DeepSeek-V3.2 class override, FP8 E4M3 KV cache, eager execution, FP32 indexer logits, GVR disabled, and FlashInfer autotuning disabled. It serially probes the 128/129-token routing boundary without setting `sparse_mla_force_mqa=true`. ## Test Result - Focused pytest: `7 passed`. - Pre-commit on all three changed files: all hooks passed. - `compileall` and `git diff --check`: passed. - Before this change, the real model passed through 127 actual prompt tokens and failed at 129 and every tested larger prompt through 1,001 tokens. Adding only `sparse_mla_force_mqa=true` made all 19 boundary cases pass, causally confirming the routing mismatch. - Patched real-model result: all 19/19 cases passed exact retrieval without the force-MQA workaround, spanning 97, 101, 122, 127, 129, 130, 131, 132, 162, 191, 192, 193, 194, 196, 202, 257, 301, 502, and 1,001 actual prompt tokens. AI assistance was used to diagnose, implement, test, and draft this change. The human submitter must review every changed line and understand and defend the change end-to-end before marking the PR ready for review. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR is described. - [x] The test plan includes exact commands. - [x] Unit and real-model results are reported. - [x] Related open work was checked for duplication. </details>

signal.title: Validate scale-out multimodal data before engine handoff
signal.text: # Validate scale-out multimodal data before engine handoff ## What this fixes The scale-out API separates a trusted render request from a later generate request. The generate route accepted the returned multimodal `features` object from the client and rebuilt internal tensors, layout choices, placeholder ranges, and cache keys without checking that they still matched the active model or the rendered data. For example, a client can render a 32×32 Qwen image, change only its grid from `[1,4,4]` to `[1,132,132]`, and replay it to `/inference/v1/generate`. Before this change, the engine trusted the larger grid while the pixel tensor still held 4 rows. The request returned 500, the GPU reported an illegal memory access, and `/health` returned 503. After this change, vLLM compares the grid with the actual tensor before the vision encoder and rejects the mismatch as request data. ## Why it matters On a deployment using scale-out multimodal serving, an authenticated client could stop the shared engine with one altered render body. Other altered fields could make a request reuse another request's cached encoder data or lose the model's sparse placeholder selection, producing wrong cross-request results. ## The change | Commit | Site | What now happens | |---|---|---| | `d05404f` | PTP-VLLM-025 — Qwen grid geometry | Grid dimensions must be positive, merge-compatible, and consistent with the pixel-tensor rows before encoding. | | `b969204` | PTP-VLLM-026 — field layout tag | Decoded fields are rebound to the active model's declared layout; a caller-selected conflicting layout is rejected. | | `803fa4d` | PTP-VLLM-027 — placeholder ranges | Offsets and lengths must be positive, non-overlapping, inside the prompt, and parallel to the feature lists. | | `ab24a35` | PTP-VLLM-112 — sparse placeholder mask | Render and generate serialization preserve the per-token `is_embed` mask and verify its length. | | `8501006` | PTP-VLLM-121 — multimodal cache key | Cache keys are derived from the serialized tensor payload, not a caller-supplied hash; cache-only reads are rejected. | ## How it was tested | Site | Without the fix | With the fix | |---|---:|---:| | PTP-VLLM-025 | 22 failed, 4 passed | 26 passed | | PTP-VLLM-026 | 6 failed, 5 passed | 11 passed | | PTP-VLLM-027 | 3 failed, 5 passed | 8 passed | | PTP-VLLM-112 | 2 failed | 2 passed | | PTP-VLLM-121 | collection failed | 4 passed | The tests mutate one field at a time and retain valid controls. The earlier live Qwen replay also changed from HTTP 500 with an unhealthy engine to an early request rejection with the engine remaining healthy. ## Reference Advisory: GHSA-ph72-cqr5-qpp7 Track B: this is a public PR against `vllm-project/vllm@main`. ## Credit - @KernelClint (Clinton Thomas) and @dhalf (Lucas Bourtoule) - Patch the Planet (Trail of Bits + OpenAI collaboration); discovered using GPT-5.5-Cyber All commits include DCO `Signed-off-by` trailers.
signal.author: KernelClint

signal.title: [Bugfix][Parser] Recover DeepSeek V4 tool calls with malformed DSML wrappers
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #51914. DeepSeek V4 can intermittently emit an otherwise complete DSML `<｜DSML｜invoke ...>` block while the outer `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>` opener is missing or malformed. One observed `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` variant changes `tool_calls` to `toolcalls`. The current `DeepSeekV4Parser` only enters the tool-call state machine from `CONTENT` or `REASONING` when the exact outer opener is recognized, so the invoke is otherwise returned as text and the structured tool call is lost. ## Relationship to #49117 This PR is a current-`main`, DeepSeek V4-only refinement derived from the orphan-invoke recovery direction developed in #49117. It is not an unrelated competing implementation. - #49117 covers both DeepSeek V4 and V3.2, foreign-wrapper handling, and additional cross-dialect behavior. - This PR extracts only the V4 behavior needed for #51914 onto the current ParserEngine implementation. - It validates names against tools declared by the current request. - It holds the complete provisional invoke, not only the name, and commits only on the configured `</｜DSML｜invoke>` transition. - It restores incomplete or rejected candidates to their original content or reasoning state unchanged. - The normal correctly wrapped path, including its existing compatibility behavior, remains unchanged. This narrower scope keeps the current-main patch to the parser engine and DeepSeek V4 parser tests. ## Fix - Add opt-in provisional-start and provisional-commit markers to parser transitions. - Let DeepSeek V4 treat a bare `<｜DSML｜invoke name="...">` seen from `CONTENT` or `REASONING` as a provisional recovery candidate. - Buffer its semantic events and raw text instead of emitting a tool call immediately. - Validate the completed function name against tools declared by the current request. - Commit only after the DeepSeek V4 `INVOKE_END` transition. - After committing a recovered invoke, return to `CONTENT` so ordinary suffix text is preserved and any following bare invoke must pass provisional validation again. - Still absorb an optional outer `TOOL_END` after a recovered invoke. - Drop unconfigured special tokens before provisional recovery buffering, so EOS and other parser-level drop tokens cannot leak into rolled-back content. - Preserve provisional recovery while the reasoning adapter is running with `skip_tool_parsing=True`; only a completed, validated invoke ends reasoning and is handed off to the tool parser. - Synchronize the current request's tools and `tool_choice` into the reasoning-side parser engine before recovery validation, so undeclared tools and `tool_choice="none"` still roll back correctly. - If `TOOL_END` arrives without `INVOKE_END`, the request has no tools, uses `tool_choice="none"`, names an undeclared tool, or generation ends early, restore the full candidate to its original content or reasoning state. - Keep the normal wrapped DSML state-machine path unchanged. The patch deliberately does not normalize specific misspelled wrapper spellings. Recovery anchors on the inner invoke structure, so the same conservative path covers missing and malformed outer openers without expanding a typo allowlist. ## Regression coverage Recovery coverage is integrated into the existing `tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py` suite: - missing outer start wrapper - corrupted `tool_calls` to `toolcalls` opener from #51914 - undeclared tool name - requests with no tools - parser reuse followed by a request with no tools - `tool_choice="none"` - truncated candidate before the tool name completes - declared tool name with no closing `</｜DSML｜invoke>` - truncated provisional invoke followed by an EOS drop token - `</｜DSML｜tool_calls>` without a preceding invoke close - streaming with the invoke marker split across chunks - streaming rollback when only the outer tool-call closer arrives - ordinary trailing content after a recovered invoke with no outer closer - multiple bare invokes with every declared tool name validated - an undeclared second invoke remains content instead of bypassing validation through the parallel-call path - a complete declared bare invoke before a missing `</think>` commits and is handed off to the tool parser - undeclared, truncated, and `tool_choice="none"` bare invokes before a missing `</think>` remain reasoning instead of becoming user-visible content ## Validation Parser tests and changed-file checks were run on commit `94ceafb1e7` before the follow-up review fixes: ```text VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py 75 passed VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/parser/engine 3802 passed pre-commit run ruff-check --files <changed Python files> Passed pre-commit run ruff-format --files <changed Python files> Passed pre-commit run typos --files <changed Python files> Passed pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files <changed Python files> Passed ``` Follow-up commit `35af231a99` addresses the suffix-preservation and parallel-name-validation review findings and adds focused regression cases to the existing DeepSeek V4 test suite. Commit `c848ab5aa4` addresses the subsequent `DROP_TERMINAL` rollback finding and adds an EOS-leak regression case. Commit `4f2aae22cd` addresses the reasoning-adapter rollback finding and adds serving-style `DelegatingParser` coverage for a valid committed invoke plus undeclared, truncated, and `tool_choice="none"` rollback cases. The follow-up commits have not yet received upstream code-check results. On the upstream PR, the `pre-commit` workflow stops at the repository contributor gate before code checks run: it requires a `verified`, `ready`, or `ready-run-all-tests` label, or at least four merged PRs by the author. The actual `pre-commit` job is therefore skipped until that gate is opened. Real-environment validation was also completed on the affected DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 plus DSpark serving stack for the original reported failure family. The original production prompt and tool payload remain private; validation used a sanitized equivalent and confirmed structured tool-call recovery in the affected serving path. ## Scope and tradeoff A fully formed DSML invoke using a real declared tool name is intentionally recoverable even if the outer wrapper is absent. Prose that reproduces an entire valid invoke for a declared tool is fundamentally ambiguous. Requiring a current-request tool match and a complete invoke bounds the recovery without broad regex repair. Unknown malformed wrapper text emitted before the inner invoke is not guessed or retracted. The parser recovers the structured invoke while preserving text it cannot safely classify. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used to analyze the parser state machine, prepare the implementation, review the provisional-commit conditions, and write regression tests. The affected serving behavior was validated in the reporter's real environment, and the original parser tree was checked with the commands and results above.

signal.title: [Bugfix][Core] Drop stale block hashes when a session truncates tokens
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #49377 (text-only path). `_update_request_as_session` discards tokens past `num_computed_tokens`, but `update_block_hashes` only appends, so the boundary block keeps a hash of the replaced tokens and is committed under that stale identity, causing incorrect KV cache hits. This deletes the hash suffix covering discarded tokens; blocks fully inside the kept prefix stay valid. Not a duplicate of #51694, which fixes multimodal hashing in `kv_cache_utils.py` and does not touch the scheduler. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py ``` ## Test Result 100 passed on `9368f548d4`. Reverting the one-line fix fails exactly the new test, so it does not pass vacuously. No accuracy eval: this is a deterministic cache-identity bug, covered by the regression test. --- AI assistance was used for this change; I have reviewed every line.

signal.title: [Core][Bugfix] Fix async scheduling stale output and dual-scheduling race in resumable streaming sessions
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #52693. Fixes an `EngineDeadError` in `AsyncScheduler` when multi-turn resumable streaming sessions run with async batch queuing (`batch_queue_size > 1`). ### Root Cause 1. **Stale In-Flight Output Delivery in `AsyncScheduler`**: When a streaming session finishes a turn and transitions to the next turn (`_update_request_as_session`), in-flight batches from the prior turn may still be running in the GPU pipeline. When returned, they are not marked as stale, causing `_update_request_with_output` to decrement `request.num_output_placeholders` below zero (`assert request.num_output_placeholders >= 0` -> `AssertionError`) and corrupting the new turn with stale tokens. 2. **Dual-Scheduling on Waiting Queue**: If a session is in `self.running` and simultaneously present in the waiting queue during pipelined continuation, it can be scheduled by both the running loop and waiting loop in the same `schedule()` step. ### Solution 1. In `_update_request_as_session`, mark existing in-flight tokens from the previous turn as stale and drop them: ```python session.drop_stale_output = True session.num_stale_output_tokens = session.num_in_flight_tokens session.num_output_placeholders = 0 ``` 2. In `schedule()`, safely drop duplicate entries from the waiting queue if the request has already been claimed by the running loop in the current step. 3. Added regression unit test `test_streaming_async_stale_in_flight_tokens` in `tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py`. ## Test Plan 1. **Unit tests**: ```bash .venv/bin/pytest tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py -v ``` 2. **Code style & format checks**: ```bash .venv/bin/ruff check vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py .venv/bin/ruff format --check vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py ``` 3. **E2E CUDA async pipelined streaming verification** on RTX 4090. ## Test Result 1. **Unit Test Output**: ```text tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py::TestStreamingScheduler::test_add_request PASSED [ 11%] tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py::TestStreamingScheduler::test_process_streaming_requests_with_finish_session PASSED [ 22%] tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py::TestStreamingScheduler::test_streaming_async_stale_in_flight_tokens PASSED [ 33%] tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py::TestStreamingScheduler::test_streaming_e2e_lifecycle PASSED [ 44%] tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py::TestStreamingScheduler::test_streaming_request_session_update PASSED [ 55%] tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py::TestStreamingScheduler::test_update_request_as_session PASSED [ 66%] tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py::TestStreamingScheduler::test_update_request_as_session_max_token PASSED [ 77%] tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py::TestStreamingScheduler::test_update_request_as_session_with_multimodal PASSED [ 88%] tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py::TestStreamingScheduler::test_update_request_as_session_with_output_tokens PASSED [100%] ======================== 9 passed in 2.37s ======================== ``` 2. **Linter & Format Output**: ```text All checks passed! 2 files already formatted ``` 3. **E2E Results**: Verified that multi-turn streaming inputs with 1-step stops and continuous async generation complete smoothly without `AssertionError` or `EngineDeadError`. --- *AI Assistance Disclosure: AI assistance was used for drafting tests and formatting the PR description. All code logic and test executions have been human-reviewed and verified.*

signal.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Drop the redundant eagle trailing-chunk pop on load
signal.text: ## Summary `_lookup()` decrements every eagle group's backend result by one chunk: ```python if is_eagle_unverified: num_hit_chunks -= 1 ``` but `storable_chunks()` **already** excludes the volatile trailing chunk on the **store** side while decoding, and its docstring records why the other case is safe: > For eagle/MTP groups the volatile trailing chunk of the offloadable range is excluded while decoding … During prefill the trailing chunk is stable (the draft input for a chunk's last position is the next prompt token), so it is stored immediately. If nothing volatile is ever offloaded, the load-side pop is a **second, redundant exclusion** that discards a chunk which is safe by construction. ## Measured impact Instrumented build on a hybrid GDN+GQA MoE with `method='mtp'`, `tokens_per_chunk` 2128, DP=4 × TP=4, 8 workers, ~3 % mirrored production traffic: | observation | count | |---|---| | `RAW_HIT 1` → popped to `0` | **1064 / 1064** | | backend-answered lookups discarded | **1064 / 1169 (91 %)** | | survivors, all with `RAW_HIT ≥ 2` | 105 | The symptom at the metric level is `kv_offload_total_bytes_total{transfer_type="GPU_to_CPU"}` climbing while `CPU_to_GPU` stays near zero — the host tier writes and almost never reads back. ## Why `RAW_HIT == 1` is the common case, not an edge case The `num_hit_chunks == 0` guard sits **before** the pop, so a raw hit of exactly 1 clears the guard and is then decremented to zero, ending at `new_num_hit_tokens < tokens_per_chunk → return 0`. And once the GPU tier already covers most of the prefix, the lookup queries a single key. A real trace: ``` ENTER req_tokens 113826 ncomp 110656 maxhit_after_align 112784 mamba_align 2128 lookup_groups 4 grp 3 eagle 1 swa None align None start 52 nchunks 53 keys 1 tpc 2128 RAW_HIT 1 grp 3 POST hit_chunks 0 maxhit 110656 new_hit_tok 0 RET0-rounding grp 3 new_hit_tok 0 tpc 2128 ``` `start_chunk_idx = 110656/2128 = 52`, `len(offload_keys) ≈ 53`, so exactly one key is queried and `RAW_HIT` is bounded at 1 by construction. The backend **has** the chunk; the pop throws it away and the request re-prefills. ## The widening is removed with it ```python # For eagle groups, query one extra chunk that will be popped. # We only need to increase the query size for sliding window groups. if is_eagle_unverified and sliding_window_size_in_chunks is not None: query_max = min(max_hit_size_tokens + tokens_per_chunk, len(offload_keys) * tokens_per_chunk) ``` It existed solely to feed the pop. I previously tried making it unconditional (#52674, now closed) and it changed nothing, which the arithmetic explains: it is clamped by `len(offload_keys) * tokens_per_chunk`, which already equals `max_hit_size_tokens` whenever the tail of the request is what is being looked up. On the trace above, widened and unwidened both yield `keys = 1`. ## Scope / caveats - All four KV groups are flagged eagle here via the `use_eagle and not eagle_groups` fallback, so the pop applies universally rather than to a draft-specific group. Narrowing that fallback may be worth doing separately, but it is not what produces this loss. - I have **not** re-run the instrumented capture with this patch applied — filing as draft for that reason and for maintainer review of the safety argument. The claim rests on `storable_chunks()` being the sole gate on what reaches the backend; if there is a path that offloads a volatile trailing chunk without going through it, the pop is load-bearing and this is wrong. - A single-KV-group model does not reproduce the loss (verified: dense model with a real eagle3 head, 75 % acceptance, reads back normally), because `keys == 1` with a large `tokens_per_chunk` is what makes the pop fatal.

signal.title: [Rust Frontend] Add multimodal processor output cache
signal.text: ## Purpose The Rust frontend currently preprocesses every image, audio clip, and video on every request, even when the same media content was processed previously. Repeated multimodal requests therefore rebuild identical model inputs and prompt replacements. Add a process-local weighted LRU cache for multimodal processor outputs. Cache keys include the modality, media hash, model dtype,and image detail variant. Cache hits retain the current request UUID while reusing the processed tensors and prompt replacement. Images and audio process only cache misses as a batch, while preserving the original request order when cached and uncached items are mixed. Video items reuse the same cache through their per-clip processing path. The cache: - accounts for the bytes held by cached tensor data; - rejects entries larger than the configured capacity; - detaches admitted tensor buffers from batch-owned storage; - avoids admitting unresolved auxiliary-frame data; - prevents requests started before a reset from repopulating the cache; - defaults to 4 GiB and can be disabled with `--mm-processor-cache-gb 0`; - is cleared together with the engine cache by `/reset_mm_cache`. ## Test Plan ``` cargo fmt --all -- --check cargo sort --workspace --check cargo deny check bans cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast cargo nextest run -p vllm-chat \ repeated_image_reuses_cached_processor_output_without_reusing_uuid \ --no-capture ``` ## Test Result - Rust formatting, dependency, lint, and workspace checks passed. The workspace test run completed with 1,561 passed and 11 skipped. - End-to-end Qwen2-VL configuration: - 896×896 RGB PNG; - Rust processor cache enabled with a 4 GiB capacity; - backend processor cache disabled; - identical image content for cold and hot requests; - different UUIDs to prevent backend encoder identity reuse. Observed results: ``` Request Latency ━━━━━━━━━ ━━━━━━━━━━━━ Warmup 0.862634 s ───────── ──────────── Cold 0.890814 s ───────── ──────────── Hot 0.244554 s ``` The hot request saved 0.646260 seconds, reducing end-to-end latency by approximately 72.5%, or a 3.64× speedup. A repeated comparison produced: ``` Request Latency ━━━━━━━━━ ━━━━━━━━━━━━ Cold 0.921750 s ───────── ──────────── Hot 0.175460 s ``` The repeated hot request reduced latency by approximately 81.0%. Cached and uncached requests returned identical results: - HTTP status: 200; - generated content: "The"; - prompt tokens: 1,051; - completion tokens: 1. The results confirm that repeated media avoids processor preprocessing while preserving the processed inputs, prompt expansion, token accounting, request identity, and generated output. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Perf] Scale num_warps with tile size in Triton reshape-and-cache kernels
signal.text: ## Purpose Both CUDA launch sites in `triton_reshape_and_cache_flash.py` hardcode `num_warps = 16`, i.e. 512 threads, regardless of tile size. When the tile is smaller than that, the surplus warps hold thread slots without doing work, which limits how many blocks stay resident on an SM. `_reshape_cache_per_token_head` in the same file already derives the count from the shape — `min(16, max(1, head_size_padded // 32))` — as does the CUDA version of this operation (`dim3 block(std::min(num_heads * head_size, 512))`). This PR applies the same rule at the two remaining sites. Only the launch geometry changes; the kernels write the same bytes to the same slots. Tiles of 512 elements or more still get 16 warps, so the shapes the original benchmarks covered are unaffected. ROCm and XPU take a separate branch and are untouched. ## Test Plan ``` pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py -k diffkv ``` The DiffKV kernel had no direct coverage. The new test checks against a PyTorch reference that key and value land in their own halves of the packed cache row, over three `(head_size_k, head_size_v)` pairs, three block sizes, two dtypes and both cache dtypes, and that padded tokens leave the cache untouched. ``` python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_reshape_and_cache_flash.py \ --implementation triton --mode cudagraph --num-heads 2 --head-size 64 ``` `--num-heads 8 --head-size 64` gives n = 512, where both versions launch identically. That row is the control. ## Test Result All 18 tests passed on an A100, on both the patched and the unpatched kernel (18 more skip below SM89, where the Triton fp8 path is unsupported). Latency change on an A100-SXM4-80GB, median of 5 repetitions alternating patched and unpatched, CUDA graph mode. Negative means the patch is faster. Rows are labelled by `n = num_kv_heads * head_size`, the value that sets `TILE_SIZE`. | config | 1024 tok | 4096 | 16384 | 65536 | |---|---|---|---|---| | n=512 (control) | −0.6% | +0.2% | +0.3% | −0.05% | | n=256 | −11.2% | −26.0% | −33.5% | −45.1% | | n=128 | −10.6% | −29.6% | −50.9% | −67.7% | | n=64 | −9.2% | −27.3% | −49.1% | −73.0% | | DiffKV 192/128 (MiMo-V2 shape) | −29.8% | −40.9% | −44.6% | −47.1% | | DiffKV 256/256 | −31.9% | −41.5% | −45.2% | −46.2% | Below ~1000 tokens there are fewer blocks than the GPU has SMs, so nothing overlaps and there is no effect. Above that the gain grows with the token count, because more blocks fit on each SM and more stores are in flight. I ran the kernel comparison three times across two A100 variants; the control stayed within 0.08% each time, and varying the DiffKV cache strides or slot pattern moved the result by less than 0.15 points. ## End-to-end gpt-oss on A100. Sinks need FA3/4, so FlashAttention is out on sm80 and Triton is the only backend vLLM can pick: `Using TRITON_ATTN attention backend out of potential backends: ['TRITON_ATTN']`. `n` is per rank, so TP is what puts gpt-oss in range: 512 at TP=1 (unchanged), 256 at TP=2, 128 at TP=4. Each cell is the mean of 3 runs, each one `llm.generate()` over the whole batch: 128 prompts of 2048 token ids, `max_tokens=1`, prefix caching off. The order alternates per run, and each run asserts that its label matches the `num_warps` line of the source it ran, and that the engine selected TRITON_ATTN. | config | `num_warps = 16` (today) | scaled | delta | |---|---|---|---| | gpt-oss-20b, 2xA100, TP=2, 16384-token steps | 7.2094 s | 7.1951 s | −0.198% | | gpt-oss-120b, 4xA100, TP=4, 16384-token steps | 6.7100 s | 6.6816 s | −0.424% | | gpt-oss-120b, 4xA100, TP=4, 65536-token steps | 6.5420 s | 6.5191 s | −0.349% | In all three, every scaled run was faster than every `num_warps = 16` run. Larger steps do not help. The per-call saving is superlinear in tokens (25.1 us at 16384, 171.4 us at 65536) but the step count falls by the same factor, and the 65536 row came out slightly worse. The DiffKV path has no e2e number; MiMo-V2-Flash does not fit in 4xA100. ## Counters `ncu` on both versions at three shapes, to confirm the change does what it claims and nothing else. Counters only: the container cannot lock clocks, so this ran with `--clock-control none` and the durations from it are not usable. | metric | n=512 (control) | n=128 (TP=4) | DiffKV 192/128 | |---|---|---|---| | `launch__block_size` | 512 → 512 | 512 → 128 (−75%) | 512 → 256 (−50%) | | `launch__waves_per_multiprocessor` | 37.93 → 37.93 | 37.93 → 9.48 (−75%) | 303.4 → 151.7 (−50%) | | `dram__bytes.sum` | −0.1% | −0.1% | −0.1% | | global store sectors | identical | identical | identical | `block_size` matches `min(16, TILE_SIZE // 32) * 32` at all three shapes and the control does not move. Waves per SM track it exactly: smaller blocks leave more of them resident per SM. DRAM bytes and store sectors are unchanged, consistent with the kernels writing the same bytes to the same slots. The correctness argument is the new test rather than these counters, and for the same reason I did not run accuracy evals. <details> <summary>DiffKV benchmark script</summary> ```python import random, time import torch from vllm.v1.attention.ops.triton_reshape_and_cache_flash import ( triton_reshape_and_cache_flash_diffkv, ) NUM_HEADS, DK, DV, BLOCK, NUM_BLOCKS, ITERS = 8, 192, 128, 16, 8192, 200 def run(num_tokens): torch.manual_seed(42) random.seed(42) dev, dt = "cuda", torch.bfloat16 key = torch.randn(num_tokens, NUM_HEADS, DK, dtype=dt, device=dev) value = torch.randn(num_tokens, NUM_HEADS, DV, dtype=dt, device=dev) slots = random.sample(range(BLOCK * NUM_BLOCKS), num_tokens) slot_mapping = torch.tensor(slots, dtype=torch.long, device=dev) # the backends pass a (B, H, N, C).transpose(1, 2) view kv_cache = torch.empty( NUM_BLOCKS, NUM_HEADS, BLOCK, DK + DV, dtype=dt, device=dev ).transpose(1, 2) k_scale = (key.amax() / 64.0).to(torch.float32) v_scale = (value.amax() / 64.0).to(torch.float32) graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph() with torch.cuda.graph(graph): triton_reshape_and_cache_flash_diffkv( key, value, kv_cache, slot_mapping, "auto", k_scale, v_scale ) torch.cuda.synchronize() def timed(n): torch.cuda.synchronize() start = time.perf_counter() for _ in range(n): graph.replay() torch.cuda.synchronize() return (time.perf_counter() - start) / n timed(3) # warm-up return timed(ITERS) for n in [64, 256, 1024, 4096, 16384, 65536]: print(f"{n:>7} {run(n) * 1e6:9.3f} us") ``` </details> --- **AI assistance disclosure** (per `AGENTS.md`): Developed with Claude Code. I reviewed and refined every line, and ran all tests. **Duplicate check**: I did not find any open or merged PR changing `num_warps` at either site. #46060 rewrites the capability check in both launch blocks of this file; if it lands first I will rebase. #47535 adds an opt-in CUDA DiffKV op and keeps Triton as the default, which is the path this PR speeds up.

signal.title: [ROCm][Perf] Enable fused KDA decode on gfx942 (MI325X)
signal.text: ## Purpose PR #50654 added the fused Kimi-K3 KDA decode kernel (`csrc/libtorch_stable/kimi_k3/fused_kda_decode_kernel_rocm.cu`), but gated it to gfx950 (MI355X) in two places, so it never activates on gfx942 (MI325X): - **Build gate** — `CMakeLists.txt` filtered the HIP source to `gfx950` only, so the kernel was not compiled and `VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_KDA_DECODE` (and therefore `torch.ops._C.fused_kda_decode`) was never defined on a gfx942-only build. - **Runtime gate** — `is_fused_kda_decode_supported()` in `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/ops/kda_decode.py` ended with `return on_gfx950()`. This change extends both gates to gfx942 as well, so MI325X can take the fused decode path instead of falling back to the three-launch Triton path. The kernel body is unchanged. It uses only CDNA-common primitives — wave64, DPP row/quad permutes (`quad_perm`, `row_half_mirror`, `row_mirror`), `__builtin_nontemporal_load/store`, and bf16 intrinsics — with no MFMA / FP8 / gfx950-only paths, so no source-level changes are required for gfx942. LDS use is ~2.8 KiB/block and register pressure ~130 VGPR, both well within CDNA3 limits. ## Changes - `CMakeLists.txt`: HIP arch filter `gfx950` -> `gfx942|gfx950` (and comment). - `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/ops/kda_decode.py`: gate `on_gfx950()` -> `on_gfx950() or on_gfx942()`. - `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_decode.py`: extend the module skip guard from gfx950 to gfx942 / gfx950 so the correctness suite runs on MI325X. All other backends and the CUDA path are unchanged; the shape/dtype/head-count guards in `is_fused_kda_decode_supported()` are unchanged. ## Performance The kernel-level win is large, but the end-to-end win on MI325X is currently small: the Kimi-K3 decode step is dominated by the MXFP4 MoE (int4) and the MLA attention plus the TP8 collectives, which dwarf the KDA linear-attention block. The fusion removes ~66 us of per-layer kernel time (mostly launch overhead), but that is a small fraction of today's total per-token cost. It should become more visible once #50817 (MXFP4 MoE Triton a16w4 for gfx942) lands and shrinks the dominant MoE cost — the fixed KDA saving then represents a larger share of a smaller decode step. ### End-to-end (tp8, 256-in / 256-out, max-concurrency 4) | Metric | Triton fallback | Fused KDA | Delta | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Mean TPOT (ms) | 425.95 | 422.66 | -0.77% | | P99 TPOT (ms) | 427.64 | 424.19 | -0.81% | | Output tok/s | 9.29 | 9.36 | +0.75% | | Mean TTFT (ms) | 1577.24 | 1574.03 | -0.20% (flat) | TTFT is unchanged, as expected for a decode-only kernel. ### Per-layer kernel sequence (torch profiler medians, us) Baseline runs the KDA decode as ~16 separate kernels per layer — the conv1d update, the recurrent delta-rule step, and the gated output RMSNorm decomposed into a chain of launch-overhead-bound (~4 us floor) elementwise ops. Fused collapses all of them into a single kernel: | # | Baseline kernel | us | Fused kernel | us | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | _causal_conv1d_update_kernel | 5.01 | kda_decode_fusion_kernel<true, 12, true, true, true> | 7.77 | | 2 | fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode_kernel | 6.45 | | | | 3 | __amd_rocclr_copyBuffer | 4.37 | | | | 4 | bfloat16->float32 copy | 4.41 | | | | 5 | pow (tensor, scalar) | 4.41 | | | | 6 | reduce Mean | 5.01 | | | | 7 | add | 4.45 | | | | 8 | rsqrt | 4.37 | | | | 9 | mul | 4.21 | | | | 10 | bfloat16->float32 copy | 4.17 | | | | 11 | mul | 4.21 | | | | 12 | bfloat16->float32 copy | 4.45 | | | | 13 | sigmoid | 5.05 | | | | 14 | mul | 4.33 | | | | 15 | float32->bfloat16 copy | 4.49 | | | | 16 | __amd_rocclr_copyBuffer | 4.57 | | | | | **total (16 kernels)** | **~73.96** | **total (1 kernel)** | **7.77** | ~9.5x less kernel time for the KDA decode block (~74 -> 7.8 us/layer). The `12` template arg is 12 heads/rank (96 KDA heads at TP8). Across the model's KDA layers (~69 per the kernel header) that is ~4.6 ms/token of raw kernel time removed, in the same ballpark as the ~3.3 ms/token TPOT drop measured above (the remainder overlaps with other work). ## Not a duplicate - `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "KDA decode gfx942"` - `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "fused_kda_decode MI325"` ## Test Plan Run on an MI325X (gfx942) box after building with gfx942 in the arch list: 1. Build compiles the kernel and registers the op: `python -c "import torch, vllm; print(hasattr(torch.ops._C, 'fused_kda_decode'))"` -> expect `True`. 2. Kernel correctness: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_decode.py -v` 3. Model accuracy (output-affecting change) — serve Kimi-K3 on MI325X and run gsm8k, compared against the Triton fallback path: `make gsm8k` 4. Decode latency / throughput before vs after (fused vs Triton fallback): `make bench-kda-mi325` ## Test Result - Op registered: **True** on the gfx942 build (`hasattr(torch.ops._C, "fused_kda_decode")`); the fused kernel appears in the trace (see Performance). - Latency/throughput: **-0.77% mean TPOT**, +0.75% output tok/s - gsm8k (fused vs Triton): **parity** — both 1.00 exact_match on flexible-extract and strict-match (5-shot, limit=100, stderr 0). The fused kernel matches the Triton fallback exactly. - `test_amd_kda_decode.py`: **12/12 passed** on MI325X (gfx942) — fused output matches the Triton reference across heads {12, 24, 96} x tokens {1, 7, 128}, plus the null-slot, no-output-norm, and padding edge cases. ## Checklist - [x] Compiles for gfx942 (kernel present in the .so with gfx942 codegen) - [x] `test_amd_kda_decode.py` passes on MI325X (12/12) - [x] gsm8k parity with the Triton path - [x] AI assistance used (see below) ## AI assistance This change was drafted with AI assistance (Claude). A human must review every line and run the build, tests, and eval on MI325X hardware before merge; the correctness and accuracy results above are not yet filled in.

signal.title: [BugFix] Cache Hit Rate with KIMI + RHAI Dspark
signal.text: Keep KV cache group block sizes commensurate when unifying page sizes For a hybrid target (e.g. MLA + linear attention, block size aligned to the mamba state page, 1536 tokens) plus a draft model whose layers have a different per-token KV footprint (e.g. an SWA DSpark drafter), unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size scaled the draft layers' block size by the byte ratio to make pages exactly equal. The resulting block size (e.g. 3456 tokens) is generally neither a multiple nor a divisor of the other groups' block sizes, so scheduler_block_size — the LCM of all group block sizes and the prefix-cache hit alignment — exploded (e.g. lcm(1536, 3456) = 13824 tokens). Every prefix-cache hit then rounds down to a 13824-token boundary, costing ~7K reusable tokens per request at 70K ISL (~10-15pp hit rate). Fix: when byte-exact scaling would break token commensurability and the layer's backend tolerates padded pages (indexes_kv_by_block_stride), pick the largest block size that divides the max-page groups' block-size LCM instead and pad the page to the shared page size. The scheduler block size then stays at the target's block size (1536), matching the behavior of an architecture-matched (e.g. MLA-native) drafter. Backends without padded-page support keep the byte-exact behavior; a new warning in resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes flags incommensurate group block sizes so the hit-granularity cost is visible. signal.title: [ROCm][Perf] Kimi-K3 Fused kernels for KDA prefill
signal.text: ## Purpose On ROCm, Kimi-K3's KDA prefill chunk path currently runs a pipeline of nine Triton kernels. This PR adds a fusion path for ROCm that fuses these operations based on the characteristics of their workloads: **Prologue**: The kernel that prepares the chunks leading up to the recurrent state update. It normalizes `q` and `k`, cumsum gate into `g` and `beta`, builds `Aqk` in each chunk, inverts the transition `Akk`, and produces w and u. Each 64-token chunk can be processed in parallel, so it is dispatched in `(chunk, head)` grids for parallelism. **Chunk recurrence**: This does the remaining recurrence state update. For each sequence, the state update is sequential, and dispatching workgroups on the number of sequences can lead to low CU occupancy. This path breaks a sequence down into groups of chunks where the number of groups is determined by device capability, and takes a two-pass approach to increase parallelism within sequences: - Pass 1: Each group walks a recurrence from a zero state and records how it transforms an incoming state - Perform a scan across groups from a sequence to recover each group's true initial state - Pass 2: Re-walks each group from the correct start to produce outputs The fusion chain is ~2x faster than the Triton chain, especially in the chunk recurrance stage. E2E tests shows this reduces TTFT by ~4%. | tokens / seqs | Triton chunk stage | fused chunk stage | speedup | Triton chain | fused chain | speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1024 / 1 | 117.4 µs | 60.7 µs | 1.93× | 139.2 µs | 79.1 µs | 1.76× | | 4096 / 1 | 301.1 µs | 113.7 µs | 2.65× | 330.5 µs | 143.0 µs | 2.31× | | 4096 / 2 | 232.7 µs | 110.0 µs | 2.12× | 278.0 µs | 154.7 µs | 1.80× | | 4096 / 8 | 192.5 µs | 84.5 µs | 2.28× | 256.6 µs | 145.2 µs | 1.77× | | 16384 / 1 | 1174.2 µs | 335.9 µs | 3.50× | 1232.4 µs | 393.5 µs | 3.13× | The fusion path is packed into two pytorch interfaces that serve as a replacement for the original Triton chain. An additional engine argument option `--kda-prefill-backend=fused` is added to enable this fused path, and it's set as the default when it is supported. The kernels have only been tested on gfx950 at the moment, so its build and dispatch is guarded on gfx950 for now. ## Test Plan Unit tests for the fused kernels lm_eval with gsm8k on MI355X Server command ``` VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \ VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1 \ AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 \ VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 \ vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \ --trust-remote-code \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \ --load-format auto \ --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \ --max-num-seqs 128 \ --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \ --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"]}' \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --kda-prefill-backend ["fused" | "triton"] ``` Benchmark ``` vllm bench serve --model moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --backend vllm --trust-remote-code --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --max-concurrency "$CONC" --num-prompts $((CONC * 4)) --temperature 0 --ignore-eos ``` lm_eval ``` lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --model_args "model=moonshotai/Kimi-K3,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,max_gen_toks=8192,timeout=3600" --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 20 --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn --seed 1234 ``` ## signal.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] DSpark: inherit the target's attention backend when the speculative config names none
signal.text: ## Purpose `load_dspark_model` passes `backend=speculative_config.attention_backend` when building the draft's config. That field is `None` unless the user names a backend inside `--speculative-config`, and `None` re-runs backend auto-selection rather than meaning "same as target" — so an explicitly pinned target backend is silently discarded and the draft can pick a different attention class. On DeepSeek V4 with `--attention-config.backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4`, the target builds `DeepseekV4FlashInferMLAAttention` (plain 512B KV row) while the draft falls back to `DeepseekV4FlashMLAAttention`, whose `__init__` rewrites the shared `cache_config.cache_dtype` to `fp8_ds_mla`. The SWA cache is then allocated at 584B/token but still reshaped at `head_dim`, on every rank at first forward: ``` RuntimeError: shape '[-1, 64, 512]' is invalid for input of size 4176917504 vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py, in _fused_qnorm_rope_kv_insert ``` `4176917504 = 111754 * 64 * 584`, the `fp8_ds_mla` geometry. Fall back to the target's backend when the speculative config names none; an explicit `attention_backend` still wins. ## Why this is not a duplicate - **#40611** (open) lets the draft *deliberately differ* from the target. This fixes the *fallback* when nothing is specified; the explicit override still wins. - **#51538** / **#51042** fix a different DSV4 + DSpark defect (`decode_swa_indices` width). Independent of this one and deliberately not included. Each masks the other, verified on one config (DSV4-Pro-0813, TP8 × 2 GB300, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4`, DSpark k=7): | fixes | result | | --- | --- | | neither | `shape '[-1, 64, 512]'` invalid (this bug) | | this PR | passes, then fails in #51538's path: `shape '[7, 128]'` invalid | | #51538 | `shape '[-1, 64, 512]'` invalid again (this bug) | | both | engine initializes and serves | ## Test plan `pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_topk.py` → **2 passed**. `pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dspark/utils.py` → all pass (incl. mypy, ruff). ## Model evaluation aime25, 4 epochs (n=120), temperature 1.0 / top_p 0.95, thinking on, `max_tokens=150000`, DSV4-Pro-0813 on TP8 × 2 GB300, same tree throughout. DSpark rows need #51538 applied too, since both are required to start: | configuration | exact_match | pass@4 | errors | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4`, no spec | 1.0000 | 1.0 | 0 | | `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4` + DSpark | 0.9917 | 1.0 | 0 | | `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV4` + DSpark (n=360) | 0.9778 | 1.0 | 0 | | `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV4`, no spec (n=360) | 0.9944 | 1.0 | 0 | Mean acceptance length 3.16 at full concurrency. The DSpark row's single miss is a `length` truncation on the one AIME problem that runs long in every configuration tested, with no repetition loop. No unfixed baseline: the configuration cannot start without this fix. ## AI assistance This work was produced with AI assistance. The submitter has reviewed every changed line, and the tests and evaluations above were executed on the hardware described.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Summary

Serving Kimi-K3 with TP16 across two 8× B200 nodes (EFA, no NVSwitch/MNNVL),any form of CUDA graph capture produces wrong output or crashes. enforce_eager is correct 100% of the time. Unlike #50147, this reproduces at batch=1 on the first request, with prefix caching disabled and no concurrency. I also tried TP=8 and PP=2, the issue persists

Critically, the FlashInfer fused all-reduce path is disabled on this topology, so the latent-MoE stale-residual fix in #50386 cannot apply here (details below).

Configuration

vllm serve flags:

  • -tensor-parallel-size 16 --trust-remote-code --load-format fastsafetensors
    --moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA
    --disable-custom-all-reduce --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune
    --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90

env: VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=0 VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM=0
VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM=0 NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=0 NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0
VLLM_ENABLE_K3_LATENT_MOE_TAIL_FUSION=0

Prefix caching is OFF. All tests below are single-stream, temperature=0, max_tokens=64, identical prompt.

Failure matrix

cudagraph config | result -- | -- enforce_eager: true | Correct output, every time, across many deploys (TP16 and TP8+PP2) default (FULL_AND_PIECEWISE) | Fluent but semantically random multilingual text; host SIGSEGV in cuGraphLaunch / at::cuda::CUDAGraph::replay() on the 3rd request cudagraph_mode: PIECEWISE | No crash. Deterministic collapse to a single repeated token (@ @ @ ...) from the first request VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 | AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered, surfaced at torch.cuda.set_rng_state during Dynamo tracing

Performance impact

Eager decode is ~2.6 tok/s at batch=1 (64 tokens in ~25 s), closely matching the ~2.7 tok/s eager figure in #50147 against ~85 tok/s with graphs. DSpark speculative decoding recovers this to ~10 tok/s, still far below the graph-enabled figure. Eager is therefore not a viable workaround for latency-sensitive serving, which makes graph capture on this topology effectively blocking.

Questions

  1. Is CUDA graph capture expected to be supported for Kimi-K3 on multi-node TP without NVSwitch, where the FlashInfer fused all-reduce path is inactive and collectives fall back to NCCL over EFA? But I tried TP=8 and PP=2 the issue still persist.
  2. Are there other buffers allocated outside capture in the K3 MoE/KDA paths, analogous to the one fixed in #50386, that would be reached on the non-FlashInfer path?

Reproduction

Serve:

vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \ --tensor-parallel-size 16 --nnodes 2 --node-rank $RANK \ --trust-remote-code --load-format fastsafetensors \ --moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA \ --disable-custom-all-reduce --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \ --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 # env: # VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=0 VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM=0 # VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM=0 NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=0 NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0 # VLLM_ENABLE_K3_LATENT_MOE_TAIL_FUSION=0 # Add --enforce-eager for the known-good control run.

Single request, greedy, no concurrency:

from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI(base_url="<http://localhost:8000/v1>", api_key="dummy", timeout=600.0) resp = client.chat.completions.create( model="moonshotai/Kimi-K3", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "can you write me a story about a cat"}], max_tokens=64, temperature=0, extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"thinking": False}}, ) print(resp.choices[0].message.content)

With --enforce-eager this returns a coherent story on every run. Without it, the first response is already corrupted. Send the same request 3+ times to reach the segfault under the default cudagraph mode.

signal.title: Add pushed-based ZMQ metrics logger support
signal.text:
## Purpose Fixes #43643 This PR introduces an optional ZeroMQ (ZMQ) metrics logger (`ZmqStatLogger`) allowing external monitoring systems to subscribe to real-time engine telemetry over a `zmq.PUB` socket. The eventual goal is to provide a lightweight alternative to Prometheus (by calling `/metrics`). Key Changes: 1. `ZmqStatLogger` & `ZmqMetricsStats`: - `ZmqStatLogger` drains a queue and broadcasts `msgspec`-encoded telemetry payloads over a ZMQ PUB socket in a background thread. - Publishes running request count, waiting request count, KV cache usage percentage, cache configuration info, and engine ID. This is an incomplete set of fields to showcase the design; more fields will be added in the future. 2. Observability & CLI Configuration: - Added `enable_zmq_metrics: bool = False` and `zmq_metrics_port: int = 5556` flags to `ObservabilityConfig`. 3. Engine Shutdown & Lifecycle Management: - Added `shutdown()` to `StatLoggerBase`, `StatLoggerManager`, `LLMEngine`, and `AsyncLLM` to cleanly close ZMQ sockets and join background publisher threads during server shutdown. _Note:_ The current implementation does not support DP yet; it assumes there is only one engine `engine_id=0`. ## Test Plan A [local standalone script](https://gist.github.com/azamikram/f91f5c329f3e0c698daa2c60e553ebd8) to test out the subscriber side: ```bash python3 subscribe_zmq_metrics.py --hosts host1:5556 host2:5556 ``` ## Test Result We added the subscriber support to `llm-d-router`. The following results are on three H100 nodes (TP=2) serving `Qwen/Qwen3-32B` under a bursty load. The HTTP baseline refers to the existing pull-based mechanism where the router periodically (after 50ms) polls the state from `/metrics`. The ZMQ implementation refers to the proposed push-based design. For HTTP baseline, we tried both Python and the Rust frontend for vLLM. Latency CDFs Throughput and CPU usage The key takeaways are that compared to HTTP-Python, push-based ZMQ metric support can: 1. **Reduce Tail Latency:** TTFT P99 improved by 16.20% (from 54.92s to 46.02s) and End-to-End P99 latency improved by 15.18%. 2. **Increase System Throughput:** Overall cluster token throughput rose by 18.44%. 3. **Lower Router Overhead:** Streaming binary msgpack frames over persistent sockets reduced the router CPU consumption by 64.51% and lowered P90 scheduling decision latency by 11.58%. ---
Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist - [X] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [X] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [X] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.

signal.title: [CI] Fix and extend PR/issue auto-labeling
signal.text: ## Purpose Auditing the labeling setup against the actual repo turned up rules that had stopped matching the code they were written for, plus issue-side labeling that covered only 6 of 62 labels. ### Rules that were missing real work - **`deepseek` missed the `vllm/models/` tree.** Newer models live in `vllm/models/<model>/` rather than `vllm/model_executor/models/`. The rule only knew the old location, so only the title match applied — **64 of 99 PRs** touching `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/` went unlabeled. Same gap for `deepseek_v32`. - **`speculative-decoding` missed the Model Runner V2 subtree.** `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/` has seen 94 PRs in 6 months, more than the original `vllm/v1/spec_decode/` at 81. This also folds `dflash` and `dspark` under the umbrella label, per review feedback that both are spec decoding techniques. ### Rules that could never fire Four conditions used `files=` (exact match) with regex syntax, or carried a doubled backslash that YAML passes through literally: ```yaml - files=^examples/features/speculative_decoding/ # never matches - files~=^\\.buildkite/intel_jobs/ # never matches ``` A further 13 conditions pointed at files that have since moved or been deleted — `harmony` moved to the Rust frontend, `pallas` is gone. Repointed where the code moved, removed where it is gone. ### Retired: `new-model` The rule fired on any PR touching a model file **and** `registry.py`. `registry.py` is edited for renames, aliases, refactors and removals, not just additions. Of the 25 most recent PRs carrying the label, 10 added a model. The rest included: - `[Model] Remove Ouro`, `[Model] Remove Plamo2`, `Remove PersimmonForCausalLM and FuyuForCausalLM` — PRs that **delete** models - `[model registry] some simple typos` - `[Perf] Optimize clamp to clamp_`, `[Kernel] ReplaySSM: cache SSM inputs`, `Revert "Blackwell decode optimizations"` Whether a new architecture was registered depends on what changed *inside* `registry.py`. Mergify matches file paths, not diff contents, so this rule cannot be made accurate — tightening the paths does not help. 111 open PRs currently carry the label. The label remains on issues, applied by the New Model template, where the requester states the intent explicitly. ### Rule that fired too often `nvidia` matched `requirements/cuda.txt`, so dependency bumps were tagged as NVIDIA backend work. Measured across 200 merged PRs, 17 carried the label and this was the one clear miss. ### New rules `scheduler`, `kv-cache-manager`, `glm`, `minimax`, `inkling`, `DSv4`, `dflash`, `torch.compile`, `ray`, `vllm-ir`. ### Issue labeling Extended from 6 labels to 31. Terms match **titles only** by design: issue bodies carry pasted `collect_env` output that names unrelated hardware and libraries, which tags the reporter's environment rather than the topic. ### Guard against recurrence `tools/pre_commit/check_label_rules.py` fails when a file condition matches nothing in the tree, and runs via pre-commit when `mergify.yml` changes. It caught two bugs in this change while it was being written. ### Also removed: the New Model issue template `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/600-new-model.yml` is deleted. - Usage fell from 155 issues in 2025 to 30 in 2026, only 3 since July - It applied a label named `new model`, but the label is `new-model`. GitHub silently skips a label that does not exist, so requests went untagged from the March rename onward — five months, unnoticed - 292 of the 304 ever filed are closed - Model support arrives as planned work rather than as community requests `blank_issues_enabled` is `false`, so model requests route to Feature Request. **Nothing applies `new-model` after this change.** The label is left in place so it stays on the 917 PRs and 304 issues carrying it; deleting the label itself is a separate call. ## Before merging **The five new labels must be created first** — `scheduler`, `kv-cache-manager`, `glm`, `minimax`, `inkling`. Mergify errors on a label that does not exist. Two related items a PR cannot do: - `mrv1-only`'s description currently reads "apply only to Model Runner V2 (not applicable to Model Runner V2)" — says V2 twice. - `DSv4` has a rule here mirroring the `kimi`/`k3` split, but whether to keep it as a distinct label is a maintainer call. ## Test Plan Rules were validated against the real file tree and against real issues and PRs, rather than by inspection. ```bash # every file condition in mergify.yml matches at least one tracked file python tools/pre_commit/check_label_rules.py pre-commit run check-label-rules --files .github/mergify.yml pre-commit run ruff-check --files tools/pre_commit/check_label_rules.py pre-commit run ruff-format --files tools/pre_commit/check_label_rules.py ``` ## Test Result ``` tracked files: 6430 rules: 44 file conditions matching >=1 file: 154 file conditions matching NOTHING: 0 Check auto-label rules still match real files............................Passed ruff check...............................................................Passed ruff format..............................................................Passed ``` Negative test: injecting a condition pointing at a nonexistent path makes the check exit 1 and name the offending rule. New rules were spot-checked against the tree — `glm` matches 21 files and correctly ignores `midashenglm.py`, which contains the substring "glm" but is an unrelated model. Issue rules were replayed over 600 real issues: 43% now receive at least one label, and the existing rules agreed with hand-applied labels (`kimi` 35 fires / 31 already labeled, `rocm` 34 / 33, `k3` 27 / 26). No model evaluation is included because this change touches only CI labeling configuration. It does not affect inference, model output, accuracy, or serving. ## Note on AI assistance AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to audit the existing rules, measure PR and issue volumes, and draft these changes. Every measurement quoted above is reproducible with the commands shown. I have reviewed each changed line.

signal.title: [Bugfix] Encode special tokens found in text for MistralCommonBackend in multimodal processors
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #50706 vLLM crashes at engine startup for Mistral3/Pixtral models whose tokenizer resolves to transformers' `MistralCommonBackend`. Per transformers' `AutoTokenizer` resolution, this happens whenever `mistral-common` is installed (`is_mistral_common_available()`) and the model's `model_type` (`mistral`/`ministral`/`mistral3`/etc) is mapped to `MistralCommonBackend` in `TOKENIZER_MAPPING_NAMES` — whether or not the checkpoint ships more than one tokenizer format plays no part (h/t @hmellor for the correction). Affected checkpoints include e.g. `nvidia/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B-NVFP4`, `mistralai/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B`. `MistralCommonBackend` never encodes special tokens (e.g. `"[IMG]"`) found in plain text. During dummy multimodal input profiling (run at engine startup to size the encoder budget), `PixtralProcessor` counts a mismatch between the placeholder in the templated text and the encoded ids and raises: ``` ValueError: Mismatch in `image` token count between text and `input_ids`. Got ids=[0] and text=[1]. ValueError: Failed to apply PixtralProcessor on data={'text': '[IMG]'} with kwargs={'truncation': False, 'return_tensors': 'pt'} ``` `InputProcessingContext.get_hf_processor` now swaps in a `MistralCommonBackend` subclass (`with_placeholder_token_support`) that resolves known special-token strings found in text back to their ids, scoped only to the tokenizer instance handed to HF processors — never used for general/user-prompt tokenization. Conceptually related to but independently derived from: - #50752 — fixes the same root cause on the default tokenizer-mode path (currently blocked on the contributor-gate CI check, not real test failures) - #45525 — fixes the sibling issue (#45289) for `--tokenizer-mode mistral` ## Test Plan - Unit tests: `pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_mistral.py -q` — 8 new tests against a real `mistralai/Pixtral-12B-2409` tokenizer, covering: bug repro (stock backend doesn't encode `[IMG]`), fix correctness, memoization/idempotency, plain-text passthrough (unaffected by the change), placeholder-prefix disambiguation (`[IMG]` vs `[IMG_BREAK]`/`[IMG_END]`), and `add_special_tokens` behavior. - Manual end-to-end repro against a real affected checkpoint, exercising the same code path as engine-startup profiling: ```python from vllm.config import ModelConfig from vllm.multimodal import MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY model_config = ModelConfig( "unsloth/Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506", tokenizer="unsloth/Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506", revision="3ed8d341b53ea3d0e4194689905477688a6cf733", tokenizer_revision="3ed8d341b53ea3d0e4194689905477688a6cf733", max_model_len=8192, ) processor = MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY.create_processor(model_config) mm_inputs = MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY.get_dummy_mm_inputs( model_config, mm_counts={"image": 1}, processor=processor, ) ``` - `pre-commit run --files vllm/tokenizers/mistral.py vllm/utils/mistral.py vllm/multimodal/processing/context.py tests/tokenizers_/test_mistral.py` ## Test Result - `tests/tokenizers_/test_mistral.py`: **69 passed, 2 skipped** (pre-existing, unrelated skips) - Manual end-to-end repro against `unsloth/Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506`: dummy multimodal input generation **crashes** with the exact `ValueError: Mismatch in image token count...` shown above **before** this fix (verified via `git stash`), and **succeeds** after. - `pre-commit run` on all changed files: **clean** (ruff check/format, mypy, forbidden-imports check, SPDX headers, typos, etc.)

signal.title: [Helion] Route fusion-only kernels to Helion during CUDA-graph capture
signal.text: vLLM's post-grad fusion passes emit native fused ops (RMSNorm+quant, SiLU+mul+quant, QK-norm+RoPE) that have no eager model call site, so the capture-time call-site router used for per_token_group_fp8_quant (#47799) cannot reach them. Instead, add a single post-fusion FX pass that runs after fix_functionalization and retargets schema-compatible native fused ops to CUDA-graph-aware routed Helion ops. - vllm/kernels/helion/routing.py: build native->routed op map for the four fusion-only ops, gated on matching mutation signatures. Each routed op dispatches to Helion only while a CUDA graph is capturing and falls back to the native op otherwise. - vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/helion_routing.py: HelionFusionRoutingPass retargets both direct calls and remaining auto_functionalized nodes. - pass_manager.py: run the pass last (after defunctionalization) so vLLM's copy-elimination rules are preserved; gated on VLLM_USE_HELION_KERNELS. - Skip fused_qk_norm_rope on B200 pending the known numerical mismatch. - silu_mul_fp8 is intentionally excluded: its functional Tensor->Tensor schema is incompatible with native silu_and_mul_quant(out, ...). Tested on H100: focused routing tests (native fallback + cold CUDA-graph capture for all 4 ops) plus test_fusion, test_silu_mul_quant_fusion, and test_qk_norm_rope_fusion pass with routing enabled. ## Purpose ## Test Plan ## Test Result --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Bugfix] Support MistralCommonBackend tokenizers in the xgrammar structured-output backend
signal.text: ## Purpose Structured output (`response_format` / guided decoding) fails with **HTTP 500** for Mistral models when the tokenizer is loaded under the default `tokenizer_mode="auto"`. `transformers>=5.5` returns a `MistralCommonBackend` for Mistral repos. That class subclasses `PreTrainedTokenizerBase` (not `PreTrainedTokenizerFast`) and is not vLLM's `MistralTokenizer`, so: - `is_mistral_tokenizer()` returns `False` (it requires `IS_MISTRAL_TOKENIZER` + `isinstance(..., MistralTokenizer)`), so the working Mistral path in `XgrammarBackend.__post_init__` is skipped; - the `else` branch calls `xgr.TokenizerInfo.from_huggingface()`, whose dispatch matches only `PreTrainedTokenizerFast`, tiktoken-backed, or sentencepiece-backed tokenizers, and otherwise raises `ValueError: Unsupported tokenizer type: ...`. `XgrammarBackend` is constructed lazily on the **first structured-output request** (`vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py` → `grammar_init()`), inside engine-core, so the uncaught `ValueError` surfaces as an HTTP 500. Plain completions on the same server keep working, which makes this look like a model problem rather than a backend one. ## Reproduction No GPU, no HF token, public model: ```python from transformers.tokenization_mistral_common import MistralCommonBackend from vllm.config import StructuredOutputsConfig, VllmConfig from vllm.v1.structured_output.backend_types import StructuredOutputOptions from vllm.v1.structured_output.backend_xgrammar import XgrammarBackend tok = MistralCommonBackend.from_pretrained("mistralai/Mistral-Nemo-Instruct-2407") cfg = VllmConfig(structured_outputs_config=StructuredOutputsConfig(backend="xgrammar")) backend = XgrammarBackend(cfg, tokenizer=tok, vocab_size=tok.vocab_size) backend.compile_grammar(StructuredOutputOptions.JSON, '{"type":"object"}') ``` On `vllm==0.27.0` (stock, from PyPI): ``` ValueError: Unsupported tokenizer type: <class 'transformers.tokenization_mistral_common.MistralCommonBackend'> ``` With this change: ``` grammar compiled: XgrammarGrammar ``` Diagnostics for that tokenizer: ``` MRO : MistralCommonBackend -> PreTrainedTokenizerBase -> PushToHubMixin -> object IS_MISTRAL_TOKENIZER : <absent> # -> is_mistral_tokenizer() == False isinstance(PreTrainedTokenizerFast) : False # -> xgrammar's first branch misses ``` ## Fix `MistralCommonBackend` already carries everything the Mistral path needs — `tok.tokenizer` is a `mistral_common.MistralTokenizer`, reachable as `.instruct_tokenizer.tokenizer` → `Tekkenizer` — and vLLM already has both a helper to detect it (`mistral_common_tekkenizer()`) and a wrapper that consumes it (`MistralTokenizer.__init__(tokenizer: MistralCommonBackend)`). So rather than adding new vocabulary-construction logic, this change routes a tekken-backed `MistralCommonBackend` through the existing `MistralTokenizer`, which already builds a correct `xgr.TokenizerInfo` (byte-fallback handling, `is_tekken` → `VocabType.RAW`, eos as stop token). The Mistral branch body is unchanged apart from reading the local `tokenizer` variable. ## Test `tests/v1/structured_output/test_backend_xgrammar_mistral_common.py` builds the backend from a `MistralCommonBackend` and compiles a JSON grammar. Verified both directions against stock `vllm==0.27.0`: - without the change: `1 failed` (`ValueError: Unsupported tokenizer type`) - with the change: `1 passed` ## Notes - The new branch is deliberately narrow: it triggers only when `mistral_common_tekkenizer()` returns a `Tekkenizer`, i.e. exactly the case reproduced above. Behaviour for every other tokenizer is unchanged, including the `backend="auto"` fallback path. - I did not extend this to sentencepiece-backed `MistralCommonBackend` instances because I have not reproduced a failure there. If maintainers know that path is also affected, widening the condition to any `MistralCommonBackend` would be a small follow-up — happy to do it in this PR if preferred.

signal.title: [Feature][DSpark]: Logprobs adaptive verification
signal.text: Solves #51873 ## Purpose Lifts the restriction blocking logprobs with enable_adaptive_verification, implementing the TODO from #47808. Adaptive verification assigns per-request draft counts on device; the CPU-side `cu_num_logits_np` only holds an evenly-distributed stand-in. Using it as `cu_num_generated_tokens` would misassign logprob rows across requests. Instead, the rejection sampler now attaches the device `cu_num_logits`. signal.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Warn when Eagle3 aux layers fall back to a default
signal.text: Eagle3 draft heads consume auxiliary hidden states captured from several target model layers. When the draft config does not name those layers, both model runners fall back to a per-architecture heuristic (`2, num_layers // 2, num_layers - 3`). If the head was trained on other layers the drafts are computed from representations it never saw, acceptance collapses, and the run ends up slower than plain decoding — while the server stays healthy and output stays correct, so nothing surfaces it. Serving `nvidia/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-Eagle3` on Llama-3.3-70B hits this. The head's config omits `eagle_aux_hidden_state_layer_ids`, so the heuristic picks `(2, 40, 77)` and the measured result is: | | this head | correctly configured head | |---|---|---| | acceptance rate | 1.21% (341 / 28281 draft tokens) | 58.9% | | mean accepted length | 1.036 | 2.77 | | per-position acceptance | 0.036 / 0.0006 / 0.000 | 0.751 / 0.567 / 0.453 | | throughput vs spec disabled | 0.70-0.79x | ~0.89x | Position 2 was never accepted once across the whole run. The only signal is the `vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total` / `..._num_draft_tokens_total` metrics; the logs say nothing about the layers having been guessed. This patch warns once when the fallback is taken and names the setting that pins the layers. The legacy runner did not log the fallback at all. No behavior change. On the specific checkpoint above, the warning is as far as vLLM can go on its own. The head ships `fc.weight` with shape `[8192, 24576]` (= 3 x 8192), so it consumes three distinct hidden states, but its config declares `num_eagle_features: 1` / `eagle_config.use_aux_hidden_state: false` and it carries TensorRT-LLM's `eagle3_layers_to_capture: [-1]`, a key vLLM does not read anywhere. Checking the three 8192-wide column blocks of `fc.weight`, all three are fully populated with near-identical magnitudes (mean |w| 1.5957e-02 / 1.5958e-02 / 1.5958e-02) and are not element-wise equal, so this is not the final hidden state replicated three times. Which three target layers the head was trained against is not recoverable from the checkpoint and is not documented, so the correct value for `eagle_aux_hidden_state_layer_ids` would have to come from the checkpoint's publisher. Making vLLM read `eagle3_layers_to_capture` would not help until that mapping is known. ## Test `pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_eagle3_aux_layer_fallback.py` — CPU only, no model download. ## Environment Measured on 2x RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell (32 GB each, sm_120), TP=2, vLLM 0.25.1 container, Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct AWQ-INT4 target, `num_speculative_tokens=3`, `max_model_len` 12288, temperature 0, 24-prompt workload. The code paths touched here are unchanged on `main`. ## Not addressed here On the V2 runner, `eagle_config.use_aux_hidden_state: false` is still ignored (`gpu/model_runner.py` sets `use_aux_hidden_state_outputs = True` unconditionally for eagle3/dflash/dspark), which makes a head that declares it fail with a `8192` vs `24576` shape mismatch. That is a separate defect with an actual behavior change — previously reported in #40551 and attempted in #40656. Happy to file it separately rather than widen this PR. --- AI assistance was used. I reviewed every changed line, ran the test, and reproduced the acceptance numbers above on the hardware listed.

signal.text: ## Purpose - Resolves #51871: adaptive verification needs decode batches with per-request query lengths - Wire FlashInfer trtllm-gen decode to `cum_seq_lens_q`/`max_q_len`; `q_len_per_req` must be `None` for varlen - Flip `supports_device_cpu_query_lens_mismatch` on SM100: device `qo_indptr` is the source of truth, CPU lengths only an upper bound - Guard: adaptive verification without the trtllm-gen kernel now fails fast at init - Not a duplicate: no open PR touches trtllm-gen varlen decode ## Test Plan - `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer_trtllm_attention.py -k varlen` (B200) - Uniform decode regression subset on the same file - E2E: Gemma4-12B NVFP4 + DSpark (q=8) through the varlen path, GSM8K 50q - Kernel perf: varlen vs uniform-padded, profiler device time (B200) ## Test Result - 4 varlen + 16 uniform regression passed, 0 failed - E2E serves correctly: GSM8K 98%, 0% invalid, 17.6 q/s | shape | rows ragged/padded | varlen | padded | |---|---|---|---| | batch=8, q~U[1,8] | 38/64 | 28.0us | 22.2us | | batch=32, q~U[1,8] | 118/256 | 70.5us | 65.4us | | batch=32, q~U[1,4] | 74/128 | 61.4us | 54.2us | - Varlen carries a small fixed kernel overhead; it enables ragged batches rather than speeding uniform ones - Adaptive E2E is blocked on a public Gemma4 drafter with a confidence head; kernel tests cover the device-CPU mismatch semantics ---

signal.title: [Bugfix][Attention]: Normalize FlashInfer prefill LSE before merging
signal.text: ## Purpose Prefix-cache hits could produce different logits from a cold prefill and eventually lead to repetitive output. This was initially observed with GLM-5.2 in a disaggregated prefill/decode deployment. KV cache digests matched before and after transfer, and the issue also reproduced with BF16 KV cache. A local prefix-cache cold/warm comparison then reproduced the logits divergence without KV transfer, narrowing the issue to the cached-context attention path. A cold prefill computes attention in one operation. On a prefix-cache hit, vLLM computes attention over the cached context and new suffix separately, then combines the two partial states with `merge_attn_states`. FlashInfer prefill kernels, including the TRT-LLM ragged kernel, return base-2 log-sum-exp values. vLLM's CUDA and Triton `merge_attn_states` implementations use natural `exp` and `log`. Passing base-2 LSE values directly therefore produces incorrect context/suffix weights. This PR: - adds a shared `log2_lse_to_ln` conversion helper; - converts LSE returned by the FlashInfer MLA prefill backend; - converts LSE returned by the TRT-LLM ragged MLA prefill backend; - converts generic FlashInfer DCP prefill LSE after the base-2 cross-rank reduction and before the natural-log attention-state merge. The conversion is performed at the external kernel boundary so the rest of vLLM continues to use the natural-log LSE contract. ### Duplicate-work check No open PR currently fixes the MLA prefill paths changed here. PR #36503 previously experimented with scaling generic FlashInfer prefill LSE in an older commit (`f10579e`), but that change is not present in its current diff. Its current scope is persistent buffer management for FlashInfer DCP decode. This PR fixes the missing conversions on current main and additionally covers both FlashInfer MLA prefill and TRT-LLM ragged MLA prefill. PR #47779 concerns SM120 sparse MLA decode DCP and does not modify these prefill merge paths. ## Test Plan ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -rs \ tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py \ -k 'test_chunked_context_backend_correctness and \ (FLASHINFER or TRTLLM_RAGGED)' .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \ vllm/v1/attention/backends/utils.py \ vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py \ vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/prefill/flashinfer.py \ vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/prefill/trtllm_ragged.py git diff --check ``` Before/after error measurements used the same B300 GPU, test selection, and random sequence. The old behavior was simulated by replacing the conversion helper with an identity function at runtime. ## Test Result Affected auto/FP8 matrix: - 6 passed - 2 skipped because FlashInfer does not support the tested GLM dimensions Maximum absolute output error against the SDPA reference: | Prefill path | Before | After | | --- | ---: | ---: | | FlashInfer / DeepSeek | 0.236328 | 0.0078125 | | TRT-LLM ragged / DeepSeek | 0.228516 | 0.0078125 | | TRT-LLM ragged / GLM | 0.265625 | 0.0078125 | The results were identical across CUTLASS_MLA, FLASHINFER_MLA, and TRITON_MLA, which is consistent with the error originating in the shared context/suffix merge. Pre-commit and `git diff --check` passed. The complete `test_chunked_context_backend_correctness` matrix produced 10 passed, 8 skipped, and 2 failures. Both failures are in the unchanged FlashAttention FA4 path because the local extension does not accept the `fp8_kv_dequant` keyword. They occur before LSE merging. ### AI assistance AI assistance was used. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR is described. - [x] The test plan and commands are included. - [x] Local test results and the environment-specific failures are included. - [ ] Model evaluation results must be added before submission. </details>

This does not duplicate the separate SM107 kernel-build and NVLink workstreams tracked by #49735. ## Validation - `pre-commit run --files docker/Dockerfile docker/versions.json .buildkite/cuda134-prerelease-pipeline.yaml .buildkite/test_areas/docker.yaml requirements/cuda134-nightly.txt` — passed - Buildkite YAML parsing with Ruby's standard YAML parser — passed - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tools/test_docker_build_metadata_args.py -v` — 7 passed - live public-source check on 2026-08-18: NVIDIA's CUDA 13.4 base/devel Docker Hub tags return 404; PyPI's latest `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` release is 4.7.0 An earlier ARM64 image from this PR passed vLLM import, CUDA 13.4 `nvcc`/`ptxas`, compiler, driver-link, `torch.compile`, FlashInfer sampling JIT, server-startup, and GSM8K smoke checks. signal.title: [Feature][DSpark]: Enable varlen for Kimi K3 (KDA)
signal.text: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch Adaptive verification has a firm requirement that the attention backend must not use the CPU-side query lengths as a source-of-truth, instead using the gpu tensors (so that we can run the confidence-based assignment on the GPU without synchronizing the CPU). Additionally, kernels must be able to support decode batches where requests have different query lengths per request. Currently, Kimi K3 kernels should (in theory) be compatible with this feature. We should wire it up, validate correctness, evaluate performance, and merge support. DEPENDS ON https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47808 ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
