signal.title: [Perf] Cache streaming parser drop metadata
signal.text: ## Summary - cache immutable special-token drop metadata used by streaming parser engines - key the bounded cache by the config and tokenizer content the builder actually reads - verify equivalent per-request parser configs hit the cache ## Why `StreamingParserEngine` is created per request, while its config and tokenizer contents are effectively engine-wide. Each construction currently recompiles escaped special-token regexes and rebuilds the same immutable `LexerShape`. In the originating B200 profile at a batch around 975, parser construction accounted for 1.9% of engine-thread samples, primarily in this builder. The cache is content-keyed rather than object-identity-keyed, so equivalent config instances share an entry and tokenizer special-token changes naturally miss. It is capped at 64 entries. ## Duplicate check I searched open vLLM PRs for `build drop info reasoning parser cache` and `_build_drop_info`. I found no open PR changing or caching this path; the broad search results were unrelated model, parser-regression, and kernel work. ## Measured performance A pinned-hardware Nebius B200 A/B (`qwen35_per_request_patch_ab_2026-08-06.md`) used an Intel Xeon Platinum 8580 host, structured mode, 1,000 concurrency, and 180-second unprofiled runs: - Output throughput was **11,857 → 11,890 tok/s (+0.28%)**, inside the independently measured **0.32% noise floor**; both arms had zero errors. - In separate py-spy captures, `_build_drop_info` fell **1.5% → 0 samples** of the EngineCore main thread. Its `_get_reasoner` parent fell **1.9% → 0.4%**. - `scheduler.schedule` fell **33.5% → 32.0%**, while `gpu_wait` rose **9.7% → 12.1%**, consistent with the removed CPU work becoming main-thread slack on an already GPU-saturated workload. The benchmark used the SafetyKit memo implementation rather than this bounded `lru_cache`, but it memoized the same pure `_build_drop_info` result. The unambiguous result is removal of the targeted parser-construction work; the +0.28% throughput delta is noise, not a claimed serving-throughput win. ## Validation - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine/test_engine.py -q` — 38 passed - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine -q` — 3,738 passed - targeted Ruff check and format hooks — passed - commit-time pre-commit suite — passed The planned Nebius validation adds a serving-level reasoning/tool-call corpus comparison and an A/B/A high-concurrency profile to confirm output identity and reduced parser initialization samples. ## AI assistance This change was prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance. The human submitter must review every changed line, understand and defend the implementation, and run the listed Nebius validation before marking the PR ready.
signal.author: Gamrix

signal.title: fix: handle quantized qkv_proj in DFlash fused-KV buffers
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes #51581 — DFlash-family speculative decoding crashes at engine init when the drafter is quantized. The DFlash fused-KV path sliced the raw `.weight` of the KV projections and fed it to a single fused GEMM, bypassing the quant method. This reworks the fused context-KV precompute into a tiered strategy: - `FUSED` — unquantized drafters: fuse qkv weights as before (fastest path, unchanged). - `SCALED_MM` — simple per-tensor FP8 with cutlass fp8 support: keep weights quantized, fuse per-output-row scales, run `cutlass_scaled_mm`. - `FUSED_DEQUANT` — simple per-tensor FP8 without cutlass fp8: dequant once into a fused bf16 weight at build time. - `PER_LAYER` — anything else (marlin / block-quant / mixed): project per layer and concat, always correct. The fused buffers are now built lazily at the first precompute (after `process_weights_after_loading`), so quantized layers are fully materialized; compute dtype follows the model config. The same strategy applies to `laguna_dflash` (stacked bmm) and `gemma4_dspark` (K-only) via a FUSED/PER_LAYER split. ## Validation - Standalone validator: **27/27 PASS** — strategy selection (incl. SCALED_MM / FUSED_DEQUANT gates), fused == per-layer bit-exact on CPU (qwen3 / laguna / gemma4), quantized projection never sliced, real FP8 precompute vs per-layer truth on GPU, fp16 path. - Real engine on Qwen2.5-7B + 4-layer synthetic draft (A100): dflash real **534.9 tok/s**, syn-accept-len **1167.5 tok/s (1.80x vs baseline 649.4)** — no regression after rework. - Bug→fix A/B: old eager build crashes (`AttributeError: workspace` on marlin path); lazy build runs clean (eager + cudagraph). - Note: A100 has no cutlass FP8 (`cutlass_fp8_supported()==False`), so `SCALED_MM` is gated there and falls to `PER_LAYER`; `SCALED_MM` is covered by CPU strategy tests.

signal.title: [RFC]: Extended online quantization roadmap
signal.text: ### Motivation. Continuation of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/32029. Online quantization API is now relatively stable at https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/online and documented at https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/features/quantization/online/. This RFC summarizes and motivates proposed features that would be helpful to make online quantization to be more flexible and more widely compatible with models, including pre-quantized ones. ### Proposed Change. ### 1. Support activation quant key override Implemented in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51808. This is necessary to dispatch on specific linear/moe backends that can be picked only through the `activation_quant_key` (see e.g. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c4e969294ecab9ffefb995b734303f13f62b723f/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/mxfp4.py#L441-L445) ### 2. Targeted online quantization configuration based on user patterns Implemented in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51285, RFC in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/50281. The goal is simply to extend the UI to support e.g. `--quantization-config.targets '{"re:.*o_proj.*":"mxfp8"}'`, e.g. to target a single layer similar to e.g. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/dc9f845ddc54c1df38fdbce5afe03f9fd15813bd/vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py#L935-L948 (that is currently hard-coded and may be causing accuracy issues if done silently https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48051), or e.g. `--quantization-config.targets '{"re:.*shared_expert.*":"fp8_per_block"}'` to enable fused shared expert. ### 3. Support online quantization with partially pre-quantized checkpoints Implemented in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51392. This is necessary to combine online quantization with already partially quantized checkpoints, which is notoriously the case recently. This is e.g. useful to test the accuracy/speed tradeoff of quantizing certain additional layers, or useful to e.g. release a single model compatible with fused shared expert / unfused shared expert. This has e.g. been requested in separate PRs: - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48983 - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49313 ### 4. Requantize already-quantized layers to different precision Not implemented yet, closest prototype is https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48427. This is similar to https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28291 & https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29328 on sglang side. This idea here would be to allow loading through a certain quantization method, dequantize and override the quantization method on request. This has e.g. been requested in: - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48427 - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51274 ### Feedback Period. One month ### CC List. @BowenBao @mgoin @kylesayrs @vkuzo @maeehart @tanpinsiang @fanxingran @access2rohit ### Any Other Things. _No response_ ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
signal.author: fxmarty-amd

signal.title: [Bugfix][V1] triton_unified_attention: apply tile_mask in USE_TD KV load
signal.text: ## Problem On Intel XPU (and CUDA with `VLLM_TRITON_ATTN_USE_TD=1`), long-context requests cause all concurrent requests to output endless `!` characters. Short-context requests are unaffected. ## Root Cause The `USE_TD` KV load path in `triton_unified_attention.py` does not apply `tile_mask` to K and V, unlike the standard non-TD path. In the final KV tile, the sequence tail contains uninitialized KV-cache memory. Without masking, these uninitialized values (NaN) reach `tl.dot(P, V)` as `0.0 * NaN = NaN`, poisoning the attention output and returning token 0 (`!`) for every subsequent position. ## Fix Apply `tile_mask` to K and V in the `USE_TD` branch, mirroring the safety logic already present in the non-TD path. ## Verification Verified without GPU via occurrence count diff and NaN propagation simulation. **Test 1 — tile_mask occurrence count (before vs after):** ```bash python - << 'EOF' import subprocess, sys FILE = "vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_unified_attention.py" r = subprocess.run(["git","show",f"main:{FILE}"], capture_output=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") b_count = r.stdout.count("tile_mask") if r.returncode==0 else 0 a_count = open(FILE, encoding="utf-8").read().count("tile_mask") print(f"BEFORE (main): tile_mask occurrences = {b_count}") print(f"AFTER (patch-2): tile_mask occurrences = {a_count}") ok = a_count > b_count print(f"RESULT: {'Fix confirmed — tile_mask added in USE_TD branch' if ok else 'Unexpected'}") EOF ``` Output: ``` BEFORE (main): tile_mask occurrences = 4 AFTER (patch-2): tile_mask occurrences = 8 RESULT: Fix confirmed — tile_mask added in USE_TD branch ``` **Test 2 — NaN propagation simulation:** ```bash python - << 'EOF' import math, sys nan = float('nan') before = 0.0 * nan print(f"BEFORE (no tile_mask): 0.0 * NaN = {before}, is_nan={math.isnan(before)}") print(f" -> [FAIL] NaN poisons tl.dot(P,V) -> logit NaN -> token '!'") after = 0.0 * 0.0 print(f"AFTER (tile_mask): 0.0 * 0.0 = {after}, is_nan={math.isnan(after)}") print(f" -> [PASS] No NaN, correct token output") ok = math.isnan(before) and not math.isnan(after) print(f"RESULT: {'Fix verified end-to-end' if ok else 'Unexpected'}") EOF ``` Output: ``` BEFORE (no tile_mask): 0.0 * NaN = nan, is_nan=True -> [FAIL] NaN poisons tl.dot(P,V) -> logit NaN -> token '!' AFTER (tile_mask): 0.0 * 0.0 = 0.0, is_nan=False -> [PASS] No NaN, correct token output RESULT: Fix verified end-to-end ``` Hardware verification on XPU needed. To reproduce, set `VLLM_TRITON_ATTN_USE_TD=1` and send a long-context request. Screenshots attached in comments. Fixes #43428
signal.author: lcheng321

signal.title: Remove VLLM_TEST_FORCE_FP8_MARLIN to replace with linear_backend/moe_backend
signal.text: ## Purpose Remove the test-only `VLLM_TEST_FORCE_FP8_MARLIN` environment variable and use the public `linear_backend` / `moe_backend` configuration to force Marlin. Marlin remains available as the FP8 fallback when earlier compatible kernels cannot be selected. This also fixes the CI failures exposed by that fallback path: - use realistic 128 x 128 block-FP8 test shapes instead of synthetic 1 x 1 blocks; - give `TestFP8Layer` the partition metadata and device placement expected by real FP8 layers; - skip forced-kernel fusion assertions when the requested kernel is unsupported and selection correctly falls back to a different kernel. The root cause was not that Marlin was selected incorrectly. On the failing L4 cases, the explicitly requested FlashInfer, DeepGEMM, or CUTLASS kernel was unsupported, so selection continued to Marlin. The fixtures then either lacked the metadata Marlin needs or asserted fusion behavior belonging to the unavailable requested kernel. This is not a duplicate contribution: it updates the existing PR that introduced/exposed these CI failures; no separate PR implements this fix. ## Test Plan - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_fp8.py -v -k test_fp8_reloading` - targeted RMSNorm/FP8 fusion test with Triton available - targeted MLA/group-FP8 fusion test with CUTLASS available - repeat both targeted fusion tests with the requested kernels disabled to exercise Marlin fallback - repository commit hooks for the four changed test files ## Test Result - FP8 reload: 3 passed, 1 expected skip - supported Triton fusion path: passed - supported CUTLASS MLA fusion path: passed - simulated Marlin fallback paths: 2 expected skips after successful fixture construction - Ruff, formatting, mypy, SPDX, configuration validation, sign-off, and the remaining applicable commit hooks: passed Model evaluations were not run because this changes backend selection configuration and test fixtures, not model computations or output accuracy. AI assistance was used for CI-log analysis and preparation of the test changes. The human submitter is responsible for reviewing every changed line and validating the final contribution.
signal.author: mgoin

signal.title: [MOE] Standardize and abstract fused shared expert optimization selection
signal.text: ## Disclosure AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually. ## Purpose Standardize fused shared-expert (FSE) detection so model construction and checkpoint loading use the same quantization-compatible decision **throughout all models implementing FSE**. This is e.g. useful for: - `shared_expert` fusion through arbitrary quantization methods/config (e.g. later on with online quantization in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51285 / https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51392), so that FSE compatibility can be detected more largely based on arbitrary quantization config across all model archs, and not simply based on logic specific to e.g. [qwen3/quark](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/fac808b36f502d0d992509a187dca94c68b0360a/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_next.py#L81-L98 ) - Be less bug-prone where FSE resolution is done differently in many different places - Make FSE API less dependent on ROCm/AITER, so that it will be useful e.g. as well for https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/50963 that is NOT rocm/aiter specific. The shared resolver validates FSE against the quantization configuration, rejects an incompatible requested FSE configuration, and ensures all MoE layers in a model agree on the resolved state. The mixed-state error reports the counts of enabled and disabled layers. Behavior change compared with `main`: - Models with mixed resolved FSE states now raise `NotImplementedError`. FSE is only supported/tested for all (or none) layers currently, within a PP rank. Left to do: - [x] Left to an other PR: Should `not get_current_vllm_config().parallel_config.enable_expert_parallel` be promoted globally (from `vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/model.py`) - [x] Left to an other PR: Should `on_gfx950()` from minimax_m3 be promoted (// backend specific?)? - [x] update `deepseek_v4/amd/model.py` - [x] Left to an other PR: `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS` for non-AITER backends to turn on FSE in MiniMax-M3 on AMD https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0e2d78028c473bb04fc74bf945eb32da29239b0c/vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/model.py#L112-L127 ==> does not require `VLLM_USE_AITER=1`, does not use `rocm_aiter_ops.is_fusion_moe_shared_experts_enabled()` ## Test Plan - `pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py -v` ## Test Result `29 passed, 14 warnings in 18.86s` on MI350. `29 passed, 14 warnings in 21.49s` on H100.
signal.author: fxmarty-amd

signal.title: [Kernel][MoE] DeepEP v2: async finalize to overlap shared experts with combine (env-gated)
signal.text: FIX #52744 ### What `prepare_finalize/deepep_v2.py` issues the ElasticBuffer combine synchronously at both call sites, so the modular-kernel shared-expert overlap window (`finalize_async` -> shared experts on the compute stream -> receiver join, `MK_INTERNAL_OVERLAPPED`) is never used: for MoE models with a shared expert (DeepSeek-R1/V3) the shared-expert FFN serializes behind the cross-node all-to-all on every MoE layer during decode. This PR makes `finalize_async` issue the combine with `async_with_compute_stream=True` (+ `allocate_on_comm_stream`) and return a receiver closure that joins via a device-side `event.current_stream_wait()` — graph-replay safe (the closure keeps `combined_x` and the event alive; no host synchronization inside the captured region). ### Safety - **Env-gated, default off**: `VLLM_DEEPEP_V2_COMBINE_OVERLAP=1`. The flag is read once in `__init__` (never touches `os.environ` inside the captured region). Default path is byte-identical to the current synchronous combine. - **DBO**: overlap is disabled under DBO (`dbo_enabled()`), synchronous fallback, log-once. - **No-event capability gate**: if a DeepEP build returns no combine event, the overlap self-disables permanently (warn-once + a single eager full-sync join) — a pre-capture decision, since warmup always precedes capture; if it is ever hit during capture anyway, a hard `RuntimeError` is raised instead of hiding a sync inside the graph. ### Tests - `tests/kernels/moe/test_deepep_v2_overlap_gate.py` (new, hermetic, no GPU collectives): contract tests for the gate — eager no-event self-disable / capture no-event raise / event-path deferred device-side join. (Ported from a validated harness; the same three contracts pass against this module logic.) - `tests/kernels/moe/test_deepep_v2_moe.py`: `test_deep_ep_v2_moe_cudagraph` parametrized over the flag, so the existing torch-reference comparison doubles as the correctness oracle with overlap ON inside captured graphs. ### Performance (deployment observation) DeepSeek-R1-671B FP8, EP8 (2 nodes x TP4xDP2, GB300 / multi-node NVLink), full cudagraphs, `--all2all-backend deepep_v2`; pre-registered A/B, 4 independent server starts (ABBA), greedy, forced 128 output tokens, steady-state: | metric | OFF | ON | delta | |---|---|---|---| | C=1 decode ITL p50 | 15.71 ms | 14.32 ms | **-8.8%** | | C=24 decode ITL p50 | 22.05 ms | 20.89 ms | **-5.3%** | | C=1 TTFT p50 (negative control) | 236.9 ms | 236.8 ms | -0.1 ms | Greedy outputs bit-identical across all four arms. Serving traces: each combine kernel overlapped by shared-expert GEMMs ~9.7 us on average with the flag ON vs exactly 0 OFF. An ablation with the event-wait placed *before* the shared-expert GEMMs (offload without overlap) shows ~0 gain — the benefit is true overlap. Full evidence in #52744. ### Validation scope GPU validation was performed on a v0.26.0-era tree; the finalize/combine region is unchanged between v0.26.0 and current main (the dispatch-side drift is unrelated), so the port is mechanical. The contract tests pass against this module logic; the parametrized cudagraph test covers the captured path wherever DeepEP v2 CI runners exist. Happy to adjust the shape (config-gated instead of env, or default-on) per maintainer preference.
signal.author: 404mario

signal.title: [Bugfix][Compile] Preserve independent input strides in piecewise create_concrete_args
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes #50046. On torch 2.13, `Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8` (and other Qwen3-Next GDN models) crash during CUDA-graph warmup with: ``` assert_size_stride(arg17_1, (3, 512), (512, 1), 'input') AssertionError: expected size 3==3, stride 4097==512 at dim=0 ``` `--enforce-eager` avoids it. The crash is provably not triton (3.6.0 still fails), not Inductor comprehensive-padding (`TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPREHENSIVE_PADDING=0` doesn't help), and not fixed by reverting the candidate torch PRs discussed on the issue — because the defect is in vLLM. ## Root cause `arg17_1` is the **M-RoPE positions tensor**. It is allocated as a persistent `(3, max_num_tokens + 1)` buffer (`gpu_model_runner.py`, the intentional `+1` from #12128) and fed to the compiled model as the slice `mrope_positions[:, :n]`, so its row-pitch stride is `max_num_tokens + 1 = 4097` — independent of the token count. The `3` is the T/H/W rope sections. For single-size piecewise compilation, `create_concrete_args` in `vllm/compilation/piecewise_backend.py` concretized **every** symbol in an input's strides/storage-offset to the compile `size`. That collapses the independent `4097` pitch to `size` (e.g. `512`), fabricating a contiguous `(512, 1)` example input. Inductor faithfully bakes a stride guard for `(512, 1)`, which the real `(4097, 1)` runtime slice then trips at warmup. This is latent before torch 2.13. torch 2.13 represents that pitch as a *symbolic* stride (2.11 kept it concrete), so the mis-concretization only bites on 2.13 — which is why reverting individual torch PRs does not recover it. It only surfaces with block-scale FP8 GDN models, where the FP8 DeepGEMM splitting ops make the RoPE gather a piecewise-partition input. ## Fix Specialize only the **size** symbols (those appearing in the tensor's `shape`) to `size`; keep other stride/offset symbols at their real value from the shape env. The compiled graph then asserts the true `(4097, 1)` input stride. This corrects what the graph *expects* rather than mutating the runtime tensor, so it stays **CUDA-graph safe**. (Forcing `.contiguous()` on the positions instead is not a valid fix: it clears the assert but breaks CUDA-graph replay — a fresh non-persistent tensor breaks the captured-address contract, giving an out-of-bounds RoPE gather.) ## Testing - Repro: `Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8`, TP=8, 8×H100, torch 2.13, block-scale FP8 + DeepGEMM env (`VLLM_BLOCKSCALE_FP8_GEMM_FLASHINFER=1`, `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1`, `VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`, `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=1`), compile + piecewise/full cudagraph, `enforce_eager=False`. - **Before:** crashes at warmup with the assertion above. - **After:** warmup + CUDA-graph capture + real text generation all succeed, no crash. Verified twice. - Ruled out as non-fixes (by direct runs on the same setup): triton 3.6.0; `TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPREHENSIVE_PADDING=0`; reverting torch PRs #179919 / #184004 / #180197 / #184519. - Lint: `ruff check` and `ruff format` clean. ## Model evaluation No accuracy impact expected for previously-working models: for inputs whose strides were already concrete/correct, this changes nothing; it only replaces a fabricated contiguous stride with the true one. The repro generates coherent output post-fix. Happy to run a full `lm-eval` if a reviewer would like one. ## Not a duplicate No open PR references #50046 or touches `create_concrete_args` / piecewise stride handling (checked). --- AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate the root cause and draft this change and description; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.
signal.author: frgossen

signal.title: Bump setuptools to a CVE-2025-47273-fixed release across build/platform/test requirements
signal.text: ## Summary Several requirement files pin or permit setuptools releases below the `78.1.1` floor that fixes [CVE-2025-47273](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-47273) ([GHSA-5rjg-fvgr-3xxf](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5rjg-fvgr-3xxf)), a path traversal in setuptools' package-index/archive handling: - `pyproject.toml`'s PEP 517 `build-system.requires` and several `requirements/build/*.txt` files allow `setuptools>=77.0.3` with no lower bound at the fixed release - `requirements/build/cpu.txt` and `requirements/cpu.txt` pin the exact vulnerable `setuptools==77.0.3` - `requirements/tpu.txt` pins `setuptools==78.1.0`, one patch release short of the fix - The generated test locks `requirements/test/cpu.txt` and `requirements/test/cuda.txt` also resolve to `setuptools==77.0.3` This bumps every affected pin/lower-bound to `78.1.1`. Other parts of the repo (`docker/Dockerfile.ppc64le`, `build_vllm_ppc64le.sh`, `requirements/test/rocm.txt`, `requirements/test/xpu.txt`) already use a setuptools version at or above this floor, so this brings the rest of the requirement set in line with that existing practice. This is a MODERATE-severity supply-chain issue per the project's own [severity guide](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/SECURITY.md) (build-time, requires a malicious package index/archive to be exercised during a build step; no RCE or privileged-access path demonstrated), which is why this is a plain PR rather than a private security advisory. **Note on `requirements/build/cpu.txt` / `requirements/cpu.txt`:** the prior exact pin carried a comment that `setuptools==77.0.3` "can reuse CMake build dir". I don't have a way to independently confirm whether `78.1.1` preserves that specific behavior, so I've flagged it inline for maintainer judgment — if it doesn't, please pick another `setuptools` release `>=78.1.1` that does. ## Test plan - [x] Confirmed no remaining `setuptools==77.0.3` / `setuptools==78.1.0` / unbounded `setuptools>=77.0.3` reference anywhere in `pyproject.toml` or `requirements/` - [ ] Maintainer: confirm `setuptools==78.1.1` still supports the CMake build-dir reuse the prior pin's comment referenced - [ ] Maintainer: confirm the generated test locks (`requirements/test/cpu.txt`, `requirements/test/cuda.txt`) don't need a full `uv pip compile` regeneration instead of the direct edit here
signal.author: gigioneggiando

signal.title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Guard read_frames against empty frame indices
signal.text: ## Summary `Qwen3VLVideoBackend.compute_frames_index_to_sample()` returns an empty list for a 0-frame video (it lacks the base class's `max(1, ...)` floor), which then crashed `VideoBackend.read_frames()`: - **frame-recovery path** (`_read_frames_with_recovery`): `IndexError: list index out of range` at `next_target_map[frame_indices[-1]] = total_frames` — the same line's neighbor `max_frame_idx = frame_indices[-1] if frame_indices else 0` is guarded a few lines above, but this one is not. - **no-recovery path**: `ValueError: max() iterable argument is empty`. `read_frames` is the single entry point shared by **every** video backend (OpenCV / PyAV / TorchCodec / DeepStream), so the guard protects all of them. This adds an early return for empty frame lists that matches the empty-shaped frames (`np.empty((0, h, w, 3))`) the recovery path already produces for empty input — the same state downstream code already receives today for 0-frame videos through the base-class path. ## Test ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ "tests/multimodal/test_video.py::test_read_frames_handles_empty_frame_indices" \ "tests/multimodal/test_video.py::test_qwen3vl_zero_frame_video_does_not_crash" -v # 3 passed ``` - `ruff check` / `ruff format` on both changed files: clean. - Full `tests/multimodal/test_video.py` run: 40 passed, 5 skipped; the 25 failures are all `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'av'/'torchcodec'` (video decode deps absent in this CPU environment), unrelated to this change. **Model evaluation:** not applicable — this is a crash-only fix for degenerate (0-frame) input; it does not change output, accuracy, or serving behavior for any valid input. ## Duplicate / overlap check No open PR references an empty-frame crash in `read_frames` or the Qwen3VL `compute_frames_index_to_sample` path. - #50990 *"Validate dynamic video sampling metadata"* is related in theme but does **not** overlap: it adds validation to `DynamicVideoBackend` only, and does not touch `read_frames`, the Qwen3VL backend, or any backend's `read_frames` boundary. - `bad_words` / YAML-config / JSON-schema empty-input fixes are unrelated code paths. ## AI assistance This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code): bug identification, fix, and tests were AI-drafted and reviewed by a human before submission.
signal.author: zuver-lab

signal.title: [Bugfix] Restore model info caching for package backends
signal.text: ## Purpose This PR only restores ModelInfo caching for package backends. It does not attempt to resolve the overall startup-time gap between the Transformers backend and native vLLM. Other startup costs discussed in #50128 are outside this PR's scope. Related to #50128. After #26906 changed the Transformers backend from `transformers.py` to a package, the ModelInfo cache continued looking for the removed file. `module_hash` therefore remained `None`, skipping cache reads and writes. This PR falls back to `importlib.util.find_spec()` when the flat file is absent, allowing package backends to use the existing cache logic. ## Test Plan Run unit tests: ```bash uvx ruff check \ vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py \ tests/models/test_registry.py python -m pytest -q --confcutdir=tests/models \ tests/models/test_registry.py -k lazy_modelinfo ``` Start the server twice in separate processes with the same cache directory: ```bash VLLM_CACHE_ROOT=/tmp/vllm-modelinfo-cache \ VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG \ vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --model-impl transformers \ --enforce-eager ``` For each run, measure from process start to the first successful `/health` response. Stop the first server before starting the second. ## Test Result ```text ruff: all checks passed pytest: 3 passed ``` RTX 4080 SUPER: ```text first startup: 49.286 s second startup: 34.683 s ``` The first run created: ```text vllm-model_executor-models-transformers-TransformersForCausalLM.json ``` The second run logged: ```text Loaded model info for class vllm.model_executor.models.transformers.TransformersForCausalLM from cache ``` Registry inspection decreased from `10.755 s` to `0.003 s`. ## AI assistance OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation and testing. I reviewed and validated the changes.
signal.author: haoyangqian

signal.title: [Bugfix][Model] Guard DeepSeek V4 compressor CuTe DSL dispatch
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #52710. The DeepSeek V4 compressor imported the optional CUDA CuTe DSL implementation unconditionally for `head_dim == 512`. Builds without CuTe DSL therefore failed at dispatch. The fallback must also respect the cache layout. The Triton compressor writes the packed `fp8_ds_mla` representation (`torch.uint8`); it is not compatible with FlashInfer's plain BF16 or per-tensor FP8 cache rows. This change therefore: - uses CuTe DSL when it is available on CUDA; - permits the Triton fallback only for packed `torch.uint8` cache rows; and - raises a clear error for plain BF16/per-tensor FP8 rows without CuTe DSL. ## Duplicate-work check Before opening this PR, I searched open PR bodies for `52710` and searched open PRs using the area keywords `DeepSeek compressor CuTe DSL guard`. No open PR was addressing this issue. ## Test Plan - Execute `DeepseekCompressor.forward` with CuTe DSL unavailable for packed `uint8`, plain BF16, and plain FP8 E4M3 cache rows. - Assert the plain layouts fail before the Triton callable can launch. - Assert the packed layout dispatches to Triton. - On SM89+, execute the real packed Triton writer against a 584-byte cache row followed by a sentinel guard region and verify the guard is unchanged. - Run the Python-specific pre-commit lint and formatting hooks. ## Test Result - RTX 3050 (SM86), driver 610.88, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130: - plain BF16 forward rejection: **passed** - plain FP8 E4M3 forward rejection: **passed** - packed `uint8` forward dispatch: **passed** - real packed FP8 write with overrun sentinel: **skipped**, because native FP8 E4M3 conversion requires SM89+ - Focused pytest result: **3 passed, 1 skipped** - Kaggle probe: Tesla P100 (SM60), also below the SM89 requirement - `pre-commit run ruff-check --files ...`: **passed** - `pre-commit run ruff-format --files ...`: **passed** - `git diff origin/main...HEAD --check`: **passed** The SM89+-gated sentinel test is included for Ada/Hopper/Blackwell CI. ## Model evaluation Not run. This change does not modify model math, kernels, output values, or model loading. It restricts dispatch according to the existing cache representation and prevents an incompatible writer from receiving plain cache rows. No documentation update is needed because this fixes internal optional-kernel dispatch without changing the public interface. AI assistance disclosure: OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation and test execution. The commit includes an `Assisted-by: OpenAI Codex` trailer.
signal.author: maithilijoshi20

signal.title: Require a PyAV build with the fixed IAMF parser
signal.text: # Require a PyAV build with the fixed IAMF parser ## What this fixes vLLM's speech path opens uploaded audio with PyAV, which includes FFmpeg parsers. Older PyAV/FFmpeg builds contain an IAMF parser bug that can corrupt the process's native memory while opening a malformed audio file. For example, an attacker can upload a specially formed IAMF file to `/v1/audio/transcriptions`. Before this change, `av.open()` ran before vLLM checked whether the installed parser contained the upstream fix. The malformed file could crash the API process and, because memory was overwritten inside native code, had the potential for more serious process compromise. After this change, vLLM refuses to call `av.open()` on a vulnerable stack and gives an actionable upgrade error instead. ## Why it matters A client able to submit speech-to-text audio could crash the serving process on deployments using an affected PyAV/FFmpeg combination. The request does not require a valid audio stream; the parser is reached while opening the file. The demonstrated outcome was process memory corruption and a crash. Code execution was not demonstrated. ## The change The audio dependency floor is now PyAV 17.1.0. A shared `require_safe_pyav_stack()` guard checks the runtime PyAV and FFmpeg versions before container parsing, and speech callers preserve its specific upgrade message. Requirements and test locks are updated to the same safe floor. ## How it was tested The unpatched focused suite could not be collected in the reconstructed environment; with the patch, all 23 collected tests passed. A separate dependency-floor check showed 6 failures and 4 passes against the old requirements, then passed with the new floor. Tests also verify that `av.open()` is never reached for a vulnerable stack. The positive "known-good IAMF file decodes" check remained environment-limited and failed once because the reconstructed fixture/runtime combination could not perform that decode. The security-relevant version-floor guard and the fail-before-`av.open()` behavior are verified. ## Reference Advisory: GHSA-m52c-39rh-f3gp Track B: this is a public PR against `vllm-project/vllm@main`. ## Credit - @KernelClint (Clinton Thomas) and @dhalf (Lucas Bourtoule) - Patch the Planet (Trail of Bits + OpenAI collaboration); discovered using GPT-5.5-Cyber All commits include DCO `Signed-off-by` trailers. ## Upstream FFmpeg references The overflow is in FFmpeg's `scalable_channel_layout_config()` (`libavformat/iamf_parse.c`) and was fixed upstream in Dec 2025: - Issue: https://code.ffmpeg.org/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/issues/21013 - Patches: https://code.ffmpeg.org/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/pulls/21017 · https://code.ffmpeg.org/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/pulls/21107 · https://code.ffmpeg.org/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/pulls/21115 - Fix commit `2d5abf27e5b0bf48a779368499d754f130bae4f4`: https://github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/commit/2d5abf27e5b0bf48a779368499d754f130bae4f4 It is distinct from the IAMF allocation-DoS CVE-2026-66037 (`mix_presentation_obu()`, same file, different function). This PR is a vLLM-side guard for deployments that link a still-vulnerable FFmpeg via PyAV.

signal.title: [Bugfix][V1] Defensive guard for stale req_id in `_update_after_schedule`
signal.text: ### Summary Add a defensive guard in `_update_after_schedule()` to handle stale `req_id` (request finished/aborted concurrently). Aligns with the existing `self.requests.get(req_id)` convention already used elsewhere in the same file. **This PR is not a fix for the underlying race.** It only prevents the engine from hard-failing when the race manifests. The race itself (e.g. abort/finish ordering) is a separate concern and out of scope here. ### Change `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` — `_update_after_schedule()`: ```diff num_scheduled_tokens = scheduler_output.num_scheduled_tokens for req_id, num_scheduled_token in num_scheduled_tokens.items(): - request = self.requests[req_id] + request = self.requests.get(req_id) + if request is None: + logger.debug( + "Skipping stale req_id %s in _update_after_schedule " + "(likely finished/aborted concurrently)", + req_id, + ) + continue request.num_computed_tokens += num_scheduled_token ``` ### Why a defensive guard, not a race fix - `_update_after_schedule()` is post-schedule accounting (advances `num_computed_tokens`). Skipping a stale id means that one request's accounting is dropped — it has no effect on KV cache state or scheduler invariants for surviving requests. - The same file already follows this defensive convention at lines 1235, 1296, 1606, 1633, 1715. Lines 944 (this PR), 1446, 2049, and 2054 are the remaining unchecked `self.requests[req_id]` callsites; this PR fixes the one that's actively crashing engines in the wild. - A real race fix (engine loop ordering, synchronization, etc.) is a much larger change and belongs in a separate PR — see #26400 for prior discussion of the ordering side. ### Test Local reproducer using vllm-omni's MiniCPM-o-Demo (`backend=vllm_omni`) over realtime WebSocket. Before the patch, cancelling an in-flight request crashes the engine core with the `KeyError` shown in the linked issue. After the patch, the stale id is logged at debug level and the engine continues normally on the next step. No existing test impact (the surviving path is unchanged). ### Risk Minimal. Same defensive pattern already used in the same file. No state-corruption risk — this runs after `super().schedule()` completes, before model execution; dropping post-schedule accounting for an already-finished request is correct behavior. ### Related Closes #42157 Related: #26400 (different layer), #25991 (different surface, same broader pattern).

signal.title: [Bugfix] Let an optional Literal flag accept the None it advertises
signal.text: ## Problem `_compute_kwargs` makes an optional field's flag accept `None` by wrapping its type, then advertising the sentinel: ```python if type(None) in type_hints and not contains_type(type_hints, bool): kwargs[name]["type"] = optional_type(kwargs[name]["type"]) if kwargs[name].get("choices"): kwargs[name]["choices"].append("None") ``` but `optional_type` returns the **object** `None`, not the string: ```python def _optional_type(val: str) -> T | None: if val == "" or val == "None": return None return parse_type(return_type)(val) ``` argparse applies `type` **before** it checks `choices`, so the converted value is `None` while the registered choice is `"None"`, and the flag rejects the value its own help text offers: ``` $ vllm serve ... --collect-detailed-traces None error: argument --collect-detailed-traces: invalid choice: None (choose from 'all', 'model', 'worker', 'None') ``` The message is self-contradictory: it lists `'None'` among the valid choices in the same breath as refusing it. The empty string, the other spelling `optional_type` accepts, fails identically. There is no way to pass these flags the value they document, so the only route to `None` is to omit the flag entirely. 16 flags are affected: ``` --kv-role --pooling-type --profiler --safetensors-load-strategy --seq-pooling-type --proton-backend --ssu-algorithm --tok-pooling-type --proton-hook --mm-encoder-attn-dtype --task --proton-output-format --collect-detailed-traces --method --moe-backend --kv-cache-dtype ``` ## Fix Append the sentinel that survives the conversion: ```python kwargs[name]["choices"].append(None) ``` argparse `str()`s choices when it renders help, so `--help` is byte-identical: ``` before: [--collect-detailed-traces {all,model,worker,None}] after: [--collect-detailed-traces {all,model,worker,None}] ``` ## Not a duplicate Searched `argparse_utils`, `load_config_file`, `optional_type`, `choices`, and `"invalid choice"` across open issues and PRs. The nearby open work is on a different defect in a different file: #49057 fixes `false` booleans in YAML configs and #51623 / #52077 handle empty YAML configs, all in `vllm/utils/argparse_utils.py`. This one is in `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py` and is about CLI choices, and this PR does not touch `argparse_utils.py` at all. ## Tests `test_optional_literal_accepts_none_on_the_cli` in `tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py`, built on the `DummyConfig.optional_literal` fixture that file already defines. It pins both spellings `optional_type` accepts, that a real choice still works, and that `None` is still advertised in help, which is what made the rejection contradictory. ``` before after test_optional_literal_accepts_none_on_the_cli FAIL PASS (SystemExit 2) ``` **How it was run.** `python -m pytest tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py` exits 139 on this machine, on a clean tree as well as with this change, because collection segfaults inside native `xgrammar` init. That is unrelated to this PR, so the test body was executed standalone against the real `get_kwargs` and the real `DummyConfig` lifted from the file with `ast`, once against unmodified `arg_utils.py` and once with the change. The 16-flag list above was produced the same way, by running `get_kwargs` over every dataclass in `vllm.config` and reporting fields whose choices contain the string `"None"` but not the object; it goes from 16 to 0 with this change. `ruff check` gains no new findings (the file's 2 pre-existing ones are unchanged) and `ruff format --check` reports both files already formatted. **No model evaluation results.** This changes argument parsing only: nothing about model output, accuracy or serving behaviour moves. The sole behavioural difference is that a value already listed in `--help` is now accepted instead of erroring out, so there is nothing to evaluate. AI assistance was used for this change.

signal.title: [Bugfix] Exclude DSpark draft-model KV-cache group from core prefix-cache lookup veto
signal.text: Fixes #48455 ### Purpose Split out from #47891 per review feedback there: this PR is the core-only half of that fix, the offloading connector's PR will be rebased to align with this once it merges. `HybridKVCacheCoordinator.find_longest_cache_hit()` (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py`) requires every KV-cache group of a hybrid model to independently report a nonzero hit before confirming any prefix reuse for a request, on the GPU tier. When serving DeepSeek-V4 with DSpark speculative decoding, the draft-model KV-cache group can never satisfy this, so it incorrectly vetoes reuse of the target model's own KV-cache groups (SWA, compressed C4A/C128A, indexer) even when those groups genuinely still hold valid, resident GPU blocks for a matching prefix. A follow-up request sharing a prefix with GPU blocks still resident from a previous request, or a request resumed after preemption, gets treated as having zero reusable prefix and is fully recomputed from scratch. ### What this PR changes - `SpeculativeConfig.has_ephemeral_draft_context()` (new, `vllm/config/speculative.py`): a predicate on the speculative method itself, following the same pattern as the existing `use_dflash()` and `use_dspark()`. Returns `True` for `"dspark"`. Identifies methods whose draft-model KV-cache group is rebuilt from the target model's auxiliary hidden states at generation time, rather than accumulated incrementally through the draft's own attention (EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP). - `KVCacheGroupSpec.eagle_group_is_veto_exempt` (new, `vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py`): a plain boolean field, computed once from the predicate above wherever `is_eagle_group` is already set (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`). - `HybridKVCacheCoordinator.find_longest_cache_hit()` (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py`, the primary fix): when a veto-exempt eagle group reports zero hit blocks in a round, that group is dropped from the round instead of zeroing the whole request's confirmed hit length. It still participates normally in every other round, including any round where it reports a nonzero hit. Neither `find_longest_cache_hit()` nor `find_longest_cache_hit_per_group()` contains a single method-name string comparison; the exemption is derived once from `KVCacheGroupSpec.eagle_group_is_veto_exempt` and consumed as a plain boolean. ### `eagle_group_is_veto_exempt` does not mean "excluded from the lookup" A veto-exempt group's hit length is still computed every round exactly like any other group's. The exemption only changes what happens when that computed hit length is zero: normally a zero from any group vetoes (truncates to zero) every other group's independently confirmed hit; for a group whose KV has no request-independent, stable meaning, a zero is not informative about whether the target model's own groups have a real, reusable hit, so it is left unconfirmed for that round instead of zeroing everyone else. A nonzero hit from the same group participates in the AND-convergence exactly like before, with no special casing. ### Why this has no downside for DSpark, unlike EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP's draft model runs its own causal self-attention over tokens it has itself drafted. Once a draft token's KV is computed, it stays valid for the rest of the request and is genuinely reusable across requests that share a prefix. DSpark's draft context KV works differently. `DSparkDeepseekV4Model.precompute_and_store_context_kv` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/dspark.py`) derives each draft layer's context KV directly from the target model's own auxiliary hidden states at that exact decode step, and writes it into that layer's context slots. This runs once per drafting round: the target produces real hidden states, DSpark writes fresh context KV from them, the draft model attends over that freshly written context to produce this round's speculative tokens, and the next round overwrites those same slots again from the target's next hidden states. It is a write-then-immediately-consume-within-round buffer, not an incrementally accumulated cache. There is no window in which reusing it would be meaningful, so this PR does not forfeit any reuse opportunity DSpark had. It never had one to begin with. ### Scope Two independent scope boundaries. **Speculative method: DSpark only, DFlash is a follow-up.** DFlash's drafter builds its context KV from the target model's auxiliary hidden states the same way DSpark's does, so `has_ephemeral_draft_context()` could mechanically be extended to cover `"dflash"` with a one-line change. This PR deliberately does not do that: DFlash has not been validated end to end in a live server (blocked on an unrelated attention-backend / KV-cache-dtype compatibility gap for the DeepSeek-V4 target, plus a checkpoint-architecture mismatch for the specific community DFlash checkpoint available), so claiming the fix for DFlash here would be a claim without evidence. **Model architecture: the whole DeepSeek-V4 family (Flash, Pro, and any other size variant), not size-specific.** `eagle_group_is_veto_exempt` is only ever set inside `_annotate_eagle_groups_deepseek_v4` (pre-existing code, `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`), which is itself hard-scoped to `model_version == "deepseek_v4"`. That value is set in exactly one place, `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py`, shared by the whole `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM` architecture regardless of size variant. Every other model architecture falls back to a different, pre-existing path that flags all groups as `is_eagle_group` uniformly and never touches this new field, so this PR has no effect there. Live serving validation of this mechanism, via #47891 which shares the same core fix, was on the Flash size variant. ### Testing | Suite | Result | |---|---| | `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py` | included in full run below | | `tests/v1/core/` (full directory, 2 GPUs) | 423 passed, 0 failed | Run inside an isolated throwaway container (source `.py` tree synced over an installed `vllm` build to avoid needing a full rebuild), on this branch alone, with no dependency on the offloading connector changes in #47891.

signal.title: Validate request indices and sampler sizes before engine work
signal.text: # Validate request indices and sampler sizes before engine work ## What this fixes Several request fields reached fixed-size GPU tables, native model code, or scheduler checks without first being compared with the limit that downstream code assumed. For example, a DeepSeek V4 pooling request could contain `"input":[-1034240]`. Before this change, vLLM checked only whether token IDs were too large, not whether they were negative. The negative value reached native GPU index calculation, caused an illegal memory access in both tensor-parallel workers, and left `/health` at 503. After this change, negative IDs are rejected as invalid request data before model execution; valid IDs are unchanged. The branch applies the same early-validation rule to oversized sampler lists, structured-output token references, a scale-out prompt offset, and embeddings-only XD-RoPE requests. ## Why it matters A client could stop a worker or the shared EngineCore with one bad value on an affected model or feature path. Some paths require an operator-enabled mode, such as routed-expert output or a specific pooling model, but once enabled the failing values are controlled by ordinary requests. The demonstrated impact is service loss. Code execution was not demonstrated. ## The change | Commit | Site | What now happens | |---|---|---| | `2dbdd53` | PTP-VLLM-093 — XD-RoPE prompt embeddings | Embeddings-only requests derive positions from the embedding length instead of asserting that token IDs exist. | | `3d4e473` | PTP-VLLM-095 — Python sampler controls | `allowed_token_ids`, `logit_bias`, and effective stop-token sets are checked against their fixed row sizes at admission. | | `db84429` | PTP-VLLM-103 — Rust sampler controls | The Rust frontend enforces the same sampler and bad-word limits before lowering the request. | | `8e68d75` | PTP-VLLM-111 — routed-expert prompt offset | The offset must fall inside the rendered prompt before `generate()` is called. | | `abc3e02` | PTP-VLLM-116 — pre-tokenized input | Negative token IDs are rejected in the shared input validator. | | `2d7ee7e` | PTP-VLLM-119 — xgrammar token references | Numeric and tokenizer-resolved token IDs must be inside the decoded vocabulary before native compilation. | ## How it was tested | Site | Without the fix | With the fix | |---|---:|---:| | PTP-VLLM-093 | 2 failed, 1 passed | 3 passed | | PTP-VLLM-095 | 4 failed, 4 passed | 8 passed | | PTP-VLLM-111 | 2 failed, 3 passed, 15 deselected | 5 passed, 15 deselected | | PTP-VLLM-116 | 3 failed, 2 passed | 5 passed | | PTP-VLLM-119 | 206 failed, 43 passed | 249 passed | The pod did not have Cargo for PTP-VLLM-103. Its Rust suite was run locally and all 24 tests passed. Live controls also changed the negative-token and routed-offset requests from engine failure to an early request rejection while `/health` remained 200. ## Reference Advisory: GHSA-98fv-r3w4-mrrv Track B: this is a public PR against `vllm-project/vllm@main`. ## Credit - @KernelClint (Clinton Thomas) and @dhalf (Lucas Bourtoule) - Patch the Planet (Trail of Bits + OpenAI collaboration); discovered using GPT-5.5-Cyber All commits include DCO `Signed-off-by` trailers.

signal.title: fix(security): use segment-boundary-aware root_path stripping in auth middleware
signal.text: ## Summary - **Fix authentication bypass** in `AuthenticationMiddleware` when `--root-path` is set to a value that is a non-segment string prefix of a guarded route (e.g. `--root-path /v` against `/v1/models`). - Replace `str.removeprefix(root_path)` with Starlette's `get_route_path(scope)`, which only strips `root_path` on a path-segment boundary — matching the same logic Starlette's router uses for dispatch. - Add 9 regression tests covering non-segment-prefix bypass, legitimate segment-boundary stripping, and unguarded route accessibility. ## Details `AuthenticationMiddleware` stripped `root_path` using `str.removeprefix`, a pure string operation with no path-segment awareness. Starlette's own route dispatcher (`get_route_path`) only strips `root_path` when it falls on a segment boundary (i.e. the path equals `root_path` exactly or `root_path` is followed by `/`). This mismatch meant: - **Auth middleware**: `"/v1/models".removeprefix("/v")` → `"1/models"` → does not start with `/v1` → auth skipped - **Starlette routing**: path still matches `/v1/models` → request dispatched normally Result: complete bypass of `--api-key` bearer-token authentication on all guarded route families (`/v1`, `/v2`, `/inference`, `/cohere`) whenever `--root-path` happens to be a non-segment prefix. ## Test plan - [x] All 20 existing auth middleware tests pass - [x] 6 new parametrized tests for non-segment-prefix bypass (`/v` vs `/v1`, `/in` vs `/inference`, `/co` vs `/cohere`, `/` vs `/v1`) - [x] 2 new tests for legitimate segment-boundary `root_path` values (`/api`, `/proxy`) - [x] 1 new test for unguarded route accessibility with `root_path` set - [x] All pre-commit hooks pass (ruff, mypy, typos, etc.) ``` .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/serve/middleware/test_authentication_middleware.py -v ``` Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

signal.title: Fix no-op num_blocks reduction in get_moe_wna16_block_config

signal.title: [Bug][ROCm] Kimi-K3 (KimiLinear/GDN hybrid) + ngram spec-decode: GPU memory access fault on concurrent mixed spec/non-spec batches (single-stream works after fixing a strided `state_indices` slice)
signal.text: ### Your current environment <details> <summary>collect_env output (summary; full output attached)</summary> - vLLM: `0.1.dev19253+g5f76ae224.d20260727` — the official ROCm Kimi-K3 image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:kimi-k3`, with aiter built from source at `ROCm/aiter@e8f438a748d27d5350b9a2d63c8e1cffc2626f52` (2026-08-17) - PyTorch: 2.11.0+gitd0c8b1f (ROCm 7.2.53211), Python 3.12.13, Ubuntu 22.04.5 - Hardware: 8× AMD Instinct MI300X (gfx942), single node, TP=8 - Model: `nota-ai/Kimi-K3-Nota-Global-Pruned-25` (MXFP4). Note: expert-pruned K3 variant — the pruning affects MoE expert counts only; the KDA/GDN and MLA attention layers are architecturally identical to stock Kimi-K3, and the files involved in this bug (`vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/ops/third_party/kda/fused_recurrent.py`, `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/kimi_gdn_linear_attn.py`, `vllm/v1/attention/backends/gdn_attn.py`) were verified byte-identical to the image's stock copies before testing. </details> ### 🐛 Describe the bug Enabling ngram speculative decoding on Kimi-K3 (KimiLinear hybrid: 69 KDA/GatedDeltaNet recurrent layers + 24 MLA layers) produces **two distinct failures** on the ROCm build: **Failure 1 (root-caused, workaround proven): strided `state_indices` rejected by the KDA single-token decode kernel.** The first decode request after enabling `--speculative-config '{"method":"ngram","num_speculative_tokens":6,"prompt_lookup_max":4,"prompt_lookup_min":2}'` dies on every TP worker: ``` File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/kimi_gdn_linear_attn.py", line 609, in _forward core_attn_out_non_spec, _ = fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode( File ".../vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/ops/third_party/kda/fused_recurrent.py", line 564, in fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode raise ValueError("`state_indices` must be contiguous and one-dimensional.") ``` Diagnostics show `state_indices` arrives as **ndim=1, shape=(1,), stride=(7,)** — a strided column-slice of the block table (`block_table_tensor[~spec_mask, 0]`, row-stride = num_speculative_tokens+1 = 7). Without spec-decode the mask is all-true and the slice comes out contiguous, which is why only the spec path trips it. The data itself is correct (one read-only state-slot index per request); only the layout is strided, so a compacting copy is lossless: ```python # fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode, before the strict guard: if state_indices.ndim != 1 or state_indices.stride(0) != 1: if state_indices.ndim == 1: state_indices = state_indices.contiguous() # <- fix else: raise ValueError("`state_indices` must be contiguous and one-dimensional.") ``` With this in place, **single-stream ngram spec-decode works and is a large win**: mean acceptance length 5.45/5.41/4.80 (num_spec=6), accepted throughput up to **33.8 tok/s** vs 25.7 tok/s baseline on retrieval-shaped prompts, output exactness verified at temp=0 against a 200k-context needle suite (50/50 facts, identical to non-spec). **Failure 2 (the blocker, unresolved): GPU memory access fault under concurrent mixed spec/non-spec batches.** With the workaround in place, running **≥8 concurrent requests** through the same server GPU-faults all 8 devices within ~a minute: ``` Memory access fault by GPU node-7 (Agent handle: 0x15c8c3d0) on address 0x73862f600000. Reason: Unknown. Memory access fault by GPU node-9 (Agent handle: 0x170d4d00) on address 0x7210ff200000. Reason: Unknown. ... (all 8 GPUs) GPU core dump failed (EngineCore pid=543) ERROR ... Worker proc VllmWorker-2 died unexpectedly (exit code: None), shutting down executor. ``` The fault correlates with batches that mix spec-accepted and non-spec requests (the spec-decode metrics immediately before the fault show acceptance collapsing as the batch mixes). Our read: the concurrent spec+non-spec KDA recurrent-state indexing walks state out of bounds — the single-request `.contiguous()` read is benign, but the multi-request spec path has a deeper state-indexing bug. We deliberately stopped patching at this point (GPU-fault-class bugs are yours to own, not something downstream should whack-a-mole). ### Repro ```bash # image: vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:kimi-k3 (+ aiter main built from source, see env) python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model nota-ai/Kimi-K3-Nota-Global-Pruned-25 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-model-len 655360 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 --max-num-seqs 64 --block-size 128 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching --language-model-only --trust-remote-code \ --speculative-config '{"method":"ngram","num_speculative_tokens":6,"prompt_lookup_max":4,"prompt_lookup_min":2}' # env: VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=0 HSA_ENABLE_IPC_MODE_LEGACY=0 # VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=FP NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=0 # PYTORCH_HIP_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:False ``` 1. Single `/v1/completions` request → Failure 1 (ValueError) on stock code; works with the `.contiguous()` workaround at 33.8 tok/s accepted throughput. 2. 8+ concurrent `/v1/completions` requests (mixed lengths) → Failure 2 (GPU memory access fault, all devices) within ~1 minute. ### The question for maintainers Since our image was built (2026-07-27), this exact path has been reworked on main: #50649 *"Fix KDA NaN on mixed batches and racy autotune config"*, #50654 *"Fused kernel for KDA decode"*, #51862 *"Remove prefill pipeline stall in chunk KDA"* — and `kimi_gdn_linear_attn.py` now materializes the non-spec batch via `index_select` (which would also fix Failure 1 by construction). - **Does the current main/next kimi-k3 ROCm image fix the concurrent mixed spec/non-spec KDA fault (Failure 2)?** #50649's NaN fix touches mixed batches but the symptom we see is an OOB fault, not NaN. - If it's believed fixed, we're happy to validate a new `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:kimi-k3` (or nightly rocm) image on our 8×MI300X node and report back — ngram spec is worth ~30% end-to-end on this model and is currently the only spec-decode path that works on gfx942 (draft-model/DSpark and aiter-MLA paths are gfx950-only). Full logs available: complete ValueError traceback (all 8 workers), the strided-shape diagnostic, spec-decode metrics leading into the fault, and the GPU-fault log. signal.title: [Feature][ROCm] Per-layer-type KV-scale calibration for hybrid models — calibrate full-attention layers only, skip recurrent layers (unblocks fp8 KV on GDN/KimiLinear hybrids)
signal.text: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch #37554 was resolved by **disabling `--calculate-kv-scales` entirely on hybrid models** with recurrent layers (GDN/Mamba/SSM): the calibration pass is unreliable because recurrent state is uninitialized, so scales silently fall back to 1.0. That fix protects correctness but leaves hybrid models with **no path to usable fp8 KV at all**, because: 1. Scale-1.0 fp8 clips attention outliers. Measured on Kimi-K3 (24 MLA layers + 69 KDA recurrent layers, 8×MI300X): every one of the 24 MLA layers reports `_k_scale_float=1.0 _v_scale_float=1.0` under `fp8_e4m3` (the checkpoint ships no KV scales); at 200k+ context this first showed as coherent-but-wrong long-context retrieval and, on the current ROCm build, a GPU worker death on the first 200k prompt. 2. Static scales (`K_SCALE_CONSTANT` etc.) need a measured abs-max from real long-context activations — which is exactly what the disabled calibration pass would have produced. Chicken-and-egg. 3. On ROCm there is no scale-free escape hatch: `fp8_e5m2` has no attention backend (`No valid attention backend found for rocm`), so e4m3+scales is the only viable fp8 KV. **The ask:** make KV-scale calibration **layer-type-aware** instead of all-or-nothing. On a hybrid, only the full-attention (KV-cache-bearing) layers need scales — the recurrent layers have fixed-size state and no growing KV cache, and they are precisely the layers that make the current calibration unreliable. Calibrating *only* the attention layers and pinning recurrent layers out of the pass would sidestep the #37554 failure mode entirely. **Why it matters:** on hybrids the KV cache is small per token but is still the context-length limiter. Concretely, Kimi-K3 on 8×192 GB MI300X: bf16 KV caps at 640k tokens with CUDA graphs; fp8 KV would fit 768k+. Anyone serving GDN-hybrid models (Kimi-K3, Qwen3.5 per #37554) at long context hits this wall. ### Alternatives - Forcing calibration on (patching out the hybrid check): vLLM's own warning says the resulting scales are unreliable — not shippable. - Static per-layer scale env vars: blocked on the same missing measurement (see 2 above). - Offline calibration (e.g. llm-compressor-style KV-scale pass) producing checkpoint scales: works in principle, but doesn't help the (common) case of checkpoints that ship without scales; runtime calibration restricted to attention layers is strictly more general. ### Additional context Measured artifacts available on request: per-layer scale dump (24 MLA layers × 8 TP ranks, all 1.0), e5m2 backend-selection failure log, e4m3 worker-death log at 200k ctx. Environment: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:kimi-k3` image (v0.1.dev19253+g5f76ae224), ROCm 7.2.53211, 8×MI300X.

signal.title: Fix no-op num_blocks reduction in get_moe_wna16_block_config
signal.text: Fix #52590 ## Root cause In `get_moe_wna16_block_config` (`vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/fused_moe.py`), this block never actually changes `num_blocks`: ```python if size_k % 256 == 0 and num_blocks >= 256 and block_size_k < 256: block_size_k = 256 num_blocks = num_blocks // (256 // block_size_k) ``` `block_size_k` is set to 256 on the first line, so by the time the second line runs the divisor is `256 // 256 == 1`, leaving `num_blocks` untouched. The guarded `block_size_k` values are 32/64/128, so the divisor was meant to be 8/4/2. ## Fix Compute the reduction factor from the *previous* `block_size_k` before clobbering it: ```python old_block_size_k = block_size_k block_size_k = 256 num_blocks = num_blocks // (256 // old_block_size_k) ``` ## Impact The inflated `num_blocks` is compared against thresholds three more times (`>= 512`, `> 1024`, `>= 1024`) before returning, biasing the heuristic toward larger tiles than intended on WNA16 MoE (performance, not correctness — the divisibility guard still runs). A sweep over 4-bit MoE shapes (Mixtral 8x7B/8x22B, Qwen3-30B-A3B, DeepSeek-V2; group_size 32/64/128; top_k 2/6/8) shows 90/504 combinations produce a different config; e.g. Mixtral-8x7B w2 (group_size 128, 1 token) now yields `BLOCK_SIZE_N=128` instead of `256`. ## Tests - `tests/kernels/moe/test_wna16_block_config.py`: adds a case that triggers the `num_blocks` reduction branch and a regression test validating the correct reduction path.

### 🐛 Describe the bug PR [#36787](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/36787) moved Gemma's `sqrt(hidden_size)` normalization from `forward()` into text-only `embed_input_ids()`, but PaliGemma retained the inverse scale that previously compensated for the old common forward multiplication. Current vLLM consequently feeds projected image features into Gemma at `1 / sqrt(hidden_size)` of their intended magnitude. Before #36787, the operations were balanced: ```text text: embed_tokens ------------------------> Gemma.forward * sqrt(H) image: projector / sqrt(H) -> merge --------> Gemma.forward * sqrt(H) ``` After #36787, current vLLM scales only text: ```text text: embed_tokens * sqrt(H) -> merge -> Gemma.forward unchanged image: projector / sqrt(H) ----> merge -> Gemma.forward unchanged ``` Current `main` scales text in [`gemma.py:284-308`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/60c3a31b12b0a735baa79684885391747771ec64/vllm/model_executor/models/gemma.py#L284-L308), but still inverse-scales images in [`paligemma.py:376-383`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/60c3a31b12b0a735baa79684885391747771ec64/vllm/model_executor/models/paligemma.py#L376-L383). Multimodal merge only replaces placeholder rows, and `GemmaModel.forward(inputs_embeds=...)` applies no compensating scale. Transformers changed both halves atomically in [`0e7cb4e3`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/commit/0e7cb4e3ea3daaeef626148522f80b751e9559bd): Gemma text lookup gained `sqrt(H)` scaling and PaliGemma stopped dividing projected image features. Transformers 5.14.1 directly inserts raw projected image features into the already-scaled text embeddings. For ColPali's `hidden_size=2048`, the contract reduction is: ```python import math hidden_size = 2048 raw_projected_image = 1.0 print( "before #36787:", raw_projected_image * hidden_size**-0.5 * math.sqrt(hidden_size), ) print("current vLLM:", raw_projected_image * hidden_size**-0.5) print("expected:", raw_projected_image) ``` ```text before #36787: 1.0 current vLLM: 0.022097086912079608 expected: 1.0 ``` The stale factor is therefore about `0.0221`: projected image features enter Gemma at about 2.21% of their intended magnitude. Controlled one-variable A/B against the pinned Transformers reference: | Variant | Text cosine mean | Image cosine mean | Image p01 | Image minimum | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Current stale inverse scale | 0.999797 | 0.903149 | 0.430221 | 0.225688 | | Inverse scale removed only | 0.999797 | 0.987502 | 0.726556 | 0.436249 | The request, preprocessing, checkpoint, plugin SHA, and reference were held constant; only `vision_embeddings *= hidden_size**-0.5` was removed. The remaining image mismatch is a separately measured Neuron eager-vision drift, so this one-line change should not be represented as fixing all ColPali parity issues. Full ColPali command used for validation: ```bash vllm serve vidore/colpali-v1.3-hf \ --revision 7d3c8ab1c1908b32d701308fb1dfb2968d150c67 \ --served-model-name vidore/colpali-v1.3-hf \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --max-num-seqs 1 \ --max-model-len 4096 \ --trust-remote-code \ --runner pooling \ --convert none \ --pooler-config.task token_embed \ --port 20000 ``` Expected behavior: PaliGemma should return raw projected image features from `embed_multimodal()`, matching Transformers' scaled-text/raw-image contract. Suggested fix: ```diff def embed_multimodal(self, **kwargs: object) -> MultiModalEmbeddings: image_input = self._parse_and_validate_image_input(**kwargs) if image_input is None: return [] vision_embeddings = self._process_image_input(image_input) - vision_embeddings = vision_embeddings * (self.config.hidden_size**-0.5) return vision_embeddings ``` Suggested tests: pass known projected `image_embeds` to PaliGemma and assert they are returned unchanged; add one fixed-image Transformers parity test that compares first-step logits or top-k probabilities. Current ColPali tests verify shape, L2 normalization, and weak relevance ordering, which cannot detect this pre-language-model scaling error. The final downstream ColPali branch passes with pristine vLLM only because its host-vision path supplies raw projected features and bypasses `PaliGemma.embed_multimodal()`. The one-line patch is not part of that final plugin apply set, and the pristine pass does not validate the stale upstream method. This regression was introduced by #36787 (`65986db6ba71abf4cf0639c5fd1477b0d8df8f5e`). Searches for PaliGemma image scaling, inverse scaling, `sqrt(hidden_size)`, `hidden_size**-0.5`, and #36787 found no matching issue or follow-up fix. Severity: major silent correctness regression. The source contract is confirmed; broad current-main CUDA generation impact has not yet been quantified. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signal.title: [Bugfix][PaliGemma] Remove stale image embedding scaling
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #52667. After Gemma moved the `sqrt(hidden_size)` scaling into text embedding lookup, PaliGemma continued to apply the old `hidden_size**-0.5` factor to projected image features. This left image embeddings at approximately `1 / sqrt(hidden_size)` of the expected magnitude. Remove the stale image-side scaling so PaliGemma passes raw projected image features to the Gemma input embedding merge, matching the Transformers contract. This is a focused bug fix: it changes no vision projection, tokenizer, scheduler, or kernel behavior. ## Test Plan - `uv run --no-project .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m py_compile vllm/model_executor/models/paligemma.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_paligemma.py` - `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu /root/autodl-tmp/vllm-52590/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_paligemma.py -v` - Ran the same regression test against the unmodified baseline; it failed as expected because every projected embedding was still inverse-scaled. - Ran the staged-file pre-commit checks: Ruff, format, typos, mypy, SPDX, import/configuration checks, and related hooks. - `bash tools/pre_commit/update-dockerfile-graph.sh` passed manually. The corresponding pre-commit hook was skipped only in the Windows commit process because its absolute `/bin/bash` executable is unavailable on Windows. ## Test Result - Targeted PaliGemma regression test: **1 passed** on the remote Linux test host with `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`. - Unmodified baseline: **1 failed as expected**, confirming that the test detects the stale scaling. - Local syntax check: **passed**. - Relevant pre-commit hooks: **passed**. ## Duplicate-work check Before creating this PR, I ran: - `gh issue view 52667 --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments` - `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "52667 in:body"` - `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "PaliGemma image scaling"` No open PR matched the issue or the affected area. ## Documentation No documentation update is needed for this internal correctness fix. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used to inspect the issue and call chain and to prepare the implementation and regression test. signal.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Accept Anthropic x-api-key auth header
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #51572 vLLM's Anthropic Messages API (`/v1/messages`) currently accepts API keys only through `Authorization: Bearer`. Anthropic-compatible clients, including the official Anthropic API format and proxies such as LiteLLM, send the key through `x-api-key` instead. As a result, valid requests can return `401 Unauthorized` unless the header is rewritten to use Bearer authentication. This PR updates authentication in both frontends to accept either header: * Python: `AuthenticationMiddleware` in `vllm/entrypoints/serve/utils/server_utils.py` * Rust: `authenticate_api_key` in `rust/src/server/src/middleware/auth.rs` Behavior remains unchanged otherwise: * Existing `Authorization: Bearer` authentication continues to work. * `x-api-key` is accepted for Anthropic-compatible clients. * Missing or incorrect keys are still rejected. * Unguarded routes such as `/health` and `OPTIONS` behavior are unchanged. Tests are included for both authentication paths to prevent regression. ## Test Plan * Python unit coverage in `tests/entrypoints/serve/utils/test_authentication_middleware.py` * Rust auth coverage for valid and invalid `x-api-key` values * Manual verification with `--api-key` enabled: * `/v1/messages` with `x-api-key` * `/v1/messages` with `Authorization: Bearer` * missing or incorrect credentials returning `401` ## Test Result Local authentication logic checks for Bearer and `x-api-key` accept/reject paths passed. The full pytest and Cargo test suites were not run locally; complete coverage will be provided by CI. ## AI Assistance Disclosure AI assistance was used to locate the authentication middleware and help draft the patch. I reviewed every changed line and take responsibility for the implementation.

signal.title: [Model] Enable LoRA support for tower and connector in LlavaNextForConditionalGeneration
signal.text: ## Purpose Adds LoRA support for the vision tower and connector modules of `LlavaNextForConditionalGeneration`, following the same pattern already used by `LlavaForConditionalGeneration`. This is part of the broader effort tracked in #31479 to enable LoRA on the tower/connector for more multimodal models. Changes: - `LlavaNextForConditionalGeneration` now inherits `SupportsLoRA` and defines `packed_modules_mapping` for the language backbone. - Added `get_mm_mapping()` to expose the `language_model` / `multi_modal_projector` / `vision_tower` module prefixes. - Added `get_num_mm_encoder_tokens()` and `get_num_mm_connector_tokens()` to compute the tower/connector token counts. - Updated `docs/models/supported_models.md` to mark LoRA support (✅) for `LlavaNextForConditionalGeneration`. ## Test Plan Ran on 2x A100-PCIE-40GB with `llava-hf/llava-v1.6-vicuna-7b-hf`: ```python from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams from vllm.assets.image import ImageAsset llm = LLM( model="llava-hf/llava-v1.6-vicuna-7b-hf", max_model_len=4096, enable_lora=True, max_lora_rank=16, enable_tower_connector_lora=True, gpu_memory_utilization=0.85, ) image = ImageAsset("cherry_blossom").pil_image prompt = "USER: <image>\nWhat is in this image? ASSISTANT:" outputs = llm.generate( {"prompt": prompt, "multi_modal_data": {"image": image}}, SamplingParams(max_tokens=32), ) print(outputs[0].outputs[0].text) ``` ## Test Result With `enable_tower_connector_lora=True`, the engine log confirms the tower/connector LoRA path is wired up correctly: ``` [punica_selector.py:20] Using PunicaWrapperGPU. [model_manager.py:233] LoRA for the tower and connector of multimodal models is experimental and may contain bugs. Please report any related issues on GitHub if you encounter them. ``` Generation completes successfully end-to-end: ``` The image shows a close-up view of cherry blossoms in bloom, which suggests the photo was taken during a season known as sakura ``` Without `enable_tower_connector_lora` set, the model still loads and runs generation correctly as before (backward compatible), with the standard `enable_lora=True` LoRA path unaffected. ## Bugfix update The original identity-mapping implementation of `get_num_mm_encoder_tokens`/`get_num_mm_connector_tokens` assumed the LLM-side placeholder token count equals the raw vision-tower/connector token count. That's wrong for LLaVA-NeXT's anyres/unpad tiling: `unpad` crops rows/cols based on the image's aspect ratio and appends newline tokens, so the final placeholder count is **not invertible** back to the true per-tile tower/connector token count (verified numerically across several grids/aspect ratios — mismatches of hundreds of tokens in either direction). Fix: added an optional `mm_data` parameter to both interface methods (`vllm/model_executor/models/interfaces.py`, threaded through `set_active_mm_loras` in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/mm/lora.py`) so implementations can compute the token count *forward* from the real per-item `pixel_values` tile count instead of relying on the placeholder count. `LlavaNextForConditionalGeneration.get_num_mm_encoder_tokens` now uses this to derive `num_tiles * patch_grid_length ** 2`, with a fallback to the old identity behavior when `mm_data` isn't supplied. Added regression tests in `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_llava_next.py` covering multiple anyres grids (2x2, 1x3/3x1, 1x2/2x1). --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [x] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Bug]: Missing `has_cutedsl()` guard in `DeepseekCompressor` (head_dim == 512 path)
signal.text: ### Your current environment cant share this at the moment. ### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Summary In the DeepSeek V4 `DeepseekCompressor` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/compressor.py`), the CuTe DSL kernel path for `head_dim == 512` is selected without checking `has_cutedsl()`. Every other DeepSeek V4 CUDA/DS kernel selection site in the repo gates on `has_cutedsl()`, so this looks like an inconsistency that was missed in one spot. ### Where the guard is already established - `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/common/ops/cache_utils.py:412` -> `if has_cutedsl():` - `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/common/ops/fused_indexer_q.py:353` and `:422` -> `if has_cutedsl():` - `vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py:57` -> `if not has_cutedsl():` - `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/ops/__init__.py` explicitly documents that leaf modules must only be imported under a `has_cutedsl()`/`is_cuda()` gate. ### The missing guard `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/compressor.py` currently uses: ```python if current_platform.is_cuda() and self.head_dim == 512: ``` which unconditionally selects the CuTe DSL compressor (`compress_norm_rope_store_cutedsl`), even when the optional `cutlass` (CuTe DSL) package is not importable. ### Suggested change ```python if current_platform.is_cuda() and self.head_dim == 512 and has_cutedsl(): ``` with the existing import (`from vllm.utils.import_utils import has_cutedsl`) added if not already present. ### Why it matters - On builds where `cutlass`/CuTe DSL is not available, the `head_dim == 512` compressor path currently fails at kernel dispatch even though the framework already supports a graceful Triton fallback and the rest of the DSv4 ops check `has_cutedsl()`. - Consistent with the established pattern in the same feature area. ### Environment (for reference) This was found while building/running vLLM 0.26 for an H200 (sm_90a) target where the optional CuTe DSL package is not shipped. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
