signal.title: [Bugfix] OffloadingConnector: stop zeroing offload hits under MTP/EAGLE spec decode
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #52735 — with `OffloadingConnector` + MTP/EAGLE speculative decoding, KV is stored to the CPU tier but never served. Root cause chain and unit-level reproduction: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52735#issuecomment-5328641909 Three defects combined: 1. **All-groups drafter fallback** (`SchedulerOffloadConfig.from_spec`): with spec decode on and no `is_eagle_group` annotation — the normal state for shared-group MTP models (Qwen3.5/3.8-style: the drafter is a regular `full_attention` decoder layer merged into the target group, see `qwen3_5_mtp.py`) — every group was treated as a drafter group. Removed: mark nothing, log once. Serving drafter KV one chunk stale can only lower speculative acceptance (the target verifies every draft); zeroing the entire offload tier is the strictly worse trade. 2. **Volatile-tail pop without widening on non-SW groups** (`_lookup_complete_chunks`): the old comment said widening is only needed for sliding-window groups. That's true for the group's own hit, but not for its **siblings**: the un-widened pop shrinks `max_hit_size_tokens` below what was queried, which pushes the confirmed boundary under a coarser group's chunk granularity (e.g. a mamba-align group) and returns 0 for the whole request. Widening now applies to every drafter group; the pop lands on the extra queried chunk and the boundary holds. This matters independently of (1) for genuinely-annotated drafter groups. 3. **Permanent trailing-chunk store hole** (`storable_chunks`): the decode-time exclusion of a drafter group's trailing chunk persisted after request finish, losing the final chunk of every drafter group per request. Once finished, no spec-token rejection can rewrite the tail; the exclusion is lifted at finish. The lookup-side pop still never serves the final *stored* chunk of an unverified drafter group directly, so this is safe including for aborts. ## Not a duplicate #47890/#47891/#48459 fix a different mechanism (a genuinely-annotated ephemeral DSpark draft group vetoing the multi-group lookup); #52047 fixes drafter-group *annotation* on the hybrid grouping path for separate-draft models. None covers the shared-group MTP case or the pop/sibling-starvation and finish-store defects. Compatible with all three. ## Test Plan `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/` → 246 passed, 2 skipped. Three new regression tests fail on main and pass here (store→finish→re-send flow with a manager that only hits stored keys: 0 → 16 tokens served, equal to the non-speculative baseline). Two existing eagle tests updated where semantics intentionally changed (boundary holds instead of zeroing; tail stored at finish — the decode-phase hold-back is still asserted separately). @greglechin has a 3-minute deterministic XPU repro and has offered validation — that run is the intended end-to-end gate. *AI-assistance disclosure: developed with Claude (Anthropic); the submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.*

signal.title: [ROCm][Perf] Fuse DeepSeek-V4 mHC post/pre and RMSNorm with AITER
signal.text:
## Purpose This PR improves the ROCm DeepSeek-V4 mHC path by wiring the existing AITER fused mHC operators into vLLM. The ROCm path can now replace the previous sequence of separate mHC/RMSNorm kernels with the fused AITER flow: - `mhc_post` + `mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum` -> `mhc_fused_post_pre_gemm_sqrsum` - `mhc_pre_big_fuse` + `add_rmsnorm_quant` -> `mhc_pre_big_fuse_rmsnorm` For unsupported fused-RMSNorm hidden sizes, the path still uses fused post+pre where available, while preserving the standalone RMSNorm fallback. > [!NOTE] > The change is scoped to the ROCm/AITER path and does not change the CUDA or XPU implementations. --- Before fuse: After fuse (**38.35%** faster): ## Test Plan Benchmark with SA InferenceX `8k1k` workload: ```bash # Launch the server vllm serve /shared/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --port 8333 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --async-scheduling \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --distributed-executor-backend mp \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --trust-remote-code \ --moe-backend aiter \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \ --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' # Bench client CONCS=${CONCS:-"1 4 16 64"} for CONC in ${CONCS}; do NUM_PROMPTS=$((CONC * 10)) NUM_WARMUPS=$((CONC * 2)) python InferenceX/utils/bench_serving/benchmark_serving.py \ --model /shared/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --backend vllm \ --base-url "http://0.0.0.0:8333" \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 8192 \ --random-output-len 1024 \ --random-range-ratio 0.8 \ --num-prompts "${NUM_PROMPTS}" \ --max-concurrency "${CONC}" \ --num-warmups "${NUM_WARMUPS}" \ --request-rate inf \ --ignore-eos \ --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el \ --trust-remote-code \ --use-chat-template --dsv4 done ``` Accuracy test with `gsm8k` dataset. ## Test Result ### Benchmark To be completed... ### Accuracy Test To be completed... ---

signal.title: [KV-offload][FS]: Batching for read/write threads
signal.text: PR #49152 introduced batched C versions of load_block / store_block. The batching was request-level, i.e. each thread in the thread_pool receives all the keys for a request and loads/stores them one after another. If there are 16 requests, each with say 100 keys to load, and we have 16 threads. Each thread will work on a separate request. This is less desirable as read jobs for different requests are interleaved on the disk, increasing any single request's total read time. This PR: Batch load/stores with the intent of parallelizing per-request loads/stores. i.e. Care about FCFS at the request level. In this PR, a single request is split into as many batches as there are threads and each thread gets an even distribution of work. ### Benchmarks Benchmark the following configurations, signal.title: [ROCm][Perf][Model] Fuse Qwen3-VL attention prologue into single AITER kernel
signal.text: ## Purpose Fuse the Qwen3-VL attention prologue's q/k RMSNorm, 3D MRoPE, FP8 KV quantization, and KV-cache write into one AITER kernel, removing four launches per layer. The path remains opt-in through `VLLM_Q3VL_FUSE_ATTN_PROLOGUE=1`; the default path is unchanged. ## Current implementation The rebased implementation follows the established `qk_norm_rope_kvcache_fusion.py` safety model: - AITER dispatch lives in the shared ROCm AITER wrapper instead of a model-local direct import. - `VLLM_Q3VL_FUSE_ATTN_PROLOGUE` is registered in `vllm.envs`. - Attention-context lookup failures propagate instead of being swallowed. - Profiling/no-cache passes explicitly zero `q_out` before attention consumes it. - The custom op handles both 1D text positions and 3D MRoPE positions. - Focused tests cover exception propagation, profiling output initialization, and the actual strided KV view. ## Hard dependency **[AITER #4531](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4531) is required before enabling this flag.** Current vLLM unified attention uses a `transpose(1, 2).split(head_size, dim=-1)` cache view. Its block, token, and head strides differ from a contiguous tensor. AITER #4531 forwards all six K/V block-token-head strides and tests this exact layout; block-stride-only support is insufficient and can silently misaddress cache entries. ## Qwen3-VL integration stack - **This PR — [vLLM #50212](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50212):** fused attention prologue; hard-depends on #4531. - [AITER #4531](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4531): full strided MRoPE KV-cache support. - [AITER #4554](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4554): gfx950 Qwen3-VL MXFP4 tuning rows; not required for the public FP8 reproduction below. - [AITER #4556](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4556): optional MXFP4 FlyDSL stage-2 override; not exercised by the FP8 checkpoint below. - [AITER #4761](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4761): independent Triton unified-attention prefill/decode optimization in the later Image C stack; not required for this fused prologue. ## Rebase provenance - Frozen vLLM `main`: `d29dc3ab87840aef42129b30825176295ea73b07` - Current PR head: `1bc846b952eb352ac198d0a4697485f1244e5281` - Required AITER #4531 head: `2b9063490be30795aa186fca3aea4b4c91b52a0a` ## Validation - `pytest -q tests/model_executor/layers/test_qk_norm_mrope_kvcache.py` — **3 passed** - Qwen3-MoE module import and custom-op registration smoke — **passed** - strict vLLM environment-variable validation with the flag enabled — **passed** - Ruff format/check and Python compile checks — **passed** - vLLM DCO check — **passed** The targeted tests specifically verify the two previously reported safety paths: context errors raise, while legitimate profiling/no-cache execution initializes the query output. ## Public FP8 reproduction The fused path was reproduced without MXFP4 weights using the public checkpoint [`Qwen/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct-FP8`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct-FP8), revision `d9748a51ae66354c4dad665aab2c71f26cf2c8cd`. Test configuration: MI355X (`gfx950`), vLLM 0.26.0 plus this PR and AITER #4531, TP1, `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN`, FP8 model weights, FP8 E4M3 KV cache, one 512×512 image per request, random input/output lengths 256/128, max concurrency 4, 16 requests and 4 warmups per repeat. The test image also contained AITER #4554/#4556, but those MXFP4-only paths were inactive for this FP8 checkpoint. The two arms differed only by: ```text VLLM_Q3VL_FUSE_ATTN_PROLOGUE=1 # fusion on VLLM_Q3VL_FUSE_ATTN_PROLOGUE=0 # fusion off ``` - vLLM resolved `Qwen3VLMoeForConditionalGeneration` with `quantization=fp8`. - The fused attention-prologue activation log appeared only in the enabled arm. - AITER #4531's exact strided-layout FP8 regression passed its strict bit-for-bit strided-vs-contiguous comparison. - All 96 measured requests succeeded. Each paired seed generated the same number of output tokens. Warm median of three paired repeats: | metric | fusion on | fusion off | delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | output throughput | 568.36 tok/s | 500.20 tok/s | **+13.6%** | | mean TPOT | 5.97 ms | 6.93 ms | **-13.8%** | | mean end-to-end latency | 798.65 ms | 920.30 ms | **-13.2%** | All three paired throughput results improved: +10.0%, +13.6%, and +18.4%. This confirms that the optimization and its AITER dependency can be reproduced with a public FP8 checkpoint; MXFP4 model weights are not required. ## Measured performance — MXFP4 235B Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B W4A4 MXFP4 on MI355X (`gfx950`), ISL/OSL 1024, 512×512 images. Warm median-of-3; each pair differed only by the fusion flag. | TP | max concurrency | fusion on (output tok/s) | fusion off | throughput delta | TPOT delta | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 8 | 4 | 903.75 | 798.43 | +13.2% | -11.7% | | 8 | 64 | 8,311.76 | 7,602.44 | +9.3% | -8.6% | | 8 | 256 | 19,301.62 | 18,160.64 | +6.3% | -6.2% | | 4 | 4 | 889.17 | 771.20 | +15.3% | -13.3% | | 4 | 64 | 7,096.29 | 6,508.54 | +9.0% | -8.9% | | 4 | 256 | 14,721.53 | 13,929.42 | +5.7% | -5.5% | | 2 | 4 | 834.52 | 722.84 | +15.5% | -13.4% | | 2 | 64 | 5,486.64 | 5,075.31 | +8.1% | -7.0% | | 2 | 256 | 10,388.40 | 9,945.26 | +4.5% | -5.0% | All nine points improved. TP4/TP2 ran without expert parallelism; only within-row on/off deltas are claimed. <details> <summary>Essential PR checklist</summary> - [x] Purpose and dependency documented. - [x] Focused safety/layout test added. - [x] Targeted and end-to-end results provided. - [x] Opt-in behavior documented. - [x] Reproduced with a public FP8 checkpoint. </details> > This PR was developed with AI assistance. signal.title: [RFC]: Extensible GEMM Epilogue Contracts for Residual, Norm, and Gated Activation Fusion
signal.text:
### Motivation. vLLM has mature linear-kernel selection and several compiler fusion passes, but the kernel interface and the graph-fusion interface do not yet share one typed contract for fusing a producer GEMM with adjacent residual, normalization, scaling, quantization, or gated-activation work. Today a provider is generally selected to produce the linear output, after which model code or a compilation pass applies downstream operations. This leaves two recurring gaps: 1. a provider that can evaluate a valid epilogue while accumulators are still in registers cannot advertise that capability through the same selection path; and 2. correctness constraints around reduction domains and tensor-parallel collective boundaries are encoded in one-off fused modules/patterns instead of one fail-closed contract. This RFC proposes an optional `GemmEpilogueSpec` understood by linear-kernel providers and compiler rewrites. It is not a request to fuse every decoder block or to require one backend. A provider may accept a spec only when it can implement the exact shape, dtype, reduction, aliasing, and distributed semantics; otherwise vLLM uses the existing unfused path. The initial target is the common Transformer structure in which GEMMs are interleaved with residual addition, RMSNorm-style normalization, scaling/quantization, and SwiGLU-like gated activations. Diffusion/omni models are a downstream consumer, but the abstraction belongs in vLLM's kernel boundary if it is sufficiently generic. ### Proposed Change. #### 1. Design principles - Optional and fail closed: existing kernels and model paths are unchanged without a matched spec. - Typed semantics, not arbitrary Python callbacks in the hot path. - Provider-neutral: CUTLASS/CuTe DSL, Triton, FlashInfer, vendor plugins, or native code may implement a capability. - Compiler-aware: a graph pass may request a spec only after matching a proven graph. - TP-aware: a row-parallel partial sum cannot be normalized as though it were the complete tensor before all-reduce. - Numerically explicit: accumulation dtype, cast points, reduction dtype, and output/alias semantics are part of the contract. - Measured enablement: a valid fusion is not automatically faster for every shape/batch. #### 2. Proposed types Illustrative API: ```python class EpilogueOp(Enum): BIAS = "bias" RESIDUAL_ADD = "residual_add" ROW_SCALE = "row_scale" RMS_NORM = "rms_norm" STATIC_QUANTIZE = "static_quantize" SILU_MUL = "silu_mul" class CollectiveBoundary(Enum): NONE = "none" PRE_COLLECTIVE_PARTIAL = "pre_collective_partial" POST_ALL_REDUCE_COMPLETE = "post_all_reduce_complete" @dataclass(frozen=True) class GemmEpilogueSpec: ops: tuple[EpilogueOp, ...] accumulation_dtype: torch.dtype output_dtype: torch.dtype reduction_dtype: torch.dtype | None collective_boundary: CollectiveBoundary auxiliary_inputs: tuple[str, ...] outputs: tuple[str, ...] mutates: frozenset[str] class MMLinearKernel(...): @classmethod def can_implement_epilogue( cls, config, spec: GemmEpilogueSpec ) -> tuple[bool, str | None]: ... def apply(self, layer, x, bias=None, *, epilogue=None, **kwargs): ... ``` The final interface may use specialized subtypes rather than an enum list. The important property is that supported compositions are explicit and inspectable. #### 3. Compiler/provider flow ```mermaid flowchart LR Graph["FX/model graph
GEMM + adjacent ops"] Match["Semantic pattern match
shape, alias, reduction, TP boundary"] Spec["Build GemmEpilogueSpec"] Select["Existing linear-kernel selector"] Cap{"Provider can implement
this exact spec?"} Fused["Provider fused GEMM + epilogue"] Fallback["Existing GEMM
+ existing separate ops"] Verify["Debug/CI reference checks
and benchmark gate"] Graph --> Match --> Spec --> Select --> Cap Cap -->|yes| Fused --> Verify Cap -->|no| Fallback ``` Graph matching remains in compilation/model integration. Kernel providers do not parse arbitrary FX graphs. Providers receive a normalized, validated spec. #### 4. Correct placement around tensor parallelism ```mermaid flowchart TD Col["Column-parallel GEMM
output shard is semantically complete
for shard-local eligible epilogues"] Row["Row-parallel GEMM
rank-local partial sums"] AR["Tensor-parallel all-reduce"] Full["Complete output tensor"] Post["Residual / norm / gated op
when reduction domain is complete"] Col --> Post Row --> AR --> Full --> Post ``` Some operations can run on a shard; others require the full hidden dimension or the globally reduced value. The pattern matcher must encode the mathematical reduction domain. A provider cannot accept `POST_ALL_REDUCE_COMPLETE` work on a rank-local partial accumulator. An implementation may eventually fuse all-reduce plus a post-collective epilogue through a communicator/provider that supports it, but that is a separate capability. This RFC must not move normalization across a collective merely to make a kernel shape convenient. #### 5. Initial supported compositions Start small and evidence-driven. Candidate specs: - GEMM + bias; - GEMM + row scale; - GEMM + static output quantization; - GEMM + residual add when aliasing and broadcast semantics are simple; - paired gate/up projections + SiLU-multiply where the provider exposes a joint output contract; and - post-all-reduce residual/RMSNorm only through an existing correctly placed fused collective capability. RMSNorm inside a GEMM epilogue is valid only if the provider can compute the full required row reduction correctly. A tiled GEMM that sees only part of the normalized dimension must reject the spec or use a proven multi-tile reduction scheme. #### 6. Integration with current kernel selection The current `MMLinearKernel` selection lifecycle already separates: - hardware support; - whether a kernel can implement a layer configuration; - parameter processing; and - execution. Add epilogue capability after ordinary layer compatibility. `--linear-backend` continues to constrain providers. A selected backend may still reject a particular epilogue and execute the ordinary linear path; no new backend should be selected solely because it claims a fusion unless the existing priority/benchmark policy allows it. The contract should also be visible in debug logs/metrics: requested spec, selected provider, rejection reason, and fallback path. #### 7. Numerical and aliasing contract Every supported spec declares: - GEMM accumulation dtype; - when the accumulator is cast; - epsilon and reduction dtype for normalization; - whether residual is read before an output write; - exact broadcasting rules for weights/scales/bias; - output dtype(s), including optional dual output; - allowed non-contiguous inputs; and - mutation/alias behavior for `torch.compile` fake/meta implementations. Tests compare against an independent high-precision reference as well as the existing unfused path. A fusion may be numerically closer to the high-precision reference while not bitwise equal to bf16 eager execution; that must be represented by a declared tolerance and model-level gate, not silently treated as exact. #### 8. Validation matrix Unit/kernel tests: - multiple `M/N/K`, including small decode and larger prefill batches; - bf16/fp16/fp8 inputs and supported accumulation/output dtypes; - contiguous and declared non-contiguous layouts; - bias/residual broadcast cases; - alias/mutation checks under eager and `torch.compile`; - negative tests for unsupported reduction domains/spec orderings; - TP world sizes 1/2/4 with a distributed reference; and - graph pass fallback when no provider accepts the spec. End-to-end tests: - at least one autoregressive decoder block; - one diffusion/omni Transformer consumer if the abstraction is shared downstream; - compilation enabled/disabled; and - output/accuracy gates appropriate to the model. #### 9. Benchmark and enablement policy For each provider/spec/shape regime report: - kernel latency and achieved compute/bandwidth; - kernel launch count; - HBM bytes when measurable; - end-to-end latency/throughput; - compile/capture compatibility; - peak workspace memory; and - numerical results. Enable only where end-to-end evidence supports it. A fusion can regress low-batch execution because fixed scheduling/collective overhead outweighs saved launches. The selector/config may need shape-regime gating rather than a universal boolean. #### 10. Alternatives considered - **Keep adding one-off fused modules.** Fast for a single pattern but duplicates capability, fallback, and correctness logic. - **Rely only on compiler-generated fusion.** Valuable and should remain the first option, but does not expose provider-specific GEMM epilogues or distributed placement semantics uniformly. - **Allow arbitrary Python epilogue callables.** Hard to validate, serialize, select, and support across providers. - **Put the abstraction only in vLLM-Omni.** Diffusion is a motivating consumer, but linear-kernel selection and several relevant fusion passes are upstream vLLM concepts. #### 11. Phased plan 1. Agree on the typed spec and rejection/fallback behavior. 2. Implement one minimal existing capability (for example bias/static scaling) through the contract without changing defaults. 3. Connect one compiler pattern and add debug observability. 4. Add distributed-boundary negative/positive tests. 5. Benchmark one residual/norm or gated-activation composition. 6. Let downstream vLLM-Omni/SGLang work evaluate additional providers separately. ### Feedback Period. At least one week. ### CC List. No specific CC requested; feedback from linear-kernel, compilation, distributed, and quantization maintainers would be valuable. ### Any Other Things. Relevant code and discussions: - vLLM linear-kernel interface and providers: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/main/vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear - `MMLinearKernel` base contract: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/base.py - Existing all-reduce/RMSNorm compilation fusion: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/allreduce_rms_fusion.py - Hardware-agnostic model-definition RFC: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/44219 - vLLM-Omni diffusion kernel optimization RFC: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/3186 - vLLM-Omni diffusion operator-boundary RFC: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/5582 - SGLang CUTLASS dynamic epilogue investigation: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/30809 ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signal.title: [RFC]: Rank-Skew-Aware Collective Attribution for Tensor-Parallel Serving
signal.text:
### Motivation. Tensor-parallel traces often report a large amount of GPU time inside all-reduce or another collective. That observation alone does not identify the cause. The interval may contain: - useful data transfer limited by the interconnect/backend; - rank-arrival skew, where an early rank waits for a slower peer; - host dispatch or graph-launch skew before the collective; - additional copies/registration imposed by a selected communicator; or - a correctness failure in which ranks issue different collective sequences. These causes require different remedies. Replacing a collective kernel cannot fix time dominated by peer arrival, while reducing host skew cannot raise a genuinely saturated bandwidth ceiling. vLLM has communicator benchmarks and several collective implementations, but it does not expose a common, request/layer-correlated attribution workflow that combines production traces, a message-size-matched zero-skew baseline, and controlled skew injection. This RFC proposes an opt-in profiling facility and offline report that classify collective cost as transfer-dominated, arrival-skew-dominated, mixed, or inconclusive. It complements, but does not duplicate, TP consensus/deadlock work such as #48720: that RFC detects/recoveries collective-sequence failures; this RFC attributes performance when execution is correct. ### Proposed Change. #### 1. Goals - Assign a stable logical ID to sampled TP collectives. - Record per-rank arrival/enqueue and completion evidence without adding a synchronizing collective to the measured hot path. - Run the same operator/message sizes in an isolated calibration benchmark. - Inject controlled rank delay to learn latency sensitivity to skew. - Produce a causally conservative classification with confidence/evidence. - Point optimization work toward host scheduling, batching/parallel policy, overlap, or communicator/backend changes based on the classification. #### 2. Non-goals - Always-on per-collective production tracing. - A new collective implementation. - Automatically changing NCCL algorithms from one trace. - Treating `collective_duration - arrival_skew` as an exact transfer time. - Detecting/recovering mismatched collective sequences (covered by separate reliability work). #### 3. Trace record Illustrative schema: ```python @dataclass(frozen=True) class CollectiveTraceRecord: run_id: str request_class: str step_id: int layer_id: str collective_ordinal: int group_name: str rank: int world_size: int op: str shape: tuple[int, ...] dtype: str payload_bytes: int backend: str execution_mode: str # eager / compile / cuda_graph host_enqueue_ns: int gpu_begin_ns: int | None gpu_end_ns: int | None ``` `(step_id, layer_id, collective_ordinal, group_name)` must be derived from control flow shared by all ranks, not assigned by a rank-local counter that can silently diverge. Trace artifacts are merged after the run. The profiler must not call an extra all-gather/barrier around each measured collective, because that would manufacture or hide the skew being measured. #### 4. Three-source attribution ```mermaid flowchart TD Prod["Sampled production/profile run
per-rank arrival and collective spans"] Base["Isolated calibration
same op, size, dtype, topology, backend"] Inject["Controlled skew sweep
delay one rank by known intervals"] Join["Join by collective signature"] Features["Derived evidence
arrival spread, zero-skew floor,
throughput headroom, skew sensitivity"] Classify{"Conservative classifier"} Wait["Arrival-skew dominated
reduce host/rank imbalance"] Transfer["Transfer dominated
backend/topology/overlap candidate"] Mixed["Mixed
optimize both / change parallel plan"] Unknown["Inconclusive
collect more evidence"] Prod --> Join Base --> Join Inject --> Join --> Features --> Classify Classify --> Wait Classify --> Transfer Classify --> Mixed Classify --> Unknown ``` Evidence sources: 1. **Production arrival spread.** Difference between earliest/latest rank enqueue/readiness for the same logical collective, after clock calibration where needed. 2. **Zero-skew calibration curve.** Latency/throughput distribution for the exact op, payload, world size, topology, backend, and registration mode under synchronized inputs. 3. **Skew-injection curve.** Repeat calibration while delaying selected ranks by controlled intervals. This establishes how the backend's observed span changes when arrival skew is known. The report should not claim an exact decomposition if clocks or execution mode cannot support it. It can still classify when multiple independent measurements agree. #### 5. Clock and execution-mode handling Same-node phase 1 can use a shared host monotonic clock source plus CUDA/CUPTI timestamps, with startup/end calibration and explicit uncertainty. Multi-node support must estimate clock offsets/drift or rely on profiler data with a documented cross-node time base. CUDA graphs require special handling because Python wrappers run at capture rather than each replay. Supported choices include: - graph-node/CUPTI/Nsight evidence correlated to a deterministic collective ordinal; - sampled eager/compile runs for arrival instrumentation plus a separate graph-mode calibration; or - backend profiler callbacks that execute on replay. The report must label evidence as capture-time or replay-time and must not reuse capture timestamps as though they describe every replay. #### 6. Instrumentation modes Proposed modes: - `off` (default): no records or extra state; - `trace`: short, explicitly profiled run with detailed sampled records and NVTX ranges; - `aggregate`: optional low-rate sampled summaries if a provider can supply replay-safe timestamps without synchronization; and - `calibrate`: isolated communicator benchmark plus optional skew sweep. Instrumentation belongs near `GroupCoordinator`/device-communicator dispatch so custom all-reduce, pynccl, symmetric-memory, and platform providers emit the same schema. High-level `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce()` can add request/layer context without owning timing. #### 7. Derived report For each collective signature, report: - call count and total payload bytes; - per-rank enqueue spread distribution; - observed collective span/duration distribution; - calibrated zero-skew p50/p95 and achieved bandwidth; - hardware/topology bandwidth ceiling when available; - skew-injection response curve; - backend/algorithm/registration and graph mode; - classification and confidence; - missing evidence/clock uncertainty; and - suggested next experiment, not an automatic configuration change. Example decision logic (thresholds to be validated, not hard-coded by this RFC): - observed latency near zero-skew calibration and bandwidth near measured ceiling -> transfer-dominated; - observed excess latency tracks arrival spread and injected-skew curve while zero-skew calibration has headroom -> arrival-skew-dominated; - both arrival spread and zero-skew transfer cost are material -> mixed; - mismatched op IDs/call counts -> stop performance attribution and route to correctness/consensus diagnostics; - otherwise -> inconclusive. #### 8. Optimization routing The report maps classifications to candidate work: | Classification | Candidate next steps | | --- | --- | | Arrival-skew dominated | profile host dispatch/pre-collective compute, remove rank-asymmetric work, reduce tiny collective fragmentation, evaluate smaller TP | | Transfer dominated | evaluate backend/algorithm/topology, fusion, overlap, payload/layout, or a different parallel axis | | Mixed | address largest source first; rerun attribution after each change | | Inconclusive | improve clock/replay instrumentation or collect a longer isolated trace | This table is guidance, not an auto-tuner. #### 9. Validation Synthetic tests: - zero injected skew with payload sweep; - fixed delay on one rank and alternating delayed rank; - compute imbalance before a collective; - bandwidth saturation with large payloads; - many small collectives dominated by launch overhead; - custom all-reduce registered/unregistered buffers; - eager, compile, and CUDA-graph replay where supported; and - intentionally mismatched collective IDs to verify handoff to reliability diagnostics. Correctness/safety tests: - `off` adds no hot-path allocation or thread; - profiler emits no additional measured-group collectives; - trace collection cannot change collective order; - bounded buffers drop samples with a counter rather than blocking execution; - artifacts exclude prompt/output tensor contents by default; and - profiler teardown works after request cancellation/error. #### 10. Benchmark plan Use the existing device-communicator benchmark as the calibration entrypoint where possible. Add: - exact production payload list import; - controlled pre-call delay per rank; - output JSON matching the trace schema/signature; - at least two TP world sizes and small/large payload regimes; and - comparison across the communicator(s) available on the test topology. Then run one representative model in trace mode and verify that the tool's classification matches the synthetic regime introduced before selected layers. #### 11. Alternatives considered - **Use only Nsight time inside NCCL.** It identifies where time is observed, not why peers entered at different times. - **Use only an isolated NCCL benchmark.** It gives a ceiling/floor but cannot show whether production ranks arrive together. - **Subtract arrival spread from duration.** Collective protocols overlap waiting and transfer nonlinearly; the result is not a reliable exact decomposition. - **Insert barriers around each collective.** This destroys the phenomenon under measurement and adds overhead. - **Reuse the TP consensus guard.** Collective-count health is valuable but does not quantify healthy-run transfer versus skew cost. #### 12. Phased plan 1. Define schema and add skew injection/output JSON to the communicator benchmark. 2. Add `trace` instrumentation for eager same-node TP behind an explicit profiler option. 3. Build the offline join/classification report with uncertainty. 4. Validate against synthetic known-skew and bandwidth regimes. 5. Add compile/CUDA-graph replay evidence. 6. Consider multi-node clock calibration and low-rate aggregate mode separately. ### Feedback Period. At least one week. ### CC List. No specific CC requested; feedback from distributed, observability, benchmark, and CUDA-graph maintainers would be especially useful. ### Any Other Things. Relevant code and discussions: - High-level TP communication operations: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/communication_op.py - Group/device communicator dispatch: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/parallel_state.py - Custom all-reduce implementation: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/device_communicators/custom_all_reduce.py - Device communicator benchmark: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_device_communicators.py - Complementary TP consensus/deadlock RFC: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48720 ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signal.title: [Bugfix][PaliGemma] Don't inverse-scale image embeddings after Gemma normalizer moved to embed time
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #52667. `PaliGemmaForConditionalGeneration.embed_multimodal` scaled projected image features by `hidden_size**-0.5` before merging them into Gemma's `inputs_embeds`: ```python vision_embeddings = vision_embeddings * (self.config.hidden_size**-0.5) ``` That inverse scale used to compensate for Gemma's `sqrt(hidden_size)` normalizer **when it ran inside `GemmaModel.forward`**. #36787 ("Make Gemma and Gemma 2 accept `inputs_embeds` like Gemma 3") moved that normalization to the text embed path: - `GemmaModel.embed_input_ids` now returns `self.embed_tokens(input_ids) * self.normalizer` (`normalizer = hidden_size**0.5`) — text is scaled at embed time. - `GemmaModel.forward` consumes the merged `inputs_embeds` **as-is** (`if inputs_embeds is not None: hidden_states = inputs_embeds`) — no compensating multiply. So after #36787, text rows enter the LM at `×sqrt(H)` while image rows enter at `÷sqrt(H)` — image features end up ~`1/H` of their intended magnitude relative to text. The issue reports the effect as image cosine ~0.90 vs HF, rising to ~0.99 once the line is removed. ## Fix Return the projected image features **unscaled**, matching HF Transformers (which scales text and leaves the projected image features unscaled) and the post-#36787 Gemma text path. `image_embeds` inputs (user-supplied pre-projected embeds) are likewise no longer wrongly divided. `ColPaliModel` (`colpali.py`) subclasses `PaliGemmaForConditionalGeneration` and does not override `embed_multimodal`, so this one-line change also fixes the `vidore/colpali-*` retrieval models. ## Test Adds `tests/models/multimodal/test_paligemma_image_embed_scale.py` — a weight-free unit test that pins the `image_embeds` pass-through contract (`embed_multimodal` must return user image embeddings unchanged). **Note on local verification:** vLLM is too heavy to build/run in my environment, so I verified the fix by tracing the three code legs (`paligemma.py:382`, `gemma.py:295` embed-time scale, `gemma.py:306` forward passthrough) against `main` and confirming the ColPali inheritance; the numeric A/B is in #52667. Happy to add a Transformers-parity logits test if you'd prefer that over (or alongside) the unit test — just point me at the right harness/marker.

signal.title: [Bug]: ModelOpt NVFP4 on SM120 dies or wedges under sustained load with CUDA graphs (not the NVFP4 GEMM backend)
signal.text: ### Your current environment <details> <summary>Environment</summary> - GPU: 2x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition (sm120, 96 GB), driver 595.71.05, ECC clean - Container: `vllm/vllm-openai` v0.26.0 (`sha256:ffb2d59b1c059a5bd8d781320c9f5189de8293693b7d95da54befddaa54abf52`) and v0.27.1 (`sha256:0a51ea5b4ae2dc5d81890e5173f54203d2a3ae0cfffe51b8fd2afd4391bfd967`), podman, `--ipc host` - CUDA 13.0.2, torch 2.11.0+cu130, flashinfer 0.6.14 - Model: Qwen3.8-27B quantized by ModelOpt 0.47.0.dev0 to `MIXED_PRECISION`. 193 layers NVFP4 (all 64 `mlp.{gate,up,down}_proj` plus `lm_head`), 208 layers FP8 (`linear_attn.*`, `self_attn.*`), `kv_cache_quant_algo: FP8`. Architecture `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` (hybrid GDN linear attention with full attention every 4th layer), hidden 5120, ffn 17408, vocab 248320, 64 layers. - vLLM resolves this to `quantization=modelopt_mixed` and selects `FlashInferCutlassNvFp4LinearKernel` for the NVFP4 GEMMs, `FlashInferFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` for FP8, and the `FLASHINFER` attention backend. </details> ### 🐛 Describe the bug Serving a ModelOpt-NVFP4 checkpoint on SM120 dies under sustained batch load, reliably, on two vLLM releases. The same base model quantized to FP8 and served from the same image with the same attention backend is stable. The failure is specific to the NVFP4 build. I have not isolated the mechanism, and two backends I suspected are now ruled out by measurement (see the update comment below). **One thing that is measured but is not the cause.** `flashinfer.mm_fp4` hands the CUTLASS FP4 GEMM a fixed 32 MiB shared workspace, and on SM120 the kernel asks for 34 MiB at every M from 1 to 256 for this model's fused gate/up projection (5120 → 34816). Every decode-sized call therefore takes a fallback branch in `csrc/fp4_gemm_cutlass_sm120.cu` that allocates a private workspace and releases it right after an asynchronous launch, including inside CUDA graph capture. That is filed as https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4549 with a fix in https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4550. Raising the shared workspace so the fallback never fires does **not** stop the crash: the patched build failed after 15.0 minutes against 16.5 for the unpatched one. Recording it here so nobody else spends the window I spent on it. **Symptoms, for searchability.** Two failure modes, both with CUDA graphs enabled: | vLLM | spec decode | time to failure | error | |---|---|---|---| | v0.26.0 | none | 16 min 35 s | illegal memory access | | v0.27.1 | none | 21 min 32 s | illegal memory access | | v0.26.0 | MTP, 3 tokens | not recorded | misaligned address | | v0.26.0 | none | 8 s, on a boot right after a prior fault | illegal memory access in `BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCache` | The exception always surfaces at an asynchronous synchronization point, so the reported frame is never the offending kernel: ``` File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 314, in get_output self.async_copy_ready_event.synchronize() torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered ``` The second mode is a wedge. The engine stops making progress without raising anything, `/v1/models` still returns 200 in about a millisecond, `/v1/chat/completions` never returns, and the GPU sits at 100% utilization. `py-spy` shows the engine thread blocked in a kernel launch that never returns, and the driver reports `Xid 8 ... GPU is probably locked` only much later. `dmesg` records MMU faults at wild addresses, `faulted @ 0x4_00000000` and `0xf_00001000`, both `FAULT_PDE`. **Differential.** The same base model quantized to FP8, same box, same image, same FlashInfer attention backend, CUDA graphs on, prefix caching on, `--max-model-len 262144`, logged 10,282 completions across 35 hours with no illegal-address or misaligned-address error. The NVFP4 build dies after roughly 570 completions. Both GPUs produce the NVFP4 fault and ECC is clean on both. `--enforce-eager` reduces the rate roughly tenfold without eliminating it. We also swept the NVFP4 GEMM for memory-safety problems and found none: every layer shape in the model, every M from 1 to 8192, all 32 SM120 CUTLASS FP4 tactics, under `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck` with `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1`, with both a zeroed and a randomly poisoned workspace. Those runs cannot catch this defect, because disabling the caching allocator turns every free into a synchronizing `cudaFree`. ### Workarounds available today from vLLM Either of these avoids the fallback path without a FlashInfer patch: 1. `VLLM_DISABLED_KERNELS=FlashInferCutlassNvFp4LinearKernel`, which falls through to vLLM's native `CutlassNvFp4LinearKernel`. On our workload that reached 0.65 completions per second against 0.67 for the FlashInfer kernel, and 50 deterministic classification prompts returned byte-identical answers, so the swap does not change results. Soak results below. 2. `--enforce-eager`, which reduces the failure rate roughly tenfold without removing it, and costs more than the kernel swap. Swapping to `CutlassNvFp4LinearKernel` does not fix the failure, so quarantining the FlashInfer kernel on SM12x would not be a fix either. Both workarounds above are partial.

signal.title: [Model] Add --video-max-pixels-per-frame to make Qwen3-VL video cost duration-proportional
signal.text: ## Purpose Qwen3-VL's video processor spreads `size["longest_edge"]` — a TOTAL pixel budget — across all sampled frames. Under a large budget (e.g. the model card's "Long Video Understanding" recipe, `longest_edge: 469762048` ≈ 224K video tokens), a short clip samples few frames at near-native resolution, so its token cost is nearly duration-independent: | Input (1080p) | Frames sampled | Prompt tokens | Tokens/frame | |---|---|---|---| | 90 s clip | 180 | 184,463 | ~1,020 | | 10 min film | 768 | 224,957 | ~293 | A 90 s clip costing ~82% of an hour-scale budget is a sharp edge: users raising the budget for long-video support pay it on every short clip too. This PR adds `MultiModalConfig.video_max_pixels_per_frame` (CLI `--video-max-pixels-per-frame`, default `None` = behavior unchanged). When set, each video's effective budget is `min(size["longest_edge"], num_sampled_frames * cap)`, applied per item in `Qwen3VLMultiModalProcessor._call_hf_processor` for presampled videos (vLLM's own loader path, where the sampled frame count is known). Setting `cap = budget / max_frames` gives every clip the same per-frame spend a fully sampled video gets, making cost scale with duration; long budget-filling videos are unaffected. Design notes: - Config-level option (precedent: `video_pruning_rate`) rather than an `mm_processor_kwargs` key, because config-level mm kwargs are re-merged before the HF processor call and unknown keys can leak into it. - Memory profiling stays exact: `get_dummy_mm_data` spreads the same total budget over `cdiv(budget, cap)` frames (clamped to the processor's `max_frames`) so the cap is not binding for the profiling dummy and the profiled maximum item still reaches the full budget. Without this, the 2-frame dummy collapses the profiled max item (we measured encoder cache 229,376 → 16,384, breaking all video requests with 400s). - Analytic max-token computation is intentionally untouched (a conservative upper bound in the corner case where the cap binds at `max_frames`). ## Duplicate check Searched open PRs/issues for per-frame video pixel budgeting ("video pixels per frame", "qwen3-vl video token budget"): no existing work addresses this. Related but distinct: #41239 (encoder budget CLI args), EVS/VidCom2 pruning (post-encoder token pruning; this PR reduces pre-encoder pixel spend and composes with it). ## Test Plan - New `test_video_max_pixels_per_frame` in `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen3_vl.py` (`Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct`, synthetic presampled videos): capped < uncapped; token count exactly duration-proportional (16-frame == 2 × 8-frame at equal per-frame budget); oversized cap is a no-op. - `pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen3_vl.py -q` - `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` (ruff, mypy, config-docstring validation, DCO) ## Test Result - `7 passed` (whole file, including the 6 pre-existing tests). - pre-commit: all hooks pass. - E2E on Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 (RTX PRO 6000, 224K-token video recipe, `--video-max-pixels-per-frame 611669` = budget/768): - 90 s 1080p clip: 184,463 → **52,701** prompt tokens (−71%), answer quality unchanged in side-by-side use. - 90 s clip + 10 min film in one prompt: 277,690 tokens, completed in 190.8 s with a correct, frame-accurate comparison answer. - Boot profiling intact: multimodal warmup 27.5 s, encoder cache unchanged, no video-request 400s. - Default-path regression: with the flag unset, processing is byte-identical (the new code path is `None`-gated). ## AI Disclosure Developed with AI assistance (Claude Fable 5). The human submitter has reviewed every changed line and run the tests above.

signal.title: [Bug]: Marlin MoE support probe raises TypeError instead of returning a verdict for unset group_size
signal.text:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Collecting environment information... ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 Clang version : Could not collect CMake version : version 4.4.2 Libc version : glibc-2.39 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.13.0+xpu Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : None ROCM used to build PyTorch : N/A XPU used to build PyTorch : 20260000 ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.3 (main, Jun 19 2026, 12:46:00) [GCC 13.3.0] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-7.0.0-28-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 ============================== Intel XPU / GPU Info ============================== Is XPU available : True XPU runtime version : 20260000 Intel GPU models : GPU 0: Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B70 Graphics --Compile time-- oneAPI compiler version : Could not collect SYCL compiler build : Could not collect oneCCL version : 2022.0.0 --Runtime-- Intel Graphics Compiler (IGC): 2.34.4 Intel GMM (libigdgmm) : 22.10.0 ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug `compressed_tensors` channel-strategy quantization leaves `group_size` unset (`None`). Two independent sites compare it against `int` instead of handling `None` — different exception, different bit-width: - **int4** — `check_moe_marlin_supports_config` (`marlin_utils.py:378`/`:383`, `group_size <= 0`) raises `TypeError` from inside `_backend_incompatibility_reason` (`int_wna16.py:163`), which is supposed to *return* a reason string, not raise — backend selection aborts instead of falling back. A second int4 site, `marlin_moe_padded_intermediate` (`marlin_utils.py:344`, `group_size if group_size > 0 else 1`), fails the same way during weight-prep. - **int8** — `CompressedTensorsWNA16MoEMethod.__init__` (`compressed_tensors_moe_wna16.py:85`, `assert self.group_size == -1`) raises `AssertionError` unconditionally, *before* backend selection even runs. Six existing sites already normalise this the same way (`-1 if group_size is None else group_size`) — e.g. `compressed_tensors_wNa16.py:67`, `compressed_tensors_moe.py:104`. This file (`compressed_tensors_moe_wna16.py:69`) doesn't. Reproducer (int4 — int8 crashes the same root cause earlier, in `__init__`, via `assert`): ```python from compressed_tensors.quantization import ( QuantizationArgs, QuantizationStrategy, QuantizationType, ) from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.marlin_utils import ( check_moe_marlin_supports_config, ) from types import SimpleNamespace args = QuantizationArgs( num_bits=4, type=QuantizationType.INT, strategy=QuantizationStrategy.CHANNEL, symmetric=True, dynamic=False, ) assert args.group_size is None config = SimpleNamespace( hidden_dim=4096, intermediate_size_per_partition_unpadded=1024, ) check_moe_marlin_supports_config(config, args.group_size, allow_tile_padding=True) ``` ### Real-world impact - Defensive-correctness gap, not an observed production failure. - Real checkpoints exist and are loadable: [Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-W4A16-channel-quantized](https://huggingface.co/nm-testing/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-W4A16-channel-quantized) (int4, hits the `TypeError` above) and [DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct-W8A8](https://huggingface.co/nm-testing/DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct-W8A8) / [Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-W8A8](https://huggingface.co/nm-testing/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-W8A8) (int8, hits the `__init__` `AssertionError` instead). - All three belong to `nm-testing` — compressed-tensors/llm-compressor's own CI-fixture account: single- to low-double-digit downloads, zero likes, over a year stale. No channel-strategy MoE checkpoint found from a more production-facing source (RedHatAI currently ships no MoE + W8A8 checkpoints at all). - Real and reproducible, but no evidence this affects an actively deployed model today. I have a patch that normalises at all read sites above (both bit-widths) and will open it against this issue. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] I have searched for similar issues. - [x] I have already asked the chatbot for help.

signal.title: [Perf] Backfill divergent local hybrid hits from the offloading connector
signal.text: ## Purpose Addresses #52773. With hybrid models (Mamba + full attention), per-group local prefix hits diverge under block pressure: the full-attention prefix survives deeper in HBM than the recurrent state, which can only resume at a boundary with a state snapshot. Today the offloading connector never sees the divergent hit (`supports_divergent_local_hybrid_hits` is `False`, #50344), so the resident full-attention KV above the common boundary is given up and re-fetched from the store; capable connectors reconcile to the common boundary whenever no external tokens lie beyond the deep hit (#48425), without asking whether the store can back an intermediate boundary. In the common write-through setup the store holds full per-group chunk sets — exactly the missing piece — but no path asks for it (measured ~80× cost per event on a revisit/fork workload, see the linked issue). This PR adds a backfill path: - **`KVConnectorBase_V1.get_hybrid_backfill_tokens(request, num_computed_tokens) -> (num_local, num_external)`** (optional, default `(0, 0)`): consulted only for connectors with `supports_divergent_local_hybrid_hits`, when the local hits diverged and `get_num_new_matched_tokens()` reported no external tokens beyond the divergent hit. - **Scheduler** (`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`): in the `hit_diverged and ext == 0` branch, if the connector reports a backed boundary, keep the local prefix below it (`truncate_computed_blocks`, whose Mamba-aware slicing already models the ragged groups) and async-load just the boundary chunk; otherwise reconcile exactly as before. - **`OffloadingConnector`**: implements the hook with a boundary-walk probe over the per-group offload keys (deepest boundary whose chunk is `HIT` in every group; boundaries being loaded are skipped), and now opts into `supports_divergent_local_hybrid_hits` when every group resumes from a single chunk: uniform `tokens_per_chunk`, every sliding window ≤ 1 chunk (recurrent groups are modeled as one-chunk windows), no eagle groups. Configs outside that (wider SWA windows, eagle) keep today's behavior — the capability stays `False`. - **`MultiConnector`**: forwards the probe; the first child reporting a backed boundary is assigned the request (the hook is only consulted when no child had matched tokens, so no child has been assigned yet). The load itself reuses the existing external-load path unchanged (`update_state_after_alloc` computes the chunk set from the probe-adjusted bookkeeping); `get_hybrid_backfill_tokens` must be called after `get_num_new_matched_tokens()`, which is the order the scheduler uses. Known minor: `update_num_hit_chunks` is recorded at the pre-backfill query, so per-group hit metrics do not count the backfilled boundary chunk. ## Test Plan ```bash VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k "hybrid" -v .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -k "backfill or partial_lookup" -v .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py -v pre-commit run --files <changed files> ``` New tests: - `test_hybrid_fa_deeper_hit_backfilled_by_connector` (core scheduler, both backfill-hit and backfill-miss parametrizations, including the async-load resume flow); - `test_hybrid_backfill_returns_deepest_fully_backed_boundary`, `test_hybrid_backfill_misses_when_no_boundary_is_fully_backed`, `test_hybrid_backfill_skips_boundaries_being_loaded` (offloading probe). ## Test Result - `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k "hybrid"`: **7 passed** (5 pre-existing divergence cases unchanged + 2 new). - `offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -k "backfill or partial_lookup"`: **5 passed**. - `test_multi_connector.py`: **21 passed, 2 failed** — the same 2 failures (`test_multi_example_connector_consistency`, `test_multi_connector_mixed_hma_disables_hybrid_kv_cache`) reproduce identically on pristine `main` in this environment and are unrelated; the override-completeness guard `test_multi_connector_overrides_all_base_methods` passes with the new base method delegated. - `pre-commit` hooks pass on all changed files. Marked as **draft**: I plan to attach paired end-to-end numbers (hybrid revisit/fork workload, offloading on, backfill on/off) from our test rig, and I'm happy to split the base-API change from the offloading implementation if preferred. --- *Disclosure per `AGENTS.md`: this PR was AI-assisted (Claude Code). I have reviewed every changed line and run the tests above. Duplicate-work check (2026-08-18): searched issues/PRs for `hit_diverged`, `get_computed_blocks_for_connector`, `supports_divergent_local_hybrid_hits`, "divergent hybrid mamba", "mamba offloading", "backfill mamba" — the correctness lineage (#48425, #50344, and open #46455 / #48195) reconciles or scopes divergent hits; no existing issue or PR consults the offload store below a divergent hit. This change affects scheduling only when the new probe reports a backed boundary; output correctness is covered by the resume-boundary invariant the existing divergence tests assert.*

signal.title: [Bugfix][Structured Output][Spec Decode] Constrain bitmask and trim grammar advance at the reasoning boundary
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #44006. When `VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=1` is combined with MTP/EAGLE speculative decoding, the engine intermittently rejects token 248069 (Qwen's `</think>`) and the request finishes with 500 "Failed to advance FSM ... grammar rejected tokens". There are two related defects in `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask`, a hardening follow-up to the first fix, and a scheduler-side fix required after rebasing onto main containing #42452 — all included here. ### 1. Mid-window reasoning-end loses the bitmask switch `should_fill_bitmask` reflects `reasoning_ended` at the *start* of the step. When MTP/EAGLE schedules multiple positions per step, the `</think>` marker can land in the middle of a spec window. The previous code prepared the entire window with the same `apply_bitmask` value the step started with, so positions *after* the marker still got the unconstrained "in-reasoning" mask. The model could then emit a token listed in `structural_tag.excludes` (e.g. another `</think>` after content has begun), and the next step rejects it via `accept_tokens`, killing the request. Fix: for each draft token in the simulated window, call `reasoner.is_reasoning_end_streaming(...)` on the running prefix. Once the marker is observed, flip `apply_bitmask=True` so all subsequent positions in the same step (including the bonus row) get the grammar-constrained mask. The marker token itself is reasoning content, so grammar advancement is skipped for that position. ### 2. Bonus row inherits stale `apply_bitmask` from `-1` padding In the async spec-decode path, `update_draft_token_ids_in_output` pads invalid draft slots with `-1`. The previous loop iterated `itertools.chain(req_tokens, (-1,))` and set `apply_bitmask=False` on the first `-1`. The trailing `-1` (the bonus-token slot) therefore inherited `False` whenever any earlier draft was padded, and the bonus row was filled with the unconstrained mask — re-introducing exactly the same class of failure as (1) but at the bonus position. Fix: compute the bonus row as `should_fill_bitmask(request) or apply_bitmask`, so a mid-window reasoning-end also reaches the bonus row and `-1` padding can no longer flip it to the unconstrained mask. ### 3. Harden the mid-window advance against grammar-invalid drafts (`0ff3348f2`) Fix (1) introduced a new path: once the marker is observed mid-window, the drafts that follow it are fed to `grammar.accept_tokens`. Those drafts were produced before the grammar became active and are not guaranteed valid. With a permissive grammar (`structural_tag`) they are usually accepted, but with a strict-start grammar (`response_format={"type": "json_object"}`) the first post-marker draft can be rejected, and the old code raised `AssertionError`. Skipping advancement entirely instead froze the bitmask at the grammar's initial state, letting the opening token repeat (e.g. `{{`). Fix: still attempt to advance through post-marker drafts so the next bitmask row reflects the advanced state, but tolerate `accept_tokens` rejection at those positions instead of asserting; advancements within the window are rolled back at the end so the persisted grammar state is unchanged. ### 4. Post-#42452: keep reasoning content out of the scheduler's grammar advance (`6b1b0ca8f`) Rebasing onto current main brought in #42452, which makes `should_advance` return True at the reasoning-boundary step for structural tags + speculative decoding, so the FSM can advance through trigger text in the same step. As a side effect the scheduler now feeds that step's tokens straight into `grammar.accept_tokens`, and they still contain reasoning content up to and including the end marker (e.g. `[198, 248069]` = `"\n</think>"`). The structural-tag grammar excludes the marker, `accept_tokens` rejects it, and the request dies with FINISHED_ERROR — re-surfacing #44006 on the rebased branch. On the pre-#42452 base this path was unreachable because `should_advance` returned False at the boundary. Fix: keep #42452's same-step advance, but record the marker's absolute index when the boundary fires (`should_advance`) and drop everything up to and including the marker before the scheduler advances (`trim_reasoning_for_advance`). A step that is entirely reasoning content skips the advance, matching the pre-#42452 behavior for that shape. The sampling side (`grammar_bitmask`, which never advances through the marker) and the accept side now agree: reasoning content never reaches the grammar. ## Why this is not a duplicate Checked open PRs: gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "44006 in:body" gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "structured_output speculative bitmask" No open PR addresses these failure modes. PR #25515 introduced the `reasoning_ended` machinery itself; this PR fixes its interaction with multi-position spec windows. #42452 (merged) fixes FSM advancement for structural tags in `should_advance`; this PR is complementary: it fixes the missing bitmask constraints inside the spec window and trims reasoning content from the tokens that #42452 now routes into `accept_tokens`. ## Test Plan ### Unit tests `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py` (added): - `-1` padding still produces an N+1 row bitmask with terminated FSM state correct - Mid-window grammar termination after EOS - Bitmask idempotent across repeated calls - **Bonus row stays constrained after `-1`-padded drafts** (regression for defect 2) - **Mid-window reasoning-end keeps post-marker positions constrained** (regression for defect 1) - **Post-marker draft the grammar rejects skips the advance instead of asserting** (regression for fix 3) - `validate_tokens` → pad with `-1` → `grammar_bitmask` round-trip does not assert - **Boundary step records the reasoning-end marker index** (regression for fix 4) - **`trim_reasoning_for_advance` drops the marker and everything before it, passes later steps through unchanged, and trims the `[198, </think>]` crash shape to empty** (regression for fix 4) Also re-ran neighbouring tests to confirm no regression: pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py -v pytest tests/v1/structured_output/ -v pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_backup_token_async_spec.py \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_synthetic_rejection_sampler_utils.py -v Result: - test_mtp_structured_output.py: 16 passed (7 cases × xgrammar / guidance, + 2 manager-level cases for fix 4; re-run on the rebased branch) - tests/v1/structured_output/: 20 passed - spec-decode rejection-sampler / backup-token subset: 34 passed ### End-to-end reproducer 2× H20-96GB, TP=2, Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B + MTP(k=1) + `--reasoning-parser qwen3` + `--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder` + `VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=1`. Fire 50× the Korean weather tool-calling request from the issue against each branch. Server: export VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}' \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \ --max-model-len 8192 \ --max-num-seqs 8 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \ --enable-chunked-prefill \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --enable-log-requests \ --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0}' \ --trust-remote-code \ --enforce-eager \ --port 8000 | Branch | 200 OK | HTTP 500 | Failure rate | |---|---|---|---| | upstream/main (baseline) | 21 | 29 | 58% | | this PR | 50 | 0 | 0% | Baseline vllm serve log shows the exact error from the issue: ERROR ... [backend_xgrammar.py:158] Failed to advance FSM for request ... for token 248069. Please file an issue. ERROR ... [scheduler.py:1429] Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [..., 248069] for request ... After this PR, no such error appears across 50 trials. Re-ran the same 50-trial reproducer after `0ff3348f2`: still 50/50, no regression. ### Re-validation after the rebase (fix 4) Same model/flags on 4× NVIDIA H20-3e 143GB, TP=4, branch rebased onto `fe04238` (post-#42452 main): | Branch | 200 OK | HTTP 500 | Failure rate | |---|---|---|---| | rebased, without fix 4 | 26 | 24 | 48% | | rebased, with fix 4 (`6b1b0ca8f`) | 50 | 0 | 0% | The without-fix-4 failures reproduce the original signature (`grammar rejected tokens [198, 248069]`), confirming the accept-side path that fix 4 closes. ---

signal.title: [Rust Frontend] Add Olmo3 tool parser
signal.text: ## Purpose Add the Olmo3 tool parser to the experimental Rust frontend. - Parses `<function_calls>...</function_calls>` blocks containing newline-separated Python-style calls. - Supports parallel calls, nested dict/list/tuple literals, Python and JSON boolean/null literals, parameterless calls, and arbitrary stream chunk boundaries. - Preserves visible text before and after tool calls in event order. - Falls back to ordinary text for incomplete or unsupported tool-call expressions instead of panicking. - Registers the `olmo3` parser and automatic `olmo-3` / `olmo3` model matchers. - Adds a real `allenai/Olmo-3-7B-Instruct` tokenizer/template roundtrip fixture. Tracks the Olmo3 tool-parser item in #44280. ### Duplicate-work check Before implementation and again before opening this PR, I checked: - comments on #44280; - open PRs referencing #44280; - open PR searches for `olmo3 rust tool parser` and related Rust frontend keywords. I found no open PR implementing the Olmo3 Rust tool parser. #47345 is an Olmo3 reasoning-parser PR and does not overlap this change. ### AI assistance AI assistance was used to inspect the existing parser architecture, implement the Rust changes, and prepare tests. The submitting human will review every changed line and must be able to explain and maintain the implementation before this PR is marked ready for review. ## Test Plan ```bash cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-parser --lib cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-chat --lib HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml \ -p vllm-chat --test roundtrip roundtrip_olmo3 cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml \ -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat --all-targets -- -D warnings pre-commit run --files \ rust/Cargo.lock rust/Cargo.toml rust/src/chat/src/lib.rs \ rust/src/chat/src/parser/tool/mod.rs rust/src/chat/src/parser/tool/tests.rs \ rust/src/chat/tests/roundtrip.rs rust/src/parser/Cargo.toml \ rust/src/parser/src/tool/mod.rs rust/src/parser/src/tool/olmo3.rs ``` The roundtrip test uses cached tokenizer/template files from the official `allenai/Olmo-3-7B-Instruct` repository; no model weights or GPU are required. A model-quality evaluation is not applicable because this change does not alter model execution or generated outputs. A full-model serving regression was performed to validate parser integration, as recorded below. ## Test Result - `vllm-parser`: 421 passed. - `vllm-chat` library: 265 passed. - Olmo3 real model-family roundtrip: 1 passed. - Clippy with `-D warnings`: passed. - Changed-file pre-commit hooks: passed. ## Full-model serving regression Downloaded and served the complete `allenai/Olmo-3-7B-Instruct` checkpoint (13.59 GiB) on the CPU backend with the locally built PR Rust binary, `--tool-call-parser olmo3`, and the real model tokenizer/chat template. - `/health` and `/v1/models`: passed. - Plain chat: returned exactly `hello`. - Required single tool: returned one `get_weather` call with `{"city":"Shanghai"}` and `finish_reason = "tool_calls"`. - Required parallel tools: returned ordered Shanghai and Beijing calls. - Text before tool call: preserved `content = "I will check."` before the parsed tool call. - Streaming parallel tools: six SSE chunks reconstructed into two complete ordered calls and ended with `finish_reason = "tool_calls"`.

signal.title: [Rust Frontend] Add MiniMax M2 append-think reasoning parser
signal.text: ## Summary - add the explicit `minimax_m2_append_think` Rust reasoning parser - prepend `<think>` once while preserving all generated output as visible content - preserve special tokens and keep automatic MiniMax model routing on the normal parser - cover parser lifecycle, empty deltas, factory registration, and parser-name diagnostics ## Duplicate-work check This does not duplicate an existing PR. Before implementation I checked: - roadmap issue #44280 and its comments - open PRs referencing `44280` - open PR searches for `minimax_m2_append_think` and MiniMax M2 append-think parser terms No overlapping Rust implementation or claim was found. The item was claimed in #44280 before implementation. ## Tests - `cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-parser --lib` — 420 passed - `cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-chat --lib` — 266 passed - `cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat --all-targets -- -D warnings` — passed - `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` — passed ## Full-model serving regression A CPU-only end-to-end serving regression was run with the locally built PR Rust binary and the full `allenai/Olmo-3-7B-Instruct` weights (13.59 GiB), using `--reasoning-parser minimax_m2_append_think`. A different model was intentionally used because the parser is selected explicitly and MiniMax M2.5 itself is approximately 434 GiB across 125 weight shards. - Rust frontend, Python engine, tokenizer/template loading, and OpenAI HTTP serving all started successfully. - Non-streaming output preserved generated text as content and prepended exactly one marker: `content = "<think>hello world"`, `reasoning = null`. - Streaming reconstruction produced `content = "<think>hello world"`, empty reasoning, one `<think>` prefix, and `finish_reason = "stop"`. A model-quality evaluation is not applicable because this change does not affect model execution, logits, or sampling; the full-model run validates parser integration and HTTP behavior. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used to analyze the parser architecture, implement the change, and run validation. This PR is intentionally opened as a draft and must be reviewed line by line by the human submitter before being marked ready.

signal.title: [Performance]: Hybrid + KV offloading discards reusable divergent prefix hits — offloaded boundary state is never consulted
signal.text: ### Proposal to improve performance With hybrid models (Mamba/recurrent + full attention), per-group local prefix hits can diverge under block pressure: the full-attention prefix often survives deeper in HBM than the recurrent state, which can only resume at a boundary where a state snapshot exists. The *correctness* side of this was settled by #46453 → #48425 (reconcile to the boundary every group agrees on) and #50344 (scope divergent hits to capable connectors). What is still left on the floor is *performance*, in both of the two regimes that exist on `main` today: 1. **Store-style connectors (e.g. `OffloadingConnector`) never see the divergent hit.** `supports_divergent_local_hybrid_hits` defaults to `False`, so `Scheduler._get_local_prefix_cache_hit()` uses `get_computed_blocks()` — the common boundary. Everything the full-attention group still holds in HBM above that boundary is re-fetched from the offload store (or recomputed where not offloaded), even though the KV is resident and only the recurrent state at one boundary is missing. 2. **Capable connectors reconcile without a second look.** On the divergent path, when `get_num_new_matched_tokens()` — queried at the *deep* boundary — returns 0, the scheduler falls back to the common boundary (the `hit_diverged and num_external_computed_tokens == 0` branch in `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`) without ever asking whether the connector can back an *intermediate* boundary. In the common write-through setup the offload store holds full per-group chunk sets, i.e. exactly the boundary state needed to keep the deeper hit — but no path ever asks for it. #### Measured impact Measured on v0.27.1, where `OffloadingConnector` still took the divergent-hit path (pre-#50344), with a Nemotron-H-style hybrid (7 recurrent + 1 full-attention KV cache groups, 1408-token offload chunks, CPU offloading, write-through) on H100: - On a revisit/fork workload, whenever the full-attention prefix was resident but the boundary state had been evicted from HBM, the resume depth collapsed from 5632 tokens to 0. - Cost per event: recomputing ~6k tokens ≈ 231 ms, vs ≈ 2.9 ms to load the one full per-group boundary set (~154 MiB H2D) that would have kept the hit — roughly **80×**. On current `main` the same scenario is served by regime 1 instead: correct, but the resident full-attention KV above the common boundary is given up and re-transferred from CPU. #### Proposed fix: backfill the boundary instead of discarding the hit Before reconciling, ask the connector for the deepest boundary at or below the divergent hit whose chunk is offloaded in *every* group. If one exists, keep the local prefix below that boundary and async-load just the boundary chunk (restoring the lagging recurrent state): - a new optional `KVConnectorBase_V1.get_hybrid_backfill_tokens(request, num_computed_tokens) -> (num_local, num_external)`, default `(0, 0)`; - `OffloadingConnector` implements it with a boundary-walk probe over the per-group offload keys, and opts into `supports_divergent_local_hybrid_hits` when every group resumes from a single chunk (uniform chunk size; recurrent groups have a one-chunk window; wider sliding-window and eagle groups keep today's behavior); - the scheduler consults it in the `hit_diverged and ext == 0` branch and otherwise reconciles exactly as today. Draft PR: (linked below.) #### Alternatives considered Re-querying `get_num_new_matched_tokens()` at the reconciled common boundary would also recover the tokens, but it re-transfers the whole `(common, deep]` range that the full-attention group already holds locally, and connector implementations do not currently expect a second query per scheduling pass. #### Related work - #46453 / #48425 / #50344 / #46455 / #48195 — the correctness lineage for divergent hybrid hits; all correctness-scoped, none consult the store below the divergent hit. - #46896 / #51358 — Mooncake-side PRs preserving recurrent boundary state in external stores: the supply side of the same problem; they do not change the scheduler-side discard. ### Report of performance regression _No response_ ### Misc discussion on performance _No response_ ### Your current environment (if you think it is necessary) Measurements taken on v0.27.1 (8× H100 80GB, CUDA), mechanism verified against `main` (d29dc3ab8).

signal.title: Fix Transformers modelling backend `RMSNormFuser.fuse` performance
signal.text: #50128 identified that `RMSNormFuser` was taking an excessively long time at startup tracing every norm module in `fuse` bypassing the caching efficiency in `match`. This PR determines and caches the attribute to read the `eps` from at in `match` so we no longer need to trace in `fuse`. Measured on the Transformers-backend fuser path: `Fusers(model, vllm_config)` (per-class matching, cold cache) plus `fuse()` on every matched instance, which is the work `recursive_replace` does. | Model | Norms | Before | After | Speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` | 113 | 998 ms | 50 ms | 20.1x | | `google/gemma-3-4b-it` | 206 | 6050 ms | 105 ms | 57.8x | | `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B` | 33 | 261 ms | 45 ms | 5.8x | | `allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0924` | 65 | 548 ms | 83 ms | 6.6x | | `mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1` | 65 | 679 ms | 84 ms | 8.1x | Split by phase, since the two changes pull in opposite directions: | Model | match (per class) | | RMSNorm `fuse` (per instance) | | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | | before | after | before | after | | `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` | 43 ms | 37 ms | 944 ms | 2.0 ms | | `google/gemma-3-4b-it` | 112 ms | 95 ms | 5931 ms | 2.4 ms | | `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B` | 27 ms | 35 ms | 224 ms | 0.6 ms | | `allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0924` | 88 ms | 80 ms | 458 ms | 1.3 ms | | `mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1` | 72 ms | 81 ms | 605 ms | 1.2 ms | `fuse` no longer traces at all, so per-instance cost collapses (350x-2500x).
