signal.title: [RFC]: Model Runner V2 Pluggable Design
signal.text: ### Motivation. vLLM's hardware pluggability (RFC #11162) lets each backend register its own Platform, Worker, Model Runner, and so on. This works, but in practice each backend ends up copying the entire GPU model runner and maintaining it independently. The v1 GPU model runner alone is ~8000 lines. Backend-specific runners are typically in the same range, and these files are mostly copies of the GPU runner with device-specific patches sprinkled in. When the GPU runner gets a bug fix or a new feature, every backend has to manually port the change. This is expensive and error-prone. Model Runner V2 already fixes the root cause on the GPU side: it breaks the single monolithic file into smaller modules (model_states, sample, spec_decode, mm, etc.). The total code drops from ~8000 to ~1800 lines. This also creates an opportunity for hardware backends. Instead of copying the runner, backends can now **reuse the V2 runner as a framework** and only override the pieces that actually differ. The problem is that V2 was not designed with this in mind. A backend that wants to reuse the V2 runner has to work around several friction points: - The runner creates internal components (RequestState, InputBatch, CudaGraphManager, Sampler, Speculator) by directly instantiating GPU-specific classes. A backend that needs its own version has to `del` the GPU object and recreate it in `__init__`. - Some logic that backends need to customize (e.g. `prepare_inputs`) is one big method. A backend either copies the whole thing or monkey-patches internal functions. - Triton kernels used inside the runner are GPU-specific. Backends have to rewrite many kernels and patch them in at runtime ### Proposed Change. The design follows three principles: - **GPU native** - **GPU zero burden** - **Flexible backend adaptation** Hardware differences show up at three different levels. Each level needs a different mechanism. Trying to solve everything at one level (either "copy the whole runner" or "make everything a plugin") is what caused the current mess. ``` Layer 3: Runner behavior -> hooks (prepare_inputs, execute_model, ...) Layer 2: Replaceable parts -> Platform factory methods Layer 1: Kernels / ops -> Triton Dispatcher (RFC #45133) ``` ### Layer 1: Kernels Already covered by the Triton Kernel Dispatcher proposal (#45133). `@pluggable_kernel` marks a kernel as replaceable, `@register_kernel(name)` lets a backend register its own implementation. On GPU, no override is registered and the default Triton kernel runs with zero overhead. V2 uses Triton kernels in sampling, rejection sampling, mamba ops, etc. With the dispatcher, backends register their kernel implementations at startup and the runner code stays untouched. **Layer 1 must be solved first** (or in parallel) because without it, backends have no clean way to handle kernel differences. --- ### Layer 2: Platform factory methods The V2 runner is built from several internal components, for example: - `InputBatch` / `InputBuffers` - holds the tensors passed to the model - `ModelCudaGraphManager` - manages CUDA graph capture and replay - `Sampler` - handles sampling logic - `PCPManager` - handles pcp feature Some backends need their own version of these. For example, a backend's attention implementation may need `seq_lens_cpu` which the GPU runner no longer tracks, so it needs an `InputBatch` subclass with that extra field. A backend may also use a different graph mechanism, so it needs a different graph manager. The runner creates these with direct instantiation today: ```python # vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py (today) self.input_buffers = InputBuffers(...) self.cudagraph_manager = ModelCudaGraphManager(...) ``` The fix is to let the Platform provide these classes, the same way it already provides `get_attn_backend_cls` and `get_device_communicator_cls`. A single method returns all V2 runner components as a group, so the Platform interface stays clean: ```python # vllm/platforms/interface.py @dataclass class V2RunnerComponents: input_batch_cls: type input_buffers_cls: type cudagraph_manager_cls: type sampler_cls: type pcp_manager_cls: type # future components can be added here class Platform: def get_v2_runner_components(self) -> V2RunnerComponents: """Return the default (GPU) component classes for V2 model runner. Backends override this to substitute their own implementations. """ from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.input_batch import InputBatch, InputBuffers from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.cudagraph_utils import ModelCudaGraphManager from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.sampler import Sampler from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.pcp_manager import PCPManager return V2RunnerComponents( input_batch_cls=InputBatch, input_buffers_cls=InputBuffers, cudagraph_manager_cls=ModelCudaGraphManager, sampler_cls=Sampler, pcp_manager_cls=PCPManager, ) ``` The runner fetches components from the Platform in `__init__`: ```python # vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py (proposed) components = current_platform.get_v2_runner_components() self.input_buffers = components.input_buffers_cls(...) self.cudagraph_manager = components.cudagraph_manager_cls(...) ``` A backend overrides a single method: ```python # backend platform class BackendPlatform(Platform): def get_v2_runner_components(self) -> V2RunnerComponents: base = super().get_v2_runner_components() return replace(base, request_state_cls=BackendRequestState, input_batch_cls=BackendInputBatch, input_buffers_cls=BackendInputBuffers, cudagraph_manager_cls=BackendGraphManager, speculator_factory=backend_init_speculator, ) ``` --- ### Layer 3: hooks (Not planned since this is much hack. Just point it here to get your feedback) Some differences are not about swapping a component, but about adding extra steps to a flow. The most common case is `prepare_inputs`: a backend may need to maintain `seq_lens_cpu` or update extra state before attention, but the rest of the logic (sorting requests, building index mappings, padding for cudagraph) is identical to GPU. A backend that needs these extra steps often copies the entire `prepare_inputs` (~200 lines) and adds its changes. When GPU fixes a bug, the backend does not get it automatically. The fix is to split large methods into steps with hooks: ```python # vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py (proposed) class GPUModelRunner(LoRAModelRunnerMixin): def prepare_inputs(self, scheduler_output, batch_desc): # Step 1: sort and compute basic numbers req_ids, num_reqs, num_tokens = self._sort_requests(scheduler_output, batch_desc) # Step 2: backend-specific setup before building the batch self._prepare_inputs_pre_hook(scheduler_output, req_ids, num_reqs) # Step 3: build the InputBatch (shared logic) input_batch = self._build_input_batch( scheduler_output, batch_desc, req_ids, num_reqs, num_tokens ) # Step 4: backend-specific post-processing input_batch = self._prepare_inputs_post_hook(input_batch, scheduler_output) # Step 5: PCP partitioning (shared) input_batch = pcp.maybe_partition_pcp_batch(self.pcp_manager, input_batch) return input_batch def _prepare_inputs_pre_hook(self, scheduler_output, req_ids, num_reqs): pass def _prepare_inputs_post_hook(self, input_batch, scheduler_output): pass ``` A backend overrides only the hooks: ```python # backend's v2 model runner (proposed) class BackendModelRunner(GPUModelRunner): def _prepare_inputs_pre_hook(self, scheduler_output, req_ids, num_reqs): ... def _prepare_inputs_post_hook(self, input_batch, scheduler_output): ... ``` Others, like `execute_model`, can add `_pre_forward_hook` / `_post_forward_hook` as well. **If a backend needs to copy more lines of a method, that method probably needs a hook.** Do not add hooks speculatively. Add them when a real backend demonstrates the need. ### Change summary The GPU path stays simple: - Factory methods return the default GPU classes. No config, no branching. - Hooks are empty no-ops. No runtime overhead. - No new dependencies, no frameworks, no containers. The only change to GPU code is replacing `RequestState(...)` with `components.request_state_cls(...)`. Mechanical, no control flow change. A backend goes from maintaining a large copy of the runner (often thousands of lines) to: - Overriding `get_v2_runner_components` on their Platform - Overriding 2-3 hooks - Registering kernels through the Triton Dispatcher (separate, not in runner ### Feedback Period. Two weeks. ### CC List. @WoosukKwon @simon-mo @youkaichao @DarkLight1337 @ProExpertProg @LucasWilkinson @njhill @ZJY0516 ### Any Other Things. - No backwards compatibility currently, since v2 is sill under develop. Once it's stable enough, We'd like to consider it then. - This RFC is about V2 only. V1 will eventually be deprecated and removed. ## Related RFCs - #11162 - Hardware pluggable - #45133 - Triton Kernel Dispatcher ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
